alt: A manuscript page with two columns of large rounded Insular majuscule script in black, each line with a small reddish-brown gloss written between the lines. At the top of the right column the Gospel text ends, followed by EXPLICIT LIBER SECUNDUM IOHANNEM in large red-brown display capitals. Below, a long note in small brown minuscule fills the rest of the column, with each paragraph marked by a cross, and further notes in the right margin.
caption: The end of the Gospel of John with the colophon of Aldred, c. 950–970, naming Eadfrith, Æthelwald, Billfrith and Aldred. Lindisfarne Gospels, fol. 259r. London, British Library, Cotton MS Nero D IV. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A small stone castle with tall chimneys and a flag on top of a steep rocky crag, rising from a green grassy mound under a wide sky with long clouds. A dry-stone wall runs across the foreground.
caption: Holy Island of Lindisfarne, with the castle on Beblowe Crag (sixteenth century, converted in 1901). Photo: Matthew Hunt, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A large dark grey stone slab set into a stone floor, with a fine crack running across it. Near the top the name CUTHBERTUS is inlaid in gilded letters of Insular form.
caption: The tomb of Saint Cuthbert in the feretory of Durham Cathedral. Photo: Rob Farrow, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A manuscript page with a large round arch on five columns. The arch and the columns are filled with tiny interlaced birds in blue, yellow and red; the capitals and bases are stepped panels of yellow knotwork. Under the arch the heading CANON PRIMUS IN QUO QUATTUOR in red and black, and four small arches labelled MAT MAR LUC IOH above four columns of Roman numerals. A red stamp of the British Museum is near the bottom.
caption: The first canon table, Lindisfarne Gospels, fol. 10r, c. 715–720. London, British Library, Cotton MS Nero D IV. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A manuscript page with a large round arch on five columns filled with interlaced birds in blue, red and yellow, with yellow knotwork capitals and bases. The heading CANON PRIMUS IN QUO QUATTUOR in red and black, four small green arches with the names of the evangelists, columns of Roman numerals, and at the bottom FINIT CANON PRIMUS IN QUO QUATTUOR in green and black letters between the columns.
caption: The end of the first canon table, Lindisfarne Gospels, fol. 11r, c. 715–720. London, British Library, Cotton MS Nero D IV. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A manuscript page entirely covered by ornament within a stepped green frame with projecting knotwork motifs at the corners and in the middle of each side. A cross with rounded, arched ends, outlined in red, is set in a field of dense interlace. Its arms are filled with green and red interlace with five small white roundels; the background panels are packed with interlaced birds and beasts in blue, pink, yellow and brown.
caption: Carpet page before the Gospel of Matthew, Lindisfarne Gospels, fol. 26v, c. 715–720. London, British Library, Cotton MS Nero D IV. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A manuscript page dominated by huge interlocking letters XP at the top, filled with spirals, interlace and small roundels in pink, red, yellow and green, outlined with rows of red dots; one letter ends in a bird's head. Below, the rest of the words in large decorated capitals filled with colour within a frame of red dots and interlace. Small reddish-brown Old English words are written between the lines and in the right margin.
caption: The Chi-Rho page, opening of the account of the birth of Christ, Matthew 1:18, Lindisfarne Gospels, fol. 29r, c. 715–720. London, British Library, Cotton MS Nero D IV. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A manuscript page with a huge decorated initial Q at the left, its bowl filled with spirals and its tail extending down the page and filled with interlace. To the right, the words QUONIAM QUIDEM MULTI CONATI SUNT ORDINARE NARRATIONEM in decorated capitals on grounds of red dots, inside a frame of interlaced birds. At the lower right corner of the frame a cat's head looks inwards, its body formed by a band containing a row of birds.
caption: The opening of the Gospel of Luke, Quoniam quidem multi, Lindisfarne Gospels, fol. 139r, c. 715–720. London, British Library, Cotton MS Nero D IV. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: San Matteo in Lindisfarne Gospels
caption: Portrait of Saint Matthew the Evangelist, Lindisfarne Gospels, fol. 25v, c. 715–720. London, British Library, Cotton MS Nero D IV.

alt: A painted page within a dark green border dotted with white. An old bearded man with a gold halo, in a green tunic and purple mantle, sits on a stool writing in a large book on his knees, his feet on a footstool. Behind him stands a tall red book cupboard with open doors and a gabled top, its shelves holding red-bound books. A small table with an inkwell stands beside him, and writing tools lie on the floor.
caption: The scribe Ezra, Codex Amiatinus, fol. 5r, Wearmouth-Jarrow, before 716. Florence, Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana, Amiatino 1. Photo: Gennadii Saus i Segura, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Beatus vir: The Opening of the Psalter
caption: Beatus vir: The Opening of the Psalter, Österreichische Nationalbibliothek, Vienna, Cod. 1861, fol. 25r.

alt: Vox Christi de Iuda: The Opening of Psalm 51
caption: Vox Christi de Iuda: The Opening of Psalm 51, Österreichische Nationalbibliothek, Vienna, Cod. 1861, fol. 67v.

alt: Vox Christi et ecclesiae: The Opening of Psalm 101
caption: Vox Christi et ecclesiae: The Opening of Psalm 101, Österreichische Nationalbibliothek, Vienna, Cod. 1861, fol. 108v.

alt: Virgin as Queen of Heaven
caption: Virgin as Queen of Heaven, 6th century, tempera on panel in encaustic, height: 164 cm, Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere, Rome.

alt: Rabula Gospels
caption: Miniature painting from the Rabula Gospels depicting the Crucifixion in the upper panel and the Resurrection in the lower panel, 586, mineral and vegetal pigments on vellum parchment, 340 x 270 mm, Biblioteca Medicea Laurenziana, Cod. Plut. I, 56, fol. 13r.

alt: Carmina Figurata
caption: Example of carmina figurata (Leaf 5 verso of Liber de Laudibus Sanctae Crucis), 11th century, mineral pigments on parchment, 42 x 34.5 cm, Bern Burgbiblothek, Cod.9.

alt: Rhabanus, Alcuin and Otgar in De Laudibus sanctae crucis
caption: Rabanus (left), introduced by Alcuin, presents the illuminated codex to Otgar, Bishop of Mainz - folio 2v, De Laudibus sanctae crucis, 830-840, mineral and vegetal pigments mixed with egg white on purple-dyed vellum parchment, 403 x 307 mm, Österreichische Nationalbibliothek, Wien, cod. 652.

alt: The building of the Tower of Babel - De Universo
caption: De Universo (The building of the Tower of Babel), c. 1023, mineral and vegetal pigments parchment, 490 x 350 mm, Monastery Library, Montecassino, Cod. 132.

caption: Terentius Comoediae, IX century, folio 2r, mineral and vegetal pigment on parchment, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat.lat.3868

alt: A wide paved square under a blue sky. At the left rises a large Baroque church of pale sandstone with a two-tower facade, a central pediment and two low domed side chapels. At the right, beyond a cypress and a terrace wall, stands a smaller medieval church of reddish stone with a round tower with a tall conical roof and a square tower with a pyramidal roof.
caption: Fulda, the cathedral square with the Baroque cathedral (left), built on the site of the Ratgar basilica, and St Michael’s Church (right). Photo: Verum, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Manuscript page with a grid of capital letters in brown ink within a pale blue frame. Over the grid is painted a frontal figure of Christ with arms outstretched, a cross-nimbus in red and gold, a short red loincloth and bare legs, the letters within his body written in red and forming separate verses. The figure covers the grid from top to bottom.
caption: Hrabanus Maurus, In honorem sanctae crucis, carmen I: Christ with outstretched arms, ninth century. Ink and colours on parchment. Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, lat. 2422. Source: gallica.bnf.fr / Bibliothèque nationale de France.

alt: A large altar of black marble with white veining set in a white vaulted chapel. Black columns with white Corinthian capitals frame a white alabaster relief of a bishop kneeling before soldiers, one of whom swings a sword. Above the cornice a coat of arms flanked by putti and a cross; at the sides two large white angels. The front of the altar table, covered with a purple cloth, is a second relief of a bishop rising from a tomb while angels lift the lid. Iron candlesticks stand on either side.
caption: Johann Neudecker the Elder (reliefs), tomb altar of Saint Boniface, early eighteenth century. Black marble and alabaster. Fulda Cathedral, crypt of Boniface. Photo: Harvey Kneeslapper, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Manuscript page with a grid of capital letters within a purple frame. A large grey-green cross is painted over the grid, its arms filled with letters. At the lower right a small monk in a grey habit kneels with his hands raised towards the cross; red letters inside his figure form a separate verse.
caption: Hrabanus Maurus, In honorem sanctae crucis, the final poem with the cross and the author kneeling in prayer, ninth century. Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, lat. 2422. Source: gallica.bnf.fr / Bibliothèque nationale de France.

alt: Interior of a round church. Eight stout stone columns with simple capitals stand in a ring, carrying round arches above which a cylindrical wall rises to a gallery and a timber ceiling. Through the arches an altar is visible at the centre, and beyond, a small apse with a window. Around the columns runs a curved ambulatory with arched openings in the outer wall. The walls are plastered in warm ochre with red borders and fragments of painting.
caption: Fulda, St Michael’s Church, the rotunda, built 820–822 under Abbot Eigil and raised in the tenth and eleventh centuries. © Superbass / CC BY-SA 4.0 (via Wikimedia Commons), original.

alt: Low vaulted crypt with plastered walls. In the centre a short thick stone column with a broad capital carved with two large spiral volutes supports the springing of the vault. At the right, against the curved wall, a small rectangular altar of rough stone blocks stands on a step beneath an arched niche closed by an iron grille. Faint traces of red painted lines on the vault.
caption: Fulda, St Michael’s Church, the crypt with its central column, 820–822. Photo: Qwertzu111111, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Close view of a fresco roundel framed by a broad red band. Inside, against a blue ground, the bust of Christ with long reddish-brown hair parted in the middle, large dark eyes and a long nose, and a golden nimbus with a cross. He wears a red tunic and blesses with his right hand; in his left hand he holds a rolled scroll.
caption: Master of Castelseprio, The clipeus of Christ, ninth–tenth century, before 948. Fresco. Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, eastern apse. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Square fresco panel framed in red. At the left a haloed woman sits on a chair before a column and a building, holding a spindle, with a basket of wool beside her; a woman looks out from a doorway behind her. An angel with a pale nimbus and large wings strides in from above, holding a staff and stretching out his right hand. At the right a tall haloed woman in a reddish mantle bends towards the left beside a large area of lost plaster.
caption: Master of Castelseprio, The Annunciation and the Visitation, ninth–tenth century, before 948. Fresco. Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, eastern apse, north side, upper register. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco fragment with a large area of lost plaster at the left. A haloed woman in a red mantle drinks from a golden vessel held to her lips by a bearded old priest with a blue halo, a tall headdress and a jewelled golden cloak. Behind them stands an altar under a round canopy on columns.
caption: Master of Castelseprio, The Trial of the Bitter Waters, ninth–tenth century, before 948. Fresco. Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, eastern apse, upper register. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco panel surrounded by bare rubble masonry. A young woman with a golden halo, wrapped in a long brown mantle, sits sideways on a brown donkey walking to the right. Behind her an old bearded man in an ochre robe bends forward leaning on a staff. Behind them a building with tall pale columns and an arched opening.
caption: Master of Castelseprio, The Journey to Bethlehem, ninth–tenth century, before 948. Fresco. Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, eastern apse, south side, upper register. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco with many losses and small spots of later keying. At the left a haloed woman reclines on a large white crescent-shaped mattress. Below her two women attend to the birth. In the centre a seated figure in a blue-green mantle. To the right an angel flies towards a shepherd among sheep and goats, with a town in the background.
caption: Master of Castelseprio, The Nativity with the Annunciation to the Shepherds, ninth–tenth century, before 948. Fresco. Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, eastern apse, south side, lower register. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Detail of a fresco showing a hillside with goats and sheep, a young shepherd among them, and an angel flying in from above, in reddish and ochre tones on a pale ground, with many small spots of damage.
caption: Master of Castelseprio, The Annunciation to the Shepherds, detail of the Nativity, ninth–tenth century, before 948. Fresco. Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, eastern apse, south side, lower register. Photo: Rostkol, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Upper part of a triumphal arch in an ochre band beneath a wooden beam and ceiling. In the centre a roundel framed in red contains a throne with a cushion and a cross. On either side an angel with a pale blue halo flies horizontally towards the centre, holding a globe and a long staff.
caption: Master of Castelseprio, The Etimasia between two angels, ninth–tenth century, before 948. Fresco. Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, triumphal arch. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Ottonian manuscript miniature of Pope Gregory the Great, haloed and wearing a blue chasuble and white pallium with red crosses, seated frontally on a cushioned throne before an arched niche, from which a jewelled votive crown hangs above his head. A white dove perches at his shoulder by his ear. He holds a gold-bound book and touches an open book on a tall wooden lectern at right. At left, behind a large white curtain hung between columns, a tonsured notary in blue leans forward, piercing the curtain with his stylus and holding a wax tablet. A red-tiled roof and columns with foliate capitals close the scene within a red and gold border
caption: Saint Gregory the Great Inspired by the Holy Spirit, with His Notary. Detached leaf from the Registrum Gregorii, Trier, between 983 and 993. Paint and gold on parchment, c. 26.5 × 19.5 cm. Trier, Stadtbibliothek (Wissenschaftliche Bibliothek der Stadt Trier), Hs. 171/1626a.

alt: Ottonian manuscript miniature of a young, beardless emperor enthroned frontally beneath a canopy with a red tiled roof and arches on marbled columns. He holds a long sceptre and a golden orb marked with a cross, and wears a pink tunic under a red mantle sprinkled with gold. Two crowned and veiled women stand on each side offering golden spheres, against a pale sky and green ground within a narrow red and gold border
caption: Emperor Otto Enthroned, Receiving the Homage of Four Provinces. Detached leaf from the Registrum Gregorii, Trier, between 983 and 993. Paint and gold on parchment, 27 × 19.8 cm. Chantilly, Musée Condé, Ms. 14 bis.

alt: Ottonian manuscript page on a painted purple ground. At the centre, inside a pointed gold mandorla, Christ sits on a cushioned throne, wearing a light blue tunic and a red mantle, with a cross-inscribed halo; he blesses with his right hand and holds a jewelled book in his left. In four green circles at the corners, haloed evangelists sit at lecterns writing on scrolls or in books. Four smaller roundels between them contain the evangelist symbols: an eagle above, a winged lion at left, a winged ox at right and an angel below. Gold Latin verses run across the purple ground, and an orange and gold border frames the page
caption: Christ in Majesty with the Four Evangelists and Their Symbols. Sainte-Chapelle Gospels, Trier, c. 984 (979–989). Paint and gold on parchment, 390 × 290 mm (page). Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Département des Manuscrits, Latin 8851, fol. 1v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript page. At left, a tall panel painted in deep purple holds a monumental gold initial B, its shafts edged with white interlace and its bowls filled with gold scrolling vines on grounds of blue, green and pink dotted with white. Gold capitals beside and below the letter complete the words BEATISSIMO PAPAE DAMASO HIERONIMUS, followed by a smaller gold initial N beginning NOVUM OPUS FACERE ME COGIS EX. At right, a single column of text in gold minuscule on bare parchment continues Jerome's letter. The folio number 3 appears at the top right.
caption: Master of the Registrum Gregorii and Trier workshop, Initial B and Incipit of Jerome's Letter to Pope Damasus (Novum opus). Sainte-Chapelle Gospels, Trier, c. 984 (979–989). Gold and paint on parchment, 390 × 290 mm (page). Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Département des Manuscrits, Latin 8851, fol. 3r.

alt: Ottonian manuscript miniature framed by an arch on two marbled columns with pink foliate capitals, set against a pink wall with blind arcades. In the lunette, a haloed, winged angel seen half-length against a blue ground holds an inscribed scroll. Below it a purple band carries two lines of gold capitals. Red curtains hang from the beam and are tied around the columns. Beneath them, on a green ground, the haloed, bearded evangelist Matthew sits on a folding stool with a red cushion, wearing a white tunic and a mauve mantle, a closed gold book on his lap and his bare feet on a footstool, writing in a book on a tall turned lectern with an inkhorn
caption: Saint Matthew Writing, with His Symbol, the Angel. Sainte-Chapelle Gospels, Trier, c. 984 (979–989). Paint and gold on parchment, 390 × 290 mm (page). Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Département des Manuscrits, Latin 8851, fol. 15v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript incipit page. A large gold monogram combining the letters L and I, filled with interlace in gold, blue and white and ending in knotted terminals, stands on a deep purple panel. Beside it, tall gold capitals spell BER and GENERATIO, and a gold line beneath reads NIS IHU XPI FILII DAVID. A green field surrounds the panel, enclosed by a broad gold frame with bands of scrolling vines. Square corner fields hold the evangelist symbols: an angel at top left, an eagle at top right, a lion at bottom left and an ox at bottom right. Circular medallions at the middle of each side contain busts of young, beardless men on gold grounds. The parchment is torn and holed in the green area at left
caption: Master of the Registrum Gregorii and Trier workshop, Incipit Page of the Gospel of Matthew (Liber generationis), with Evangelist Symbols and Four Ruler Medallions. Sainte-Chapelle Gospels, Trier, c. 984 (979–989). Gold and paint on parchment, 390 × 290 mm (page). Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Département des Manuscrits, Latin 8851, fol. 16v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript miniature framed by a large arch on marbled green columns with gold spiral ornament. In the lunette, a haloed, winged golden lion holding a book lies on a purple band inscribed with two lines of gold capitals. Below, within a pink arcade of three arches on slender columns against an ochre ground, the haloed evangelist Mark, elderly and grey-haired, sits frontally on a throne with animal-head arms and lion-paw feet. He wears a blue chasuble and a white pallium marked with black crosses, holds a closed book, and dips a quill into an inkwell on a slender turned stand at left. At right stands a tall cabinet lectern with books and a hanging scroll. A faint sketch of a seated figure is visible in the lower margin
caption: Saint Mark Enthroned as Bishop, with His Symbol, the Lion. Sainte-Chapelle Gospels, Trier, c. 984 (979–989). Paint and gold on parchment, 390 × 290 mm (page). Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Département des Manuscrits, Latin 8851, fol. 52v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript miniature framed by an arch on marbled columns with white vine tendrils and pink foliate capitals. In the lunette, a haloed, winged, horned ox in reddish brown reclines on a purple band inscribed with two lines of gold capitals, its forelegs on a closed book. Below, between drawn mauve curtains and slender white columns on a green ground, the haloed evangelist Luke, with white hair and beard, sits on a gold block throne. He wears a light blue tunic and an orange-red mantle with a circular fold over his belly, holds a pen in one hand, and reaches with the other to an open book on a grey pedestal lectern. Behind him at left, a tall stand holds a book showing the opening lines of his Gospel. His bare feet rest on an arcaded footstool
caption: Saint Luke Writing, with His Symbol, the Ox. Sainte-Chapelle Gospels, Trier, c. 984 (979–989). Paint and gold on parchment, 390 × 290 mm (page). Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Département des Manuscrits, Latin 8851, fol. 75v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript miniature framed by an arch on pink marbled columns with blue foliate capitals; gold vine scrolls fill the mauve spandrels and bands of blue and green leaf ornament run around the arch. In the pink lunette, a haloed golden eagle with raised wings grips a closed book in its talon above a purple band inscribed in gold capitals. Below, against a blue ground, the young, beardless, haloed evangelist John sits on a large jewelled gold throne draped with a green cloth. He wears a blue tunic and a rose mantle, holds closed white books on his lap, raises his left hand with open palm, and looks upward toward the eagle. At right stands a tall arcaded pedestal lectern with a sloping desk bearing an inkwell and quill. A white inscription above reads IOHANNES APOSTOLUS ET EVANGELISTA.
caption: Master of the Registrum Gregorii, Saint John the Evangelist Inspired, with His Symbol, the Eagle. Sainte-Chapelle Gospels, Trier, c. 984 (979–989). Paint and gold on parchment, 390 × 290 mm (page). Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Département des Manuscrits, Latin 8851, fol. 115v.

alt: Page of a Carolingian Gospel book on pale parchment. Across the top margin runs a single line in small reddish-brown medieval minuscule: the ownership note of Saint Martin's church on the Moselle with a curse against theft.
caption: Ownership note of the church of Saint Martin, Trier, and text of Jerome’s letter to Pope Damasus (Novum opus). Strahov Gospels, text written in uncial script, probably at Tours, c. 860; ownership note in a later minuscule hand. Ink on parchment, codex 270 × 168 mm. Prague, Strahov Library (Royal Canonry of Premonstratensians at Strahov), DF III 3, fol. 2r.

alt: Ottonian manuscript page on purple-stained parchment. In a narrow upper register on a lilac ground, a half-length haloed angel with blue-grey wings holds a gold book, flanked by faded gold inscriptions. Below, a purple band carries a line of gold capitals beginning HOC EVANGELIUM. In the main field, on a green ground with areas of paint loss, the haloed evangelist Matthew, young and beardless, sits bent forward on a gold block throne with a red cushion. He wears a white tunic and a deep purple mantle and writes on a long sheet laid across a desk on a red turned stand. His bare feet rest on a blue-green footstool. Gold capitals beside his head name him. A small parchment tab with Gothic script projects from the left edge
caption: Saint Matthew Writing, with His Symbol, the Angel. Leaf added to the Strahov Gospels (text written at Tours, c. 860), Trier, church of Saint Martin, late tenth century. Paint and gold on purple-stained parchment, codex 270 × 168 mm. Prague, Strahov Library (Royal Canonry of Premonstratensians at Strahov), DF III 3, fol. 8v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript page on purple-stained parchment. In an upper register on a pale pink ground, a haloed, winged golden lion with raised tail rests a forepaw on a closed book. Below it, a purple band carries one line of gold capitals: MARCUM TERRIBILIS DESIGNAT FORMA LEONIS. In the main field, on a warm golden-orange ground, the haloed, tonsured evangelist Mark sits on a violet block throne with a green cushion. He wears a light blue tunic and a rose mantle with a circular fold over his thigh, and dips a quill into an inkwell on a tall foliate stand at left, while a long inscribed scroll in his other hand unrolls toward a lectern on a green column at right. His bare feet rest on a grey footstool. A small parchment tab projects from the left edge
caption: Saint Mark Writing, with His Symbol, the Lion. Leaf added to the Strahov Gospels (text written at Tours, c. 860), Trier, church of Saint Martin, late tenth century. Paint and gold on purple-stained parchment, codex 270 × 168 mm. Prague, Strahov Library (Royal Canonry of Premonstratensians at Strahov), DF III 3, fol. 69v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript page on purple-stained parchment. In an upper register on a blue ground, a haloed, winged, horned ox in reddish brown reclines over a book. Below it, a purple band carries one line of gold capitals beginning LUCAS AETHEREI SPECIEM. In the main field, on a rose ground, the haloed evangelist Luke, young and beardless, sits on a gold folding stool with animal-head terminals and a red cushion, wrapped in a green mantle over a blue tunic. He rests his chin on one hand and holds a small scroll in the other, gazing at an open book on a tall mauve pedestal lectern from which a scroll hangs. His bare feet rest on a gold footstool. A small parchment tab projects from the left edge
caption: Saint Luke in Contemplation, with His Symbol, the Ox. Leaf added to the Strahov Gospels (text written at Tours, c. 860), Trier, church of Saint Martin, late tenth century. Paint and gold on purple-stained parchment, codex 270 × 168 mm. Prague, Strahov Library (Royal Canonry of Premonstratensians at Strahov), DF III 3, fol. 107v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript page on purple-stained parchment. In an upper register on a pale mauve ground, a haloed eagle with spread wings and head in profile perches above a book. Below it, a purple band carries one line of gold capitals: EST AQUILA ALTA PETENS NARRANS DIVINA IOHANNES. In the main field, on a blue-violet ground, the haloed evangelist John, elderly with long hair and a grey beard, sits frontally on a gold block throne with a green cushion. He wears a white tunic and a bright red mantle and holds an open book filled with script in one hand, writing in it with a quill held in the other. His feet rest on a green footstool. At right stands a tall mauve pedestal lectern with an arched niche, bearing scrolls and an inkwell. A small parchment tab projects from the left edge.
caption: Saint John the Evangelist Writing, with His Symbol, the Eagle. Leaf added to the Strahov Gospels (text written at Tours, c. 860), Trier, church of Saint Martin, late tenth century. Paint and gold on purple-stained parchment, codex 270 × 168 mm. Prague, Strahov Library (Royal Canonry of Premonstratensians at Strahov), DF III 3, fol. 176v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript miniature within an orange and gold frame. Christ hangs on a gold cross against a lilac sky above and a deep blue ground below, his arms straight, his bearded head with a cross-inscribed halo inclined to one side, his pale body modelled with a rounded abdomen and an orange loincloth knotted at the waist. Above the crossbar, two roundels show the Sun as a young man with a radiant halo and the Moon as a veiled woman beneath a crescent. Gold letters near the top of the cross name Jesus Christ our Lord. At left the Virgin Mary, veiled in white and purple over a blue gown, bows her head in grief; at right the young Saint John, in a pink tunic and green mantle, holds a jewelled book and raises his hand. Gold inscriptions name both. They stand on a green ground with small plants.
caption: Master of the Registrum Gregorii (attributed), The Crucifixion with the Virgin Mary and Saint John, the Sun and the Moon. Lorsch Sacramentary, Trier, c. 975–980, for the abbey of Lorsch. Paint and gold on parchment. Chantilly, Bibliothèque du château (Musée Condé), Ms. 40 (formerly 1447), fol. 4v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript page on pale parchment dominated by a monumental gold initial T. Its upright stem is filled with a narrow band of silver-white interlace, interrupted at mid-height. From the stem, symmetrical gold acanthus scrolls spiral outward on both sides, forming four roundels with rosettes at their centres: the upper two on violet grounds, the lower two on turquoise grounds, all outlined in orange. To the right of the stem's foot stands a gold capital E, and beneath it the word IGITUR in large gold capitals completes the opening words Te igitur. Faint letters from the other side of the leaf show through the parchment
caption: Master of the Registrum Gregorii and Trier workshop (attributed), Initial T Opening the Canon of the Mass (Te igitur). Lorsch Sacramentary, Trier, c. 975–980, for the abbey of Lorsch. Gold and paint on parchment. Chantilly, Bibliothèque du château (Musée Condé), Ms. 40 (formerly 1447), fol. 5r.

alt: Ottonian manuscript page on pale parchment with a rectangular decorated panel. A gold initial B dominates a deep purple field: its tall shaft curls up into a knotted loop that breaks through the top of the frame, and its large round bowl, joined to the shaft by gold interlace knots, holds a green ground filled with a gold beast whose head with pointed ears and open jaws emerges from a dense knot of interlace ending in leaves. Smaller gold and coloured letters E and A stand above the bowl and T, I and S beside its base; below, gold capitals read SIMO PAPAE DA / MASO HERONIMUS. Small white and gold sprays are scattered over the purple. The panel is framed by gold bands, a lilac border with gold vine scrolls, a dark green border with gold foliage, orange corner squares with gold rosettes, and leaf-shaped finials at the outer corners
caption: Master of the Registrum Gregorii and workshop (attributed), Initial B and Incipit of Jerome's Letter to Pope Damasus (Novum opus). Gospel book made for Otto III, Trier, 996–1002. Gold and paint on parchment. Manchester, The University of Manchester, John Rylands Library, Latin MS 98, fol. 1v.

alt: Ottonian manuscript incipit page. On a mauve panel, a gold monogram combines the letters L and I: the L runs down the left side and along the bottom, the I rises in the centre, both filled with white interlace, ending in gold knots. Symmetrical gold scrolls spring from the I, forming four roundels with rosettes on blue grounds over green. Small gold letters spell BER, GENE, and at the bottom RATIONIS. The panel is enclosed by gold, pink, lilac and orange borders with stylised plant stems, blue corner squares with foliage, and gold foliate crests. Four blue squares at the midpoints of the frame hold gold medallions with busts of a young beardless man, each surrounded by a tiny inscription. Gold rosette finials project from the outer corners
caption: Master of the Registrum Gregorii and workshop (attributed), Incipit of the Gospel of Matthew (Liber generationis), with Four Medallions of the Emperor Otto. Gospel book made for Otto III, Trier, 996–1002. Gold and paint on parchment. Manchester, The University of Manchester, John Rylands Library, Latin MS 98, fol. 16r.

alt: Ottonian manuscript incipit page. On a deep purple panel, a monumental gold initial I rises through the centre, its stem left partly in bare parchment and bound by gold bands, with dense knots of gold interlace at top and bottom that break through the frame. Symmetrical gold scrolls spring from the stem, enclosing a green oval at the centre and four roundels with gold rosettes on lilac grounds. Gold capitals NI and TI stand in the upper corners and V and M in the lower corners, spelling INITIUM. The frame consists of orange, gold and green bands with gold interlace, with lilac acanthus leaves at the corners, gold interlace knots at the midpoints of the sides, and heart-shaped gold finials projecting diagonally from the outer corners. A short note in small minuscule appears in the right margin
caption: Master of the Registrum Gregorii and workshop (attributed), Incipit of the Gospel of Mark (Initium). Gospel book made for Otto III, Trier, 996–1002. Gold and paint on parchment. Manchester, The University of Manchester, John Rylands Library, Latin MS 98, fol. 65r.

alt: Ottonian manuscript incipit page. On a deep purple panel with stepped lilac edges, a monumental gold initial Q fills the upper part: its oval bowl encloses a green field with symmetrical gold vine scrolls, gold rosettes and small white quatrefoils on lilac grounds, and its tail descends as a straight vertical stem filled with a white scroll pattern. Beside the stem, gold capitals read UONI AM / QUI DEM, completing QUONIAM QUIDEM, with small white sprigs scattered on the purple. The frame consists of orange, gold and white bands with gold interlace. Bevelled square fields at the midpoints of the sides hold geometric motifs: a saltire pattern at top and bottom, eight-pointed stars at left and right. Heart-shaped gold finials project diagonally from the outer corners
caption: Master of the Registrum Gregorii and workshop (attributed), Incipit of the Gospel of Luke (Quoniam quidem). Gospel book made for Otto III, Trier, 996–1002. Gold and paint on parchment. Manchester, The University of Manchester, John Rylands Library, Latin MS 98, fol. 98r.

alt: Ottonian manuscript incipit page. On a deep purple panel, a gold monogram combines the letters I and N: the I rises through the centre, filled with white interlace, while the N is formed by two uprights of dense gold interlace and foliage joined by a diagonal band of white interlace. Gold capitals read PRINCIPIO above and ERAT VERBU(M) below. A small square at the centre of the monogram shows a white Lamb of God with a slender staff. Four further squares on the axes of the frame hold the evangelist symbols on gold grounds: the eagle above, the winged ox at left, the winged lion at right and the angel below. The frame has gold, green and blue bands with white foliate ornament, gold foliate crests at the midpoints and gold fleur-de-lis finials at the corners. A short note in small minuscule appears in the right margin
caption: Master of the Registrum Gregorii and workshop (attributed), Incipit of the Gospel of John (In principio erat Verbum), with the Lamb of God and the Four Evangelist Symbols. Gospel book made for Otto III, Trier, 996–1002. Gold and paint on parchment. Manchester, The University of Manchester, John Rylands Library, Latin MS 98, fol. 154r.

alt: The white stone west façade of a Romanesque cathedral under a blue sky. A tall central gable with a large rose window is flanked by lower side gables; a gallery of small arches runs across the front. In the centre a projecting porch on two columns resting on lions frames the main door; long horizontal relief friezes are set into the wall on both sides of the porch and above the two side doors. At the left rises a tall bell tower.
caption: Modena Cathedral, the west façade, begun in 1099: Lanfranco's arcaded front with Wiligelmo's four Genesis slabs and main portal; the rose window and the side doors were added by the Campionese masters in the thirteenth century. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A curved stone apse wall built of large pale blocks. In the upper part a rectangular marble plaque carries fourteen lines of inscription in Roman capitals, the last two in different lettering. Below it a round-headed window is framed by a carved arch of acanthus scrolls.
caption: The inscription on the main apse naming Lanfranco as master of the work, composed by the canon Aimo, with a thirteenth-century addition naming the massarius Bozzalino. Modena Cathedral. Photo: Username.Ruge, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A manuscript page with a coloured drawing in a frame of orange lattice and blue bands. At the left bishops in mitres with crosiers stand in a group; at the right a woman in a green mantle, labelled Matildis comitissa, gestures towards them, with attendants.
caption: Matilda of Canossa receives the bishops for the translation of Saint Geminianus, drawing in the Relatio de innovatione ecclesie sancti Geminiani, c. 1200–1210 (facsimile). Modena, Archivio Capitolare, O.II.11. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A rectangular marble slab set into a stone wall. In the centre a smooth tablet is carved with twelve lines of large Roman capitals. At either side stands a bearded prophet in a long mantle holding the tablet; the names ENOC and ELIA are carved on the base.
caption: Wiligelmo, Enoch and Elijah holding the foundation inscription of the cathedral, with the couplet naming the sculptor, 1099. Modena Cathedral, west façade, left of the main portal. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A long stone relief under a cornice and a row of small arches. At the left the Creator, with an open book, sits in an almond-shaped glory held by two angels. Next he touches the head of the naked Adam; in the centre he draws Eve from the side of the sleeping Adam; at the right Adam and Eve stand beside a tree, Eve holding a fruit.
caption: Wiligelmo, the first slab of Genesis: the Creator in glory, the Creation of Adam, the Creation of Eve and the Fall, c. 1099–1110. Modena Cathedral, west façade, above the left side door. Photo: Szeder László, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A long stone relief seen from below. At the left the naked Adam and Eve, covering themselves with leaves, stand before the haloed Creator, who holds a scroll. Next an angel with large wings drives them out; at the right Eve bends with a hoe and Adam works the ground beside a tree.
caption: Wiligelmo, the second slab of Genesis: the Reproach, the Expulsion and the Labour of Adam and Eve, c. 1099–1110. Modena Cathedral, west façade, left of the main portal. Photo: Szeder László, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A long stone relief under small arches. At the left Abel holds a lamb, and the Creator blesses from a round glory; in the centre Cain offers a sheaf of grain; then Cain swings a club at Abel, who falls; at the right the haloed Creator lays his hand on the shoulder of Cain.
caption: Wiligelmo, the third slab of Genesis: the offerings of Cain and Abel, the murder of Abel and God questioning Cain, c. 1099–1110. Modena Cathedral, west façade, right of the main portal. Photo: Mattis, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A long stone relief under small arches. At the left a bearded archer in a pointed cap shoots an arrow at a man half hidden among the branches of a tree. In the centre an ark in the form of a two-storey arcaded building with heads at the openings. At the right four men stand together, talking and pointing.
caption: Wiligelmo, the fourth slab of Genesis: Lamech kills Cain, the Ark, and Noah and his sons leaving the Ark, c. 1099–1110. Modena Cathedral, west façade, above the right side door. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The upper part of a round-arched portal. A broad archivolt is filled with scrolling vines inhabited by small human figures, animals and birds. Below, a lintel is carved with vine scrolls bearing grapes, with a large leafy mask at the centre.
caption: Wiligelmo and workshop, the main portal: archivolt with inhabited vine scrolls and lintel with a foliate mask, c. 1099–1110. Modena Cathedral, west façade. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A tall carved stone panel. In the lower half a kneeling man in a short belted tunic, seen from behind with his head bowed, raises both arms to support a ledge on his shoulders. Above, a dense vine scroll with deeply drilled leaves encloses a small four-legged creature and a bird.
caption: Wiligelmo, a kneeling telamon at the foot of a jamb of the main portal, supporting the inhabited vine scroll, c. 1099–1110. Modena Cathedral, west façade. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A tall carved stone panel. In the lower half a stocky man in a short tunic, standing barefoot with his knees bent, holds a beam on his head with both hands. Above, a deeply undercut vine scroll encloses a winged creature attacking a crouching figure.
caption: Wiligelmo, a standing telamon at the foot of the opposite jamb of the main portal, c. 1099–1110. Modena Cathedral, west façade. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A carved stone panel lit by warm evening light. Under a beaded arch on spiral columns, between two small towers, stands a bearded prophet with long wavy hair, holding a closed scroll against his body. The name MICHEAS is carved above the arch.
caption: Wiligelmo and workshop, the prophet Micah, from the jambs of the main portal, c. 1099–1110. Modena Cathedral, west façade. Photo: Chiara Salazar Chiesa, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A carved stone panel. Under an arch with a scalloped moulding, between two small domed towers, stands a beardless prophet with short fringed hair and large inlaid eyes, holding a closed book against his chest. The name IEREMIAS is carved above.
caption: Wiligelmo and workshop, the prophet Jeremiah, from the jambs of the main portal, c. 1099–1110. Modena Cathedral, west façade. Photo: FrDr, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A carved stone panel. Under an arch between two small towers stands a bearded prophet with long wavy hair, turning slightly to the left, holding a book and gathering his mantle with his other hand; the hem falls in drilled folds. The name ISAIAS is carved above.
caption: Wiligelmo and workshop, the prophet Isaiah, from the jambs of the main portal, c. 1099–1110. Modena Cathedral, west façade. Photo: Klaus Graf, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A carved stone panel. Under an arch on columns carved with palmettes stands a beardless prophet with cropped hair, raising one finger towards heaven and holding an unrolled scroll; his garments end in rows of drilled folds. The name EZECHIEL is carved above.
caption: Wiligelmo and workshop, the prophet Ezekiel, from the jambs of the main portal, c. 1099–1110. Modena Cathedral, west façade. Photo: FrDr, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A marble relief set into a stone wall below two carved corbel heads. A naked winged boy with curly hair leans with crossed legs on a long torch held upside down, its flame touching the ground; in one hand he holds a wreath. At the right a long-necked bird with a long beak stands facing him.
caption: Wiligelmo, a winged genius leaning on an inverted torch, with a wreath and a bird, c. 1099–1110. Modena Cathedral, west façade. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A rectangular marble relief set into a stone wall. Two stags stand facing each other with their bodies seen in profile, sharing a single head shown frontally at the centre, with large branching antlers. Small incised plant scrolls fill the background.
caption: Workshop of Wiligelmo, two stags with a single head, early twelfth century. Modena Cathedral, west façade. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A carved stone relief at the corner of a building, below a cornice carved with scale ornament. Two lions and a creature with a human face stand interlaced with the long necks and tails of serpent-like beasts; on the return face of the corner a further figure can be seen.
caption: Workshop of Wiligelmo, a corner relief with lions and hybrid creatures entwined by serpents, early twelfth century. Modena Cathedral, west façade. Photo: Manesti, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A carved stone block on a pedestal in a museum. At the left a long-haired figure in a pleated garment sits hugging her knees and looks out. At the right a second figure is shown upside down, his legs raised against the upper edge of the block and his head and long hair at the bottom.
caption: Master of the Metopes (attributed to Wiligelmo by Quintavalle), the Antipodes, early twelfth century. Modena, Musei del Duomo, Museo Lapidario. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A carved stone block on a pedestal. A naked youth with long straight hair sits with his legs crossed and holds the neck of a dragon whose winged body coils in a great loop beside him, its head turned towards its own clawed foot.
caption: Master of the Metopes (attributed to Wiligelmo by Quintavalle), a youth with a dragon, traditionally identified as one of the Psylli, early twelfth century. Modena, Musei del Duomo, Museo Lapidario. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A carved stone block on a pedestal. A naked bearded man with very long hair falling to his waist reclines with one leg folded under him, against a ground with two large leaf rosettes; one of his feet is raised behind his back.
caption: Master of the Metopes (attributed to Wiligelmo by Quintavalle), the man with long hair, early twelfth century. Modena, Musei del Duomo, Museo Lapidario. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A carved stone block on a pedestal. A large figure with long hair and a heavy pleated skirt is curled tightly into the block, knees drawn up to the upper edge and head pressed against them, filling the whole field.
caption: Master of the Metopes (attributed to Wiligelmo by Quintavalle), the great girl, early twelfth century. Modena, Musei del Duomo, Museo Lapidario. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The upper part of a round-arched portal. The archivolt is carved with interlacing bands forming roundels. A long lintel is divided into six panels of small figures under an inscription: a bishop on horseback, a ship, a saint healing a young woman, a ruler offering a cup, a group riding, and a funeral.
caption: Workshop of Wiligelmo (Maestro di San Geminiano), the Porta dei Principi: lintel with the life of Saint Geminianus and archivolt with inhabited interlace, c. 1106–1110. Modena Cathedral, south side. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A carved stone panel in shallow focus. Under an arch, a bearded saint with a fringe of curly hair and inlaid eyes holds a cross-staff and a large bunch of keys, looking upwards.
caption: Workshop of Wiligelmo, Saint Peter, from the jambs of the Porta dei Principi, c. 1106–1110. Modena Cathedral, south side. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A carved stone panel in a plain rectangular frame. A bearded man with large dark inlaid eyes, barefoot, holds before him a tablet inscribed QUICUMQUE BAPTIZATI SUMUS IN XPO IHU.
caption: Workshop of Wiligelmo, Saint Paul with the words of Romans 6:3, Quicumque baptizati sumus in Christo Iesu, underside of the lintel of the Porta dei Principi, c. 1106–1110. Modena Cathedral, south side. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A semicircular stone archivolt set into a brick arch. Knights on horseback with lances and shields ride towards the centre from both sides, where a castle rises from water with a woman and a man inside; a man with a pick attacks a wooden tower. Inscriptions along the upper edge name the figures.
caption: Workshop of Wiligelmo, the archivolt of the Porta della Pescheria with the siege of a castle by Arthur and his knights, early twelfth century. Modena Cathedral, north side. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A detail of a stone archivolt with the inscription ARTUS DE BRETANI above a knight in a mail hauberk and pointed helmet, riding a horse and holding a lance with a pennant.
caption: The Porta della Pescheria, detail: Artus de Bretania, King Arthur. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A detail of a stone archivolt: at the left a bearded man in a short tunic swings a pick; in the centre a tall wooden tower of crossed beams; at the right a veiled woman looks out from behind a stone wall above stylised waves.
caption: The Porta della Pescheria, detail: Burmaltus with his pick, a siege tower and Winlogee (Guinevere) within the walls of the castle. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A tall, narrow view of a carved portal jamb beside a wooden door. On the inner face a column of small arched niches each holds a figure at work, with names of months above; the outer face is carved with dense vine scrolls inhabited by birds and animals.
caption: The Porta della Pescheria, left jamb: Labours of the Months in arched niches and inhabited vine scroll, early twelfth century. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A semicircular stone lunette under a carved archivolt of vine scrolls and lattice. At the centre Christ sits enthroned, blessing and holding an open book, between two standing angels holding staffs and discs; four roundels contain the winged man, the eagle, the winged lion and the winged ox. Two lines of inscription run along the lintel below.
caption: Wiligelmo or his workshop, the lunette of the portal with Christ in Majesty, angels and the symbols of the Evangelists, and the lintel inscription recording the collapse of 1117. Nonantola, abbey church of San Silvestro. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A stone panel with a short-legged man in a belted tunic and pointed shoes, his head bowed under a ledge which he holds up with both hands.
caption: Followers of Wiligelmo, a telamon at the foot of the right jamb of the portal. Nonantola, abbey church of San Silvestro. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A stone panel under two small arches. At the left a winged angel holding a book points towards a veiled woman with a halo who raises her hand. Inscriptions above and below read S MARIA ELISABET and GABRIEL MARIA.
caption: Followers of Wiligelmo, the Annunciation, right jamb of the portal. Nonantola, abbey church of San Silvestro. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A stone panel under two small arches. Two haloed women in long veils and mantles stand facing each other, one older, one wearing a crown-like headdress. The inscription below reads S MARIA ELISABET.
caption: Followers of Wiligelmo, the Visitation, right jamb of the portal. Nonantola, abbey church of San Silvestro. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A stone panel in two registers. Above, a veiled woman lies on a bed under two small arches; below, a woman in a tall headdress bathes a haloed child in a basin. The inscription reads XPC LAVATUR.
caption: Followers of Wiligelmo, the Virgin resting and the Bath of the Child, right jamb of the portal. Nonantola, abbey church of San Silvestro. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A stone panel under two small arches with rosettes. The heads of an ox and an ass bend over a swaddled child with a cross halo, lying in a manger carved with a band of leaves. The inscription below reads PRESEPIUM.
caption: Followers of Wiligelmo, the Child in the manger with the ox and the ass, right jamb of the portal. Nonantola, abbey church of San Silvestro. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A stone panel in two registers. Above, under an arch, an angel leans down from the sky over two kneeling shepherds who point downwards, on either side of a plant. Below, a flock of sheep with inlaid eyes fills the field. Inscriptions read MAGI AD XPM and PASTORES.
caption: Followers of Wiligelmo, the Annunciation to the Shepherds, right jamb of the portal. Nonantola, abbey church of San Silvestro. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A stone panel under two small arches with a rosette between them. At the left three Magi in pointed caps, one kneeling and offering a bowl; at the right the Virgin, seated, holds the Child, who blesses. Inscriptions read S MARIA IOSEPH S SIMEON and MAGI AD XPM.
caption: Followers of Wiligelmo, the Adoration of the Magi, right jamb of the portal. Nonantola, abbey church of San Silvestro. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A stone panel under two small arches. The Virgin, at the left, and Joseph, bending forward with a pair of doves, present the Child, held by a bearded old man at the right. Inscriptions read TEMPLUM DOMINI and S MARIA IOSEPH S SIMEON.
caption: Followers of Wiligelmo, the Presentation in the Temple, right jamb of the portal. Nonantola, abbey church of San Silvestro. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A stone panel under two small arches. A winged angel speaks to a bearded old man who holds a scroll and raises his hand to his beard. The inscription above reads ANGELUS ALLOQUITUR IOSEPH.
caption: Followers of Wiligelmo, the angel speaking to Joseph, right jamb of the portal. Nonantola, abbey church of San Silvestro. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A tall, narrow marble figure carved on a jamb. A bearded prophet with long braided hair and a halo stands frontally, holding a book and a long scroll covered with lines of capitals beginning DIC SCE DANIHEL.
caption: Wiligelmo or the Master of the Prophets, the prophet Daniel, from the portal of the old façade, c. 1107–1117. Cremona Cathedral, main portal. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A tall, narrow marble figure carved on a jamb beside a column resting on a small crouching figure. A prophet with a very long rippling beard and a halo holds a book and points to a scroll with a short inscription.
caption: Wiligelmo or the Master of the Prophets, the prophet Ezekiel, from the portal of the old façade, c. 1107–1117. Cremona Cathedral, main portal. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A tall, narrow marble figure carved on a jamb. A bearded prophet with long hair and a halo, his mantle falling in chevron folds, holds a long scroll inscribed in capitals; the name IEREMIAS is carved on the base.
caption: Wiligelmo or the Master of the Prophets, the prophet Jeremiah, from the portal of the old façade, c. 1107–1117. Cremona Cathedral, main portal. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A tall, narrow marble figure carved on a jamb. A bearded prophet with a halo raises his right hand in speech and holds a long scroll inscribed ECCE VIRGO CONCIPIET ET PARIET FILIUM ET VOCABITUR NOMEN EIUS EMANUEL.
caption: Wiligelmo or the Master of the Prophets, the prophet Isaiah with the words of Isaiah 7:14, from the portal of the old façade, c. 1107–1117. Cremona Cathedral, main portal. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A painted cross on a dark wooden ground studded with round iron nail heads. Christ stands upright with open eyes and a gold halo set with raised bosses, wearing a loincloth of white and blue knotted at the waist; his feet rest on a footrest. Beside the body stand the Virgin in blue and red, raising her hand to her face, and Saint John in red. In the cimasa Christ ascends in a blue mandorla among angels, above a titulus. At the foot a small figure and two lines of inscription with a date.
caption: Alberto Sozio, painted cross, signed and dated 1187, tempera on parchment laid on panel. Spoleto, cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, from the church of Santi Giovanni e Paolo. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The side wall of a small medieval church of rough grey stone, with a round-arched doorway closed by an iron grille. Above the door, under a small wooden canopy, a faded fresco shows standing figures with haloes. A yellow sign reads CHIESA DEI SS. GIOVANNI E PAOLO (EX), 1174, CON AFFRESCHI DEI SEC. XII-XIII E XIV. At the right, a narrow street passes under stone arches towards steps.
caption: Spoleto, the church of Santi Giovanni e Paolo, consecrated in 1174, side wall with a fresco above the entrance. Photo: Manuelarosi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A detached fresco in the shape of a lunette, much damaged, on a pale ground. At the left an enthroned ruler, largely lost, and a man at an open door. In the centre two young haloed saints stand on either side of a tall doorway decorated with a meander pattern, beneath a half-mandorla with Christ. At the right an executioner raises a sword over a saint who falls forward, and a severed head lies at the lower right corner.
caption: Alberto Sozio (attributed), the martyrdom of Saints John and Paul, c. 1174, detached fresco, 168 × 238 cm, from the crypt of Santi Giovanni e Paolo. Spoleto, Museo Nazionale del Ducato. Photo: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A damaged fresco with many small losses. Under red arches on columns with gilded capitals, against a deep blue ground, a knight in chain mail at the left thrusts a long sword at the head of a haloed archbishop, who stands at an altar and turns his head; a severed hand hangs in the air. Behind a column at the right a cleric in a red and ochre garment looks on. On the altar lie a chalice and an open book with letters. At the far right, a red border and a band with crosses.
caption: Alberto Sozio (attributed) or a follower, the martyrdom of Thomas Becket, fresco, late twelfth or first half of the thirteenth century. Spoleto, Santi Giovanni e Paolo, left wall. Photo: Silvio Sorcini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A black-and-white photograph from a printed book of a fresco framed by an ornamental frieze. Under a tiled roof and an arcade, three knights in chain mail with raised swords attack an archbishop standing behind an altar, while a cleric looks on behind a column and lamps hang from the arches. At the left a seated figure; at the right, beyond a decorated band, a standing bishop saint with a halo and a pallium. A caption below reads, in part, Martirio di S. Tomaso di Canturbury.
caption: The martyrdom of Thomas Becket in Santi Giovanni e Paolo, Spoleto, in a photograph from a printed book, with the caption "Alberto Sozio, Martirio di S. Tomaso di Canturbury". Photo: scan by a Wikimedia Commons user, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A damaged fresco of the Crucifixion on a deep blue ground scattered with small losses. Christ hangs on a red wooden cross with closed eyes and bowed head. At the left the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle and red sleeves, raises one hand and extends the other; at the right Saint John in a red mantle holds his hand to his breast. At the lower left, small kneeling figures. The lower centre of the fresco is lost.
caption: Crucifixion with the Virgin and Saint John, fresco, later Gothic, date not established, for comparison. Spoleto, Santi Giovanni e Paolo. Photo: Silvio Sorcini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A tall narrow panel in a gilded frame. On a worn gold ground with large raised round bosses, the Virgin stands in a dark blue mantle over a red-violet robe, her head veiled in red, a dotted halo around her head. She touches her cheek with her left hand in sorrow and points with her right hand to the right. At the top a strip of blue; at her feet a red band with the letters S C A M and an ornamental band below.
caption: Alberto Sozio, the Mourning Virgin, fragment of a painted cross, c. 1180–1190, tempera and gold on parchment laid on panel, painted surface 84.5 × 24.5 cm. Baltimore, Walters Art Museum, 37.1155. Photo: Walters Art Museum, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A roughly circular fragment of a panel on a dark cloth. On a brown ground within a ring of small white dots, the frontal face of the Virgin with large round eyes, arched brows, a long nose and a small mouth looks out. She wears a tall gold crown of three arched plates set with painted red and blue stones and three empty oval settings, and a red veil patterned with white spirals and dots falls beside her face.
caption: Alberto Sozio, head of the Virgin from a Maestà, late twelfth century, tempera on panel, 32.5 × 35.5 cm. Milan, Pinacoteca di Brera, inv. 7412. Photo: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A painted cross, heavily damaged and eaten by worms, set in a modern frame covered with green velvet and hanging on wires against a grey wall. Christ stands upright with open eyes, a long face and a drooping moustache, his halo lost to the bare wood; he wears a long white loincloth knotted at the waist with a broad white band. Beside the body stand four saints, two on each side: at the left a young saint in red and the Virgin in a dark red mantle, at the right a saint holding a book and another in a patterned robe. At the right end of the crossbar a small half-figure survives.
caption: Workshop of Alberto Sozio, painted cross, c. 1190–1210, tempera on panel. Jacorossi collection. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Close detail of the head of Christ on a damaged painted cross. The face is long and pale, with large brown eyes outlined in black under arched brows, a long thin nose, a drooping dark moustache and a short pointed beard. Dark hair falls in parallel strands on both sides. Around the head the halo is lost, and the bare wood, eaten by worms into a spongy texture, shows. Behind, a green velvet frame and suspension wires.
caption: Workshop of Alberto Sozio, head of Christ, detail of the painted cross of the Jacorossi collection, c. 1190–1210. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A painted cross against a black background. Christ stands upright with open eyes and a red and gold halo, his arms stretched along a blue crossbar, in a long golden-brown loincloth. Beside the body stand the Virgin in red at the left and Saint John in red and green at the right. In the cimasa a bust of Christ in a circle between two angels. At the ends of the crossbar small damaged scenes, and at the foot a damaged scene with several figures.
caption: Circle of Alberto Sozio, painted cross, late twelfth century, tempera on canvas laid on panel, 219.5 × 170 cm. London, Victoria and Albert Museum, 850-1900. Photo: Victoria and Albert Museum, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A tall panel of the enthroned Virgin nursing the Child. She wears a tall jewelled crown with pendants, a blue garment and a red mantle that falls over her knees; her large eyes look straight out. The Child, in a gold-patterned robe, sits on her lap and drinks at her breast. Two small angels fly at the upper corners against a gold ground. At the foot of the panel an inscription reads, in part, DE AMBRO.
caption: Madonna d'Ambro, the Virgin and Child enthroned, thirteenth century, tempera on panel; attributed to Alberto Sozio by Boskovits, an attribution rejected by Cochetti Pratesi. L'Aquila, MuNDA – Museo Nazionale d'Abruzzo. Photo: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A fragment of fresco on a brick wall. At the left, in a separate panel, a bishop saint with a mitre and a red chasuble with a white pallium stands frontally with a halo. At the right, against a green and blue ground, four young men in red and ochre tunics thrust long swords at a haloed bishop in a red chasuble who stands at an altar at the right. The edges of the fresco are broken and the brick shows around it.
caption: Unknown painter, the martyrdom of Thomas Becket, fresco, first half of the thirteenth century, for comparison; not by Alberto Sozio. Pavia, San Lanfranco. Photo: Albero300, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
