alt: Ruins of a long rectangular stone building without a roof, seen from above along its length. Two high side walls of yellowish rubble masonry, pierced by rows of small rectangular openings and recesses, enclose a grassy interior. At the far end rises a tall gabled wall with small windows, a projecting pointed hood in the middle, and a round-arched doorway at ground level. Dense green trees surround the ruin.
caption: Disibodenberg, ruins of the lay brothers' building and hospice, fourteenth century, from the later Cistercian phase of the abbey. Photo: E-W / Wikipedia, original, CC BY-SA 3.0 DE.

alt: Small landscape painting. On a hilltop stand two ruined gabled stone buildings with small windows, a fragment of wall and a broken pier between them, with further ruins among trees at the left. A large tree dominates the left side. In the foreground a shepherd with a staff, a seated woman, a child and a boy stand around a small fire, with goats grazing around them. In the distance a river valley with hills and a town with a church spire.
caption: After Caspar Scheuren, The Ruins of Disibodenberg on the Nahe, after a lithograph published in 1834, between 1834 and 1900. Oil on canvas, 21.7 × 27.9 cm. Formerly on the art market (Karl & Faber, Munich). Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Miniature in a broad frame. Within an arched opening on a yellow ground a nun in a dark habit and veil sits on a cushioned seat with her feet on a footstool, holding a stylus and a red-framed wax tablet on her knees; five long red tongues of flame descend from above onto her head. To the right, in a narrow tower-like building, a tonsured monk in a brown habit leans his head through a gap in the wall, holding a book or a bundle of leaves. The buildings have small arched windows, red domes and a roof of grey scale-like tiles.
caption: Rupertsberg, illuminator working for Hildegard of Bingen, Hildegard receiving the vision, with Volmar, opening miniature of the Scivias, fol. 1r of the Rupertsberg codex, c. 1165–1180. Formerly Wiesbaden, Landesbibliothek, Hs. 1 (lost since 1945); reproduced from the hand-painted copy made at the Abbey of St Hildegard, Eibingen, 1927–1933. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Full-page miniature on a blue starry ground within a pink and lilac scrolling border. At the centre an upright oval shape, pointed at the top, is formed by concentric bands: an outer ring of golden flames, then a dark band with red flickers and white clusters, then a blue field sown with red and gold stars with a crescent moon and a pale orb near the top. At the centre lies a small circular earth surrounded by wavy bands of water. Above the flames a large red star is topped by three smaller ones; small grey and red heads at the sides and bottom blow streams of wind towards the centre.
caption: Rupertsberg, illuminator working for Hildegard of Bingen, The Cosmos as an Egg, Scivias I.3, fol. 14r of the Rupertsberg codex, c. 1165–1180. Formerly Wiesbaden, Landesbibliothek, Hs. 1 (lost since 1945); reproduced from the hand-painted copy made at the Abbey of St Hildegard, Eibingen, 1927–1933. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Full-page miniature with a large circle that extends beyond a rectangular gold-ground frame with a cloud border. The circle is formed of nine concentric rings of figures. The two outer rings are winged angels with haloes, in pale blue, pink, green and white wings. Within them come rings of green faces, a broad gold band written with fine red scrolls, a red band with sawtooth edges, two rings of pale grey and white faces, and a blue band with white dots. At the centre a ring of red figures covered with eyes and outlined in gold surrounds an empty white circle.
caption: Rupertsberg, illuminator working for Hildegard of Bingen, The Choirs of Angels, Scivias I.6, fol. 38r of the Rupertsberg codex, c. 1165–1180. Formerly Wiesbaden, Landesbibliothek, Hs. 1 (lost since 1945); reproduced from the hand-painted copy made at the Abbey of St Hildegard, Eibingen, 1927–1933. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Full-page miniature on a deep blue ground within a red border filled with white and gold flower-like ornament. At the centre a large pale silver disc encloses a smaller disc of concentric wavy rings in gold and orange outlined in black. In the middle stands a frontal male figure in a long blue-grey robe, with dark shoulder-length hair, both hands raised with palms outward at chest height; his figure is outlined by a narrow silver contour that separates him from the rings.
caption: Rupertsberg, illuminator working for Hildegard of Bingen, The Trinity, Scivias II.2, from the Rupertsberg codex, c. 1165–1180. Formerly Wiesbaden, Landesbibliothek, Hs. 1 (lost since 1945); reproduced from the hand-painted copy made at the Abbey of St Hildegard, Eibingen, 1927–1933. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Full-page miniature on a pale pink ground within a purple and orange scroll border. A large crowned female figure with long brown hair stands frontally, with tall golden wings or flames rising on either side of her head and long golden sleeves hanging down at her sides. Against her breast she holds a group of small figures: at the centre a maiden in a red tunic, surrounded by figures in red, white and grey. Below the waist her body is formed by a column of pale white and grey rock-like shapes outlined in black.
caption: Rupertsberg, illuminator working for Hildegard of Bingen, Ecclesia and the Orders of the Church, Scivias II.5, from the Rupertsberg codex, c. 1165–1180. Formerly Wiesbaden, Landesbibliothek, Hs. 1 (lost since 1945); reproduced from the hand-painted copy made at the Abbey of St Hildegard, Eibingen, 1927–1933. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Manuscript page written in two columns of dark brown Romanesque minuscule on pale parchment. At the top of the left column a red rubric reads Incipit prima pars libri Scivias. Below it a tall red initial E, its shaft filled with a wavy line and its arms with fine scrolls, is followed by the letters CCE in smaller red capitals; the text begins Ecce quadragesimo tertio temporalis cursus mei anno.
caption: Rupertsberg, Opening of the Scivias, with the Protestificatio, from the Riesencodex, fol. 3r, c. 1180–1190. Ink and red pigment on parchment. Wiesbaden, Hochschul- und Landesbibliothek RheinMain, Hs. 2. Image: Hochschul- und Landesbibliothek RheinMain, Wiesbaden, CC BY 4.0.

alt: Manuscript page in two columns of chant. Each line of Latin text is surmounted by small black neumes placed on a staff of fine ruled lines, one of which is drawn in red; clef letters stand at the beginning of the lines. Several chants begin with red initials O, some with internal decoration, and small red letters in the margin mark the genre of each piece. The text of the first chant begins O vis eternitatis.
caption: Rupertsberg, Antiphons from the Symphonia (O vis eternitatis, O quam magna est benignitas, O magne Pater, O eterne Deus, O virtus Sapientie, O quam mirabilis), from the Riesencodex, fol. 466r, c. 1180–1190. Wiesbaden, Hochschul- und Landesbibliothek RheinMain, Hs. 2. Image: Hochschul- und Landesbibliothek RheinMain, Wiesbaden, CC BY 4.0.

alt: Manuscript page in two columns of chant with neumes over the text. At the foot of the left column a red rubric reads Incipit ordo virtutum. The right column begins with a red rubric Patriarche et prophete and a red initial Q, Qui sunt hi qui ut nubes, followed by speeches introduced by red rubrics such as Virtutes, Querela animarum in carne positarum and Felix anima, each opening with a red initial O.
caption: Rupertsberg, End of the Symphonia and beginning of the Ordo Virtutum, from the Riesencodex, fol. 478v, c. 1180–1190. Wiesbaden, Hochschul- und Landesbibliothek RheinMain, Hs. 2. Image: Hochschul- und Landesbibliothek RheinMain, Wiesbaden, CC BY 4.0.

alt: Manuscript page with a tall miniature on a gold ground in a blue foliate border. A standing figure with a red face and a red robe edged with jewelled bands has a second head, bearded and grey-haired, above her own. Two great pairs of wings in brown, blue and white rise from her shoulders, ending in the head of an eagle at the left and a human head at the right. She holds a small lamb against her breast and her feet tread on a dark, scaly, monstrous figure lying on the ground, around which a serpent is coiled. Below the main miniature a smaller panel shows, at the left, a monk writing at a desk and, at the right, a nun seated with red streams descending on her head, holding writing tablets, with a second nun standing behind her.
caption: Rhenish illuminator, Divine Love (Caritas), with Hildegard, her secretary and a nun, Liber Divinorum Operum, vision 1, fol. 1v, c. 1210–1230. Tempera and gold on parchment. Lucca, Biblioteca Statale, Ms. 1942. Image: Biblioteca Statale di Lucca, Ms. 1942, World Digital Library (Library of Congress), no known copyright restrictions.

alt: Manuscript page with a full-page miniature on a gold ground in a red and pink border. A huge red figure, whose bearded old man's head appears above her own head at the top and whose feet emerge at the bottom, embraces with her arms a great circle. The circle consists of concentric bands: an outer ring of red fire with flame-like edges, a black and red twisted band, a broad blue band with wavy white lines, and a white inner field with fine rays. In the centre a naked man stands with arms outstretched, his body overlapping a dark red disc; golden lines radiate from the edges of the circle towards him. Animal heads around the rings blow winds, and small dark clouds float in the white field. At the lower left, in a small arched niche, a nun sits writing at a desk with an open book.
caption: Rhenish illuminator, The Cosmic Wheel and the Universal Man, Liber Divinorum Operum, vision 2, fol. 9r, c. 1210–1230. Tempera and gold on parchment. Lucca, Biblioteca Statale, Ms. 1942. Image: Biblioteca Statale di Lucca, Ms. 1942, World Digital Library (Library of Congress), no known copyright restrictions.

alt: Manuscript page with a full-page miniature on a gold ground in a blue foliate border. A great wheel of concentric rings fills most of the page: an outer ring of red flames, a thin black and red twisted band, a broad blue band with wavy white lines, and an inner white field. At the centre a small globe is divided into four quarters coloured green, dark red, brown and grey. Around it, set radially in the white field, are trees and small human figures at work: digging, pruning, harvesting, reaping and resting. Animal heads around the rings, among them a stag, a bear and a crab, blow winds towards the centre, and stars are scattered in the outer zones. At the lower left, in an arched niche, a nun seated at a desk writes in an open book; below the wheel a hand holds a long white scroll.
caption: Rhenish illuminator, The Earth, the Seasons and the Labours of Humanity, Liber Divinorum Operum, vision 4, fol. 38r, c. 1210–1230. Tempera and gold on parchment. Lucca, Biblioteca Statale, Ms. 1942. Image: Biblioteca Statale di Lucca, Ms. 1942, World Digital Library (Library of Congress), no known copyright restrictions.

alt: Wide altar frontal of deep red silk embroidered in gold thread, divided into three fields by vertical borders of scrolling ornament. In the centre, within a pointed oval mandorla edged with an inscription, Christ sits enthroned, blessing and holding a jewelled book, between the letters alpha and omega and stars. At either side stand pairs of haloed saints under a band of fret ornament: at the left Peter with a key and a crowned Virgin, at the right a crowned saint with a sceptre and a veiled woman holding a church and a book. Below them two small figures lie prostrate, an archbishop at the left and a duchess at the right. The outer fields show John the Baptist with a medallion of the Lamb, with a small woman and a kneeling man beside him, and a bishop with a crozier and a book. Along the lower edge a row of small kneeling nuns with raised hands faces the centre, with two further prostrate figures in the corners.
caption: Rupertsberg (?), Antependium of the Rupertsberg, c. 1210–1230. Red silk embroidered with gold and silver thread and coloured silks, c. 100 × 232 cm. Brussels, Royal Museums of Art and History. Photo (1976): KIK-IRPA, Brussels (Belgium), cliché G001135, CC BY 4.0.

alt: A large painted wooden cross on a gold ground, hanging against a grey wall. Christ stands upright with open eyes and outstretched arms, his head in a raised gold halo pierced by three holes, wearing a deep blue loincloth tied with a gold knot. Above, a titulus in gold letters on blue bands. On the left arm the Virgin and Saint John, on the right a single holy woman. Beside the body, three small scenes on each side, and below the feet a damaged scene with a group of figures.
caption: Maestro della Croce 432, painted cross with Christ triumphant, the mourners and stories of the Passion and the Redemption, second half of the twelfth century, tempera and gold on panel, 276 × 231 cm. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi, inv. 1890 no. 432. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Detail of the upper part of the painted cross. The head of Christ, with long dark hair, a short beard and large open eyes, is set in a raised gold halo pierced by three dark holes. Above, the gold letters NUS REX IU DEORUM on blue bands. The pale grey-green body has a broad chest, a pear-shaped abdomen with a spiral navel and a gold belt with a large knot over a dark blue loincloth. At the sides are the scenes of the Washing of the Feet and the Arrest on the left, the Deposition and the Entombment on the right.
caption: Maestro della Croce 432, Christ, head and body, with the scenes of the Washing of the Feet, the Arrest, the Deposition and the Entombment. Detail of the cross no. 432. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The left end of the crossbar of a painted cross, framed by a thick gilded moulding with concave ends. On a gold ground two standing figures turn their heads towards the centre: the Virgin, in a dark purple mantle over a blue robe, with gold edges, and Saint John, beardless, in a blue tunic and a red cloak, both with their hands crossed before them. To the right, along the crossbar, the open hand of Christ with a nail wound.
caption: Maestro della Croce 432, the Virgin and Saint John, left end of the crossbar of the cross no. 432. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The right end of the crossbar of a painted cross, framed by a gilded moulding. At the left, the open left hand of Christ with a nail wound and a thin stream of blood, on a gold ground between ornamental borders. In the end panel a single standing woman in a dark blue mantle and a green robe raises her right hand to her breast and looks towards Christ. The rest of the panel to her right is a plain gold surface without figures.
caption: Maestro della Croce 432, the left hand of Christ and a holy woman, right end of the crossbar of the cross no. 432; the rest of the panel is lost and regilded. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Detail of the lower shaft of a painted cross: the two pale feet of Christ placed side by side and slightly apart on a gold ground, each with a nail wound shown as a gold disc ringed with small red or dark rays, from which thin wavy streams of blood run down between the toes. Narrow red bands and ornamental borders of blue, green and red palmettes run along the sides.
caption: Maestro della Croce 432, the feet of Christ. Detail of the cross no. 432. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A small scene on a gold ground. At the left Christ, in a blue robe and a mantle scattered with gold dots, kneels before a green basin and washes the foot of Peter, seated in a red mantle, who raises his hand to his head. Behind them the other apostles crowd together, their haloed heads in rows; one at the front bends to untie his sandal. Above, a long red roof and a small blue domed building with a cross, and at the left a column and a looped curtain. At the bottom edge appear the tops of lances.
caption: Maestro della Croce 432, the Washing of the Feet, upper left scene of the cross no. 432. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi. Photo: Oursana, public domain (CC0), via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A small crowded scene on a gold ground. In the centre Judas, in a dark blue mantle with gold dots, embraces and kisses Christ, who stands in a dark blue robe scattered with gold dots. Soldiers and men crowd on either side; one at the left grasps Christ's arm. Above them rise lances, torches, a hooked staff and a square lantern on a pole. At the lower left Peter, with a gold halo, kneels and seizes a young man by the head. To the right, part of the blue loincloth of Christ on the cross.
caption: Maestro della Croce 432, the Arrest of Christ with the Kiss of Judas, middle left scene of the cross no. 432. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi. Photo: Oursana, public domain (CC0), via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Close detail of a painted scene with crackled surface. Saint Peter, an old man with grey hair and beard and a gold halo, in a blue tunic and a red cloak, kneels and holds down the head of a young dark-haired man, Malchus, whose face is streaked with red; a dark blade shows at his ear. At the right falls the dark blue mantle of Judas, scattered with small squares of gold leaf, above bare feet in sandals. A red and gold lozenge border runs along the left edge.
caption: Maestro della Croce 432, Peter cutting off the ear of Malchus. Detail of the Arrest of Christ, cross no. 432. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A small scene on a gold ground under an arch of red and blue domes resting on two columns. In the centre Christ stands frontally, naked but for a light blue loincloth flecked with gold, his hands behind his back. On either side a man in a short red or pink tunic and leggings raises his arms to strike him with a whip. At the far left two bearded men in green, red and blue garments watch, one pointing. At the right edge, the gold and blue drapery of the loincloth of Christ on the cross.
caption: Maestro della Croce 432, the Flagellation, lower left scene of the cross no. 432. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Close detail of the Flagellation. Christ, with long brown hair, a short beard and a faint incised halo, stands frontally with his hands behind his back, naked but for a pale blue loincloth scattered with gold leaf. At the left a young man in a pink tunic with a wavy fringe of hair raises his arms to strike; behind him a bearded man in blue and red points. At the right another man in red raises his arms with a dark whip. Above, red and blue domes on columns with blue capitals.
caption: Maestro della Croce 432, Christ at the Flagellation. Detail of the cross no. 432. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi. Photo: Francesco Bini, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A badly damaged scene at the foot of a painted cross, framed by red lines on a gold ground. In the centre Christ, in a blue robe, walks to the right, led by a bearded man in red who grasps his arm. Behind them a man in a green tunic carries a large blue cross on his shoulder. At the left a bearded man in red holds a coil of rope, and behind him the faded remains of other figures. Large areas of paint are lost, showing the gold or the preparation beneath.
caption: Maestro della Croce 432, the Way to Calvary, scene at the foot of the cross no. 432. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A small scene on a gold ground. A dark blue cross stands in the middle. A bearded man behind it holds the dead body of Christ, which sags across him; a man in red kneels at the foot of the cross and draws a nail from the feet with pincers. At the left a woman in a dark mantle and a young man in green, Saint John, grieve with their hands to their faces. At the right two women in dark blue mantles, one supporting the arm of Christ. Above at the right a small angel flies with spread wings.
caption: Maestro della Croce 432, the Deposition from the Cross, upper right scene of the cross no. 432. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi. Photo: Oursana, public domain (CC0), via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A small scene on a gold ground, under a red dome resting on columns, with small hanging lamps. The body of Christ, wrapped in a pale blue shroud crossed with white bands, is laid on a red marble sarcophagus with a dark green lid. The Virgin, in a dark blue mantle, bends over him and presses her cheek against his face. Two men in blue and green hold the ends of the shroud at the left; a woman in a dark mantle raises her hand to her mouth behind them. At the right a haloed woman in a green and red mantle holds the other end of the shroud.
caption: Maestro della Croce 432, the Entombment, middle right scene of the cross no. 432. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi. Photo: Oursana, public domain (CC0), via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A small scene on a gold ground. Christ, in a gold robe drawn with fine lines and holding a long staff topped with a cross, strides to the right and grasps by the wrist an old bearded man in blue and red, Adam, who kneels and reaches up to him. Behind Adam a woman in a pale green mantle, Eve, raises her hands. At the left two crowned kings, one bearded, stand behind a green marble parapet. Above, dark rocky shapes in blue-green; below Christ's feet, broken doors, a blue lock and flames.
caption: Maestro della Croce 432, the Descent into Limbo, lower right scene of the cross no. 432. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi. Photo: Oursana, public domain (CC0), via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Close detail of two crowned kings on a crackled gold ground, standing behind a parapet of green speckled marble. The king at the left has a grey pointed beard and wears a red robe over a blue tunic; the beardless king at the right wears a green patterned robe with a jewelled gold collar. Both wear gold crowns with trefoils and hold a hand to their breast. Above them dark blue-green rocks. At the left an ornamental border and the dark blue loincloth of Christ on the cross; at the right the gold robe of Christ in the Limbo.
caption: Maestro della Croce 432, the kings David and Solomon. Detail of the Descent into Limbo, cross no. 432. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Close detail of the lower part of the Descent into Limbo. Two broken door panels, white and crackled, lie crossed diagonally on a dark ground with red and black flames. A blue lock with two hooked bolts lies on them. The bare feet of Christ, in sandals, stand on the doors, and the hem of his gold robe, drawn in red and blue lines, falls above them. At the upper left a parapet of green speckled marble; at the left an ornamental border; at the right the hand of Adam and his knee.
caption: Maestro della Croce 432, the broken gates of Hell under the feet of Christ. Detail of the Descent into Limbo, cross no. 432. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Twelfth-century painted cross from the monastery of Santa Maria a Rosano: a living, open-eyed Christ in a blue loincloth stands against a gold ground, arms outstretched along a blue crossbar, flanked by six small Passion and Resurrection scenes in two columns, with mourning figures in the arm terminals and the Denial of Peter on the lower shaft, the whole cross displayed on a moulded stone corbel against a black background
caption: Maestro di Rosano, painted cross with Passion scenes, c. 1129–1134, tempera and gold on chestnut panel, 253 × 230 cm, for comparison. Rignano sull'Arno (Florence), monastery of Santa Maria a Rosano. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A large painted wooden cross in a glass case against a red damask. Christ stands upright with open eyes and outstretched arms, in a long white loincloth, his halo set with stones. At the top a small panel shows Christ in a mandorla above the Virgin and apostles, with red and blue bands of inscription below it. The arms end in panels with Evangelist symbols and scrolls. Beside his body stand the Virgin with a holy woman at the left and Saint John with a holy woman at the right; below them small scenes of the Passion fill the panel.
caption: Guglielmo, painted cross, signed and dated 1138, tempera and gold on panel, 299 × 214 cm; the figure of Christ is a repainting of about fifty years later; for comparison. Sarzana, concattedrale di Santa Maria Assunta, chapel of the Crucifix. Photo: Benjamin Smith, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A painted cross on a gold ground. Christ stands upright and frontal with open eyes, a relief halo and a long knotted loincloth, his arms stretched along a dark blue band. The ends of the crossbar show two crowded scenes with the apostles at table and under arcades. Three scenes on each side of the body, with many small figures under arches; a panel at the foot with seated apostles; at the top a cimasa with the Virgin among angels and apostles, above a titulus.
caption: Maestro della Croce del Santo Sepolcro, painted cross (Croce n. 15), second half of the twelfth century or about 1200, tempera and gold on panel, 282 × 236 cm, for comparison. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, inv. 1578, from the church of the Santo Sepolcro. Photo: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A large painted cross hanging in a dark stone apse. Christ stands upright with open eyes, a severe long face and a gold-bordered halo, in a short gilded loincloth. The ends of the arms and the top are rounded and painted with angels and a seated figure. Beside his body stand the Virgin and Saint John, and small arched scenes of the Passion fill the panel below.
caption: Lucchese painter, painted cross, c. 1150–1200, for comparison. Lucca, San Michele in Foro. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A painted cross on a dark wooden ground studded with round iron nail heads. Christ stands upright with open eyes and a gold halo set with raised bosses, wearing a loincloth of white and blue knotted at the waist; his feet rest on a footrest. Beside the body stand the Virgin in blue and red, raising her hand to her face, and Saint John in red. In the cimasa Christ ascends in a blue mandorla among angels, above a titulus. At the foot a small figure and two lines of inscription with a date.
caption: Alberto Sozio, painted cross, signed and dated 1187, tempera on parchment laid on panel, for comparison. Spoleto, cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A painted cross on a gold ground against a black background. Christ hangs with bowed head and closed eyes, his body golden-brown with strongly marked muscles and ribs, his hips swaying to the side, in a long pale blue loincloth; his feet are crossed and pierced by a single nail. The halo is in relief, with radiating ribs and set with stones. Beside the body, four scenes on each side, among them the Flagellation, the Way to Calvary, the Deposition, the Entombment, the holy women at the tomb and the supper at Emmaus.
caption: Maestro della Croce 434, painted cross, c. 1240–1250, tempera and gold on panel, 247 × 202 cm, for comparison. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi, inv. 1890 no. 434. Photo: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Twelfth-century Pisan painted cross on a gold ground. A living, frontal Christ with open eyes, a relief halo and a long knotted loincloth stands with horizontal arms against a dark blue cross. The crossbar terminals show the Last Supper and the Washing of the Feet. Six Passion and post-Resurrection scenes, including the Mocking, the Crucifixion, the Holy Women at the Tomb and the Supper at Emmaus, flank his body. The damaged cimasa shows an Ascension and the foot shows Pentecost
caption: Painted Cross with Christus Triumphans and Gospel Scenes (Croce n. 15), Pisa, second half of the 12th century. Tempera and gold on panel, 282 × 236 cm. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, inv. 1578; from the church of the Santo Sepolcro, Pisa.
entry: Maestro della Croce del Santo Sepolcro

alt: Romanesque painted cross showing a living Christ with open eyes and a gold nimbus, arms stretched horizontally, wearing a long translucent blue-grey loincloth. Six small Passion and post-Resurrection scenes flank his torso, a Pentecost fills the top panel, and a standing prophet appears at each end of the crossbar. Two superimposed Latin inscriptions are visible above his head.
caption: Master of the San Frediano Cross (first painting) and Master of Rosano (attr., repainting), Painted Cross with Christ Triumphant, Scenes of the Passion and Resurrection, Pentecost, and the Prophets David and Isaiah. First painting c. 1110–1120; repainted c. 1130–1140. Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, church of San Frediano. The face of Christ belongs to the earlier layer; the narrative scenes, cimasa and terminals belong to the twelfth-century repainting uncovered in the restoration of 1960–1972.
entry: Maestro della Croce di San Frediano

alt: Twelfth-century painted cross from the monastery of Santa Maria a Rosano: a living, open-eyed Christ in a blue loincloth stands against a gold ground, arms outstretched along a blue crossbar, flanked by six small Passion and Resurrection scenes in two columns, with mourning figures in the arm terminals and the Denial of Peter on the lower shaft, the whole cross displayed on a moulded stone corbel against a black background
caption: Maestro di Rosano, painted cross with Christ triumphant and scenes of the Passion and the Resurrection, c. 1129–1134, tempera and gold on chestnut panel, 253 × 230 cm (Fondazione Zeri). Rignano sull'Arno (Florence), monastery of Santa Maria a Rosano. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Detail of the upper part of a painted cross. Christ's head, with a long face, large dark eyes, a long straight nose, a greenish beard and long locks of hair on the shoulders, is set in a raised gold halo with a cross of jewelled bands. His arms are stretched along a deep blue band framed by red lines and borders of rosettes and lilies. At the left end, the Virgin and Saint John grieving; at the right end, two holy women.
caption: Maestro di Rosano, the head of Christ, the arms and the terminals with the mourners. Detail of the painted cross of Rosano. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (detail).

alt: The left half of a painted cross. At the end of the arm, the Virgin and Saint John stand together grieving. Christ's right arm stretches along a blue band with a pierced hand. Below, three scenes are stacked beside the blue loincloth of Christ: the Capture with Judas kissing Christ and Peter attacking Malchus, the Descent into Limbo with Christ grasping Adam, and Emmaus with Christ dressed as a pilgrim beside two disciples and a city.
caption: Maestro di Rosano, the left side of the cross, with the Virgin and Saint John and the scenes of the Capture of Christ, the Descent into Limbo and Emmaus. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Detail of the left terminal of a painted cross. On a worn gold ground the Virgin, in a dark red mantle over a deep blue robe, wipes her eyes with her veil and holds the hand of Saint John, who stands beside her in an orange-red mantle over a blue tunic, his hand raised to his cheek. A horizontal crack crosses their faces. At the right, the ornamental border of the crossbar.
caption: Maestro di Rosano, the Virgin and Saint John, left terminal of the painted cross of Rosano. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (detail).

alt: Three stacked scenes on a gold ground with gold captions on dark green bands. Top: Judas in red embraces and kisses Christ amid a crowd with spears and torches, while Peter with a halo seizes Malchus and a red lantern lies on the ground. Middle: Christ in a dark mantle with a cross-staff grasps the wrist of Adam, an old man in red and blue, before a crowd of heads framed by rocks, with broken doors and flames under his feet. Bottom: Christ dressed as a pilgrim with a red hat, staff and bag meets two disciples beside a walled city.
caption: Maestro di Rosano, the Capture of Christ, the Descent into Limbo and the meeting at Emmaus, left column of the painted cross of Rosano. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (detail).

alt: The right half of a painted cross. Christ's left arm stretches along a blue band to an open pierced hand. At the end of the arm, two holy women stand in mourning, one in red with folded hands, the other in green and blue holding a jar. Below, three scenes are stacked beside the blue loincloth: the Deposition with a ladder, the Entombment under a canopy and the Holy Women with an angel at the tomb.
caption: Maestro di Rosano, the right side of the cross, with two holy women and the scenes of the Deposition, the Entombment and the Holy Women at the Sepulchre. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Three stacked scenes on a gold ground with gold captions on red bands. Top: below a blue cross, Joseph of Arimathea on a ladder lowers the body of Christ, the Virgin at the right holds his head, John in green supports him at the left, and Nicodemus kneels to draw the nails from the feet. Middle: under a dark canopy on a column, the body wrapped in a white shroud is laid down by several men while the Virgin presses her cheek to his face. Bottom: three women with jars approach an angel with red wings seated on a red stone beside the open door of the tomb with grave cloths.
caption: Maestro di Rosano, the Deposition, the Entombment and the Holy Women at the Sepulchre, right column of the painted cross of Rosano. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (detail).

alt: Detail of the right terminal of a painted cross. On a worn gold ground two women stand side by side. The first, in a red mantle over an ochre dress, with a red veil, holds her hands folded before her and inclines her head. The second, in a green veil, a dark red mantle and a deep blue dress, rests her cheek on her hand and holds a small jar. The wood around them is bare and pierced with small holes.
caption: Maestro di Rosano, two holy women, right terminal of the painted cross of Rosano. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (detail).

alt: Detail of the foot of a painted cross, above a modern moulded stone corbel. On a gold ground, beneath a skyline of red and green towers, two men in red and blue robes stand at the left under arches, one gesturing, while a woman in red stands at the open door of a small house with a red roof at the right; a red cock is perched on the roof. Below, the stone corbel with fluting and a carved rosette.
caption: Maestro di Rosano, the Denial of Peter, foot of the painted cross of Rosano, above the modern stone corbel. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (detail).

alt: The entrance of a monastery seen from the street. A plastered enclosure wall under a tiled roof has a round-arched stone doorway closed by an iron gate. Behind it rise the plain stone gable of a church with a small round window and a tall square bell tower of grey stone with round-arched openings on several storeys. At the right, a tall white monastery building with stone quoins and a clock.
caption: Rignano sull'Arno, monastery of Santa Maria a Rosano, the enclosure, the gable of the church and the Romanesque bell tower. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The interior of a Romanesque church seen from the nave. Rows of square stone piers carry round arches under a wooden roof. Steps and iron railings lead up to a raised presbytery; below it an arched opening gives onto a lit crypt with an altar. At the back, in the apse beneath a semi-dome painted with a figure in a black habit among angels, the painted cross hangs lit on the white wall behind the altar.
caption: Rignano sull'Arno, monastery of Santa Maria a Rosano, the church, with the raised presbytery, the crypt and the painted cross behind the high altar. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A Romanesque crypt seen through a stone arch. Slender columns of grey stone with simple capitals carry low groin vaults. Wooden benches stand in the aisles. At the back a small apse with a narrow window holds an altar whose front is inlaid with geometric marble patterns. In the stone floor in the foreground is a round slab with a star.
caption: Rignano sull'Arno, monastery of Santa Maria a Rosano, the crypt beneath the presbytery. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A painted cross on a pale wall. At the top, a rounded cimasa with the apostles seated in a row under a canopy, above a double titulus in white letters. Christ stands upright with open eyes and a gold halo set with bosses, his arms along a dark blue band, in a long grey translucent loincloth knotted with a gold band. At the ends of the arms, two standing figures. Beside the body, three scenes on each side, among them a group of sleeping apostles, a boat and Christ rising from the tomb.
caption: Painted cross of San Frediano, first painting c. 1110–1120, repainting c. 1130–1140 attributed to the Maestro di Rosano, tempera and gold on panel, for comparison. Pisa, church of San Frediano. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A heavily worn painted cross on a stand, lit against a wall with a blue light strip. Christ stands upright and frontal with large staring eyes, a long nose and a dark beard, in a gold halo, his arms stretched along a crossbar where most of the paint is lost to bare wood. He wears a pale blue loincloth with a large gold knot. Beside the body, fragments of small scenes with figures in red and blue on gold. At the top, a damaged cimasa with a bust of Christ and two angels.
caption: Pisan painter, painted cross with Christ triumphant, c. 1100–1120, tempera and gold on panel, from San Paolo all'Orto, for comparison. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A large painted wooden cross in a glass case against a red damask. Christ stands upright with open eyes and outstretched arms, in a long white loincloth, his halo set with stones. At the top a small panel shows Christ in a mandorla above the Virgin and apostles, with red and blue bands of inscription below it. The arms end in panels with Evangelist symbols and scrolls. Beside his body stand the Virgin with a holy woman at the left and Saint John with a holy woman at the right; below them small scenes of the Passion fill the panel.
caption: Guglielmo, painted cross, signed and dated 1138, tempera and gold on panel, 299 × 214 cm; the figure of Christ is a repainting of about fifty years later; for comparison. Sarzana, concattedrale di Santa Maria Assunta. Photo: Benjamin Smith, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A large painted wooden cross on a gold ground, hanging against a grey wall. Christ stands upright with open eyes and outstretched arms, his head in a raised gold halo pierced by three holes, wearing a deep blue loincloth tied with a gold knot. Above, a titulus in gold letters on blue bands. On the left arm the Virgin and Saint John, on the right a single holy woman. Beside the body, three small scenes on each side, and below the feet a damaged scene with a group of figures.
caption: Maestro della Croce 432, painted cross with Christ triumphant, the mourners and stories of the Passion and the Redemption, second half of the twelfth century, tempera and gold on panel, 276 × 231 cm, for comparison. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi, inv. 1890 no. 432. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Romanesque church of San Pietro in Villore at San Giovanni d'Asso: stone lower façade with blind arcades and carved portal, brick upper storey with oculus, bell-gable and cypresses
caption: San Pietro in Villore, San Giovanni d'Asso (Montalcino, Siena), second half of the 12th century. Three-quarter view of the façade: lower register in squared sandstone and alberese with four blind arches on half-columns flanking the splayed portal; upper register in brick, rebuilt after later damage, with oculus; the brick bell-gable dates from the early 20th-century restoration.
entry: Maestro di San Pietro in Villore

alt: Twelfth-century painted cross: frontal living Christ with open eyes on a blue cross, blessing Redeemer between angels above, two mourning women at left, John and a woman at right; surface heavily worn and split
caption: Christ Triumphant, last quarter of the 12th century, tempera and gold on an oak panel covered with canvas, 177 × 116.5 × 12 cm, from the church of San Pietro in Villore, San Giovanni d'Asso. Pienza, Museo Diocesano di Palazzo Borgia.
entry: Maestro di San Pietro in Villore

alt: Twelfth-century painted cross from Sant'Antimo: living Christ with open eyes and cross-inscribed nimbus, knotted blue loincloth, Redeemer in a clipeus between angels above, Saint John at right; left panel and lower shaft largely lost
caption: Maestro di San Pietro in Villore (attr.), Christ Triumphant, last quarter of the 12th century (c. 1190 in museum literature), tempera and gold on poplar panel, from the abbey of Sant'Antimo, Montalcino, Museo Civico e Diocesano d'Arte Sacra.
entry: Maestro di San Pietro in Villore

alt: A large painted wooden cross in a glass case against a red damask. Christ stands upright with open eyes and outstretched arms, in a long white loincloth, his halo set with stones. At the top a small panel shows Christ in a mandorla above the Virgin and apostles, with red and blue bands of inscription below it. The arms end in panels with Evangelist symbols and scrolls. Beside his body stand the Virgin with a holy woman at the left and Saint John with a holy woman at the right; below them small scenes of the Passion fill the panel.
caption: Guglielmo, painted cross, signed and dated 1138, tempera and gold on panel, 299 × 214 cm; the figure of Christ is a repainting of about fifty years later. Sarzana, concattedrale di Santa Maria Assunta, chapel of the Crucifix. Photo: Benjamin Smith, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The top of a painted cross: in an oval mandorla Christ ascends, seated; below, the Virgin stands between two groups of apostles. Under the panel two red bands carry the letters AZARENU and IDEORU, and a blue panel below has three lines of white capitals. At the bottom, the top of a gold halo and the forehead of Christ.
caption: Guglielmo, the cimasa with the Ascension, the titulus and the inscription with the date 1138 and the name of the painter. Detail of the cross of Sarzana. Photo: Benjamin Smith, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A narrow vertical strip of a painted cross. At the top the Virgin in a dark blue mantle over a red robe raises her hand to her breast, with a holy woman behind her. Below, under bands of faded inscription, a crowded scene of Christ seized by soldiers, and Christ bound naked to a column between two men with whips.
caption: Guglielmo, the Virgin and a holy woman, the Kiss of Judas and the Flagellation. Detail of the cross of Sarzana, left side. Photo: Benjamin Smith, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A narrow vertical strip of a painted cross. At the top Saint John in a pale mantle over a red robe bows his head onto his hand, with a holy woman behind him. Below, under bands of faded inscription, Christ in a dark mantle among a group of figures before buildings, and the body of Christ lowered from the cross.
caption: Guglielmo, Saint John and a holy woman, the Way to Calvary and the Deposition. Detail of the cross of Sarzana, right side. Photo: Benjamin Smith, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A Baroque chapel lined with red, grey and yellow marble, under a cupola painted with frescoes and lit by windows. On the altar wall, between two columns of red marble and below two kneeling marble angels on the cornice, a painted cross hangs in a glass case against red damask. Marble busts stand in niches on the side walls.
caption: The chapel of the Crucifix, rebuilt in 1713 for Cardinal Lorenzo Casoni, with the cross of Guglielmo in its case. Sarzana, concattedrale di Santa Maria Assunta. Photo: Parma1983, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A white marble church façade under a deep blue sky, with a rose window, a round-arched portal with a painted lunette and statues of saints on the gable, where the date A N D MCCCCLXXIIII is carved. At the right rises a tall bell tower of dark rough stone with mullioned windows and a crenellated top.
caption: Sarzana, concattedrale di Santa Maria Assunta, the façade dated 1474 and the bell tower. Photo: Chabe01, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A large painted cross hanging in a dark stone apse. Christ stands upright with open eyes, a severe long face and a gold-bordered halo, in a short gilded loincloth. The ends of the arms and the top are rounded and painted with angels and a seated figure. Beside his body stand the Virgin and Saint John, and small arched scenes of the Passion fill the panel below.
caption: Lucchese painter, painted cross, c. 1150–1200, for comparison. Lucca, San Michele in Foro. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The white and pink marble west front of a large cathedral under a blue sky, with three gables crowned by galleries of small arches, and its long south flank with a loggia of shops at ground level. At the centre a tall projecting porch rises in three storeys: at the bottom a round-arched doorway on columns resting on crouching lions, above it a loggia with a statue of the Virgin, and at the top a gable filled with figures.
caption: Ferrara Cathedral, the west front and the south flank. The lower storey of the porch, with its lions, belongs to the campaign of Nicholaus (inscription of 1135); the loggia and the gable above were added in the thirteenth century. Photo: almusaiti (Flickr), CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The upper storeys of a cathedral porch in white marble. Under a triangular gable with Christ enthroned in a mandorla among angels and the elect, a frieze shows rows of standing figures, angels weighing souls and naked figures led away to the right. Below, a loggia of three pointed arches with quatrefoils encloses a crowned statue of the Virgin and Child; at the sides, two relief lunettes show Abraham holding souls in his lap and devils tormenting the damned.
caption: Ferrara Cathedral, the upper storeys of the porch with the Last Judgement, thirteenth century. They were added above the porch of Nicholaus and are not his work. Photo: Alain Rouiller, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A round-arched portal seen from below, framed by several mouldings in white and pink marble carved with cables and lattice. In the lunette a mounted knight in mail with a raised sword spears a dragon under his horse's hooves, within a border of foliage. Below, a lintel is divided into eight small arched panels with scenes: the Annunciation, the Visitation, the Nativity, the Annunciation to the Shepherds, the Adoration of the Magi, the Presentation, the Flight into Egypt and the Baptism.
caption: Nicholaus, the lunette with Saint George and the dragon and the lintel with scenes of the Infancy of Christ, c. 1135. Ferrara Cathedral, main portal. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 2.5, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A close view of a stone relief: a young knight in a mail hauberk with a round face and a halo rides a galloping horse, his sword raised in his right hand, while his lance pierces a winged dragon lying under the horse. Letters of an inscription run along the curved border above him.
caption: Nicholaus, Saint George, detail of the lunette, c. 1135, with part of the signature on its border. Ferrara Cathedral, main portal. Photo: Nicola Quirico, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The left jamb of a portal: several marble shafts carved with lattice, zigzag and spiral patterns, between which two pier edges carry small standing figures of prophets holding long inscribed scrolls, set among panels with animals and flowers. At the top right, part of a carved lintel with two embracing women under an arch.
caption: Nicholaus, the left jamb of the main portal with prophets holding scrolls, c. 1135. Ferrara Cathedral. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 2.5, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The right jamb of a portal: marble shafts carved with spirals and zigzags, the edges of the piers carrying small figures of a winged angel and of bearded prophets with scrolls, set among panels with beasts. At the left a small crouching figure at the corner of a capital; at the right a column of the porch and an inscription on a plaque.
caption: Nicholaus, the right jamb of the main portal with the angel of the Annunciation and prophets, c. 1135. Ferrara Cathedral. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 2.5, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A crouching lion of pink veined marble at the foot of a portal column, holding a ram's head between its paws. On its back a squatting bearded man in a short tunic, his hand at his cheek, supports the base of a column on his shoulders. At the left, carved jambs with small figured panels.
caption: Lion and telamon at the foot of the porch of Ferrara Cathedral, right side: a modern replica of the group of the workshop of Nicholaus (c. 1135). Photo: Sailko, CC BY 2.5, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A crouching lion of pink veined marble with open jaws, holding a ram under its paws, at the foot of a porch column, lit by low sunlight. On its back a squatting youth with curly hair and a heavy pleated garment raises both arms to support the base of the column.
caption: Lion with a ram and a telamon at the foot of the porch of Ferrara Cathedral, left side: a modern copy of the group of the workshop of Nicholaus (c. 1135). Photo: Alain Rouiller, CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The pale stone west front of a Romanesque church under a blue sky, with a central gable and lower sloping side wings, a large wheel window, and a tall striped bell tower at the right. In the centre a small projecting porch on two columns frames a wooden door; on both sides of the door the wall is covered by panels of reliefs.
caption: Verona, basilica of San Zeno Maggiore, the west front, with the porch and portal of Nicholaus (c. 1138) and the reliefs at the sides of the door. Photo: Andrea Bertozzi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A close view of a projecting porch on a stone church front. The gable shows a blessing hand in a roundel; the arch is lined with small square reliefs of animals and the Lamb; standing saints are carved at the sides. Squatting telamons sit on the capitals of the two columns. Under the arch a painted lunette shows a bishop between soldiers on foot and on horseback, above a frieze of small arched scenes; at the bottom left and right, panels of reliefs with biblical figures.
caption: Nicholaus, the porch of San Zeno Maggiore, Verona, c. 1138: the gable with the hand of God, the arch with the Lamb, the two Saints John, telamons on the capitals and the lunette of Saint Zeno. Photo: NorbertNagel, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A painted stone lunette under an arch. At the centre a bishop with a green mitre, a halo and a crozier stands frontally, blessing, with a dark devil under his feet. At the left a crowd of foot soldiers with red caps receives a banner with a cross; at the right mounted knights with lances and shields advance. Inscriptions run along the arch, and below a frieze of small arcades shows scenes with figures, a cauldron, oxen and a cart.
caption: Nicholaus, Saint Zeno giving the banner to the people of Verona, with the signature on the arch and miracles of the saint below, c. 1138. Verona, San Zeno Maggiore, lunette of the main portal. Photo: Zairon, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A stone relief under a small arch flanked by towers and columns: a man in a pointed cap and a long garment sits on a chair, warming his hands before a fire. The inscription below reads IANOARIUS.
caption: Nicholaus and workshop, January warming himself at the fire, from the cycle of the Months, c. 1138. Verona, San Zeno Maggiore, main portal. Photo: Retogenes, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A tall panel of marble reliefs in two columns, weathered and stained. Scenes include, from the top, the Creation of Eve from the side of the sleeping Adam, the Fall with Adam and Eve beside the tree, the Expulsion and the Labour, with standing saints at the sides; at the bottom a horseman with a hunting horn and a stag pursued by hounds.
caption: Nicholaus and workshop, the reliefs at the right of the main door, with scenes from Genesis and the hunt of Theodoric, c. 1138. Verona, San Zeno Maggiore, west front. Photo: MM, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A tall panel of marble reliefs in two columns: the Betrayal and the Crucifixion at the top, then the Flight into Egypt and the Baptism of Christ, the Presentation in the Temple, the Annunciation, Visitation and Nativity, and at the bottom two combats of mounted and armed men, with a standing figure between them.
caption: Guglielmo, the reliefs at the left of the main door, with scenes of the life of Christ and combats, signed by him, c. 1138. Verona, San Zeno Maggiore, west front. Photo: MM, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A two-storey porch projecting from a stone cathedral front. The lower storey is a deep round arch on columns resting on crouching griffins, framing a portal with many carved mouldings, a painted lunette and tall standing figures on the outer jambs; above, a second arch on columns rising from small lions shelters a large clock face. A bronze statue of an angel stands at the right.
caption: Nicholaus, the porch of Verona Cathedral (Santa Maria Matricolare), c. 1139: the lower storey on griffins, the upper on lions, with the lunette, the prophets of the jambs and the two paladins. Photo: Andrea Bertozzi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A painted stone lunette with a blue ground. The Virgin sits frontally on a throne holding the Child; at the left an angel announces the birth to three shepherds with their sheep, goats and dog; at the right a kneeling king offers a gift and two crowned kings on horses approach. The inscription HIC DOMINUS MAGNUS LEO CRISTUS CERNITUR AGNUS runs around the arch. Below, a lintel with three crowned half-figures in roundels inscribed FIDES, CARITAS, SPES.
caption: Nicholaus, the lunette with the Virgin and Child, the Annunciation to the Shepherds and the Magi, and the lintel with Faith, Charity and Hope, c. 1139. Verona Cathedral, main portal. Photo: Jakub Hałun, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The left jamb of a portal seen at an angle. At the far left a tall standing warrior with a helmet holds a long shield; to the right, between shafts carved with spirals and zigzags, four small prophets stand on pier edges holding scrolls inscribed ECCE EGO MITTAM ANGELUM and VIRGO CONCIPIET ET PARIET FILIUM.
caption: Nicholaus, the left jamb of the main portal with the paladin traditionally identified as Roland and four prophets, c. 1139. Verona Cathedral. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The right jamb of a portal seen at an angle. Four small prophets stand on pier edges between spiral and zigzag shafts, holding scrolls inscribed VENIET DESIDERATUS CUNCTIS GENTIBUS and ECCE SEXTUS VENIT; at the far right a tall standing figure with long hair, bareheaded, holds a long shield.
caption: Nicholaus, the right jamb of the main portal with four prophets and the figure traditionally called Oliver, c. 1139. Verona Cathedral. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A deep round-arched doorway with several stepped mouldings set in a wall of grey stone. On each side, marble columns and carved white jambs stand behind protective glass panels; at the right a lintel-like cornice and foliate capitals project over the jambs. Through the arch, steps lead into darkness.
caption: The Porta dello Zodiaco at the head of the Scalone dei Morti, Sacra di San Michele, with the carved jambs of Nicholaus (c. 1120s) under protective glass. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A close view of a white marble jamb carved with a vine scroll that encloses a bird, a lion's mask, fruits and a winged beast. Along its two edges run lines of capital letters, among them QUIS BONUS EXI and COMIXTOS.
caption: Nicholaus, the inhabited vine scroll of the Porta dello Zodiaco, with the verses Hoc opus intendat quisquis bonus exit et intrat and Flores cum beluis comixtos cernitis on its edges. Sacra di San Michele. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A white marble jamb carved with a vine scroll forming roundels: at the top a winged beast, in the middle a large rosette, at the bottom a crouching lion. Along the edges, letters read ENDAT QUIS BO and BELUIS COM.
caption: Nicholaus, the lower part of the same jamb, with the verses on its edges. Sacra di San Michele, Porta dello Zodiaco. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A white marble jamb carved with a vine scroll enclosing a bird, a naked youth, a rosette and fruits, set between a capital of acanthus leaves at the left and a carved cornice and figured capitals above and at the right.
caption: Nicholaus, an inner face of a jamb of the Porta dello Zodiaco with an inhabited vine scroll, next to reused capitals and cornices. Sacra di San Michele. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A white marble jamb seen from below, carved with panels framed by braided bands: from the top an eagle, a winged horse, a knotted triangle and a youth holding a sword. Along the edges, inscriptions read ORION, DELTOTON, PEGASUS and SERPENS.
caption: Nicholaus, the jamb of the constellations of the Porta dello Zodiaco, with the eagle, Pegasus, the Triangle and Orion, named on its edge. Sacra di San Michele. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A stone lintel with two arched panels under an inscription. At the left the Virgin and Joseph present the Child to the bearded Simeon over an altar; at the right the Virgin holding the Child rides a donkey led by Joseph. Small towers rise between the arches. The upper border reads OFFERTUR DEUS ATQUE FUGIT, the lower + HOC OPUS INTENDA.
caption: Nicholaus, the lintel of the south portal of Piacenza Cathedral, left part: the Presentation in the Temple and the Flight into Egypt, c. 1122–1130. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A stone lintel with arched panels under an inscription: at the left an angel and John the Baptist baptise Christ, who stands in rippling water with a dove above him; at the right a grinning devil sits beside Christ, who holds a book. The upper border reads SIC FONTE LAVATUR TEMPTATUR TRIPLICI, the lower NDAT QUIS QUIS BON.
caption: Nicholaus, the lintel of the south portal of Piacenza Cathedral, central part: the Baptism and the first Temptation of Christ, c. 1122–1130. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A stone lintel with arched panels: Christ stands on a mountain beside a tower, with a devil crouching at his side, and again stands on a rock beside a second devil. The upper border reads TRIPLICI DEUS ARTE DOLI SINI, the lower BONUS EXIT ET INTRA.
caption: Nicholaus, the lintel of the south portal of Piacenza Cathedral, right part: the second and third Temptations, c. 1122–1130. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A stone capital carved with two figures in short garments, a youth and a bearded man, walking away with anxious faces, each raising a hand to the side of his head.
caption: Nicholaus and workshop, a capital of the south portal of Piacenza Cathedral with two clothed figures moving away in shame, identified as Adam and Eve, c. 1122–1130. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A stone lintel with two arched panels under small towers: at the left the crowned Virgin sits holding the Child, under a star; at the right three bearded kings in crowns bring gifts, the first kneeling.
caption: Workshop of Wiligelmo, the lintel of the north portal of Piacenza Cathedral with the Adoration of the Magi, c. 1122–1130, for comparison with the south portal of Nicholaus. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Painted cross with a living Christ on a deep blue ground, open-eyed beneath a raised gilded halo, his arms outstretched along the crossbar. Gold side panels show the Virgin in a dark blue mantle on the left and Saint John in a red mantle on the right. The terminals of the arms hold the four Evangelist symbols. The top shows the Virgin between two angels and the foot shows small scenes of the Denial of Peter
caption: Berlinghiero, Christus Triumphans (Cross of Santa Maria degli Angeli), c. 1210–1220. Tempera and gold on shaped panel, 174.7 × 140.5 cm. Lucca, Museo Nazionale di Villa Guinigi, inv. 226. Signed: BERLINGERIUS ME PINXIT. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A Romanesque church faced in pale grey and white marble, seen at an angle in a narrow street after rain. The façade has a central gabled upper storey with a two-light window and a small cross, lower side parts with sloping roofs and a single doorway under a small pediment. The long side wall runs back along the street between yellow houses.
caption: The church of Sant'Alessandro in Lucca, for which Barone undertook a crucifix, a Madonna and a Saint Andrew in 1282. Photo: Chabe01, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Painted cross with a living Christ on a dark blue ground edged with red pearled bands. His head, under a gilded halo, inclines to one side, and he wears a long pink loincloth. Gold side panels show the Virgin in a dark mantle and Saint John in a pink mantle, above small scenes of the Capture of Christ and the Holy Women at the Tomb. At the top Christ blesses between two angels, small winged Evangelist symbols occupy the ends of the arms, and small figures flank the feet
caption: Berlinghieri workshop (attributed to Berlinghiero and his circle, or to Bonaventura Berlinghieri), Painted Cross (Tereglio Cross), c. 1235–1245. Tempera and gold on panel. Tereglio (Coreglia Antelminelli, Lucca), church of Santa Maria Assunta.

alt: Painted cross with a slender, living Christ on a dark ground framed by red bands. His head, under a raised gilded halo, tilts towards his right shoulder with a sorrowful expression, and a thin white loincloth is knotted at the centre. Gold side panels show the Virgin in a dark blue mantle and Saint John in a red mantle, each raising a hand to the cheek in grief. The red top panel bears the monogram IC XC, and the ends of the crossbar have been cut away
caption: Berlinghiero, Crucifix from the abbey of San Salvatore at Fucecchio, c. 1230–1235. Tempera and gold on shaped panel, c. 156 × 100 cm (arm terminals detached). Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, inv. 5773. Signed: BERLINGERIUS VULTERRANUS ME PINXIT (recovered during the 1981 restoration).

alt: Gabled gold-ground panel showing a tall, frontal Saint Francis in a dark hooded habit, blessing and holding a book, with stigmata on his hands and feet and a half-length winged angel on each side of his head. Three small narrative scenes run down each side: at upper left the Stigmatization, at upper right Francis beneath a canopy with kneeling laymen; a dated inscription lies between his feet
caption: Bonaventura Berlinghieri, Saint Francis and Six Stories (three from his life, three posthumous miracles), signed and dated 1235. Tempera and gold on panel, c. 160 × 123 cm. Pescia, Church of San Francesco. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Manuscript page with a tall initial P running down the left margin. Its stem is divided into compartments of red and blue with stylised leaves and ends in a curling dragon-like tail; its bowl, in gold and blue, encloses a crowned king in a red mantle who points with his right hand. Red capital letters to the right read PARABOLE SALOMONIS, followed by the text in a Gothic book hand.
caption: Marco di Berlinghiero, initial P with King Solomon, opening of the Book of Proverbs, from the Bible of the hospital of San Martino, completed by 1250. Tempera and gold on parchment. Lucca, Biblioteca Capitolare Feliniana, MS 1. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Painted cross with a living Christ on a deep blue ground, open-eyed beneath a raised gilded halo, his arms outstretched along the crossbar. Gold side panels show the Virgin in a dark blue mantle on the left and Saint John in a red mantle on the right. The terminals of the arms hold the four Evangelist symbols. The top shows the Virgin between two angels and the foot shows small scenes of the Denial of Peter
caption: Christus Triumphans (Cross of Santa Maria degli Angeli), c. 1210–1220. Tempera and gold on shaped panel, 174.7 × 140.5 cm. Lucca, Museo Nazionale di Villa Guinigi, inv. 226; from the monastery of Santa Maria degli Angeli, Lucca. Signed: BERLINGERIUS ME PINXIT. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Painted cross with a slender, living Christ on a dark ground framed by red bands. His head, under a raised gilded halo, tilts towards his right shoulder with a sorrowful expression, and a thin white loincloth is knotted at the centre. Gold side panels show the Virgin in a dark blue mantle and Saint John in a red mantle, each raising a hand to the cheek in grief. The red top panel bears the monogram IC XC, and the ends of the crossbar have been cut away
caption: Crucifix from the abbey of San Salvatore at Fucecchio, c. 1230–1235. Tempera and gold on shaped panel, c. 156 × 100 cm (arm terminals detached). Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, inv. 5773. Signed: BERLINGERIUS VULTERRANUS ME PINXIT (recovered during the 1981 restoration).

alt: Arched gold-ground panel within a raised red frame. The Virgin, in a dark purple mantle marked with gold stars, holds the Christ Child on her right arm and raises her other hand towards him. The Child wears a pale blue tunic and a gold-hatched mantle, holds an open book inscribed in Greek, and looks up at his mother. Both figures wear applied metal crowns
caption: Berlinghiero (Berlinghiero di Melanese), attributed, Madonna and Child, known as the Madonna di sotto gli organi, c. 1220 (before 1226?). Tempera and gold on arched panel, 93 × 55 cm. Pisa, Cathedral, altar of the Madonna di sotto gli organi. Extensively restored in 1789–1790; the crowns are copies made in 1912.

alt: Gold-ground panel with the half-length Virgin in a deep blue mantle edged in orange and marked with gold stars. Her long, narrow face with almond eyes looks out sideways with a melancholy expression. She points with long fingers of her right hand towards the Christ Child, who sits on her left arm in an orange robe hatched with gold, holding a red scroll and raising his right hand in blessing. Red Greek monograms flank the Virgin's head
caption: Madonna and Child, possibly 1230s. Tempera on wood, gold ground; overall 80.3 × 53.7 cm, painted surface 76.2 × 49.5 cm. New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of Irma N. Straus, 1960 (60.173).

alt: Small open triptych on gold ground. In the centre the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle, holds the Christ Child, who embraces her with his cheek pressed to hers, while two angels fly in the upper corners. The left wing shows the Crucifixion of Saint Andrew above Saints Francis and Paul; the right wing shows Christ in a mandorla with the instruments of the Passion above the deacon saints Stephen and Lawrence
caption: Virgin and Child with Saints, triptych (tabernacle), c. 1230s. Tempera and gold on poplar panel; overall 42.6 × 51.5 cm (centre 42.8 × 27 cm; left wing 42.5 × 12.5 cm; right wing 42.4 × 12 cm). Cleveland, The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of the John Huntington Art and Polytechnic Trust, 1966.237.

alt: Arched gold-ground panel in a plain gilded frame. The Virgin, in a dark blue-green mantle with gold stars on her forehead and shoulder and a fringed, striped border, holds the Christ Child on her left arm. The Child, in an orange-red robe, raises his right hand in blessing and holds a small white scroll, while her long-fingered hand rests beneath him. The upper corners retain only worn fragments of painted figures
caption: Workshop of Berlinghiero di Melanese, Central panel of a triptych: Virgin and Child “Hodegetria”; (in the spandrels above) The Annunciation, c. 1225–1250. Tempera and gold leaf on panel, 71.8 × 48.9 cm; frame 84.8 × 59.7 cm. Raleigh, North Carolina Museum of Art, Gift of Wachovia Bank and Trust Company, GL.57.16.1.

alt: Painted cross with a living Christ on a dark blue ground edged with red pearled bands. His head, under a gilded halo, inclines to one side, and he wears a long pink loincloth. Gold side panels show the Virgin in a dark mantle and Saint John in a pink mantle, above small scenes of the Capture of Christ and the Holy Women at the Tomb. At the top Christ blesses between two angels, small winged Evangelist symbols occupy the ends of the arms, and small figures flank the feet
caption: Berlinghieri workshop (attributed to Berlinghiero and his circle, or to Bonaventura Berlinghieri), Painted Cross (Tereglio Cross), c. 1235–1245. Tempera and gold on panel. Tereglio (Coreglia Antelminelli, Lucca), church of Santa Maria Assunta; probably from the church of San Martino at Bori (Alborio). Restored 1998.

alt: Gabled gold-ground panel showing a tall, frontal Saint Francis in a dark hooded habit, blessing and holding a book, with stigmata on his hands and feet and a half-length winged angel on each side of his head. Three small narrative scenes run down each side: at upper left the Stigmatization, at upper right Francis beneath a canopy with kneeling laymen; a dated inscription lies between his feet
caption: Saint Francis and Six Stories (three from his life, three posthumous miracles), 1235. Tempera and gold on panel, c. 160 × 123 cm (151 × 114 cm according to the diocese of Pescia). Pescia, Church of San Francesco. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Gold-ground panel dominated by a dark blue cross on which the dead Christ hangs with bowed head, flanked by two angels. Groups of mourners stand in the upper corners; below are the Way to Calvary at left and the Deposition at right, all within a dark ornamented border
caption: Attributed to Bonaventura Berlinghieri (or Master of the Oblate Cross), Crucifixion with Mourners, the Way to Calvary and the Deposition, right wing of a diptych from Santa Chiara, Lucca, c. 1255–1257. Tempera and gold on panel, 103 × 61 cm. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi, inv. 1890 n. 8575–8576.

alt: Two hinged gold-ground panels side by side. On the left, the Virgin in a deep blue mantle holds the Christ Child cheek to cheek, surrounded by small standing saints, among them two Franciscan friars and the Archangel Michael. On the right, the dead Christ hangs from a blue cross between mourners, above scenes of the Way to Calvary and the Deposition
caption: Attributed to Bonaventura Berlinghieri (or Master of the Oblate Cross), Diptych with the Virgin and Child with Saints and the Crucifixion with Scenes of the Passion, from Santa Chiara, Lucca, c. 1255–1257. Tempera and gold on panel, 103 × 123 cm overall (each wing 103 × 61 cm). Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi, inv. 1890 nos. 8575–8576.

alt: Painted cross with a living, open-eyed Christ in a pink loincloth on a dark ground edged with red, his arms outstretched along the crossbar. The Virgin and Saint John stand full-length in the gold side fields above two small scenes. At the top, a blessing Christ between two angels sits above a red titulus; small figures fill the ends of the crossbar
caption: Circle of Bonaventura Berlinghieri, Crucifix (Triumphant Christ), 1250-60, tempera and gold leaf on wood panel, 286 x 187 x 6 cm, Palazzo Barberini, Roma.

alt: Irregular, worm-eaten fragment of a painted cross showing the head and upper chest of a living Christ. His eyes are open, his long dark hair falls in wavy strands onto his shoulders, and his bearded face is set within a raised gilded halo with empty round sockets for inlays. A strip of blue cross ground survives at the right, and the edges are broken bare wood and gesso
caption: School of Bonaventura Berlinghieri (Lucca), Crucifix (fragment: head and chest of Christ), c. 1245–1255. Tempera and gold on panel, 43 × 34 cm. Avignon, Musée du Petit Palais, inv. Calvet 22812.

alt: Damaged fragment of the end of a painted cross. A long horizontal arm of Christ, modelled in greenish-yellow flesh, lies against a dark blue ground framed by red bands with rows of small circles. The open hand is pierced by a nail wound from which three streams of blood fall. To the right, in the square terminal, a young winged figure with curly hair and a halo, in a red mantle over a blue-green tunic, holds a thin staff and inclines his head sorrowfully
caption: Lucchese or Pisan painter (attributed to Bonaventura Berlinghieri; also given to the Master of Calci), Fragment of a painted cross: left arm of Christ and terminal with a mourning figure (an angel, or Saint John in the Petit Palais notice), mid-13th century. Tempera and gold on panel. Rio de Janeiro, Museu Nacional de Belas Artes.
