caption: Miracles at the Tomb: The St Peter Martyr Wall of the Spanish Chapel, 1366-67, fresco, tempera and plaster, Florence, Santa Maria Novella, Spanish Chapel.

alt: Fresco by Andrea di Bonaiuto showing the paralytic Agata, a young woman in red, rising healed among astonished onlookers and Dominican friars, from the Scenes of the Life of St Peter Martyr, entrance wall of the Spanish Chapel, Santa Maria Novella, Florence, 1366-67
caption: The Healing of the Paralytic Agata: A Posthumous Miracle of St Peter Martyr, 1366-67, fresco, tempera and plaster, Florence, Santa Maria Novella, Spanish Chapel.

alt: Fresco by Andrea di Bonaiuto showing the young St Peter Martyr, haloed and seen from behind, receiving the white Dominican habit from an elderly friar beneath a pink arcade, with friars in black cappas looking on, from the Scenes of the Life of St Peter Martyr, entrance wall of the Spanish Chapel, Santa Maria Novella, Florence, 1366-67
caption: The Investiture of St Peter Martyr: The Young Saint Receives the Dominican Habit, 1366-67, fresco, tempera and plaster, Florence, Santa Maria Novella, Spanish Chapel.

alt: Fresco by Andrea di Bonaiuto showing the martyrdom of St Peter of Verona: an assassin in a pink tunic raises a curved blade over the kneeling, bleeding Dominican saint in a rocky landscape with a dark forest above, from the Scenes of the Life of St Peter Martyr, entrance wall of the Spanish Chapel, Santa Maria Novella, Florence, 1366-67
caption: The Martyrdom of St Peter Martyr, 1366-67, fresco, tempera and plaster, Florence, Santa Maria Novella, Spanish Chapel.

alt: Documentation photograph showing Andrea di Bonaiuto's fresco of the apparition of St Peter Martyr to the sick Rufino di Canapiccio in its setting on the entrance wall of the Spanish Chapel, beside the portal with its iron gate opening onto the Chiostro Verde, above the painted quatrefoil dado, Santa Maria Novella, Florence, 1366-67
caption: St Peter Martyr Appears to the Ailing Rufino, 1366-67, fresco, tempera and plaster, Florence, Santa Maria Novella, Spanish Chapel.

alt: Fresco by Andrea di Bonaiuto showing St Peter Martyr preaching from a wooden pulpit to a dense crowd in a city square, with listeners leaning from the balconies of surrounding palazzi, from the Scenes of the Life of St Peter Martyr, upper entrance wall of the Spanish Chapel, Santa Maria Novella, Florence, 1366-67
caption: St Peter Martyr Preaching (detail), 1366-67, fresco, tempera and plaster, Florence, Santa Maria Novella, Spanish Chapel.

alt: Fresco by Andrea di Bonaiuto showing St Peter Martyr preaching from a wooden pulpit to a dense crowd in a city square, with listeners leaning from the balconies of surrounding palazzi, from the Scenes of the Life of St Peter Martyr, upper entrance wall of the Spanish Chapel, Santa Maria Novella, Florence, 1366-67
caption: St Peter Martyr Preaching, 1366-67, fresco, tempera and plaster, Florence, Santa Maria Novella, Spanish Chapel.

alt: The quadripartite vault of the Spanish Chapel seen from below, with Andrea di Bonaiuto's four frescoed cells — Resurrection, Ascension, Navicella and Pentecost — radiating around the crossing of ribs sheathed in ornamental borders with prophet medallions, Santa Maria Novella, Florence, 1366-67
caption: Four Sails of Heaven: The Vault of the Spanish Chapel, 1366-67, fresco, tempera and plaster, Florence, Santa Maria Novella, Spanish Chapel.

alt: Fresco by Andrea di Bonaiuto showing the Resurrection: Christ rising with a cross banner in a mandorla of golden rays above the empty pink sarcophagus with two seated angels, the three Maries approaching from a city gate, sleeping soldiers below, and the Noli me tangere with the kneeling Magdalene at right, vault cell above the Passion wall, Spanish Chapel, Santa Maria Novella, Florence, 1366-67
caption: The Resurrection Cell of the Vault, 1366-67, fresco, tempera and plaster, Florence, Santa Maria Novella, Spanish Chapel.

alt: Fresco by Andrea di Bonaiuto showing the Ascension: Christ rising in a golden mandorla amid music-making angels, with the Virgin standing at centre in prayer, the apostles kneeling in two groups on the Mount of Olives, and two white-robed angels gesturing at the edges, vault cell above the entrance wall, Spanish Chapel, Santa Maria Novella, Florence, 1366-67
caption: The Ascension Cell of the Vault, 1366-67, fresco, tempera and plaster, Florence, Santa Maria Novella, Spanish Chapel.

alt: Fresco by Andrea di Bonaiuto showing the Navicella: the apostles' ship with a great swollen sail tossed on a dark stormy sea, Christ standing on the water at lower right grasping the sinking St Peter by the wrist, and a fisherman angling on the shore at lower left, vault cell above the east wall, Spanish Chapel, Santa Maria Novella, Florence, 1366-67
caption: The Navicella Cell of the Vault, 1366-67, fresco, tempera and plaster, Florence, Santa Maria Novella, Spanish Chapel.

alt: Fresco by Andrea di Bonaiuto showing the Pentecost: the dove of the Holy Spirit descending toward the praying Virgin and apostles gathered in an open upper loggia, while a crowd of men from many nations in turbans and exotic dress gathers before the closed door below, vault cell above the west wall, Spanish Chapel, Santa Maria Novella, Florence, 1366-67
caption: The Pentecost Cell of the Vault, 1366-67, fresco, tempera and plaster, Florence, Santa Maria Novella, Spanish Chapel.

alt: Portable diptych by Andrea di Bonaiuto showing St Agnes with a haloed lamb and martyr's palm and the crowned St Domitilla holding a disc with the yhs monogram, both in red and gold against punched gold grounds, tempera on panel, c. 1365-1370, Galleria dell'Accademia, Florence
caption: Sts Agnes and Domitilla, 1365–70, tempera and gold on panel with punchwork, portable diptych (two panels joined by metal eyelets), 66 x 28 cm, Florence, Galleria dell'Accademia.

alt: Triptych by Niccolò di Tommaso showing the Mystic Marriage of St Catherine: the enthroned Virgin holds the Christ Child as he places a ring on the finger of the crowned saint, flanked by St John the Baptist with a scroll and St Dominic with book and lily, tempera and gold on panel, third quarter of the 14th century, Palais Fesch, Ajaccio
caption: Niccolò di Tommaso (documented in Florence and Pistoia, 1346–1376), The Mystic Marriage of St Catherine between St John the Baptist and St Dominic, third quarter of the fourteenth century, tempera on panel, 178.5 × 166 cm, Ajaccio, Palais Fesch – musée des beaux-arts.

alt: Long narrow panel by Andrea di Bonaiuto showing the Virgin and Child in a central gabled arch flanked by ten named saints in arcaded compartments with spiral colonnettes on gold ground, including three Dominican saints, three evangelists with their symbols, Catherine, the Magdalene, Gregory and Thomas Becket, egg tempera on poplar, c. 1365-70, National Gallery, London
caption: The Virgin and Child with Ten Saints, 1365–70, egg tempera on wood (probably poplar), 28 × 105.8 cm, in its original fourteenth-century Tuscan frame, London, National Gallery.

alt: Digital reconstruction of a dispersed Florentine portable triptych attributed to the young Andrea di Bonaiuto: the Nativity on the left wing and the Crucifixion on the right wing, both Museum of Fine Arts Houston, flanking the gabled central panel of the Virgin and Child enthroned with saints and angels, Statens Museum for Kunst Copenhagen, tempera and gold on panel, c. 1350-80
caption: Unknown Florentine painter (attributed by Miklós Boskovits to the young Andrea di Bonaiuto), dispersed portable triptych, c. 1350–1380, tempera and gold leaf on panel. Centre: The Virgin and Child Enthroned with Saints and Angels, 47 × 22 cm, Copenhagen, Statens Museum for Kunst, inv. KMS3479. Left wing: The Nativity, 30.1 × 12.9 cm; right wing: Christ on the Cross with the Virgin, Saint John and Saint Mary Magdalen, 30.1 × 12.9 cm; Houston, Museum of Fine Arts, inv. 44.570.1–.2.

alt: Gabled panel attributed to the circle of the Cione, possibly the young Andrea di Bonaiuto, showing the Virgin enthroned in blue pointing to the Christ Child in red, surrounded by four angels and six saints including John the Baptist, a bishop and Anthony Abbot, against tooled gold, centre of a dispersed portable triptych, c. 1350-70, Statens Museum for Kunst, Copenhagen
caption: Circle of the Cione (attributed by Miklós Boskovits to the young Andrea di Bonaiuto), The Virgin and Child Enthroned with Saints and Angels, 1346–79, tempera and gold on panel, 47 x 22 cm, Copenhagen, Statens Museum for Kunst, KMS3479.

alt: Small vertical panel attributed to the young Andrea di Bonaiuto showing the Nativity: the Virgin in blue reclining beside the gold-brocaded manger with the Christ Child, ox and ass behind, Joseph seated in red below, and an angel announcing to shepherds above the stable beam, tempera and gold on wood, c. 1360-80, Museum of Fine Arts, Houston
caption: Unknown Florentine painter (attributed by Miklós Boskovits to the young Andrea di Bonaiuto), The Nativity, 1360–80, tempera and gold leaf on wood, 30.1 × 12.9 cm, Houston, Museum of Fine Arts, The Edith A. and Percy S. Straus Collection, inv. 44.570.1 (left wing of a dispersed portable triptych; centre panel Copenhagen, Statens Museum for Kunst, KMS3479)

alt: Small vertical panel attributed to the young Andrea di Bonaiuto showing the Crucifixion against an unbroken tooled gold ground: Christ on the dark cross, thorn-crowned head sunk toward his right shoulder and blood threading from hands, side and feet, with the Virgin in a blue mantle over an orange gold-patterned gown at left, St John the Evangelist in rose pressing a hand to his cheek and clasping a dark tooled book at right, and the Magdalene in red kneeling at the foot of the cross, her golden hair loose down her back, tempera and gold on wood, c. 1360-80, right wing of a dispersed portable triptych, Museum of Fine Arts, Houston
caption: Unknown Florentine painter (attributed by Miklós Boskovits to the young Andrea di Bonaiuto), Christ on the Cross with the Virgin, Saint John and Saint Mary Magdalen, 1360–80, tempera and gold leaf on wood, 30.1 × 12.9 cm, Houston, Museum of Fine Arts, The Edith A. and Percy S. Straus Collection, inv. 44.570.2 (right wing of a dispersed portable triptych; centre panel Copenhagen, Statens Museum for Kunst, KMS3479).

alt: Small devotional panel attributed to Andrea da Firenze showing Christ crucified against punched gold with blood streaming from his wounds, the star-spangled Virgin in blue at left, St John with a book at right, and the red-cloaked Magdalene kneeling and reaching up to Christ's bleeding feet, tempera and gold on walnut, c. 1360s, Cleveland Museum of Art
caption: The Crucifixion, c. 1360s, tempera and gold on wood (walnut), 31 × 13.4 cm unframed, Cleveland, The Cleveland Museum of Art, Holden Collection, inv. 1916.776.

alt: Five-part polyptych by Andrea di Bonaiuto in the sacristy of Santa Maria del Carmine, Florence, showing the Virgin and Child embracing on a throne with two angels, flanked by St Leonard with fetters, St Nicholas of Bari with crozier and golden balls, John the Baptist pointing, and the prophet Elijah in the white Carmelite mantle holding a scroll, tempera and gold on panel, c. 1360-62
caption: Madonna and Child with Sts Leonard, Nicholas, John the Baptist and the Prophet Elijah, 1360-62, tempera and gold on panel, Florence, Santa Maria del Carmine, sacristy.

alt: The four surviving laterals of a dismembered polyptych attributed to Andrea di Bonaiuto, set side by side in their presumed order against black: St Agnes in a green gown and gold-worked orange mantle cradling a white lamb, St Bartholomew in a white mantle strewn with red flowerets holding a flaying knife and a book, St Nicholas of Bari in a jewelled mitre and orange-gold cope with crozier, and St Elizabeth of Hungary in a rose-violet mantle holding roses, each standing full-length under an ogival arch against tooled gold, mid-1360s, Museum of Fine Arts, Houston
caption: The four surviving laterals of a dismembered polyptych, reassembled in their presumed order: Saints Agnes, Bartholomew, Nicholas of Bari and Elizabeth of Hungary, mid-1360s, tempera and gold leaf on panel, each c. 87 × 29 cm, Houston, Museum of Fine Arts, inv. 44.557, 44.556, 44.559 and 44.558. The central compartment, almost certainly a Virgin and Child, has never been identified; the four panels entered Houston with the Straus bequest of 1944.

alt: Tall gabled panel attributed to Andrea di Bonaiuto showing St Agnes standing in a green gown and gold-worked orange mantle, cradling a white lamb against a tooled gold ground, lateral of a dismembered polyptych, mid-1360s, Museum of Fine Arts, Houston
caption: Saint Agnes, mid-1360s, tempera and gold leaf on panel, 86.2 × 28.9 cm, Houston, Museum of Fine Arts, inv. 44.557.

alt: Tall gabled panel attributed to Andrea di Bonaiuto showing the apostle St Bartholomew standing frontally in a white mantle strewn with red and gold flowerets, holding a flaying knife upright and a dark book, against tooled gold, lateral of a dismembered polyptych, mid-1360s, Museum of Fine Arts, Houston
caption: Saint Bartholomew, mid-1360s, tempera and gold leaf on panel, 87.2 × 29.1 cm, Houston, Museum of Fine Arts, inv. 44.556.

alt: Tall gabled panel attributed to Andrea di Bonaiuto showing St Nicholas of Bari standing in a jewelled white mitre and orange-gold brocaded cope with a dark jewelled orphrey, holding a crozier and a gem-studded book, against tooled gold, lateral of a dismembered polyptych, mid-1360s, Museum of Fine Arts, Houston
caption: Saint Nicholas of Bari, mid-1360s, tempera and gold leaf on panel, 86.2 × 28.6 cm, Houston, Museum of Fine Arts, inv. 44.559.

alt: Tall gabled panel attributed to Andrea di Bonaiuto showing St Elizabeth of Hungary crowned and veiled in a deep crimson mantle, holding roses gathered in a fold of her mantle, against tooled gold, lateral of a dismembered polyptych, mid-1360s, Museum of Fine Arts, Houston
caption: Saint Elizabeth of Hungary, mid-1360s, tempera and gold leaf on panel, 87.2 × 28.9 cm, Houston, Museum of Fine Arts, inv. 44.558.

alt: Central panel of a portable triptych attributed to Andrea di Bonaiuto in its original gabled Gothic frame with a roundel of the blessing Redeemer, showing the Virgin and Child with two angels and four saints including St Peter with keys above a Nativity with the Virgin and Joseph kneeling around the Child; Left wing showing the kneeling angel of the Annunciation above the Adoration of the Magi, with the eldest king kneeling at the Child's feet and Joseph seated pensively below; Right wing showing the seated Virgin Annunciate above a Crucifixion with the swooning Virgin among the holy women, St John, and the Magdalene in yellow kneeling at the foot of the cross, tempera and gold on panel, Pushkin Museum, Moscow
caption: The Virgin and Child Enthroned with Saints and Angels; the Annunciation, the Nativity, the Adoration of the Magi and the Crucifixion, third quarter of the fourteenth century, tempera and gold on panel, 95 × 69.8 cm overall with the original carpentry; central field 61 × 34.5 cm, each wing 61 × 17.3 cm, Moscow, Pushkin State Museum of Fine Arts, inv. Ж-230.

alt: Left half of a predella compartment attributed to Andrea di Bonaiuto showing St Paul half-length in a white-bordered quatrefoil, bald with a long dark beard, raising a sword and holding a red book, tempera on poplar, 1370-77, Pinacoteca Vaticana; Right half of a predella compartment attributed to Andrea di Bonaiuto showing St Michael the Archangel half-length in a quatrefoil, with red wings, a lance, and a tall white shield bearing a red cross, tempera on poplar, 1370-77, Pinacoteca Vaticana
caption: Sts Paul and Michael the Archangel, predella compartment, 1370–1377, tempera on poplar panel, 19.5 × 39.5 cm, Vatican City, Pinacoteca Vaticana, inv. MV.40115.2.1.

alt: Small devotional panel attributed to Andrea di Bonaiuto showing the Crucifixion against a dark blue ground: Christ on the cross between two mourning angels, the Virgin in a rose mantle and St John the Evangelist below, and a tonsured Dominican friar in black cappa kneeling and embracing the foot of the cross, tempera and gold on panel, 1370-77, Pinacoteca Vaticana
caption: Crucifixion with the Virgin, St John the Evangelist and a Dominican Friar, 1370–1377, tempera and gold on panel, 32.5 × 22.2 cm, Vatican City, Pinacoteca Vaticana, inv. MV.40118.0.0.

alt: Nativity and Annunciation to the Shepherds
caption: Nativity and Annunciation to the Shepherds, 1340-47, fresco, south wall of the Cappella dell'Annunciazione (formerly the Strozzi funerary chapel), Chiostro dei Morti, convent of Santa Maria Novella, Florence.

alt: The Crucifixion with the Swooning Virgin and the Witnesses of Golgotha
caption: The Crucifixion with the Swooning Virgin and the Witnesses of Golgotha, 1340-47, fresco, west wall of the Cappella dell'Annunciazione (formerly the Strozzi funerary chapel), Chiostro dei Morti, convent of Santa Maria Novella, Florence.

alt: The Expulsion of the Duke of Athens
caption: The Expulsion of the Duke of Athens, 1343–1349, fresco, transferred (strappo, 1964); circular field, diameter c. 300 cm, originally on a wall of the Carcere delle Stinche, Florence; now Museo di Palazzo Vecchio, Florence.

alt: Triptych with the Virgin and Child, and Saints Mary Magdalene and Ansanus
caption: Triptych with the Virgin and Child, and Saints Mary Magdalene and Ansanus, 1350, tempera and gold on panel, with integral gilded frame, overall 146 × 119.5 × 8 cm; central panel 91 × 47.5 cm; right panel 82.5 × 30.5 cm; left panel 82 × 24.5 cm, Amsterdam, Rijksmuseum.

alt: Portable tabernacle (folding triptych) with the Crucifixion and three hagiographic scenes
caption: Portable tabernacle (folding triptych) with the Crucifixion and three hagiographic scenes, 1340–1345, tempera and gold on panel, with engaged and gilded frame; iron pin hinges, Newark, Delaware, Alana Collection.

alt: Virgin and Child enthroned with two music-making angels; Saints Andrew, Nicholas of Bari, John the Baptist and James the Greater
caption: Virgin and Child enthroned with two music-making angels; Saints Andrew, Nicholas of Bari, John the Baptist and James the Greater, 1353–1355, tempera and gold on panel, Florence, Galleria dell'Accademia, from the basilica of Santissima Annunziata, chapel of the Del Palagio family.

alt: Pentecost
caption: Pentecost, 1362–1365, tempera and silver leaf and gold on panel, 195 × 287 cm, Florence, Galleria dell'Accademia, probably from the high altar of the church of Santi Apostoli, Florence.

alt: Hell
caption: Hell, dated variously c. 1345, c. 1350 or 1360–65 — unresolved fresco, detached; six fragments surviving, originally on the wall of the right (south) aisle of the nave, Basilica di Santa Croce, Florence, now Florence, Museo dell'Opera di Santa Croce, in the refectory (Cenacolo).

alt: Triumph of Death at Santa Croce
caption: Triumph of Death, fragments dated variously c. 1345, c. 1350 or c. 1360–65; unresolved fresco, detached, originally on the wall of the right (south) aisle of the nave, Basilica di Santa Croce, Florence, now Florence, Museo dell'Opera di Santa Croce, refectory (Cenacolo).

alt: The Last Supper
caption: Crucifixion and Last Supper, 1360–1365/66, fresco, in situ East wall of the former refectory (Cenacolo) of the Augustinian convent of Santo Spirito, Florence; now Fondazione Salvatore Romano.

alt: The Strozzi Altarpiece
caption: Christ in Glory with the Virgin, the Baptist and Saints; predella with the Mass of Saint Thomas Aquinas, Saint Peter Saved from the Waters, and the Death of the Emperor Henry II Contracted 1354; signed and dated 1357, tempera and gold on panel; five compartments with a three-scene predella, Florence, Basilica di Santa Maria Novella, Cappella Strozzi di Mantova (left transept), in situ on its original altar.

alt: The Tabernacle of Orsanmichele
caption: Orcagna with a team of sculptors and masons, Tabernacle of Orsanmichele, contracted 1349, executed 1352–1359; signed and dated 1359, marble, with inlay of gold, coloured glass and mosaic tesserae; bronze (door leaf and grille); painted and gilded elements; the cloth curtain now lost, 1042 × 610 cm, Florence, Orsanmichele.

alt: Crucifixion and Last Supper
caption: Crucifixion and Last Supper, 1360–1365/66, fresco, in situ, occupying the entire east wall of former refectory (Cenacolo) of the Augustinian convent of Santo Spirito, Florence; now the Fondazione Salvatore Romano.

alt: Saint Matthew and stories from his life
caption: Andrea di Cione, called Orcagna, and Jacopo di Cione, with workshop (the so-called Master of the Ashmolean Predella), Saint Matthew and stories from his life, 1367–1368, tempera and gold on panel, 291 × 265 cm, Florence, Galleria degli Uffizi, painted for a pillar of Orsanmichele, Florence.

alt: The Crucifixion with the Virgin, the Magdalene and Saint John: The Fresco of Santa Marta
caption: Orcagna school [?], Crucifixion, 1343- 1355 [C], fresco, in situ, fragmentary Church of the monastery of Santa Marta (a Montughi), via Santa Marta, Florence: above the altar, on the wall dividing the church from the nuns' choir.

alt: The Crucifixion: The Pinnacle of a Camaldolese Altarpiece
caption: museum attribution; contested among the Cione brothers and Don Silvestro dei Gherarducci, The Crucifixion, c. 1365, tempera on wood, gold ground; 137.5 × 81.9 cm, including the later frame, New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Robert Lehman Collection, The six angels in the frame: Jacopo di Cione.

alt: The Throne of Grace: A Florentine Panel of the Trinity
caption: Throne of Grace (Thronus Gratiae), 1340s, also described as second quarter of the fourteenth century, tempera and gold on wood, with engaged and gilded frame, Warsaw, Muzeum Narodowe, on deposit from a private collection.

alt: Gabled gold-ground panel of the Annunciation by Andrea di Nerio: at left, the angel Gabriel kneels in golden robes in a blue starred vaulted room, holding a dark branch; at right, beyond a twisted column, the Virgin in a dark mantle sits on a chequered bench with her hand on her breast and a book in her lap; in the gable, a divine figure in a red glory sends an angel, while another angel flies down and the dove of the Holy Spirit descends towards Mary.
caption: Annunciation, c. 1350. Tempera and gold on panel. Arezzo, Museo Diocesano di Arte Sacra (MuDAS), from the destroyed church of San Marco a Murello, Arezzo.

alt: Gabled gold-ground panel by Andrea di Nerio showing the half-length Virgin facing the viewer in a dark mantle marked with a gold star over an orange-red gown, holding on her left arm the Christ Child in a pale rose tunic dotted with red rosettes, who grasps her raised right hand and lifts his other hand with open palm.
caption: Virgin and Child (the "Madonna Sarti"), c. 1330. Tempera, gold and silver on panel, 80 × 62 cm. Paris, Galerie G. Sarti. Provenance: London, Colnaghi (1954–1955); Oxnead Hall, Norwich (Norfolk), collection of Mrs Jeremy Harris (1971).

alt: Small gabled gold-ground panel showing the Virgin enthroned frontally, in a white veil and dark mantle with a pale cloth over her knees, holding the Christ Child in a mauve robe on her knee; at the sides of the throne stand two haloed nuns in black habits and white wimples, and below them sit two youthful haloed saints in orange and red.
caption: Andrea di Nerio (attributed), Virgin and Child Enthroned with Four Saints, early 14th century. Tempera on panel, 41.9 × 32.4 cm. Baltimore, Baltimore Museum of Art, Bequest of Saidie A. May, inv. 1951.392.

alt: Fresco on a round church pier showing two standing saints against a dark ground: on the left, Saint Francis in a brown hooded habit with a knotted cord, raising a hand marked with the stigmata and holding a red book; on the right, a taller Saint Dominic in a white habit and black hooded cloak, holding a sprig of lily and a red book.
caption: Andrea di Nerio (attributed), Saints Francis and Dominic, c. 1350. Fresco. Arezzo, Pieve di Santa Maria.

alt: Small gold-ground panel of the birth of Saint John the Baptist: the aged Elizabeth sits up in a bed with a striped coverlet while two attendants bring her a bowl and a jug; in the foreground the Virgin in a blue mantle holds the haloed newborn John, who reaches towards an old woman seated opposite; on the right a pale Gothic building opens the room.
caption: The Nativity of Saint John the Baptist, c. 1350. Tempera and gold on panel, 29 × 39 cm. Paris, Musée du Louvre (MI 385), on deposit at the Musée du Petit Palais, Avignon.

alt: Small gold-ground panel: Saint John the Baptist, barefoot in a camel-hair garment and rose mantle, stands at the centre holding a slender cross-staff and points to a white lamb with a red-cross banner on a hill at left, while a group of bearded listeners in red, yellow and pale robes gathers at right.
caption: The Sermon of Saint John the Baptist, c. 1350. Tempera and gold on poplar panel, 31.3 × 44.5 cm. Bern, Kunstmuseum, Bequest of Adolf von Stürler, Versailles (inv. G 0882).

alt: Small gold-ground panel: on the right, a tall angel in a pink robe with gold roundels leads the haloed boy John the Baptist, dressed in a dark tunic, by the hand and points the way; on the left, beside a grove of slender trees, a second angel in a pale robe waits holding a camel-hair garment.
caption: Saint John the Baptist as a Boy Led into the Wilderness, c. 1350. Tempera and gold on poplar panel, 31.5 × 44.5 cm. Bern, Kunstmuseum, Bequest of Adolf von Stürler, Versailles (inv. G 0881).

alt: Damaged fresco arranged around a central enthroned Virgin in a white mantle holding the Christ Child in a Gothic niche; on the left, scenes of Saint Christopher carrying the Child across a river, standing amid arrows suspended in the air, and lying beheaded before soldiers; on the right, scenes of Saint James the Greater, including a beheading before soldiers and his disciples laying his body in a boat.
caption: Virgin and Child with Stories of Saints Christopher and James the Greater, 1340–60. Fresco. Arezzo, Cathedral of Santi Pietro e Donato, Cappella Bertoldini.

alt: Fresco in two fields on a dark red ground: on the left, Christ stands in the Jordan with arms crossed over his chest while John the Baptist in a rose mantle raises his arm above his head and two angels in white hold his red garment; on the right, the Virgin sits on a gilded Gothic throne and the Christ Child on her lap places a ring on the finger of Saint Catherine, who kneels in a white mantle.
caption: Andrea di Nerio and Spinello Aretino (attributed), The Baptism of Christ and The Mystic Marriage of Saint Catherine of Alexandria, c. 1370. Fresco. Arezzo, San Francesco, Cappella Gozzari.

alt: Damaged fresco: on the left, Saint Francis in a brown habit stands in an arched niche, holding a red book and raising a hand marked with the stigmata; on the right, in a cell with walls of square panels and a narrow window, the Virgin in a dark mantle sits on a gilded Gothic throne and gestures towards Saint John of Damascus, seated in a lilac robe at a desk with an open book, his face lost to damage.
caption: Andrea di Nerio and Spinello Aretino (attributed), The Virgin and Saint Francis Comforting Saint John of Damascus in Prison, c. 1370. Fresco. Arezzo, San Francesco, Cappella Gozzari.

alt: Damaged fresco of a wooded mountain landscape: at left, Saint Francis kneels before a small church with a bell-cote and raised hands, his head lost to damage; a red-winged crucified seraph appears in the sky at upper right, and a friar at a doorway on the right shields his eyes; a woman in black kneels in prayer at lower left, and two circular consecration crosses are painted over the sky.
caption: Andrea di Nerio and Spinello Aretino (attributed), The Stigmatisation of Saint Francis, second half of the 14th century. Fresco. Arezzo, San Francesco, Cappella Gozzari.

alt: Fresco of Saint Michael the Archangel standing frontally in a painted Gothic niche with pinnacles and twisted columns, wearing pale blue armour under a rose mantle lined with green, with large golden wings, holding a long sword diagonally across his body; a small donor in red with a white headdress kneels in prayer at his feet.
caption: Andrea di Nerio and Spinello Aretino (attributed), Saint Michael the Archangel, c. 1370. Fresco. 254 x 103 cm. Arezzo, San Francesco, Cappella Gozzari.

alt: Fresco of the Annunciation within painted Gothic architecture: at left, the angel Gabriel in a lilac mantle with green and gold wings arrives with his hand on his breast; at centre, a vase with a flowering plant stands on a red tiled floor; at right, the Virgin in a blue mantle stands with crossed hands beneath a Gothic canopy beside a lectern with an open book; above, a divine figure in a glory of red seraphim sends a kneeling angel.
caption: Andrea di Nerio and Spinello Aretino (attributed), The Annunciation, c. 1370. Fresco. Arezzo, San Francesco, Cappella Gozzari.

alt: South Door of Florence Baptistery
caption: South Door of Florence Baptistery, 1330-36, gilded bronze, 494 x 295 cm, Museo dell'Opera del Duomo, Florence.

alt: Tomb of Archbishop Simone Saltarelli
caption: Tomb of Archbishop Simone Saltarelli, 1342-43, white marble, church of Santa Caterina d'Alessandria, Pisa.

alt: Christ Blessing
caption: Christ Blessing, 1330-43, marble, Museo dell'Opera del Duomo, Florence.

alt: Saint Reparata
caption: Saint Reparata, 1330-43, marble, 71 x 24 x 21 cm, Museo dell'Opera del Duomo, Florence.

alt: Madonna del latte
caption: Madonna del Latte (with his son Nino), 1343-48, marble with traces of original polychromy and gilding, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, Pisa.

alt: Madonna della Rosa
caption: Madonna della Rosa (with his son Nino), 1345-48, marble with surviving traces of polychromy and gilding, church of Santa Maria della Spina (presbytery), Pisa.

alt: Madonna with Child
caption: Madonna with Child (with Nino?), 1345-49, marble, Museo dell'Opera del Duomo, Pisa.

alt: Madonna with Child
caption: Madonna with Child, c. 1335, marble, 48,5 x 19 x 16,5 cm (without octagonal plinth), Staatliche Museen zu Berlin.

alt: Madonna with Child
caption: Madonna with Child, 1330-40, marble with traces of gilding, Base: 5 x 15.9 x 15.1 cm; without base: 32.7 x 15 x 9.6 cm, The Cleveland Museum of Art, Cleveland.

alt: Upright panel with a pointed top and a gold ground. Saint Catherine of Alexandria is shown at half length, frontally, with long wavy fair hair and a tall crown of gold set with red and black stones over a large punched halo. She wears a red mantle patterned with small dark motifs, fastened at the chest with a large round gold clasp bearing an inscription, over a white and blue dress. With both hands she holds a closed book with red ties, and in her left hand a dark green palm. In the foreground before her stands a large spiked wheel in ochre and yellow.
caption: Bartolomeo Bulgarini, Saint Catherine of Alexandria, c. 1335/1340, lateral panel of a polyptych from the church of San Cerbone, Lucca. Tempera on panel, painted surface 73.5 × 41 cm; overall 73.5 × 42 × 1 cm. Washington, National Gallery of Art, Samuel H. Kress Collection, 1943.4.20. National Gallery of Art, Washington, open access, CC0.

alt: Small panel with a pointed gable in a gilded frame. The Virgin, in a dark blue mantle over a gold dress, sits frontally on a throne before a cloth of honour of red and gold brocade, held up at the top by two angels in blue with joined hands. On her lap the Child, in a blue tunic over orange sleeves, holds a small bird and looks up at her. Two angels in dark garments with gold haloes stand behind the throne at the sides. In front, at the left, stands a young female saint in a blue dress and red mantle holding a palm; at the right Saint John the Baptist, in a camel-hair garment and an orange mantle, holds a scroll. The throne stands on a marbled step, and in the gable is a round gilded boss.
caption: Bartolomeo Bulgarini, Virgin and Child Enthroned with Four Angels, a Female Martyr and Saint John the Baptist, c. 1340–1345. Tempera and gold on panel. Madrid, Museo Nacional Thyssen-Bornemisza. Photo: Daderot, public domain (CC0), via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Three arched panels with gold grounds, shown side by side. In the taller central panel Saint Peter, with short grey curly hair and beard, sits frontally on a throne with a patterned cushion, wearing a red tunic, an orange mantle and a pallium embroidered with crosses; he holds a red book on his knee and a key in his right hand. At the left Saint Paul, bald and with a long dark beard, in a blue tunic and a red mantle, holds a sword and a book. At the right Saint John the Evangelist, old and bald with a white beard, in a red mantle over a grey garment, holds an open book with writing.
caption: Bartolomeo Bulgarini, Saint Peter Enthroned between Saints Paul and John the Evangelist (triptych from Sestano), before 1350. Tempera and gold on panel. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Tall panel in a gilded frame with a pointed gable and an inner round arch. Inside a shelter of pale blue architecture with thin white columns, the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle over a red dress, sits at the centre with her hands crossed on her breast; her halo is inscribed. At the left Saint Joseph, in an orange mantle, sits with his hand at his chin; behind him the ox and the ass look over a wooden manger in which the swaddled Child lies. In the foreground stand a gold ewer and basin. At the right a shepherd with a staff kneels and looks towards the Virgin; above him a hand and part of a second figure are cut off by the edge. At the top, God the Father appears among red seraphim, a white dove descends towards the manger, and two groups of angels with gold wings hover at the sides.
caption: Bartolomeo Bulgarini, The Adoration of the Shepherds (also known as The Nativity), c. 1350, central panel of the altarpiece of the altar of Saint Victor, Siena Cathedral. Tempera on panel, 172.4 × 123.2 cm; frame 212.7 × 142.2 cm. Cambridge, Mass., Harvard Art Museums/Fogg Museum, Friends of the Fogg Art Museum Fund and Henry Goldman Fund, 1917.89. Image © President and Fellows of Harvard College, for non-commercial educational use.

alt: Tall narrow panel with a gold ground under a cusped arch, in a gilded frame with a gable and pilasters. A young haloed saint with curly fair hair and a short beard stands frontally. He wears a long pink tunic with gold buttons and a gold belt, lined with grey-white fur, under a red cloak with a blue lining thrown over his shoulders, and blue hose. In his right hand he holds an olive branch with dark fruit, and with his left he holds a sword in a black scabbard decorated with gold, its point resting on the ground, which is painted as pink stone.
caption: Bartolomeo Bulgarini or Master of the Palazzo Venezia Madonna, Saint Victor, c. 1350, before 1351, lateral panel of the altarpiece of the altar of Saint Victor, Siena Cathedral. Tempera and gold on wood, 158 × 47.5 cm. Copenhagen, Statens Museum for Kunst, KMS3625; gift, 1923. Statens Museum for Kunst, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Tall narrow panel with a gold ground under a cusped arch, in a gilded frame with a gable and pilasters. A young haloed female saint with fair hair bound by a band stands frontally, slightly turned to the left. She wears a dress of gold brocade and a large blue mantle lined with pink and red, edged with gold borders, which falls in broad folds to the ground. In her hands she holds a gold crown set with stones and two blue palm fronds.
caption: Bartolomeo Bulgarini or Master of the Palazzo Venezia Madonna, Saint Corona, before 1351, lateral panel of the altarpiece of the altar of Saint Victor, Siena Cathedral. Tempera and gold on wood, 155 × 48 cm. Copenhagen, Statens Museum for Kunst, KMS3624; gift, 1923. Statens Museum for Kunst, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Horizontal predella panel with a gold ground. At the centre Christ hangs dead on a tall cross. At the left a group of holy women in blue, pink and yellow mantles supports the fainting Virgin, while a woman with long fair hair turns towards her; behind them an old man looks on, and on a dark hill with trees soldiers on horseback carry spears. At the right of the cross Saint John the Evangelist, in a pink and blue mantle, stands with his head bowed. Further right a centurion on a white horse raises his arm towards the cross, surrounded by soldiers with spears, a red banner and a group of bearded men in turbans and hoods.
caption: Bartolomeo Bulgarini, The Crucifixion, c. 1350, central panel of the predella of the altarpiece of the altar of Saint Victor, Siena Cathedral. Tempera on gold ground on panel, 43.6 × 77 cm; with frame 61 × 92.4 cm. Paris, Musée du Louvre, INV 312; acquired in 1828 from the collection of Pierre Révoil. © Musée du Louvre, image for non-commercial educational use.

alt: Almost square predella panel. In front of a pink building with pointed arches and a gold ground behind, a judge in a red and white robe leans over a balustrade at the top and points down. Below, Saint Victor, haloed, in a blue mantle over a red robe, is held by an executioner in a pale blue tunic, who embraces him and puts out his eyes; two soldiers in brown armour and blue helmets, one with a club, stand at the left, and two soldiers with spears and a red shield stand at the right. At the far right a group of onlookers in yellow, blue and red mantles, with white veils and turbans, turn towards each other. The floor is pale green.
caption: Bartolomeo Bulgarini, The Blinding of Saint Victor, c. 1351, panel of the predella of the altarpiece of the altar of Saint Victor, Siena Cathedral. Mixed technique on poplar, 41 × 39.6 cm. Frankfurt am Main, Städel Museum, inv. 2135; gift of Robert von Hirsch in memory of Georg Swarzenski, 1977. Städel Museum, Frankfurt am Main, public domain.

alt: Small tall panel with a steep pointed gable in its engaged gilded frame. Against a gold ground, before a low wall with panels, the Virgin sits on a cushion on the ground, in a blue mantle over a gold brocaded dress, with a white veil. She inclines her head and holds an open book in her left hand, while with her right arm she embraces the Christ Child, who stands beside her in a short pink tunic with a blue belt and suckles at her breast. Above, a column of dark blue seraphim descends, and in a quatrefoil at the top of the gable is the bust of Christ in profile.
caption: Bartolomeo Bulgarini, Madonna of Humility, c. 1353, probably one wing of a diptych. Tempera on panel, 57 × 24.5 cm with engaged frame. Amsterdam, Rijksmuseum, SK-A-4002. Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam, public domain.

alt: Upright painted wooden cover in two parts, joined by a dark iron band. Above, under a gilded vault decorated with foliage, four coats of arms hang in a row. Below them, in a plain room with ochre walls, two men sit behind a long counter: at the left a man in a red hood over a dark garment points with his finger; at the right a man in a dark blue robe and a red cap raises one hand and opens a chest beside him with the other. On the counter lie two strapped books, an inkwell with a pen, a sheet of paper and two piles of coins, one dark and one gold. Below the iron band a long inscription in large black Gothic capitals on a white ground fills the lower half of the cover.
caption: Attributed to Bartolomeo Bulgarini, Biccherna cover with the Camarlingo and his Scribe in their Office, January–June 1353. Tempera and gold on panel. Siena, Archivio di Stato, Biccherna no. 17. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Tall panel with a pointed arch, almost entirely gold. At the centre the Virgin sits frontally with joined hands, wrapped in a mantle and dress of gold brocade patterned with small motifs, her face framed by a white veil; behind her a cusped mandorla of gold is set with red seraphim. Around and below her, crowds of angels in gold garments with gold wings fly in tiers, some playing instruments, among them a tambourine and a lute. At the bottom centre the apostle Thomas, in a blue tunic and a pink mantle, is seen from behind with his arms raised towards the Virgin. In the spandrels above the arch, at either side, groups of prophets and saints with scrolls look on.
caption: Bartolomeo Bulgarini, The Assumption of the Virgin with Saint Thomas Receiving the Girdle, early 1360s, from Santa Maria della Scala, Siena. Tempera and gold on panel, 205 × 112 cm. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale, no. 61. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small panel in an elaborate gilded tabernacle frame with a steep gable, crockets, finials and twisted columns. In the gable, in a trefoil, Christ blesses and holds an open book. Below, under a cusped arch with a dark blue starred vault, the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle, sits on a throne covered with a gold-patterned red cloth and holds the Child in pink, who turns towards her. Five angels look over the back of the throne. At the left stand Saint Paul with a sword and a book and, in front, a female saint in red and blue holding an ointment jar, the Magdalen; at the right Saint Peter with a key and, in front, Saint Catherine of Alexandria with her wheel. In narrow panels at the sides, under the arch, stand Saint John the Evangelist and Saint Anthony Abbot at the left, Saint John the Baptist and a bishop saint at the right. The throne stands on a step above a patterned floor.
caption: Bartolomeo Bulgarini, The Virgin and Child Enthroned with Saints and Angels, 1355–1360, centre of a portable triptych whose wings are in the Philadelphia Museum of Art. Gold and tempera on panel, 65 × 46 × 10.5 cm. Boston, Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, P15n8. Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, Boston, www.gardnermuseum.org, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

alt: Two small wings of a triptych framed together in a gilded frame, divided into compartments against a gold ground. At the top left the angel of the Annunciation kneels in a lilac robe with spread wings, holding a scroll inscribed with the angelic salutation; at the top right the Virgin Annunciate sits in a dark blue mantle beside a vase of lilies, her hand at her face, with a book on a bench. Between them, a painted ornament with crossed keys. Below, in eight compartments, standing saints: at the left Andrew with his cross and a book, a bishop in mitre and red cope with a crozier, Dominic in black and white with a lily and a book, and Francis in a grey-brown habit looking up at a seraph; at the right Bartholomew with a knife and a red book in a violet mantle, Lawrence in a deacon's blue and gold dalmatic, Lucy with a dish and a sword, and Agatha in pink with a dish and pincers.
caption: Bartolomeo Bulgarini, Annunciate Angel, the Apostle Andrew, a Bishop Saint (Savinus?), and Saints Dominic and Francis of Assisi (left wing); Virgin Annunciate and Saints Bartholomew, Lawrence, Lucy and Agatha (right wing), c. 1355–1360, wings of a portable triptych whose centre is in the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, Boston. Tempera and tooled gold on panel, 63.8 × 42.9 cm (framed together). Philadelphia Museum of Art, John G. Johnson Collection, 1917, Cat. 92. Image: Philadelphia Museum of Art, for educational use.

alt: Tall panel with a pointed arch carved with tracery, framed by pilasters with twisted colonnettes. The crowned Virgin sits frontally on a large white marble throne with a gabled back, covered with a red and gold cloth. She wears a deep blue mantle that falls to the floor over a dress striped in white and gold, and raises her right hand. On her left knee sits the Child in a gold brocaded tunic, holding a small scroll and looking out at the viewer. Around the gable of the throne crowd ten angels with golden curls and haloes, their hands joined or crossed, and two further angels stand at the sides of the throne. In the spandrels above the arch, smaller angels appear in rows against the gold.
caption: Bartolomeo Bulgarini, Madonna and Child Enthroned with Angels, c. 1355–1360, probably the central panel of the polyptych from Santa Maria della Scala whose lateral saints are in the Uffizi. Tempera and gold on panel. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale, no. 76 (?). Photo: Fabrizio Garrisi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Two tall narrow panels side by side, each with a gold ground under a carved cusped arch, and below each a small compartment with a half-length figure in a quatrefoil. In the left panel Saint Peter, with grey curly hair and beard, wears an orange mantle over a pink robe and holds a blue book and a large gold key; the name S. PETRUS is inscribed at his feet. In the right panel Saint John the Baptist, gaunt, with long dark hair and a camel-hair garment under a red mantle tied with a blue belt, points upwards and holds a scroll inscribed ECCE AGNUS DEI; his name is inscribed at his feet. In the quatrefoil below Peter is a haloed bearded apostle with a red book, perhaps James the Great; below John is a bald bearded saint with a book and a sword, Saint Paul.
caption: Bartolomeo Bulgarini, Saint Peter and Saint John the Baptist, with half-length saints below, c. 1355–1360, lateral panels of a polyptych from the hospital church of Santa Maria della Scala, Siena. Tempera and gold on panel; Saint Peter 167 × 44 cm, Saint John the Baptist 168 × 43.5 cm. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi, inv. 1890 nos. 6136 and 6137. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons; reproduction subject to the Italian Code of Cultural Heritage (D.Lgs. 42/2004).

alt: Damaged panel with a round-arched top and a carved cusped arch. The Virgin, at half length, in a dark blue mantle over a red dress, holds the Child on her left arm and inclines her head towards him; her halo is richly punched. The Child, in a lilac mantle, turns his face up to her and pulls at the white edge of her veil. Behind them hangs a red cloth of honour patterned with green and gold scrolls. Above, in the lobes of the arch, two angels with joined hands look down. At the bottom the seat of the throne, covered with a patterned cloth, is visible at the sides. Large areas of paint are lost, especially in the Virgin's mantle and at the edges, where the bare wood and preparation show.
caption: Bartolomeo Bulgarini, Virgin and Child Enthroned with Two Angels, c. 1355–1360, central panel of a polyptych whose lateral saints are in the Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, Pisa. Tempera, gold and silver on panel, 69.3 × 60.1 cm; picture surface 67.2 × 56.4 cm. New Haven, Yale University Art Gallery, Bequest of Maitland F. Griggs, B.A. 1896, 1943.244. Yale University Art Gallery, public domain (CC0).

alt: Rectangular panel with a main field and a predella. Under a trilobed arch carried by two twisted white columns, against a dark blue ground scattered with small gold stars, the Virgin sits low on the ground, turned three-quarters to the left, wrapped in a light blue mantle with a gold border over a red dress. Gold rays spread from her head. On her lap she holds the Child, wrapped in an orange-yellow cloth, who sucks at her breast while turning his eyes towards the viewer. The ground beneath her is dark brown, flecked with gold. Gold capital letters run in short lines at either side of the field. In the spandrels above the arch, set in a geometric inlaid pattern, are the angel of the Annunciation at the left and the Virgin Annunciate at the right. A frieze of inlay and rosettes frames three sides, and the bare wood of the support is visible around the edges. The predella has three compartments: at the centre the instruments of the Passion before a pale wall, with a column, a ladder, a lance, scourges and a vessel; at the left a group of kneeling men; at the right a group of kneeling women; each group is led by two figures in white hooded habits.
caption: Bartolomeo da Camogli, Madonna of Humility, signed and dated 1346. Tempera and gold on panel. Palermo, Galleria Regionale della Sicilia, Palazzo Abatellis. Photo: Fabrizio Garrisi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (cropped).

alt: Detail of the upper part of the panel. At the centre, the top of the trilobed arch encloses a dark blue ground with gold stars and the gold rays around the head of the Virgin, whose blue veil appears at the bottom edge. At either side, the spandrels are filled with a pattern of small squares and diamonds in blue, white and gold. In the left spandrel an angel with pale wings and a gold halo kneels in a white robe, raising one arm towards the right. In the right spandrel the Virgin, in a blue mantle with a gold halo, sits on a bench before a lectern with an open book, her head bowed towards a ray of light that descends from the upper left.
caption: Bartolomeo da Camogli, Madonna of Humility, 1346, detail of the spandrels with the Annunciation. Palermo, Galleria Regionale della Sicilia, Palazzo Abatellis. Photo: Fabrizio Garrisi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (detail).

alt: Detail of the predella, a long horizontal strip divided into three compartments. In the central compartment, before a pale wall, stand a column with a rope tied round it, a tall lance, a crossbar on a post from which hang two scourges and a dark bowl or bucket, a ladder at the right, and smaller objects along the top, among them a bird. In the left compartment a crowd of men in long robes of white, grey and blue kneels towards the centre, led by two figures in white habits with tall pointed hoods covering their faces. In the right compartment two similar hooded figures kneel in front with joined hands, followed by a crowd of women in white veils, one in a black mantle and one in a red mantle. The paint surface is crossed by cracks and worn.
caption: Bartolomeo da Camogli, Madonna of Humility, 1346, detail of the predella. Palermo, Galleria Regionale della Sicilia, Palazzo Abatellis. Photo: Fabrizio Garrisi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (detail).

alt: Small upright panel with a gold ground in a gilded moulded frame. The Virgin sits low, turned slightly to the right, on a round gold cushion patterned with a dark lattice, placed on a carpet with red, white and blue geometric motifs that runs across the bottom of the panel. She wears a deep blue mantle with a gold border of ornamental letters, lined in white, over a dress of gold brocade with a floral pattern on a dark ground. Her head, framed by the mantle and a punched halo with radiating lines, is inclined towards the Child. The Child, wrapped from the waist down in a pink cloth with a gold hem, lies across her lap, holds her breast with both hands as he feeds and turns his eyes towards the viewer. The gold ground is bordered by a band of punched ornament.
caption: Circle of Lippo Memmi, Madonna of Humility (The Virgin Nursing the Child), c. 1340. Tempera and gold on poplar panel, 32.2 × 23.4 cm. Berlin, Staatliche Museen, Gemäldegalerie, inv. 1072; acquired in 1821 with the Solly collection. Photo: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, Gemäldegalerie / Jörg P. Anders, Public Domain Mark 1.0.

alt: Panel shaped as a pointed arch, with a gold ground and a frame decorated with a running foliate ornament. The Virgin sits low at the centre on a red cushion placed on a dark red marbled ground. She wears a very dark mantle, lined in green and edged with gold, over a red dress, and turns her head slightly towards the viewer. Her halo bears an inscription in gold letters. On her lap the Child, in a red tunic, feeds at her breast and looks out of the picture. At either side, two columns of six small angels with rainbow-coloured wings fly towards her with outstretched arms. Two black labels in the gold ground read MAT. at the left and OMNIUM at the right. On the ground at the left are a shield with battlements and a red band and a crescent moon; at the right a shield with diagonal bands and a two-handled vase with white lilies.
caption: Roberto d'Oderisio (attributed; also given to the Master of the Tempere Francescane), Madonna of Humility, c. 1340–1345, from San Domenico Maggiore, Naples. Tempera and gold on panel. Naples, Museo e Real Bosco di Capodimonte. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
