alt: Medieval parchment manuscript page written in brown ink in two dense columns of small Gothic cursive script. In the upper half of the left column, a few lines of red text mark the heading of a new story, followed by a large red initial F decorated with fine blue pen flourishes. Smaller initials appear below it, one blue and one red. The pages are slightly stained and the inner edge of the binding is visible at the right.
caption: Giovanni Boccaccio, Decameron, autograph, c. 1370; Berlin, Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin – Preußischer Kulturbesitz, Ms. Ham. 90, fol. 84v (Day VIII, tale 3). Public Domain Mark 1.0.

alt: Very wide medieval fresco in faded reds and ochres. At the left, an elegant hunting party on horseback halts before three open coffins containing corpses in increasing decay, while hermits occupy a rocky mountain above with a small chapel. At the centre, a rocky cleft divides the scene and a crowd of beggars gestures upward. In the sky at the right, angels and winged demons fight over small naked souls. At the lower right, richly dressed young men and women sit in a grove of orange trees with musicians, unaware of Death flying toward them with a scythe
caption: Buonamico Buffalmacco (attr.), The Triumph of Death, c. 1336–1341, fresco (detached), Camposanto Monumentale (south wall), Pisa.

alt: Large medieval fresco of the Last Judgement. At the top, Christ and the Virgin Mary sit side by side in two almond-shaped glories with rainbow borders, flanked by rows of seated apostles. Below, angels blow trumpets and hold scrolls, while armoured archangels with swords separate two dense crowds of resurrected figures: the blessed on the left, the condemned on the right. The painted surface is faded and shows the joins of the detached sections.
caption: Buonamico Buffalmacco (attr.), Last Judgement, c. 1336–1341, fresco (detached), Camposanto Monumentale (south wall), Pisa.

alt: Large medieval fresco of Hell painted almost entirely in reds and browns. A gigantic horned Lucifer stands at the centre of a rocky mountain divided into tiers of cave-like compartments, devouring sinners while serpents issue from his body. Around him, demons torment crowds of naked souls with fire, cauldrons, and instruments of torture. At the upper right, a pocket of rock encloses a dense cluster of small souls; at the left edge appear haloed figures from the adjoining Last Judgement
caption: Buonamico Buffalmacco (attr.), Hell, c. 1336–1341, fresco (detached, with later repainting), Camposanto Monumentale (south wall), Pisa.

alt: Very wide medieval fresco of a rocky desert landscape in pale ochres and greens, scattered with small chapels, huts, and caves. Dozens of elderly hermits in brown and grey habits pray, read, weave baskets, draw water, and converse across the terraced mountainside. A river with boats and a small bridge runs along the lower edge. Some hermits confront small dark demons and animals; large patches of plaster are lost, leaving blank areas
caption: Buonamico Buffalmacco (attr.), Thebaid (Lives of the Desert Fathers), c. 1336–1341, fresco (detached), Camposanto Monumentale (south wall), Pisa.

alt: Triangular web of a Gothic vault frescoed in red-brown, framed by white ribs with red geometric borders. At the centre, a quatrefoil medallion with red and white ornamental bands encloses an elderly haloed prophet with a long ochre beard, dressed in pale robes, holding an unfurled scroll whose surface is abraded and blackened in patches
caption: Buonamico Buffalmacco (attr., after Ghiberti), Prophet holding a scroll, c. 1315, fresco, vault web of the former armarium (Cappella di San Jacopo), Badia a Settimo, Scandicci (Florence).

alt: Gothic vault web frescoed in mottled red-brown, framed by white ribs with red ornament. A quatrefoil medallion encloses a haloed bearded figure whose halo has turned black, draped in pale blue-grey robes, holding up a large unfurled scroll; the painted surface is severely abraded, with the design surviving mainly as ghostly outlines
caption: Buonamico Buffalmacco (attr., after Ghiberti), Prophet (or apostle) with unfurled scroll, c. 1315, fresco, vault web of the former armarium (Cappella di San Jacopo), Badia a Settimo, Scandicci (Florence).

alt: Triangular web of a Gothic vault in deep red-brown, bordered by white ribs with red star-and-chequer ornament meeting at a painted boss. A haloed figure in pale yellow-white robes sits frontally on a large architectural marble throne with a high back and projecting stepped footrest; the surface is heavily abraded, the face nearly effaced, the throne drawn in confident perspective lines.
caption: Buonamico Buffalmacco (attr., after Ghiberti), Enthroned evangelist, c. 1315, fresco, vault web of the former armarium (Cappella di San Jacopo), Badia a Settimo, Scandicci (Florence).

alt: Gothic vault web in mottled red-brown framed by white ribs with red ornament. A haloed, bearded evangelist in a dark red tunic and pale mantle sits frontally on a wide architectural throne, one hand raised before his chest; at his feet, between the folds of his robe, crouches a dark, heavily damaged four-legged winged creature, his evangelist symbol. The surface is abraded throughout
caption: Buonamico Buffalmacco (attr., after Ghiberti), Enthroned evangelist with his symbol, c. 1315, fresco, vault web of the former armarium (Cappella di San Jacopo), Badia a Settimo, Scandicci (Florence).

alt: Fragmentary medieval fresco under a stone arch. In the lunette above, a half-length Christ with open arms displays his wounds among the instruments of the Passion against dark blue. Below, the Virgin in a blue mantle sits on a golden throne with a patterned cloth of honour, holding the standing Christ Child whose face is lost; to the left stand a young saint and a sainted pope in a white tiara and red cope. Large areas of bare plaster interrupt the scene
caption: Buonamico Buffalmacco (attr.), Christ in Pietà, with the Madonna and Child Enthroned and Saints, probably 1320s, fresco, Cathedral of Arezzo.

alt: Nearly square medieval painting of the Virgin and Child on a dark red ground framed by a red-and-black border of leaf motifs. The Virgin, in a very dark blue mantle over a bright red dress, sits on a pale green and ochre Gothic throne with pointed openings and pinnacle finials, turning her head toward the Child. The curly-haired Christ Child, in a red tunic patterned with small gold stars, sits on her lap holding her hand. The edges of the panel are worn and damaged.
caption: Buonamico Buffalmacco (attr.), Virgin and Child Enthroned, first half of the 14th century, tempera on panel, 58 × 55 cm, Church of San Donato, Pergognano (Castiglion Fiorentino, Arezzo).

alt: Night view of the Fonte Nuova in Siena, a Gothic public fountain built in red brick. Two large pointed arches with moulded brick frames rest on clustered piers. They open onto vaulted chambers lit from inside in warm yellow light, where pale turquoise water fills two rectangular basins. Above the arches rises a tall, weathered brick wall with small square openings and traces of blind arcading. On the left, a lower brick wall with a round arch links the fountain to the street. On the right stand ochre and red houses with green shutters. A lawn fills the foreground under a black sky.
caption: Siena, Fonte Nuova (Fonte Nuova d’Ovile), Pian d’Ovile. Project defined on 10 August 1298 by a communal commission of five masters, among them Camaino di Crescentino; completion traditionally dated 1303. Brick, with stone bases and capitals; two pointed arches on the main front open onto cross-vaulted basins. Night view.

alt: Early twentieth-century black-and-white plate of a square marble slab with a raised frame, carved with twelve lines of Gothic capital letters. The upper lines are clearly legible and begin with a cross and the words MILLE DUCENTENOS ANNOS. A deep diagonal crack runs from the upper left towards the bottom centre. The left side of the lower lines is badly eroded. Short incised strokes fill the ends of several lines. Below the image is printed -FONTE NUOVA (Iscrizione in facciata)-, and -Tav. XIX- appears in the upper right corner.
caption: Siena, Fonte Nuova (Fonte di Borgo Franco), Pian d’Ovile. Foundation inscription in the right-hand pier of the main front, white Sienese marble, Gothic majuscule, August 1298. Photograph from F. Bargagli Petrucci, Le fonti di Siena e i loro acquedotti, vol. I, Siena–Florence–Rome 1906, pl. XIX (transcription p. 296).

alt: Upper part of the marble façade of Siena Cathedral against a pale blue sky. Three pointed gables, the tallest in the centre, hold mosaics on gold grounds: Christ crowning the Virgin among angels in the middle, the Presentation of the Virgin in the Temple on the left, and the Nativity on the right. A winged statue holding a lance stands on the central apex. Below the central gable, a large round window with clear glass reflects the clouds; it sits in a square frame filled with small niches of half-length figures. Tall pinnacled turrets flank the gables, rows of statues line the lower edge, and the black-and-white striped bell tower rises at the right.
caption: Siena, Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, upper zone of the west façade. Dated by Middeldorf Kosegarten to the campaign completed by c. 1317, when Camaino di Crescentino was the senior master of the Opera; traditionally assigned to Giovanni di Cecco and to the later fourteenth century. Gable mosaics executed in Venice in 1878 (Presentation of the Virgin, Coronation of the Virgin, Nativity) after cartoons by Sienese painters of the nineteenth century; statues largely replaced by copies, originals in the Museo dell’Opera del Duomo.

alt: Front view of the Baptistery of San Giovanni in Siena, reached by a wide flight of steps. The marble façade is banded in white and dark green. Its lower storey has three round-arched portals with striped arches and carved jambs. A pointed gable with a carved rosette rises above the central portal, and lozenge-shaped panels decorate the wall surfaces. Above a band of small gables, the upper storey has three tall pointed bays: the two outer bays hold slender mullioned windows, and the central one is blind. Higher up stands a plain brick wall with a large round window, the end wall of the cathedral above. On the left, a staircase climbs beside the striped marble flank of the cathedral. Brick palaces close the square on both sides, and the one on the right is pierced by a large archway.
caption: Siena, Baptistery of San Giovanni, Piazza San Giovanni. The baptistery hall was built in the substructure of the cathedral’s eastward extension, begun on 21 April 1316, when Camaino di Crescentino was the senior master of the Opera di Santa Maria; its vaults were closed in 1326. The marble façade belongs to a later fourteenth-century phase generally associated with Giovanni d’Agostino and was left unfinished. Above it rises the brick end wall of the cathedral’s extended choir.

alt: Six white and grey-veined marble statuettes of standing saints, set in a row on a low dark plinth against a beige museum wall. From left to right: three bearded men in heavy mantles, the first holding a rolled scroll, the second holding a long blank scroll that hangs from his right hand, the third raising his right hand beside a long unrolled scroll, with traces of blue paint in his drapery folds; then three beardless young men with curly hair, one holding a vertical scroll with incised lines of writing, one with his right hand on his chest, and one looking down at a book held open in both hands. Several mantles have incised ornamental borders.
caption: Massa Marittima, Museo di Arte Sacra (former convent of San Pietro all'Orto). Six of eleven marble statuettes of prophets, apostles and saints, probably from the choir screen of the cathedral of San Cerbone; Sienese, c. 1300–1320. The museum assigns eight figures in white marble to Gano di Fazio and three in painted grey-white marble to Camaino di Crescentino; the attribution to Camaino is tentative.

alt: Marble statuette of a standing bearded prophet against a beige wall. He has a furrowed forehead, deep-set eyes and a long curling beard carved with drill holes. A heavy mantle, fastened at the left shoulder with a rosette brooch, covers his body; its borders and his cuffs carry incised chevron ornament. From his right hand a long, blank unrolled scroll hangs straight down in front of him, and his left hand rests on the drapery at his side.
caption: Camaino di Crescentino (attributed), Bearded Prophet with an Unrolled Scroll, c. 1300–1320. Grey-white marble with traces of colour. Massa Marittima, Museo di Arte Sacra; probably from the choir screen of the cathedral of San Cerbone.

alt: Marble statuette of a beardless young apostle in grey-veined white stone, standing against a beige wall. His curly-haired head turns to his right. His left hand rests flat on his chest. A long mantle with a carved fringe and incised ornamental border falls over his right shoulder and sweeps diagonally across his body; bare feet show beneath the hem.
caption: Camaino di Crescentino (attributed), Beardless Apostle, c. 1300–1320. Grey-veined white marble. Massa Marittima, Museo di Arte Sacra; probably from the choir screen of the cathedral of San Cerbone.

alt: Polychrome marble statuette of a young beardless deacon saint on a wooden base against a dark background. He has gilded curly hair, rosy cheeks and a flat gilded halo disc above his head. His white dalmatic is painted with a pattern of red lozenges, gold rosettes and sprigs, with broad gilded ornamental panels on the chest and near the hem. His right hand is raised in a loose fist with a hole for a missing attribute, and his left hand is extended, palm down. Gilded shoes show beneath the robe.
caption: Camaino di Crescentino (attributed), Beardless Cleric (deacon saint), c. 1300–1320. Marble with extensive polychromy and gilding; halo of later date (?). Massa Marittima, Museo di Arte Sacra; probably from the choir screen of the cathedral of San Cerbone.

alt: Tall arched gold-ground panel in a gilded frame: Christ, in a red tunic and a blue mantle streaked with gold, holds a sceptre and crowns the Virgin seated beside him on a wide throne hung with a red and gold cloth; a blue starry arc and a dense choir of haloed angels with a vielle, lutes, a psaltery and a portative organ rise above them, other angels lean over the throne, and three small angels kneel at its foot between two dark cartouches bearing the date 1372 and the painters' names
caption: Donato and Catarino di Marco, Coronation of the Virgin, signed and dated August 1372, tempera and gold on panel, Venice, Fondazione Querini Stampalia, Pinacoteca. Central panel of a dismembered polyptych.

alt: Arched gold-ground panel: Christ, crowned and in a rose tunic and gold-patterned blue mantle, sets a crown on the head of the Virgin seated beside him on a shared throne; behind them hang an orange cloth with dark floral motifs and a starry blue hemisphere, over which eight angels lean, some playing a lute, a portative organ and a vielle; a three-line signature with the date 1375 runs along the step below
caption: Coronation of the Virgin, signed and dated March 1375, tempera and gold on panel, 89 × 58 cm, Venice, Gallerie dell'Accademia, cat. 16 (purchased from Count Vincenzo Galli, 1877).

alt: Three unframed gold-ground panels shown side by side. In the arched central panel Christ, in a blue tunic and red mantle, crowns the Virgin, who wears a blue mantle with large gold motifs; they sit on a pink Gothic throne before a starry blue arc with five angels above, and a fragmentary signature runs along the base. At the left stands Saint Lucy, crowned, in red and green, holding a lamp; at the right Saint Nicholas of Tolentino, in a black habit, holds a red book
caption: Coronation of the Virgin with Saints Lucy and Nicholas of Tolentino, signed, after 1375, tempera and gold on panel, Venice, Gallerie dell'Accademia, cat. 702 (purchased from Tommaso Mazzoli of Venice, 1902).

alt: Gilded Gothic polyptych in three tiers. In the centre the Virgin, in a blue mantle with large gold motifs, sits on a flowering meadow holding the Child, with a tiny donor kneeling at her side. Four standing saints flank her: Anthony Abbot, John the Baptist, Christopher carrying the Christ Child through water, and James the Great. Above are four half-length saints and, at the top, a Crucifixion between two small standing female saints. A painted base carries the signature
caption: Madonna and Child, the Crucifixion, and Saints, signed, c. 1380–1389, tempera and gold on panel, 176.5 × 185.9 cm with frame and original base, Baltimore, The Walters Art Museum, inv. 37.635 (acquired by Henry Walters, 1908–1909).

alt: Small gold-ground panel in a gilded frame with a cusped arch and twisted colonnettes. The Virgin, in a dark blue mantle with fine gold scrollwork over a red dress, sits low on a flowering meadow and nurses the Child, who is wrapped in an orange and gold cloth. Gold rays spread from her figure, a white crescent moon lies at her feet, and a small scroll at the lower right carries the painter's signature
caption: Madonna of Humility, signed, 1380–82, tempera and gold on panel, 40.6 × 33.4 cm, Worcester, Massachusetts, Worcester Art Museum, inv. 1923.213 (from Eugene Bolton, London).

alt: The Virgin, in a plain blue mantle over a red dress, bends her head towards the Child, who lies across her arm wrapped in an orange cloth and turns to look up at her. Both have gold haloes, and thin gold rays spread from them across a bright red ground with a lobed upper edge. Grey patches mark losses in the haloes and at the Virgin's breast
caption: Catarino di Marco (attr.) or a follower, Madonna of Humility, 1370–80, tempera on panel, 85 × 67 cm, Faenza, Pinacoteca Comunale, inv. 102.

alt: Gold-ground panel under a round gilded arch with carved foliage in the corners. The Virgin, in a blue mantle with large gold motifs and a green lining over a pink dress, sits low on a broad red ground and nurses the Child, who wears a red tunic patterned in gold. A small gold sun with rays shines on her breast and a gold star on her shoulder, faint gold rays spread around her, and a Latin inscription naming the Madonna of Humility runs along the bottom
caption: Catarino di Marco (attr.), Madonna of Humility, late 1370s, tempera and gold on panel, 79.6 × 54.6 cm (91.5 × 70 × 4 cm framed), Cleveland, The Cleveland Museum of Art, inv. 1963.500, gift of Dr. Rudolf J. Heinemann.

alt: Small round-arched gold-ground panel. The Virgin, in a dark blue mantle scattered with small flower sprigs over a pink dress, sits low and nurses the Child, who is wrapped in an orange and yellow cloth on her green-lined lap. An orange cushion lies at her side, and a dark flowering meadow fills the lower right corner
caption: Catarino di Marco (attr.), Madonna of Humility, tempera and gold on panel, 28.9 × 25.4 cm, Columbus, Ohio, Columbus Museum of Art, inv. 1931.041, gift of Ferdinand Howald.

alt: Unframed gold-ground panel. Christ, in a red tunic and a dark mantle patterned with large gold star-shaped motifs, holds a long sceptre and places a jewelled crown on the head of the Virgin, who sits beside him with joined hands in a matching dark mantle. Behind them hangs a red cloth patterned in gold, held up by winged angels, and above it a dark blue sky full of gold stars shows a sun with a face at the left and a crescent moon at the right, under a crowded choir of haloed angels
caption: Coronation of the Virgin, fourteenth century, tempera and gold on poplar panel, 120 × 75 cm, St Petersburg, State Hermitage Museum, inv. ГЭ-6662 (formerly N. P. Likhachev collection; State Russian Museum from 1914; Hermitage from 1923).

alt: Small cusped-arched panel set in a later gilded frame on green velvet. Christ, in a red tunic patterned with gold and a dark blue mantle, raises a jewelled crown over the head of the Virgin, who sits at the left with joined hands in a blue mantle with gold flowers and a white veil. They sit in a dark architectural throne with small angel heads looking in from the sides, and above a cornice three winged angels lean over a parapet
caption: Catarino di Marco (attr.), Coronation of the Virgin, 1370s, tempera and gold on panel, 27.8 × 13.7 cm, Munich, Lingenauber collection.

alt: Large shaped wooden cross with a gold ground and stepped edges. The dead Christ hangs on a dark painted cross, his head fallen to his right shoulder, his ribs and swollen belly sharply modelled, a thin white loincloth at his hips and his feet crossed. In the quatrefoil terminals the grieving Virgin in green appears at the left, Saint John in pink and blue at the right, and a winged archangel holding a staff and an orb at the top. A small titulus above the head reads I.N.R.I., and the lower terminal shows a dark rocky mound
caption: Catarino di Marco (attr.), Painted Crucifix, 1375–1400, tempera and gold on panel, 348 × 250 cm, Zadar, collection of sacred art.

alt: Fresco of an interior seen as an open architectural box, with a pedimented building and a domed structure above. Saint Gregory, haloed, bearded and wearing a cap, lies propped on a long bed, his head resting on his raised hand, while a man in a striped hood holds his wrist. At the left two men in long brown and purple garments with caps lean toward him. Behind the bed an open cupboard with books, a lectern with an open book, and a Gothic inscription on the back wall. On the step of the bed lie a round fruit and a glass flask. In the foreground, a painted panel with a diamond and a quatrefoil framing a lion's head holding a ring.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Gregory, Ill with Fever, and the Books He Composed, from the Stories of Saint Gregory the Great, c. 1336–1346, fresco. Florence, Santa Maria Novella, Bardi chapel (Cappella di San Gregorio).

alt: Fresco within painted borders of geometric ornament, with large areas of loss filled in a neutral tone on the right. In a rocky landscape with a palm tree, the emperor Trajan, crowned and wearing a pink cloak over armour, rides a rearing white horse, followed by soldiers with a shield, a white banner, a lance and a helmet, and a second, brown horse. At the left a woman in a dark mantle, her head lost, stands before him and lays her hand on the horse. At the right a man in a yellow tunic, his head also lost, walks away carrying a staff over his shoulder.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), The Justice of Trajan (Trajan and the Widow), from the Stories of Saint Gregory the Great, c. 1336–1346, fresco. Florence, Santa Maria Novella, Bardi chapel (Cappella di San Gregorio).

alt: Tall, heavily damaged fresco framed by painted borders with geometric patterns and rosettes; most of the centre and right side is lost, showing bare plaster and traces of an earlier painted layer with architectural motifs at the top. On a dark ground, a winged angel in pink with a halo flies upward, pointing toward a cloud from which a second figure in grey leans down. Below at the left, a haloed figure in a brown and red mantle is seen from behind, head raised; at the lower right survive the lower part of a standing figure in a pale robe with an embroidered hem, and a rocky outcrop.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Gregory and the Angel, from the Stories of Saint Gregory the Great, c. 1336–1346, fresco, fragmentary. Florence, Santa Maria Novella, Bardi chapel (Cappella di San Gregorio).

alt: Tall fresco within a painted border of geometric patterns and rosettes, with losses at the upper left revealing an earlier layer with foliate motifs. A pink-and-white building with pediments, a round window, an arcaded cornice, a cross and a small statue on top frames the scene. At the left, on a raised platform beside a lectern, sits a figure in a grey habit whose head is lost, handing a flat object across a slender column. At the right stands a barefoot bearded man in a white cap, a torn white tunic and a ragged ochre mantle, his hand on his breast; wings rise behind his shoulders. Above the doorway behind, a small lunette contains a painted winged figure.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Gregory's Alms to the Shipwrecked Man, from the Stories of Saint Gregory the Great, c. 1336–1346, fresco. Florence, Santa Maria Novella, Bardi chapel (Cappella di San Gregorio).

alt: Fresco within painted borders of geometric patterns and rosettes. In a bare, pale rocky landscape, Saint Gregory, haloed and hooded in a grey-brown habit, stands at the left with his hands joined, before a dark cleft in the rock; a broad column of golden light descends upon him from a cloud. At the right a group of Romans approaches: an old bearded man in a blue and gold cope, a man in red pointing toward the saint, and others in caps and mantles of yellow, pink and green, one stooping. On a hill at the upper right rises a walled city with pink towers and buildings.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Gregory Found by the Romans: The Column of Light over His Hiding Place, from the Stories of Saint Gregory the Great, c. 1336–1346, fresco. Florence, Santa Maria Novella, Bardi chapel (Cappella di San Gregorio). Photo: Richard Stracke, CC BY-NC-SA 3.0.

alt: Fresco within painted borders of geometric patterns and rosettes. Inside an open, many-sided Gothic pavilion with three arches, slender columns, pinnacles and a sloping roof, Saint Gregory sits frontally on a raised throne, wearing a tall white papal tiara, a gold halo, white gloves, a white alb and an orange-red mantle with a pallium; he blesses with his right hand and holds a red book in his left. Mitred bishops sit on either side, turning toward him, some holding books; a cleric in a red cap appears at the left. A large lacuna filled in a neutral tone covers much of the right side, where a kneeling figure in ochre is partly preserved.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Gregory Enthroned among the Bishops, from the Stories of Saint Gregory the Great, c. 1336–1346, fresco. Florence, Santa Maria Novella, Bardi chapel (Cappella di San Gregorio).

alt: Pointed lunette beneath an ornamented vault rib and above a painted frieze of foliate panels and lozenges, heavily damaged and crossed by cracks. At the left, within a timber structure, a haloed figure lies asleep on a bed with an ochre base and a green cover; faint pale forms appear above against a blue sky. At the right a young haloed figure stands beside a hanging length of dark red cloth, and beyond a large area of loss a figure in pink bends forward toward him.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), The Dream of the Palace and the Gift of the Mantle, lunette of the left wall, from the Stories of Saint Francis, probably c. 1343, fresco. Pistoia, San Francesco, main chapel.

alt: Black-and-white historical photograph of the same lunette in a much better state of preservation. At the left, in an open bedchamber with slender posts, a drawn curtain and a coffered ceiling, the haloed young Francis lies asleep propped on pillows; above the roof a figure flies against the dark sky. At the right, the young haloed Francis in a cap stands facing an older man in a cap who bends toward him; between them lies a large blank area of plaster loss. Below runs a frieze of foliate panels and lozenges.
caption: The lunette of the left wall, with the Dream of Saint Francis and the Gift of the Mantle, in a photograph of c. 1920–1939 by the Gabinetto Fotografico della Soprintendenza, Florence (negative 19271). Bologna, Fondazione Federico Zeri, Fototeca, inv. 28806.

alt: Square fresco within a broad border of geometric patterns in red, white and blue. A dilapidated church is shown in cross-section, its tiled roof broken open to reveal the rafters and its walls cracked. Inside, beneath a colonnade, the young Francis, haloed and wearing a long pink lay garment, kneels with raised hands before a painted crucifix set on an altar in an apse with a coffered half-dome; the crucifix stands at an angle. At the left are inlaid choir stalls and a small bell hanging by a rope. A Gothic inscription runs along the base of the floor.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), The Prayer in San Damiano, from the Stories of Saint Francis, probably c. 1343, fresco. Pistoia, San Francesco, main chapel.

alt: Square fresco within a broad geometric border. At the left, a large church with a tiled roof and a Romanesque bell tower leans dangerously; Saint Francis, haloed and in a grey-brown habit, props it up with his shoulder against a column, one hand on his hip. At the right, in a bedchamber with a drawn-back curtain under a roof with trefoil gables, the pope sleeps in a red mantle on a bed with a blue cover, while a haloed young angel on a cloud, holding a book, points toward him. Two attendants sit on the floor at the foot of the bed, one in pink with a white cap, the other in a dark mantle seen from behind.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), The Dream of Innocent III, from the Stories of Saint Francis, probably c. 1343, fresco. Pistoia, San Francesco, main chapel.

alt: Fresco within a broad geometric border, its centre almost entirely lost. The upper half shows a monumental pink and ochre building against a blue sky: a pedimented front with a roundel in the tympanum, a large round arch flanked by trefoil oculi, gabled side niches and a bell tower at the upper left. A large irregular area of bare plaster, with faint drawn lines, covers the lower centre, where the figures stood. At the left survives a fragment of a brown garment; at the right, under the niche, part of a seated figure in yellow and pink beside a slender column.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), The Approval of the Rule, from the Stories of Saint Francis, probably c. 1343, fresco, fragmentary. Pistoia, San Francesco, main chapel.

alt: Pointed lunette beneath a richly ornamented vault rib and above a painted frieze of foliate panels and lozenges, heavily damaged. At the left a large area of loss covers much of the field. At the centre a walled city with crenellated pink walls, towers and a large arched gate rises against a blue sky. At the right two friars in habits stand before the walls; the one at the right raises his hand, while the head of his companion is covered by a greenish patch of filling. A few Gothic letters survive at the lower right.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), The Sermon to the Birds, lunette of the right wall, from the Stories of Saint Francis, probably c. 1343, fresco. Pistoia, San Francesco, main chapel.

alt: Black-and-white historical photograph of the same lunette in a better state of preservation. A walled city with a columned gate and a dense cluster of towers and houses fills the centre. At the lower left a small flock of long-legged birds stands on the ground; above a large area of loss, a haloed head and a second head appear. At the right two friars stand before the walls, the haloed one raising his hand, the head of the other lost. At the lower right the letters ICAVIT are visible.
caption: The lunette of the right wall, with the Sermon to the Birds, in a photograph of c. 1920–1939 by the Gabinetto Fotografico della Soprintendenza, Florence (negative 19367). Bologna, Fondazione Federico Zeri, Fototeca, inv. 28810.

alt: Damaged fresco within a geometric border, with large losses filled in grey across the lower left and centre. At the right, under a round canopy on slender columns with a balustrade and a coffered underside, the Sultan sits on a Gothic throne on a polygonal dais: bearded, wearing a turban and a red mantle, he stretches out his arm toward the centre. Turbaned councillors crowd behind him, and at the far right a bearded guard in a long yellow coat and turban holds a bow. In the centre a fire blazes on the ground; at the left survive fragments of figures in brown, red and white garments, most of their heads lost. Behind them rises a palace with a loggia, two-light windows and panels of foliate ornament against a dark sky.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), The Trial by Fire before the Sultan, from the Stories of Saint Francis, probably c. 1343, fresco. Pistoia, San Francesco, main chapel.

alt: Fresco within a broad geometric border, its lower edge cut by a later arched opening with a decorated intrados. A mountain landscape of pale, cleft rocks rises to a wood of tall trees and a small pink chapel with a bell gable. Near the top, against a dark radiant aureole, hovers the crucified Christ in the form of a seraph with red wings, its rays directed downward to the left, where a large area of loss has removed the kneeling Francis. On the rocks are a deer lying down, a walking bear and a falcon perched on a ledge. At the right a friar in a pinkish habit and hood sits reading a book.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), The Stigmatization of Saint Francis on La Verna, from the Stories of Saint Francis, probably c. 1343, fresco. Pistoia, San Francesco, main chapel.

alt: View straight up into a rib vault divided into four triangular webs by diagonal ribs painted with a twisted pattern of blue and gold. Each web has a deep blue ground scattered with gold stars, edged by scalloped borders and framed by wide bands of foliate ornament and octagonal motifs. At the centre of each web, a gold-ground medallion within a pink frame contains a half-length figure: at the top a grey-robed elder, at the left a friar bearing a yoke, at the right a veiled woman in a tower inscribed CASTITAS, at the bottom a haloed Saint Francis with raised hands. At the crossing of the ribs, a gilded boss holds a small bust of Christ blessing, surrounded by four small lozenges with painted shields.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), vault of the main chapel with allegories of the Franciscan virtues and the Glory of Saint Francis, probably c. 1343, fresco and gilding. Pistoia, San Francesco, main chapel.

alt: Triangular web of a vault with a deep blue ground covered in gold stars, framed by bands of ornament. At the centre, inside a pink-framed medallion with a gold ground, a veiled woman with a pale face and downcast eyes appears at the top of a red crenellated tower with two turrets. The tower bears the inscription CASTITAS in Gothic letters.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Chastity (CASTITAS), medallion of the vault of the main chapel, probably c. 1343, fresco and gilding. Pistoia, San Francesco, main chapel.

alt: Triangular web of a vault with a deep blue ground covered in gold stars, framed by bands of ornament. At the centre, inside a pink-framed medallion with a gold ground, an elderly man with a short grey beard, wearing a white headcloth and a grey-blue mantle over a white collar, raises his right hand to his face with curled fingers and holds a staff or cord in his left hand across his body.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), A Grey-Robed Elder (Obedience?), medallion of the vault of the main chapel, probably c. 1343, fresco and gilding. Pistoia, San Francesco, main chapel.

alt: Triangular web of a vault with a deep blue ground covered in gold stars, framed by bands of ornament. At the centre, inside a pink-framed medallion with a gold ground, a tonsured friar in a brown habit with a hood carries a wooden yoke across his shoulders, the ends of which project on either side of his head; with both hands he holds the cords attached to it, and a knotted cord hangs from his waist. His head is bowed and turned slightly to the right.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), A Friar Bearing the Yoke of Obedience, medallion of the vault of the main chapel, probably c. 1343, fresco and gilding. Pistoia, San Francesco, main chapel.

alt: Triangular web of a vault with a deep blue ground covered in gold stars, framed by bands of ornament. At the centre, inside a pink-framed medallion with a gold ground, Saint Francis appears frontally at half length in a grey-brown hooded habit, his head surrounded by a gilded halo with fine radiating rays; he raises both hands, palms outward, at shoulder height. A crack runs down through the lower part of the figure.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), The Glory of Saint Francis, medallion of the vault of the main chapel, probably c. 1343, fresco and gilding. Pistoia, San Francesco, main chapel.

alt: Tall painted Gothic tabernacle with a gable, pinnacles and twisted columns against a dark blue ground, within a border of red, white and blue geometric patterns. The figure of the Baptist standing in the niche is almost entirely lost: only part of a gold halo, an oval area where the head was, traces of long brown hair and of a hairy garment at shoulder and waist level, and the outline of the feet survive on the abraded plaster.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Saint John the Baptist, probably c. 1343, fresco, fragmentary. Pistoia, San Francesco, main chapel, pilaster of the entrance arch (upper tabernacle).

alt: Tall painted Gothic tabernacle with a gable, pinnacles and twisted columns against a dark blue ground, within a border of red, white and blue geometric patterns. In the niche, against a warm ochre background, stands a young saint with curly fair hair and a radiant gold halo, wearing a long rose-red tunic and mantle. In the right hand he holds a thin rod, perhaps a palm; in the left, a covered vessel of pale metal.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), A Young Martyr with a Palm and a Covered Vessel (Saint Cosmas or Damian?), probably c. 1343, fresco. Pistoia, San Francesco, main chapel, pilaster of the entrance arch (lower tabernacle, below Saint John the Baptist).

alt: Tall painted Gothic tabernacle with a gable, pinnacles and twisted columns against a dark blue ground, within a border of red, white and blue geometric patterns. In the niche stands a young female saint with fair curly hair, a small white cap and a radiant gold halo, wearing a pale green garment and a red mantle drawn across the body. In the right hand she holds a slender rod, in the left a tall white vessel with a pointed lid.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Mary Magdalene with Her Ointment Jar (?), probably c. 1343, fresco. Pistoia, San Francesco, main chapel, pilaster of the entrance arch (upper tabernacle, above Lazarus).

alt: Tall painted Gothic tabernacle with a gable, pinnacles and twisted columns against a dark blue ground, within a border of red, white and blue geometric patterns. In the niche stands a figure whose head is lost, leaving only a pale disc of halo against a red background; he is wrapped from shoulders to feet in white grave-clothes, gathered at the chest by his right hand and bound at the waist by a band, with the loose end of a winding sheet curling at the lower right.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Lazarus, probably c. 1343, fresco, fragmentary. Pistoia, San Francesco, main chapel, pilaster of the entrance arch (lower tabernacle, below Mary Magdalene).

alt: Gabled gold-ground panel of the Crucifixion. Christ, pale and slender, hangs on a cross made of a rough tree-trunk; above the titulus the cross sprouts a green tree in which a pelican spreads its wings over her nest. Two half-length prophets fly in on billowing red and pink mantles, holding inscribed scrolls. Below, on the left, the swooning Virgin is supported by two companions while Saint John in vermilion leans toward her and the Magdalene, in red with long blonde hair, embraces the foot of the cross; on the right a man in yellow raises the reed with the sponge among a dense crowd of bearded elders and soldiers. Carved and gilded frame with spiral colonnettes.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Crucifixion with Mourners (Gesù Cristo crocifisso e dolenti), c. 1335–1340, tempera on panel, 125 × 61.5 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 215; from the church of San Martino Maggiore, Bologna.

alt: Gold-ground panel in a red velvet frame. Within a cusped arch drawn in the gold, Christ stands stripped to the waist in a white loincloth, hands bound behind him to a slender column beneath a small canopy on grey colonnettes. Two executioners flank him in mirrored motion: on the left a man in a rose-pink tunic, seen from behind, raises a scourge high overhead; on the right a bearded man in ochre with a white turban grips Christ's shoulder and draws back his whip.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), The Flagellation of Christ, c. 1330–1339, egg tempera and gold on panel, 57.5 × 36.8 cm (71.1 × 49.5 cm with frame). Seattle Art Museum, Samuel H. Kress Collection, 61.147; formerly Achillito Chiesa and Contini Bonacossi collections.

alt: Rectangular gold-ground panel, heavily crackled and abraded. The Virgin, in a mauve mantle over a white gown, sits frontally on a deep blue cloth of honour instead of a throne, holding on her lap the half-naked Christ Child wrapped in a red blanket; with her right hand she holds open a small book toward which the Child reaches. Two kneeling angels in orange robes grip the corners of the cloth at either side, and two more angels stand behind it at the top. Below, a veined marble platform and step; three dark scorch marks from candles run up from the bottom edge.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Virgin and Child Enthroned with Four Angels, c. 1340–1345 (museum dating; c. 1338–1342 in the reconstruction of the San Martino altarpiece), tempera and gold on panel, 51.1 × 39.9 cm. New Haven, Yale University Art Gallery, Bequest of Maitland F. Griggs, B.A. 1896, inv. 1943.260; probably from the high altar complex of San Martino Maggiore, Bologna. Catalogued by Yale as "Pseudo-Dalmasio".

alt: Horizontal panel strip in a plain modern wood frame. On a dark blue-green ground sit four gilded quatrefoil medallions, each holding the bust of a figure against gold: at left a bearded man in a dark blue-black cloak over a pink-red tunic; then a beardless youth in red with long fair hair; then a young figure with abundant auburn hair holding up an unfurled white scroll; at right another fair-haired youth in dark red and blue with a curling white scroll.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Four Saints, c. 1335–1340, tempera on panel, 14 × 55.9 cm overall; each picture surface 10.2 × 10.8 cm. New Haven, Yale University Art Gallery, lent by the Estate of Richard L. Feigen, ILE2019.3.39. Catalogued by Yale as "Pseudo-Dalmasio".

alt: Horizontal panel strip in a plain modern wood frame. On a dark mottled ground sit four gilded quatrefoil medallions, each holding a bust against gold: at left a mitred saint in a black habit over white; then an elderly bishop with a long grey beard, white mitre and rose vestments, hand raised; then a white-bearded elder in a broad red cardinal's hat holding a green book; at right a bishop with a jewelled golden mitre and pale cope.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Four Saints, c. 1335–1340, tempera on panel, 14.3 × 55.9 cm overall; each picture surface 10.8 × 10.8 cm. New Haven, Yale University Art Gallery, lent by the Estate of Richard L. Feigen, ILE2019.3.40. Catalogued by Yale as "Pseudo-Dalmasio".

alt: Gilded quatrefoil medallion on a dark blue-green ground. Against gold, the bust of Saint John the Baptist, with long, unkempt grey-brown hair and a full beard, in a blue mantle; he raises his right hand with the forefinger pointing and holds a thin red staff topped by a small red cross. His eyes look sideways, toward the viewer's right.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Saint John the Baptist, c. 1335–1340 (museum dating 1370–1377), egg tempera on wood panel, in a quatrefoil; the four-panel strip 14.3 × 56 × 3 cm overall. Detroit Institute of Arts, Founders Society Purchase, General Membership Fund, 37.189.1. Catalogued by the Detroit Institute of Arts as "Dalmasio di Jacopo".

alt: Gilded quatrefoil medallion on a dark blue-green ground. Against gold, the bust of Saint Thomas Aquinas in the black cappa and white habit of the Dominican order, with a tonsure and a round, heavy face, his head bowed and turned to the left; with his right hand he holds a red book before his chest. A faint incised halo surrounds his head.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Saint Thomas Aquinas, c. 1335–1340 (museum dating 1370–1377), egg tempera on wood panel, in a quatrefoil; the four-panel strip 14.3 × 56 × 3 cm overall. Detroit Institute of Arts, Founders Society Purchase, General Membership Fund, 37.189.2. Catalogued by the Detroit Institute of Arts as "Dalmasio di Jacopo".

alt: Gilded quatrefoil medallion on a dark blue-green ground. Against gold, the bust of Saint Paul, balding with a fringe of brown hair and a long dark beard, in a rose-red mantle; he grips a sword by its hilt, pommel raised, the blade running diagonally across his chest with its point in his other hand. He looks sideways toward the right.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Saint Paul, c. 1335–1340 (museum dating 1370–1377), egg tempera on wood panel, in a quatrefoil; the four-panel strip 14.3 × 56 × 3 cm overall. Detroit Institute of Arts, Founders Society Purchase, General Membership Fund, 37.189.3. Catalogued by the Detroit Institute of Arts as "Dalmasio di Jacopo".

alt: Gilded quatrefoil medallion on a dark blue-green ground. Against gold, the bust of Saint Peter, with a cap of tight grey curls and a short grey beard, in a red tunic and a yellow-green mantle; he holds a large silver key upright in his left hand; a dark mass of mantle gathers at his right. His head is bowed and his expression sorrowful.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Saint Peter, c. 1335–1340 (museum dating 1370–1377), egg tempera on wood panel, in a quatrefoil; the four-panel strip 14.3 × 56 × 3 cm overall. Detroit Institute of Arts, Founders Society Purchase, General Membership Fund, 37.189.4. Catalogued by the Detroit Institute of Arts as "Dalmasio di Jacopo".

alt: Horizontal panel strip with four gilded quatrefoil medallions on a dark blue-green ground. From left: a fair-haired young woman in blue holding a white banner with a red cross; a crowned young woman in red with a palm and a fragment of a white wheel, raising her right hand; a beardless elderly bishop in a jewelled white mitre, white hood and yellow vestments, blessing and holding a crozier; a tonsured, grey-bearded friar in a black cappa over a white habit, with a small red star on his forehead and a red-and-white book.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Four Saints: Saint Ursula, Saint Catherine of Alexandria, Saint Augustine (?) and Saint Dominic, c. 1335–1340, tempera on panel; each medallion 12 × 12 cm unframed, 19.3 × 60.6 × 7.8 cm framed overall. Dublin, National Gallery of Ireland, NGI.1113, purchased 1943. Catalogued by the National Gallery of Ireland as "Pseudo Dalmasio".

alt: Half-length Virgin against a worn gold ground, wearing a white veil, a dark blue-black mantle lined with lighter blue and a pale pink gown with a vertical embroidered band of red, blue and green rosettes. A gold crown, faint against the gold, rises above her veil, within a large tooled halo. She looks out at the viewer with a grave, sidelong gaze while the curly-haired Christ Child, wrapped in a red mantle over a sheer white shirt, presses his cheek to hers and tugs at her veil; in his other hand he holds a tiny white dog. Her right hand holds a closed book bound in green.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Virgin and Child with a Dog, c. 1330–1335, tempera and tooled gold on panel, 46.5 × 30.5 cm. Philadelphia Museum of Art, John G. Johnson Collection, 1917, Cat. 3. Photo: Philadelphia Museum of Art. Image for educational use only.

alt: Upright gold-ground panel in a later gilt frame. The Virgin, in a dark blue-black mantle densely hatched with gold over a gown with orange-gold borders, sits on a tall rose-coloured Gothic throne with a round-arched back, cusped tracery, pinnacles, scrolled consoles and side blocks inset with green marble, on a crimson cushion. She holds a closed book on her knee and turns her gaze sidelong toward the viewer. The Child, in a red tunic hatched with gold, sits on her left arm, reaching up to touch her veil and holding a small bird in his other hand. Six angels with richly tooled haloes crowd and peer over the back of the throne.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Madonna and Child Enthroned with Six Angels (Vierge à l'Enfant en majesté avec des anges), second quarter of the 14th century (regarded in part of the recent literature as among the master's earliest surviving panels), tempera on panel, gold ground. Newark, Delaware, Alana Collection; formerly Del Pero collection, Imola, and R. Kirk Askew, New York.

alt: Upright gold-ground panel of the Descent from the Cross; the bare gesso at the upper corners shows the outline of a lost cusped arch frame. Behind the cross, beneath the titulus I.N.R.I., a bearded man in red with a red headcloth lifts the dead Christ under the arms; a ladder leans against the crossbar, from which blood drips. The Virgin in deep blue reaches up to embrace her son's freed arm, while a grieving woman in mauve stands behind her. The Magdalene, kneeling in red with long fair hair, raises her hand toward the bleeding feet. At right, Saint John in green holds a nail wrapped in a blue cloth, and an old bearded man in pink kneels to draw the nail from Christ's feet with pincers; blood runs down the cross and pools on the ground. A grey rock rises at the right edge.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), The Descent from the Cross, second quarter of the 14th century, tempera and gold on panel. New York, private collection (photographed on loan at The Metropolitan Museum of Art); formerly Visconti di Modrone collection, Milan.

alt: Black-and-white photograph of a crowded panel of the Crucifixion. Christ hangs on a tall cross beneath a titulus inscribed I.N.R.I., his head bowed. At left, horsemen in armour carry lances and two banners, one bearing a winged beast; below them the Virgin swoons among the holy women and is supported by a long-haired young man, Saint John. The Magdalene kneels at the foot of the cross, looking up and clasping it. At right, a young man raises the reed with the sponge; behind him a rider lifts his arm toward the cross, and a dense group of bearded elders and priests in long mantles, one with an ornamented border, turn to one another. The ground is strewn with stones.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), The Crucifixion, early 1330s (dating proposed in the recent literature), tempera on panel. Florence, Villa La Pietra, Acton Collection (New York University). Black-and-white photograph: Bologna, Fondazione Federico Zeri, Fototeca.

alt: Fresco on a narrow engaged column set into a pier. Against a dark blue-black ground stands Saint Onuphrius, full length and naked, his body covered by very long grey hair and a long white beard that fall to his waist, with a girdle of leaves at his loins; his hands are joined in prayer and his head is surrounded by a gold halo. Above him two small winged angels hold a large golden crown topped by a cross. He stands on brown, rocky ground. At the top edge appears the lower part of an octagonal frame, at the bottom the top of a round medallion.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Saint Onuphrius, c. 1336–1340, fresco on an engaged column (with Elijah above and Saint Anthony Abbot below). Bologna, San Martino Maggiore, third pier on the right, between the third and fourth bays.

alt: Upper part of a frescoed column beneath a carved stone capital with curling acanthus leaves. Below a band of red hexagonal ornament, an octagonal frame in white with red lines encloses a lobed opening on a dark blue ground. Within it is the haloed bust of the prophet Elijah, an old man with grey hair and a long white beard, in a pale mantle, holding a long unfurled scroll that curves across his chest. At the bottom edge the top of a golden crown is visible.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Bust of the Prophet Elijah, detail of the frescoed column, c. 1336–1340. Bologna, San Martino Maggiore.

alt: Detail of a frescoed column, much abraded. At the top, the bare feet of Saint Onuphrius stand on brown ground. Below, a round medallion framed in white, distorted into an oval by the curve of the column, encloses on a dark blue ground the haloed bust of Saint Anthony Abbot, an old bearded monk in a brown hooded habit, his head bowed toward an open book held in his hand. A plain patch of modern filling interrupts the top of the frame and the halo, and a horizontal crack crosses the medallion. Below it, a reddish field begins.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Bust of Saint Anthony Abbot Reading, detail of the frescoed column, c. 1336–1340. Bologna, San Martino Maggiore.

alt: Detail of the lower part of a frescoed column, heavily abraded. At the top, part of a round medallion with a blue ground and a white frame. Below it, on a reddish-brown and ochre ground, the tawny body of a lion is visible, with its mane drawn in dark curving strokes and its large clawed paws turned toward the ground, as if digging. A thin dark band closes the field at the bottom.
caption: Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi (attributed; the "Pseudo-Dalmasio" of part of the critical literature), Lions Digging the Grave of Saint Onuphrius, detail of the frescoed column, c. 1336–1340. Bologna, San Martino Maggiore.

alt: Gabled triptych with gold ground and marbled frames, shown open. The central panel shows the Crucifixion: the dead Christ on a tall cross, the swooning Virgin in black supported by Saint John and a holy woman at the left, the Magdalene in red kneeling at the foot of the cross, and at the right a soldier in armour with a shield and a red banner among a group of helmeted men. In the gable, the Coronation of the Virgin in a quatrefoil, flanked by the winged lion and ox with books. The left wing shows the angel of the Annunciation, the Virgin of Mercy sheltering kneeling devotees under her mantle, and three female saints. The right wing shows the Virgin Annunciate, the Nativity with the Virgin lying on a bed with a red border, and three male martyrs.
caption: Master of 1333 (formerly attributed to the Pseudo-Dalmasio), Triptych with the Crucifixion, the Coronation of the Virgin, the Annunciation, the Virgin of Mercy, the Nativity and Saints, dated 1333, tempera on gold ground on panel; height 135 cm, width 73 cm (museum record). Paris, Musée du Louvre, Département des Peintures, INV 20197 (Campana 324); probably from a confraternity of San Vitale, Bologna.

alt: Detached fresco with irregular, damaged edges, framed at the sides by red ornamental bands. Against a dark purple ground, the Virgin in a red gown and dark mantle sits low, nursing the Child, who is wrapped in a yellow cloth; behind her a large golden sunburst disc. Above, two flying angels with rose-garlanded hair hold the swags of a great green pavilion. At left, Saint Dominic in black and white holds a lily and a red book and presents a small kneeling bearded donor; at right, the crowned Saint Catherine of Alexandria, with her wheel, points down to a small kneeling woman in a grey veil. The lower part of the fresco is lost.
caption: Lippo di Dalmasio (attributed; also given to Dalmasio degli Scannabecchi and, in the older literature, to other Pistoiese painters), Madonna of Humility under a Pavilion with Saints Dominic and Catherine of Alexandria and Two Donors (the "Madonna del Padiglione"), c. 1380, detached fresco. Pistoia, San Domenico, refectory.

alt: Saint Dominic Altarpiece
caption: Saint Dominic Altarpiece, 1344-45, tempera and gold on panel, Central panel: 175 × 74 cm; each wing: 163 × 93 cm (ensemble: 175 × 260 cm), Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, Pisa.

alt: Madonna and Child with Saint Anne
caption: Madonna and Child with Saint Anne, 1340-45, tempera on panel, 84.9 × 56 cm (frame 101.3 × 76.5 × 14.6 cm), Princeton University Art Museum, Princeton.

alt: The Virgin and Child
caption: The Virgin and Child, c. 1345, tempera and gold on panel, 48 x 42 cm, Museo Nacional del Prado, Madrid.

alt: The Virgin and Child
caption: The Virgin and Child, c. 1325, tempera and gold on panel, 63.5 x 51.5 x 3 cm (with microclimate frame: 66.8 x 60.5 cm), Louvre Abu Dhabi.

alt: Small gilded tabernacle panel with a pointed Gothic frame and twisted colonnettes: the Virgin, seated low in a dark blue gold-patterned mantle and red gown, nurses the Christ Child against a gold ground.
caption: Our Lady of Humility, c. 1350–1355, tempera and gold on panel, 34.6 × 19.9 cm, Pinacoteca Vaticana, Vatican City.

alt: The Virgin of Humility seated on the ground nursing the Child, in a dark blue mantle with gold lozenges and a red gown with gold birds, before a white cloth of honour tied with red ribbons; a crescent moon lies at her feet.
caption: Our Lady of Humility, 1359, tempera on panel, 173 × 122 cm, Pinacoteca civica Bruno Molajoli, Fabriano.

alt: Two-register panel on gold: above, the Man of Sorrows in his tomb between two mourning angels; below, the Christ Child lying on the ground, adored by two angels, the Virgin and St Joseph.
caption: Dead Christ and angels; Adoration of Baby Jesus, c. 1360, tempera and gold on panel, 39.3 × 28.5 cm, Pinacoteca Vaticana, Vatican City.

alt: Five-part gabled polyptych: the Virgin and Child at the centre, a bishop saint and St John the Evangelist on the left, St John the Baptist and a young martyr on the right, small figures in the gables; the gold is heavily abraded.
caption: Madonna and Child between a Saint Bishop and Saints John the Evangelist, John the Baptist and Venantius; in the cusps: Christ adored by two angels between Saint Catherine of Alexandria and Saint Anthony the Abbot, follower of Allegretto Nuzi (Francescuccio Ghissi?), c. 1375–1399, tempera on panel, 122 × 173 cm, Pinacoteca civica Bruno Molajoli, Fabriano.

alt: The Virgin of Humility nursing the Child against a gold ground tooled with vine scrolls and scattered dark stars, in a dark mantle with vine leaves and a red gown patterned with birds.
caption: Our Lady of Humility, tempera and gold on panel, 95 × 77 cm, Pinacoteca civica, Fermo.

alt: The Virgin and Child enthroned cheek to cheek, in a dark blue mantle with gold lozenges before a red and gold cloth of honour, with three angels on each side, hands joined or crossed.
caption: Enthroned Madonna with Six Angels, tempera and gold on panel, 138 × 99 cm, Musée du Petit Palais, Avignon.

alt: Small hinged triptych in a glazed case on green velvet: the nursing Virgin of Humility in the centre, the Nativity in the left wing and the Crucifixion in the right, the Annunciation in the two gables.
caption: Our Lady of Humility; The Nativity; The Crucifixion; The Annunciation (top left and right), tempera on panel, 450 × 209 mm (central panel), National Trust, Polesden Lacey, Surrey.

alt: St John, at left, raises his hand toward a bier draped in red and carried by two bearers, while a kneeling man entreats him and a woman raises her arms before a white building with a tower; a red seraph hovers at upper left; the frame nameplate reads Allegretto Nuzi.
caption: The Resurrection of Drusiana, c. 1370, tempera on panel, 34.3 × 36.8 cm, Portland Art Museum, Portland.

alt: Gold-ground panel framed by a gilded arch on twisted columns. On the left, Saint John the Evangelist, haloed and wearing a pink mantle over a blue tunic, leans forward and gathers small fragments of gems from a long wooden counter, followed by a bearded, hooded disciple. On the counter lie a heap of fragments and an anvil. Facing him, a bearded philosopher in a red gown and a grey fur cape holds a hammer. Two young men stand behind the philosopher. At the upper corners, outside the arch, fragments of other figures are visible: a haloed figure in red holding a palm on the left, and a nude figure in a vat on the right.
caption: Saint John the Evangelist Correcting a Philosopher Named Crato, panel from a dismembered altarpiece of Saint John the Evangelist, c. 1370–1380. Tempera and gold leaf on panel, 35.6 × 41.3 cm (frame 55.2 × 57.1 cm). Raleigh, North Carolina Museum of Art, GL.60.17.18, Gift of the Samuel H. Kress Foundation.

alt: Gold-ground panel showing Saint John the Evangelist, haloed and wearing a blue tunic and pink mantle, at the centre. Two young men in long robes stand to his right and beg him with outstretched hands; one offers him a handful of gold. Behind them, reeds grow on a rocky slope, pebbles lie along the shore, and a sailing ship rides on a dark sea. On the left, two young men in short secular tunics watch; one points and wears a purse at his belt.
caption: Acteus and Eugenius Implore Saint John the Evangelist to Restore Their Wealth, panel from a dismembered altarpiece of Saint John the Evangelist, c. 1370–1380. Tempera and gold leaf on panel, 34.9 × 38.1 cm (frame 55.2 × 57.1 cm). Raleigh, North Carolina Museum of Art, GL.60.17.19, Gift of the Samuel H. Kress Foundation.

alt: Gold-ground panel with a punched ornamental border along the top. Saint John the Evangelist, haloed and wearing a dark tunic and rose mantle, stands at the left of centre and points to a bier covered with a red cloth. On it lies a young man wrapped in a white shroud, his eyes opening. Two bearers hold the bier poles, a man in grey kneels with joined hands, and two veiled women kneel in prayer before the saint. Mourners crowd at both sides; on the right a man in a black and orange mantle raises his hand.
caption: Saint John the Evangelist Raises Satheus to Life, panel from a dismembered altarpiece of Saint John the Evangelist, c. 1370. Tempera on wood, gold ground, overall 35.9 × 41 cm; painted surface 34.9 × 39.4 cm. New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, 69.280.1, Gift of Mrs. W. Murray Crane, 1969.

alt: Gold-ground panel framed by a gilded round arch. Above, a dark almond-shaped form fringed with short rays. On the left, a bearded young man in a red cap, salmon tunic and red hose raises his index finger heavenward and speaks to two youths in short tunics and striped hoods, one wearing a purse at his belt. On the right, Saint John the Evangelist, haloed, in a dark tunic and rose mantle, lays his hand on the head of one of two men kneeling in grey robes; the other holds out a few pieces of gold. Behind them rise reeds and a dark rocky slope. In the upper corners, outside the arch, a friar holding a red book and a bishop with a crozier.
caption: Saint John the Evangelist with Acteus and Eugenius, panel from a dismembered altarpiece of Saint John the Evangelist, c. 1370. Tempera on wood, gold ground, 36.5 × 41.3 cm. New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, 69.280.2, Gift of Mrs. W. Murray Crane, 1969.

alt: Gold-ground panel framed by a gilded arch. On the left, Saint John the Evangelist, haloed and wearing a red mantle over a dark tunic, kneels in prayer with raised hands, followed by a bearded elder in a turban. In the centre stands a small temple with a tiled roof, its walls cracking; inside, a nude idol topples from a broken column, and fallen stones lie on the ground. On the right, a man wearing a wreath, a purple mantle and red sleeves points at the temple and holds a staff, with a bearded companion behind him. In the upper right corner, outside the arch, a red seraph.
caption: Saint John the Evangelist Causes a Pagan Temple to Collapse, panel from a dismembered altarpiece of Saint John the Evangelist, c. 1370. Tempera on wood, gold ground, 35.9 × 38.7 cm. New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, 69.280.3, Gift of Mrs. W. Murray Crane, 1969.

alt: Gold-ground panel in a gilded frame with twisted colonnettes at the lower corners. On the left, Saint John the Evangelist, haloed and wearing a dark tunic and red mantle, stands upright and raises a small cup to his lips. On the bare ground in the centre lie two dead men side by side, dressed in short tunics, their heads toward the right. On the right a group of onlookers watches: a man in a red mantle and turban raises his hand in astonishment, and a white-bearded elder in a yellow mantle and hood points at the bodies. Other heads crowd behind them.
caption: Saint John the Evangelist and the Poisoned Chalice, panel from a dismembered altarpiece of Saint John the Evangelist, c. 1370–1380. Tempera and gold leaf on panel, 35.2 × 38.6 cm (frame 42.9 × 44.5 × 4.4 cm). Raleigh, North Carolina Museum of Art, GL.60.17.20, Gift of the Samuel H. Kress Foundation.

alt: Rectangular marble slab against a black background, carved with five lines of Gothic capital letters beginning with a small cross. Below the text, two pointed shields flank a shorter line giving the date; each shield bears three roundels and a central cinquefoil. The surface is weathered and slightly cracked, with a museum number on a label at the lower right.
caption: Foundation tablet of the oratory of the Virgin and Saint Thomas the Apostle, founded by Tommaso d’Andrea, bishop of Pistoia, at Casole d’Elsa, 1296. Incised slab in marble. 21.6 x 38 x 6 cm. London, Victoria and Albert Museum, inv. 5802-1859.

alt: Gothic marble wall tomb under a crocketed gable. At the apex, a roundel holds a half-figure of the blessing Christ; below it, a dark roundel shows the white Lamb of God with a cross-banner, between two small heads in medallions. Inside the arch, a painted green curtain with an orange fringe and a tassel is drawn back at both sides. On the sarcophagus lies the mitred bishop in vestments, his hands crossed. Behind him, three standing attendants hold up a draped cloth, and two kneel at his head and feet. A one-line signature runs along the moulding beneath the effigy. Below are a chest with five rosette panels, a frieze of shields alternating with rosettes, and a tablet carved with a two-column Latin epitaph.
caption: Gano di Fazio, Funerary monument of Tommaso d’Andrea, bishop of Pistoia (d. 1303), marble with painted lunette, signed, 1303–c. 1305. Casole d’Elsa, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta.

alt: Tall Gothic marble wall aedicule on volute brackets, with a crocketed gable, a pierced tracery wheel and two pinnacled piers. In a plain round-headed niche stands a life-size man in a tall cap, long belted gown and heavy mantle, holding a book to his chest and gripping a sword at his hip. Outside the piers, on separate consoles, stand a bearded elder holding a scroll and a beardless youth in a gentle sway.
caption: Marco Romano (formerly attributed to Gano di Fazio), Funerary monument of messer Porrina (Bernardino degli Albertini?), marble, c. 1309–1312. Casole d’Elsa, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta.

alt: Gothic marble wall tomb under a plain steep gable with a small carved shield at the apex. A pointed arch on two colonnettes with leaf capitals frames a fragmentary fresco of the Madonna and Child enthroned between two angels, its lower half lost. Below, the front of the sarcophagus shows in relief a bishop lying on a bier with mitre and vestments, his hands crossed. A Dominican friar reading a book stands at his head and another at his feet. Heraldic shields mark the ends of the chest, which rests on two corbels.
caption: Gano di Fazio (attributed), Funerary monument of Ranieri degli Ubertini, bishop of Volterra, marble with frescoed lunette, c. 1295–1300. 300 x 200 cm. Arezzo, San Domenico.

alt: Three marble relief panels side by side in moulded frames. Left: a small haloed youth climbs steps to knock at the arched door of a tall crenellated gateway. Centre: a haloed friar collapses at the left, held by the arm by a hooded companion, while a table laid with bowls, cups and knives tilts steeply before three seated friars, one praying; nothing falls from it. Right: a priest raises his arm at an altar with an open book, a tall candle stands unsupported in the air beside him, and a haloed friar lies collapsed on the ground.
caption: Gano di Fazio (attributed), Scenes from the Life of the Blessed Gioacchino Piccolomini: his admission to the Order; the miracle of the table; the miracle of the candle. Marble, c. 1310–1312. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale (from his tomb in Santa Maria dei Servi).

alt: Gothic marble wall tomb set in a pointed recess in a banded wall. Under two crocketed gables with trefoil openings, two standing figures lift a coffered canopy with hanging drapery above the effigy of a woman in a plain habit. The sarcophagus front bears four relief scenes, and a lower register on carved corbels holds smaller reliefs. On the outer columns, at the height of the gables, stand Gabriel and the Virgin of the Annunciation.
caption: Gano di Fazio (attributed; traditionally given to Angelo and Francesco di Pietro), Funerary monument of Saint Margaret of Cortona, marble, before 1317 or second half of the fourteenth century. Cortona, Basilica di Santa Margherita.

alt: Five marble statuettes of standing male saints displayed in a row on a dark table. From left: a bald elder with a long wavy beard; an elder with a long beard in deep corkscrew curls and a blue-lined mantle; Saint John the Baptist in a shaggy camel-hair garment beneath a blue-lined mantle; a beardless youth with short curls holding a closed book, his mantle lined in bright blue; and Saint Peter with a short beard, a brooch at his chest and a key in his hand. Several figures keep traces of blue paint and patterned borders.
caption: Gano di Fazio (attributed), Five statuettes of saints and prophets, including Saint John the Baptist and Saint Peter, marble with traces of polychromy and gilding, c. 1315–1318. Massa Marittima, Museo di Arte Sacra (former convent of San Pietro all’Orto), from the cathedral of San Cerbone.

alt: Marble half-figure of a beardless youth, cut off at the waist, turning his head to look up and away with lips slightly parted. His hair falls in tight spiral curls with drilled centres. He wears a mantle fastened at the shoulder with a square brooch, its borders and cuffs decorated with rows of drilled dots, and a square ornamental panel on the chest. With both hands he holds a small polygonal casket shaped like a miniature building, with arched openings and a lid.
caption: Gano di Fazio (attributed), Half-figure of a young saint holding a covered vessel (Saint Mary Magdalene or Saint Galgano; proposed as Caspar from an Adoration of the Magi), marble, c. 1310, 46 x 29 x 16 cm. Berlin, Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, Skulpturensammlung (Bode-Museum), inv. 2955.
