alt: Painted crucifix by Giovanni da Rimini in San Francesco, Mercatello sul Metauro: the dead Christ against a gold patterned cloth of honour, with a dark crossbeam, a blue lower shaft and a blue footrest, and polylobed gold terminals showing the mourning Virgin in a dark mantle, Saint John the Evangelist in a rose mantle, and the blessing Redeemer above a red tablet.
caption: Painted crucifix, signed and dated 1309 (or 1314), tempera and gold on panel, 300 × 227 cm, church of San Francesco, Mercatello sul Metauro.

alt: Diotallevi Crucifix by Giovanni da Rimini, Museo della Città, Rimini: the dead Christ with a transparent loincloth on a dark cross with gilded lobed terminals showing the mourning Virgin, Saint John the Evangelist and the blessing Redeemer with the Gospel book
caption: Diotallevi crucifix, 1300–05, tempera and gold on panel, 185 × 179 cm, Rimini, Museo della Città "Luigi Tonini", inv. 11 PQ.

alt: Painted crucifix attributed to Giovanni da Rimini in San Lorenzo, Talamello: the dead Christ on a dark blue cross with rectangular stepped terminals showing the mourning Virgin, Saint John the Evangelist, the blessing Redeemer above, and the skull of Adam at the foot
caption: Giovanni da Rimini (attr.), Painted crucifix, 1300–05 or after 1309 (dating disputed), tempera and gold on panel, 230 × 160 cm, church of San Lorenzo, Talamello.

alt: Painted crucifix by Giovanni da Rimini, known as the Goudstikker Crucifix. The panel is cut down to the shape of the cross itself: the dead Christ hangs against a dark green cross edged in gold, his head fallen to the right, eyes closed, with a gold cruciform halo decorated with red panels. A transparent white loincloth reveals the legs beneath. At the top, a red tablet bears the Greek christogram IC XC in white letters. Blood falls in thin trickles from the hands, side and feet. Moretti Gallery, London
caption: Painted crucifix ("Goudstikker Crucifix"), 1309–14, tempera and gold on panel, 160.5 × 130 cm, London, Moretti Gallery (formerly Jacques Goudstikker collection, Amsterdam).

alt: Gilded panel by Giovanni da Rimini divided by red ornamental bands into six scenes from the life of Christ: top row, the Nativity with the bath of the Child and the Crucifixion; middle row, the Lamentation over Christ's body on a pink tomb and the Descent into Limbo, with Christ raising Adam from a dark cave; bottom row, a winged angel on the tomb before the three Holy Women with the Risen Christ behind, and the Last Judgement with Christ enthroned in a blue mandorla above the rising dead. Gallerie Nazionali di Arte Antica, Palazzo Barberini, Rome
caption: Scenes from the Life of Christ (Nativity, Crucifixion, Lamentation, Descent into Limbo, Resurrection, Last Judgement), 1300–05, tempera and gold on panel, 52.5 × 34.5 cm, Rome, Gallerie Nazionali di Arte Antica, Palazzo Barberini, inv. 1441. Photo: Francesco Bini (Sailko), Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0.

alt: Gilded panel by Giovanni da Rimini with four scenes of unequal size. Upper left: mourners bow at an altar-tomb beneath a hexagonal canopy while, high above, Saint John the Evangelist is received in heaven by Christ, the Virgin, angels and saints. Upper right: Christ crowns the Virgin on a Gothic throne above a crowd of angels looking up. Lower left: Saint Catherine, crowned, preaches from a pulpit to philosophers and the enthroned Emperor Maxentius. Lower right: Saint Francis kneels in a rocky landscape receiving the stigmata from a red seraph, beside Saint John the Baptist. National Gallery, London
caption: Scenes from the Lives of the Virgin and other Saints, probably about 1300–05, egg tempera on wood, 54.4 × 36.5 cm, London, National Gallery, NG6656. Acquired with a generous donation from Ronald S. Lauder, 2015. Photo © The National Gallery, London, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

alt: Small gilded panel by Giovanni da Rimini in two registers. Above, the Virgin in a dark blue mantle bends her head to press her cheek against the Child, who twists toward her with his back to the viewer; two angels in white with dark wings hold a purple cloth behind them. Below, five saints stand in a row against the gold: Francis in a brown habit, the Archangel Michael with wings and a globe, a bishop saint with mitre and crozier, the crowned Catherine in red, and Clare in a black veil. Pinacoteca Comunale, Faenza.
caption: Virgin and Child with Two Angels and Saints Francis, Michael the Archangel, Augustine (?), Catherine of Alexandria and Clare, 1300–05, tempera and gold on panel, 50 × 35 cm, Faenza, Pinacoteca Comunale, inv. 92.

alt: Damaged fresco of the Dormition of the Virgin by Giovanni da Rimini in the church of Sant'Agostino, Rimini. At the centre Christ, in a red mantle, stands behind the deathbed holding the Virgin's soul as a small figure wrapped in white. Crowds of haloed apostles and young figures surround him in overlapping rows. The Virgin lies on a long dark bier, her pale face visible at the right end. The dark background has lost most of its blue paint, large patches of plaster are missing, and painted twisted columns frame the scene at both sides
caption: Dormition of the Virgin, before 1307 (possibly before 1303), fresco, Rimini, church of Sant'Agostino (formerly San Giovanni Evangelista), chapel at the base of the campanile. Photo: Sailko, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0.

alt: Hexagonal baptismal font in the Pieve di Santa Maria, Arezzo, on a stepped stone base: three white marble relief panels attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1332, set into its faces — the Baptism of Christ at the centre between the young John led into the desert and the Ecce Agnus Dei — beneath a plain moulded cornice.
caption: Giovanni di Agostino (attr.), Baptismal font with three Stories of St John the Baptist (John led into the desert, Ecce Agnus Dei, Baptism of Christ), marble reliefs in a hexagonal stone chest, c. 1332, Arezzo, Pieve di Santa Maria.

alt: Marble relief attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1332, on the baptismal font of the Pieve di Santa Maria, Arezzo: an angel flies horizontally across the top, drapery streaming over the frame's edge, arms extended toward a grove of trees on a smooth rocky hill, while below the young Baptist in his tufted camel-hair tunic climbs with hands joined in prayer, face upturned to the messenger
caption: Giovanni di Agostino (attr.), The young Baptist sent into the desert by an angel, marble relief panel of the baptismal font, c. 1332, Arezzo, Pieve di Santa Maria.

alt: Marble relief attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1332, on the baptismal font of the Pieve di Santa Maria, Arezzo: the Baptist in his camel-hair tunic stands at left among trees, arm extended toward a pressed crowd of seven figures at right, within which the haloed Christ gazes frontally at the viewer between two haloed companions
caption: Giovanni di Agostino (attr.), The Baptist points out Christ (Ecce Agnus Dei), marble relief panel of the baptismal font, c. 1332, Arezzo, Pieve di Santa Maria.

alt: Marble relief attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1332, on the baptismal font of the Pieve di Santa Maria, Arezzo: Christ stands waist-deep in the smooth mound of the Jordan, a carved drop of water running down his chest, while the Baptist lays a hand flat on his head from the left bank and three bowing angels hold his garments at either side.
caption: Giovanni di Agostino (attr.), The Baptism of Christ, marble relief panel of the baptismal font, c. 1332, Arezzo, Pieve di Santa Maria.

alt: Marble relief of the Madonna and Child enthroned between two standing angels beneath a carved canopy, signed by Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1330–1340, vestibule of the upper Oratory of San Bernardino, Siena. The sculptor's Latin signature runs along the lower frame
caption: Madonna and Child enthroned between two angels, signed ("Ioh(anne)s magist(r)i Agostini de Se(n)is me fecit"), 1330–40, marble, Siena, vestibule of the upper Oratory of San Bernardino (Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra).

alt: Chapel of Ciuto Tarlati in Arezzo Cathedral: Gothic marble aedicule by Giovanni di Agostino, 1334, with Annunciation statuettes and gable relief, framing the Crucifixion fresco attributed to the Maestro del Vescovado with a kneeling armoured donor, above a reused fourth-century sarcophagus
caption: Arezzo, Cathedral of Santi Pietro e Donato, fifth bay of the right aisle: chapel of Ciuto Tarlati. Marble aedicule and sculptures (Annunciation, gable relief) contracted with Giovanni di Agostino on 28 January 1334; Crucifixion and archivolt frescoes attributed to the Maestro del Vescovado, c. 1334 or shortly after; below, a reused fourth-century strigilated sarcophagus.

alt: Marble Sacrament tabernacle attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1331–32: the archangel Gabriel and the Virgin Annunciate flank a central door opening beneath crocketed Gothic gables; from Sant'Eugenio a Monistero, now in the chapel of Palazzo Chigi Saracini, Siena
caption: Giovanni di Agostino (attr.), Sacrament tabernacle with the Annunciation, 1331–32, marble with traces of red polychromy, from the church of Sant'Eugenio a Monistero; Siena, Palazzo Chigi Saracini, chapel.

alt: Triangular marble gable relief attributed to Giovanni di Agostino: Mary Magdalene, clothed only in her long hair, hands joined in prayer, raised toward heaven by two flying angels; c. 1333–34, Basilica di San Francesco, Siena
caption: Giovanni di Agostino (attr.), Mary Magdalene raised by two angels, gable relief from a dismantled monumental canopy, c. 1333–34 (current guides: c. 1340), marble, Siena, Basilica di San Francesco, Cappella Turchi (second chapel to the right of the Cappella Maggiore).

alt: Marble relief attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1331, from a dismembered saint's shrine in Volterra: an elderly bearded saint at left hands a garment down to a bowing pauper, while five more poor men with staffs, sacks and wrapped heads press forward to receive; Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra, Volterra
caption: Attributed to Giovanni di Agostino (Kreytenberg), The saint distributing his goods to the poor, relief from the dismembered shrine of a saint formerly believed to be St Octavian, c. 1331, marble, Volterra, Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra (since 2017 in the church of Sant'Agostino).

alt: Marble relief attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1331, from a dismembered saint's shrine in Volterra: a procession of tonsured religious carries the bearded corpse of the saint shoulder-high toward the arched portal of a crenellated church at right, accompanied by a mitred bishop and a young acolyte at left; Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra, Volterra.
caption: Attributed to Giovanni di Agostino (Kreytenberg), The translation of the saint's body, relief from the dismembered shrine of a saint formerly believed to be St Octavian, c. 1331, marble, Volterra, Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra (since 2017 in the church of Sant'Agostino).

alt: Fragmentary marble relief attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1331: a winged angel with a soft oval face and downcast eyes, mantle bordered by an embroidered hem, raises one hand high and lowers the other over the surviving folds of a curtain whose swags hang from the top edge; the slab is broken diagonally where the curtain and the saint's effigy once continued; Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra, Volterra.
caption: Attributed to Giovanni di Agostino (Kreytenberg), Curtain-bearing angel, fragment from the dismembered shrine of a saint formerly believed to be St Octavian, c. 1331, marble, Volterra, Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra (since 2017 in the church of Sant'Agostino).

alt: Fragmentary marble relief attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1331: a winged angel in profile leans left with its whole body, one raised hand gripping the gathered knot of a great curtain whose swags fill the upper corner, the other hand lowered to press the cloth against its hip; from a dismembered saint's shrine, Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra, Volterra
caption: Attributed to Giovanni di Agostino (Kreytenberg), Curtain-drawing angel, fragment from the dismembered shrine of a saint formerly believed to be St Octavian, c. 1331, marble, Volterra, Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra (since 2017 in the church of Sant'Agostino).

alt: Marble effigy of a dead saint attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1331, from a dismembered shrine in Volterra: an elderly bearded man in a hooded religious habit lies full length, hands crossed at the wrists on his body, head tilted slightly outward, the drapery running in long parallel folds to the feet; Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra, Volterra
caption: Attributed to Giovanni di Agostino (Kreytenberg), Effigy of the dead saint, from the dismembered shrine of a saint formerly believed to be St Octavian, c. 1331, marble, Volterra, Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra (since 2017 in the church of Sant'Agostino).

alt: Detail of the marble head of a dead saint attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1331: an elderly bearded face framed by a monastic cowl, eyes closed, lips slightly parted, forehead marked by a vertical groove, the long wavy beard articulated by rows of drilled dots; from a dismembered shrine, Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra, Volterra.
caption: Attributed to Giovanni di Agostino (Kreytenberg), Effigy of the dead saint, detail of the head, from the dismembered shrine of a saint formerly believed to be St Octavian, c. 1331, marble, Volterra, Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra (since 2017 in the church of Sant'Agostino).

alt: Weathered marble statue attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1331, from a dismembered saint's shrine in Volterra: a seated, veiled Madonna with heavily eroded features inclines her head toward the Christ Child, who stands upright on her knee in a belted tunic, reaching one hand toward her face; photographed against rough masonry; Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra, Volterra.
caption: Attributed to Giovanni di Agostino (Kreytenberg), Madonna and Child from the presentation group, from the dismembered shrine of a saint formerly believed to be St Octavian, c. 1331, marble, Volterra, Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra (since 2017 in the church of Sant'Agostino).

alt: Two views of a weathered marble group attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1331, from a dismembered saint's shrine in Volterra: a youthful figure with a rolled bob of hair kneels in prayer between two standing angels, one with loose waves laying a large hand on his back, the other with drilled coiled curls, hand on breast and lips parted in speech; Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra, Volterra.
caption: Attributed to Giovanni di Agostino (Kreytenberg), Angels presenting the commended figure, from the presentation group (shown in two views), from the dismembered shrine of a saint formerly believed to be St Octavian, c. 1331, marble, Volterra, Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra (since 2017 in the church of Sant'Agostino).

alt: Two marble fragments of a tabernacle attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, c. 1331, set into a plastered museum wall: above, a triangular gable with the half-figure of Christ blessing in a mandorla, cross-nimbed, a book at the frame; below, a cusped ogee-arched niche opening into a dark cavity, flanked by pilaster strips of scrolling vine; Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra, Volterra
caption: Attributed to Giovanni di Agostino (Kreytenberg), Fragments of a tabernacle with the blessing Christ, from the ensemble of the dismembered shrine of a saint formerly believed to be St Octavian, c. 1331, marble, Volterra, Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra (since 2017 in the church of Sant'Agostino).

alt: Tall narrow marble high relief attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, Pinacoteca Nazionale di Siena: a standing veiled Madonna, her head inclined toward the Child once carried on her left arm, the surfaces rough and abraded, the Child largely lost to a break, the drapery's fold system legible beneath an unfinished or weathered skin
caption: Giovanni di Agostino (attr.), Madonna and Child, marble high relief, second quarter of the 14th century, Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale. The surface, deeply abraded and perhaps never brought to completion, preserves the design in its formative state.

alt: Marble figure of Christ blessing, attributed to Giovanni di Agostino: a pale stone half-length with long hair, a beard, draped robes and the right hand raised before the chest, on a black ground
caption: Giovanni di Agostino (attr.), Christ Blessing (Redentore benedicente), c. 1340, marble, from San Domenico, Siena; Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale.

alt: Marble relief attributed to Giovanni di Agostino: Saint Galgano, a beardless youth with wavy hair, inclines his head as he rests one hand on the hilt of a sword planted in a rock at lower left and gathers his mantle with the other, foliage in the upper corners
caption: Giovanni di Agostino (attr.), Saint Galgano Plunging His Sword into the Rock, 1335–40, marble relief, from the church of Santa Lucia, Poggibonsi; Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. IBS 40.

alt: Marble half-length figure of a bearded apostle, identified as Saint Paul and attributed to Giovanni di Agostino: head turned to the viewer's left, a deeply folded mantle, the lowered hand at the left beside a beaded rectangular object, the lower edge broken off
caption: Giovanni di Agostino (attr.), Saint Paul, first half of the fourteenth century, marble, Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale (reported provenance: Sant'Agostino).

alt: Gothic wall monument of the jurist and poet Cino da Pistoia, attributed to Agostino di Giovanni, 1337–1339: a sarcophagus carved with Cino lecturing to students, statues of the master teaching among four disciples above, under a canopy on twisted columns crowned by an aedicule with the Virgin and Child; Pistoia Cathedral
caption: Agostino di Giovanni (attr.; contract awarded to Cellino di Nese, 11 February 1337; final payment 27 December 1339), Funerary monument of Cino dei Sighibuldi, called Cino da Pistoia, marble, Pistoia, Cathedral of San Zeno, right aisle.

alt: Marble statue group from the tomb of Cino da Pistoia, attributed to Agostino di Giovanni, 1337–1339: the jurist, seated at larger scale in doctor's cap and gown, raises his right hand in a teaching gesture beside a small colonnette, flanked by four smaller standing students holding books and scrolls; Pistoia Cathedral
caption: Agostino di Giovanni (attr.), Cino da Pistoia teaching among four students, detail of the funerary monument of Cino dei Sighibuldi, 1337–1339, marble (Cino's right hand restored in stucco), Pistoia, Cathedral of San Zeno.

alt: Marble sarcophagus relief from the tomb of Cino da Pistoia, attributed to Agostino di Giovanni, 1337–1339: the jurist lectures from a tall lectern at left while nine students follow at sloped desks — listening, writing, conferring and reading — and a figure stands at the school door at right; Pistoia Cathedral
caption: Agostino di Giovanni (attr.), Cino da Pistoia lecturing to his students, front relief of the sarcophagus, funerary monument of Cino dei Sighibuldi, 1337–1339, marble, Pistoia, Cathedral of San Zeno.

alt: Marble baptismal font attributed to Giovanni di Agostino, 14th century, Montepulciano Cathedral: a polygonal basin carved with the Baptism of Christ and attendant figures, on a stem formed of three standing Apostles back to back, rough octagonal base
caption: Attributed to Giovanni di Agostino (the basin with the Baptism reliefs; the supporting Apostles referred to Agostino di Giovanni), Baptismal font, marble, under way c. 1337–39, from the old Pieve di Santa Maria; Montepulciano, Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, baptistery (first chapel on the left), before Andrea della Robbia's Altare dei Gigli (c. 1512).

alt: Openwork marble relief attributed to Giovanni di Agostino: the Madonna and Child enthroned beneath pierced Gothic canopies, between Saint Catherine holding a book and Saint John the Baptist with his scroll, c. 1340–50, Cleveland Museum of Art
caption: Giovanni di Agostino (attr.) Dalton by his nephews, George S. Kendrick and Harry D. Kendrick).

alt: Upright panel with a pointed cusped arch carved in relief, its spandrels filled with gilded foliage, shown against a black background. On a gold ground the Virgin sits on a green floor beside a patterned cushion, in a dark blue mantle with a punched border over a pink dress, her head inclined and her halo inscribed AVE MARIA GRATIA PLENA DOMINUS TECUM. She nurses the Child, who lies across her lap wrapped in a cloth patterned in red, white and gold, his bare legs crossed, sucking at her breast and looking out at the viewer. Losses in the flesh tones reveal the green underpaint in the faces and hands.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola (attributed), Madonna of Humility, c. 1330–1340. Tempera and gold on panel. Venice, Galleria Giorgio Franchetti alla Ca' d'Oro. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Upright panel in a gilded rectangular frame with a dentilled cornice and a base inscribed in gold on black AVE MARIA GRATIA PLENA DOMINUS TECO. Within a pointed cusped arch on a richly tooled gold ground, the Virgin sits low, her deep blue mantle spreading in a broad curve to the lower edge, its gold border falling in loops at the right. She wears a dress of gold brocade and inclines her head over the Child, who lies in her lap in a gold-patterned robe, nursing at her breast and holding it with one hand, his bare legs crossed. In the upper corners, outside the arch, small half-length angels with gold haloes crowd together, three at each side, looking towards the Virgin.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola, Madonna of Humility with Angels, c. 1330–1340. Tempera and gold on panel, 76.8 × 47 cm. Williamstown, Massachusetts, Williams College Museum of Art, 60.13; Samuel H. Kress Collection. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Upright panel in a plain modern frame, its original pointed arch preserved only at the left and its gold ground largely worn to the red bole, with a large loss at the right. The Virgin, in a dark blue mantle scattered with gold patterns and edged with a punched border, over a pink dress, sits low with her head steeply inclined, eyes half closed. With her right hand she offers her breast to the Child, who nurses, held in her left arm; he wears a red tunic under an orange mantle patterned with small blue motifs. A red cushion is visible at the lower left, and the Virgin's mantle spreads over the ground at her feet.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola (attributed), Madonna of the Milk, c. 1330–1340. Tempera and gold on panel. Palermo, Galleria Regionale della Sicilia, Palazzo Abatellis. Photo: Fabrizio Garrisi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons, cropped.

alt: A five-part polyptych on gold grounds, displayed against a brick wall. In the taller central panel, under a pointed trilobed arch, the Virgin in a dark blue mantle, partly lost at the left, over an orange dress, holds the naked Child, who wears a coral pendant and grasps a goldfinch. At the left, under round trilobed arches, Saint Bona in a black habit and white veil and wimple joins her hands in prayer, and Saint John the Baptist, with long hair and beard and a violet mantle over his hair shirt, points to an open scroll. At the right Saint Mary Magdalene, in a red mantle, holds an ointment jar, and Saint Bartholomew, with a long dark beard, holds a knife and a red book. In the gabled pinnacles above, Christ blessing with an open book at the centre and, at the sides, half-length saints including a mitred bishop and Saint Anthony Abbot with his white beard. The bases carry painted inscriptions.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola, Polyptych of the Madonna and Child with Saints Bona, John the Baptist, Mary Magdalene and Bartholomew, signed and dated "MCCC[.]", read as 1350. Tempera and gold on panel, 215 × 148 cm. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, inv. 1595; from the church of Santa Marta. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The central compartment of the polyptych with its gabled pinnacle. In the pinnacle, half-length Christ in a blue mantle and red stole over an orange robe blesses and holds an open book with large letters. Below, under a pointed trilobed arch with a row of dentils above, the Virgin in a dark blue mantle, largely lost at the left, holds the Child, who grasps a goldfinch; the base carries the remains of an inscription.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola, The central compartment with Christ blessing, from the Santa Marta polyptych. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, inv. 1595. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons, cropped.

alt: Close view of the Virgin and Child. The Virgin, with a long oval face, slanting eyes and a white veil under her dark mantle edged with a gold border, inclines her head; her orange dress has a punched gold neckline. The plump Child, naked but for a patterned cloth, wears a coral pendant on a dark cord and holds a goldfinch with a red face by its wings. The punched haloes and the spandrels are tooled with foliage.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola, The Virgin and Child, from the Santa Marta polyptych. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, inv. 1595. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Saint Bona under a round trilobed arch, half-length, in a black habit with a white veil, a white wimple and a white scapular-like collar bordered with a band of pseudo-lettering. She joins her hands in prayer and holds a small double-armed cross with fleur-de-lis ends. In the pinnacle above, a bearded bishop in a mitre and a patterned cope, with a dark habit beneath, holds a book.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola, Saint Bona, with a bishop saint in the pinnacle, from the Santa Marta polyptych. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, inv. 1595. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Saint John the Baptist under a round trilobed arch, with long brown hair and beard and a sorrowful expression, wearing a pale violet mantle over a camel-hair garment and an orange lining. He points to himself and holds an open scroll inscribed Ecce agnus dei ecce qui tollit peccata mundi. In the pinnacle above, a balding bearded bishop in a patterned vestment with a jewelled orphrey holds a red book.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola, Saint John the Baptist, with a bishop saint in the pinnacle, from the Santa Marta polyptych. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, inv. 1595. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Saint Mary Magdalene under a round trilobed arch, in a red mantle drawn over her head and lined with blue, holding a white ointment jar with a domed lid. In the pinnacle above, a bearded bishop wearing a low mitre and a patterned cope blesses and holds a red book.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola, Saint Mary Magdalene, with a bishop saint in the pinnacle, from the Santa Marta polyptych. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, inv. 1595. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Saint Bartholomew under a round trilobed arch, frontal, with curly reddish hair and a long pointed beard, in a mantle patterned with small white and brown flowers over a dark tunic. He holds a knife and a red book with gold clasps. The base bears the remains of his name. In the pinnacle above, Saint Anthony Abbot, with a long grey beard and a dark habit, holds a book and a tau-shaped staff.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola, Saint Bartholomew, with Saint Anthony Abbot in the pinnacle, from the Santa Marta polyptych. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, inv. 1595. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Half-length Saint Anthony Abbot on a gold ground under a round arch with carved cusps, the spandrels filled with gilded foliage in relief, all within a plain moulded frame. The aged saint, with a long, wavy white beard and furrowed brow, looks sideways to the left. He wears a black hooded cloak over a brown habit, with a tawny cap visible under the hood. His right hand rests on the curved handle of a tau-shaped staff; in his left he holds a book, its spine with small blue clasps.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola, Saint Anthony Abbot, about 1350. Egg tempera on wood, 61.5 × 36 cm. London, National Gallery, NG3896; presented by Henry Wagner, 1924. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Four panels displayed side by side before a brick wall: a taller central Madonna and Child flanked by three narrower panels with half-length saints, John the Baptist at the left, Peter and Bartholomew at the right. Each figure stands on a gold ground under a round arch with carved cusps; the lateral panels have gilded foliage in relief in the spandrels and a row of small dentils along the top.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola, Madonna and Child with Saints John the Baptist, Peter and Bartholomew, c. 1340–1360. Tempera and gold on panel; Madonna 79.5 × 48.3 cm, saints c. 64.5 × 35 cm. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, inv. 1597, 1596, 1598, 1599; from the Zucchetti collection, given in 1796. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Half-length Virgin under a cusped round arch on a gold ground, with punched haloes. She wears a dark blue mantle with a star on the shoulder and a gold-patterned border over a pink dress, and a fine white veil. She looks down at the Child, seated on her left arm, who wears a coral pendant on a blue cord and a red cloth with a yellow lining over a white loincloth; he looks up at her and grasps her veil. Her right hand, below, holds a white ribbed form.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola, Madonna and Child, from the Zucchetti panels. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, inv. 1597. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Half-length Saint John the Baptist under a cusped round arch, with gilded foliage in relief in the spandrels. He has long dark hair and beard, wears a grey hair shirt under a blue mantle lined with yellow, gestures with his right hand and holds a scroll inscribed ECCE AGNUS DEI ECCE QUI TOLLIT.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola, Saint John the Baptist, from the Zucchetti panels. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, inv. 1596. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons, cropped.

alt: Half-length Saint Peter under a cusped round arch with gilded foliage in the spandrels. He has short curly grey hair and beard and a furrowed brow, and wears a blue tunic under a yellow mantle with a patterned border. In his right hand he holds a large red key, in his left a black book with red clasps.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola, Saint Peter, from the Zucchetti panels. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, inv. 1598. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Half-length Saint Bartholomew under a cusped round arch with gilded foliage in the spandrels. He has curly reddish-brown hair and a long pointed beard, and wears a mantle patterned with small flowers in blue, red and brown, lined in black. He holds a knife and a red book with clasps.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola, Saint Bartholomew, from the Zucchetti panels. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, inv. 1599. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Half-length Virgin and Child on a worn gold ground under a round arch, with a moulded red base below. In the green spandrels, painted with dark scrolling ornament and small triangles, two gold roundels hold the Annunciation: the angel at the left, much worn, and the Virgin Annunciate at the right. The Virgin, in a dark green-black mantle with a yellow lining over a red dress, smiles faintly and looks out at the viewer; with her right hand she holds a small bird by a string. The Child, naked but for a white cloth wrapped around his lower body, sits on her left arm, turns his face up to her and touches her cheek with his outstretched hand.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola (attributed), Madonna and Child, c. 1350. Tempera and gold on panel. Grosseto, Museo Archeologico e d'Arte della Maremma; from the church of San Michele, later in Grosseto Cathedral. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons, cropped.

alt: Upright panel with a rounded top, its frame lost. On a gold ground, worn at the upper right, the Virgin sits on a white marble throne with green cornices and narrow inlaid bands of blue and gold, its armrests ending in small carved finials; a red cloth hangs behind her. She wears a deep blue mantle with a star on the shoulder and a gold border over a pink dress, and her halo is inscribed AVE MARIA GRATIA PLENA DOMINUS TE[...], the end hidden behind the Child's halo. The Child, seated on her left knee and wrapped from the waist in a gold-patterned orange cloth, wears a coral pendant and a small cross, grasps the edge of her mantle with one hand and holds a goldfinch in the other. At the lower right, very small, a donor in a black hooded habit kneels with joined hands on the step of the throne.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola, Madonna and Child Enthroned with a Benedictine Donor, c. 1350–1355. Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo; from the church of San Vito. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Detached fresco framed by bands of geometric inlay with small coats of arms. At the left, under an arcade carried on slender columns, the angel Gabriel kneels in a pink robe patterned with red flowers, his wings of red, white and black feathers raised behind him, a branch of lilies above. At the centre the Virgin sits frontally on a throne in a dark mantle over a red dress, an open book on her knee, one hand on her breast. At the right, before a red tower and a green building, the Virgin in a dark mantle over red greets Elizabeth, older, in a grey-pink mantle, the two women touching each other's arms.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola (attributed), The Annunciation and the Visitation, 1350s. Detached fresco. Pisa, church of San Martino. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Detached fresco of a bedchamber seen in a boxed interior with red walls. Elizabeth, haloed, lies in a bed with a chequered red, green and ochre cover, propped on her elbow, and reaches towards a bowl offered by a young attendant at the left, who wears a close-fitting orange dress with a low neckline and long sleeves patterned in dark scrolls, her hair dressed in braids. In the foreground the Virgin, seated on the floor in a dark mantle, holds the newborn John in striped swaddling. At the right Zacharias, haloed, sits in a green mantle and writes the child's name on a tablet, while women look in at the door. A large crack and losses run down the right side.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola (attributed), The Birth and Naming of Saint John the Baptist, 1350s. Detached fresco. Pisa, church of San Martino. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Two adjacent detached frescoes under a geometric frieze, both with round losses at the top. At the left, the Nativity: under a wooden shed the Virgin reclines beside a box-shaped manger in which the swaddled Child lies, with the ox and ass behind; Joseph sits wrapped in an orange mantle in the foreground; angels fly above and announce the birth to a shepherd, while two shepherds, one playing a pipe, stand at the right. At the right, the Adoration of the Magi: the Virgin sits under a shed with the Child on her knee, the eldest king kneels to kiss his foot, and the two younger kings stand with their gifts, while a groom and the horses of their train appear behind.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola (attributed), The Nativity and the Adoration of the Magi, 1350s. Detached frescoes. Pisa, church of San Martino. Photo: Samuele, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Detached fresco in a painted frame, with a geometric inlaid frieze at the top and a large round loss at the upper centre. The scene is set in and before a temple shown as a long building with a grey tiled roof, slender columns and small round and arched windows, with towers and a red-roofed house behind against a dark sky. At the left Joseph, in a red mantle, holds two doves; beside him the Virgin, in a dark mantle over a red dress, holds the Child, who stretches out his arms towards the aged Simeon, in a pale robe, who reaches out to receive him. At the right the prophetess Anna, in a black veil and white wimple, joins her hands behind an altar covered with a white cloth with black wavy bands, on which stand a vessel and a dove. A small modern plaque at the foot names Giovanni di Nicola.
caption: Giovanni di Nicola (attributed), The Presentation in the Temple, 1350s. Detached fresco. Pisa, church of San Martino. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Five panels shown side by side against a black background. At the centre, taller and with a pointed top, the Virgin in a dark blue mantle with a gold border and a star on the shoulder, over a red dress, holds the Child, wrapped in a pink cloth, who reaches up to the neckline of her dress and looks into her face. At the left, on two rectangular panels cut at the top, Saint Paul, bald with a long dark beard, holds a sword and a red book, and Saint John the Baptist, with long dark hair and a hair shirt under a green mantle lined with red, points to a scroll. At the right a young female saint crowned with a wreath of red and white flowers, in a red dress embroidered with gold, holds a palm, and Saint Peter, with curly white hair and beard, in a green tunic and an orange mantle, holds a book with metal clasps. All the figures are half-length on gold grounds.
caption: Francesco Traini (formerly attributed to Giovanni di Nicola), Madonna and Child with Saints Paul, John the Baptist, a virgin martyr and Peter, c. 1325–1345. Tempera and gold on panel; Madonna 80 × 58 cm, Saint Paul 58 × 39.5 cm, Saint John the Baptist 59.5 × 38.5 cm. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, inv. 5727 (Madonna), 1591 (Paul), 1592 (Baptist); from the Zucchetti collection and the Opera del Duomo. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Tall panel with a pointed arch and a gabled pinnacle, shown against a dark background. In the pinnacle, Christ in a pink robe and blue mantle blesses and holds an open book, above red seraphim. Below, on a gold ground, the Virgin, with reddish hair braided around her head under a dark mantle, much of which is lost down to the preparation, inclines her head towards the Child. He wears a pink robe, stretches up his arm to touch her chin and holds a small bird in his other hand; she supports him with a long, slender hand. The lower part of the panel is largely lost, and a plain modern strip closes the base.
caption: Anonymous painter from Fabriano active in Perugia (formerly attributed to Giovanni di Nicola), Madonna and Child, with Christ Blessing, central panel of a polyptych, c. 1360–1365. Tempera and gold on panel; the polyptych 140 × 237 cm overall. Perugia, Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria, inv. 12. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Lateral panel with a pointed arch; the pinnacle above is a later replacement in plain wood. Saint Lawrence, young and beardless, in a tonsure-like cap, wears a deacon's dalmatic of olive green patterned with small gold flowers and with embroidered bands; he holds the gridiron of his martyrdom in front of him and a palm, now largely lost, in his right hand. Paint losses at the left edge and along the base.
caption: Anonymous painter from Fabriano active in Perugia (formerly attributed to Giovanni di Nicola), Saint Lawrence, lateral panel of the polyptych, c. 1360–1365. Tempera and gold on panel. Perugia, Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria, inv. 12. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Lateral panel with a pointed arch and a gabled pinnacle, the frame riddled with worm holes. In the pinnacle the angel Gabriel, in pink and blue, kneels and raises his hand in salutation. Below, Saint John the Baptist, with long dark curling hair and beard, wears a pale violet mantle over a hair garment belted with a white cord; he points upwards with his right hand and holds a scroll inscribed with the beginning of Ecce agnus dei. A vertical loss runs down the mantle at the centre.
caption: Anonymous painter from Fabriano active in Perugia (formerly attributed to Giovanni di Nicola), Saint John the Baptist, with the angel of the Annunciation, lateral panel of the polyptych, c. 1360–1365. Tempera and gold on panel. Perugia, Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria, inv. 12. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Lateral panel with a pointed arch and a gabled pinnacle. In the pinnacle the Virgin Annunciate, in a dark mantle over a red dress, stands with hands raised beside a lectern with a book. Below, a bearded apostle with long brown hair, in a pink tunic and a light blue mantle, looks to the left; the left half of the panel and the lower part have lost most of their paint, down to the wood.
caption: Anonymous painter from Fabriano active in Perugia (formerly attributed to Giovanni di Nicola), An apostle, with the Virgin of the Annunciation, lateral panel of the polyptych, c. 1360–1365. Tempera and gold on panel, 104.5 × 41 cm. Perugia, Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria, inv. 12. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Lateral panel with a pointed arch and a gabled pinnacle. In the pinnacle, a small half-length figure in pink holds a red object. Below, a young female saint with reddish hair falling to her shoulders, in a pink mantle over a red dress patterned in gold with a tasselled cord at the neck, holds a blue book decorated with gold and a sprig of white flowers.
caption: Anonymous painter from Fabriano active in Perugia (formerly attributed to Giovanni di Nicola), A female saint, lateral panel of the polyptych, c. 1360–1365. Tempera and gold on panel. Perugia, Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria, inv. 12. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A five-part polyptych in three tiers, with a richly carved and gilded frame of twisted colonnettes, cusped arches and gabled pinnacles, shown without its predella against a black background. At the centre the Virgin, crowned, in a dark mantle over a red dress, sits on a marble throne and holds the Child in a pink robe. At the sides stand four full-length saints: Nicholas in a red cope with a crozier, Jerome in a white habit with a red book, Benedict in a white habit with a staff and book, and Margaret richly dressed, with a cross. In the middle tier, eight small half-length saints in pairs and, above the centre, the Annunciation; in the pinnacles, Christ blessing at the centre and four prophets with scrolls.
caption: Cecco di Pietro, Polyptych from Agnano, c. 1386–1395. Tempera and gold on panel, c. 295 × 265 cm. Pisa, Palazzo Blu; from Agnano, San Giuliano Terme. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The Baptistery of Bergamo
caption: The Baptistery of Bergamo, Piazza Vecchia, Città Alta, Bergamo.

alt: The North Portal (Protiro) of Santa Maria Maggiore
caption: The North Portal (Protiro) of Santa Maria Maggiore, Città Alta, Bergamo.

alt: The South Portal (Protiro) of Santa Maria Maggiore
caption: The South Portal (Protiro) of Santa Maria Maggiore, Città Alta, Bergamo.

alt: Giuliano da Rimini, Virgin and Child Enthroned with Saints, 1307, tempera and gold on panel, Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, Boston: the Virgin enthroned with the Child between censing angels and kneeling women, flanked by eight saints in two registers under arcades on twisted columns — Francis, John the Baptist, Clare and Catherine on the left; John the Evangelist, Mary Magdalene, Agnes and Lucy on the right
caption: Virgin and Child Enthroned with Saints, 1307, tempera and gold on panel, 164 x 300 cm, Boston, Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum. Photo: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, Boston (www.gardnermuseum.org).

alt: Giuliano da Rimini, Crucifixion with the Virgin and St John the Evangelist, c. 1307-08, detached fresco from the chapter house of the Servite convent of San Pellegrino, Forlì: the crucified Christ on an ochre cross against a dark blue-green ground, with the half-length mourning Virgin in a dark mantle at the left and the young St John resting his cheek on his hand at the right, all three with gold rayed haloes
caption: Crucifixion with the Virgin and St John the Evangelist, 1307–08, detached fresco, 137 × 220 cm, Complesso di San Pellegrino (Palazzo dei Servi di Maria), Forlì.

alt: Giuliano da Rimini, Virgin and Child Enthroned, c. 1307-1310, fresco, Oratorio della Madonna del Carmine, Urbania: the Virgin in a dark blue mantle over a patterned crimson dress seated on a Gothic throne with pinnacled uprights and inlaid panels, holding the standing Christ Child in a rose-red tunic who reaches up toward her face, both with gold rayed haloes, within an arched Renaissance frame
caption: Virgin and Child Enthroned, 1307–10, fresco, Oratorio della Madonna del Carmine, Urbania.

alt: Giuliano da Rimini, Triptych of the Coronation of the Virgin, c. 1320, tempera and gold on panel, Museo della Città, Rimini: in the centre Christ crowns the Virgin, both enthroned on a patterned textile, with the Crucifixion in the gable above and Annunciation roundels; on the left wing a female martyr saint and St John the Baptist below the Mocking of Christ; on the right wing St John the Evangelist and St Andrew below the Lamentation, all within gilded Gothic framing with crocketed gables and twisted colonnettes
caption: The Coronation of the Virgin with Saints ("Norfolk Triptych"), c. 1320, tempera and gold on panel, central panel 190.5 × 71.5 cm, wings 155 × 67 cm each, Fondazione Cassa di Risparmio di Rimini, on deposit at the Museo della Città, Rimini.

alt: Crucifixion fresco attributed to Giuliano da Rimini, c. 1310–1320, in the pointed lunette of the church of San Marco at Jesi: Christ on the cross at the centre between the gold discs of sun and moon, angels gathering at his wounds, the Magdalene embracing the foot of the cross, the swooning Virgin among the holy women at the left, and at the right a crowd of soldiers with lances, trumpets and red banners around the haloed centurion on a white horse, all beneath a blue vault with ornamental bands
caption: Crucifixion, 1310–20, fresco, church of San Marco, Jesi. Attributed to Giuliano da Rimini (the attribution is debated between Giuliano and Giovanni da Rimini).

alt: Head of the crucified Christ, fragment of a painted cross attributed to Giuliano da Rimini, c. 1320, tempera and gold on panel, Fondazione Cassa di Risparmio di Rimini: the dead Christ's head fallen toward his right shoulder, eyes closed, long dark hair spreading over the shoulders, against a gold ground with traces of the punched halo and ornamented borders
caption: Head of the Crucified Christ (fragment of a painted cross), c. 1320, tempera and gold on panel, c. 30 × 20 cm, Fondazione Cassa di Risparmio di Rimini, Rimini. Attributed to Giuliano da Rimini.

alt: Painted cross in the church of San Francesco at Sassoferrato, c. 1310–1320, tempera and gold on panel, shown in a black-and-white archival photograph: the dead Christ hangs against an apron decorated with a rosette-patterned textile, head fallen to his right shoulder within a large punched halo; the shaped cross has eight-lobed star terminals, with a blessing figure at the summit and abraded mourning figures at the ends of the arms; the paint surface shows extensive flaking losses
caption: Painted Cross, 1310–20, tempera and gold on panel, church of San Francesco, Sassoferrato. Attribution debated between Giuliano da Rimini and Giovanni da Rimini. Photo: Fondazione Federico Zeri, Università di Bologna, Fototeca Zeri.

alt: White marble reliquary shrine in the form of a sarcophagus, photographed against a black background. The sloping lid carries five roundels with half-length figures, the Virgin and Child at the centre, set in carved foliage. The chest below shows three framed narrative reliefs with horsemen, landscapes and a city gate, separated by ornamental bands, above a stepped moulded base bearing a Latin inscription.
caption: Arca di San Cerbone (Reliquary Shrine of Saint Cerbonius), 1324. Marble with traces of polychromy and gilding. Massa Marittima, Cathedral of San Cerbone, canons' choir. Long side with the Virgin and Child on the lid and scenes 5–7 of the saint's legend on the chest.

alt: A marble wall tomb set in a round-arched niche, photographed against a black background. The arch is framed by a broad border of alternating dark and light squares and red and blue chevrons. Inside the niche, the effigy of the deceased lies on its back, head resting on a cushion, on top of a casket whose front has three shields alternating with two plain square panels. A thin band of inscription runs along the moulding beneath this casket, above a cornice with small dentils. The large chest below carries a single long relief. On the left, a teacher sits at a lectern with an open book. Beside him, more than a dozen students in long robes sit in two rows, most holding books, some reading, some turning towards one another. The base below has five lion masks.
caption: Funerary monument of Guglielmo di Ciliano, c. 1324–1325, reassembled with elements of the tomb of Niccolò Aringhieri (d. 1374). Marble. Width: 232 cm, Depth: 23.5 cm. Siena, Università degli Studi, courtyard of the Palazzo del Rettorato; from the church of San Domenico, Siena.

alt: A standing marble statuette of a friar, photographed against a black background. The hood of his habit is drawn up over his head, framing a face with a fringe of tonsured hair; the nose and lower face are badly worn. His right hand is raised before his chest in blessing, with the fingers broken. His left hand holds a closed book against his side, its spine marked by raised bands. A knotted cord hangs from his waist down the front of the figure and ends in a loop near the knee. The habit falls in long, nearly vertical folds to the feet. The greyish-white marble is worn and chipped, especially on the face and along the edges.
caption: Blessing Friar with a Book, after 1324. Marble from the Montagnola Senese, 73.8 × 20.5 × 14.2 cm. Asciano, Castello di Gallico, Collezione Salini; formerly Milan, private collection (R. Bartalini, La Collezione Salini, II, 2009, pp. 68–75, cat. 11).

alt: The front of a marble tomb chest on a stepped base, set against a wall decorated with mosaic. At the top, the white marble effigy of the archbishop lies on a bier, his head at the right, against a gold mosaic ground framed by bands of green and red tesserae and by pilasters with a red and green scale pattern. The upper casket below carries four chequered shields, each flanked by small carved foliage scrolls. The main chest has three fields. On the left is the Annunciation, set before a crenellated building with an arcade and a staircase. In the centre is a damaged inscribed tablet in Roman capitals, in which the words DE TABIATIS, SANCTU[M] PROCLAMANTIBUS and INSIGNITAM can be read. On the right is the Adoration of the Magi, under round arches, with small figures looking down from a gallery and horses, attendants and a dog below. A long band of worn Gothic lettering runs beneath the chest. The lowest register has a frieze of acanthus scrolls enclosing small heads and animals, with a chequered shield at each end. Reddish modern elements fill gaps in the cornices and mouldings.
caption: Funerary monument of Archbishop Guidotto de' Tabiati (d'Abbiate), c. 1326–1333. Carrara marble, in a modern reassembly with mosaic surround. Messina, Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta.

alt: A nineteenth-century wood engraving in fine black lines showing the front of a marble tomb. At the top, the archbishop’s effigy lies on a bier with his head at the left, resting on a cushion. He wears low headgear and his hands are crossed on his breast. Below, a casket bears four chequered shields set among acanthus scrolls. The main chest has three fields. On the left is the Annunciation: the angel kneels before the seated Virgin, in front of a crenellated building with an arcade and a staircase. The central tablet carries a seven-line Latin inscription in capitals beginning GUIDOCTUS DE TABIATIS ARCHIEPISCOPUS MESSANENSIS. On the right is the Adoration of the Magi, under round arches and an upper gallery, with a horse and a dog at the left and a kneeling king before the seated Virgin and Child at the right. A band of Gothic letters runs beneath the chest. The base has a frieze of scrolls with roundels between two chequered shields. The engraver’s signature, BARBERIS, appears at the lower right.
caption: Monument to Archbishop Guidotto de Tabiatis in Messina Cathedral, wood engraving, 1892. The tomb (Goro di Gregorio, c. 1326–1333) is shown before its damage in the earthquake of 1908 and the fire of 1943.

alt: A white marble statue of the seated Virgin and Child, seen in three-quarter view from the left against a black background. The Virgin sits on a plain block seat, her head covered by a veil that falls to her shoulders. She bends her head gently to her left and looks down at the Child. He stands upright on her left knee, supported by her left hand, which grips his garment at the side. He tilts his curly head back to gaze up into her face and grasps the edge of her mantle at her breast with one hand. The Virgin's right hand rests on her lap, holding a fold of her mantle. The mantle falls across her knees in deep, curving folds that break into rippling hems over the seat and her feet. The lower edge of the base is chipped at the right.
caption: Virgin and Child (the "Madonna degli Storpi"), after 1326. Carrara marble, height c. 90–100 cm. Messina, Museo Regionale (MuMe).

alt: A standing marble statue of an elderly bearded man, shown against a black background. His head is framed by thick, wavy hair and a long beard divided into twisted locks. His deeply lined face looks straight ahead under knitted brows. He wears a long tunic and a heavy mantle, which falls in a broad loop across his body. With his left hand he gathers the mantle at his side, and a long rolled scroll, the attribute of the prophets, hangs along that side down to his knee. His right arm hangs close to his body. The lower drapery falls to the feet in long folds, crossed by visible repaired fractures. The figure stands on a low base.
caption: Prophet, c. 1335. Marble, h. 75 cm. Asciano, Castello di Gallico, Collezione Salini (C. Bardelloni, La Collezione Salini, II, 2009, pp. 76–81, cat. 12).

alt: A small marble relief of the half-length Virgin holding the Christ Child, set within a round arch inside a rectangular frame with sunken triangular spandrels at the upper corners. The Virgin, covered by a veil that falls over her shoulders, bends her head towards the Child, who is seated on her left arm. The Child, with short curly hair and wearing a tunic, turns his head outward. One of his hands reaches up to touch his mother’s veil at her neck, and the other rests on his breast. The Virgin’s right hand supports his legs, which stretch across her body, and her mantle falls in deep curving folds over her lap. The marble is creamy white with brownish stains, and the Virgin’s nose and the edges of the frame are chipped.
caption: Madonna and Child, c. 1335. Marble, 26 × 17.6 cm. Asciano, Castello di Gallico, Collezione Salini (catalogue entry by G. Amato, La Collezione Salini, III, 2015, pp. 108–115, cat. 13).

alt: A painted wooden figure of the crucified Christ, shown without its cross against a black background. The arms rise diagonally upward from the shoulders, and the open hands show red nail wounds. The head, with long brown hair and a forked beard, sinks towards Christ’s right shoulder, and the eyes appear closed. The thin torso is modelled with ribs, sternum and a swelling abdomen. A wound in the right side sends thin streams of blood down towards the loincloth. The loincloth is pale grey-white, with a blue lining visible at the waist and along one side, and a reddish-brown border. The knees bend slightly, the legs are drawn together, and the feet are crossed one over the other, with blood at the nail wound.
caption: Crucified Christ, second quarter of the fourteenth century. Carved walnut, painted and gilded, 156 × 152 × 35 cm. Roccalbegna (Grosseto), Arcipretura dei Santi Pietro e Paolo; restored for Restituzioni 2018 (catalogue entry by Alessandro Bagnoli).

alt: A small terracotta statue of the Virgin seated on a rectangular block, set on a modern octagonal base and photographed against a black background. Her head is covered by a veil and tilts gently to her left, and she looks down towards her left side. A heavy mantle falls from her shoulders in deep U-shaped folds across her breast and lap, then breaks into sharp, curving folds over her knees and feet. Her right hand gathers a fold of the mantle at her waist. Her left arm projects from her side and ends in a broken stump with a small round hole. The terracotta is reddish-orange, crossed by cracks, with pale whitish traces on its surface.
caption: Goro di Gregorio (attributed), Enthroned Virgin, first half of the fourteenth century. Terracotta, 44.8 × 25.4 × 24.1 cm. New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Cloisters Collection and Rogers Fund, 1998 (1998.214).

alt: A marble relief in the shape of a pointed gable, its lower edge cut in the shallow curve of an arch moulding, shown against a brick wall. Christ hangs at the centre on a tall cross with a titulus board. His arms are stretched upward in a V, his head is inclined to one side, his ribs are visible above a knotted loincloth, and his legs are bent, with the feet nailed at the foot of the cross on a rocky mound. On the left the Virgin sits on the ground, wrapped in her mantle, her long hair falling loose, resting her head on her hand. On the right Saint John sits clasping one knee with both hands, his head thrown back to look up at Christ. The ground is formed of faceted rocks, and a raised border runs along the sloping sides of the gable.
caption: Tino di Camaino (attributed; also given to Goro di Gregorio), Crucifixion with Two Mourners (catalogued as Cristo in pietà fra i due dolenti), 1329–1332. Marble, 54.7 × 65 cm. Asciano, Castello di Gallico, Collezione Salini (F. Aceto, La Collezione Salini, II, 2009, pp. 94–101).

alt: A standing marble statuette of a bearded friar, photographed against a pale wall. He has a tonsure ringed by a thick band of curls and a short, curly beard, and the hood of his habit lies around his neck. His right hand is raised before his chest, palm outward, in blessing. His left arm presses a closed book with a strap or clasp against his side. The habit has wide sleeves and falls in long vertical folds. It is girded with a knotted cord whose end hangs down the front of the figure. At the hem the cloth gathers in curling folds over the bare toes. The figure stands on a rectangular plinth of veined marble.
caption: Gano di Fazio or Goro di Gregorio (attributed), Blessing Franciscan Friar with a Book, early fourteenth century. Marble. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale.

alt: The Bassano Crucifix
caption: Painted Cross, c. 1332, tempera and gold on panel, 360 x 280 cm, Museo Civico di Bassano del Grappa.

caption: The Coronation of the Virgin Altarpiece, 1344, tempera and gold on panel, 218.4 x 265.1 cm, Norton Simon Museum, Pasadena.

caption: Virgin and Child Enthroned, 1350-60, tempera and gold on panel, 81.4 x 59.8 cm, The Courtauld Gallery, London.

alt: Christ on the Cross between the Virgin Mary, John, and Mary Magdalene
caption: Christ on the Cross between the Virgin Mary, John, and Mary Magdalene, c. 1370, tempera and gold on panel, Palazzo dei Diamanti, Ferrara.

caption: The Virgin of Humility with Saints Anthony of Padua, John the Baptist, Francis, and Giles, c. 1360, tempera and gold on poplar panel, 41.6 x 23.2 cm, North Carolina Museum of Art, Raleigh.

caption: Armed Angel (Principatus), 1354-60, tempera on panel, 96 x 64.6 x 5.6 cm, Fogg Museum, Harvard Art Museums, Cambridge, MA.

caption: Angelic Hierarchies, 1360-65, fresco, Reggia Carrarese, Padua.

caption: The Eremitani Choir Frescoes: Vestments and Baptism of Augustine, Scene from Stories of St Philip and St Augustine, 1360s, fresco, church of the Eremitani, Padua.

caption: Paradiso: Coronation of the Virgin before the Celestial Hierarchies, 1365-68, fresco, Sala del Maggior Consiglio, Palazzo Ducale, Venice.

caption: Paradiso: Coronation of the Virgin before the Celestial Hierarchies, 1365-68, fresco, Sala del Maggior Consiglio, Palazzo Ducale, Venice.

caption: Madonna and Child ("Madonna del cardellino"), signed "Jacobus Mini de Senis" and dated 1342 (or 1344), tempera and gold on panel, Sarteano, church of San Martino, Sala d'arte "Domenico Beccafumi.

alt: Mystic Coronation of Saint Catherine of Alexandria, with Saints Mary Magdalene, Lucy, and Agnes, between Saints Anthony Abbot and Michael the Archangel

alt: Coronation of the Virgin with Eleven Angels
caption: Coronation of the Virgin with Eleven Angels, central compartment of a dismembered polyptych, tempera and punched gold leaf on panel, mid-fourteenth century, Montepulciano, Museo Civico–Pinacoteca Crociani (Palazzo Neri Orselli).

alt: Coronation of the Virgin with Eleven Angels
caption: Taddeo di Bartolo (formerly attributed to Jacopo di Mino del Pellicciaio), Madonna 'Belverde' — Madonna and Child Enthroned between Two Angels, c. 1405, tempera on gold ground on panel, 150.7 × 65.7 cm, Siena, Basilica di Santa Maria dei Servi.

alt: Madonna and Child with Saints John the Baptist and John the Evangelist
caption: Madonna and Child with Saints John the Baptist and John the Evangelist; in the crownings, the Annunciation, Paired Apostles, and Angels, c. 1340s, tempera and gold leaf on panel, church of San Francesco at Sarteano.

alt: The Annunciation: The Archangel Gabriel and the Virgin Annunciate
caption: The Annunciation: The Archangel Gabriel and the Virgin Annunciate, devotional diptych, undated, tempera and gold on panel, Fiesole, Museo Bandini.

alt: Coronation of the Virgin with Music-Making Angels; below, Scenes of the Martyrdom of a Female Saint (Victoria?)
caption: Coronation of the Virgin with Music-Making Angels; below, Scenes of the Martyrdom of a Female Saint (Victoria?), fresco ensemble from the ruined pieve of Santa Vittoria (?), Sarteano, church of San Francesco.

alt: Maestà (Madonna and Child Enthroned)
caption: Maestà (Madonna and Child Enthroned), detached fresco from the cloister of the convent of San Francesco, before 1396, Siena, Basilica di San Francesco, first transept chapel.

alt: Maestà (Madonna and Child Enthroned)
caption: Madonna and Child with Saints Clare, John the Baptist, Augustine, and Francis; in the pinnacles, the Crucifixion with the Virgin, Saint John the Evangelist, and the Magdalene, and Half-Length Saints, cusped polyptych, tempera and gold on panel, Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale.

alt: Maestà (Madonna and Child Enthroned)
caption: Mystic Marriage of Saint Catherine of Alexandria, with Saint Ansanus and Angels; on the wings, Saints Mary Magdalene and Elizabeth of Hungary (?); in the pinnacles, the Annunciation and the Blessing Redeemer, portable triptych, 1355–60, tempera and gold on panel, Perugia, Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria.

alt: Detached arched fresco attributed to Lippo di Dalmasio: the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle over a rose dress, sits nursing the Christ Child within a pointed aureole of golden rays against a green ground; around her rises a painted pavilion of white twisted columns carrying a scalloped white arch with hanging cusps, Gothic pinnacles at the sides and, above, a golden canopy crowned by a small aedicule against blue; two red-robed angels fly in adoration above the arch, and two more kneel below, one playing a bowed vielle, the other a lute; the whole is enclosed by a painted border of dark red bands with geometric star inlay, and the plaster shows large losses and abrasions.
caption: The Madonna of Humility with Four Angels, c. 1389(?). Detached fresco. Pistoia, Palazzo del Comune. Attribution to Lippo di Dalmasio debated: a communal deliberation of 1407 also bears on the work.

alt: Detached fresco attributed to Lippo di Dalmasio: the Virgin, in a red dress and dark blue mantle, sits within a round rayed aureole of gold nursing the Christ Child, who lies across her lap in a yellow wrap; at the left stands Saint Dominic in the black and white Dominican habit, holding a lily and a book, with a small kneeling male donor at his feet; at the right Saint Catherine of Alexandria, crowned, rests her hand on her wheel, a small kneeling female donor beside her; above, two flying angels draw open the flaps of a great pavilion, a blue-grey tent with scalloped white, fur-lined edges, whose peak rises at the top centre; the lower edge of the plaster is lost in a broad irregular band.
caption: The Madonna of Humility between two angels, with Saints Dominic and Catherine of Alexandria and two donors ("Madonna del Padiglione"), c. 1380. Detached fresco. Pistoia, convent of San Domenico, old refectory (Sala San Domenico). Attributed to Lippo di Dalmasio; also given to Antonio Vite and to Paolo Serafini da Modena.

alt: Small Gothic panel by Lippo di Dalmasio in its carved gilt frame with acanthus crockets: in the gabled cusp a haloed figure in a red garment and blue mantle raises his right hand in blessing and holds an open book with lines of script; in the main field below, under a painted cusped arch, Christ in a rose mantle sets a crown on the head of the Virgin, who bows with hands crossed on her breast in a white mantle over a rose dress, before a red cloth of honour; behind the pair a choir of blue angel heads with gold haloes fills the arch; along the bottom edge runs a narrow white band with a minute inscription in Gothic script.
caption: Coronation of the Virgin, with St John the Evangelist in the gable; central panel of a dispersed triptych. Signed and dated 24 April 1394, with the name of the patron, Rodolfo de' Lambertini. Tempera on panel, 63 × 27 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 1092 (provenance Stanislao Rinaldi). The wings are in Florence, Museo Stibbert, inv. 10348.

alt: The two wings of Lippo di Dalmasio's Lambertini triptych, displayed joined, each under a gabled gilt frame with acanthus crockets: in the left gable the Virgin Annunciate in a rose dress sits at a lectern against a red ground; in the right gable the Archangel Gabriel, in blue with a gold wing, kneels with raised hand; below, on the left wing, John the Baptist in camel skin and a grey-brown mantle points upward and unrolls a scroll lettered ECCE AGNUS DEI; on the right wing Saint Jerome, in the scarlet robe and broad hat of a cardinal, stands with a golden-brown lion rearing up against him.
caption: The wings of the Lambertini triptych: the Annunciation, above Saints John the Baptist and Jerome, 1394. Tempera on panel. Florence, Museo Stibbert, inv. 10348. Photo: Guido Barbi.

alt: Detached fresco by Lippo di Dalmasio: the Virgin, in a deep blue mantle over a red dress, sits low on a red tasselled cushion against a dark ground scattered with gold eight-pointed stars, suckling the Christ Child, who lies across her lap wrapped in a yellow cloth and reaches for her breast; behind the pair glows a sunburst of gold rays rimmed with red and orange flame; green curtains, knotted and lined with red, are drawn back at both sides, and at the upper left hangs a small tablet-like scroll inscribed in Gothic letters, partly abraded.
caption: The Madonna of Humility, signed and dated 1397. Detached fresco, 140 × 105 cm. Signed "lippus dalmassi". Bologna, Santa Maria della Misericordia. Photo: © Church of Santa Maria della Misericordia, Bologna. Courtesy of MIBAC – Archivio Fotografico Soprintendenza BSAE – Bologna.

alt: Medieval painting of the Virgin Mary seated on the ground in a flowering meadow, embracing the Christ Child, who is wrapped in red cloth and gazes up into her eyes; behind the pair rises a huge golden disc of the sun with radiating rays, twelve small stars circle the Virgin's halo and a crescent moon lies at her feet among the plants; her dark blue cloak, lined with green, has slipped back from her head to reveal fair hair under a transparent veil and a red dress, with a golden sunburst on her shoulder; in each upper corner three adoring angels lean inwards with joined hands, and at the bottom edge, among the flowers, runs the painter's Latin signature on a white band.
caption: The Madonna of Humility, c. 1390 (National Gallery dating; also placed c. 1400–1410). Egg tempera on canvas, 110 × 88.2 cm. Signed "lippus dalmasij pinxit". London, The National Gallery, inv. NG 752. Bought from Michelangelo Gualandi, 1866. Photo: © The National Gallery, London.

alt: Tall canvas by Lippo di Dalmasio: the Virgin, her head veiled by a dark mantle over a red dress with a star on her shoulder, sits on a dark flowered ground suckling the Christ Child, who lies across her lap wrapped in a yellow cloth; behind the pair rises a great plain disc of gold, and above and beside it a crowd of adoring angels, painted in gold against the dark ground, arches over the sun like a second glory; a crescent moon lies in the grass at the lower left.
caption: The Madonna of Humility with Angels, c. 1390–1400 (also placed 1400–1405). Tempera on canvas, 175 × 103.5 cm. Signed LIPPUS DALMAXIJ FECIT. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 786. Photo: © Pinacoteca Nazionale Bologna. Courtesy of MIBAC – Archivio Fotografico Soprintendenza BSAE – Bologna.

alt: Detached fresco by Lippo di Dalmasio in a later carved gilt frame: the Virgin, her head covered by a blue mantle over a white veil, in a rose dress with a gold-trimmed neckline, sits with her mantle spreading about her and holds the nearly naked Christ Child on her left arm; he is wrapped in a transparent white cloth and raises one hand to his mouth; behind the figures the ground is a field of radiating gold, and in the upper corners two fragmentary red-toned angels adore with joined hands against a blue-green sky; the plaster surface shows losses and abrasion at the edges.
caption: The Madonna of Humility, c. 1400 (also dated 1400–1405). Detached fresco transferred to canvas, 120 × 72 cm. San Martino in Soverzano (Minerbio), Michelangelo Poletti collection.

alt: Two-register panel by Lippo di Dalmasio: above, Christ in a rose tunic and blue mantle kneels in prayer on a shelf of grey rock strewn with small trees, turning towards a red-robed angel who flies down from a burst of gold at the upper left; a strip of dark meadow dotted with flowers runs along the lower edge of the scene; below, two bishop saints stand against a yellow cloth of honour with a punched border, the left one in a red cope over white holding an open book with lines of script and a crozier, the right one, dark-bearded, in a red cope, holding a crozier and a model of a towered city; the panel's edges are bound by rusted metal strips.
caption: The Agony in the Garden, with Saints Ambrose and Petronius, c. 1380–1390. Tempera on panel. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 613. Photo: Guido Barbi.

alt: Gothic triptych by Lippo di Dalmasio in three gabled panels on gold ground: at the centre the Virgin, in a red dress and dark blue mantle, sits on a pink and white pinnacled throne with the Christ Child in a yellow wrap on her lap, two angels in pale lavender robes with red wings kneeling at the throne's base above a white band bearing the painter's signature; on the left panel stand John the Baptist, holding an inscribed scroll, and a bishop saint in a black habit under a green cope with mitre and crozier, with a cusp above showing a mitred saint holding a model of a towered city; on the right panel stand Peter, with keys and book, and Paul, with sword and book, with a cusp above showing an elderly man holding a carpenter's tool; the two wings keep their carved and gilded cuspidate frames.
caption: Triptych: the Virgin and Child Enthroned with Two Angels, between Saints John the Baptist and Ambrose (or Augustine) and Saints Peter and Paul; in the cusps, St Petronius with the model of Bologna and St Joseph. c. 1390. Tempera and gold on panel, central panel 160 × 86 cm, wings 169 × 64 cm each. Signed on the base of the throne. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale (from the church of the Conservatorio di Santa Croce; on deposit since 1940).

alt: Half-length panel by Lippo di Dalmasio: the Virgin, crowned with a gold diadem over a transparent pearl-edged veil, her halo a broad band of punched foliate goldwork, wears a crimson dress and a dark mantle densely patterned with gold scrolls and winged heraldic beasts; she holds the nearly naked Christ Child, seated on a yellow cloth with a pale fur lining, who looks up at her while grasping a goldfinch in one hand and a golden ear of grain in the other, a small red element hanging at his breast; her long right hand supports his leg.
caption: Madonna del Velluto (Madonna of the Velvet). Tempera on panel, 80 × 57 cm; datings in the literature range from the early 1390s to the painter's last years (c. 1400–1408). Bologna, Museo della Basilica di San Domenico.

alt: Small horizontal panel by Lippo di Dalmasio: at the right, under a thatched shed on wooden poles, the Virgin in blue sits with the Christ Child on her lap, Joseph seated behind her and the ox and ass leaning over a wattle crib; the eldest magus, in a red mantle, kneels bowed before the Child; at the centre two standing magi in sumptuous courtly dress, one in a red brocade houppelande with a white collar, converse and gesture; at the left waits a retinue of young attendants in short tunics and parti-coloured hose with swords, and above them, among grey rocks, a groom tends the horses; two long horizontal scratches cross the painted surface.
caption: The Adoration of the Magi, c. 1405–1410. Tempera on panel, 42 × 76.5 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 279. Photo: Guido Barbi.

alt: Triptych of three standing saints by Lippo di Dalmasio in a carved gilt frame of three cuspidate tabernacles with twisted colonnettes and crocketed gables: at the left an elderly grey-bearded saint in an orange-red mantle holds a blue book; at the centre John the Baptist, gaunt in a camel-skin tunic under a rose mantle, barefoot, holds a long unrolled scroll of Gothic script that hangs from his hand by a red cord; at the right a saint in a green mantle over a blue robe holds a pair of keys on a cord and a red book; the figures stand on a pale ground strip against dark red backdrops with punched gold haloes.
caption: Saints Andrew, John the Baptist and Peter, c. 1405–1410. Tempera and gold on panel, 130 × 105 cm. Bologna, Savelli private collection.

alt: Black-and-white photograph of a panel by Lippo di Dalmasio: the Virgin, seated full-length on a bench throne before a patterned cloth of honour that falls in angular folds, her mantle drawn over her head, supports the Christ Child, who stands half-naked on her lap, a white cloth about his hips, raising his right hand in blessing; along the base of the panel runs the inscription in Gothic minuscule, lipus dalmaxij pinsit 1409.
caption: Madonna and Child Enthroned, signed and dated: "lipus dalmaxij pinsit 1409". Panel; dimensions unrecorded in the sources consulted. Formerly (1968) Norton Hall, Gloucestershire, collection of Capt. W. M. H. Pollen; present whereabouts untraced. Reproduced from B. Berenson, Italian Pictures of the Renaissance: Central Italian and North Italian Schools (1968), pl. 285.

alt: Painted cross by Lippo di Dalmasio: the dead Christ hangs with closed eyes and bowed head against a deep blue field bordered in gold, his elongated pale body sagging, a white loincloth at his hips, blood running in rivulets along his outstretched arms; in the left terminal the mourning Virgin in blue presses a hand to her cheek, in the right terminal the young Saint John clasps his hands in grief; in the panel above the cross the Redeemer, half-length in rose and blue, blesses and displays an open book with columns of script; the gold ground is heavily worn, with losses exposing the gesso, and the lower end of the shaft is ruined.
caption: Painted Cross (Christus patiens), c. 1395–1400. Tempera and gold on panel, 138 × 101 cm. Bologna, Collezioni Comunali d'Arte, inv. P 75, from the church of San Girolamo della Certosa. Photo: Guido Barbi.

alt: Painted cross by Lippo di Dalmasio with a shaped silhouette and no figured terminals: the dead Christ hangs against a gold field crossed by a dark blue band behind his arms, the cross edged in red; his head with reddish hair sinks to his right shoulder, blood beading at the brow; long rivulets of blood run down his arms, a jet springs from the wound in his side, and streams pour from his feet over a dark rocky mound at the base; a red titulus panel lettered I N R I stands above his halo, and at the summit a dark spreading form rises against the gold.
caption: Painted Cross (Christus patiens), 1395 (dating from the exhibition material). Tempera and gold on panel, 162 × 116 cm. Florence, Museo Casa Rodolfo Siviero, inv. 29G. Photo: Guido Barbi.

alt: Small gold-ground panel from the workshop of Lippo di Dalmasio: the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle over a rose dress, sits on a throne hung with a red cloth patterned in gold scrollwork, holding on her left arm the Child wrapped in yellow and extending her right hand; at the left stand a crowned young female saint in a red mantle resting her hand on a large spoked wheel, and behind her John the Baptist in camel skin with an inscribed scroll and a tall cross-staff; at the right a young tonsured friar in a grey-brown Franciscan habit and, before him, a beardless youth in a blue tunic and rose mantle holding a model ship.
caption: Madonna and Child Enthroned with Four Saints (Catherine of Alexandria, John the Baptist, a Franciscan saint and a youthful saint with a ship), c. 1400. Lippo di Dalmasio, workshop(?). Tempera and gold on poplar, 30.2 × 25.8 cm. Altenburg, Lindenau-Museum, inv. 11.

alt: Fresco attributed to Lippo di Dalmasio in a wall niche: the Virgin, in a red dress and deep blue mantle with a gold star on her shoulder, her halo a disc of fine gold rays, nurses the Christ Child, who lies across her lap in a yellow wrap and reaches for her breast; behind the pair four angels, two at each side, hold open a red-brown cloth of honour patterned with faint gold stars; the plaster is abraded, with losses along the edges of the drape.
caption: The Madonna of Humility nursing the Child, with four angels holding a cloth of honour (the "Madonna dell'Orazione"), 1399. Fresco. Bologna, complex of San Colombano, chapel of the Madonna dell'Orazione. Photo: Guido Barbi.

alt: Fresco imitating a three-panel polyptych, attributed to Lippo di Dalmasio: at the centre the Virgin sits enthroned before a green cloth of honour patterned with dark sprigs, holding the Christ Child who stands on her lap in a small grey-violet buttoned tunic, her free hand raised holding a pale flower; at the left stands an elderly female saint in a dark veil and rose-red robe holding a small round vessel; at the right a male saint in a red hood and blue robe holds a gilt casket; painted borders with quatrefoil ornament divide the three fields, and wide areas of plaster are lost along the lower edge.
caption: Madonna and Child Enthroned between two saints: fresco in the form of a polyptych, late fourteenth or early fifteenth century. Bologna, Basilica di Santa Maria dei Servi. Attributed to Lippo di Dalmasio. Photo: Guido Barbi.
