alt: Detached fresco fragment by Lippo di Dalmasio in a gilt frame: against a red ground, the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle over a red dress, her rayed halo in relief gold, looks down at the Christ Child she holds across her body; the Child, nearly naked, looks up at her and wears a necklace of red coral beads with a branch of coral hanging at his chest; the Virgin's two long-fingered hands cross over his legs; the plaster edges are irregular where the fragment was cut from its wall.
caption: Madonna and Child, fragment of a detached fresco, late fourteenth century. Bologna, Basilica di San Martino Maggiore. Attributed to Lippo di Dalmasio. Photo: Guido Barbi.

alt: Heavily worn fresco attributed to Lippo di Dalmasio in a wall niche: the Virgin, half-length, her mantle largely covered in gold, her great halo of radiating gold in relief, holds the Christ Child, who stands supported on her arm in a golden tunic, both figures facing the viewer; the Virgin's right hand, a ring on one finger, holds a small dark object, perhaps a rose or pomegranate; large areas of the surface are abraded to the plaster, and the gilding is worn through across the mantle.
caption: Madonna and Child (the "Madonna della Neve"), late fourteenth century. Fresco. Bologna, complex of Santo Stefano, crypt of the church of the Crocifisso. Attributed to Lippo di Dalmasio. Photo: Guido Barbi.

alt: Framed detached fresco attributed to Lippo di Dalmasio: the Virgin, seated, in a dark blue mantle over a purple-red dress with a large gold star on her shoulder, within a glory of golden rays, supports the Christ Child who stands on her lap in a golden tunic patterned with dark star-like flowers, one hand at her neckline; two angels in red lean down in adoration at the top against a dark red ground; the fresco's irregular edges are set in a narrow gilt frame on a pale striated wall.
caption: Madonna and Child in glory with two angels, fourteenth century. Detached fresco. Bologna, church of Sant'Isaia, sacristy. Attributed to Lippo di Dalmasio. Photo: Guido Barbi.

alt: Arched venerated image attributed in its core to Lippo di Dalmasio: the Virgin, seated in a blue mantle within a glory of golden rays, stars scattered about her haloed head, holds an open book in one hand and supports the Christ Child seated on her lap; at the left stands John the Baptist with a tall thin staff and a red mantle, at the right an elderly saint wrapped in a red-brown mantle; above, two angels in later, Baroque style hold a golden crown over the Virgin's head; the whole surface shows heavy craquelure and extensive repainting.
caption: Madonna and Child with an open book, between Saint John the Baptist and another saint (the "Madonna delle Grazie"), fourteenth-century core under later repainting. Bologna, church of Santi Bartolomeo e Gaetano, baptistery chapel. Attributed to Lippo di Dalmasio. Photo: Guido Barbi.

alt: Venerated fresco attributed to Simone dei Crocifissi or to Lippo di Dalmasio: the Virgin, enthroned between painted classical pilasters, in a pale gold-grey mantle over a rose dress with a jewelled ring on her finger, inclines her head to the Christ Child, who stands on her lap in a golden tunic and presses his cheek to hers, one arm around her neck; two gilded metal votive crowns, worked with red velvet and gems, are mounted over the heads of both figures; the surface is heavily worn, with the throne architecture abraded on both sides.
caption: Madonna and Child in tender embrace (the "Madonna della Vita"), late fourteenth century. Bologna, Santuario di Santa Maria della Vita. Attributed to Simone dei Crocifissi or to Lippo di Dalmasio; votive crowns applied later. Photo: Guido Barbi.

alt: Wide fresco covering a whole wall on a deep blue ground. A canopy with chequered valances and a red patterned cloth stretches across almost the entire width on thin gilded poles. At the centre the Virgin sits enthroned with the Child on a tall gilded Gothic throne. On either side a continuous row of standing saints extends to the edges of the wall, with tiers of haloed angels behind them; among them are two bishops, two young female saints in pale gold, Saint John the Baptist in camel hair, Saint Peter with his keys and young saints holding the canopy poles. To the right of the throne a man in a long pink gown with black stripes kneels with joined hands. At the far left stand an old bearded saint in a dark habit and a young female saint; at the far right a saint in a grey habit and a young saint in a red mantle. At the lower left and right, two marble door surrounds cut into the painted floor.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Maestà (the Virgin and Child enthroned with saints, angels and the podestà Nello di Mino Tolomei). Signed, dated 1317; saints at the outer edges added in 1366–1367; restored by Benozzo Gozzoli in 1467. Fresco. San Gimignano, Palazzo Comunale, Sala di Dante. Photo: Palazzo Comunale, San Gimignano, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Central section of the fresco. In the centre the Virgin sits frontally on a tall gilded Gothic throne whose central gable is pierced by a rosette, wearing a thin crown, a tooled gold halo and a pale blue-grey mantle strewn with small gold flowers. On her left knee the Child raises his right hand in blessing and holds an open scroll inscribed Diligite iustitiam qui iudicatis terram. On either side stands a young female saint in a pale gold gown with an ermine-trimmed hem, her arms crossed on her breast; behind them stand haloed angels. At the left a white-bearded bishop in a jewelled mitre grasps a canopy pole; at the right a bishop holds a long scroll of Latin text above a kneeling man in a long pink gown with broad black stripes. Along the lower border run white name labels and the painter's signature.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Maestà, central section (detail). San Gimignano, Palazzo Comunale, Sala di Dante. Photo: Comune di San Gimignano; Fondazione Musei Senesi, via Google Arts & Culture.

alt: Panel painting on a gold ground. In the centre the Virgin stands frontally, much larger than every other figure, her hands joined in prayer before her breast. She wears a dark crown over a white veil, a tooled gold halo, a red gown densely strewn with small gold stars, and a deep blue mantle edged with a gold ornamental border and lined in pale ivory, with an eight-pointed gold star on each shoulder. Her mantle is spread wide to both sides and its edges are held up by the nearest of two groups of angels, red-haired and haloed, in red and orange tunics, who crowd the gold ground on either side of her head and shoulders. Beneath the mantle kneel and stand the members of a confraternity: on the left the men, in caps and hoods of red, pink, green and brown, led by an elderly man in a white cap who looks up with joined hands; on the right the women, most in white veils and wimples, led by a crowned young woman in red who joins her hands in prayer. The lower edge of the panel is cut off within the crowd.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Madonna dei Raccomandati (Madonna of Mercy), signed, early 1320s. Tempera and gold on panel. Orvieto, Cathedral, Cappella del Corporale. Photo: Opera del Duomo di Orvieto, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Gold-ground altarpiece in a Gothic frame of gilded pinnacles, crocketed gables and twisted columns, divided into a wide central field and two narrow side compartments. In the centre the Archangel Gabriel kneels on the left, crowned with olive and holding an olive branch, his wings and plaid cloak still raised; between him and the Virgin stands a gold vase of lilies, and above them the dove of the Holy Spirit is ringed by eight angels. On the right the Virgin, in a deep blue mantle, sits on a carved throne and draws back from the angel. In the left compartment stands Saint Ansanus, a young man in red holding a banner and a palm; in the right compartment a female saint in a grey-blue mantle over a red dress holds a cross and a palm. Four small roundels with half-length prophets sit in the gables of the side compartments.
caption: Simone Martini and Lippo Memmi, Annunciation with Saint Ansanus and a Female Martyr, signed and dated 1333. Tempera and gold on panel, 184 × 210 cm (184 × 168 cm in the Uffizi's online record), in a nineteenth-century frame incorporating the original base. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi, inv. 1890 nos. 451–453. From the altar of Sant'Ansano in Siena Cathedral. Photo: Gleb Simonov, Wikimedia Commons (CC0).

alt: Narrow gold-ground compartment framed by twisted gilded columns. A beardless young saint with short reddish-gold curls and a tooled halo stands frontally on a green marbled hexagonal base. He wears a long rose-red tunic and a deeper red mantle edged with gold, falling in cascading folds on his left side. In his right hand he holds a tall staff with a small cross at the top and a black-and-white banner; in his left hand, held across his body, a palm frond. His feet are covered in pale ochre hose.
caption: Saint Ansanus, left compartment of the Annunciation of 1333 (detail). Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi. Photo: Gleb Simonov, Wikimedia Commons (CC0).

alt: Narrow gold-ground compartment framed by twisted gilded columns. A female saint with a long pale face and heavy-lidded eyes stands frontally on a green marbled base, wearing a white wimple, a large grey-blue mantle drawn over her head and wrapped around her body, and a red dress beneath it. In her right hand she holds a slender red cross; in her left hand, raised across her breast, a palm frond. The mantle is edged with a gold border and lined in dark green.
caption: Female martyr, right compartment of the Annunciation of 1333 (detail). Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi. Photo: Gleb Simonov, Wikimedia Commons (CC0).

alt: Tall narrow panel with a steep triangular gable, panel and frame in one piece, entirely gilded and densely tooled. In the gable, a small roundel contains a kneeling winged angel holding a lily. Below, within a painted Gothic arch of tooled gold, the Virgin is shown in half length, turned slightly to the right, in a deep blue mantle edged with gold over a red dress and a white veil, with a small gold star on her right shoulder. She inclines her head towards the Child, who sits on her left arm with his cheek against hers and looks out at the viewer. He wears a white tunic and a crimson mantle with a gold border, and holds in his left hand a small unrolled scroll with a Latin inscription. One of the Virgin's hands supports him at the waist; the other, lower down, holds his foot. Along the lower edge of the gold ground runs a faint inscription.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Virgin and Child, wing of a diptych, signed; dated 1333 by the museum. Tempera and gold on poplar, panel and frame in one piece, 66.5 × 27.4 cm including the gable. Berlin, Staatliche Museen, Gemäldegalerie, cat. 1081A. Photo: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, Gemäldegalerie / Jörg P. Anders (Public Domain Mark 1.0).

alt: Gold-ground panel in an engaged gilded frame with canted upper corners, its outer band decorated with small red crosslets. The Virgin is shown in half length, her head inclined towards the right, in a very dark blue mantle drawn over a white veil and wimple, its gold border inscribed with letters, over a red dress; a small gold star shines on her right shoulder. On her left arm she holds the Child, who sits upright, faces the viewer with a grave expression and wears a pink-red tunic with a gold neckline and a gold embroidered panel on the breast. With his right hand he holds out an unrolled scroll inscribed EGO SUM VIA VERITA[S]; in his left he holds a small goldfinch. The Virgin's left hand, with long fingers, supports him from below, and her right hand rests over his crossed bare feet. The gold ground is worn, with patches of red bole showing, especially to the right of the Virgin's head.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Madonna del Popolo, signed on the frame, later 1320s or after 1333. Tempera and gold on panel. From Santa Maria dei Servi, Siena; recorded in the Pinacoteca Nazionale di Siena when photographed in 2011. Photo: Combusken, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (background modified).

alt: Small rectangular gold-ground panel with a punched border. The Virgin sits on a throne entirely covered by a cloth of honour of orange-red brocade patterned in gold and lined with ermine, its white lining and black tails visible where the cloth falls over the sides of the throne. She wears a dark blue-green mantle edged with gold over a pink dress and a white veil, with a small gold star on her right shoulder, and inclines her head so that her cheek rests against the Child's head. The Child stands on her left knee, in a pale tunic with a pink mantle and a light blue sash; he raises his right hand and holds out in his left a small scroll inscribed EGO SUM LUX MUNDI. The Virgin's left hand supports him at the chest, while her right hand rests at her waist. Along the lower edge of the gold ground runs the inscription LIPPUS MEMMI DE SENIS ME PINXIT.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Enthroned Virgin and Child, left wing of a diptych, signed, c. 1320–1322 according to the museum. Tempera and gold on poplar, 51.2 × 34.3 cm. Altenburg, Lindenau-Museum, inv. 43. Photo: Derbrauni, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (cropped).

alt: Tall gold-ground panel with a pointed arched top. Saint John the Baptist sits frontally on a folding stool whose arms end in carved lion heads and whose legs end in lion paws, his bare feet crossed and resting on a hexagonal footstool. He is gaunt and dark-skinned, with wild dark hair standing up in spikes and a long dark beard, and a tooled gold halo. Over a shaggy fur garment tied with a knotted white cord he wears a large deep red mantle that covers his shoulders and falls over his knees. He raises his right hand with the index finger pointing upward and holds in his left a long thin staff topped by a small cross.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Saint John the Baptist, from the polyptych of San Paolo a Ripa d'Arno, Pisa, c. 1330 (?) according to the museum. Tempera and gold on poplar, 111 × 50.8 cm. Altenburg, Lindenau-Museum, inv. 42. Photo: Lindenau-Museum Altenburg, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Tall gold-ground panel with a pointed arched top. An old apostle with long grey hair and a long grey beard, haloed, sits frontally on a folding stool whose arms end in carved lion heads, his bare feet resting on a white hexagonal footstool. He wears a rose-red tunic with an embroidered collar and a large green mantle lined with orange-yellow and edged with gold. In his right hand he holds a long thin staff topped by a small cross; in his left, resting on his knee, a red book with a metal clasp. His eyes are turned sideways to the right. A patterned red cloth covers the seat, and traces of an inscription are visible on the base.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Saint Andrew, from the polyptych of San Paolo a Ripa d'Arno, Pisa, 1325–1329. Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Image for educational use only.

alt: Gold-ground panel in a round-arched moulded frame. Saint Peter, old, with short grey curly hair and a grey beard, haloed, sits on a folding stool whose arms end in carved lion heads, his bare feet on a white hexagonal footstool. He wears a blue tunic, over it a white pallium marked with black crosses that falls in a long strip down the front, and a large orange-yellow mantle with a gold-patterned border. In his right hand he holds two large gold keys with ornamented bits; his left hand rests on a red book with a clasp standing on his knee. He looks sideways to the right. A patterned cloth covers the seat, and the number 83 is painted in the lower right corner.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Saint Peter, from the polyptych of San Paolo a Ripa d'Arno, Pisa, 1325–1329. Tempera and gold on panel, 91 × 47 cm. Palermo, Galleria Regionale della Sicilia, Palazzo Abatellis, formerly Chiaramonte Bordonaro collection. Photo: Fabrizio Garrisi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Gold-ground panel in a round-arched moulded frame. Saint Paul, bald with a fringe of dark hair and a long dark beard, haloed, sits on a folding stool whose arms end in carved lion heads, his bare foot on a white hexagonal footstool. He wears a dark blue tunic and a large violet mantle with a gold-patterned border that covers his shoulders and knees. In his right hand he holds a sheaf of white letters with inscriptions; in his left he holds upright a sheathed sword, its scabbard wrapped with a belt with gilded fittings. He looks sideways to the right. The number 87 is painted in the lower right corner.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Saint Paul, from the polyptych of San Paolo a Ripa d'Arno, Pisa, 1325–1329. Tempera and gold on panel, 91 × 47 cm. Palermo, Galleria Regionale della Sicilia, Palazzo Abatellis, formerly Chiaramonte Bordonaro collection. Photo: Fabrizio Garrisi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Gabled pinnacle panel with an engaged gilded frame. In the gable, a roundel with a dark ground contains a gold six-pointed star. Below, under a pointed trilobed arch on two engaged colonnettes, Christ appears in half length, frontal, with long reddish-brown hair, a short beard and a halo set with small red stones. He wears a dark blue-green tunic with an embroidered collar and a large orange-red mantle over his left shoulder. He raises his right hand in blessing and rests his left hand on a closed green book standing upright before him.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Christ Blessing, central pinnacle of the polyptych of San Paolo a Ripa d'Arno, Pisa, 1325–1329. Tempera and gold on panel, 52 × 33 cm. Douai, Musée de la Chartreuse, inv. 34. Image for educational use only.

alt: Narrow gold-ground panel with a steep triangular gable and an engaged gilded frame. In the gable, a roundel set in a tooled border contains a gold six-pointed star on a dark blue ground. Below, under a pointed trilobed arch carried on two slender engaged colonnettes, a tonsured elderly monk is shown in half length, turned three-quarters to the left and looking to the left. He has grey hair, a short white beard and ruddy cheeks, and wears a dark grey-violet habit with a deep cowl. With his left hand he holds a red book with white page edges against his body; with his right he grasps a wooden staff with a curved handle. A tooled gold halo with a leaf pattern surrounds his head.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Vallombrosan Saint (Saint John Gualbert or Blessed Torello da Poppi?), pinnacle from the polyptych of San Paolo a Ripa d'Arno, Pisa (?), c. 1330 (?) according to the museum. Tempera and gold on poplar, 57.7 × 26.4 cm. Altenburg, Lindenau-Museum, inv. 44. Photo: Lindenau-Museum Altenburg, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Narrow gold-ground panel with a steep triangular gable and an engaged gilded frame. In the gable, a roundel set in a tooled border contains a gold six-pointed star on a dark blue ground. Below, under a pointed trilobed arch carried on two slender engaged colonnettes, a tonsured monk with a grey-white beard is shown in half length, frontally, looking out at the viewer with heavy-lidded eyes. He wears a dark grey-violet habit with a cowl. In his right hand, at the lower left, he holds a wooden staff with a curved handle; in his left, covered by a fold of the habit, he holds a red book with white page edges upright against his side. A tooled gold halo surrounds his head.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Vallombrosan Saint (Saint John Gualbert or Blessed Torello da Poppi?), pinnacle from the polyptych of San Paolo a Ripa d'Arno, Pisa (?), c. 1330 (?) according to the museum. Tempera and gold on poplar, 57.5 × 26 cm. Altenburg, Lindenau-Museum, inv. 45. Photo: Lindenau-Museum Altenburg, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Irregular fragment of detached fresco set into a neutral plaster ground, with large losses. At the left, against a dark ground, a bald saint with a long brown beard holds a large upright sword whose blade rises diagonally past his head; he wears a blue tunic and a red mantle. In the centre, a winged angel with curly blond hair and a pale pink robe, its wings tinged with green and pink, holds out with both hands a golden bowl heaped with white and red roses. Behind the angel hangs a pink cloth patterned with small orange motifs. At the right, the Virgin's head in a white veil and dark mantle, with a pale halo, looks out with a grave expression; at the right edge appears part of the Child's halo and curly head. Several large holes in the painted surface have been filled with neutral plaster.
caption: Lippo Memmi, fragment of a Virgin and Child Enthroned with an Angel and Saints Paul, Peter and Dominic, with Saint Paul, an angel and the head of the Virgin, later 1340s. Detached fresco. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale, from the cloister of San Domenico. Photo: Fabrizio Garrisi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small irregular fragment of detached fresco set into neutral plaster. It shows the head of an elderly saint with thick curly white hair and a short curly white beard, turned three-quarters to the left and looking to the left with a slightly raised gaze. His cheeks are ruddy, his brow furrowed, and a red garment appears at his neck. Behind his head is a large pale halo in ochre and white, outlined by incised circles, against a fragment of dark ground.
caption: Lippo Memmi, fragment of a Virgin and Child Enthroned with an Angel and Saints Paul, Peter and Dominic, with the head of Saint Peter, later 1340s. Detached fresco. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale, from the cloister of San Domenico. Photo: Combusken, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Irregular fragment of detached fresco on a neutral plaster panel. It shows the bust of a tonsured saint with short dark hair, seen frontally and looking out at the viewer, his face heavily abraded. He wears a dark mantle over a white tunic whose collar shows at the neck, and a pale halo surrounds his head. At the lower left rises a white lily on a slender stem. At the upper right a large dark curving shape, perhaps part of a drapery or of another figure, extends beyond the saint's shoulder.
caption: Lippo Memmi, fragment of a Virgin and Child Enthroned with an Angel and Saints Paul, Peter and Dominic, with Saint Dominic, later 1340s. Detached fresco. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale, from the cloister of San Domenico. Photo: Fabrizio Garrisi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Detached sinopia on a neutral plaster panel, an irregular area of pale ochre plaster on which a bust-length figure is drawn in red-brown lines. The figure has a round tonsured head within a halo drawn as a large circle, a long face with eyes, nose and mouth indicated by a few lines, and a collar and mantle shown by broad curving outlines across the shoulders. The whole surface is covered with small regular marks of a pointed tool. Screw holes are visible at the corners of the panel.
caption: Lippo Memmi, sinopia of the fragment with Saint Dominic, from the Virgin and Child Enthroned with an Angel and Saints Paul, Peter and Dominic, later 1340s. Detached sinopia. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale, from the cloister of San Domenico. Photo: Fabrizio Garrisi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Detached sinopia on a square neutral plaster panel, consisting of three irregular areas of pale ochre plaster. On the largest, at the left, a young figure with curly hair is drawn in red-brown lines in profile facing right, with a ribbon or cord at the neck and long lines of drapery falling below. A separate area at the upper right shows faint horizontal and curving lines, and a smaller area at the bottom shows further traces of drawing. The whole surface is covered with small marks of a pointed tool. Screw holes are visible at the corners of the panel.
caption: Lippo Memmi, sinopia of a fragment from the Virgin and Child Enthroned with an Angel and Saints Paul, Peter and Dominic, later 1340s. Detached sinopia. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale, from the cloister of San Domenico. Photo: Fabrizio Garrisi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Narrow gold-ground panel with a tall triangular gable. The Virgin, seen at half length, wears a dark blue mantle with a gold border and a small gold star on her right shoulder over a white veil; her head is inclined to the right and her tooled halo fills the upper part of the panel. On her left arm she holds the Christ Child, dressed in a transparent shirt and wrapped in a red mantle, who stretches his right arm towards the edge of her veil. With her right hand she touches the Child's chest; her left hand supports his bare feet. At lower left a tiny tonsured donor in a pale grey habit kneels with joined hands, looking up at the Virgin.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Virgin and Child with a Donor, c. 1325/1330. Tempera and gold on panel, painted surface 50.8 × 23.5 cm. Washington, National Gallery of Art, Andrew W. Mellon Collection, 1937.1.11. Photo: National Gallery of Art, Washington, Open Access (CC0) (background modified).

alt: Tall gold-ground panel with a pointed arched top framed by a gilded moulding, with a trefoil arch inside it and punched decoration in the spandrels. Saint John the Baptist stands at three-quarter length, his head turned to the right and his eyes looking sideways. He has long reddish-brown hair falling in locks and a long beard, and a tooled gold halo. He wears a grey-green camel-skin tunic rendered with wavy white strokes, tied with a knotted white cord, under a large red mantle with a gold edge. His right hand crosses his chest and points to the right; his left hand holds a scroll that unrolls diagonally across his body, inscribed in Gothic capitals ECCE AGNUS DEI ECCE Q.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Saint John the Baptist, probably c. 1325. Tempera and gold on panel, 94.3 × 45.3 cm overall. Washington, National Gallery of Art, Samuel H. Kress Collection, 1939.1.291. Photo: National Gallery of Art, Washington, Open Access (CC0) (background modified).

alt: Fresco of the Virgin enthroned, nursing the Child, against a blue-violet ground. The Virgin, in a white veil and a long blue-violet mantle with a red and gold border and a small gold star on her right shoulder, sits frontally on a white marble throne with tall pinnacles topped by flame-shaped finials and a red cushion. Her head inclines to the left and she looks out at the viewer; she holds the Child against her breast with her left hand and raises her right hand to her breast. The Child, in a brown tunic, turns to suckle, holding the breast with one hand; one bare foot shows below his tunic. The throne stands on a grey-green platform above red steps between two white twisted columns with leafy capitals. At the left edge are part of a wing, a pink robe, a jewelled belt, a spear point and a dragon's head; at the right edge a strip of red drapery.
caption: Lippo Memmi (attributed), Virgin and Child Enthroned (Madonna del Latte) with Saint Michael and a Saint, central part, c. 1315–1320. Fresco, whole painting 310 × 250 cm. San Gimignano, church of Sant'Agostino, altar of the Madonna delle Grazie. Chiesa di Sant'Agostino, San Gimignano, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A whole bay of a frescoed aisle wall. In the lunette under a pointed arch, the Annunciation is set in an open pale building: at the left the angel in a white robe kneels before a staircase, at the centre the Virgin in a dark blue mantle sits with a book before a green curtain, and in a separate room at the right a young woman in an orange dress sits holding a distaff. Below, two registers of two scenes each, framed by painted bands: above, Christ riding a white ass among apostles and onlookers, with boys in the trees and a man spreading a cloak, and next to it a crowd coming out of a crenellated city gate to meet him; below, priests handing coins to Judas inside a small Gothic aedicule, and the Last Supper, with Christ and the haloed apostles around a long table, John asleep on his breast and several apostles seated in front with their backs turned.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed; formerly "Barna da Siena"), Scenes from the New Testament, first bay of the right aisle: Annunciation; Entry into Jerusalem; Pact of Judas; Last Supper. 1330s–1340s (?). Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta, San Gimignano, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Lunette with a pointed top. In the apex, a burst of golden rays surrounds a cluster of small angels' heads with wings. Below, a pale pink building is cut away at the front to show its interior. At the left, before a staircase rising to an upper floor, the angel Gabriel kneels in a white robe patterned with small gold motifs, his golden wings raised and his hands crossed on his breast, his head bowed. At the centre, before a green curtain with an inscribed border and beside a bed with a yellow and red coverlet, the Virgin sits in a blue-green mantle over a white veil, holding a book in her left hand and raising her right to her breast, her head inclined. In a separate room at the right a young woman in an orange dress sits on the floor, holding a distaff with wool and looking towards the Virgin's chamber.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed; formerly "Barna da Siena"), Annunciation, lunette of the first bay of the right aisle. Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta, San Gimignano, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Square fresco framed by bands of star motifs. Christ, haloed, in a red robe and a blue mantle, rides sideways on a white ass towards the right, raising his right hand in blessing; a white foal walks beside the ass. Behind him a dense group of haloed apostles follows, Peter in a yellow mantle holding keys walking beside the ass. In front a kneeling man spreads a dark brown cloak on the ground. At the right a tree with dense foliage rises, in which a boy in yellow climbs to cut branches, while another boy below gathers them; at the upper left another leafy tree.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed; formerly "Barna da Siena"), Entry into Jerusalem, left compartment, first bay of the right aisle, middle register. Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Photo: Holger Uwe Schmitt, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Square fresco framed by bands of star motifs. Behind crenellated walls with towers rise the buildings of a city, among them a church with a rose window and a bell tower. Through an arched gate at the right a dense crowd of men and women pours out towards the left. In front, a man in a red mantle turns back to the crowd, two young men in short tunics, one in red and one in green, walk forward, and a man in a short patterned tunic spreads his arms. At the far left a man in a pink mantle holds a palm branch, and beside him a woman in red.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed; formerly "Barna da Siena"), Entry into Jerusalem, right compartment, first bay of the right aisle, middle register. Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Photo: Holger Uwe Schmitt, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco of a hall with a ceiling on carved brackets and three arched openings in the back wall. Behind a long table covered with a white cloth with a patterned border, set with bowls, bread, glasses, knives and a dish with a roast lamb, sit Christ at the centre and the haloed apostles. John sleeps with his head on the table against Christ's breast. Christ reaches across the table with a morsel towards an apostle in a pink mantle seated in front, who stretches out his hand to receive it. Four apostles sit on a bench in front with their backs turned, and others sit at the ends of the table; one at the right holds a knife and a loaf.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed; formerly "Barna da Siena"), Last Supper, first bay of the right aisle, lower register. Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Photo: Holger Uwe Schmitt, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Square fresco framed by bands of star motifs. Inside a pale green Gothic aedicule with a gabled roof, pointed windows and a vaulted interior, a group of priests and elders with long beards gathers around Judas, who stands at the right in a pink mantle over a pale green robe. A bearded priest at the centre counts coins into Judas's outstretched hand. At the left a young man in a pink robe with a yellow skirt looks on. All the figures stand on a pale floor before the aedicule.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed; formerly "Barna da Siena"), Pact of Judas, first bay of the right aisle, lower register. Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Photo: Holger Uwe Schmitt, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A whole bay of a frescoed aisle wall under a vault with striped ribs. In the lunette, the Nativity: a wooden shed set against a rocky slope shelters the Virgin, the Child in the manger, the ox and the ass, with Joseph seated at the left and two shepherds with staffs at the right; an angel flies at the upper right and a group of angels fills the top of the arch. Below, two registers of two square scenes framed by painted bands: above, the Transfiguration, with Christ in a pale mandorla between two prophets and three apostles fallen below, and the Raising of Lazarus, with Christ, the sisters and a crowd before the tomb from which Lazarus emerges in his grave-clothes; below, the Betrayal of Christ, with Judas kissing Christ amid soldiers with lances, torches and shields and Peter attacking Malchus, and the Agony in the Garden, with Christ praying to an angel among trees and the apostles asleep.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed; formerly "Barna da Siena"), Scenes from the New Testament, second bay of the right aisle: Nativity; Transfiguration; Raising of Lazarus; Betrayal of Christ; Agony in the Garden. 1330s–1340s (?). Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta, San Gimignano, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Lunette under a pointed arch framed by a band of star motifs. A wooden shed with a sloping roof on thin posts stands against a rocky slope. Inside, the Virgin in a dark blue mantle sits beside a manger in which the swaddled Child lies, with the ox and the ass behind it. At the left Joseph, in a pink-red mantle, sits on the ground with his head in his hand. At the right two shepherds in short tunics with staffs approach, and an angel flies above them; at the top of the arch, a faint group of angels.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed), Nativity, lunette of the second bay of the right aisle. Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta, San Gimignano, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons (cropped).

alt: Square fresco. At the centre Christ, haloed, stands in a white and gold garment within a pale green and golden mandorla of light, his right hand raised and a book in his left. At his sides, on the mountain, stand two bearded prophets with haloes, an old one in grey at the left and one in green at the right. Below, three apostles have fallen to the ground: one in yellow and blue at the left raises a hand to his face, one in brown in the centre covers his head with his arms, and one in white and green at the right raises his hand towards the vision.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed), Transfiguration, second bay of the right aisle, middle register. Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta, San Gimignano, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons (cropped).

alt: Square fresco. At the left Christ, haloed, in a blue mantle over a red robe, raises his right hand towards a tomb at the right. A crowd of men and women presses behind him; a woman in a blue mantle stands beside him and another, in a brown mantle, kneels at his feet. At the right, in the doorway of a pale stone tomb whose slab is held open by two men, Lazarus stands upright, wrapped in white grave-clothes bound with bands, his face pale.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed), Raising of Lazarus, second bay of the right aisle, middle register. Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta, San Gimignano, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons (cropped).

alt: Square fresco crowded with figures. At the centre Judas, in a yellow and red mantle, embraces and kisses Christ, who wears a dark blue mantle and is surrounded by soldiers. Above them rise many lances, halberds and two lanterns against a dark sky. At the lower left an apostle in an orange mantle bends over a man fallen on the ground, cutting his ear; at the right a soldier in armour with a sword and soldiers with round red shields press in.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed), Betrayal of Christ, second bay of the right aisle, lower register. Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta, San Gimignano, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons (cropped).

alt: Square fresco set in a garden with slender trees with pale foliage on a rocky ground. At the upper left Christ, haloed, in a red mantle, kneels and raises his hands towards a small angel appearing in the sky at the left corner. At the upper right three haloed apostles sit asleep against a slope. In the lower part, separated by a ledge of rock, a larger group of haloed apostles sleeps huddled together.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed), Agony in the Garden, second bay of the right aisle, lower register. Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta, San Gimignano, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons (cropped).

alt: A whole bay of a frescoed aisle wall. At the top, inside a pointed arch framed by a painted band of small star motifs, a lunette shows the Adoration of the Magi, with the Virgin and Child under a wooden shed at the left and the kings, attendants and horses to the right. Below, two registers of two square scenes each, separated by the same painted bands: above, Christ calling two fishermen in a boat, and the Marriage at Cana with a long white table and six water jars, partly lost; below, the Flagellation of Christ at a column before a crowned judge, and Christ led before the high priest, who sits on a stone throne. The ribs of the vault above are painted with ornamental patterns, and small carved corbels mark the springing of the arch.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed; formerly "Barna da Siena"), Scenes from the New Testament, third bay of the right aisle: Adoration of the Magi; Calling of Peter and Andrew; Marriage at Cana; Flagellation; Christ before Caiaphas. 1330s–1340s (?). Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Photo: Nicola Quirico, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Lunette with a pointed arched top framed by a band of star motifs. At the left, under a wooden shed with a sloping roof on thin posts set against a rocky slope, the Virgin in a dark blue mantle sits holding the Child, who leans towards an old bald king kneeling before him in a pink robe with a gold collar. Beside him stand two crowned kings: a bearded one in a red robe holding a round gold vessel, and a young beardless one in a blue-grey robe holding a gift and looking up. Behind them, attendants hold a red and white striped cloak, and at the right a brown horse with a red saddle and harness stands with the heads of two pale horses above.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed), Adoration of the Magi, lunette of the third bay of the right aisle. Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Photo: Nicola Quirico, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (cropped).

alt: Square fresco against a dark blue-black sky. At the left Christ, haloed, stands barefoot on the shore in a red mantle over a dark blue tunic, raising his right hand towards a boat. In the boat, floating on pale green water, are two haloed fishermen: in front a grey-haired, short-bearded man in a green tunic holds an oar and turns to Christ with an open hand; behind him an older man with long white hair and beard in a pink tunic draws a white net over the side of the boat.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed), Calling of Peter and Andrew, third bay of the right aisle, middle register. Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Photo: Nicola Quirico, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (cropped).

alt: Square fresco with large losses of plaster in the upper centre and the lower left. Behind a long table covered with a white cloth, on which lie round loaves, knives and glasses, sit guests: at the left a bearded man in grey standing with a glass in his hand, an old bearded man in red, and Christ, haloed, in a blue mantle. At the right, beyond the lost area, a bearded figure in an orange robe and another with joined hands. In front of the table six pale grey jars stand on a bench; at the left a servant in orange bends to tip one jar, and at the right a servant in a green tunic pours water from a jug into the last jar.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed), Marriage at Cana, third bay of the right aisle, middle register. Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Photo: Nicola Quirico, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (cropped).

alt: Square fresco set in a hall with a Gothic arcade, a red patterned cloth of honour with a green fringe and a row of spears behind. At the centre Christ, haloed, nearly naked but for a white loincloth, is bound to a thin striped column, his head inclined. Two tormentors strike him: at the left a man in a yellow tunic swings his arm back, at the right a man in a green tunic raises his arm. Behind, on a raised step, stands a tall crowned figure in a pink robe with a pointing gesture. At the right a group of bearded old men watches, the nearest in a pale pink and white mantle.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed), Flagellation, third bay of the right aisle, lower register. Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Photo: Nicola Quirico, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (cropped).

alt: Square fresco. At the centre, on a grey stone throne set against a dark rocky background, sits an old high priest with a long white beard, in a red mantle, grasping the neck of his robe with both hands. At the left a group of bearded elders stands below the throne, the nearest in a grey-green mantle over a yellow robe. At the right Christ, haloed, in a dark blue mantle, is led forward by soldiers in armour carrying lances and a shield; a man in a short brown tunic raises his arm high to strike him. Behind rise many spears and halberds.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed), Christ before Caiaphas, third bay of the right aisle, lower register. Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Photo: Nicola Quirico, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (cropped).

alt: Square fresco framed by painted bands of star motifs, against a dark blue sky. Christ, haloed and naked, stands in the river Jordan, its green water rising to his hips and filled with small fish, his right hand raised in blessing. At the right, on a rocky bank, Saint John the Baptist, haloed, in a camel-skin garment and a red mantle, pours water from a small bowl over Christ's head. At the left two haloed angels hold Christ's garments, a white cloth and a red robe.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed; formerly "Barna da Siena"), Baptism of Christ, fourth bay of the right aisle, middle register. Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Photo: Holger Uwe Schmitt, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Square fresco within a painted border of star motifs. Christ, haloed, in a long brownish-red robe and barefoot, carries a large cross on his shoulder and is dragged forward by a rope tied round his neck, held by a soldier in green scale armour at the left. Behind him a man in a short pink-red tunic pushes him and the cross. Around him crowd soldiers in dark helmets with lances, a man holding a hammer, a man in orange holding a bundle of nails and a white-bearded old man in a turban; above them two other crosses and a ladder are carried. At the right, beneath the crenellated walls and gate of a city, the Virgin in a dark blue mantle and the holy women look on in grief, while a soldier's sword is held out towards them.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed; formerly "Barna da Siena"), Way to Calvary, fourth bay of the right aisle, lower register. 1330s–1340s (?). Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Photo: LivioAndronico, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Tall bay of a frescoed wall under a vault painted with gold stars on blue and patterned ribs. In the lunette, the Massacre of the Innocents: Herod sits enthroned at the top pointing down, while soldiers stab and seize infants, mothers clutch their children and lament, and a heap of dead infants lies on the ground. Below, filling the two upper registers, the Crucifixion: Christ on the central cross against a red ground surrounded by flying angels, the two thieves on crosses at either side, with angels above the left one and demons above the right one. Horsemen surround the crosses, one piercing Christ's side with a lance, another raising a club against the thief at the right; a haloed centurion points up at Christ. At the lower left the Virgin faints among the holy women, with John beside them; at the bottom centre men struggle over a garment; at the right a crowd of soldiers with a red banner.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed; formerly "Barna da Siena"), Massacre of the Innocents (lunette) and Crucifixion, fifth bay of the right aisle. 1330s–1340s (?). Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Photo: Holger Uwe Schmitt, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco detail. In the lower half the Virgin, fainting, lies back with closed eyes and parted lips, her head wrapped in a white veil under a dark red-brown mantle that covers a blue-grey dress. At the left a haloed woman with loose fair hair, wrapped in a large grey-green mantle over an orange-yellow dress, kneels and holds the Virgin's head, weeping. Behind, a haloed woman in a mauve-brown veil bends over her with an anguished face and lays a hand on her breast. At the right a haloed figure with long fair hair and a red-brown mantle clasps its hands. Above, a crowd of women in white turbans and fair braided hair look upwards, a woman in a blue hood looks aside, and a bearded man in a white turban and green robe bends towards the Virgin with raised hands. Children with headbands peer from both sides; at the upper right are the legs of a grey horse.
caption: Lippo Memmi and workshop (attributed; formerly "Barna da Siena"), Crucifixion, detail with the swooning Virgin, 1330s–1340s (?). Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta, right aisle wall. Photo: Nicola Quirico, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small rectangular panel in an engaged gilded frame. Against a gold ground bordered by bands of punched lozenge and quatrefoil patterns, the Virgin is shown in half length in a deep blue mantle edged with gold over a white veil and a red dress, a gold star on her shoulder. Her long pale face inclines towards the Child, who sits on her left arm in a pale blue tunic, a rose-pink mantle wrapped round his legs, and grasps a fold of the pink cloth at his chest while looking out at the viewer. The Virgin's long fingers support his feet. Below, a narrow predella of five arches on twisted colonnettes contains tiny full-length figures: a crowned female saint holding a cross, a bearded saint with a sword, a Dominican friar with a lily and a red book, a deacon in a red dalmatic with a book, and a kneeling nun in a black habit with her hands raised in prayer.
caption: Simone Martini (and Lippo Memmi?), Virgin and Child over Saints Helen, Paul, Dominic, Stephen (?) and a Dominican Nun, c. 1325. Tempera and tooled gold on panel, 33.4 × 25.4 × 4.4 cm with engaged frame (painted surface 28.4 × 20.1 cm). Boston, Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, P30w8. Possibly from the convent of San Paolo, Orvieto. Photo: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, Boston (gardnermuseum.org).

alt: Small rectangular gold-ground panel in a broad gilded frame. The Virgin, in half length, wears a black mantle patterned with gold palmettes and lined with green over a white veil and a red dress with a gold radiant ornament on the breast; her head, under a tooled halo, inclines towards the Child and she looks out sadly. On her left arm she holds the Child, in a white shirt and a pink-red mantle, who looks up at her and pulls the edge of her veil with his right hand while holding a small scroll in his left. Her right hand supports him from below. In two roundels in the upper corners are a bishop saint with a mitre and a book at the left and Saint John the Baptist at the right, whose hand points down from the roundel towards the Child.
caption: Simone Martini (formerly attributed to Lippo Memmi), Virgin and Child with a Bishop Saint (Augustine?) and Saint John the Baptist, c. 1325–1330. Tempera and gold leaf on panel, 47.9 × 39 cm overall. Kansas City, Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, F61-62, gift of the Samuel H. Kress Foundation. Photo: Daderot, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Tall panel with a pointed arch and inner trefoil, its upper corners cut, the outer spandrels dark with sgraffito ornament and the edges of bare wood. Against a worn gold ground, a young beardless bishop with a tooled halo stands in half length, turned slightly to the right. He wears a tall white mitre with jewelled bands, a dark blue cope patterned with gold fleurs-de-lis and edged with a broad jewelled orphrey fastened by a large round morse, over a brown Franciscan habit tied with a white knotted cord. In his right hand he holds a red book with metal clasps; in his left a gilded crozier whose crook ends in leafy ornament around a flower.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Saint Louis of Toulouse, from the polyptych of San Francesco, San Gimignano, c. 1325–1330. Tempera and gold on panel, about 105 × 46 cm. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale. Photo: Fabrizio Garrisi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (background modified).

alt: Tall panel with a pointed arch and inner trefoil, its upper corners cut, the outer spandrels dark with sgraffito ornament and the edges of bare wood. Against a gold ground, Saint Francis stands in half length in a dark brown habit with a hood, tied with a knotted white cord. He is bearded, tonsured and haloed, his head inclined to the left and his eyes turned sideways. He raises his right hand, showing the wound of the stigma in the palm, and with his left hand, also marked with a wound, he draws open a slit in his habit to show the wound in his side.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Saint Francis of Assisi, from the polyptych of San Francesco, San Gimignano, c. 1325–1330. Tempera and gold on panel, about 105 × 46 cm. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale. Photo: Fabrizio Garrisi, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (background modified).

alt: Panel with a pointed arch and inner trefoil, in a gilded moulded frame. Against a worn gold ground with red bole showing through, Saint Peter stands in half length, frontal, with short grey curly hair, a short grey beard and a tooled halo. He wears a blue tunic with a dark embroidered collar and an orange-yellow mantle, and over his shoulders a white pallium marked with black crosses that falls down the front. In his right hand he holds two large keys with ornamented bits, in his left a closed red book with black clasps.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Saint Peter, from the polyptych of San Francesco, San Gimignano, second quarter of the 14th century. Tempera on gold ground on poplar, 94 × 44.2 cm. Paris, Musée du Louvre, Département des Peintures, MI 690. Photo © 2017 GrandPalaisRmn (musée du Louvre) / Franck Raux (background modified).

alt: Tall panel with cut upper corners and a pointed arch with an inner trefoil framed by a pink moulding; the outer spandrels are painted with blue and red ornament, and a split runs from the top of the panel down to the saint's forehead. Against a gold ground much worn to the red bole, a young beardless saint with short red-gold curls and a tooled halo stands in half length, frontal. He wears a light blue tunic with an embroidered collar and a large red mantle over his left shoulder. In his left hand he holds an open green book; in his right a white quill pen, above a small dark inkwell at the lower edge. At the bottom is a plain wooden board.
caption: Lippo Memmi (or workshop of Simone Martini), Saint John the Evangelist, from the polyptych of San Francesco, San Gimignano, c. 1330. Tempera on panel, 104.9 × 44.7 × 2.5 cm. New Haven, Yale University Art Gallery, 1943.239, bequest of Maitland F. Griggs. Yale University Art Gallery, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Panel with a pointed arch and inner trefoil in a gilded moulded frame. Against a gold ground, Saint Paul stands in half length, frontal, bald with a dark fringe of hair, a long dark brown beard and a tooled halo. He wears a green tunic with an embroidered collar and a mauve-violet mantle. In his right hand he holds upright a long sword with a dark blade and a gilded hilt; in his left he holds a fan of white letters, the front one inscribed AD ROMANOS and PAVLUS, the others beginning with A.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Saint Paul, from the polyptych of San Francesco, San Gimignano, c. 1330. Tempera on wood, gold ground, painted surface 89.2 × 41.9 cm (95.9 × 48.3 cm overall with arched top and engaged frame). New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, 88.3.99, gift of Coudert Brothers, 1888. Photo: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, Open Access (CC0), via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small gold-ground panel with a triangular gable, set in a modern gilded frame with crockets, a finial, two pinnacles and twisted colonnettes. Saint Clare is shown in half length, her head inclined to the left, in the brown habit of the Poor Clares girded with a knotted cord, a white wimple and a black veil that falls over her shoulders. A large tooled halo surrounds her head. In her right hand she holds a red book with gold clasps and ornament; in her left she raises a small golden lamp. The gold ground is crossed by a network of cracks.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Saint Clare, pinnacle from the polyptych of San Francesco, San Gimignano, c. 1330. Tempera on wood, gold ground, painted surface 39.4 × 19.1 cm (48.3 × 20.3 cm overall with shaped top and modern engaged frame). New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, 64.189.2, gift of Irma N. Straus, 1964. Photo: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, Open Access (CC0).

alt: Small gold-ground pinnacle panel with a steep gable edged by a crocketed moulding, much worn. Saint Elizabeth is shown in half length, her head inclined to the right, with a white wimple edged with small pearls and a grey-brown veil and mantle that cover her head and shoulders. A tooled halo surrounds her head. With her right hand she holds up a fold of her mantle, in which lie red and white roses. The gold ground is crossed by a dense network of cracks.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Saint Elizabeth of Hungary, pinnacle from the polyptych of San Francesco, San Gimignano, c. 1330. Tempera and gold on panel. Milan, Museo Poldi Pezzoli. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (background modified).

alt: Small gold-ground pinnacle panel with a steep gable edged by a crocketed moulding and flanked by twisted colonnettes. Mary Magdalene is shown in half length, frontal, with long fair hair falling at the sides of her face, a red mantle lined with light blue drawn over her head and shoulders and a red dress with gold borders. A tooled halo surrounds her head. With both hands she holds before her breast a white covered ointment jar.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Mary Magdalene, pinnacle from the polyptych of San Francesco, San Gimignano, c. 1330. Tempera and gold on panel, 49.5 × 22.5 cm. Providence, RISD Museum, 21.250, Museum Appropriation Fund. Photo: RISD Museum, Providence, Open Access (CC0).

alt: Small gold-ground pinnacle panel with a steep gable edged by a crocketed moulding, photographed against a brick wall. A bishop saint with a white beard is shown in half length, frontal, wearing a white mitre with jewelled bands and a red chasuble patterned with dark arabesques, crossed by a broad orphrey set with red and dark stones and rows of pearls. A tooled halo surrounds his head. In his right hand, which wears a ring, he holds a dark green book with clasps; in his left, also ringed, an ivory-coloured crozier with a spiral crook.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Bishop Saint (Saint Gimignanus or Saint Augustine?), pinnacle from the polyptych of San Francesco, San Gimignano, c. 1330. Tempera and gold on panel, 51 × 22 cm. Montecalvoli (Asciano), Castello di Gallico, Salini Collection. Image for educational use only.

alt: Gold-ground panel with a pointed arch enclosing a trefoil, its spandrels dark. The Virgin, in half length, wears a dark blue mantle drawn over her head above a white veil and a red dress, with a small gold star on her right shoulder; her head inclines towards the Child and she looks out sadly. On her left arm sits the Christ Child, in a white shirt and a red mantle lined in gold, who pulls the edge of her white veil with his right hand and looks out at the viewer. Her left hand supports him from below, and her right hand holds his bare foot. Both have tooled haloes.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Virgin and Child, 14th century (c. 1325–1330?). Tempera and gold on poplar, 86.1 × 55.4 cm with the pointed top, including a modern addition in the upper part. Berlin, Staatliche Museen, Gemäldegalerie, no. 1067. Photo: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, Gemäldegalerie / Jörg P. Anders (Public Domain Mark 1.0).

alt: Tall gold-ground panel with a steep triangular gable, in a gilded moulded frame. In the apex of the gable, a small scene of Christ crowning the Virgin, both seated on a bench. Below it, a band of dark blue starry sky in the form of an arch, in which Christ appears in half length, with rays around him, stretching out his arms; at either end of the arch, groups of bearded prophets and patriarchs with scrolls, among them a crowned king with a psaltery at the left. In the main field the Virgin, seated frontally with joined hands on a dark cloud and surrounded by golden rays, wears a blue-grey mantle patterned with gold over a dress with a lozenge pattern. Around her a ring of angels, some red-winged, holds her up, while others play instruments: long trumpets at the upper left and right, a drum, a lute, a portative organ and pipes; the angels in the lower part are seen from behind, completing the circle.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Assumption of the Virgin, with the Coronation of the Virgin in the gable, c. 1340. Tempera and gold on poplar, 72.5 × 32.5 cm. Munich, Bayerische Staatsgemäldesammlungen – Alte Pinakothek, WAF 671 (Wittelsbacher Ausgleichsfonds). Photo: Bayerische Staatsgemäldesammlungen – Alte Pinakothek München, CC BY-SA 4.0.

alt: Tall gold-ground panel with a steep gable, in a gilded frame with crockets, pilasters and a moulded base. The Virgin, in half length, wears a black mantle with a gold border over a red dress, with a small gold star on her right shoulder; her head inclines towards the Child and she looks out. The Child, in a transparent shirt and a red and gold mantle, sits on her left arm, pulls at the edge of her veil with his right hand and holds a small sprig in his left. Around them, in the gable and down the sides, small angels in tiers fill the gold ground; at the lower corners stand tiny full-length figures of Saint John the Baptist at the left and Saint Francis holding a red book at the right. In a narrow predella below, seven half-length saints stand under arches.
caption: Lippo Memmi, Virgin and Child with Saints and Angels, left wing of a diptych, c. 1350 according to the museum. Tempera on wood, gold ground, painted surface 50.2 × 25.7 cm (66.7 × 33 cm overall with shaped top and partially modern engaged frame). New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, 43.98.6, Maitland F. Griggs Collection, Bequest of Maitland F. Griggs, 1943. Photo: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, Open Access (CC0).

alt: Tall gold-ground panel with a triangular gable, in a gilded frame. At the centre a tall cross rises from a rocky mound with a skull and bones at its foot, stained with blood. Christ hangs dead, his head inclined on his right shoulder, a white loincloth around his hips, blood flowing from the wound in his side and from his feet. Above the cross-bar a red titulus with white letters is flanked by two small angels, and at the top of the cross a pelican stands in its nest. At the left a group of haloed women supports the Virgin, who wears a dark mantle and turns her face upwards; behind them a soldier in a mail hood points to the cross, and a spear rises. At the right Saint John the Evangelist, in a blue tunic and red mantle, clasps his hands; behind him a haloed bearded man and a crowd of soldiers with spears, a sponge on a reed and a red banner.
caption: Lippo Memmi (or Simone Martini?), Crucifixion, wing of a diptych, c. 1340. Tempera and gold on poplar, 60.8 × 28.8 cm. Paris, Musée du Louvre, Département des Peintures, RF 1984 31. Photo © 2017 GrandPalaisRmn (musée du Louvre) / Franck Raux.

alt: Tall gold-ground panel with a pointed gable, its edges worn. In the gable, God sits enthroned in a blue mantle within a mandorla of red seraphim, raising his hand. Below him, a band of heaven: rows of angels in coloured robes seated in tiers on choir stalls at either side, and at the centre the archangel Michael in armour with other armed angels standing guard before empty seats. A strip of dark blue sky with gold stars runs beneath them. In the large lower field, on a worn gold ground, the rebel angels tumble headlong through the air, the upper ones still with feathered wings and human forms, the lower ones turned into black, bat-winged demons with claws and tails, falling towards a dark mound of earth at the bottom.
caption: Memmi family (Master of the Rebel Angels; attributed to Lippo Memmi or Simone Martini), The Fall of the Rebel Angels, originally the other face of the Saint Martin Dividing his Cloak (DL 1967 1 B), first half of the 14th century. Gold ground, transferred from panel to canvas in 1967, 64 × 29 cm. Paris, Musée du Louvre, Département des Peintures, DL 1967 1 A, on deposit from the Musée du Berry, Bourges. Photo © 2017 GrandPalaisRmn (musée du Louvre) / Franck Raux.

alt: Narrow gold-ground panel with a pointed gable, its edges worn and irregular. At the right Saint Martin, haloed, with reddish-gold hair held by a band and a short red beard, stands in half length with his eyes lowered. He wears a dark green tunic with gold borders and holds with his left hand a red mantle lined with blue, which he cuts with a sword whose blade is visible at the lower edge. At the left only the head of the beggar survives, dark-haired and bowed, seen in profile; the rest of his figure and the lower left part of the panel are lost, showing the bare preparation.
caption: Memmi family (Master of the Rebel Angels; attributed to Lippo Memmi or Simone Martini), Saint Martin Dividing his Cloak, originally the reverse of the Fall of the Rebel Angels (DL 1967 1 A), first half of the 14th century. Gold ground, transferred from panel to canvas in 1967, 64 × 29 cm. Paris, Musée du Louvre, Département des Peintures, DL 1967 1 B, on deposit from the Musée du Berry, Bourges. Photo © 2017 GrandPalaisRmn (musée du Louvre) / Franck Raux.

alt: Large gabled panel with a central pinnacle. In the pinnacle, Christ sits in a gold mandorla, holding a book. Below, against a blue band under the gable, six haloed authors lean down with open books and scrolls, among them Evangelists accompanied by the angel, the ox, the eagle and the lion; rays pass from their writings to the central figure. At the centre Saint Thomas Aquinas, in the black and white Dominican habit, sits frontally within a large dark circle, holding an open book inscribed in Gothic script, with other open books on his lap and rays spreading from him. At the left Aristotle, labelled ARISTOTILES, and at the right Plato, labelled PLATO, hold up books towards him. At the bottom Averroes, labelled AVERROIS, lies on the ground with his closed book, between two crowds of clerics and laymen, Dominican friars, monks in white and a cardinal in red.
caption: Lippo Memmi (attributed; with Francesco Traini?), Triumph of Saint Thomas Aquinas, c. 1323–1330. Tempera and gold on panel, about 375 × 258 cm. Pisa, church of Santa Caterina d'Alessandria. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Five-part polyptych displayed against a brick wall, its red-painted frame partly worn. In the main register, under trefoil arches, half-length figures on gold ground: at the left Saint John the Evangelist writing in a book and a bearded saint presenting a small kneeling donor in blue; at the centre, in a taller panel, the Virgin in a blue mantle holding the Child, who holds a scroll; at the right Saint Stephen with stones on his head and a book, and Saint Thomas Aquinas in the Dominican habit holding an open book from which rays radiate. Above, five triangular pinnacles: a white-bearded prophet with a scroll, Saint Paul with a sword, Christ blessing with a book at the centre, Saint Peter with keys and a book, and a long-haired prophet with a scroll.
caption: Lippo Memmi (attributed), Virgin and Child with Saints John the Evangelist, Matthias with a Donor, Stephen and Thomas Aquinas; in the pinnacles Isaiah, Saint Paul, Christ Blessing, Saint Peter and a Prophet. Polyptych from the altar of Saint Stephen in Pisa Cathedral, later in San Niccolò at Casciana Alta, 1320s (?). Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo (on deposit). Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Panel under a trefoil arch with gilded tracery, the gold ground largely lost to red bole. A young beardless saint with reddish-brown hair and a tooled halo, in a light blue tunic and a large pink-red mantle with an embroidered border, holds an open green book against his body and dips a white quill pen into a small black inkwell at the lower edge, his eyes turned sideways to the right.
caption: Lippo Memmi (attributed), Saint John the Evangelist, left lateral panel of the polyptych from the altar of Saint Stephen in Pisa Cathedral, 1320s (?). Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Panel under a trefoil arch, the gold ground worn to red bole at the left. A tall bearded saint with dark hair and a tooled halo, in a red tunic and a large green mantle shot with pink and violet, turns to the right and raises both hands over a small kneeling donor in a blue gown with a white hood, who looks up with joined hands.
caption: Lippo Memmi (attributed), Saint Matthias Presenting a Donor, panel to the left of the centre of the polyptych from the altar of Saint Stephen in Pisa Cathedral, 1320s (?). Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Central panel under a trefoil arch with gilded tracery, the gold ground much worn to red bole. The Virgin, in half length, wears a pale blue mantle drawn over her head above a white veil and a dark red dress, with a small gold star on her right shoulder; her head inclines towards the Child and she looks out. The Child sits on her left arm in a light blue shirt and a red mantle, holding a small scroll in his left hand and raising his right in a gesture towards her. Her right hand supports his bare feet.
caption: Lippo Memmi (attributed), Virgin and Child, central panel of the polyptych from the altar of Saint Stephen in Pisa Cathedral, 1320s (?). Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Panel under a trefoil arch, the gold ground worn to red bole. A young tonsured deacon with brown hair and a tooled halo, with streams of blood on his forehead and neck, wears a red dalmatic richly embroidered with gold and coloured stones along its bands and sleeves. He holds a grey-green book against his body with both hands and looks sideways to the left.
caption: Lippo Memmi (attributed), Saint Stephen, panel to the right of the centre of the polyptych from the altar of Saint Stephen in Pisa Cathedral, 1320s (?). Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Panel under a trefoil arch, the gold ground worn to red bole. A stout tonsured friar with a broad face and a tooled halo, in the black mantle and white habit of the Dominicans, holds frontally an open book inscribed in Gothic script, from which black rays radiate in all directions; a rosary hangs from his right hand.
caption: Lippo Memmi (attributed), Saint Thomas Aquinas, right lateral panel of the polyptych from the altar of Saint Stephen in Pisa Cathedral, 1320s (?). Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Triangular pinnacle with a moulded red frame against a brick wall. On a worn gold ground, an old prophet with grey hair and a long curling white beard, haloed, in an orange tunic and a blue mantle, turns to the right and holds an unrolled white scroll inscribed in Gothic script beginning ECCE.
caption: Lippo Memmi (attributed), The Prophet Isaiah, left pinnacle of the polyptych from the altar of Saint Stephen in Pisa Cathedral, 1320s (?). Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Triangular pinnacle with a moulded red frame against a brick wall. caption: Lippo Memmi (attributed), Saint Paul, pinnacle of the polyptych from the altar of Saint Stephen in Pisa Cathedral, 1320s (?). Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Triangular pinnacle with a moulded red frame against a brick wall, its gold ground almost entirely lost to red bole. alt: Triangular pinnacle with a moulded red frame against a brick wall. caption: Lippo Memmi (attributed), Saint Peter, pinnacle of the polyptych from the altar of Saint Stephen in Pisa Cathedral, 1320s (?). Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Triangular pinnacle with a moulded red frame against a brick wall. FEMINA CIRCUMDABIT.
caption: Lippo Memmi (attributed), A Prophet (Jeremiah?), right pinnacle of the polyptych from the altar of Saint Stephen in Pisa Cathedral, 1320s (?). Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Triangular pinnacle panel with a sawn apex, photographed against a brick wall, its unpainted wooden margins worm-eaten. On a cracked gold ground, Christ is shown in half length, frontal, with long fair hair, a short beard and a tooled halo, his head slightly inclined. He wears a light blue tunic and a pink mantle lined with yellow, raises his right hand in blessing and holds in his left a red book with dark clasps against his body.
caption: Lippo Memmi (or Simone Martini?), Christ the Redeemer, pinnacle of a lost polyptych, c. 1320–1350. Tempera and gold on panel, 45 × 52.3 cm. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, inv. 5728. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Round-arched panel on a gold ground, set in a dark frame decorated with small gold flame motifs and a base inscribed S. ANTONIUS DE PADUA. The Virgin, in half length, wears a very dark blue-green mantle over a red dress, its border edged in gold; her head inclines towards the Child, and her face is long and pale with heavy-lidded eyes. The Child sits on her arm in an orange tunic and a rose-pink mantle, with a pale green sash tied at his waist; he looks out at the viewer and holds a small goldfinch in his left hand, while the Virgin's right hand supports his foot. Both haloes are richly tooled with punched patterns.
caption: Simone Martini, Madonna and Child, central panel of the polyptych of Sant'Agostino, San Gimignano, c. 1316–1317. Tempera and gold on poplar, 79.5 × 57 cm (dimensions as given by the museum). Cologne, Wallraf-Richartz-Museum & Fondation Corboud, WRM 0880. Photo: Raimond Spekking, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Three gabled panels in a modern gilded frame, each with a half-length saint under a round arch on a gold ground and a half-length angel in the gable above. On the left, Saint Geminianus, an elderly bearded bishop in a jewelled mitre, red chasuble and white gloves, holds a crozier and a green book. In the centre, the Archangel Michael, with red-gold hair, a jewel on his brow and folded wings, holds a sword upright and a pair of scales in which a tiny figure of a soul sits in one pan. On the right, Saint Augustine, a bearded bishop in a jewelled mitre and a patterned white and gold cope over the black habit of his order, holds a crozier and a red book.
caption: Simone Martini and workshop, Saints Geminianus, Michael and Augustine, each with an Angel above, lateral panels of the polyptych of Sant'Agostino, San Gimignano, c. 1316–1320. Tempera and gold on panel, each panel about 110.5 × 38.3 cm. Cambridge, The Fitzwilliam Museum, no. 552. Image © The Fitzwilliam Museum, Cambridge.

alt: Wall-sized fresco within a broad painted frame of red and green foliate scrolls set with twenty medallions of prophets, evangelists and doctors of the Church, with Christ blessing at the top centre and a two-faced figure at the bottom centre, alternating with small roundels bearing the black-and-white arms of Siena and the lion of the People. In the centre, against a deep blue ground, the Virgin sits crowned on a tall openwork Gothic throne, holding the standing Christ Child, who unrolls a scroll. Above her stretches a great canopy of red fabric with a valance of blue, red, black and white heraldic panels, its poles held by apostles and saints. Some thirty saints and angels stand in tiers on either side, and in the foreground four patron saints of Siena kneel with two angels who offer bowls of flowers.
caption: Simone Martini, Maestà, completed June 1315, partly repainted by the artist in 1321. Fresco with applied materials, 763 × 970 cm. Siena, Palazzo Pubblico, Sala del Mappamondo (Sala del Consiglio), north wall. Photo: Museo Civico, Palazzo Pubblico, Siena, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Damaged gabled panel showing the Virgin in half length with her head inclined, wearing a white veil and a red dress fastened with a round brooch, holding on her right arm the Christ Child as a swaddled infant who looks up at her; her left hand rests across her body; much of the gold ground and of the blue mantle is lost, revealing the preparation beneath.
caption: Simone Martini, Madonna and Child, c. 1321, tempera on wood, 88 × 51 cm. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale (from the Pieve di San Giovanni Battista, Lucignano d'Arbia). Photo: Pinacoteca Nazionale di Siena, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Polychrome wooden statue of the crucified Christ without its cross, arms raised diagonally. The emaciated body shows carved ribs, a bleeding side wound with painted blood running down the right leg, and red scourge marks on the limbs. The bowed head with closed eyes and brown hair is serene; a long grey-green loincloth with gilded borders reaches the knees
caption: Christ Crucified, second half of the 14th century, polychrome wooden statue, height 210.2 cm, Fabriano, Pinacoteca civica "Bruno Molajoli"; from the Oratory of the Holy Sepulchre (Oratorio dei Beati Becchetti), Sant'Agostino.

alt: Life-size wooden statue of the dead Christ lying on his back, seen foreshortened from the feet, whose soles show carved nail holes. The forearms are crossed over the lower chest, the bearded head rests with closed eyes, and a deeply folded cloth wraps the hips. The painted surface is almost entirely worn away, exposing bare brown wood
caption: Dead Christ, second half of the 14th century, polychrome wooden statue, length 188 cm, Fabriano, Pinacoteca civica "Bruno Molajoli"; from the Oratory of the Holy Sepulchre (Oratorio dei Beati Becchetti), Sant'Agostino.

alt: Polychrome wooden Pietà: the Virgin, seated in a dark hooded mantle with a pale, still face, holds the rigid pale body of the dead Christ horizontally across her lap. His bearded head falls sharply backward over her knee with mouth open, one arm dangling, and a long white cloth in sharp parallel folds wraps his hips and thighs. Red wounds mark the chest and limbs
caption: Pietà, second half of the 14th century, polychrome wooden statue, height 131.8 cm, Fabriano, Pinacoteca civica "Bruno Molajoli"; from the Oratory of the Holy Sepulchre (Oratorio dei Beati Becchetti), Sant'Agostino.

alt: Polychrome wooden statue of a young, beardless St John the Evangelist standing with hands tightly clasped at his chest. His head tilts toward one shoulder, brows knotted and eyes raised in grief. He wears a grey-brown tunic with a gilded collar under a deep green, gold-bordered mantle that crosses the body in heavy diagonal folds, falling to his feet on a small octagonal base
caption: St John the Evangelist, second half of the 14th century, polychrome wooden statue, height 171.6 cm, Fabriano, Pinacoteca civica "Bruno Molajoli"; from the Oratory of the Holy Sepulchre (Oratorio dei Beati Becchetti), Sant'Agostino.

alt: Polychrome wooden statue of the grieving Virgin standing upright, entirely wrapped in a dark hooded mantle falling to the ground. A white veil with ornamented ends frames her pale, still face with lowered eyes, and descends over a dark violet dress carved in dense vertical pleats. Her bare hands hang open and empty at her sides in a gesture of helpless sorrow
caption: Grieving Virgin, second half of the 14th century, polychrome wooden statue, height 178.5 cm, Fabriano, Pinacoteca civica "Bruno Molajoli"; from the Oratory of the Holy Sepulchre (Oratorio dei Beati Becchetti), Sant'Agostino.

alt: Life-size wooden effigy of the dead Virgin lying on her back, seen foreshortened from the feet. Her forearms are crossed over the breast, one hand laid over the other arm, her pale aged face rests with closed eyes, framed by carved waves of hair. The dress covering the whole body is carved into long, thin parallel pleats that break over the feet in sharp angular folds. The painted surface is largely worn away to bare brown wood
caption: Dead Virgin, second half of the 14th century, polychrome wooden statue, length 187 cm, Fabriano, Pinacoteca civica "Bruno Molajoli"; from the Oratory of the Holy Sepulchre (Oratorio dei Beati Becchetti), Sant'Agostino.
