caption: Standing Magus (Balthazar), 1360–70, carved and painted wood (poplar, single block), 178 × 65 cm, Rome, Museo Nazionale del Palazzo di Venezia (VIVE – Vittoriano e Palazzo Venezia), inv. 14035.

alt: Fourteenth-century painted wooden statue of Saint Anatolia, crowned and standing in a red rosette-patterned gown with gilded borders, holding a miniature walled town with towers on her left hand; the visible paint is probably later repainting. Maestro dei Magi di Fabriano, Museo Diocesano Giacomo Boccanera, Camerino.
caption: Sant'Anatolia with the Model of Her Town, second half of the fourteenth century (the visible polychromy probably later), carved and painted wood, dimensions unpublished, Camerino, Museo Diocesano "Giacomo Boccanera"; from Esanatoglia.

alt: Fourteenth-century life-size painted wooden statue of a standing woman, presented in 2014 as St Helena though no surviving sign confirms it, with braided hair coiled about her head and no crown, in a fitted green bodice with applied bosses and a patterned skirt and mantle; a dark stump of the lost attribute survives between the fingers of her left hand at the hip. Attributed to the Maestro dei Magi di Fabriano, private collection.
caption: Female saint presented as St Helena, attributed to the master, 1375–78, carved and painted poplar wood, traces of gilding, height 185 cm (with base; c. 170 cm reported without), Private collection.

alt: Left panel of the Sterbini Diptych: on a gold ground, the half-length Virgin in a dark blue star-studded mantle holds the Christ Child, who reaches for a small bird offered by the grey-bearded Saint Joseph; below, three standing saints — Lawrence in a red patterned dalmatic, Philip in a pink mantle, and John the Baptist in a green mantle holding a scroll; Right panel of the Sterbini Diptych: above, Christ crucified against a gold sky with a flying angel, the Virgin in blue on the left, Saint John the Evangelist in a pink mantle on the right, and Mary Magdalene in red kneeling at the foot of the cross before a green wall; below, Saint Francis kneels in a rocky landscape receiving the stigmata from a red six-winged seraph, beside Saint Louis of Toulouse in a mitre and a blue cope sown with gold fleurs-de-lis.
caption: Sterbini Diptych, left panel: Virgin and Child with Saint Joseph; Saints Lawrence, Philip and John the Baptist; right panel: Crucifixion; Stigmatisation of Saint Francis; Saint Louis of Toulouse, third–fourth decade of the 14th century, tempera and gold on panel, 32.5 × 25.5 cm (each), Rome, Museo Nazionale del Palazzo di Venezia, inv. 10202.

alt: Half-length Virgin on a gold ground, wearing a dark blue mantle with gold borders over a red-brown veil, and a broad white turned-back lining across her shoulders; she inclines her head towards the curly-haired Christ Child seated on her left arm, who wears a rose mantle shot with gold, grasps the edge of her veil with one hand and holds a small white bird against his chest with the other
caption: The Madonna and Child, second quarter of the 14th century, tempera and gold on panel, 47.5 × 34.2 cm, private collection (formerly Sir Kenneth Clark, Saltwood; Christie's, London, 8 July 2021, lot 34).

alt: Damaged fourteenth-century triptych with three round-arched gold-ground panels framed by twisted gilt colonnettes: at the centre the half-length Virgin in a star-strewn blue mantle with a white turned-back lining holds the Christ Child; on the left Saint Agatha in a blue robe patterned with double-headed eagles holds a cross; on the right the bearded Saint Bartholomew in a pink mantle holds a scroll; two small roundels between the arches, one bearing a black eagle
caption: Madonna and Child between Saints Agatha and Bartholomew, 14th century, tempera and gold on panel, Messina, Museo Regionale, inv. 964 (from the church of San Gioacchino, Messina).

alt: Small gabled triptych on gold ground: the central panel shows the Crucifixion in the gable, the Virgin and Child enthroned among angels with Saints Peter and Paul, and four standing saints below; the left wing shows the Angel Gabriel, the lion of Saint Mark, Saint Michael between two saints, and Saint George slaying the dragon; the right wing shows the Virgin Annunciate, an evangelist symbol, Saint John the Baptist between two saints, and Saints Francis, Dominic and Louis of Toulouse
caption: Master of the Sterbini Diptych (attributed; catalogued by the National Trust as Italo-Byzantine School), The Virgin and Child Enthroned with Saints (Polesden Lacey Triptych), c. 1317–50, tempera and gold on panel, 39.4 × 27.9 cm, Polesden Lacey, The McEwan Collection (National Trust), inv. NT 1246462. Bequeathed with the estate by Margaret Helen Greville, 1942. Image: Art UK (artuk.org/artworks/2177); licence terms on the Art UK website.

alt: Half-length Virgin on a gold ground richly incised with foliate ornament, wearing a dark blue-black mantle strewn with gold stars, a red-edged veil framing her pale face, and a broad white turned-back lining across her shoulders; she inclines her head towards the auburn-haired Christ Child on her left arm, who wears an olive-green tunic and a red mantle sprinkled with gold, looks up at her, raises one hand to her veil and holds a rolled scroll in the other; the panel has a raised gilt frame, fine craquelure and scattered wormholes
caption: Master of the Sterbini Diptych (attr.), Madonna and Child, 1330–1340, tempera and gold on panel, 33.2 × 26.7 cm, Assisi, Museo del Tesoro della Basilica di San Francesco, Collezione F. M. Perkins.

alt: Fresco of the Crucifixion in the Tarlati chapel of Arezzo Cathedral, attributed to the Maestro del Vescovado. Christ, his feet crossed and fixed with a single nail, hangs against a deep blue ground beneath a red titulus reading IHS NAZARENUS REX IUDEORUM, surrounded by eight small angels, four bearing inscribed scrolls and three gathering his blood in vessels. Below stand Saint Michael with a lowered sword, the mourning Virgin, Saint John the Evangelist and Saint Francis holding a red book; a small armoured donor kneels at the foot of the cross beside a skull on the rocky ground.
caption: Maestro del Vescovado (attributed), Crucifixion with the Virgin, Saints Michael, John the Evangelist and Francis, and the kneeling donor Ciuccio Tarlati, fresco, c. 1334. Arezzo, Cathedral of San Donato, chapel of Ciuccio Tarlati.

alt: Gothic triptych on a gold ground with three standing figures under pointed arches. At left, Saint Dominic in a black mantle over a white habit holds a lily and a red book; at centre, Saint Michael in dark armour and a pink mantle, his grey wings spread, drives a long lance into the head of a dragon coiled beneath his feet; at right, the bearded Saint Paul in a green tunic and mauve mantle holds an upright sword and a red book. Small roundels in the spandrels show the Annunciation, with Gabriel and the Virgin flanking the central arch, and two Dominican saints at the outer corners, identifiable as Thomas Aquinas with his open book and, probably, Peter Martyr.
caption: Maestro del Vescovado (attributed), Saint Michael the Archangel between Saints Dominic and Paul, with the Annunciation and two Dominican saints in the spandrel roundels, tempera and gold on panel, c. 1340–1360. Arezzo, San Domenico.

alt: Fragmentary fresco from San Domenico in Arezzo. At right, a youthful Christ sits on a white Gothic throne with crocketed pinnacles, wearing a blue robe spangled with gold; his raised right hand gestures toward the lost left half of the scene, and a long scroll bearing many lines of text hangs beside the throne. Large plaster losses interrupt the centre and left, where remnants of kneeling figures and small heads survive from the group once sheltered by the Virgin’s mantle. Along the lower edge runs a fragmentary painted inscription, and beneath the scene a broad ornamental band of interlaced circles with rosettes.
caption: Maestro del Vescovado (attributed), Virgin of Mercy with Christ Enthroned, fragmentary fresco, mid-fourteenth century. Arezzo, San Domenico.

alt: The end wall of a transept with Baroque gilded stucco. In the upper half, inside a stucco frame, a fresco of a tree with Christ crucified at the foot of a green trunk and many round scenes on white scroll-bands that run diagonally from the trunk; at the right of this field a damaged fresco of a horseman. A marble prophet with a tablet sits at the left of the frame. Below a cornice, the lower part of the same tree with branches, round scenes and a row of standing saints in brown habits and a figure in red, and a white plaque with an inscription at the centre. At the right a large wooden vestibule with a fanlight and bronze statues covers part of the wall.
caption: Maestro dell'Albero della Vita, Tree of Life, c. 1347, fresco. Bergamo, Santa Maria Maggiore, end wall of the right transept. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The lower part of the fresco below a gilded meander cornice. A green trunk rises at the centre and divides into branches with round scenes: at the left an Annunciation in a double Gothic shrine and a Nativity with a golden manger and shepherds; at the right a Circumcision and an enthroned Virgin with a Magus. On a sandy ground stand, from left, a nun praying, a friar raising a scroll, a hooded figure in brown, Saint Bonaventure kneeling with a book and scroll beside a red cardinal's hat, a small kneeling man in red, a young saint in red and green, and two friars raising scrolls. At the centre below, a white plaque with fourteen lines of capitals.
caption: Maestro dell'Albero della Vita, Tree of Life, the lower field, c. 1347, fresco. Bergamo, Santa Maria Maggiore. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (detail).

alt: Three standing haloed figures on a grey-green ground above a sandy strip. At the left a nun in a dark habit and white wimple, hands joined, looking up with an anguished face. In the centre Saint Francis, tonsured, in a brown habit with a cord, raising in his right hand an unrolled scroll inscribed in Gothic letters EGO STIGMATA DNI YHU IN CORPORE MEO PORTO, his mouth open. At the right a figure wrapped in a brown-red mantle drawn over the head, one hand at the breast, looking upwards. A gilded candlestick crosses the foot of the image.
caption: Maestro dell'Albero della Vita, Tree of Life, Saint Clare, Saint Francis and the Virgin, c. 1347, fresco. Bergamo, Santa Maria Maggiore. Photo: Fabrizio Garrisi, public domain (CC0), via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A tonsured friar with a gilded halo, in a brown habit, holds a red book against his body and raises with his right hand a large pale scroll, its upper edge inscribed in Gothic letters IESUM CRISTUM PREDICAMUS CRUCIFIXUM. Behind him the green trunk of the tree divides into branches; at the upper left a round scene of the Nativity with the Virgin and Child, a golden manger and shepherds; at the upper right a round scene of the Circumcision. At the right of the friar a broad red cardinal's hat lies on the ground. The plaster is stained and worn, with nails in it.
caption: Maestro dell'Albero della Vita, Tree of Life, Saint Bonaventure, c. 1347, fresco. Bergamo, Santa Maria Maggiore. Photo: Richard Mortel, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons (detail).

alt: At the lower left a small kneeling man in a long red gown lined with white and a red hood, hands joined, in profile. Beside him a young saint with curly hair and a gilded halo, in a green tunic and a red-orange mantle, his hands clasped at his waist, looking up. At the right two tonsured friars with gilded haloes in brown habits, each raising a pale scroll above his head; the outer scroll is inscribed in Gothic letters VESTIGIA EIUS SECUTUS EST PES MEUS. At the upper left, part of a round scene with a priest holding a child.
caption: Maestro dell'Albero della Vita, Tree of Life, the donor, Saint John the Evangelist and two Franciscan saints, c. 1347, fresco. Bergamo, Santa Maria Maggiore. Photo: Fabrizio Garrisi, public domain (CC0), via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A round scene on a blue ground set on a green branch. At the left, an old priest with a white head-cloth and a pink mantle holds the legs of the Child and bends to circumcise him; a bearded man stands behind. The Virgin, haloed, in a dark red mantle, holds the Child, who clings to her face; Joseph, haloed, with white hair, in a yellow mantle, stands at the right. A boy in green kneels below and holds out a basin. Above at the right, part of another round scene with the Virgin seated on a turned wooden chair. At the left, part of a pale scroll; at the top, a branch scroll with red letters.
caption: Maestro dell'Albero della Vita, Tree of Life, the Circumcision, c. 1347, fresco. Bergamo, Santa Maria Maggiore. Photo: Fabrizio Garrisi, public domain (CC0), via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A pale rectangular painted plaque framed in yellow, ruled with fine lines, with fourteen lines of black classicising capitals beginning VENERABILIS VIR DNVS FRATER BONAVENTVRA and ending DEPINGERE FECIT ANNO A NATIVITATE DNI MCCCXLVII. At its sides, fragments of painted ornament in red, ochre and grey.
caption: Maestro dell'Albero della Vita, Tree of Life, the inscription below Saint Bonaventure, probably repainted in the seventeenth century. Bergamo, Santa Maria Maggiore. Photo: Richard Mortel, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The upper part of the fresco inside a white and gilded stucco frame. At the centre a green trunk; at its foot Christ crucified, his arms stretched along the lowest branches, his head bowed, with a white loincloth. White scroll-bands with Gothic writing run diagonally from the trunk on both sides, with round scenes between them: several Crucifixions, a Deposition with a ladder, a Lamentation over the dead Christ, and higher up the Virgin and Christ enthroned and crowds of saints and angels. At the right edge, standing and half-length figures with scrolls outside the tree. At the left a carved prophet holds a tablet.
caption: Maestro dell'Albero della Vita, Tree of Life, the upper field, c. 1347, fresco. Bergamo, Santa Maria Maggiore. Photo: Rollroboter, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A tall panel with a gabled top on a black ground. At the centre Christ crucified on a green tree trunk, from which twelve branches with leafy orange borders spread, six on each side, each carrying four round gold-ground scenes. At the top, the Virgin and Christ enthroned above rows of saints and angels in choir stalls; above the cross a pelican in its nest. At the foot, two writing figures with scrolls on each side of the trunk and, along the bottom, small scenes of the creation and fall of Adam and Eve.
caption: Pacino di Bonaguida, Tree of Life, c. 1305–1310, tempera and gold on panel. Florence, Galleria dell'Accademia. Photo: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The end wall of a refectory under a wooden roof. At the centre a large fresco of the Tree of Life: Christ crucified on a tree whose scroll-like branches carry round medallions with prophets holding scrolls; at its foot the mourning women and Saint John at the left, a Franciscan embracing the cross, a seated friar writing, and standing saints and a bishop at the right. At the sides, four scenes: Saint Francis receiving the stigmata, a bishop and friars serving at a table, a hermit in a rocky landscape, and a supper with a woman at Christ's feet. Along the bottom, the Last Supper with Christ and the apostles at a long table.
caption: Taddeo Gaddi, Tree of Life with the Last Supper and four scenes, mid-fourteenth century, fresco. Florence, Santa Croce, former refectory. Photo: Armin Kleiner, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Detached fresco of the Crucifixion under a round arch: Christ on the cross against a dark blue sky, God the Father in a red circular glory above, the fainting Virgin supported by holy women at left, the Magdalene embracing the cross, Saint John and Longinus at right, a Gothic inscription below.
caption: Crucifixion, 1345, detached fresco, 450 × 398 cm, from the abbey of San Biagio in Caprile, Fabriano, Pinacoteca Civica "Bruno Molajoli".

alt: Detached fresco of the Crucifixion under a round arch: Christ on the cross against a dark blue sky: detail of the whole fresco
caption: Crucifixion (detail), 1345, detached fresco, 450 × 398 cm, from the abbey of San Biagio in Caprile, Fabriano, Pinacoteca Civica "Bruno Molajoli".

alt: Detached round-arched painted niche: an Annunciation with the kneeling angel at left and the Virgin in a slender pavilion at right, separated by a blank window; badly damaged Flagellation fragments below; bishop and monk saints on the side walls; quatrefoils with saints in the arch.
caption: Annunciation, Flagellation, Enthroned Saint and Saints, 1345, detached fresco, 339 × 249 × 61 cm, from the abbey of San Biagio in Caprile, Fabriano, Pinacoteca Civica "Bruno Molajoli".

alt: Fresco of the archangel Gabriel kneeling in profile to the right, in a rose-red robe with a turquoise sash, large pink wings open behind him, one hand raised in a speaking gesture, against a dark ground within an orange frame.
caption: The Archangel Gabriel, detail of the Annunciation in the San Biagio niche, 1345, detached fresco, Fabriano, Pinacoteca Civica "Bruno Molajoli".

alt: Fresco of the Virgin kneeling in profile to the left with arms crossed on her breast and head bowed, in a pale mantle over a red dress, enclosed in a slender white pavilion on a polygonal platform, with a doorway behind and a saint in a quatrefoil above
caption: The Virgin Annunciate, detail of the Annunciation in the San Biagio niche, 1345, detached fresco, Fabriano, Pinacoteca Civica "Bruno Molajoli".

alt: Fresco detail from the arch intrados: half-length Saint Paul in profile to the left, bald with a dark beard and stern expression, in a salmon-red mantle over a green tunic, holding a white rounded pommel, within a white quatrefoil on a dark ground surrounded by red and green lozenges
caption: Saint Paul, quatrefoil from the intrados of the San Biagio niche, 1345, detached fresco, Fabriano, Pinacoteca Civica "Bruno Molajoli".

alt: Fresco of Saint Blaise, frontal half-length bishop with a white mitre and long white beard, wide staring eyes, in a red vestment, against a dark blue ground in a green frame with a pearl-pattern frieze; the lower half is lost and filled with neutral plaster
caption: Saint Blaise, side wall of the San Biagio niche, 1345, detached fresco, Fabriano, Pinacoteca Civica "Bruno Molajoli".

alt: Fresco of Saint Benedict in three-quarter view to the left, wearing a grey monastic hood and habit, gaunt stern face, holding a short rod in his right hand, against a grey ground in a green frame; the lower part is heavily damaged and partly lost
caption: Saint Benedict, side wall of the San Biagio niche, 1345, detached fresco, Fabriano, Pinacoteca Civica "Bruno Molajoli".

alt: Wide view of a damaged fresco wall: at left a Crucifixion with the mourning Virgin and Saint John against a dark mottled ground; at right, after a patterned border, an Annunciation with the standing Virgin in a Gothic loggia and a kneeling pink-robed angel with green wings
caption: Crucifixion with the Virgin and Saint John and Annunciation, 1330s, fresco, Fabriano, Santa Maria Maddalena.

alt: Gabled gilded panel painting: in the triangular top, Christ enthroned in a blue mantle surrounded by haloed apostles; below, in a vaulted room, Christ bound to a column scourged by two tormentors, flanked at left by holy women in blue and red and at right by three saints, a bishop, a deacon and a saint in red
caption: Master of Campodonico (attr.), Last Judgement, Flagellation of Christ and Saints, 1320–1340, tempera on panel, 93 × 106 cm, La Valletta, MUŻA (già National Museum of Fine Arts).

alt: Gold-ground altarpiece. At the centre the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle with gold stars over a red dress, sits on a tall throne holding the Christ Child, with two winged archangels behind her. Six standing saints in two tiers flank each side, each named on a red band below. A small woman in black kneels at the Virgin's feet
caption: Virgin and Child Enthroned with Archangels, Saints and the Donor Elena (Dossal of Domina Elena), dated 1308, tempera and gold on panel, Cesi (Terni), church of Santa Maria Assunta, chapel of the Santissimo Sacramento (Archdiocese of Spoleto-Norcia).

alt: Gold-ground triptych with a tall central panel between two narrow wings. In the centre, inside a pointed mandorla edged in red and pale blue and lifted by eight winged angels, Christ embraces the Virgin, who leans her head against his; below, the apostles crowd behind a long pink marble tomb. Each wing holds four small scenes stacked one above another and separated by red inscription bands. On the left the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle, receives a heavenly messenger, an angel, the apostle John and the gathered apostles. On the right the apostles surround her deathbed, carry her bier in procession and lower her body into the tomb
caption: Triptych of the Assumption and Dormition of the Virgin (the "Stella triptych"), c. 1300, tempera and gold on panel; central panel 186 × 92 cm (91 cm in AGORHA), each wing 177 × 44 cm. Paris, Musée Marmottan Monet, on deposit since 1993 from the Académie des Beaux-Arts, Institut de France (Ephrussi de Rothschild bequest). From the convent of Santi Stefano e Tommaso, called "della Stella", Spoleto.

alt: Large painted cross on a black background. Christ hangs with outstretched arms against a gold field, his head upright and his eyes open, his pale body wrapped in a striped loincloth. Two small angels with blue wings hover beneath his arms. The Virgin, in a dark mantle, stands to the left of his body and John, in pink, to the right. In the square ends of the arms stand two small saints, and at the top Christ blesses from a red mandorla between two angels. At his feet kneel Francis in a brown habit and Dominic in black and white, and blood runs down the shaft below
caption: Christus triumphans (painted cross with Christ blessing, the Virgin, John the Evangelist, Saints Stephen and Thomas, and Saints Francis and Dominic), c. 1300–1310, tempera and gold on panel, 245 × 158 cm. Spoleto, Museo Nazionale del Ducato di Spoleto, Rocca Albornoziana; probably from the convent of Santi Stefano e Tommaso, called "della Stella", Spoleto.

alt: Small open triptych with arched wings, its gold ground worn and darkened. In the upper half of the central panel, under a round arch divided by a red column, the Virgin in a dark blue mantle holds the Christ Child in red, and beside her Saint Anne in a grey mantle holds the child Mary; two small angels fly above. Below, Christ hangs on the cross between the Virgin and John, and to the right Christ kneels in prayer on a pale rocky hill with dark trees. Each wing holds three registers of standing saints in pairs, among them a bishop in a mitre, a friar in a brown habit, an angel and a figure in a black habit
caption: Attributed to the Maestro di Cesi, Portable triptych with the Virgin and Child and Saint Anne with the Child Mary Enthroned, the Crucifixion, the Agony in the Garden, and Saints including Augustine and Sperandeo, c. 1290–1325, tempera and gold on panel, c. 95 × 93 cm (open). Perugia, Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria.

alt: Tall arched gold-ground panel. The Virgin, in a dark blue mantle with a gold-studded border over a red dress, and a white veil striped with red, sits on a throne with round red cushions, her feet on a pale step above a blue-green floor. On her knee sits the Christ Child in an olive-green tunic and mantle, with a gilded cross halo; he reaches up to touch her face and holds a small scroll. In the corners above the arch, two half-length prophets hold scrolls that curve along the frame. A two-line inscription runs along the base
caption: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco (identified by recent scholarship with the late Maestro di Cesi), Madonna and Child Enthroned with a Donor and Two Prophets (Madonna della Selvetta), 1332, tempera and gold on panel, 157 × 63 cm. Castel Ritaldi, Colle del Marchese, parish church; from Santa Maria della Selva Mattutina, Montefalco.

alt: Detached fresco: the Virgin, enthroned beneath a painted canopy with a pointed arch, nurses the Christ Child; two angels hold a patterned cloth of honour behind her. To the left stands Saint Lucy, her face lost to damage; to the right, Saint Catherine of Alexandria in a pleated gown and a mitred bishop saint with crozier raised in blessing. Painted balconies with geometric marble inlay recede on either side; areas of bare plaster mark old losses.
caption: Madonna and Child Enthroned (Madonna lactans) with Saints Lucy, Catherine of Alexandria and Emilian (identified from the abbey's dedication), second decade of the 14th century, detached fresco transferred to a stretcher support, 349 × 346 cm, Fabriano, Pinacoteca Civica "Bruno Molajoli", from the abbey of Sant'Emiliano in Congiuntoli, Scheggia e Pascelupo.

alt: Gothic chapel wall in fresco: a pointed lancet window with blue leaded glass is framed by painted marble ornament and four standing saints on two levels, several damaged. In the lunette above, a dead monk lies on a bed mourned by black-robed friars, while a mitred bishop amid four angels carries the small figure of his soul heavenward
caption: Fabriano, Sant'Agostino, Gothic chapel of Saint Augustine: window wall with flanking saints and, in the lunette, the Transitus of a Monk (the Hugues de Fontenay legend), first decades of the 14th century.

alt: View up into a quadripartite vault: four ribs painted with bands of chevrons, chequers and rosettes meet at a central boss. In the dark blue-grey webs, roundels contain half-length saints — a figure in a red mantle, a mitred bishop with a book, and another bishop holding an open scroll — with large areas of plaster loss
caption: Fabriano, Sant'Agostino, Gothic chapel: rib vault with half-length saints in medallions, first decades of the 14th century.

alt: Detail of a fourteenth-century fresco: Christ, with cruciform halo and a red nail-wound on his extended right hand, draws aside his mantle at the breast while a youthful figure with long auburn hair reaches to touch the wound. Behind press haloed apostles, including grey-haired Peter, before rose-coloured architecture.
caption: Fabriano, Sant'Agostino, Magdalen chapel: the Risen Christ shows his wounds (probably the Incredulity of Thomas), detail, first decades of the 14th century.

alt: Fourteenth-century fresco on a dark blue ground: at left a haloed bishop saint rides a white horse, right hand raised in blessing, attended by three angels, two holding lilies and one flying above. At right a tall pink prison tower with a wooden gallery; a man in a pale tunic climbs down from an opening, stepping on a crouching companion, while another figure holds up broken fetters toward the saint. Large plaster losses interrupt the lower centre.
caption: Fabriano, Sant'Agostino, chapel of Saint Augustine: Saint Augustine frees the prisoner from the tower, first decades of the 14th century.

alt: Close view of a fourteenth-century fresco Crucifixion: the head and torso of Christ on an ochre cross against a dark slate-blue ground. His head, in a radiate halo with red jewelled compartments, sinks to the right shoulder with closed eyes; thin rivulets of dark red blood run from the side wound down his flank; a transparent loincloth veils the hips. The pale surface is worn and scratched
caption: Fabriano, Sant'Agostino, chapel of Saint Augustine: Crucifixion, detail of Christ, first decades of the 14th century.

alt: Detail of a fourteenth-century fresco: four women in profile look up toward the left, praying. The first wears a gold fleur-de-lis crown and a white gown with jewelled bands; behind her stand a young woman in rose, an older woman in ochre, and an aged woman in grey-green with a deeply wrinkled face. At the left edge, red drapery and a pole with a knotted white cloth mark the object of their gaze, outside the frame.
caption: Fabriano, Sant'Agostino, Magdalen chapel: female devotees led by a crowned princess (probably the audience of the Magdalen's preaching at Marseille), detail, first decades of the 14th century.

alt: Fourteenth-century fresco lunette: a mitred bishop saint, enthroned frontally in a red cope over white robes, extends both arms to place his hands on the heads of two kneeling young figures in courtly dress, each holding a small white object. Two differently patterned cloths of honour hang behind; small dark winged creatures — the expelled demons — fly toward the upper corners. A painted corbel cornice runs below; ornamental borders frame the arch.
caption: Fabriano, Sant'Agostino, chapel of Saint Augustine: Saint Augustine liberates two possessed, lunette, first decades of the 14th century.

alt: Semicircular fresco framed by a red band and a border of small ornaments, with a roundel of green leaves on a red ground in the corner at the upper left. At the left a young female saint with a gold halo and a small diadem, in a red dress with gold bands and a yellow mantle lined in green, stands against a blue ground holding a small round object between her fingers. At the centre the Virgin, in a white veil and a grey-green mantle, stands or sits before a red cloth of honour with a gold border, holding on her left arm the Child, who wears a red cloak and raises his hand to her face. The right half of the fresco is almost entirely lost, reduced to bare plaster with a few traces of red.
caption: Memmo di Filippuccio (attributed), Virgin and Child with a Female Saint, c. 1305. Fresco. San Gimignano, Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta. Collegiata di Santa Maria Assunta, San Gimignano, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Wall of a small vaulted room under a pointed arch, pierced at the centre by a deep window niche. The upper register, on a blue ground with trees, shows at the right a pink house where a man in a pink gown with a white fur collar holds out a green and gold purse to a youth in red, while an old woman in a white veil stands behind them; at the centre three figures with long hair, the first holding a yellow flower, stand before a large white pavilion with a conical roof and a striped border, at whose entrance a youth in red embraces a woman in black who holds a yellow purse behind his back; at the far left a youth in red covers his face while two figures, one raising a stick, drive him away, and one of them holds a yellow purse. The lower register shows at the left two youthful figures at a window above a woman in red who rides and whips an old bearded man crawling on all fours, and at the right a figure in red holding a book before striped curtains, his head lost, with a figure in pink leaning on his shoulder. At the right edge part of the adjoining wall is visible, with two standing women and a small white dog; above the arch, painted coats of arms on the vault.
caption: Memmo di Filippuccio (attributed), Scenes of Profane Love: the Story of a Youth, Aristotle and the Courtesan, and a Reader, c. 1305–1311. Fresco. San Gimignano, Palazzo Comunale, Camera del Podestà (Musei Civici). Photo: Holger Uwe Schmitt, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco detail. At the left, in a red building with a round-arched window, two youthful figures with fair bobbed hair and gold-bordered collars look out, one raising a hand. In front of a dark blue ground, a young woman in a red gown sits sideways on the back of an old bearded man in a blue-grey robe and a red cap, who crawls on hands and knees across a green meadow with small plants; she raises a whip with long white thongs above her head and holds his belt with her other hand. At the right edge, the painted frame and the wooden shutter of the window niche.
caption: Memmo di Filippuccio (attributed), Aristotle Ridden by the Courtesan, detail of the window wall, c. 1305–1311. Fresco. San Gimignano, Palazzo Comunale, Camera del Podestà (Musei Civici). Photo: Holger Uwe Schmitt, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Wide fresco band above a door with a pointed arch. At the left, under an arcade of pink buildings, a young woman in a long white gown stands beside a companion in a red dress and a dark mantle; a small white dog walks below them. Further right, two men in green and pink gowns and caps stand close together, and in a doorway a man in a red gown and cap turns to a woman in a dark mantle and white veil, who raises her hands. At the centre, under a canopy striped in red, green and yellow, a young man and a young woman, both naked and wearing caps, sit facing each other in a large wooden tub bound with pale hoops. At the right, in a room hung with yellow and red curtains, a maid draws back a curtain while a young man naked to the waist lifts the sheet to climb into a bed with a green and yellow chequered coverlet, where a young woman lies. Below, on the plain wall, two later coats of arms, one with the inscription of a podestà.
caption: Memmo di Filippuccio (attributed), Scenes of Married Life: the Bride Led to the Groom's House, the Bath and the Spouses Retiring to Bed, c. 1305–1311. Fresco. San Gimignano, Palazzo Comunale, Camera del Podestà (Musei Civici). Photo: Holger Uwe Schmitt, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Wide rectangular gold-ground panel divided into a tall arched central compartment and four vertical boards, two at each side, each with two arched compartments one above the other. At the centre the Virgin, in a dark mantle over a red dress, sits enthroned before a red patterned cloth of honour, holding the Child dressed in pale violet and gold; a small nun kneels at the lower right. At the left, above, Saint Peter in a pallium with black crosses holding keys and a red book, and Saint John the Evangelist with an open book; below, Saint Catherine crowned and Saint Agnes holding a lamb with a banner. At the right, above, Saint John the Baptist with a cross-staff and an inscribed scroll, and the Archangel Michael with wings, a lance and an orb; below, Saint Francis with the stigmata and a red book, and Saint Clare in a black veil. Each saint is named by an inscription in the gold ground.
caption: Memmo di Filippuccio (attributed), Virgin and Child Enthroned with a Poor Clare Donor and Saints Peter, John the Evangelist, Catherine of Alexandria, Agnes, John the Baptist, Michael, Francis and Clare, c. 1305–1317. Tempera and gold on panel, 120 × 217 cm. San Gimignano, Pinacoteca (Musei Civici), from the convent of Santa Chiara. Pinacoteca, Musei Civici di San Gimignano, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Tall arched gold-ground compartment. The Virgin, frontal and slightly turned, sits on a throne covered with a red cloth of honour patterned with gold quatrefoils and small crosses; she wears a dark mantle over her head and body, a red dress visible at the cuffs and a green lining spread over her knees. On her left knee sits the Child, with a cross halo, in a pale violet tunic and a gold garment, a white cloth with an embroidered border behind him; he reaches with one hand to the edge of his mother's mantle at her neck, while she rests her hand on his body. At the lower right a small kneeling nun in a brown habit and dark veil raises her hands in prayer. Two gilded rosettes decorate the upper corners, and a painted marble step forms the base.
caption: Memmo di Filippuccio (attributed), Virgin and Child Enthroned with a Poor Clare Donor, central compartment of the dossal from Santa Chiara, c. 1305–1317. Tempera and gold on panel. San Gimignano, Pinacoteca (Musei Civici). Pinacoteca, Musei Civici di San Gimignano, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons (cropped).

alt: Long low gold-ground panel with a shallow gabled top, divided into seven arched compartments separated by gilded colonnettes; small half-length angels fill the spandrels between the arches against a blue-green ground. At the centre, in a taller arch, the Virgin in a dark blue mantle with red lining holds the Child, who wears a red tunic and reaches towards her neck. At the left, a bearded old monk in a dark habit with a staff, a female saint in a red mantle drawn over her head with a raised hand, and a young beardless saint in a dark tunic and red mantle holding a book and raising his hand. At the right, a female saint with braided hair in a green dress holding a small red cross, a young saint with long hair in a red tunic with embroidered bands, and Saint Francis in a brown habit holding a red book. The lower edge of every compartment is lost, showing the bare preparation.
caption: Attributed to Memmo di Filippuccio, Virgin and Child with Six Saints and Angels, late 13th or early 14th century. Tempera and gold on panel. Oristano, Palazzo Arcivescovile. Palazzo Arcivescovile, Oristano, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Panel with a cut-down pointed top, its gold ground surrounded by bare preparation. The Virgin, in half length, wears a dark blue mantle with a gold border drawn over her head, a dark brown veil and a red dress with gold bands at the neck and cuffs; her head is inclined and her eyes look out at the viewer. On her left arm sits the Child, with thick golden curls and a halo with incised decoration, in a bright pink-red tunic with gold collar and cuffs; he holds in one hand a goldfinch and in the other the cord tied to it, while his bare feet show below the tunic. The Virgin raises her right hand towards the bird and supports the Child with her left. The gold ground is tooled with foliate patterns; two metal clamps hold the panel at the sides.
caption: Memmo di Filippuccio (attributed), Virgin and Child with a Goldfinch, c. 1300–1320. Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco in a gabled niche set into a brick wall, its sides painted with fictive marbled panels and its soffit with a patterned band and an oval. At the centre the Virgin, in a dark mantle over a white veil, sits on a white Gothic throne with pinnacles, gables, trefoil arches and oculi, before a red cloth of honour; on her left knee the Child, in a green tunic and a red mantle, raises his right hand in blessing and holds a closed book. At the left a bearded apostle with long hair, in a green tunic and a pink mantle, holds a book and lays his hand on the head of a kneeling young woman in a gold dress and a dark green mantle dotted with white, who joins her hands in prayer. At the right an elderly apostle with short grey curly hair and beard, in a pale blue tunic and an ochre mantle, holds keys and a book and looks up towards the Virgin.
caption: Attributed to Memmo di Filippuccio, Virgin and Child Enthroned with Two Apostles and a Donor, 14th century. Fresco. Certaldo, Chiesa dei Santi Jacopo e Filippo. Chiesa dei Santi Jacopo e Filippo, Certaldo, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

caption: Polittico di Montelabate, c. 1320, tempera and gold leaf on panel, 246 x 236 cm, Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria, Palazzo dei Priori, Perugia.

caption: Altarpiece on both sides depicting Christ on the throne, the Twelve Apostles, 1330-33, mixed technique on poplar panel, 59,9 x 305,5 x 1,6 cm, Städel Museum, Frankfurt am Main.

caption: Madonna col Bambino (scomparto di polittico), 1308-10, tempera on poplar panel, 89,5 x 69,5 x 8 cm Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria, Perugia.

alt: Small gold-ground panel in its original gilded frame, with a cusped trefoil arch and foliate spandrels. In an open courtyard before a grey loggia, a high priest in a jewelled gold cope joins the hands of Joseph, at the left, barefoot in a pink mantle over a blue tunic and holding a rod, and Mary, at the right, in a dark blue dress covered with gold patterns. Behind them stand haloed witnesses, among them an old man and a veiled woman. At the left a crowd of young suitors holds bare rods, and at the lower left a kneeling youth in a dark blue cloak bends his rod; a small boy in a gold-patterned tunic and red hose looks on. At the right musicians play long trumpets, a pipe and a pair of small drums. The figures stand on a red and yellow carpet over a green marbled floor. Above the loggia a balustrade of trefoil arches holds potted plants before a tall tree, women look out from a tower at the upper right, and a bird flies in the gold sky. Along the bottom of the frame runs a gold inscription on a blue band.
caption: Niccolò di Buonaccorso, The Marriage of the Virgin, about 1380. Egg tempera on wood (probably poplar), 50.9 × 33 cm, in its original frame. Signed: NICHOLAVS. BONACHVRSI. DE SENIS. ME P[I]NXIT. London, The National Gallery, NG 1109. The National Gallery, London, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small gold-ground panel in its original gilded frame, with a cusped arch and spandrels decorated with foliage and rosettes in relief; two metal fittings are fixed to the right edge of the frame. The temple is an open pavilion on slender grey columns with pink capitals and cornices, roofed by a pyramid with a small lantern; on its corners two winged putti hold a blue garland. Inside, under a dark blue vault, stands an altar with a silver Gothic tabernacle. At the top of a flight of white steps the high priest, bearded, in a mitre and a gold cope, bends forward with open hands towards the child Mary, who stands on the top step in a dark dress patterned with gold, her hands crossed on her breast. At the foot of the steps, at the left, Saint Anne in a purple mantle and a white wimple looks up at her, followed by young women in gold, blue and red. At the right Joachim, an old bearded man in a blue mantle, stands with a group of men and a woman in a red mantle. Behind a parapet at the right a group of young girls watches. The floor is paved with blue-grey and white marble squares.
caption: Niccolò di Buonaccorso, The Presentation of the Virgin in the Temple, c. 1380. Tempera on panel, 51 × 34 cm (with frame). Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi, inv. 1890 n. 3157, from the hospital of Santa Maria Nuova, Florence. Gallerie degli Uffizi, Florence, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small gold-ground panel in its original engaged frame, with a cusped arch and spandrels decorated with foliage and a small round boss in each corner. At the top, against the gold, a fan of dark blue winged heads of cherubim spreads above a band of white clouds with small heads of angels. Below, surrounded by red seraphim, the Virgin, at the left, in a blue-grey mantle covered with gold patterns, bows her head and crosses her hands on her breast, while Christ, at the right, in a pink tunic and a dark blue mantle, places a crown on her head. They sit side by side on a red cloud with small winged heads. Tiers of haloed angels in gold-patterned garments stand at either side, singing, and two of them play pipes. In the lower half four angels kneel on a carpet with an interlocking fret pattern: at the left one plays a portable organ, at the right one plays a fiddle, and in the centre two angels with wreaths of flowers in their hair face each other.
caption: Niccolò di Buonaccorso, The Coronation of the Virgin, ca. 1380. Tempera on wood, gold ground; overall, with engaged frame, 50.8 × 32.7 cm; painted surface 44.8 × 26.7 cm. New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Robert Lehman Collection, 1975, 1975.1.21. Photo: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, Open Access, public domain.

alt: Tall, narrow gold-ground panel with a gabled top and a carved cusped arch. The Virgin, crowned, with a white veil, wears a deep blue mantle marked with a gold star on the shoulder over a dress patterned with gold. She sits on a Gothic throne painted in pink and orange, whose cusped back opens onto a small vaulted niche. She holds between her fingers the stem of a white flower, which the Christ Child, seated on her knee, grasps while looking up at her. The Child, with curly golden hair, wears a light blue tunic with a gold belt and a red mantle over his legs, and holds in his other hand a small gold basket filled with fruit and flowers. The throne rests on a white step with a zigzag pattern in pink and orange.
caption: Niccolò di Buonaccorso, Madonna and Child, central panel of the polyptych dated 1387, from Santa Margherita at Costalpino. Tempera and gold on wood panel, 152.5 × 58.5 cm. San Diego, Timken Museum of Art, Putnam Foundation, 1998:001. Photo: courtesy of the Timken Museum of Art, San Diego, reproduced with permission.

alt: Tall, narrow gold-ground panel in a carved frame that has lost its gilding, closed at the top by a cusped trefoil arch under a sloping gable decorated with rosettes and scrolls. Saint Lawrence, a young tonsured deacon with a punched halo, stands turned slightly to the left in a long red dalmatic patterned with gold, beneath which a pale tunic with a lozenge pattern and a white alb appear. In his right hand he holds a slender processional cross and a dark palm, in his left a red book. Behind him at the left rises a large gridiron, drawn in gold lines against the gold ground. At the lower left, on a green ground, a woman in a black habit and a white wimple kneels in prayer with two small children, one in red and one in blue.
caption: Niccolò di Buonaccorso, Saint Lawrence with a Kneeling Donor and Two Children, lateral panel of the polyptych dated 1387, from Santa Margherita at Costalpino, later in Sant'Andrea a Montecchio. Tempera and gold on panel, c. 140 × 47 cm. Siena, Museo Diocesano d'Arte Sacra (Oratorio di San Bernardino). Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (background modified).

alt: Fragment of a panel cut to an irregular arched shape, with the edges worn down to the wood. It shows the head and shoulders of the Virgin, turned towards the right, her eyes glancing sideways. She has pale skin with pink cheeks and wavy blond hair, covered by a white veil and a dark blue mantle whose gold border is set with small round dots of red and dark colour. Around her head a large gold halo, now largely worn to the red bole, carries traces of an incised inscription and punched rings. A large loss exposing the brown wood runs from below the lips over the chin and down the breast. At the right edge appear areas of green and ochre.
caption: Niccolò di Buonaccorso, Virgin (fragment), ca. 1377–1383. Tempera and gold on poplar, 36.4 × 27.8 × 1.6 cm. Frankfurt am Main, Städel Museum, inv. 1006. Städel Museum, Frankfurt am Main, public domain.

alt: Narrow gold-ground panel with a pointed arch, showing Saint Lawrence in half length. He is a young tonsured deacon with a broad face, turned slightly to the right, under a punched halo. He wears a red dalmatic with a collar of gold set with red and blue stones and a broad band of gold lattice ornament across the chest; dark blue sleeves appear at his wrists. In his right hand he holds an upright gridiron, painted in black, and in his left a dark palm. The gold ground is worn, revealing the red bole in many places.
caption: Niccolò di Buonaccorso, Saint Lawrence, c. 1370–1375. Tempera on panel, 58.8 × 27.6 cm. Glasgow, Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, acc. 3359, gift of Julius Lewis Lyons, 1980. Photo: Glasgow Life Museums, via Art UK, CC BY-NC-ND.

alt: Small gilded triptych with three steep gables edged with carved crockets. In the central gable Christ hangs on the cross between the Virgin in dark blue and Saint John in yellow, with a kneeling figure at the foot of the cross. Below, the Virgin, in a dark mantle over a dress with gold, sits low on a patterned cushion on the floor, holding the Child, who is dressed in pink, on her knee; behind them runs a low bench with small objects on it. In the left wing the angel of the Annunciation kneels in the gable above Saint Catherine, crowned, in a pink mantle, with her wheel and palm. In the right wing the Virgin Annunciate sits in the gable above Saint Christopher, in red, carrying the Child on his shoulder across the water with a staff.
caption: Niccolò di Buonaccorso, Madonna of Humility with Saints Catherine of Alexandria and Christopher, the Annunciation and the Crucifixion, ca. 1370–1375. Tempera and gold on wood panel, 65.8 × 54.6 cm. San Diego, Timken Museum of Art, Putnam Foundation, 1967:002. Photo: courtesy of the Timken Museum of Art, San Diego, reproduced with permission.

alt: Gabled gold-ground panel in a gilded frame, with broken projections at the sides where wings were once attached. Under a cusped arch the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle over a dress patterned with gold, sits on a throne whose back, patterned in red and gold, rises to a point. She holds the Christ Child, dressed in pink, on her lap. Four angels with gold haloes surround the throne: the two above join their hands in prayer, the two below cross them on their breasts. At the left stands Saint John the Baptist, barefoot, in a camel-hair tunic and a pink mantle lined in blue, pointing to an unrolled scroll with an inscription. At the right stands a bearded bishop saint in a mitre and a gold cope over a white alb, holding a crozier and a red book and looking up. The throne rests on a white step with a patterned riser, above a floor painted to imitate green and white marble.
caption: Niccolò di Buonaccorso, Virgin and Child Enthroned with a Bishop Saint, Saint John the Baptist, and Four Angels, about 1380. Tempera on panel, 46.3 × 31.7 cm. Boston, Museum of Fine Arts, 20.1860, gift of Mrs. Thomas O. Richardson. Photo: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, public domain.

alt: Gabled panel whose frame has lost its gilding and shows the bare wood. In the gable, against a red ground scattered with gold, God the Father, bearded, appears in a mandorla, blessing and holding a book, surrounded by red seraphim and dark blue cherubim; below him a small white dove descends through golden rays. In the main field is a room with a pink and white chequered floor and a low bench running along the walls, its panels painted yellow with small stars, with a hinged panel opening at each side. On the bench at the left lie a round work basket with spools of thread, a piece of needlework and a pair of scissors; on the bench at the right lies a red book. In the centre the Virgin, in a black mantle over a dress patterned with gold, sits on the floor on a gold-patterned cushion and nurses the Christ Child, dressed in pink, whom she holds in her arms, inclining her head towards him.
caption: Niccolò di Buonaccorso, The Virgin of Humility, second half of the 14th century. Tempera on wood (poplar), 54 × 30 cm. Paris, Musée du Louvre, Département des Peintures, RF 1976 7. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (background modified).

alt: Small portable triptych with its wings open, displayed against a brick wall. The central panel stands in a gilded tabernacle frame with twisted colonnettes, a steep gable edged with carved crockets set with red and green glass stones, and a base with three roundels. In the gable Christ blesses in half length. In the main field the Virgin, in a black mantle over a dress patterned with gold, sits on a throne and offers her breast to the Christ Child, who stands on her lap in a white garment; two angels kneel in prayer behind the throne. At the left Saint Catherine of Alexandria, crowned, in a pink mantle, holds a palm and a book beside her wheel; at the right Saint Anthony Abbot, bearded, in a brown habit, holds a book and a tau-headed staff, with a small black pig at his feet. The left wing shows the angel of the Annunciation in its triangular top and a bishop saint in a gold-patterned cope below; the right wing shows the Virgin Annunciate in its top and Saint Christopher, in a red tunic, carrying the Christ Child on his shoulders across the water.
caption: Niccolò di Buonaccorso and workshop, Portable Triptych with the Virgin and Child, Saints Catherine of Alexandria and Anthony Abbot, a Bishop Saint and Saint Christopher, the Annunciation and Christ Blessing, about 1370–1380. Tempera and gold on panel, with original frame. Asciano, Salini Collection. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small gilded triptych with three gabled panels on a moulded base. In the central gable Christ blesses in a quatrefoil. Below, under a cusped arch, the Virgin, in a black mantle over a dress patterned with gold, sits on a throne covered with a red and gold cloth whose back rises to a point, and holds the Christ Child, dressed in pink, standing on her knee; two angels stand behind the throne. In front, at the left, Saint John the Baptist, barefoot in a camel-hair tunic and a green mantle, holds an unrolled scroll; at the right Saint Catherine of Alexandria, in a pink mantle, holds a palm. The left wing shows the angel Gabriel kneeling in its gable and, below, Saint Anthony Abbot, an old bearded hermit in a brown habit with a tau-headed staff, in a rocky landscape with a tree. The right wing shows the Virgin Annunciate seated in its gable and, below, Saint Christopher in a red tunic carrying the Christ Child, who holds a globe, across the water with the help of a leafy staff.
caption: Niccolò di Buonaccorso, Triptych with the Virgin and Child Enthroned between Saints John the Baptist and Catherine of Alexandria, Saints Anthony Abbot and Christopher, the Annunciation and Christ Blessing, about 1370–1380. Tempera and gold on panel. Prague, Národní galerie, O 11916. Národní galerie, Prague, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons (background modified).

alt: Tall, narrow gold-ground panel in its gilded frame, with a steep gable edged with carved crockets. In the gable Christ hangs on the cross on a dark hill, between the Virgin, in a blue and orange mantle, and Saint John the Evangelist, in a pink mantle over a blue tunic. In the main field, under a cusped arch with carved foliage in the spandrels, the Virgin sits on a throne covered with a gold cloth and nurses the Christ Child, dressed in pink, whom she holds in her arms; her mantle has turned a brownish ochre. Three saints stand on either side, one above the other. At the left are a bishop saint in a mitre, Saint Peter with his keys and a young female saint in a gold-patterned dress holding a book; at the right a saint with a pilgrim's staff, Saint Paul with a sword and a book, and Saint Catherine of Alexandria in a pink mantle with a palm and a book. The floor is painted green with scattered leaves.
caption: Niccolò di Buonaccorso, Nursing Virgin Enthroned with Saints Nicholas, Peter, Lucy, James the Greater, Paul and Catherine of Alexandria, and the Crucifixion, about 1370. Tempera and gold on panel, 64.5 × 28 cm (with frame). Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 121. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (background modified).

alt: Small diptych of two rectangular gold-ground panels, hinged together and slightly open, each in its moulded gilded frame with a cusped arch and carved spandrels. In the left panel the Virgin, in a deep blue mantle, sits on a throne covered with a red and gold cloth and holds the Christ Child, in a gold-patterned tunic, on her knee; the Child leans forward to place a ring on the finger of Saint Catherine of Alexandria, who stands at the left, crowned, in a pink mantle, holding a palm. At the right stands Saint John the Baptist, in a camel-hair tunic and a green mantle, pointing to the Virgin and holding a scroll. Two angels stand behind the throne. In the foreground a young haloed figure in a red tunic and a violet mantle kneels in prayer on a floor of pink and white squares, before a stepped dais. In the right panel Christ hangs on the cross against the gold, with four small blue angels in flight around him. The Virgin, in a blue mantle, stands at the left with her hands joined; Saint John, in a pink mantle over a blue tunic, stands at the right looking up; Mary Magdalene, in red, with long golden hair, kneels and embraces the foot of the cross. A skull and bones lie on the rocky ground.
caption: Niccolò di Buonaccorso, Diptych with the Mystic Marriage of Saint Catherine, with Saint John the Baptist and Angels, and the Crucifixion, about 1380. Tempera and gold on panel. L'Aquila, Museo Nazionale d'Abruzzo, from Santa Maria la Nova at Cellino Attanasio. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (background modified).

alt: Two tall, narrow panels painted in grisaille, shown side by side in black-and-white photographs, each closed by a round arch. In the left panel a crowd of haloed saints in tiers turns towards the right: in the front rows stand female saints, among them a young woman with long loose hair holding a small jar, a saint holding a book, a crowned saint and a veiled older woman; behind them rise bearded apostles, one holding a sword and another a staff. In the right panel a crowd of male saints in three rows turns towards the left: in front stand a friar in a habit, two young deacons, one of them holding a gridiron, and an old hermit with a long beard; behind them are bishops in mitres, a saint holding a banner and other bearded saints. The paint surface is crossed by fine cracks.
caption: Niccolò di Buonaccorso, Two Rows of Female Saints and Apostles (left wing), 1375–1399, poplar, 83.2 × 18.8 cm, WAF 265, and Male Saints in Three Rows (right wing), about 1400, wood, 82 × 17.6 cm, WAF 266. Munich, Bayerische Staatsgemäldesammlungen – Alte Pinakothek. Photos: Bayerische Staatsgemäldesammlungen – Alte Pinakothek München, CC BY-SA 4.0 (combined).

alt: Small rectangular panel in its gilded frame, with a cusped arch carved with foliage. The scene is set in a grey house with an upper balcony and an open loggia of round arches with blue vaults. At the left the angel Gabriel, with golden wings, in a pink robe and a gold tunic, kneels on a red and white chequered floor and holds a scroll inscribed Ave Maria Gratia Plena. At the right the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle over a gold-patterned dress, stands beneath the loggia before a red cloth of honour, her hand on her breast and a small red book in her other hand. A golden beam descends diagonally towards her from a small red figure in the upper left corner. In the room behind, a bed with a blue and white checked cover stands against a red wall.
caption: Niccolò di Buonaccorso or workshop, The Annunciation, 1370–1388. Tempera and oil on panel (as catalogued by the museum), 39.1 × 26.4 cm (panel), 46.4 × 31.8 × 3.8 cm (frame). Hartford, Wadsworth Atheneum Museum of Art, The Ella Gallup Sumner and Mary Catlin Sumner Collection Fund, 1951.94. Image for educational use only.

alt: Small rectangular gold-ground panel with a cusped arch carved with foliage in the spandrels. An empty cross rises from a rocky hill against the gold, and four small angels, two dark and two red, fly in grief around it. In the foreground the dead Christ lies on the ground across the laps of the mourners, his body pale and wounded, a gold-patterned cloth over his legs. The Virgin, in a dark mantle, holds his head; a woman with long golden hair in a red dress and a dark mantle spreads her arms; a veiled woman in brown joins her hands in prayer; and Mary Magdalene, in red, with long loose hair, kneels at his feet. At the left a woman in a yellow mantle sits on the ground and Saint John, in a red mantle over a dark tunic, stands with open hands. At the right an old bearded man in a pink and yellow mantle holds a dark jar of ointment, beside a figure in green seen from behind.
caption: Workshop of Niccolò di Buonaccorso, The Lamentation over the Dead Christ, ca. 1380. Tempera on wood, gold ground; overall 41 × 26.7 cm, painted surface 39.4 × 25.4 cm. New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Robert Lehman Collection, 1975, 1975.1.20. Photo: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, Open Access, public domain.

alt: Small rectangular gold-ground panel in a moulded gilded frame, with a punched border of small rosettes around the field. Christ hangs on a tall cross, his slender body pale and bleeding from the side, his head bowed under a punched halo. Two small angels with spread wings fly at either side; the one at the left holds a chalice towards the wound in his side. At the foot of the cross, at the left, the Virgin sits on the ground in a dark mantle, her hands joined, looking up; at the right Saint John sits on the ground in a pink mantle over a blue tunic, clasping his hands and looking up. Between them a small figure in a red cardinal's robe and hood kneels and embraces the foot of the cross, where the blood runs down to the ground.
caption: Niccolò di Buonaccorso, Crucifixion with the Mourning Virgin and Saint John, Two Angels and a Cardinal Saint, about 1380–1388. Tempera and gold on panel. Perugia, Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (background modified).

alt: Illuminated statute leaf. In a red-framed miniature on blue ground, the Virgin and Child sit on a tall grey Gothic throne with pinnacles; the Virgin in blue holds an open book, the Child in red a scroll. At the left stands a bishop saint labelled S. Petronius in white vestments and red-and-blue cope, blessing with crozier; at the right a bishop labelled S. Alle in a pale rose cope holds an open book and crozier. Below, a Latin text in brown ink opens with a pink initial A on gold containing a blessing Christ, with blue, red and green acanthus and gold besants in the left margin. At the foot, three shields: white with a red cross under a blue chief with gold fleurs-de-lis, blue strewn with gold fleurs-de-lis, and blue with a gold chalice.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, Madonna and Child Enthroned between Saints Petronius and Alle (Eligius), with Christ in the Initial A, headpiece leaf from a copy of the 1383 Statutes and Ordinances of the Goldsmiths' Guild of Bologna, in or after 1383. Miniature on vellum, 35.6 × 21 cm. Washington, National Gallery of Art, Rosenwald Collection, 1946.21.149.

alt: Illuminated antiphonary cutting with a large initial F, its stem red and its bow green, on a gold ground. Inside the letter, in a birth chamber with a carved wooden bedhead against a blue flourished ground, the aged, haloed Saint Elizabeth sits up in a bed with a red-and-blue coverlet, one hand to her cheek; a woman in red stands behind the bed with raised hands. In the foreground a midwife in pink lays the haloed newborn Baptist into a wooden tub while a young woman in blue kneels holding a cloth. Blue, red and pink acanthus with gold besants fills the left and upper margins; fragments of brown Gothic letters and square notation on red staves surround the initial.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, The Birth of Saint John the Baptist in an Initial F, cutting from an antiphonary, second half of the fourteenth century. Miniature on vellum, 25.8 × 22.5 cm. Washington, National Gallery of Art, Rosenwald Collection, 1949.5.86.

alt: Full leaf of a legal manuscript in two columns of Gothic script. At the head of the left column, a miniature on gold shows a wedding beneath a loggia: a groom in red places a ring on the finger of a bride in pale pink with long blonde braids, among crowned maidens, men in blue and red, a musician at the left, a long trumpet above and a kneeling drummer with two small drums; five onlookers peer down from the balcony. Below, a large initial P on gold holds a crowned bride kissing a man in red, with a full-length lady in pink standing along the letter's silver stem; further down, an initial D holds a lone young woman in green and pink. A red rubric between miniature and text marks the end of Book III and the beginning of Book IV, De sponsalibus.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, The Marriage, with the Kiss of the Bride (initial P) and the Bride Abandoned (initial D), leaf from a copy of Giovanni d'Andrea's Novella on the Decretals of Gregory IX, opening of Book IV (De sponsalibus et matrimoniis), mid-1350s. Miniature on vellum, 44.5 × 27.3 cm. Washington, National Gallery of Art, Rosenwald Collection, 1961.17.5.

alt: Full-page Crucifixion miniature on a gold ground covered with dark scrolling filigree, within a red frame. The pale, grey-toned Christ hangs on an ochre cross under a titulus scroll; four angels in green, red and blue catch the blood from his hands and side in chalices. At the left the Virgin stands in a deep blue mantle, hands clasped; at the right Saint John, in a pale yellow mantle over blue, raises a hand to his cheek. The red-cloaked Magdalene kneels embracing the foot of the cross and kissing Christ's bleeding feet. In the lower right corner, dark Gothic letters read NICOLAUS F.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, The Crucifixion, single leaf, signed "NICOLAUS F", c. 1390. Ink, tempera and gold on vellum, 26.8 × 20.2 cm (sheet). Cleveland, The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift from J. H. Wade, 1924.1013.

alt: Register page with a full-length Saint Dominic in a red-framed miniature on blue flourished ground: black cloak over white habit, gold halo, red book under one arm, lily stems in the raised hand. Beside and below the miniature, columns of names in Gothic script with later additions in different inks, marginal crosses and 'mor' notes; a red rubric names the quarter of Porta San Procolo. At the foot, a cusped blue-and-red frame holds a shield with black shoemaker's wares on a marbled field. A gold bar with acanthus and gold besants borders the page; Roman foliation xij at top right.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, Saint Dominic, leaf from the register of the shoemakers' guild of Bologna, c. 1386. Tempera and gold on parchment. Los Angeles, J. Paul Getty Museum, Ms. 82.

alt: Illuminated manuscript cutting with a large initial E in two tones of pink, set on a burnished gold square. Below the letter's crossbar Saint Stephen kneels in profile in a grey deacon's dalmatic with gold bands, blood running from his tonsured head, hands raised. Above the bar a man in red lifts a large stone with both hands over the saint, flanked by another stone-thrower in green; at the right a crowned king enthroned under a starry canopy points at Stephen beside a white-veiled, bearded priest gesturing in protest. Fragments of red music staves, square notation and brown Gothic letters surround the initial, with a blue, red and green acanthus border at the left.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, The Martyrdom of Saint Stephen in an Initial E, cutting from the gradual of the Charterhouse of Santo Spirito at Farneta, near Lucca, c. 1394–1402. Tempera, gold and ink on parchment, 19 × 17.6 cm. New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, 2007.236.

alt: Large pink initial S on tooled gold from a choir book. In the upper curve the Virgin stands praying in blue among haloed apostles beneath a domed interior, red rays of fire descending from its vault; in the lower curve six more apostles look upward with raised hands, Peter white-bearded at the centre in red and blue. Blue, red and pink acanthus border at the left; red four-line staves with square notation at the right.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, Initial S: Pentecost, cutting from the gradual of the Charterhouse of Santo Spirito at Farneta, c. 1392–1402. Tempera and gold on parchment. Los Angeles, J. Paul Getty Museum, Ms. 86 (2004.48).

alt: Pink initial S on tooled gold from a choir book, read in two registers. Above, an enthroned bearded ruler in red holds a great sword upright and points to it, beside a man in green with a blue hat raising his hand against a blue flourished ground. Below, the beheaded Saint Paul in pale blue lies fallen, his severed haloed head on the ground; two veiled women hold a white cloth, a bearded executioner stands behind them with his sword, and a red garment lies on the seat at the right. Acanthus border at the left, music staves around.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, Initial S: The Beheading of Saint Paul and the Miracle of Plautilla's Veil, cutting from the Farneta gradual, c. 1392–1402. Tempera and gold on parchment. Los Angeles, J. Paul Getty Museum, Ms. 115 (2017.122.3).

alt: Initial B from a choir book, its red stem knotted with green and its pink bow opening on tooled gold. Inside, three identical bearded figures in sculptural white robes sit side by side beneath a blue canopy; the central one holds an open book and blesses, the outer two raise a hand toward him. Acanthus sprays with gold besants surround the letter; brown Gothic letters and a red stave fragment above; pencil foliation 98 at the upper right.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, Initial B: The Trinity, cutting from the Farneta gradual, c. 1392–1402. Tempera and gold on parchment. Los Angeles, J. Paul Getty Museum, Ms. 115 (2017.122.1).

alt: Tall pink initial from a choir book opening on a blue flourished arch over tooled gold. An executioner in red, seen from behind, grips his sword two-handed, point down, over the fallen body of Saint Paul in grey-blue; the severed bearded head with gold halo lies on the grey ground, blood running from it in streams. Around the executioner press four soldiers in pale blue bascinets and mail, one in a green brigandine pointing. Acanthus border at the left; brown chant letters and red staves around; pencil foliation 94 at the upper right.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, Initial N: The Beheading of Saint Paul, cutting from the Farneta gradual, c. 1392–1402. Tempera and gold on parchment. Los Angeles, J. Paul Getty Museum, Ms. 115 (2017.122.2).

alt: Large pink initial M on tooled gold from a choir book, its middle leg dividing twelve haloed apostles into two groups of six. At the lower left Peter, white-bearded in red and blue, holds a bound book; at the lower right Andrew, long-bearded, holds a tall cross over an open book; behind them rise rows of haloed heads with a knife, books and staves among the attributes. A red rubric above reads that the Common of Saints begins; acanthus border at the left, music staves around; pencil foliation 100 at the upper right.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, Initial M: The Apostles, cutting from the Farneta gradual, c. 1392–1402. Tempera and gold on parchment. Los Angeles, J. Paul Getty Museum, Ms. 115 (2017.122.6).

alt: Round pink initial on tooled gold from a choir book. Inside, on a blue flourished disc, Saint Mary Magdalene stands clothed only in her own long hair, which covers her body like a tawny fleece; her hands cross on her breast and she looks upward to a half-figure of Christ blessing in a white robe among clouds. Four angels in red, orange and green, with golden wings and haloes, bear her up at shoulders and knees. A red rubric above reads magdalene; acanthus border at the left, music staves at the right; pencil foliation 91 at the upper right.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, Initial G: The Assumption of Saint Mary Magdalene, cutting from the Farneta gradual, c. 1392–1402. Tempera and gold on parchment. Los Angeles, J. Paul Getty Museum, Ms. 115 (2017.122.4).

alt: Round initial from a choir book on tooled gold. Under a thatched shed the Virgin kneels in a deep blue mantle, hands joined, before the Child, who lies haloed and swaddled on a wicker manger draped in red; Joseph in red stands behind with his hand to his chin, the ox and the ass lean in at the right, and the saddled donkey stands below. At the left two shepherds in grey, one with a straw hat slung on his staff, look on over their sheep; an angel in red dives over the roof from the upper left. Acanthus border with gold besants above and at the left; music staves at the edges.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, Initial P: The Nativity, cutting from the Farneta gradual, c. 1392–1402. Tempera colors, gold and ink on parchment, 18.8 × 16 cm. Los Angeles, J. Paul Getty Museum, Ms. Burke 30 (2025.59), Gift of T. Robert and Katherine States Burke; formerly Burke Collection.

alt: Full-page Crucifixion from a liturgical manuscript, on a gold ground patterned with dark scrollwork within a red frame. Christ, cross-nimbed and crowned with thorns, hangs on the cross beneath a titulus scroll; four angels in red and green catch the blood from his hands and side, one holding a chalice. The Virgin stands at the left in blue and Saint John at the right in a pale blue mantle, both with clasped hands; the red-clad Magdalene kneels at the foot of the cross on rocky ground. The artist's signature runs along the ground at the lower right.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, The Crucifixion, signed "Nicolaus de Bononia F.", from a liturgical miscellany (ordinal), Bologna, c. 1370. New York, The Morgan Library & Museum, MS M.800, fol. 39v, facing the Canon of the Mass. Image © The Morgan Library & Museum.

alt: Entire antiphonary folio with a monumental initial P at the left, its gold bow and long stem reaching most of the page's height, framed by blue, red and pink acanthus with gold besants on all four margins. In the bow, the Virgin and haloed apostles gaze upward where only a swirl of white drapery remains; Christ himself, haloed and in white, climbs out of the picture field into the upper margin among the acanthus. More apostles stand stacked in the letter's descending stem, and a small two-line signature is painted on the dark blue ground at its base. The chant Post passionem suam per dies quadraginta apparens eis et loquens runs beside the initial in large Gothic letters on red four-line staves.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, Folio from an Antiphonary with Initial P: The Ascension of Christ, signed "EGO NICHOLAUS D(E) BOLONIA FECI(T)", c. 1365. Tempera and gold leaf on vellum, 73.7 × 53.3 cm. Los Angeles, Los Angeles County Museum of Art, M.75.3, Gift of Anna Bing Arnold. Photo: Los Angeles County Museum of Art.

alt: Manuscript page with four lines of Latin verse above a large framed miniature. Inside a grey field tent, against a gold ground worked with scrolling foliage, Julius Caesar sits on a golden bench-throne holding a commander's baton: an elderly, balding, bearded man in a white surcoat strewn with red fleurs-de-lis over blue mail, with gold leg armour. Two shields with the same red fleurs-de-lis hang on the tent walls. Around him press officers and soldiers in bascinets, mail and coloured hoods, with swords; a counsellor in a long blue robe and white coif speaks at his right, and squires seen from behind stand in the foreground.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, Julius Caesar among his Officers, in Lucan, De bello civili (Pharsalia), dated 1373, made for Francesco Gonzaga. Milan, Biblioteca Trivulziana, cod. 691, fol. 86v. Photo: Biblioteca Trivulziana, Milan.

alt: Opening page of the Decretum Gratiani with a large frontispiece on red-and-gold brocade: Christ enthroned in a blue mandorla holding an open book, surrounded by music-making angels with an organ and a lute. Below, two angels flank a golden fountain-tabernacle on an altar between two kneeling crowds — clerics, monks and a mitred prelate at the left, laymen and an armoured knight at the right. On the pale band of the platform runs the signature NICOLAUS DE BONONIA F. Beneath, the text of the Decretum begins in two columns framed by gloss, with Gratian writing at his desk in the initial H and an author bust in a second initial.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, frontispiece of the Decretum Gratiani, signed "NICOLAUS DE BONONIA F(ECIT)", c. 1360. Jena, Thüringer Universitäts- und Landesbibliothek, Ms. El. f. 51c, fol. 2r. Photo: Thüringer Universitäts- und Landesbibliothek Jena, urn:nbn:de:urmel-c7357c1b-e4f0-4028-ab0d-5b01f569a56d0, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

alt: Page of the Decretum with a large miniature on gold brocade: a pope enthroned beneath a gabled canopy, blessing and holding a green book, flanked by red-hatted cardinals, bishops, friars and clerics presenting scrolls. In the foreground jurists in blue and red stand at a long bench with open scrolls and documents. The signature, split in two, runs along the base of the bench. The gloss and text of the Causae surround the miniature; the folio number 101 is visible at the top corner.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, opening of the Causae (Pars II), signed "NICOLAV(S) DE BONONIA F(ECIT)", c. 1360. Jena, ThULB, Ms. El. f. 51c, fol. 101r. Photo: Thüringer Universitäts- und Landesbibliothek Jena, urn:nbn:de:urmel-c7357c1b-e4f0-4028-ab0d-5b01f569a56d0, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

alt: Page of the Decretum with a wide miniature on red-gold brocade in three episodes: at the left a mitred bishop preaches from a pulpit to a seated crowd; at the centre, before a round chapel with a gold chalice displayed above, a monk in white embraces and absolves a half-naked penitent whose body bears bleeding marks, the short signature NICOLAUS F on the ground below; at the right, inside a church, a priest celebrates mass at an altar while a woman kneels in confession before a seated friar in brown. The text below, in two glossed columns, opens the treatise De penitentia.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, opening of the treatise De penitentia, signed "NICOLAU(S) F(ECIT)", c. 1360. Jena, ThULB, Ms. El. f. 51c, fol. 271r. Photo: Thüringer Universitäts- und Landesbibliothek Jena, urn:nbn:de:urmel-c7357c1b-e4f0-4028-ab0d-5b01f569a56d0, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

alt: Opening page of a large missal with a four-compartment frontispiece in a gold interlace frame: the Annunciation; Christ enthroned in judgment above crowds of the blessed and the rising dead; a dark cave crowded with patriarchs and prophets holding scrolls; and a hell-mouth full of demons and the damned. Below, a red rubric opens the order of the missal according to the Roman curia and a large initial A with figures begins the Advent Introit. At the foot, two golden lions flank a shield azure strewn with gold fleurs-de-lis within a red border; the painted signature DE BONONIA F is legible on the frame beside the shield's point.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, Advent frontispiece with the initial A (Ad te levavi), signed "NICOLAU(S) DE BONONIA F(ECIT)", 1374. Missal of Cardinal Pierre d'Estaing, Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 10072, fol. 8r (pencil foliation). Photo: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek München.

alt: Full page of a missal divided into seven rows of gold-framed narrative compartments, each row keyed to a red marginal petition beginning with P: scenes of the Annunciation and Visitation, the Nativity with the annunciation to the shepherds, the Circumcision and Presentation, the Adoration of the Magi, Christ among the elders, the paralytic of Capernaum lowered on his bed through the opened roof toward Christ, beside the painted signature NICOLAUS DE BONONIA F, and the Baptism of Christ among further episodes, all on gold and blue grounds.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, pictorial litany of the mysteries of Christ, first page, signed "NICOLAU(S) DE BONONIA ·F·", 1374. Missal of Cardinal Pierre d'Estaing, Munich, BSB, Clm 10072, fol. 170v. Photo: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek München.

alt: Full page of a missal divided into seven rows of gold-framed narrative compartments keyed to red marginal petitions: the Transfiguration; the Entry into Jerusalem and the betrayal; the Last Supper and the way of the cross; the Crucifixion and Deposition; the Resurrection with sleeping soldiers and the Marys at the tomb; the Ascension watched by the apostles; Pentecost in an arcaded room; and at the foot the Last Judgment with the dead rising from a stormy sea and the earth, all on gold and blue grounds. The folio number 171 in Roman numerals stands at the top corner.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, pictorial litany of the mysteries of Christ, second page, 1374. Missal of Cardinal Pierre d'Estaing, Munich, BSB, Clm 10072, fol. 171r. Photo: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek München.
