alt: Page of a missal opening the Canon of the Mass. In the historiated initial at the top left, God the Father, red-mantled on a golden throne beneath a canopy, blesses and holds an open book among ranks of angels. The large Gothic text of the Te igitur follows, with small gold crosses painted into the lines at the words hec dona, hec munera; a red rubric marks the Commemoratio pro vivis. In the right column, after the rubric Infra actionem, the Communicantes lists the names of the Virgin, the apostles and the martyr-popes in gold and pink decorated initials. Acanthus with gold besants frames the upper margins; folio number 172 at the top corner.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, opening of the Canon (Te igitur), 1374. Missal of Cardinal Pierre d'Estaing, Munich, BSB, Clm 10072, fol. 172r. Photo: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek München.

alt: Missal page with two text columns. At the head of the right column a red rubric opens Easter Sunday with its station at Saint Mary Major; below it a large initial R on gold holds the risen Christ in a red mantle with a cross-banner, pointing upward over a pink sarcophagus on which a white-clad angel sits, with two haloed Marys at the left, one carrying an ointment jar, and sleeping armoured soldiers below; an inverted bearded mask hides in the pink acanthus under the letter, and a gold panel beside it carries the continuing display letters of the Introit. Lower down, an initial D on blue holds the Magdalene in red raising her hand to the risen Christ. The left column, framed by tall blue filigree panels, carries the priest's communion prayers ending with the Placeat; gold besants and acanthus edge the margins.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, Easter Sunday opening with the initials R (Resurrexi) and D (Deus qui hodierna die), 1374. Missal of Cardinal Pierre d'Estaing, Munich, BSB, Clm 10072, fol. 176v. Photo: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek München.

alt: Opening page of the Clementines. In a large miniature on burnished gold, a pope enthroned beneath a blue star-spangled canopy promulgates the law between cardinals and mitred prelates at his right and lay doctors in blue and pink at his left, several holding scrolls; below the throne a tonsured clerk kneels at a blue star-covered desk over an open book, and a crouching old man supports the whole structure like an atlas. Above the miniature two flying angels flank a domed aedicule with a writing figure. In the lower left, a small gold panel shows a bishop handing a document to a standing cleric, beside a tall monk in blue in the margin. The text of the bull Quoniam nulla, addressed to the doctors and scholars of Bologna, begins beside the miniature within frames of gloss.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, promulgation frontispiece of the Constitutiones Clementinae, 1350s. Madrid, Biblioteca Nacional de España, MSS/1146, fol. 1r. Photo: Biblioteca Nacional de España, Biblioteca Digital Hispánica, CC BY 4.0.

alt: Double opening of the Clementines with text islands framed by gloss on both pages. Red rubrics mark the titles on the offices of vicar, delegated judge, ordinary judge and legate; gold square initials hold small busts of judges and clerics. In the margins, painted figures interact with the initials: a woman in blue reaches toward a bust at the left; a traveller in pink with a hat and a flask at his belt hands a document toward an initial; a veiled woman leans from the gloss on the right page; and a mitred bishop in a long blue mantle strides across the lower margin to point at the bust beside the rubric of the legate. A small crowned stamp of the Biblioteca Nacional sits in the lower margin.
caption: Nicolò di Giacomo da Bologna, opening of Book I with the titles on offices, 1350s. Madrid, Biblioteca Nacional de España, MSS/1146, ff. 14v–15r. Photo: Biblioteca Nacional de España, Biblioteca Digital Hispánica, CC BY 4.0.

alt: Polyptych with the Crucifixion and Saints Nicholas, Bartholomew, Florentius, and Luke
caption: Polyptych with the Crucifixion and Saints Nicholas, Bartholomew, Florentius, and Luke, 1315-20, tempera on panel, 182 x 249 cm, Galleria dell'Accademia, Florence.

alt: Tree of Life
caption: Tree of Life, 1305-10, tempera and gold on panel, 248 × 151 cm, Galleria dell'Accademia, Florence.

alt: The Martyrdom of Saint Lawrence
caption: The Martyrdom of Saint Lawrence (from Laudario della Compagnia di Sant'Agnese), c. 1340, tempera and gold leaf on vellum, 19 × 20.8 cm, The J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles, Ms. 80b, verso, 2006.13.verso.

alt: Christ in Majesty
caption: Christ in Majesty (from Laudario della Compagnia di Sant'Agnese), c. 1340, tempera and gold leaf on vellum, 454 x 335 mm, Morgan Library and Museum, New York, MS M.742.

alt: The Last Supper
caption: The Last Supper (from Vita di Cristo e del Beato Gherardo da Villamagna), c. 1320, tempera and gold leaf on vellum, 245 x 176 mm, Morgan Library and Museum, New York, MS M.643.

alt: Trivulziana Bible
caption: Trivulziana Bible, 1325-30, mineral pigments on parchment, 351 x 251 mm, Biblioteca Trivulziana, Milano, MS 2139.0270r.

alt: Antiphonaries of Santa Maria a Impruneta
caption: Antiphonary, 1325-30, mineral pigments on parchment, 540 x 384 mm, Basilica di Santa Maria, Impruneta, Cod. VII.19r.

alt: Illustrated Copies of the Divina Commedia
caption: Illustrated Copies of the Divina Commedia (Inferno, fol. 1r), 1330-37, mineral pigments on vellum, 340 x 250 mm, Morgan Library and Museum, New York, MS M.289.

alt: Upright panel in its engaged gilded frame. The frame is covered with raised foliate ornament in gold and set with small coloured stones and round glass medallions with tiny painted heads. Against a gold ground tooled with a cusped arch and quatrefoils, the half-length Virgin faces the viewer in a black mantle with a gold-embroidered border and a small gold star on her right shoulder, over a gold dress; a white veil frames her face and falls on her chest, fastened by a round brooch. She holds the Child on her left arm and supports his legs with her right hand. The Child, in a pink mantle with a gold border, feeds at her breast, pressing it with one hand, and turns his eyes towards the viewer, his left foot held in his right hand.
caption: Paolo di Giovanni Fei, Madonna and Child, 1370s. Tempera on wood, gold ground; overall, with engaged frame, 87 × 59.1 cm; painted surface 68.6 × 42.9 cm. New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Bequest of George Blumenthal, 1941, 41.190.13. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, open access, CC0.

alt: Triptych with tall pointed gables and pinnacles. The wide central panel shows the interior of a house seen through three arches divided by thin columns, with rib vaults painted dark blue with gold stars and a gold sun. Saint Anne, haloed and veiled, sits up in a bed with a chequered cover, receiving a cloth from a woman in red; at the left two women bring a bowl and a towel through a curtained doorway. In the foreground a woman in red holds the newborn Virgin on her lap beside a basin and tests the water with her hand, while a kneeling woman and another seen from behind assist. At the right, in an adjoining room, the grey-bearded Joachim sits with a halo, while a bald man and a youth lean towards him; beyond, a window opens onto a garden with roses. In the gables are roundels with Christ blessing and, at the sides, the angel and the Virgin of the Annunciation. The left wing shows Saint James with a staff and book and Saint Catherine of Alexandria with her wheel; the right wing shows a crowned saint in a dark veil, Elizabeth of Hungary, and Saint Bartholomew with a knife and a red book. Several losses in the lower part of the central panel are filled with a neutral tone.
caption: Paolo di Giovanni Fei, Triptych of the Birth of the Virgin with Saints James, Catherine of Alexandria, Elizabeth of Hungary and Bartholomew, 1380s, from San Maurizio, Siena. Tempera and gold on panel, 259 × 204 cm. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 116. Pinacoteca Nazionale, Siena, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Polyptych of five panels under carved gables with cusped arches against gold, framed by narrow lateral pilasters painted with small standing saints and, at their bases, coats of arms. In the larger central panel the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle lined in white over a white brocaded dress, holds the Child, who embraces her and presses his cheek against hers, his hand under her chin; he wears a pink mantle over a gold brocaded tunic. To the left stand Saint John the Baptist, bearded, in a green mantle over a camel-hair garment, pointing and holding a scroll, and Saint Andrew, white-haired, in a pink mantle over blue, with a tall cross and a red book. To the right stand a bearded friar in a grey habit holding a red book, identified as Saint Francis, and a young prophet in pale violet and orange holding a scroll inscribed DANIELLO PROFETA. The saints stand on a ground strewn with flowers. Large areas of paint are lost in the central panel and in the panel of Saint Andrew, exposing the preparation.
caption: Paolo di Giovanni Fei, Madonna and Child with Saints John the Baptist, Andrew, Francis and the Prophet Daniel, early 1390s. Tempera and gold on panel. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale. Photo: Combusken, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Upright panel in its engaged frame of gilded pastiglia foliage set with small stones, with a round arch against gold. At the centre the Virgin, in a dark mantle, sits on a throne before a red cloth of honour patterned in gold, which angels hold up at the top; she nurses the Child, dressed in gold, on her lap. Above, angels with haloes crowd around the cloth with joined or crossed hands. At the left stand Saints Agnes and Catherine of Alexandria and, below them, Saint John the Evangelist, old and bearded, with a book, and Saint Peter with the keys. At the right stand Saint Lucy, holding a dish, and another female saint, and below them Saint Paul with a sword and Saint John the Baptist in a lilac mantle over his camel-hair garment. In the foreground, below the steps of the throne, Eve reclines half-naked, holding a branch and a scroll inscribed EVA, beside a tree around which the serpent is coiled. In roundels in the spandrels are the angel and the Virgin of the Annunciation.
caption: Paolo di Giovanni Fei, Madonna and Child Enthroned with Saint John the Evangelist, Saint Peter, Saint Agnes, Saint Catherine of Alexandria, Saint Lucy, an Unidentified Female Saint, Saint Paul and Saint John the Baptist, with Eve and the Serpent; the Annunciation, 1390s. Tempera on wood, gold ground; overall, with engaged frame, 87 × 59.1 cm; painted surface 70.8 × 43.8 cm. New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Robert Lehman Collection, 1975, 1975.1.23. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, open access, CC0.

alt: Fresco in a round-arched niche, framed by a painted border of small coloured squares and stars imitating inlay; in the intrados above, against a blue ground with stars, is the Holy Face. Within the niche a painted triptych with dark Gothic gables and pinnacles stands against a blue sky. In the central field the Virgin, in a blue mantle over a white dress, holds the Child on her left arm; he wears a green tunic and reaches up to touch her chin, while a small bird flies at the left of her head. At the left Saint Anthony Abbot, white-bearded, in a hooded brown habit, holds a red book and a staff. At the right Saint Christopher, with long fair hair, carries the Child on his shoulder and holds a staff. In the gables above, Christ blesses and holds an open book in the centre, between the angel and the Virgin of the Annunciation. The lower part of the fresco is lost, leaving bare plaster.
caption: Paolo di Giovanni Fei (attributed), Madonna and Child with a Goldfinch between Saints Anthony Abbot and Christopher, late fourteenth century. Fresco. Poggibonsi, basilica of San Lucchese. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Large panel divided into three arched fields by painted white pillars, showing the interior of a Gothic church in pale grey and white with red accents, with a rose window, tall lancet windows and a gilded tabernacle above the altar. At the centre the young Virgin, haloed, in a gold brocaded dress, stands at the top of a flight of white steps between red columns, received by a haloed high priest in gold vestments and a mitre and by an older priest in pink and red. In the left field Saint Anne, veiled, and Joachim, with a grey beard, stand among other figures, and a kneeling woman in green, seen from behind, is half hidden by a pillar. In the right field a group of young women with books lean over a carved balustrade, and below them two bearded men, one in an orange mantle and one in pink over blue, look on. In the foreground two boys in red and in a spotted tunic stand on a patterned floor at the foot of the steps, one pointing upwards.
caption: Paolo di Giovanni Fei, The Presentation of the Virgin in the Temple, 1398–1399, central panel of the altarpiece of the chapel of San Pietro, Siena Cathedral. Tempera on wood transferred to hardboard, painted surface 146.1 × 140.3 cm; overall 147.2 × 140.3 cm. Washington, National Gallery of Art, Samuel H. Kress Collection, 1961.9.4. National Gallery of Art, Washington, open access, CC0.

alt: Upright panel in its gilded engaged frame, with a round arch of raised gilded ornament enclosing the scene against a gold ground. Above, the Virgin, in a white mantle patterned with small gold motifs, sits frontally on a bank of white cloud with her hands joined in prayer. Two angels in white robes with blue lower folds fly beneath the cloud and hold it, and on either side three angels in pink and white play musical instruments, among them a portable organ, a fiddle, a psaltery and lutes, while two more pray at the top. Below, an apostle in blue and pink kneels with his back to the viewer on a dark rocky mount, arms raised towards the Virgin. In the lower part eleven haloed apostles crowd around an open stone sarcophagus filled with red and white flowers, two of them bending into it in the foreground; the ground is dark and scattered with small plants. In the spandrels, roundels show the archangel Gabriel at the left and the Virgin of the Annunciation at the right.
caption: Paolo di Giovanni Fei, The Assumption of the Virgin with Busts of the Archangel Gabriel and the Virgin of the Annunciation, c. 1400–1405. Tempera on panel, painted surface 66.5 × 38.1 cm; overall 79.8 × 51 cm. Washington, National Gallery of Art, Samuel H. Kress Collection, 1961.9.71. National Gallery of Art, Washington, open access, CC0.

alt: Upright painted panel in three zones. Above, the interior of an office with pink walls, a barred window at the right and a row of small white labelled boxes on a shelf; at the top centre is the black and white shield of Siena. Behind a long counter stand two officials in red caps: at the left the scrivener in blue, holding up a slip of paper, at the right the camarlingo in red, with his hand in a bowl of coins; on the counter are inkwells, pens and papers. In front of the counter three taxpayers in short tunics of blue, pink and white approach, one holding a coin. Strongboxes stand on the bench at the left, on the bench at the right and on the floor, beside a small open door. In the middle zone six coats of arms are painted on a gold band. Below, a long inscription in black Gothic capitals on a white ground fills the lower half, damaged at the left. The panel is framed by a border of small roundels.
caption: Workshop of Paolo di Giovanni Fei, Biccherna cover with the Camarlingo Niccolò di Leonardo della Gazaia, his Scrivener and Three Taxpayers, 1402. Tempera on panel, with tooled gilding and silver, 44 × 32.4 cm. London, Victoria and Albert Museum, 414-1892. © Victoria and Albert Museum, London; image for non-commercial educational use only.

alt: Two small upright panels side by side, each in a gilded tabernacle frame with a steep gable decorated with crockets and topped by a pine-cone finial. In the gables are roundels with the angel of the Annunciation at the left and the Virgin Annunciate at the right. In the left panel the Virgin, in a dark mantle, sits on a throne covered with a red patterned cloth, holding the Child in pink, who holds an inscribed scroll; two angels stand behind the throne, Saint John the Baptist with a cross-staff stands at the left and Saint James the Great with a pilgrim's staff and a red book at the right, on a green floor. In the right panel Christ hangs on the cross under a red inscription, the Virgin in a dark mantle stands at the left, Saint Mary Magdalen in red kneels and embraces the foot of the cross, and Saint John the Evangelist in pink and dark blue stands at the right with his hands joined. Small old metal labels are fixed to the lower edges of the frames.
caption: Workshop of Paolo di Giovanni Fei, Madonna and Child Enthroned with Two Angels and Saints John the Baptist and James the Great, and the Annunciatory Angel (left wing); Crucifixion with the Virgin, Saint Mary Magdalen and Saint John the Evangelist, and the Virgin Annunciate (right wing), c. 1400–1410. Tempera on wood, gold ground; each wing 45.4–45.7 × 19.7 cm with engaged frame. New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Robert Lehman Collection, 1975, 1975.1.22. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, open access, CC0.

alt: Tall rectangular panel in a painted frame of small blocks in red, blue and gold. The Virgin, seated and filling almost the whole field, wears a dark blue mantle scattered with gold rosettes over a red gown; her head, inclined slightly to her right, is framed by a large tooled gold halo. Against her breast she holds an oval blue medallion edged in gold and streaked with gold rays, within which the Christ Child in a golden robe raises his right hand in blessing. Behind her two angels in green and blue, flying in from the upper corners, spread a red cloth of honour patterned with dark flowers. At the lower left, very small in scale, a woman in red with a white veil and a man in a dark robe kneel with joined hands under the edge of the Virgin's mantle, which she lifts over them with her right hand.
caption: Paolo Veneziano, Madonna and Child Enthroned with Two Donors, c. 1320–1330. Tempera and gold on panel, 142 × 90 cm. Venice, Gallerie dell'Accademia, cat. 786; acquired from the dealer Antonio Salvadori, 1913. Photo: Didier Descouens, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Three panels. In the wide central panel the Virgin lies on a bier covered with a red and gold cloth, wrapped in a dark blue mantle, surrounded by the apostles, among them Peter at her head and Paul at her feet, and by rows of angels with gold haloes. Behind the bier Christ stands in a pointed mandorla of light, holding the small swaddled soul of the Virgin in his arms; two red seraphim spread their wings above the mandorla. At the top, in a blue roundel with angels, Christ receives the Virgin. Along the bottom runs an inscription in white letters. In the narrow lateral panels Saint Francis, in a brown habit, shows an open book, and Saint Anthony of Padua, also in a brown habit, holds a red book; both are named in red letters above their heads.
caption: Paolo Veneziano, The Dormition of the Virgin with Saint Francis and Saint Anthony of Padua, signed and dated 1333, surviving panels of the polyptych from San Lorenzo, Vicenza. Tempera and gold on panel. Vicenza, Musei Civici, Pinacoteca di Palazzo Chiericati. Image for educational use only.

alt: Small horizontal panel of the Annunciation on a worn gold ground. At the left the archangel Gabriel, with large wings of brown, gold and green feathers, kneels on a strip of rocky ground in a green tunic and a red mantle, raising his right hand in salutation; beside him a faint inscription begins AVE MARIA. At the right the Virgin, in a dark mantle, sits within a small building with red-capitalled columns and a gabled roof, raising one hand. From the upper edge a ray descends towards her, carrying the dove of the Holy Spirit. Between the two figures stands a low pedestal decorated with painted scrolls.
caption: Attributed to Paolo Veneziano, The Annunciation, c. 1330. Tempera and gold on panel. Venice, church of San Pantalon, Chapel of the Sacred Nail. Image: Chiesa di San Pantalon, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small horizontal panel of the Nativity. A mountain of pale, sharply faceted rocks opens at the centre into a dark cave, where the Christ Child, swaddled and haloed, lies in a manger shaped like a stone chest decorated with arches; the ox and the ass bend their heads over him. The Virgin, in a dark mantle, kneels at the right with her hands extended towards the Child. At the left Saint Joseph, named by an inscription, sits with his hands raised, and behind him a shepherd looks up towards an angel. Angels with long dark wings appear above the rocks on both sides, and a star with radiating points shines above the cave.
caption: Attributed to Paolo Veneziano, The Nativity, c. 1330. Tempera and gold on panel. Venice, church of San Pantalon, Chapel of the Sacred Nail. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small horizontal panel of the Presentation in the Temple. At the centre an altar covered with a red cloth embroidered with a gold cross stands under a ciborium with a starry blue vault. At the left Saint Joseph, in a blue tunic and red mantle, holds two doves, and the Virgin, in a dark mantle, stretches out her hands. At the right the aged Simeon, with long grey hair and beard, holds the Child, who reaches back towards his mother. At the far right the prophetess Anna, in a red mantle over a green dress, raises one hand and holds an unfurled scroll.
caption: Attributed to Paolo Veneziano, The Presentation in the Temple, c. 1330. Tempera and gold on panel. Venice, church of San Pantalon, Chapel of the Sacred Nail. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small horizontal panel of the Dormition of the Virgin. The Virgin lies on a long bier covered with a red cloth patterned in gold, wrapped in a dark mantle. Behind her Christ stands in a pointed mandorla of blue-green light, holding her soul as a small swaddled child. Apostles with gold haloes crowd on either side: at the left an apostle in a dark green mantle bends over the foot of the bier, at the right Peter, in a yellow mantle, holds a censer. Angels fill the upper part of the panel, one of them holding a globe, and a white architectural form closes the scene at the upper right.
caption: Attributed to Paolo Veneziano, The Dormition of the Virgin, c. 1330. Tempera and gold on panel. Venice, church of San Pantalon, Chapel of the Sacred Nail. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Large polyptych in an elaborately carved and gilded frame with pinnacles, crockets and a central lunette filled with a carved shell. At the centre, under an arch, Christ crowns the Virgin, both seated on a broad throne in mantles of gold-patterned silk against a starry blue sky, surrounded by a choir of angels with gold haloes playing instruments. At each side, in two rows of two arched compartments, eight scenes from the life of Christ on gold grounds: at the left the Nativity and Adoration of the Magi, the Baptism, the Last Supper, and the Agony in the Garden with the Arrest; at the right the Way to Calvary, the Crucifixion, the Resurrection with the Noli me tangere, and the Ascension. Along the top, under gables, smaller scenes alternate with standing saints, and two tall pinnacles beside the shell hold prophets.
caption: Paolo Veneziano, Polyptych of the Coronation of the Virgin, from the convent of Santa Chiara, Venice, c. 1335–1340. Tempera and gold on panel, 168 × 279 cm overall. Venice, Gallerie dell'Accademia, cat. 21. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Panel in a carved gilded frame with a pointed arch, cusped and scalloped, carried on twisted colonnettes, with rosettes in the spandrels. Against a gold ground, the Virgin is shown at half length in a deep blue mantle with a gold-embroidered border and a star on the shoulder, over a white veil and an orange-red dress. She inclines her head to the right and holds the Child with both hands. The Child, almost naked except for a white loincloth and a pale cloth beneath him, stretches his right arm round her neck and holds a small object in his left hand, looking out at the viewer. Both haloes are decorated with punched rosettes.
caption: Paolo Veneziano, Virgin and Child, c. 1340. Tempera and gold on poplar panel, 44 × 40 cm. Paris, Musée du Louvre, INV 20194 (Campana 315), on deposit at the Musée du Petit Palais, Avignon (D. 228). © Musée du Louvre, image for non-commercial educational use.

alt: Small horizontal panel with a round-arched top on a gold ground. At the centre Christ hangs dead on a tall wooden cross under a tablet inscribed I.N.R.I.; blood flows from his hands and side. Four angels in dark blue with dark wings fly around the cross, two catching the blood from his hands in cups and one from his side, while the fourth covers his face in grief. Behind the figures runs a low green crenellated wall, the wall of Jerusalem. At the left the fainting Virgin, in a dark blue mantle, is supported by holy women in yellow and black. At the foot of the cross the Magdalen, in a pale mantle, kneels and embraces the cross; beneath it, in a cleft of red rock, lies the skull of Adam. At the right Saint John, in a red mantle over blue, gazes up with clasped hands, and beside him soldiers in blue armour and helmets, one in a red cloak pointing to the cross.
caption: Paolo Veneziano, The Crucifixion, c. 1340–1345, probably the upper centre of a portable triptych; the upper corners are later additions. Tempera on panel, painted surface 31 × 38 cm; overall 33.85 × 41.1 cm. Washington, National Gallery of Art, Samuel H. Kress Collection, 1939.1.143. National Gallery of Art, Washington, open access, CC0.

alt: Two small panels shaped as half-gables, joined by two small iron hinges, in their original gilded frames. In the left panel the angel Gabriel, in a pink robe with blue and gold wings and a blue ribbon in his curly hair, kneels in profile on a rocky ground and holds a slender staff; beside him red letters read AVE GRATIA PLENA DOMINUS TECUM. In the right panel the Virgin, in a blue dress patterned with gold scrolls and a white veil, sits on a yellow throne with a red cushion before a gold-patterned cloth of honour; she raises her right hand and holds a book in her left, while a small white dove descends towards her. At the left of her panel a white stone parapet with a plant growing from it stands on the ground.
caption: Paolo Veneziano, The Annunciation, c. 1348–1350, gables of the wings of a portable triptych. Tempera and gold leaf on panel, 16.7 × 20.3 cm (both panels). Los Angeles, J. Paul Getty Museum, 87.PB.117. J. Paul Getty Museum, Open Content Program, public domain.

alt: Two long horizontal panels, one above the other, each divided into seven compartments with gold grounds. In the upper row, half-length figures: from left to right Saint George with a lance and shield, Saint Mark with a book, the mourning Virgin in dark blue, the dead Christ standing upright before the cross with crossed hands, Saint John the Evangelist in blue and red, Saint Peter with the keys, and Saint Nicholas in a bishop's vestments with crosses. In the lower row, seven narrative scenes set in architecture and landscape: a consecration of a bishop, Saint Mark with a cobbler before a city with a tall tower, a prison with two haloed figures at a window and soldiers below, a scene of violence under a canopy, a ship with a large patterned sail in a storm beside red rocks, a crowd with clergy and a doge inside a church, and a scene with soldiers and a man on the ground before a building.
caption: Paolo Veneziano with his sons Luca and Giovanni, Pala Feriale, signed and dated 22 April 1345, the weekday cover of the Pala d'Oro of San Marco. Tempera and gold on panel, two panels, each c. 59 × 325 cm. Venice, Museo di San Marco. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Upright panel with a round top. The crowned Virgin sits on a tall wooden throne with Gothic pinnacles and a cushioned seat, in a dark blue mantle patterned with gold stars over an orange dress. She holds out in her right hand a pear to the Child, who stands on her lap in a transparent shirt and a green cloak, reaching for the fruit. Eight small angels in blue and red with coloured wings stand behind and above the throne. On the base of the throne an inscription in white capitals gives the signature and date. The panel shows losses at the edges.
caption: Paolo Veneziano, Madonna and Child with Eight Angels (Madonna della Pera), signed and dated 1347, from Santa Maria at Carpineta. Tempera on panel transferred to canvas, 122.5 × 74 cm. Cesena, Museo Diocesano e della Cattedrale. Image for educational use only.

alt: A large painted cross hangs within the pointed stone arch of a church apse, set in a later surround of gilded openwork foliage that spreads around the arms and shaft. Christ hangs with his head inclined to his right and his body curving gently to the side, arms stretched almost horizontally, wearing a thin loincloth. Above his head a small darkened panel shows a haloed figure, and two carved gilded angels in flight flank the upper arm. The four terminals hold quatrefoil medallions with the symbols of the Evangelists: the eagle at the top, the winged lion at the left, the angel with a book at the right, the winged ox at the foot. Below, at either side, two separate narrow panels in gilded pinnacled frames show the mourning Virgin in a blue mantle, one hand raised to her face, at the left and Saint John the Evangelist in a pink mantle over blue at the right, both standing on gold grounds.
caption: Paolo Veneziano, Crucifix with the mourning Virgin and Saint John the Evangelist, c. 1350. Tempera and gold on panel. Dubrovnik, Dominican church (Sveti Dominik), triumphal arch. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Four tall narrow panels shown side by side against a black background, each with a standing saint on a gold ground and a plain upper section where the original arched tops have been lost. At the far left Saint John the Baptist, with long dark hair and beard, wears a camel-hair garment under a brownish mantle fastened with a blue jewel; he points with his right hand and holds an unfurled scroll inscribed ECCE AGNUS DEI. In the two central panels two bishop saints in mitres raise their right hands in blessing and hold croziers in their left: the first wears a green chasuble with a red orphrey, the second a red chasuble patterned with gold motifs and a dark blue orphrey decorated with interlace, both over blue and white vestments. At the far right Saint Paul, bearded and balding, wears a red mantle over a blue tunic and holds a sword and a closed book with clasps. All four stand on a strip of green ground.
caption: Paolo Veneziano, Saint John the Baptist, two Bishop Saints and Saint Paul, from a dismembered polyptych, c. 1350–1355. Tempera and gold on panel, each c. 75 × 23.5 cm. Brescia, Pinacoteca Tosio Martinengo, invv. 112, 1974–1976; on deposit from the Congregazione di Carità since 1866. Photo: Mattes, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Half-length Virgin and Child on a gold ground under a rounded arch, photographed before cleaning with the bare edges of the panel visible. The Virgin, in a dark blue mantle scattered with small gold stars and a veil edged in gold, inclines her head and looks out at the viewer; in her right hand she holds a red poppy by its stem. The Child, seated on her left arm, wears a short red tunic with an embroidered gold panel on the chest and white undersleeves, looks up at his mother and reaches for the flower. In the spandrels above the arch carved and gilded acanthus leaves on a red ground frame two roundels, each with a small half-length figure on gold.
caption: Paolo Veneziano, Madonna and Child (Madonna of the Poppy), c. 1350. Tempera and gold on panel, 98 × 74 cm. Venice, church of San Pantalon, Chapel of the Sacred Nail. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Tall panel with a rounded top edged by a dark band of night sky with small stars. On a gold ground Christ hangs dead on a tall dark cross beneath a white tablet inscribed I.N.R.I., his head fallen on his shoulder and blood flowing from his hands and side. Small angels in white and pale green fly around the cross in attitudes of grief, two of them catching his blood in chalices. Behind the cross runs the crenellated dark red wall of Jerusalem, decorated with gold scrolls. On both sides mounted soldiers with spears and helmets crowd the scene; at the right a haloed horseman points upwards towards Christ, and a red banner rises above the soldiers. At the lower left the Virgin, in a dark mantle, faints into the arms of the holy women and Saint John, while Mary Magdalene, with long loose hair, kneels and embraces the foot of the cross. At the lower right a dense crowd of figures includes a soldier with a round shield marked with a star, a group dividing Christ's garment, and two old men talking together. At the foot of the cross blood runs into a cleft in the rock.
caption: Paolo Veneziano (attributed) or workshop, The Crucifixion, mid-fourteenth century. Tempera and gold on panel, 109 × 60.5 cm. Athens, Byzantine and Christian Museum, BXM 01097. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Polyptych of three panels in carved gilded frames with round arches, twisted colonnettes and a foliate base. In the taller central panel the crowned Virgin sits on a pink and white architectural throne with green cushions, before a red cloth of honour, in a dark blue mantle patterned with gold over a red dress; the Child, in a white shirt and an olive-green cloak, sits on her knee and reaches towards her hand. Each lateral panel contains two standing saints under arches: at the left Saint Francis in a brown habit with a book and a cross, and Saint John the Baptist in a green mantle with a scroll; at the right Saint John the Evangelist in blue and red with an open book, and Saint Anthony of Padua in a brown habit with a red book. Their names are inscribed in red beside their heads.
caption: Paolo Veneziano and workshop, Polyptych of the Virgin and Child Enthroned with Saints Francis, John the Baptist, John the Evangelist and Anthony of Padua, dated 1354. Tempera and gold on poplar; central panel 100 × 60.5 cm, lateral panels c. 83.4 × 52.5 cm. Paris, Musée du Louvre, MI 396, MI 396 bis and MI 396 ter (Campana 314). © Musée du Louvre, image for non-commercial educational use.

alt: Central panel of a polyptych in a carved gilded frame with a round arch and twisted colonnettes. The crowned Virgin sits on a pink and white marble throne with two green cushions, before a cloth of honour of red and gold brocade patterned with small dark crosses. She wears a white veil, a round gold brooch and a dark blue mantle densely patterned with gold palmettes, over a red dress patterned in gold, and holds out her right hand. The Child, in a white shirt and an olive-green cloak, sits on her left knee, reaches out to her hand and looks down. On the base of the throne an inscription in small capitals gives the date.
caption: Paolo Veneziano and workshop, Virgin and Child Enthroned, central panel of the polyptych dated 1354. Tempera and gold on poplar, 100 × 60.5 cm. Paris, Musée du Louvre, MI 396. © Musée du Louvre, image for non-commercial educational use.

alt: Lateral panel of a polyptych with two arches in a carved gilded frame and twisted colonnettes. At the left Saint Francis, in a brown habit with a cord, stands frontally, holding a red book with clasps and a small gold cross; his name is inscribed in red beside his head. At the right Saint John the Baptist, gaunt, with long hair and beard, wears a green mantle over a dark camel-hair garment, points with his right hand and holds an unrolled scroll inscribed ECCE AGNUS DEI ECCE QUI TOLLIS PECCATA; his name is inscribed beside his head. Both stand barefoot on a dark ground.
caption: Paolo Veneziano and workshop, Saints Francis and John the Baptist, left lateral panel of the polyptych dated 1354. Tempera and gold on poplar. Paris, Musée du Louvre, MI 396 bis. © Musée du Louvre, image for non-commercial educational use.

alt: Lateral panel of a polyptych with two arches in a carved gilded frame and twisted colonnettes. At the left Saint John the Evangelist, old, bald and with a curly white beard, wears a blue tunic and a large red mantle lined in green; he bends his head over an open book inscribed IN PRINCIPIO, which he holds in both hands. At the right Saint Anthony of Padua, young and tonsured, in a brown Franciscan habit, stands frontally holding a red book with clasps. Their names are inscribed in red beside their heads. Both stand barefoot on a dark ground against gold.
caption: Paolo Veneziano and workshop, Saints John the Evangelist and Anthony of Padua, right lateral panel of the polyptych dated 1354. Tempera and gold on poplar, 83.4 × 52.5 cm. Paris, Musée du Louvre, MI 396 ter. © Musée du Louvre, image for non-commercial educational use.

alt: Upright panel in a gilded frame with a trilobed pointed arch, a band of blind tracery above and a small plaque at the base naming P. and G. Veneziano. Within the arch, on a gold ground, Christ and the Virgin sit side by side on a large pink and red architectural throne with two pointed gables, each with a blue roundel. Christ, at the right, in a gold tunic and a deep blue mantle, holds a slender cross-staff and stretches his right arm to place a crown on the Virgin's head. The Virgin, at the left, in a deep blue mantle over a gold dress, bows her head and crosses her hands on her breast. Between them hangs a gold cloth of honour patterned with small motifs. Above and around the throne angels with red and gold wings play instruments, among them fiddles, lutes, psalteries, trumpets, a tambourine and two portative organs at the sides. At their feet are a dark disc with a face, the sun, and a pale face, the moon. Along the base of the throne run inscriptions in gold letters on red and green.
caption: Paolo Veneziano and his son Giovanni (Giovannino), The Coronation of the Virgin, signed and dated 1358. Tempera on panel, 109.9 × 68.6 cm. New York, The Frick Collection, purchased 1930, 1930.1.124. Image: The Frick Collection, New York, for educational use only.

alt: The two wings of a dismembered polyptych, reassembled side by side against a red wall, with the place of the lost central panel closed up. The lower register is a continuous row of eight arched compartments with twisted colonnettes, each with a standing saint on a gold ground: Catherine of Alexandria, crowned, with her wheel; the archangel Michael in armour, holding a globe and spearing a dragon; John the Baptist in a green mantle with a scroll; Peter in a yellow mantle with the keys and a scroll; Paul with sword and book; a young apostle in a pink mantle with a scroll; Dominic in the black and white habit with a lily and a red book; and Ursula, crowned, in a yellow ermine-lined mantle, with two companions. Above runs a band of shell-shaped lunettes, and over the outer compartments rise two groups of three gabled pinnacles with half-length saints: a bishop in a blue starred chasuble, a young saint with a red banner and the model of a walled town, Peter Martyr with a palm, Thomas Aquinas with an open book and a church, and two apostles with scrolls.
caption: Paolo and Giovannino Veneziano, lateral panels of the polyptych from Santa Maria del Mercato, c. 1358. Tempera and gold on panel. San Severino Marche, Pinacoteca civica "Pietro Tacchi Venturi". Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco of the Crucifixion filling a pointed lunette beneath a ribbed vault. Christ hangs on a tall cross inscribed INRI, flanked by six grieving angels whose bodies trail into clouds. On the left, the holy women support the fainting Virgin beside a small barred window cut into the wall; soldiers with spears, a sponge on a reed and a red banner crowd behind a rider on a brown horse. Mary Magdalene in green embraces the foot of the cross, beside a small kneeling donor in black. On the right, a rider on a white horse and helmeted soldiers look up at Christ, one raising his hand, while Saint John sits mourning in the lower corner. Ornamental bands and Evangelist symbols decorate the vault above
caption: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco (late Maestro di Cesi?), Crucifixion, 1333. Fresco, altar wall of the Cappella di Santa Croce, Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco (Perugia). Commissioned by Jean d'Amiel, papal rector of the Duchy of Spoleto. Photo: Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco, for educational use only.

alt: View up into a ribbed cross vault painted in fresco. Four triangular compartments with deep blue grounds each hold a winged, haloed Evangelist with a human body and a book, turned towards the central boss: at the top, upside down, a figure with a human face; at the left, a figure with the head of an eagle; at the right, a figure with the head of an ox; at the bottom, a figure with the head of a lion. The ribs carry narrow bands of geometric inlay, and broad borders of scrolling foliage and rosettes on a dark ground frame each compartment. At the upper edge, upside down, part of the lunette of a side wall with Christ in a mandorla; at the lower edge, the lunette of the opposite wall with Christ blessing between two angels and the gable of a painted tabernacle
caption: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco (late Maestro di Cesi?), Vault with the Four Evangelists, 1333. Fresco, vault of the Cappella di Santa Croce, Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco (Perugia). Commissioned by Jean d'Amiel, papal rector of the Duchy of Spoleto. Photo: Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco, for educational use only.

alt: Fresco within a pointed gable framed by bands of foliage and geometric inlay. The Virgin, in a white veil and a dark mantle over a red dress, sits enthroned before a cloth of honour patterned with a small red and white chequer; the Christ Child, in a pale tunic and barefoot, stands on her lap, embracing her neck and pressing his cheek to hers. At either side stands a haloed, winged angel in a red-brown mantle, hands held to the chest; faint inscriptions beneath them read GABRIEL and RAPHAEL
caption: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco (late Maestro di Cesi?), Maestà between the Archangels Gabriel and Raphael, 1333. Fresco, upper part of the painted tabernacle, side wall of the Cappella di Santa Croce, Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco (Perugia). Commissioned by Jean d'Amiel, papal rector of the Duchy of Spoleto. Photo: Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco, for educational use only.

alt: Frescoed side wall of a chapel. At the top, in a lunette, Christ blesses between two angels. Below, a painted Gothic tabernacle with a pointed gable frames the Virgin and Child enthroned between two archangels, and underneath, Christ carrying a large cross before a nun, with a second haloed nun holding a palm at right. To the upper left a tall woman in a grey mantle walks with a small girl praying behind her; to the upper right the Virgin before a patterned cloth lowers the Christ Child towards a little nun. Lower left, a bishop in a cave holding a cross, with a verse inscription; lower right, a bishop's head at a barred window and other small scenes
caption: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco (late Maestro di Cesi?), the wall of the tomb, with Christ blessing, scenes of the childhood of Chiara, the painted tabernacle with the Maestà and Christ planting the Cross in Chiara's heart, and scenes of Saint Blaise, 1333. Fresco, Cappella di Santa Croce, Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco (Perugia). Photo: Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco, for educational use only.

alt: Fresco of a tall standing Virgin in a white veil and grey-green mantle over a red dress, her head bowed towards the right. She draws her mantle open, and from beneath it the barefoot Christ Child, in a green tunic and cruciform halo, steps forward and reaches out his hand. On the right a smaller haloed nun in a brown habit and white veil kneels and raises both hands towards him. Behind the Virgin hangs a cloth patterned with white and red rosettes; to the right is a dark blue ground scattered with stars. An inscription at lower right reads SCA CLARA, and a border of red and white triangles runs along the arch at the edge
caption: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco (late Maestro di Cesi?), The Virgin Brings the Christ Child to the Blessed Chiara (traditionally La Madonna fa giocare Santa Chiara con Gesù Bambino), 1333. Fresco, upper register of the side wall beside the painted tabernacle of the Cappella di Santa Croce, Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco (Perugia). alt: Fresco on a dark blue-black ground. At the centre, Christ, haloed, with long fair hair and beard and a sorrowful face, wears a long reddish-brown garment and steps forward with bent knee, carrying a large red cross on his shoulder and holding its shaft, whose end reaches a haloed nun in a white veil at the left, who grasps it with both hands. At the right stands a second haloed nun in a brown habit and white veil, holding a palm branch. Christ stands on an ochre mound; the surface is worn, with losses and whitish efflorescence

Commissioned by Jean d'Amiel, papal rector of the Duchy of Spoleto. Photo: Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco, for educational use only.

alt: Fresco of a haloed nun in a black habit and white veil sitting upright on a bed, hands folded on her lap, eyes raised to heaven. Behind her a wall of square panels alternates dark red and ochre beneath a painted cornice with Gothic leaf ornament. Crowds of grieving nuns in white veils fill both sides, hands clasped. Two tonsured friars stand beside her: one raises his hand and holds a red book; the other rests his cheek on his hand and holds a small round flask. In the foreground a nun kneels at the bed looking up at her, and another, seen from behind in a dark mantle, kneels at the right. The bed is covered with an ochre cloth patterned in red
caption: Second hand of the chapel (Maestro di Sant'Alò?), Death of the Blessed Chiara, 1333. Not by the Primo Maestro: shown for comparison. Fresco, side wall of the Cappella di Santa Croce, Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco (Perugia). Commissioned by Jean d'Amiel, papal rector of the Duchy of Spoleto. Photo: Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco, for educational use only.
entry: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco

alt: Frescoed side wall of a chapel. In the lunette, Christ in a mandorla among angels; at left a bishop in a red cope presents a kneeling tonsured cleric with a bundle above him, at right a crowned female saint presents the same cleric holding a red shield with a white cross, with a small building above. A painted inscription runs below. In the lower register, at left, a nun sits up in bed among nuns and friars; in the centre, under a deep window, Christ as the Man of Sorrows; at right an angel descends as an executioner raises his sword over a crowned saint among a crowd before a city
caption: Second painter of the Cappella di Santa Croce, the wall of the patron, with Christ in a mandorla and Jean d'Amiel presented by Saints Blaise and Catherine, the Death of the Blessed Chiara, the Man of Sorrows and the Martyrdom of Saint Catherine, 1333. Not by the Primo Maestro: shown for comparison. Fresco, Cappella di Santa Croce, Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco (Perugia). Photo: Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco, for educational use only.

caption: St Stanislaus Raises a Dead Man, 1330-40, fresco, Lower Basilica of San Francesco, Assisi.

alt: Martyrdom of St Stanislas
caption: Martyrdom of St Stanislas, 1337-47, fresco, Lower Basilica of San Francesco, Assisi.

alt: Crucifixion
caption: Crucifixion, c. 1340, fresco, Sala Capitolare (former Chapter Room, now Cappella delle Reliquie), Sacro Convento, Assisi.

alt: The Crucifixion
caption: The Crucifixion, c. 1330, tempera and gold leaf on panel, 17.8 x 14.0 cm, North Carolina Museum of Art, Raleigh.

alt: Madonna and Child enthroned among angels with Annunciation and Saints Catherine of Alexandria, Agnes, Lucia, Mary Magdalene, Elizabeth of Hungary, Clare, Agate
caption: Madonna and Child with the Crucifixion, Angels and Saints (votive tablet - attr.), 1335–45, tempera on parchment, 33.5 × 48.5 x 2 cm, Galleria Nazionale dell'Umbria, Perugia.

alt: Madonna and Child Enthroned with Angels, the Annunciation and Saints
caption: Madonna and Child Enthroned with Angels, the Annunciation and Saints, c. 1330, tempera and gold on board, golden frame, 36.5 x 24 cm, Pinacoteca Vaticana, Vatican City.

alt: Annunciation
caption: Annunciation, 1330-40, fresco, Monastero di San Giuseppe (ex chiesa di Sant'Apollinare), Assisi.

alt: Gold-ground panel with a pointed arch, its cusped border modelled in relief and its sides framed by twisted colonnettes. At the centre, on a white Gothic throne with pinnacles and a red cloth of honour patterned in gold, Christ, seated at the right in a pink tunic and a blue mantle strewn with gold stars, places a crown on the head of the Virgin, who sits at the left in a matching blue mantle over a pink dress, her head bowed and her hands crossed on her breast. Angels stand behind the throne. At either side rise tiers of haloed saints: at the left the Baptist, apostles, a bishop and a nun; at the right Peter with keys, a bishop with a mitre, a Franciscan, a Dominican, a crowned female saint and a monk. In the lower part, on a gold ground, groups of angels in coloured robes play musical instruments, among them a long trumpet, and a group of angels in white robes dance in a circle at the centre.
caption: Puccio di Simone, Coronation of the Virgin with Saints and Angels, c. 1340–1345 (according to the museum). Tempera on panel, 68.9 × 38 cm. Altenburg, Lindenau-Museum, inv. 16. Lindenau-Museum, Altenburg, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons (background modified).

alt: Gold-ground panel with a round-headed arch whose cusped border, gilded and modelled in relief, is studded with small bosses; twisted colonnettes frame the sides. At the top, against the gold, Christ, seated at the right in a blue mantle over a gold-patterned tunic, places a crown on the head of the Virgin, who sits at the left in a pale cream mantle, her head bowed and her hands crossed on her breast; angels with red and blue wings fly at either side under the arch. Below them a red cloth patterned in gold spreads behind tiers of haloed saints, among them a bishop, the Baptist, Saint Anthony Abbot in a dark habit, an apostle with a book and a scroll, and several female saints with books and palms. At the centre two angels raise long trumpets hung with red and white banners, crossing them, and at the bottom, on a blue ground, two kneeling angels in blue and yellow robes play a fiddle and a small portable organ.
caption: Puccio di Simone, Coronation of the Virgin with Saints and Angels, 1340s. Tempera and gold on panel. Avignon, Musée du Petit Palais. Photo: Musée du Petit Palais, Avignon, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Five separate gold-ground panels without their frames, the central one taller. In the centre, under a carved trilobed arch, Christ hangs on the cross with the titulus above, four small angels in blue flying around him; below, the Virgin in a dark mantle stands with bowed head at the left, Mary Magdalene in red kneels embracing the foot of the cross, and Saint John in a pale mantle looks up at the right. In the lateral panels stand four saints: at the far left Mary Magdalene, covered only by her long golden hair, holding a scroll with an inscription; then the Archangel Michael in armour with blue and red wings, holding a sword and a red shield with a white field and a red cross, standing on a green dragon; at the right a bearded saint in a red tunic and a white fur-lined mantle holding a long sword, identified as Saint Julian; at the far right Saint Martha in a blue and white mantle, holding a thin staff, with a dragon at her feet.
caption: Bernardo Daddi and Puccio di Simone, Crucifixion with the Virgin, Mary Magdalene and Saint John, and Saints Mary Magdalene, Michael, Julian and Martha, c. 1345–1348. Tempera and gold on panel, lateral panels c. 81 × 33 cm. Florence, Galleria dell'Accademia, inv. 1890 no. 6140. Galleria dell'Accademia, Florence, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Tall gabled panel under a cusped arch with gilded lobes; the gable is decorated with gold foliage on a dark blue ground. Against a red ground patterned with fine gold ornament, Christ, seated at the right in a pink tunic and a blue mantle covered with gold foliate patterns and lined in white, places a tall jewelled crown on the head of the Virgin, who sits at the left in a similar blue and gold mantle over a red dress, her head bowed and her hands crossed on her breast. Below them kneel six small angels with multicoloured wings, three at each side, some holding musical instruments, among them a portable organ and a stringed instrument. Along the base runs the inscription of the Ave Maria.
caption: Puccio di Simone, Coronation of the Virgin, central panel of the polyptych for the Dominicans of Perugia, c. 1345–1350. Tempera and gold on poplar panel, 159.6 × 69 cm. Ghent, Museum voor Schone Kunsten, 1903-A. Photo: Museum voor Schone Kunsten Gent, public domain (background modified).

alt: Two tall panels with pointed arches and cusped borders, each with a single standing saint on a gold ground with a punched border. At the left Saint Catherine, crowned and with long fair hair, in a red dress and a blue mantle with a gold border, holds a palm and a small book, with the halves of a wheel visible at her sides. At the right Saint Lawrence, young and tonsured, in a red dalmatic with gold bands patterned with blue quatrefoils and a jewelled collar, holds a blue book and rests his hand on a black gridiron; a blue maniple hangs from his left arm. Both stand on a red carpet patterned with flowers, and their haloes are richly punched.
caption: Puccio di Simone, Saint Catherine of Alexandria and Saint Lawrence, lateral panels of the polyptych for the Dominicans of Perugia, c. 1345. Tempera and gold on poplar panel; Saint Lawrence 121.7 × 39.5 cm (with frame). Berlin, Staatliche Museen, Gemäldegalerie, acquired in 1821 with the Solly collection. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (background modified).

alt: Small horizontal panel. In a rocky landscape of pale, faceted rocks against a gold ground, a wooden shed with a sloping roof shelters a rectangular manger lined with a white cloth, in which the Christ Child lies wrapped in red and white swaddling bands; behind the manger an ox and an ass lean their heads towards him. At the left the Virgin, wrapped from head to foot in a pale cream mantle, kneels and reaches into the manger to touch the Child. At the right Joseph, an old bearded man in a yellow-orange mantle, sits on the ground with his head resting on his hand, turned towards the scene. Dark trees grow on the rocks at the upper right, and small plants with red flowers dot the ground.
caption: Puccio di Simone, The Nativity, predella panel of the polyptych for the Dominicans of Perugia, c. 1345–1350. Tempera on wood, gold ground, 20 × 38.1 cm. New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Robert Lehman Collection, 1975, 1975.1.105. Photo: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, Open Access, public domain.

alt: Small horizontal panel. Against a gold ground, in front of a plain wooden cross whose arm shows a knot and traces of blood, the dead Christ lies on a white shroud in a rocky hollow, his body marked with wounds. The Virgin, in a black mantle decorated with gold stars, bends over his head. Around the body are four women: one in red with joined hands, one in dark red raising her arms in grief, one seen from behind in a green mantle, and one in a light blue mantle wrapped around her, seated on the ground at the right. At the left Joseph of Arimathea, an old bearded man in a red and orange mantle, and the young Saint John, in a blue tunic and a pale mantle, approach the group with outstretched hands. Pale rocks close the scene at both sides, with small plants on the ground.
caption: Puccio di Simone, The Lamentation, predella panel of the polyptych for the Dominicans of Perugia, c. 1345 (the museum's record gives c. 1355). Tempera and gold on poplar panel, 19.8 × 37.8 cm. Berlin, Staatliche Museen, Gemäldegalerie, acquired in 1821 with the Solly collection. Photo: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, Gemäldegalerie / Christoph Schmidt, Public Domain Mark 1.0.

alt: Small horizontal panel. In a landscape of pale rocks with small leafy trees at either side, against a gold ground, a large closed sarcophagus of white marble decorated with green lozenges and small squares stands at the centre. The Virgin, in a black mantle with gold stars, collapses over the lid of the tomb, her head resting on her arm and her eyes closed, her other arm stretched across the lid. A woman in a blue mantle bends over her and supports her. Behind the tomb stand two other haloed women and a bearded old man in an orange mantle, joining their hands in prayer, and at the left a young woman in a long red mantle stands with joined hands. Small flowering plants grow on the ground.
caption: Puccio di Simone, The Swooning of the Virgin at the Tomb of Christ, with the Three Marys, predella panel of the polyptych for the Dominicans of Perugia, 1348–1352 (according to the museum). Tempera on wood, gold ground. Copenhagen, Statens Museum for Kunst, KMS3756. Photo: SMK, Statens Museum for Kunst, public domain.

alt: Tall arched panel in a modern gilded frame lined with red velvet. On a gold ground Saint James the Greater stands frontally, a bearded man with long reddish-brown hair and a punched halo decorated with flower motifs. He wears a blue tunic with gold-embroidered borders and a cream mantle patterned with gold ornament and lined in pink, drawn over his left shoulder. In his right hand he holds a pilgrim's staff from which hangs a black pouch with a white scallop shell; in his left he holds an unrolled scroll with an inscription in Gothic capitals. He stands on a red carpet, his sandalled feet visible below the hem.
caption: Puccio di Simone, Saint James the Greater, late 1340s. Egg tempera on wood, 92.7 × 29.6 cm. Seattle Art Museum, Samuel H. Kress Collection, 61.172. Photo: Another Believer, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (cropped, background modified).

alt: Five-part gabled polyptych in a gilded frame with colonnettes; the gables, painted green and dark red, each contain a gilded roundel. In the taller central panel the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle over a red dress, sits low on a patterned cloth and nurses the Child, who lies across her lap in a red tunic; below her runs an inscription with the painter's name, and in the base the words of the Ave Maria. In the lateral panels stand four saints on gold grounds, each named in the base: at the far left Saint Lawrence, young and tonsured, in a red dalmatic, holding a palm and a book; next to him Saint Onuphrius, an emaciated hermit covered only by his long hair and beard, with a staff, among rocks; at the right Saint James the Greater, bearded, in a blue tunic and a pink mantle, with a pilgrim's staff and a book; at the far right Saint Bartholomew, with a dark beard, in a pale patterned mantle, holding a knife and a book.
caption: Puccio di Simone, Madonna of Humility with Saints Lawrence, Onuphrius, James the Greater and Bartholomew, signed, c. 1348–1350. Tempera and gold on panel, 132 × 190.5 × 12 cm. Florence, Galleria dell'Accademia, inv. 1890 no. 8569. Galleria dell'Accademia, Florence, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Gabled panel in a gilded frame with twisted colonnettes and Corinthian capitals; in a trefoil in the gable, the dove of the Holy Spirit on a gold ground, the spandrels painted with gold foliage on dark blue. On a gold ground the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle over a red dress, sits on a throne covered with a red patterned cloth, holding the Child on her left arm; he wears a yellow cloth and a red sash, and leans towards her, touching her chin, while she raises her right hand to his breast. Her halo carries an inscription. At her feet kneel two small angels in pale green and yellow robes, each playing a fiddle with a bow, turned towards each other. In the base the inscription AVE GRATIA PLENA.
caption: Puccio di Simone, Madonna and Child with Angels, c. 1350. Tempera on panel, 96.5 × 57.2 cm. Pasadena, Norton Simon Museum, The Norton Simon Foundation, F.1965.1.046.P. Photo: Wmpearl, CC0 1.0, via Wikimedia Commons (background modified).

alt: Small gabled triptych with the wings open, in a gilded frame with twisted colonnettes, pinnacles and a crocketed gable topped by a large carved leaf. In the central panel, on a gold ground, the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle over a pink dress patterned in gold, sits low on a red cloth and nurses the Child, who lies across her lap wrapped in a gold cloth and wears a small cross on a cord. The left wing shows, in the triangular top, the angel of the Annunciation kneeling, and below the Nativity: an angel flying over dark hills, the Virgin kneeling beside the manger where the swaddled Child lies before the ox and the ass, and Joseph seated in a yellow mantle with his head on his hand. The right wing shows, in the top, the Virgin Annunciate seated with a book, and below the Crucifixion, with the Virgin and Saint John standing at the foot of the cross and a skull on the ground.
caption: Puccio di Simone, Portable Triptych with the Madonna of Humility, the Nativity and the Crucifixion, and the Annunciation in the gables of the wings, mid-14th century. Tempera and gold on panel. Avignon, Musée du Petit Palais. Photo: Herbert Frank, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons (background modified).

alt: Three separate gold-ground panels without their frame, the central one taller, all with cut corners at the top. In the centre the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle over a pale dress patterned with small dark motifs, sits before a red cloth patterned with quatrefoils, holding the Child, who wears an orange tunic and a red coral pendant and presses his cheek against hers. In the left panel a bearded monk in a pale habit, Saint Benedict, holds an open book with an inscription, beside Saint Catherine, crowned, in a pink dress with a book and a palm, her wheel behind her. In the right panel an old bearded hermit in a white habit, Saint Romuald, with a book and a staff, stands beside a young bishop in a mitre and a red cope patterned with gold fleurs-de-lis over a brown habit, Saint Louis of Toulouse, holding a crozier and a book.
caption: Puccio di Simone (attributed), Triptych with the Madonna and Child and Saints Benedict, Catherine of Alexandria, Romuald and Louis of Toulouse, mid-14th century. Tempera on panel, 100 × 163 cm (overall). Urbino, Palazzo Ducale, Galleria Nazionale delle Marche, inv. 1990 D 22. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (background modified).

alt: Tall gabled panel in a plain gilded frame. Against a gold ground Saint Anthony Abbot, an old man with a long grey beard, stands frontally in a grey-brown mantle over a dark habit, holding a tall staff in his right hand and a red book with clasps in his left; his halo carries an inscription. At either side rise squared grey rocks with a dark tree on each, and on rocks and trees perch pairs of small birds. At the left, on a smaller scale, a group of kneeling men looks up at him with joined hands, among them a man in a mail hood, a bearded man in a red tunic with mail sleeves, and a kneeling figure in red boots with spurs. At the right a group of kneeling women in veils and coloured dresses, one holding a baby swaddled in red and white bands. At the saint's feet stand two black pigs with a white band around the body. A fragmentary inscription runs along the bottom edge.
caption: Puccio di Simone, Saint Anthony Abbot Venerated by Two Groups of Devotees, 1353. Tempera and gold on a gabled panel, 195.2 × 106 cm. Fabriano, Pinacoteca Civica "Bruno Molajoli", from the church of Sant'Antonio Abate fuori Porta Pisana, Fabriano. Photo: Pinacoteca Civica "Bruno Molajoli", Fabriano. Image for educational use only.

alt: Gothic triptych in a gilded frame with three pointed gables and twisted colonnettes. In the taller central panel the Virgin, in a blue mantle, sits on a hexagonal throne holding the naked Child, surrounded by eighteen angels in tiers; in front stand four smaller saints, a crowned female saint with a wheel and a bearded monk in black at the left, another bearded monk with a staff and a female saint holding flowers in her skirt at the right; a small Crucifix in a quatrefoil occupies the gable. The left panel shows Saint Anthony Abbot, standing in a grey-brown habit with a dark hood and a tau-shaped staff, with the angel of the Annunciation in the trefoil above. The right panel shows Saint Venantius, a young man with long fair hair in an orange brocade tunic patterned with blue rosettes and a long blue mantle, holding a banner, with the Virgin Annunciate in the trefoil above. The saints stand on red carpets patterned in gold.
caption: Puccio di Simone and Allegretto Nuzi, Madonna and Child Enthroned with Saints and Angels, and Saints Anthony Abbot and Venantius, 1354. Tempera and gold on panel; framed dimensions: central panel 150.5 × 66.7 × 8.3 cm, left panel 123.8 × 45.7 × 8.3 cm, right panel 123.8 × 43.2 × 8.3 cm. Washington, National Gallery of Art, Andrew W. Mellon Collection, 1937.1.6.a–c. Photo: National Gallery of Art, Washington, Open Access (CC0) (background modified).

alt: Tall gabled panel in a gilded frame. In the gable, a small figure of the crucified Christ in a gold quatrefoil on a dark blue ground. Below, under a cusped arch, the Virgin in a blue mantle with a gold border and a star on the shoulder sits on a hexagonal throne covered with an orange cloth patterned in gold, holding the naked Child, who is wrapped from the hips in a gold-embroidered cloth, wears a red coral pendant and holds a small black and white bird; she points her finger towards him. At either side eighteen haloed angels stand in tiers, some with hands crossed on their breasts. In front stand four saints: at the left a crowned young woman in a gold mantle lined with blue, with a wheel, and a bearded monk in black; at the right a bearded monk in black leaning on a staff and a young woman in a pink dress holding flowers in her skirt. A fragmentary inscription runs along the base.
caption: Puccio di Simone, Madonna and Child Enthroned with Four Saints and Eighteen Angels, central panel of the triptych of Sant'Antonio Abate in Fabriano, 1354. Tempera and gold on panel, 150.5 × 66.7 × 8.3 cm (framed). Washington, National Gallery of Art, Andrew W. Mellon Collection, 1937.1.6.b. Photo: National Gallery of Art, Washington, Open Access (CC0) (background modified).

alt: Tall gabled panel in a gilded frame with twisted colonnettes. Under a cusped arch on a gold ground stands Saint Anthony Abbot, an old man with a long white beard, in a grey-brown habit with a dark hood, turned slightly to the right; he raises his right hand and holds with his left a long tau-shaped staff. His halo carries an inscription. At his feet, at the lower left, a small black pig; he stands on a red carpet patterned with gold trefoils. In the gable, in a gold trefoil, the angel of the Annunciation in half length holding a lily.
caption: Allegretto Nuzi, Saint Anthony Abbot, left panel of the triptych of Sant'Antonio Abate in Fabriano, 1354. Tempera and gold on panel; painted surface 89.3 × 33.6 cm, 123.8 × 45.7 × 8.3 cm (framed). Washington, National Gallery of Art, Andrew W. Mellon Collection, 1937.1.6.a. Photo: National Gallery of Art, Washington, Open Access (CC0) (background modified).

alt: Tall gabled panel in a gilded frame with twisted colonnettes. Under a cusped arch on a gold ground stands Saint Venantius, a beardless young man with long wavy fair hair, turned to the left. He wears a knee-length tunic of orange-red brocade patterned with large blue rosettes, foliage and small animals, with an embroidered hem, a long blue mantle falling from his left shoulder, and blue hose. With his right hand he holds a staff with a banner patterned in black, gold and red; his left hand rests at his belt. His halo carries an inscription. He stands on a red carpet patterned with gold trefoils. In the gable, in a gold trefoil, the Virgin Annunciate in half length, her hand on her breast.
caption: Puccio di Simone, Saint Venantius, right panel of the triptych of Sant'Antonio Abate in Fabriano, 1354. Tempera and gold on panel; painted surface 89.2 × 33 cm, 123.8 × 43.2 × 8.3 cm (framed). Washington, National Gallery of Art, Andrew W. Mellon Collection, 1937.1.6.c. Photo: National Gallery of Art, Washington, Open Access (CC0) (background modified).

alt: Five-part gabled polyptych in a worn frame with colonnettes; in each gable a small half-length figure in a gold roundel, Christ blessing at the centre. In the taller central panel the Virgin, in a light blue mantle over a pink dress, sits on a throne with a red cloth of honour, holding the Child, who wears a pale tunic, reaches up to her veil and holds a small bird; she points her finger towards him. At the sides of the throne stand two small female saints, at the left Saint Lucy in a violet mantle holding a palm and a small vessel, at the right Saint Catherine crowned, with a book and a wheel. In the lateral panels stand four saints turned towards the centre: Saint Anthony Abbot with a tau staff and a small pig at the lower left; Saint Nicholas in bishop's vestments with mitre, crozier and book; Saint John the Baptist in a camel skin and a violet mantle, with a cross-staff and an inscribed scroll; Saint Francis in his habit, his hands crossed on his breast.
caption: Puccio di Simone, Madonna and Child Enthroned with Saints Lucy and Catherine, and Saints Anthony Abbot, Nicholas, John the Baptist and Francis, sixth decade of the 14th century (1357?). Tempera and gold on panel, 144 × 191 cm. Certaldo, Museo d'Arte Sacra, inv. 4, from the oratory of San Pietro a Petrognano, later in the church of San Giovanni Battista in Jerusalem at San Donnino. Museo d'Arte Sacra, Certaldo, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Gabled triptych with a worn wooden frame. In the taller central panel Saint Matthew, bearded, in a green mantle over a grey-blue tunic, sits frontally on a Gothic throne with pinnacles and a red cloth of honour, holding a pen in his raised right hand and an open book on his knee; two angels in white stand at the sides of the throne, and small kneeling devotees in black, a man with a boy at the left and two women at the right, pray at its foot. In the left panel a young tonsured deacon saint in a red dalmatic holds a palm and a book, with a small kneeling woman at the left; in the right panel Saint James the Greater, bearded, in a dark blue mantle lined with red, holds a pilgrim's staff, with two small kneeling figures at the right. Roundels in the gables show Christ blessing at the centre and two half-length figures in the wings. In the base, roundels with the mourning Virgin, the Man of Sorrows and a third abraded figure, two diamond-shaped panels, and two coats of arms, a red shield at the left and a white shield with a black wheel at the right.
caption: Puccio di Simone, Saint Matthew Enthroned with Two Angels, a Deacon Saint, Saint James the Greater and Seven Devotees, c. 1350–1360. Tempera and gold on panel. Florence, Galleria dell'Accademia, inv. 1890 no. 5063. Galleria dell'Accademia, Florence, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Black-and-white photograph of a triptych in an elaborate frame with crocketed gables, finials and twisted colonnettes, standing in front of an iron grille. In the central panel Christ hangs on the cross; at its foot a kneeling figure, presumably Mary Magdalene, embraces it, and a skull lies on the ground; the Virgin stands at the left in a dark mantle, Saint John at the right, and behind him a bearded soldier raises his hand; a rocky outcrop closes the scene at the left. In the left panel stand Saint Francis, his hands crossed on his breast, and a bearded apostle with a staff, identified as Saint James. In the right panel stand a young female saint holding a palm, with a spiked wheel at her feet, Saint Catherine, and a veiled female saint in a dark mantle. Each gable contains a small roundel with a half-length figure.
caption: Puccio di Simone, Crucifixion with Saints (triptych), 1350–1362. Panel (described by the museum as oil on cradled panel), 168.7 × 179.3 × 10.2 cm. Cambridge, Mass., Harvard Art Museums/Fogg Museum, Bequest of Lucy Wallace Porter, 1962.292. Harvard Art Museums, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons (cropped); historical black-and-white photograph.

alt: Gothic triptych on gold ground with three gables. In the centre the Virgin, crowned and wearing a gold-patterned mantle, is enthroned with the Christ Child, surrounded by tiers of haloed angels and four standing saints, with an inscription on the base of the throne. In the left panel Saint Anthony Abbot, bearded and in a brown hooded habit, holds a tau-shaped staff and raises his right hand. In the right panel the young Saint Julian, in a gold brocade tunic and dark cloak, holds a lance with a red banner. The gables show the crucified Christ in a quatrefoil between the angel Gabriel and the Virgin Annunciate.
caption: Allegretto Nuzi, Madonna and Child Enthroned with Angels and Saints, between Saints Anthony Abbot and Julian, 1369. Tempera and gold on panel. Macerata, Duomo di San Giuliano, from the church of Sant'Antonio Abate, Macerata. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (background modified).

alt: Gold-ground panel with a pointed arch and twisted colonnettes. Under a Gothic canopy with a red cloth of honour patterned with gold fleurs-de-lis, Christ, seated at the right in a pink tunic and a large blue mantle, places a crown on the head of the Virgin, who sits at the left in a pale gold mantle patterned with small motifs, bowing her head with her hands crossed on her breast. They sit side by side on a red cushion patterned in gold.
caption: Bernardo Daddi, The Coronation of the Virgin, c. 1340–1345. Tempera and gold leaf on wood, 111.7 × 75.5 cm. London, The National Gallery, NG 6599. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (background modified).

alt: Vertical panel on gold ground. The Virgin, wrapped in a deep blue mantle, supports the dead Christ, who lies diagonally across her lap, his emaciated torso marked by a bleeding side wound, his head crowned with thorns and held close to her face. A long sword descends from the upper right toward the Virgin's breast. Above, six half-length mourning angels in red and white appear behind a banded arc of blue and white, with large yellow wings at the outer edges. At the lower left a small figure in a white liturgical garment raises a golden chalice beneath Christ's wounded side and hanging right arm; below, a tiny bearded donor in a red robe kneels with raised hands. A painted scroll at the bottom carries a Latin dedication and the signature 'Symon pinxit'.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Pietà with Angels and the Donor Giovanni da Elthinl, 1368 or shortly after, tempera and gold on panel, c. 78 × 50 cm. Bologna, Museo Civico d'Arte Industriale e Galleria Davia Bargellini, inv. 173. Signed "Symon pinxit".

alt: Shaped painted cross photographed against a dark ground. The dead Christ hangs with his head sunk forward and inclined, long fair hair, greenish pallid flesh and a bleeding side wound, his grey-white loincloth knotted at the hip; the cross field behind him is deep blue edged with gold. The mixtilinear terminals hold half-length figures: at the top a blessing figure with an open book above a small field with a bird spreading its wings over a nest, then a scroll lettered INRI; at the left the mourning Virgin in a dark mantle; at the right the weeping Saint John the Evangelist. At Christ's feet two diminutive mourning women stand on the shaft, and his blood runs in a long rivulet down to a rocky mound sheltering the skull of Adam. At the bottom, below the skull terminal, a small tablet carries a Latin inscription.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Crucifix with the Mourning Virgin, Saint John the Evangelist and the Blessing Father, dated the last day of February 1370, tempera and gold on shaped panel. Bologna, San Giacomo Maggiore. Signed "Symon fecit".

alt: Arched panel on gold ground, framed by a cusped arch with trefoil openings and twisted columns at the sides. The Virgin, in a salmon-pink dress and a blue mantle densely patterned in gold and lined in green, sits on a tall throne with a red cloth of honour and side wings pierced by pointed arches, crowned by blue flame-like finials. She holds the Child, who stands on her knee in a sheer pale shift, one hand grasping the edge of her mantle at the neck, and looks up into her face. Two angels in pale robes stand at the sides with hands crossed on the breast, gazing upward. At the lower right a small donor in a dark brown habit and a red cap kneels with joined hands. Along the base runs a Gothic inscription.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Madonna and Child Enthroned with Two Angels and the Donor Giovanni da Piacenza, c. 1378 (after 9 May 1378), tempera and gold on panel, 142 × 99.5 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 225; formerly Santa Maria del Monte, then Istituto delle Scienze.

alt: Rectangular panel on gold ground. Above, a banded arc in blue and green, studded with gold stars on its lower edge, separates a row of half-length angels with golden haloes and red garments from the scene below. Beneath the arc, Christ and the Virgin sit side by side on a bench with red cushions. At the right Christ, crowned, bearded, in a white tunic with a gold belt and a pink mantle lined in blue, holds a slender sceptre on his knee and with his raised right hand sets a crown on the Virgin's head. At the left the Virgin, in a dark green mantle patterned with gold fleurons over a pale dress, bows her head and crosses her hands on her breast. On the step below runs the signature 'Symon fecit hoc opus'; a second inscription along the bottom edge gives the date 1382.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Coronation of the Virgin, completed October 1382, tempera and gold on panel. Bologna, Raccolta Lercaro, on loan from the Istituto Zoni; formerly Terziarie dell'Annunciata in Borgo Orfeo, then Santa Maria Incoronata (from 1669). Signed "Symon fecit hoc opus" and dated.

alt: Detached fresco, square in format, with large losses at the lower left where bare plaster shows, and painted decorative borders at the sides.
