At the left, beneath a house with a red tiled roof and round arches, Christ in a pink mantle raises his hand toward a crowd; on the roof above, a man in green leans down, and below the roof a patterned blue cloth hangs among bearded heads, while turbaned men sit in the foreground with their backs to the viewer and a large figure in red is seated at the centre. At the right, beyond a slender column, a group of bearded elders in yellow and red mantles stands under a second arch, and beside a rocky outcrop a young man in a yellow tunic strides away carrying a rolled bed on his shoulder; below him a man bends over a staff.
caption: "Jacobus" and Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", The Healing of the Paralytic at Capernaum and the Healing at the Pool of Bethesda, c. 1355–1360, detached fresco. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 7031; from the church of Santa Maria (now Sant'Apollonia) di Mezzaratta, right wall.

alt: Square detached fresco, heavily damaged, most of its surface reduced to a pale, flaking ground with scattered traces of colour and a large area of bare grey plaster at the left. At the centre survives the head of the Virgin, veiled and haloed, turned slightly to the right, with a hand raised before her breast. Behind her is a deep blue sky crossed by cracks. At the upper left a curving red band and yellowish forms suggest a figure or a building; at the upper right a series of curved, striated strokes may belong to the fronds of a tree. At the lower left a vertical strip of red drapery survives beside a yellow border.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", The Flight into Egypt, fragment, c. 1355–1360, detached fresco, 146 × 140 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 6355; from the church of Santa Maria (now Sant'Apollonia) di Mezzaratta.

alt: Large detached fresco of which only an irregular band along the top and a patch at the right survive; the lower two-thirds is bare, neutral plaster. At the left a dense crowd of heads, some with traces of haloes, looks toward the centre. In the centre Christ, in a pink mantle over a blue garment, leans toward a man in a grey-blue tunic and raises his hands to the man's head and face. Behind them a slender tree with a dark green crown stands against a blue sky. At the right rises a pink building with battlements and an arched doorway, and beneath it a group of men — one bearded in a cap, one in a turban, one young and fair-haired — stands together, turned toward the left.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Miracles of Christ, fragment, c. 1355–1360, detached fresco, 246 × 265 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 7030; from the church of Santa Maria (now Sant'Apollonia) di Mezzaratta.

alt: Tall, narrow strip of detached fresco, most of it bare plaster, with painted remains concentrated in the upper half along the right side. Beneath a band of dark blue sky, a cluster of heads survives: at the top left a figure in a white head-cloth; below, a bearded man in a red cap pressing a yellow cloth to his nose and mouth; beside him a veiled figure in a green mantle with a hand raised to the face. From the left a long white form, wrapped like a bandaged arm or shroud, extends across the group. Lower down appear a veiled female head and fragments of reddish-brown drapery with a pale vertical object. At the very top, above the sky, a small separate fragment shows a red and white shield-like motif.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", The Raising of Lazarus, fragment, c. 1355–1360, detached fresco, 246 × 72 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 7033; from the church of Santa Maria (now Sant'Apollonia) di Mezzaratta.

alt: Large detached fresco, wider than tall, with a painted ornamental border at the left and losses at the top, including a grey patch of bare plaster at the upper left. At the right, beneath a shed with a sloping roof of straw or planks, the Virgin in a dark blue mantle sits holding the Child on her lap; behind her stands Joseph, bearded, in a red cap. Before them an old king in a voluminous yellow mantle kneels and bends toward the Child. In the centre a second king, bearded and crowned, stands in a red tunic patterned with white, holding his gift; at the left a third, with long fair hair and beard, wears a pink-violet mantle that he gathers in his hand. Behind him, at the left edge, stand bearded attendants, one in yellow. A large pale banner or cloth billows across the upper centre against a rocky landscape and a blue sky; at the far right a figure in a white garment spotted with green is cut by the edge.
caption: "Jacobus" and Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", The Adoration of the Magi, mid-fourteenth century, detached fresco, 220 × 288 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 6352; from the church of Santa Maria (now Sant'Apollonia) di Mezzaratta.

alt: Tall detached fresco with extensive losses filled with neutral plaster. At the top runs an ornamental band of eight-pointed stars and diamonds in red, ochre, white and blue, above an ochre border. Against a deep blue ground stands Saint Peter Martyr in the Dominican habit, white tunic under a black mantle, his tonsured head haloed and inclined to the left; a green palm rests against his shoulder, and fragmentary Gothic letters beside him read '...us mar...'. His right hand, now isolated by losses, reaches out toward the left. Below, the white folds of his tunic survive, with a small green object at the top and, at the right edge, a pink strip with a small red cross. At the lower left a small Dominican nun in a black veil and white wimple kneels in profile, hands joined, looking up at the saint. At the left edge a narrow strip of an adjacent field survives, with an ochre border and ornament.
caption: Painter close to Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Saint Peter Martyr and a Dominican Nun, c. 1375–1380, detached fresco, 228 × 107.5 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 4685; from the monastery of Sant'Agnese, Bologna.

alt: Triangular gable panel in a plain wooden frame from which the gilding has worn away, with a long crack running down the upper right. Within a pointed, trilobed gold field the Archangel Gabriel appears at half length, turned three-quarters to the right. His fair hair is bound with a pearled fillet and small white flowers, and a tooled gold halo frames his head; vermilion wings rise behind his shoulders. He wears a pale blue tunic with a dark collar and a cream mantle lined in green, draped over one shoulder. His right hand is raised, palm outward, in a gesture of salutation, and his left holds a slender stem of white lilies.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", The Archangel Gabriel, c. 1350–1355, tempera and gold on panel, 50.5 × 31.7 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 224; from the Istituto delle Scienze. Companion to the Virgin Annunciate, inv. 223. Photo: Pinacoteca Nazionale di Bologna.

alt: Triangular gable panel in a plain wooden frame from which the gilding has worn away, with a long crack running down the upper left. Within a pointed, trilobed gold field the Virgin appears at half length before a red cloth of honour patterned with small dark quatrefoil flowers, its upper edge held by a brown rail. She wears a pale dress under a very dark mantle that leaves her fair hair uncovered, and inclines her haloed head to her right, gazing outward; her right hand is raised, palm forward, and her left is laid across her breast. At the lower left stands a lectern with an open book. Above her, at the apex of the gold field, a small blue-grey cloud sends down golden rays along which the white dove of the Holy Spirit descends toward her halo.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", The Virgin Annunciate, c. 1350–1355, tempera and gold on panel, 50.5 × 32 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 223; from the Istituto delle Scienze. Companion to the Archangel Gabriel, inv. 224. Photo: Pinacoteca Nazionale di Bologna.

alt: Large two-tiered Gothic polyptych in an elaborate gilded frame with pinnacles, crocketed gables, twisted colonnettes and fan-shaped lunettes above the lower arches. In the centre of the lower tier, beneath an arc of blue sky with a row of angel heads and a gold cloth of honour, Christ in a pink mantle crowns the Virgin, who bows with crossed hands in a blue mantle patterned with gold; the signature 'Symon fecit hoc opus' runs along the base. Three standing saints flank each side: at the left a bearded saint in a green tunic and a pink mantle with a staff and a book, a bearded saint in red with a sword and a book, and an old bearded saint with a book and keys; at the right Saint John the Baptist in camel skin with an unrolled scroll, an old bearded saint in a brown habit with a tau-headed staff, bells and a book, and a crowned, bearded saint in a red mantle with a sceptre and a book. In the centre of the upper tier Christ hangs on the cross between the mourning Virgin and Saint John, with a kneeling figure embracing the foot of the cross; three half-length saints flank each side, including two crowned female saints at the ends, a monk in black with a book and mitred bishops.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Polyptych with the Coronation of the Virgin, the Crucifixion and Saints, c. 1385–1390, tempera and gold on panel, 142.5 × 186.5 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 298; from the chapter house of Santi Leonardo e Orsola, Bologna. Signed "Symon fecit hoc opus".

alt: Large three-tiered polyptych in a gilded frame, photographed against a black ground, made of seven vertical stacks of compartments. In the centre of the lowest tier, under a blue arc, Christ in a white mantle crowns the Virgin, who bows in a dark blue mantle scattered with gold; a small inscribed plaque sits at the foot of the compartment. Three standing saints flank each side in arched niches: at the left a mitred bishop in a gold cope, a saint in blue and yellow with keys and a book, and Saint John the Baptist in a white mantle holding a disc; at the right a bearded saint in red with a book, a saint in yellow and white with a book, and a mitred bishop in a green cope. Above the Coronation, a gabled compartment holds a crowded Crucifixion with many figures; above it, a small pinnacle contains a seated blessing figure. The middle tier shows six smaller standing saints, among them figures in white habits, a bishop and a saint in a green mantle; the top tier carries six slender pinnacles with tiny standing figures.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Polyptych with the Coronation of the Virgin, the Crucifixion and Saints, c. 1365–1370, tempera and gold on panel, 180 × 248.5 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 254; acquired on the antiques market, formerly in San Domenico, Bologna.

alt: Small painting with a multilobed, cusped top edge against a gold ground tooled with ornamental borders, crossed by horizontal cracks and small losses. At the right stands Saint Bernard, haloed, tonsured, with a long grey beard, wearing a white habit under a red mantle fastened with a gold brooch; he holds out an open book inscribed with lines of Gothic script. Behind him a monk in white holds his crozier, and several tonsured monks in white crowd at his shoulders. At the left a kneeling monk in a brown habit reaches up to receive the book, and behind him rise rows of monks in brown habits and dark caps, and of nuns in white veils and wimples, their heads massed into receding rows of rounded hoods. At the saint's feet a small figure lies prostrate. Along the lower edge runs the inscription 'S. bernardus'.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Saint Bernard Gives the Monastic Rule, c. 1370, tempera on canvas, 54.5 × 48 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 1078; from the Istituto delle Scienze. Inscribed "S. Bernardus".

alt: Tall painting on canvas. A plain wooden cross with nail holes and a white titulus lettered I.N.R.I. rises against a blue-green sky, before a rocky landscape with two pale hills at the left. At the right Saint Helena kneels in profile toward the cross, hands joined, gazing upward; she wears a white dress patterned with small gold stars and a voluminous red mantle lined in yellow, and her head is framed by a gold halo set with a crown. At the lower left, much smaller, a nun in a black mantle, white habit and white wimple kneels with joined hands, looking up at the cross. From each figure a band of Gothic script rises toward the cross: a long one from the nun along the upright, a shorter curving one from Helena's head.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Saint Helena Adoring the Cross, with a Nun, c. 1370–1380, tempera on canvas, 212 × 135.5 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 220; from the Dominican nuns of Sant'Agnese, Bologna.

alt: Tall, narrow panel with a gabled top on gold ground. Pope Urban V, clean-shaven, with a long nose and a direct, slightly asymmetrical gaze, sits frontally in a red cope bordered with gold embroidery and fastened with a lozenge-shaped morse, over a white alb; he wears a tall triple tiara. His right hand is raised in blessing; on his left he holds a small gabled diptych with the half-length figures of Saint Peter, grey-haired, and Saint Paul, dark-bearded. Two angels in pink above him hold the tiara on his head, and two angels below hold a patterned gold cloth of honour behind him. At the apex of the gable a cloud sends down red rays, a dove descends, and two crossed keys appear beneath it. Along the footboard runs the signature 'Symon fecit', and on the base the inscription 'Beatus Urbanus papa quintus'.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Blessed Pope Urban V, c. 1375, tempera and gold on panel, 196.8 × 62.5 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 303; provenance unknown. Signed "Symon fecit" and inscribed "Beatus Urbanus papa quintus".

alt: Two long, narrow predella panels shown one above the other, each divided into arched compartments with scalloped tops against a dark red-brown ground. The upper panel holds four scenes: Saint Anne in bed after the birth of the Virgin, with women attending and a maid at a basin, and a pale square with a cross at the far left; the child Mary climbing the steps of the Temple toward the high priest; the marriage of Mary and Joseph under an arcade; and the presentation of the Child in the Temple, held over an altar between the Virgin and Simeon. The lower panel holds three scenes: the Virgin lying dead on a bed covered with gold cloth, surrounded by the apostles; the apostles carrying her bier while a man in yellow kneels and grasps it; and the Virgin borne up in a mandorla above an open red tomb, with apostles and a haloed figure in blue below, and a coat of arms with a green diagonal band at the lower right.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Predella with Seven Scenes from the Life of the Virgin, from the Cospi polyptych, c. 1396–1398, tempera and gold on panel, two panels, 23 × 124 cm (inv. 274, four scenes) and 23 × 93.8 cm (inv. 275, three scenes). Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 274–275; formerly Zambeccari collection; originally Bologna, San Petronio, Cospi chapel. With the Cospi arms.

alt: Small gabled panel on gold ground in a plain brown frame. At the apex, above a clump of dark green foliage, a white pelican pierces her breast to feed her young in a nest. Below, a white titulus lettered I.N.R.I. tops the cross, on which Christ hangs dead, emaciated, his head inclined, blood running from his wounds down the cross to the ground. At the left the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle, swoons into the arms of the holy women and Saint John; the Magdalen, in red, with long fair hair, kneels and embraces the foot of the cross. Behind them helmeted soldiers raise a black-and-white banner and a lance. At the right a large bearded man in a red cloak over gilded armour and a tall pointed hat raises his right hand toward Christ beneath a red pennant; behind him stand bearded men, one holding up a large white cloth.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", The Crucifixion, c. 1370, tempera and gold on panel, 51.5 × 37 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 286; from the Istituto delle Scienze.

alt: Gabled panel in a carved, gilded frame with a running foliate ornament. In the upper register, against gold, the dead Christ hangs on the cross between the Virgin in a dark mantle and Saint John in pink, with the Magdalen in red kneeling at the foot; at the left kneel a young figure in orange and a bearded saint in a brown habit, with a red cardinal's hat hanging behind him, at the right a mitred bishop in an orange cope and a figure in blue, both kneeling; small inscriptions run beneath the side figures. A curved band separates the lower register, where Christ and the Virgin sit side by side on a broad throne before a red cloth of honour held by angels, the Virgin in a grey-white mantle with a hand on her breast, Christ in a blue mantle over pink. The twelve apostles crowd on either side. In the foreground a saint in yellow and pink presents a small kneeling nun in black at the left, and a bearded saint presents a small kneeling layman in ochre at the right. In the lower corners appear the bust of a haloed woman in a black veil and white wimple at the left and the bust of a pope wearing a tiara at the right. The signature 'Symon fecit hoc opus' runs along the step of the throne.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Christ and the Virgin Enthroned among the Apostles, with the Crucifixion, Saints and Two Devotees, c. 1390–1395, tempera and gold on panel, 80.5 × 77 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 302; from the Istituto delle Scienze. Signed "Symon fecit hoc opus"; inscribed "S. Jeronimus" and "S. Agustinus".

alt: Long, low strip of detached fresco on a pale ground, its upper part lost. Four seated or kneeling women occupy the centre and right: at the left a woman in a light blue dress and white head-cloth holds a dead infant across her lap; beside her a figure in a crimson garment bends forward over a white cloth, her head lost; then a woman in a bright yellow dress, a white cloth bound round her head, leans forward with her cheek resting on her hand beside a small dead child; at the far right a figure in a dark red mantle, seen from behind, is reduced to its silhouette. At the left edge, beyond a painted border of red and white ornament, survive fragments of another figure in brown and blue. Along the bottom runs a painted base with traces of ornament and a few illegible letters at the lower left.
caption: Master of the Massacre of the Innocents (associated in part of the literature with Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi"), The Massacre of the Innocents, fragment, mid-fourteenth century, detached fresco, 105 × 255 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 6354; from the church of Santa Maria (now Sant'Apollonia) di Mezzaratta.

alt: Detached fresco, nearly square, framed by painted borders, with a large abraded area in the upper part where an interior architecture with red cornices, a round arch and a slender building at the right survives in faint outline. In the centre an old bearded priest in a red cap, a yellow cloak and a white veil over his shoulders holds up the naked Christ Child, while a figure in a pink-red mantle, seen from behind and seated, bends toward the Child's lap to perform the rite; behind them a bearded man in a blue mantle and white hood leans forward. At the left stand two women, one in pink with a white head-dress, the other, the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle, holding a white cloth. At the right stand a group of bearded old men in yellow and red; at the far right a tall old man with a long white beard, in a dark blue habit and a white hood, stands behind a small kneeling figure in a grey garment with a row of round buttons, hands joined in prayer.
caption: "Jacobus" (Mezzaratta painter), The Circumcision of Christ, mid-fourteenth century, detached fresco, 235 × 220 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 6353; from the church of Santa Maria (now Sant'Apollonia) di Mezzaratta.

alt: Large shaped painted cross on a gold ground with a dark blue border along the arms and shaft, photographed against black. The dead Christ hangs with his head inclined, long fair hair falling on his shoulder, his body pale and lean, a white loincloth knotted at the hip, blood running from the side wound and the nailed feet. The terminals are lobed: at the top the half-length blessing Christ, in white and red against a burst of yellow and red rays, above a white titulus lettered I.N.R.I.; at the left the mourning Virgin in a dark mantle, her hand raised to her cheek; at the right Saint John in yellow and green with hands clasped. Beneath Christ's feet, on either side of the shaft, two small pale tablets carry lines of Gothic script. In the lower terminal a fair-haired kneeling figure, most probably the Magdalen, appears at the left, a smaller figure at the right, and a dark rocky form below.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Crucifix with the Mourning Virgin, Saint John and the Blessing Redeemer, c. 1375–1380, tempera and gold on shaped panel, 325 × 236 cm. Bologna, complex of Santo Stefano, Chiesa del Crocifisso. Signed.

alt: Small gabled panel on gold ground with carved leaf crockets along the sloping sides and a carved finial at the apex. At the top a pelican pierces her breast above a dark nest, over a white titulus lettered I.N.R.I. The dead Christ hangs on the cross, his body lean and grey, his head bowed, a white loincloth around his hips. At the left the Virgin, in a dark blue-black mantle, rests her cheek on her hand; at the right Saint John, in a pink mantle over a blue garment, presses his clasped hands to his chin. In the lower left foreground the Magdalen, with long red-gold hair, in an olive-green dress and a red mantle lined in white that spreads across the ground, kneels and lays her hand on the foot of the cross, which rises from a small rocky mound.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", The Crucifixion with the Virgin, Saint John and the Magdalen, c. 1395–1399, tempera and gold on panel, gabled, 52 × 22 cm. Bologna, private collection, on deposit at the Musei Civici d'Arte Antica.

alt: Portable triptych in a gilded Gothic Revival frame with crocketed gables and a carved finial, standing on a base inscribed 'PECCATA NOSTRA TULIT'. In the central panel, under a pointed arch with a pelican feeding her young in a nest at the top and a titulus lettered I.N.R.I., the dead Christ hangs on the cross between the Virgin, in a dark mantle with her hand to her cheek, and Saint John in a red mantle with clasped hands; the Magdalen kneels and embraces the foot of the cross. The left wing shows, from top to bottom, the Angel Gabriel in a small gabled field, a haloed saint at half length, and a gold cross on a dark ground; the right wing shows the Virgin Annunciate, Saint James with a pilgrim's staff, and a gold cross on a dark ground with the faint figure of a kneeling donor.
caption: Attributed to Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Portable Triptych: The Crucifixion (centre); The Angel Gabriel and a Saint (left); The Virgin and Saint James (right), c. 1380, tempera and gold on panel, 45.5 × 58 cm (open). Oxford, Ashmolean Museum, WA1892.8; bequeathed by the Revd Greville John Chester, 1892. Nineteenth-century frame. Photo: Ashmolean Museum, University of Oxford. Image for educational use only.

alt: Horizontal panel on gold ground. At the centre, before a red cloth of honour patterned in gold, Christ and the Virgin sit side by side on a bench. Christ, at the right, crowned, in a white tunic with a gold belt and a blue mantle lined in yellow, sets a crown on the head of the Virgin with his raised right hand and rests his left hand, holding a small sceptre, on his knee. The Virgin, at the left, in a white mantle over a blue dress, bows her head and crosses her hands on her breast. Above, two angels with dark wings hold the ends of a grey cornice from which gold drapery hangs in swags, and a row of seven angel heads looks down from behind it. Six apostles, haloed and praying, crowd at either side, kneeling or standing, among them Peter with a short grey beard at the left. A pale grey floor runs along the bottom.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi" (catalogued by the Louvre as School of Simone dei Crocifissi), The Coronation of the Virgin with the Apostles, 1380s, tempera and gold on poplar panel, 51 × 75 cm (painted surface 50 × 73 cm). Paris, Musée du Louvre, Département des Peintures, INV 20202 (Campana 337); on long-term loan to Avignon, Musée du Petit Palais. Photo: Musée du Louvre.

alt: Gilded reliquary triptych standing on a tall stepped base, its upper part pierced by a band of quatrefoil openings and its sloping sides incised with lozenge patterns. The central panel is framed by rows of small round cavities, empty and lined with red, crowned by a gable with leafy crockets. In the centre, on a densely punched gold ground marked with the Greek letters MP ΘY, the Virgin in a dark mantle presses her cheek against that of the Child, who wears an orange tunic and embraces her. Above, in a small field, the dead Christ rises half-length from the tomb before the cross. The left wing shows the Angel of the Annunciation in red kneeling on clouds and, below, Saint John the Baptist in a camel-skin tunic and white mantle with an unrolled scroll. The right wing shows the Virgin Annunciate seated with a book and, below, Saint Mary Magdalene clothed only in her long hair, hands joined, between two angels and two small trees.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Reliquary Triptych: the Virgin and Child, the Dead Christ, Saint John the Baptist, Saint Mary Magdalene and the Annunciation, c. 1355–1370, tempera and gold on panel, 50 × 55 cm. Paris, Musée du Louvre, Département des Peintures, DL 1973-15; Fondation de France, gift of Léon Salavin and his wife, née Jeanne Fournier, 1973. Photo: Musée du Louvre.

alt: Small gabled panel in a stepped, moulded gilt frame, on a worn gold ground through which the red-orange bole shows. At the apex a white pelican pierces her breast above a dark, leafy nest; below, a white titulus reads I.N.R.I. Christ hangs dead on the cross, his head bowed under the crown of thorns, his body pale and lean, a white loincloth around his hips; blood pours from his nailed feet down the shaft and pools on the ground. At the left the Virgin, in a black mantle over a dark blue-green dress, presses her clasped hands against her cheek. Kneeling before her, the Magdalen, with long golden hair, in a pale blue dress and a red mantle, reaches both hands toward the bleeding foot of the cross. At the right Saint John, in a green tunic and a pink-red mantle, presses his clasped hands to his chin. Low dark hills close the horizon.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", The Crucifixion with the Virgin, the Magdalen and Saint John the Evangelist, c. 1390, tempera and gold on panel with a shaped top, 45.7 × 34.6 cm (framed 53.3 × 39.4 cm). Formerly Venice, Ettore Viancini collection; London, private collection; offered at Sotheby's, New York, Master Paintings & Sculpture Day Sale, 31 January 2019, lot 103, and again at Sotheby's, New York, Old Masters Online, 24 January – 4 February 2020, lot 501, without reserve. Present whereabouts unknown. Photo: Sotheby's.

alt: Two tall gilded lateral panels, each crowned by a sloping gable with large carved leaf crockets, framing a pointed, trilobed arch over the main panel and a small carved base below. In the left gable the Angel Gabriel, in a pale dalmatic patterned with dark crosses, kneels on a green meadow beside a lily plant and raises his hand; beneath, under the arch, stand Saint Anthony Abbot, white-bearded, in a dark habit, holding a red book and a staff, and Saint John the Baptist in a camel-skin tunic and a pale mantle, pointing to an unrolled scroll inscribed 'Ego vox clamantis in deserto parate viam'. In the right gable the Virgin Annunciate, in a dark mantle, stands with crossed hands before a red brocade hanging, beside a lectern with an open book, as a dove descends from the upper right; beneath stand a saint in a pink mantle holding a book and a large knife with a red hilt, and a black-bearded saint in a red tunic and a grey patterned mantle, holding a red book and a pilgrim's staff. In the base of each wing appear two small busts of female saints, one of them crowned.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi" (attributed; catalogued as Bolognese school), Two Lateral Panels with the Annunciation; Saints Anthony Abbot and John the Baptist (left); Saints Bartholomew and James the Greater (right); with four female saints in the bases, c. 1360–1390, tempera and gold on panel, each 60 × 14.5 cm. Ferrara, Pinacoteca Nazionale (Palazzo dei Diamanti), Sacrati Strozzi collection, inv. 7120 (left panel) and 7121 (right panel); purchased from the Sacrati Strozzi heirs, 1992.

alt: Rectangular panel whose painted area once ended in a rounded top: above the heads of the angels the surface is unpainted, and the original curved outline is still visible. Christ and the Virgin sit side by side on a grey stone throne with red cushions, before a gold-brocaded cloth of honour held up at the corners by two angels. The Virgin, at the left, in a dark blue-black mantle over a pink dress, bows her head and crosses her hands on her breast. Christ, at the right, crowned and bearded, in a pale blue tunic with a gold belt, and a pink mantle, lowers a gold crown onto her head with his right hand and holds in his left a sceptre whose lily finial rests against his breast. Above the throne, behind a grey parapet, a dense choir of haloed angels in pastel garments joins hands in prayer. On the step of the throne runs the signature 'Symon pinxit hoc opus'.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", The Coronation of the Virgin, 1390–1399, tempera and gold on panel, 87 × 60 cm. Ferrara, Pinacoteca Nazionale (Palazzo dei Diamanti), inv. 6930 (formerly 361); gift of Natalia Valli, 1977. Signed "Symon pinxit hoc opus".

alt: Gabled panel with a stepped, lobed outline in a gilded frame. At the bottom the Virgin, haloed, in a black mantle, lies asleep on a bed with a red coverlet patterned with flowers; at the left a young woman in a white mantle sits at the head of the bed, resting her head on her hand over an open red book. From the sleeping Virgin rises a slender tree, its trunk speckled with gold, spreading branches with large leaves across the gold ground; on the branches, without a cross, hangs the crucified Christ, his arms stretched along the boughs, his head bowed. Two red seraphim hover beside his hands, and mourning angels emerge from small grey clouds among the leaves. At the top of the tree, above a dark nest, a pelican pierces her breast to feed her young. Small towns with towers rise on hills at the left and right edges.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", The Dream of the Virgin, c. 1355–1360, tempera and gold on panel, 75 × 52 cm. Ferrara, Pinacoteca Nazionale (Palazzo dei Diamanti), inv. 57; from the convent of Corpus Domini, Ferrara; purchased from the Galleria Costabili, Ferrara, 1874.

alt: Small panel in which a large almond-shaped mandorla, bordered in blue and white, fills the field against a red ground where red angels with punched gold haloes support it. Inside the mandorla, before a dark brown ground with a tall plain wooden cross and faint rows of heads, Christ and the Virgin sit side by side on a bench covered with gold brocade, with white marble sides. Christ, at the right, in a yellow tunic marked on the breast with a small red lozenge-shaped wound, and a white mantle lined in green, wears a crown of white pearls on his halo and sets a similar pearl crown on the Virgin's head with his raised right hand, while with his left he clasps her hands. The Virgin, at the left, in a dark green mantle over a white dress, bows her head toward him. Horizontal cracks cross the panel. At the bottom the signature 'Symon fecit'.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", The Coronation of the Virgin, c. 1355–1359, tempera and gold on panel, 43 × 36 cm. Budrio, Pinacoteca Civica "Domenico Inzaghi", on deposit from the Pinacoteca Nazionale di Bologna; probably from San Domenico, Bologna. Signed "Symon fecit".

alt: Panel in a gilded frame carved with a trilobed arch and foliate spandrels, on a heavily crackled gold ground. At the upper left, within a red and blue mandorla of clouds, God the Father appears half-length and sends golden rays down toward the Virgin, along which a small white dove descends. At the left the Angel Gabriel, haloed, in a pale robe and a mantle lined in red and yellow, kneels on a green floor, raising his right hand in salutation and holding a slender lily stalk in his left. At the right, beneath a projecting wooden canopy, the Virgin sits on a throne with a red brocade back, in a dark blue mantle bordered with gold over a pale dress, laying her right hand on her breast and holding an open book on her knees. On the ledge of the throne, between them, stands a red vase with a small round plant.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", The Annunciation, early 1380s, tempera and gold on panel, 55.6 × 34.5 cm. Moscow, Pushkin State Museum of Fine Arts, inv. 236; formerly D. M. Khomyakov collection, Moscow; Rumyantsev Museum, 1901; Pushkin Museum since 1924. Photo: Pushkin State Museum of Fine Arts.

alt: Arched panel in a gilded frame with a coloured dentil border and punched foliate spandrels. Beneath a tiled roof on wooden posts, before a dark cave and a wattle fence, an ox and a braying donkey stand behind a wicker manger draped with a white cloth; a golden star shines between them. In the foreground the Virgin, in a blue mantle, sits holding the naked Child on her lap and lifting a white cloth to her breast; beside her Joseph, in a pink robe, a blue mantle and a red cap, dozes with his head propped on his hand, next to a yellow pack-saddle on the ground. Above, two groups of angels hold up a jewelled crown over the stable, and at the right a flying angel in red points down to a shepherd, who stands with his staff, looking up in alarm and raising his hand, while black goats graze below him. At the bottom the signature 'Symon pin[xit]'.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", The Nativity, c. 1365–1382, tempera and gold on panel, arched, 47 × 25 cm. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi, inv. 1890 no. 3475; gift of Ugo Baldi to the Galleria dell'Accademia, 1863; Uffizi since 1906. Signed "Symon pin[xit]".

alt: Gilded portable tabernacle in three parts, with a tall central panel and two hinged wings, all crowned by gables with large carved leaf crockets; a carved rosette fills the central gable. In the central panel, under a canopy held by two angels, Christ in a pale tunic and blue mantle, with a red scarf, sets a crown on the head of the Virgin, who sits beside him in a dark green mantle with her hands crossed; above them a starry blue vault holds three red seraphim and a group of angel heads. At the foot of the central panel runs a Gothic signature. In the gables of the wings, the Angel of the Annunciation kneels at the left and the Virgin Annunciate sits at a lectern at the right. Below, in the left wing, Saint John the Evangelist, white-bearded, writes in a book on a rocky island, looking up at a vision in the sky with his eagle beside him; under him stands Saint Benedict in a dark habit with an open book and a staff. In the right wing, Saint John the Baptist kneels in a wooded wilderness holding a scroll; under him stands a mitred bishop saint, Martial, in a red cope over a blue vestment.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Tabernacle: the Coronation of the Virgin, with the Annunciation, Saint John the Evangelist on Patmos, Saint John the Baptist in the Wilderness, and Saints Benedict and Martial, fourteenth century (1370s), tempera and gold on panel, 87.5 × 71.5 × 2.9 cm. Cambridge, Mass., Harvard Art Museums/Fogg Museum, 1962.283; bequest of Lucy Wallace Porter, 1962. Photo: Harvard Art Museums. Image for educational use only.

alt: Front view of a small gilded wooden casket on four bracket feet, with a lid shaped like a pitched roof, an iron handle on top and an iron hasp and lock plate at the front. On the front slope of the lid, Christ stands naked in the river Jordan while Saint John the Baptist, at the left on a rocky bank, pours water over his head; at the right, angels kneel holding his garments. On the front of the box, beneath a painted arcade, six half-length saints with gold haloes are arranged in two groups of three on either side of the lock: at the left Saint Peter with his keys, a young saint with a book and a young saint in red; at the right a dark-bearded saint who appears to hold a knife, a young saint in blue and an old bearded saint in red with a book. Gothic inscriptions name some of them beneath their figures.
caption: Workshop of Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Casket with Scenes from the Life of Saint John the Baptist and Saints: front, with the Baptism of Christ on the lid, c. 1360 (also dated c. 1380), tempera and gilding on gesso over wood, 24 × 33.5 × 15.5 cm. London, Victoria and Albert Museum, 351-1864; purchased from M. Delange, Paris, 1864. Photo: Victoria and Albert Museum, London.

alt: The casket seen from above: the two slopes of the lid, with the Birth of Saint John the Baptist at the top and the Baptism of Christ at the bottom, meet at a flat ridge carrying an iron handle and a short Gothic inscription; the two triangular ends show the repeated coat of arms with mitre, crossed keys and crozier.
caption: The same casket seen from above, showing both slopes of the lid and the two coats of arms. Photo: Victoria and Albert Museum, London.

alt: Back view of the same casket. On the rear slope of the lid, Saint Elizabeth lies in a bed hung with red curtains at the left; a woman in a pale green dress and cap leans toward her, the Virgin in a blue mantle holds the swaddled infant John, and two women with white head-cloths follow; the bed's coverlet, striped in red with gold scrolls, fills the right half. Gothic inscriptions above name Saint Elizabeth and the Virgin Mary. On the back of the box, beneath a painted arcade, eight half-length saints stand side by side: an old bearded saint in red, a bearded saint in blue and white, a young saint in green with a book, an old bearded saint in red writing in a green book, Saint Christopher with the Christ Child on his shoulder and a palm, Saint Anthony Abbot in a dark habit, a mitred bishop in red and a crowned pope in green. A Gothic inscription below names several of them.
caption: The same casket, back, with the Birth of Saint John the Baptist on the lid. Photo: Victoria and Albert Museum, London.

alt: End view of the casket: on the triangular end of the lid, two half-length angels support a shield charged with three fishes in pale, under a red chief bearing a mitre, crossed keys and a crozier; on the end of the box, three half-length bearded saints with gold haloes under a painted arcade, one of them holding a book. The inventory number 351-64 is painted at the lower right.
caption: The same casket, end, with the arms of a bishop, probably of the Baisi family, on the lid and three unidentified saints. Photo: Victoria and Albert Museum, London.

alt: The other end of the casket: on the triangular end of the lid, two angels support the same coat of arms with mitre, crossed keys and crozier; on the end of the box, three haloed half-length figures under a painted arcade, the central one in a blue and red mantle between two bearded saints in green and white.
caption: The same casket, other end, with the arms repeated on the lid and three unidentified saints. Photo: Victoria and Albert Museum, London.

alt: Triptych-shaped panel in its moulded frame, with three standing saints on gold ground, each under a pointed, crocketed arch carried on twisted colonnettes. At the left Saint Benedict, white-bearded and tonsured, in a dark brown habit, holds a red book bound with metal clasps; his halo is inscribed 'S. Benedictus'. In the centre Pope Sixtus II, wearing a tall gold tiara and a red cope with blue and gold orphreys fastened by a large lozenge-shaped gold morse over a white alb, raises his gloved right hand in blessing and holds an open book with Gothic script; his halo is inscribed 'S. Sistus'. At the right Saint Proculus, young and bearded, in a white fur cap, a green tunic, a pink mantle lined in blue and red hose, holds a palm in his left hand and gathers his mantle with his right; his halo is inscribed 'S. Proculus'.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Saints Benedict, Sixtus II and Proculus, c. 1385–1390, tempera and gold on panel. Bologna, Museo di Santo Stefano. Inscribed with the saints' names on the haloes.

alt: Damaged rectangular panel, its unpainted wooden margins worn and worm-eaten, crossed by several vertical splits. The painted field is divided into two scenes on gold ground. At the left, the Crucifixion: Christ hangs on the cross, with the Virgin in a dark mantle at the left, her hand to her cheek, the Magdalen in a red mantle over a blue dress kneeling and embracing the foot of the cross, and Saint John in a green tunic and a pink mantle at the right, his hands clasped. At the right, the Coronation of the Virgin: under a blue starry canopy held up by a crowd of haloed angels, before a red cloth of honour patterned in gold, Christ in a light blue tunic and a pink mantle places a crown on the head of the Virgin, who sits beside him in a dark blue-green mantle over a pink dress, her hands joined in prayer. Along the bottom runs a narrow frieze of thirteen half-length haloed figures: Christ among the twelve apostles.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", The Crucifixion; The Coronation of the Virgin; Christ between the Twelve Apostles, c. 1385–1390, tempera and gold on panel, 56.9 × 66.7 cm (painted surface 49.4 × 59.3 cm). New Haven, Yale University Art Gallery, 1959.15.3; gift of Hannah D. and Louis M. Rabinowitz; formerly Gozzadini collection, Bologna.

alt: Black-and-white photograph of two hinged rectangular panels set side by side, each divided by a moulded frame into three tiers of arched compartments, with empty round and square cavities in the frame. Left panel, top: the Resurrection, Christ stepping from the tomb with a cross banner above a sleeping soldier, and the Ascension, the Virgin and the apostles kneeling and looking up at the feet of Christ disappearing into a cloud. Middle: the Death of the Virgin, the Virgin lying on a bier covered with striped cloth, surrounded by apostles, one reading from a book and one holding a palm, with a small figure among angels above. Bottom: Saints Margaret, with a cross and a dragon at her feet, and Christina, her hands joined; Saint Ursula holding a cross banner among her maidens. Right panel, top: Pentecost, the Virgin seated among the apostles in a polygonal enclosure under a tiled roof. Middle: four standing saints, three deacons with books, one of them with a palm, and a Dominican friar with a blade in his head. Bottom: the Last Judgement, Christ in a rayed mandorla showing his wounds, with the Virgin and Saint John the Baptist kneeling before a crowd of saints.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", New Testament and Apocryphal Scenes with Saints, 1360–1369, tempera and gold leaf on panel, two panels, overall 54.93 × 52.23 cm (right panel 54.93 × 26.04 cm; left panel 54.93 × 25.72 cm). Baltimore, Walters Art Museum, 37.723; acquired by Henry Walters with the Massarenti Collection, 1902.

alt: Small portable triptych with pointed gables and moulded wooden frames, the wings hinged to the centre. In the central panel the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle over a gold-patterned dress, sits on a throne hung with a red cloth and holds the Child on her left arm; the Child, in a gold-orange tunic, turns to look up at her. At the left Saint John the Baptist, barefoot in a brown garment, gestures towards the Virgin and holds a long scroll inscribed in Gothic letters; at the right Saint James, in an orange mantle, holds a book and a slender pilgrim's staff. In the left wing, above, a crowned young female saint holds a book, and below a crowned, bearded king in a red mantle holds a book. In the right wing, above, a bearded saint in a red mantle holds a closed book in both hands, and below a mitred bishop in a gold cope with a red morse holds a crozier and a book; a partly legible inscription runs beneath his feet.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Madonna and Child Enthroned between Saints John the Baptist and James; wings: Saint Ursula and Saint Louis IX of France (left), an Evangelist (?) and Saint Blaise (right), portable triptych, tempera and gold on panel, 46 × 47 cm. Parma, Complesso Monumentale della Pilotta, Galleria Nazionale, GN 427; GN 433. Provenance unknown; inventoried in 1887. The museum's record dates the work to the first half of the fourteenth century; its catalogue entry suggests the late 1370s or early 1380s.

alt: Small panel on gold ground in a gilded frame. At the right, before a pink hut with a thatched roof, the Virgin in a dark green mantle over a pale dress sits on a stone seat and holds the naked Child on her knee; with her left hand she passes a golden cup to Saint Joseph, who stands at the far right in a white habit and dark cap, leaning on a staff. At the centre the eldest king, in a voluminous red mantle, kneels and bows his head to the Child's feet. Behind him the second king, bearded and crowned, in a white robe, raises one hand towards the sky, and the youngest king, crowned and beardless, in red brocade, holds a golden cup. Two young attendants stand at the far left before a rocky hill with trees. At the top a group of angels flies on a cloud, and the faint outline of a lobed arch is visible in the gold.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi" (attributed), The Adoration of the Magi, tempera on panel. Piacenza, Musei Civici di Palazzo Farnese, Rizzi-Vaccari collection; donated by Mariapia and Augusto Rizzi, 2006. Regional catalogue no. D0000094. Dated by the record within Simone's documented activity, 1355–1399.

alt: Five painted and gilded wooden statues set in a row against a black background. At the far left Saint Joseph, bearded, in a dark blue robe and a broad flat halo, joins his hands in prayer. Next to him the Virgin, seated on a block-like throne, wears a red-lined gold mantle over a blue dress scattered with gold stars and holds the curly-haired Child on her knee; the Child turns towards the kneeling king. At the centre the eldest king, bareheaded, with long grey hair and beard, kneels in profile in a gold robe patterned with dark lattice and quatrefoils, offering an open round gold vessel. At the right stand the two other kings, crowned: a bearded king in a gold tunic with a jewelled belt, a green cloak lined with red, holding a gift shaped like a small building and raising his right hand, and a young king with a short beard in a red mantle over a gold robe, holding a tall covered vessel.
caption: Bolognese sculptor, with polychromy by Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", The Adoration of the Magi (Saint Joseph, the Virgin and Child, and the three kings), c. 1360–1380, lime and elm wood, carved, painted and gilded. Bologna, complex of Santo Stefano, church of the Trinità, chapel of San Martino; originally in the chapel of the Magi under Bolognini patronage in the same church. Regional catalogue no. 08 00054406.

alt: Large cross with moulded gilt edges and stepped, rectangular terminals, painted dark blue-green along the arms and the upright, with a light gilded panel behind the body. Applied to it is a carved and painted wooden figure of Christ, crowned, with a large round halo carved with rays, long hair falling on his shoulders and a short forked beard; his head is slightly bowed, his eyes lowered, his arms stretched almost horizontally, and his hands nailed. He wears a long loincloth with fine vertical pleats, knotted at the waist and falling below the knee on one side; his feet are crossed and pierced by a single nail. At the top a white tablet carries the inscription I·N·R·I. In the left terminal the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle over a red dress, rests her cheek on her hand; in the right terminal Saint John, in a pink mantle, leans his head on his hand.
caption: Anonymous sculptor, Crucified Christ, painted wood (thirteenth century?), mounted on a painted cross with the mourning Virgin and Saint John by Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", tempera and gold on panel, second half of the fourteenth century. Bologna, Collezioni Comunali d'Arte (Palazzo d'Accursio).

alt: Small upright panel in an elaborate carved frame, its gilding darkened, with a round arch, a pointed gable, crockets, foliate finials and small pinnacles at the sides. In three lobed medallions set in the frame: Christ blessing and holding an open book at the top, the angel of the Annunciation at the left and the Virgin Annunciate at the right. Under the gable a pelican feeds her young in a nest above the cross. The Crucifixion fills the arched field on gold ground: Christ on a tall cross, his head bowed; the two thieves, small, bound to their crosses at the upper left and right. At the lower left the Virgin swoons, supported by Saint John in a pale robe and by a holy woman; the Magdalen in red kneels at the foot of the cross. Mounted soldiers on a white and a brown horse crowd behind; at the right a bearded man in a red hat raises his hand towards Christ, a woman in blue prays, and in the foreground soldiers crouch to divide the robe of Christ.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", The Crucifixion, with Christ blessing, the Annunciation and the Pelican in its Piety, fourteenth century, paint on wood panel, 62.9 × 33.7 × 3.5 cm (overall). Detroit, Detroit Institute of Arts, 61.349; bequest of Mrs. Lillian Henkel Haass; formerly Achillito Chiesa collection, Milan.

alt: Small gilded triptych with carved crockets along the gables and pointed arches. In the central panel the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle over a pink dress, sits on a throne whose red brocade cloth is held up by two angels; she holds the Child, partly wrapped in a transparent veil, on her lap, and the Child reaches towards a young saint in a pink mantle who stands at the right holding a palm. In the gable above, the Man of Sorrows rises from the tomb. Left wing: the angel of the Annunciation kneeling in the gable, Saint Peter in half-length with keys and book, and below a bearded saint in a red mantle kneeling in a rocky landscape, praying towards a small dark winged form beside a red radiant sun. Right wing: the Virgin Annunciate in the gable, Saint Paul in half-length with sword and book, and below Saint Jerome in a dark habit seated at his desk, tending the paw of a lion, his red cardinal's hat hanging above.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Madonna and Child with Saints, portable triptych, 1370–1380, tempera on wood panels, 38.7 × 32.7 cm (sight); 52.4 × 45.4 × 7.3 cm (frame). Athens (Georgia), Georgia Museum of Art, University of Georgia, 1961.1895; The Samuel H. Kress Study Collection, K1201. Photo: Georgia Museum of Art.

alt: Tall rectangular panel in a carved frame painted green and gilded, with twisted colonnettes at the sides and a round arch with a stepped, ribbed soffit. Within the arch, two rows of haloed angel heads, sixteen in all, wearing small pointed blue-and-white caps, crowd above a rainbow-coloured arc; beneath it a dark blue canopy with gold stars and a green border hangs over a red cloth of honour patterned in gold. Christ, crowned, long-haired and bearded, in a light blue tunic with a gold belt and a pink mantle lined with yellow, sits at the right holding a sceptre ending in a fleur-de-lis and with his right hand sets a crown on the head of the Virgin. She sits at the left, bowing, her arms crossed on her breast, in a white veil and a dark blue mantle brocaded with gold over a lilac dress. A grey step runs along the bottom.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", The Coronation of the Virgin, c. 1380–1385, tempera and gold on panel, 110.5 × 55.3 cm. Newark (Delaware), Alana Collection. Formerly Count of Turin, Turin; William Randolph Hearst, New York; Walter P. Chrysler Jr. Photo: The Alana Collection.

alt: Small gilded triptych with an elaborate openwork frame of pointed gables, pinnacles and leafy finials, standing on a low base painted with ornament. In the central panel the Virgin, in half-length, wears a dark mantle patterned with gold over a red dress and holds the naked Child, who raises one arm and turns towards her; above them, under a pointed arch, the Man of Sorrows rises in half-length from the tomb before the cross, his arms resting on its edge. In the gables of the wings, the angel of the Annunciation at the left and the Virgin Annunciate at the right. Below them, under pointed arches, stand Saint Peter in a red mantle holding the keys at the left and Saint Paul in a blue tunic and red mantle holding a red book at the right.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Triptych: the Virgin and Child, the Man of Sorrows, the Annunciation and Saints Peter and Paul, c. 1390–1395, tempera with gold leaf on wood panel, 60.2 × 47.3 cm (overall). Austin, Blanton Museum of Art, The University of Texas at Austin, The Suida-Manning Collection, 2017.1372. Photo: Blanton Museum of Art, The University of Texas at Austin.

alt: Early twentieth-century black-and-white photograph of a fresco fragment. The Virgin, in half-length, wears a dark veil and mantle over a dark dress; her head is tilted to her left, her eyes look down and sideways, and her hands are joined in prayer before her breast. Light streaks radiate across the background around her, and the lower part of the image fades into a pale, worn area. A crack runs down from the upper left, and at the upper right and lower corners appear fragments of a beaded border.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi" (attributed), The Virgin in Prayer, 1370 (?), fresco. Bologna, former Certosa, now Cimitero Monumentale, Chiostrino delle Madonne. Photograph, first quarter of the twentieth century: Ministero della Pubblica Istruzione photographic archive, MPI137997.

alt: Small gilded triptych with pointed gables and plain moulded frames. In the central panel the Virgin, in a deep blue mantle edged with gold over a pink dress, sits on a broad throne hung with a red cloth patterned in gold, held up at the top by two angels; two more angels stand at the sides of the throne. She holds on her knee the Child, partly wrapped in a yellow cloth, who reaches towards her breast. A patch of blue sky with golden rays fills the apex of the gable. On the step of the throne is the inscription symon pincxit. In the left wing the angel of the Annunciation kneels in the gable; below stands a white-bearded bishop in a red cope and white vestments, blessing and holding a crozier. In the right wing the Virgin Annunciate sits reading at a lectern before a red hanging; below stands a nun in a white wimple and black habit, holding a string of coloured beads ending in a small cross.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", Triptych: the Virgin and Child Enthroned with Angels; the Annunciation; a Saint Bishop and a Nun, 1380–1390, tempera on panel, central panel 64 × 27 cm, wings 63 × 13.2 cm and 63.2 × 13.5 cm. Signed on the step of the throne: SYMON PINXIT. Rome, Gallerie Nazionali di Arte Antica, Palazzo Barberini, inv. 1537 (F.N. 14891). Formerly Ferrara, Costabili collection; acquired from Sangiorgi, 1912; on deposit at the Museo di Palazzo Venezia from 1927.

alt: Tall panel with a lowered arched top cut into small scallops, on gold ground. The Virgin, in half-length to the knees, sits on a throne whose back is edged with a dark band of ornament and a red border. She wears a transparent white veil over her head and neck and a mantle covered with gold patterns over a green dress with embroidered gold bands. She looks out towards the viewer, her head slightly inclined, and holds the Child on her left knee. The Child, curly-haired, wrapped in a transparent white cloth, turns his face up towards her and touches his chest with his right hand. Losses and old fillings are visible along the edges and at the bottom.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", The Madonna della Vittoria (Virgin and Child), c. 1355–1360 (catalogue: c. 1340–1360), egg tempera and gold on panel, 90 × 45 cm. Bologna, church of the Santissimo Salvatore, third chapel on the right; formerly in the church of the Madonna del Monte. State property, Fondo Edifici di Culto.

alt: Small gabled triptych in a carved and gilded frame crowned with large crockets of curling leaves, much worn and with losses. In the central panel, under a pointed arch with twisted colonnettes, the Virgin, in a blue mantle over a pink dress, sits enthroned against a red cloth and holds the naked Child, who reaches up towards her face; small angel heads surround the throne. In the left wing the angel of the Annunciation kneels in the upper field, and below stands Saint John the Baptist in a camel-hair garment, holding an unrolled scroll. In the right wing the Virgin Annunciate sits with a book in the upper field, and below stands Saint Lawrence in a red dalmatic, holding a gridiron and a book.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi", and workshop, Triptych: the Virgin and Child Enthroned with Angels; Saint John the Baptist and the Angel of the Annunciation; Saint Lawrence and the Virgin Annunciate, c. 1390, tempera on panel, central panel 40 × 18 cm, wings 39 × 9 cm. Bologna, Collezioni Comunali d'Arte, Palazzo d'Accursio, Pelagio Palagi collection, inv. P71 (also 1299; Museo Civico 301).

alt: Severely ruined fresco fragment by Vitale da Bologna: at the upper left the Virgin lies asleep, her haloed head with loose blond hair resting on her joined hands against a white pillow, her body in a pale blue robe stretched diagonally across a red bed of which little more than the colour survives; around and beneath her run the traces of a walled town seen from above, with a rose tower and church front at the upper left, clustered white houses and tiled rooftops below the bed and further towers at the right, the whole reduced to islands of paint on bare plaster.
caption: Vitale da Bologna, The Dream of the Virgin, c. 1353–1355, fresco, detached and transferred to canvas; 114 × 155 cm and inv. 6347 according to the museum's online record, which has not been verified against the printed catalogues. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, Room 8; from the entrance wall of Santa Maria di Mezzaratta, lower left wing.

alt: Fragmentary fresco on a wall, its irregular edges surrounded by later plaster; above it, partly overlapping, a painted tablet with the date ANNO M·DC·XIX. A young woman with long curly blond hair and a faint halo sits against a dark blue ground, her head tilted to one side, eyes half closed and lips parted. She wears a long, loose greyish-brown dress that swells over her pregnant belly; her arms hang down and her hands rest open on her knees, and a closed book lies in her lap. At the left a small table on a slender stand carries a terracotta basin pierced with round holes. At the lower left a small furry animal raises its paws and grasps the hem of her dress.
caption: Simone di Filippo, called "dei Crocifissi" (attributed), or Vitale da Bologna, The Pregnant Virgin (Madonna del Parto, also called Madonna in meditazione or Madonna dell'attesa), c. 1350–1360, fresco, fragment, 80 × 58 cm. Bologna, Santa Maria dei Servi, ambulatory, first bay on the left. State property, Fondo Edifici di Culto.

alt: Arched panel painting on gold ground showing the Virgin in half length, her head inclined, wearing a very dark mantle densely streaked with fine gold hatching and edged with gold borders set with small lozenge ornaments, over a white veil and a red dress. With her right hand she holds the right hand of the Christ Child, who sits on her left arm, his body almost bare beneath a transparent veil and his hips and legs wrapped in a rose-pink cloth; he turns his curly head away to the right. The Virgin's halo is tooled with punched rings, and the Child's halo carries a cross of simulated gems. A moulded arch frames the figures, and trefoil ornaments decorate the darkened spandrels above; the sides and lower edge of the panel are cut and worn
caption: Simone Martini (attributed), Madonna and Child, c. 1305–1310, tempera and gold on panel, 88 × 57 cm. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale (inv. 583). Photo: Pinacoteca Nazionale di Siena, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Gabled panel painting on gold ground showing the Virgin standing frontally at monumental scale, her face severe and her gaze fixed straight ahead. She wears a long red gown girdled by a braided cord whose tasselled ends hang to her knees, and a very dark mantle edged in gold that covers her head and spreads wide from her shoulders. With both hands she holds the mantle open at her sides, and beneath it, at a much smaller scale, crowds of devotees look up at her with joined hands: on the left mitred bishops, clerics and veiled women, on the right laymen, women with jewelled headdresses and a tonsured friar, with young men in long robes kneeling in the foreground. A painted frame with small four-leaf ornaments follows the gable and the sides
caption: Simone Martini (attributed), Madonna of Mercy (Madonna dei Raccomandati), first decade of the fourteenth century. Tempera and gold on panel, 154 × 88 cm. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale, on deposit from the parish church of San Bartolomeo at Vertine in Chianti. Attribution disputed: formerly given to Niccolò di Segna, also discussed in relation to the workshop of Memmo di Filippuccio. Photo: Pinacoteca Nazionale di Siena, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Large fresco framed by twisted-ribbon borders and ornamental side bands, showing the Virgin seated within a golden almond-shaped glory against a blue sky, with the dove of the Holy Spirit at the top. She wears a blue mantle lined in green over a white dress with small red motifs, and holds the Christ Child on her lap; he wears a rose-red cloak and grasps a small bird in one hand. Two angels hold a crown above her head. Tiers of angels fill both sides of the glory: those at the top pray with joined hands, others play portative organs, a fiddle, trumpets, a tambourine and pipes, two offer vases of flowers, and two angels in white kneel in prayer at the bottom
caption: Cenni di Francesco, Madonna in Glory, 1413, incorporating the face of the Virgin from an earlier fresco attributed to Simone Martini (c. 1310). Fresco. San Gimignano, church of San Lorenzo in Ponte, right wall of the former loggia. Photo: Chiesa di San Lorenzo in Ponte, San Gimignano, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Detail of a damaged fresco showing the head and shoulders of the Virgin against a golden ground streaked with dark radiating rays. Her oval face, with a long straight nose, small closed mouth and eyes turned slightly to the right, is framed by a reddish inner veil and a green mantle drawn over the head; below, a white dress embroidered with small red cross-shaped motifs and a blue mantle, heavily abraded at the lower left. Around the head is a large halo with incised rays and a red outer ring, partly broken away. At the top, two hands reach in from either side, holding up a largely lost crown above the halo
caption: Simone Martini (face of the Virgin, attributed), c. 1310, with repainting by Cenni di Francesco, 1413. Madonna in Glory, detail of the head. Fresco. San Gimignano, church of San Lorenzo in Ponte, right wall of the former loggia. Photo: Chiesa di San Lorenzo in Ponte, San Gimignano, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Wall-sized fresco within a broad painted frame of red and green foliate scrolls set with twenty medallions of prophets, evangelists and doctors of the Church, with Christ blessing at the top centre and a two-faced figure at the bottom centre, alternating with small roundels bearing the black-and-white arms of Siena and the lion of the People. In the centre, against a deep blue ground, the Virgin sits crowned on a tall openwork Gothic throne, holding the standing Christ Child, who unrolls a scroll. Above her stretches a great canopy of red fabric with a valance of blue, red, black and white heraldic panels, its poles held by apostles and saints. Some thirty saints and angels stand in tiers on either side, and in the foreground four patron saints of Siena kneel with two angels who offer bowls of flowers. Verses in vernacular run along the throne step and the lower edge of the scene
caption: Simone Martini, Maestà, completed June 1315, partly repainted by the artist in 1321. Fresco with applied materials, 763 × 970 cm. Siena, Palazzo Pubblico, Sala del Mappamondo (Sala del Consiglio), north wall. Photo: Museo Civico, Palazzo Pubblico, Siena, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Long horizontal fresco showing a mounted commander in profile riding to the left across a bare, ochre landscape under a deep blue sky. Both rider and horse are covered in matching golden cloth patterned with black lozenges and sprigs of green vine; the rider wears a soft cap and holds a baton of command. On the left, a walled hill town with tall towers rises above a winding road, enclosed below by a wooden palisade bristling with lances. On the right, a fortified enclosure with six towers flies a black-and-white banner beside a timber siege engine, and beyond it, on the slope, lies a military camp of white tents, lances and pennants. A border with small black-and-white shields runs along the bottom, with the inscription ANO DNI MCCCXXVIII at its centre
caption: Simone Martini (traditional attribution, disputed), Guidoriccio da Fogliano at the Siege of Montemassi, inscribed with the date 1328; usually connected with a payment of 1330. Fresco, 340 × 968 cm. Siena, Palazzo Pubblico, Sala del Mappamondo, west wall. Photo: Museo Civico, Palazzo Pubblico, Siena, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: View of the upper part of a frescoed wall. At the top, the long fresco of a horseman in a golden caparison with black lozenges riding between a hill town and a military camp, framed by a border with small shields and the date ANO DNI MCCCXXVIII. Below it, at the centre, a partly damaged earlier fresco shows a walled hill town with towers and a wooden palisade, and on the left two standing figures, one of whom, in a long robe with a sword at his side, appears partly effaced. This fresco is flanked by two sixteenth-century saints in painted classical niches: on the left St Ansanus baptising kneeling converts, on the right St Victor in Roman armour with a raised sword and putti. A large circular abrasion runs across the lower centre of the wall
caption: The west wall of the Sala del Mappamondo. Above: the Guidoriccio da Fogliano (traditionally attributed to Simone Martini). Below, centre: the fresco discovered during the restoration of 1979–80, with a castle and two figures (attribution and subject disputed). Left and right: Sodoma, St Ansanus and St Victor, 1530. The circular abrasions are usually connected with Ambrogio Lorenzetti's lost revolving map. Siena, Palazzo Pubblico. Photo: Museo Civico, Palazzo Pubblico, Siena, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Gabled altarpiece on gold ground with three arched compartments. In the centre, the Blessed Agostino Novello stands full length in the black habit of the Augustinian hermits, holding a red book in both hands, while a small winged angel at his right shoulder whispers into his ear; two slender trees with dark foliage, in which small birds perch, rise behind him. Two roundels in the spandrels above show bearded, white-haired holy men in dark habits holding books. Each side compartment contains two miracle scenes stacked one above the other: on the left, a child attacked by a wolf outside a walled town and a child falling from a broken balcony in a city street; on the right, a knight whose horse plunges into a mountain ravine and an infant who falls from a hanging cradle, followed by a procession of women with candles. In each scene the saint flies in from the sky to help
caption: Simone Martini, The Blessed Agostino Novello and Four of His Miracles, c. 1324. Tempera and gold on panel, 198 × 257 cm. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale, from the church of Sant'Agostino, Siena. Photo: Pinacoteca Nazionale di Siena, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Arched panel showing a walled town with crenellated walls, square towers and an open gate. The Blessed Agostino Novello, in a black habit and with a gold halo, swoops down from a greenish cloud beside a tall tower, his hand extended. In the foreground on the left, a black wolf seizes the head of a small child lying on the ground, bleeding, while an old woman bends over to pull the child free and a man in red raises a stick to strike the animal. On the right, the restored child sits between his kneeling mother and another woman in red, while two men stand behind with joined hands in prayer
caption: Simone Martini, The Blessed Agostino Novello Altarpiece: The Child Attacked by a Wolf, upper left scene, c. 1324. Tempera and gold on panel. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale. Photo: Pinacoteca Nazionale di Siena, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Square panel showing a narrow city street lined with pink houses, arched windows and a projecting wooden gallery supported on curved timber brackets. A woman leans out of the gallery with her hand to her head in alarm. A plank has broken away from the gallery and falls, and a small child tumbles headfirst towards a doorway. The Blessed Agostino Novello flies in diagonally from the upper left, trailing a dark cloud, and reaches towards the falling plank. On the right, the restored child stands among his family: a man with a white bandage round his head, a woman in a grey-green cloak holding out her hands, and others in prayer
caption: Simone Martini, The Blessed Agostino Novello Altarpiece: The Child Falling from a Balcony, lower left scene, c. 1324. Tempera and gold on panel. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale. Photo: Pinacoteca Nazionale di Siena, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Arched panel showing a steep mountain landscape of pale, jagged crags with small castles on distant peaks and dark trees on a green slope at the right. A horse in red trappings plunges head first down into a ravine, its rider tumbling with it. The Blessed Agostino Novello flies in from the upper right on a dark cloud, reaching out towards the fall. In the lower left foreground, the rescued knight kneels in a red cloak, his hands raised in thanksgiving, beside small plants growing from the rock
caption: Simone Martini, The Blessed Agostino Novello Altarpiece: The Knight Fallen into a Ravine, upper right scene, c. 1324. Tempera and gold on panel. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale. Photo: Pinacoteca Nazionale di Siena, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Square panel divided into two registers. Above, an interior with a large bed covered by a red coverlet patterned in white, and a cloth cradle hanging from cords above it. A woman seated on the bed throws out her arms in alarm; in a doorway another woman kneels in prayer with her hands joined. On a terrace at the right, a woman in a dark cloak bends over an infant lying on the ground with a bleeding head. The Blessed Agostino Novello appears at the upper right, holding a red book and stretching out his hand. Below, women walk in procession carrying candles: one in red holds a swaddled child, and two others in dark green and pink mantles follow. A staircase opens at the right
caption: Simone Martini, The Blessed Agostino Novello Altarpiece: The Child Fallen from a Cradle, lower right scene, c. 1324. Tempera and gold on panel. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale. Photo: Pinacoteca Nazionale di Siena, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Gold-ground altarpiece in an elaborate Gothic frame of gilded pinnacles, crocketed gables and twisted columns. In the wide central field, the Archangel Gabriel kneels on the left on a marbled floor, crowned with an olive wreath and holding an olive branch, his wings patterned like peacock feathers and his tartan-like cloak still fluttering behind him; the words of his greeting run in raised gold letters from his lips towards the Virgin. Between them stands a golden vase of white lilies. On the right, the Virgin, in a deep blue mantle over a red dress, sits on a throne, drawing her mantle to her chin with one hand and turning away in alarm, while her other hand holds a red book. Above, in the central arch, the dove of the Holy Spirit is surrounded by a ring of eight winged angels. In narrow side compartments stand Saint Ansanus on the left, in red, holding a black-and-white banner and a palm, and on the right a female saint in a grey-blue mantle holding a cross and a palm. Four small roundels of prophets with scrolls sit in the gables of the side compartments
caption: Simone Martini and Lippo Memmi, Annunciation with Saint Ansanus and a Female Martyr (Maxima, Margaret or Julitta?), signed and dated 1333. Tempera and gold on panel, 184 × 210 cm (184 × 168 cm in the Uffizi's online record), in a nineteenth-century frame incorporating the original inscription. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi, inv. 1890 nos. 451–453. From the altar of Sant'Ansano in the transept of Siena Cathedral. Photo: Gleb Simonov, Wikimedia Commons (CC0).

alt: Gabled altarpiece within a broad blue frame sown with raised gold fleurs-de-lis. On a gold ground, Saint Louis of Toulouse sits frontally on a throne draped with red cloths, wearing a jewelled mitre and a richly embroidered cope with heraldic borders over the grey-brown habit and knotted cord of a Franciscan friar. A large round morse closes the cope at his breast, and he holds a gilded crozier in his right hand. Two flying angels above hold a heavenly crown over his head, while with his left hand he lowers an earthly crown onto the head of his brother Robert, who kneels in profile at the right in a blue robe with gold borders, his hands joined. The throne stands on a dais over a patterned carpet. Below, a predella with five arched scenes from the saint's life runs the width of the panel
caption: Simone Martini, Saint Louis of Toulouse Crowning Robert of Anjou, c. 1317. Tempera and gold on panel, 250 × 188 cm overall (main panel 200 × 138 cm; predella 56 × 158 cm). Naples, Museo e Real Bosco di Capodimonte, from the church of San Lorenzo Maggiore, Naples. Signed on the predella SYMON DE SENIS ME PINXIT. Photo: Museo e Real Bosco di Capodimonte, Naples, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Long predella divided by slender gilded columns into five round-arched compartments, each containing a scene from the life of Saint Louis of Toulouse. From left to right: Louis kneeling before Pope Boniface VIII, who sits enthroned among cardinals; Louis taking the Franciscan habit and being consecrated bishop under an arcade; Louis serving the poor at a long table in a hall; the funeral of Louis, with his body laid out on a bier surrounded by friars and mourners; and a posthumous miracle in which a dead child is restored to life before a house. Letters of the painter's signature run along the upper edge, interrupted by small coats of arms
caption: Simone Martini, Saint Louis of Toulouse Crowning Robert of Anjou: predella with five scenes from the life of the saint, c. 1317. Tempera and gold on panel, 56 × 158 cm. Naples, Museo e Real Bosco di Capodimonte. Photo: Museo e Real Bosco di Capodimonte, Naples, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco showing a Gothic canopy of pale stone with a crocketed gable, pinnacles, trefoil tracery and slender columns with foliate capitals, set before a balustrade with pierced quatrefoils against a deep blue background. Beneath it, Saint Martin stands on the left in a yellow cope dotted with small dark motifs and a white mitre, his halo behind his head, holding a crozier. With his right hand he takes the hand of Cardinal Gentile Partino da Montefiore, who kneels on the right in a long pink cardinal's mantle, his tonsured head raised towards the saint and his other hand on his breast
caption: Simone Martini, The Dedication of the Chapel: Cardinal Gentile Partino da Montefiore Kneeling before Saint Martin, c. 1312–1318. Fresco. Assisi, Lower Church of San Francesco, Chapel of Saint Martin. Photo: Basilica di San Francesco, Assisi, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco showing two haloed saints standing in Gothic niches with trefoil arches, against a blue ground sown with gold fleurs-de-lis, separated by a slender twisted column. On the left, Saint Louis of France, young and crowned, with shoulder-length fair hair, wears a red mantle with gold borders over a tunic and holds a sceptre. On the right, Saint Louis of Toulouse wears the brown habit and knotted cord of a Franciscan friar and holds a tall crozier, a ring on his finger. The surface of the king's mantle is heavily abraded
caption: Simone Martini, Saint Louis of France and Saint Louis of Toulouse, c. 1317–1318. Fresco. Assisi, Lower Church of San Francesco, Chapel of Saint Martin. Photo: Basilica di San Francesco, Assisi, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco showing two haloed Franciscan saints standing in Gothic niches with trefoil arches against a blue ground, separated by a slender twisted column. On the left, Saint Anthony of Padua, young and tonsured, in a heavily abraded habit, holds a red book. On the right, Saint Francis, bearded, in a grey-brown habit with a knotted cord, raises his left hand to show the wound of the stigmata and with his right draws aside his habit to reveal the wound in his side; the wounds are also visible on his bare feet
caption: Simone Martini, Saint Anthony of Padua and Saint Francis, c. 1317–1318. Fresco. Assisi, Lower Church of San Francesco, Chapel of Saint Martin. Photo: Basilica di San Francesco, Assisi, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco showing two haloed female saints standing in Gothic niches with trefoil arches against a blue ground, separated by a slender twisted column. On the left, Mary Magdalene, with a white veil over her head, wears a pale robe with a rose and dark green mantle and holds up a tall covered ointment jar. On the right, Saint Catherine of Alexandria, with fair hair bound by a circlet, wears a pale rose mantle over a patterned dress and holds a palm of martyrdom and a small wheel
caption: Simone Martini, Saint Mary Magdalene and Saint Catherine of Alexandria, c. 1317–1318. Fresco. Assisi, Lower Church of San Francesco, Chapel of Saint Martin. Photo: Basilica di San Francesco, Assisi, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco showing two haloed female saints standing in Gothic niches with trefoil arches against a blue ground, separated by a slender twisted column. On the left, Saint Clare, in the dark veil, white wimple and grey-brown habit of a Poor Clare with a knotted cord, holds a stem of white lilies and looks towards her companion.
