On the right, Saint Elizabeth of Hungary, in profile, with braided fair hair bound by a circlet, wears a rose-red mantle patterned with dark and gold stripes over a white garment and a dark green cloak, and gathers up the folds of her mantle with one hand
caption: Simone Martini, Saint Clare and Saint Elizabeth of Hungary, c. 1317–1318. Fresco. Assisi, Lower Church of San Francesco, Chapel of Saint Martin. Photo: Basilica di San Francesco, Assisi, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco showing a young haloed knight in an orange cloak lined with ermine, mounted on a white horse that walks to the right in front of a pink city gate with towers. Turning back in the saddle, he cuts his cloak with a sword and hands half of it to a barefoot beggar in a ragged green tunic, who stands at the left by the gate, clutching the cloth and raising his face towards the knight. The background is a dark, abraded blue
caption: Simone Martini, The Division of the Cloak, c. 1312–1318. Fresco. Assisi, Lower Church of San Francesco, Chapel of Saint Martin. Photo: Basilica di San Francesco, Assisi, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco showing a large bed covered with a checked coverlet in orange, pink, green and blue, on a red wooden chest, in which the young haloed Martin sleeps with his head resting on his hand. Behind the bed, before a dark patterned curtain, Christ stands among a group of haloed angels with curling golden hair; he wears the half cloak in blue over a red tunic and turns his head towards the angels, pointing towards the sleeping Martin
caption: Simone Martini, The Dream of Saint Martin, c. 1312–1318. Fresco. Assisi, Lower Church of San Francesco, Chapel of Saint Martin. Photo: Basilica di San Francesco, Assisi, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco set in an arcaded loggia with a coffered ceiling and brackets. In the centre, the young haloed Martin stands in a pink robe with his hands raised, looking upwards, while a crowned man in a cream robe with a laurel wreath girds a sword round his waist and a kneeling servant in blue fastens a spur to his foot. At the right, musicians in striped and checked costumes play a double pipe and a lute; at the left, courtiers in checked dress watch, one holding a falcon and another holding a helmet on a staff
caption: Simone Martini, The Investiture of Saint Martin as a Knight, c. 1312–1318. Fresco. Assisi, Lower Church of San Francesco, Chapel of Saint Martin. Photo: Basilica di San Francesco, Assisi, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco showing a military camp among pale, faceted rocks under a blue sky. On the left, the laurel-crowned emperor sits on a folding chair before a white tent decorated with heraldic shields, holding a coin and distributing pay from a tray to soldiers in armour. In the centre, the young haloed Martin, in a red cloak over armour, stands turned away from the emperor, raising one hand and holding a small cross in the other. Beside him stands a soldier in a padded tunic and a tall fur-trimmed hat with a horse behind. On the right, beyond a rock, an enemy army with helmets, lances and shields bearing a lion rampant gathers before its own tents
caption: Simone Martini, The Renunciation of Arms, c. 1312–1318. Fresco. Assisi, Lower Church of San Francesco, Chapel of Saint Martin. Photo: Basilica di San Francesco, Assisi, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco showing a crowd gathered before a pale rock with a tree and a white bell tower against a blue sky. In the foreground, the haloed bishop Martin, in a yellow cope and white mitre, kneels with his back to the viewer before a dead child lying on a red patterned cloth on the ground. A kneeling woman with long hair reaches towards the child. Behind, men and women of different ages stand with joined hands or watch with intense expressions; several areas of the surface are abraded and grey
caption: Simone Martini, The Resurrection of a Child, c. 1312–1318. Fresco. Assisi, Lower Church of San Francesco, Chapel of Saint Martin. Photo: Basilica di San Francesco, Assisi, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Tall arched fresco showing a Gothic interior with ribbed vaults, a traceried window and a tiled floor. In the centre, the haloed bishop Martin sits on a folding chair in a blue cope with gold borders and a jewelled mitre, his eyes closed and his chin resting on his hand in deep meditation. Behind him, a cleric in a white surplice and gold stole lays a hand on his shoulder to rouse him. On the left, a young cleric in a blue cope kneels holding a book, looking up at the saint
caption: Simone Martini, The Meditation of Saint Martin, c. 1312–1318. Fresco. Assisi, Lower Church of San Francesco, Chapel of Saint Martin. Photo: Basilica di San Francesco, Assisi, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Tall arched fresco showing a chapel interior with a green wall and a dark vault. The haloed bishop Martin, in a gold chasuble, stands at an altar covered with an embroidered white cloth, raising the host above his head. Two winged angels fly in from the left and place a precious cloth on his bare arms. On the altar stand a chalice, a cross and an open missal. On the right, a cleric in a white surplice kneels holding a tall candle and looking up. Above, in the dark vault, a radiant sphere of light appears over the saint's head
caption: Simone Martini, The Miraculous Mass, c. 1312–1318. Fresco. Assisi, Lower Church of San Francesco, Chapel of Saint Martin. Photo: Basilica di San Francesco, Assisi, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco showing a palace interior with round arches below and a crenellated loggia above. On the left, the haloed bishop Martin, in a gold cope and mitre, raises his hand in blessing over the crowned emperor, who kneels before him in a dark green mantle and embraces him. A courtier watches from behind a column at the left. On the right, through another arch, an empty throne is engulfed in flames, and a figure leans in through a door behind it
caption: Simone Martini, The Miracle of Fire, c. 1312–1318. Fresco, 265 × 230 cm. Assisi, Lower Church of San Francesco, Chapel of Saint Martin. Photo: Basilica di San Francesco, Assisi, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco showing an arcaded interior with Corinthian columns and a loggia above, against a blue sky in which four haloed angels with red wings fly together at upper left. In the foreground, the haloed Martin lies dead on the ground in gold vestments, his head resting on a cloth. Clerics in gold and white vestments kneel around him, one bending over his body; a bishop reads from a book, a friar in a brown habit bows his head, and others stand with joined hands or look up towards the angels
caption: Simone Martini, The Death of Saint Martin, c. 1312–1318. Fresco. Assisi, Lower Church of San Francesco, Chapel of Saint Martin. Photo: Basilica di San Francesco, Assisi, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco showing a Gothic interior with tall traceried windows and slender twisted columns. In the foreground, the haloed body of Martin lies on a bier covered with a blue cloth sown with gold motifs, wearing a mitre and gold vestments. At the left, a haloed bishop in a mitre and cope blesses the body, assisted by clerics, one of whom swings a censer. Behind the bier stands a haloed figure in a red mantle with hands crossed. On the right, clerics in grey habits sing with open mouths and hold tall candles, and a boy in the foreground looks up at the foot of the bier
caption: Simone Martini, The Funeral of Saint Martin, c. 1312–1318. Fresco. Assisi, Lower Church of San Francesco, Chapel of Saint Martin. Photo: Basilica di San Francesco, Assisi, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Wide fresco on a gold ground richly tooled with punched floral patterns and a punched border, imitating the surface of a gold-ground panel. In the centre, the Virgin, crowned over a white veil and wrapped in a blue and red mantle, holds the Christ Child, who sits on her arm in a golden tunic, his red curly head turned to the right as he reaches towards the saint beside him. On the left stands a bearded crowned king in a dark cape over a blue and red garment, holding an orb and a sword. On the right stands a beardless young crowned king in a green mantle sprinkled with dark spots, holding an orb and a slender golden sceptre
caption: Simone Martini, Madonna and Child between Two Royal Saints (Stephen and Ladislaus of Hungary?), c. 1318–1322. Fresco, 110 × 200 cm. Assisi, Lower Church of San Francesco, right transept. Photo: Basilica di San Francesco, Assisi, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco showing two half-length haloed saints in separate rectangular fields with a blue-grey ground, divided by a narrow ornamental band. On the left, Saint Francis, bearded and tonsured, in a pale grey habit, turns to the right, touching his breast with one hand and showing the wound in his side through a tear in the habit; the wounds of the stigmata are visible on his hands. On the right, Saint Louis of Toulouse, young and beardless, wears a jewelled mitre and a pale yellow cope over a red garment, and holds a crozier diagonally across his body, a ring on his finger
caption: Simone Martini, Saint Francis and Saint Louis of Toulouse, c. 1318–1322. Fresco, 120 × 152 cm. Assisi, Lower Church of San Francesco, right transept. Photo: Basilica di San Francesco, Assisi, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco showing three half-length haloed saints in separate rectangular fields with a blue-grey ground, divided by narrow ornamental bands. On the left, a crowned young woman with braided fair hair, Saint Elizabeth of Hungary, wears a pale patterned mantle and raises both hands, gesturing towards the right. In the centre, a female saint in a white veil and a pale grey-brown mantle looks out frontally, holding a thin rod or arrow in one hand. On the right, a young beardless saint with long auburn hair, a faint crown drawn above his halo, wears a dark brown cloak over a red garment and holds a stem of lilies
caption: Simone Martini, Saint Elizabeth of Hungary, a Female Saint (Clare or Margaret of Hungary?) and a Young Royal Saint (Henry of Hungary?), c. 1318–1322. Fresco, 120 × 228 cm. Assisi, Lower Church of San Francesco, right transept. Photo: Basilica di San Francesco, Assisi, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small gabled panel with a pointed arch, its gold ground densely tooled with punched patterns that trace an inner arcade, a halo and vertical borders. Saint Ladislaus of Hungary stands frontally on a dark ground, crowned, with a short dark beard and shoulder-length hair. He wears a rose-pink mantle over a blue-green tunic, with a white lining visible at the sides, and a round morse bearing a red and white striped shield at his breast. With his right hand he holds a long-handled weapon diagonally across his body, and his left hand rests at his waist. The inscription S. LADICLAUS REX VGARIE is painted in two lines on either side of his head. A gilded bunch of grapes carved in relief fills the top of the gable
caption: Simone Martini (attributed), Saint Ladislaus of Hungary, c. 1326–1328 (dating debated). Tempera and gold on panel, 45.5 × 21.5 cm. Altomonte (Cosenza), Museo Civico di Santa Maria della Consolazione, from the church of Santa Maria della Consolazione. Inscribed S. LADICLAUS REX VGARIE. Photo: Museo Civico di Santa Maria della Consolazione, Altomonte, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Round-arched panel on a gold ground, set in a dark frame decorated with small gold flame motifs and a base inscribed S. ANTONIUS DE PADUA. The Virgin, in half length, wears a very dark blue-green mantle over a red dress, its border edged in gold; her head inclines towards the Child, and her face is long and pale with heavy-lidded eyes. The Child sits on her arm in an orange tunic and a rose-pink mantle, with a pale green sash tied at his waist; he looks out at the viewer and holds a small goldfinch in his left hand, while the Virgin's right hand supports his foot. Both haloes are richly tooled with punched patterns
caption: Simone Martini, Madonna and Child, central panel of the polyptych of Sant'Agostino, San Gimignano, c. 1316–1317. Tempera and gold on poplar, 79.5 × 57 cm (dimensions as given by the museum). Cologne, Wallraf-Richartz-Museum & Fondation Corboud, WRM 0880, gift of the State of North Rhine-Westphalia, 1961. Photo: Raimond Spekking, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Three gabled panels in a modern gilded frame, each with a half-length saint under a round arch on a gold ground and a half-length angel in the gable above. On the left, Saint Geminianus, an elderly bearded bishop in a jewelled mitre, red chasuble and white gloves, holds a crozier and a green book. In the centre, the Archangel Michael, with red-gold hair, a jewel on his brow and folded wings, holds a sword upright and a pair of scales in which a tiny figure of a soul sits in one pan. On the right, Saint Augustine, a bearded bishop in a jewelled mitre and a patterned white and gold cope over the black habit of his order, holds a crozier and a red book. The three angels above wear robes of red, blue, green and pink
caption: Simone Martini and workshop, Saints Geminianus, Michael and Augustine, each with an Angel above, lateral panels of the polyptych of Sant'Agostino, San Gimignano, c. 1316–1320. Tempera and gold on panel, each panel about 110.5 × 38.3 cm. Cambridge, The Fitzwilliam Museum, no. 552. Image © The Fitzwilliam Museum, Cambridge.

alt: Large gold-ground polyptych of seven arched compartments, each crowned by a register of two small saints under arcades and by a triangular gable with a prophet, above a long predella. In the tall central compartment, the Virgin in a blue mantle holds the Christ Child, who reaches up to her veil; above her are two archangels and, in the central gable, Christ blessing with an open book. In the side compartments, from left to right, stand Saint Dominic with a lily and a book, Saint John the Evangelist with a green book, Mary Magdalene with an ointment jar, Saint Catherine of Alexandria crowned with a palm and a book, Saint John the Baptist in a red mantle over a camel-skin garment, and Saint Peter Martyr in the Dominican habit with a palm. Above them are the apostles in pairs, and in the gables David, Moses and the prophets. The predella shows fifteen half-length saints under arcades, with the Man of Sorrows in the tomb at the centre between the Virgin and Saint Mark
caption: Simone Martini, Polyptych of Santa Caterina, c. 1319–1320. Tempera and gold on panel, c. 195 × 340 cm. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo, from the high altar of the Dominican church of Santa Caterina. Signed SYMON DE SENIS ME PINXIT. Photo: Miguel Hermoso Cuesta, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Panel with a half-length figure of Saint Dominic under a gilded trefoil arch on a gold ground. He wears the black mantle and white habit of the Dominican order, with a narrow tonsure of brown hair, and inclines his head slightly to the left with a gentle, thoughtful expression. In his right hand he holds a long stem of lilies, its flowers now darkened, and with his left he holds open a book whose pages carry a few lines of Gothic script. A small star is incised in the gold to the right of his halo
caption: Simone Martini, Polyptych of Santa Caterina: Saint Dominic, c. 1319–1320. Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Miguel Hermoso Cuesta, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Panel with a half-length figure of Saint John the Evangelist under a gilded trefoil arch on a gold ground, framed by slender twisted colonnettes. He is young and beardless, with red-gold curling hair, and looks to the right with a serious expression. He wears a blue tunic with an embroidered neckline and a red mantle with a gold border draped over one shoulder, and holds a green book sprinkled with small gold rosettes, its pages slightly open to show a red initial
caption: Simone Martini, Polyptych of Santa Caterina: Saint John the Evangelist, c. 1319–1320. Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Miguel Hermoso Cuesta, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Panel with a half-length figure of Mary Magdalene under a gilded trefoil arch on a gold ground. She is wrapped in a red mantle drawn over her head and edged with a narrow gold border, over a dark blue-green dress, with a small gold motif on her shoulder. Her face, inclined to the right, is pale and melancholy, with heavy-lidded eyes glancing sideways. In her raised left hand she holds a small round ointment jar with a domed lid, painted in veined cream and ochre like alabaster, and her right hand rests on the folds of her mantle at her waist
caption: Simone Martini, Polyptych of Santa Caterina: Mary Magdalene, c. 1319–1320. Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Miguel Hermoso Cuesta, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Central panel with a half-length Virgin and Child under a gilded trefoil arch on a gold ground. The Virgin wears a deep blue mantle edged with gold over a white veil and a red dress, with small gold stars on her forehead and shoulder; her long face is inclined towards the Child. The Child, with red curling hair, sits on her left arm in a pale yellow tunic, his legs wrapped in a red mantle with a gold-embroidered border. He reaches with his right hand to grasp the edge of his mother's mantle and holds a small red book in his left. The Virgin's long fingers support his foot
caption: Simone Martini, Polyptych of Santa Caterina: The Virgin and Child, central panel, c. 1319–1320. Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Signed on the frame below SYMON DE SENIS ME PINXIT. Photo: Miguel Hermoso Cuesta, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Panel with a half-length figure of Saint Catherine of Alexandria under a gilded trefoil arch on a gold ground. She wears a gold crown with fleur-de-lis points set with pearls and stones over braided red-gold hair, and looks sideways to the left with a grave expression. Her mantle is a rich gold brocade patterned with small lozenges and shaded in dark blue, edged with jewelled borders in relief, over a red dress, with a white fur collar fastened by a jewelled brooch. She holds a long palm of martyrdom against her shoulder and a red book with clasps against her waist
caption: Simone Martini, Polyptych of Santa Caterina: Saint Catherine of Alexandria, c. 1319–1320. Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Miguel Hermoso Cuesta, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Panel with a half-length figure of Saint John the Baptist under a gilded trefoil arch on a gold ground. He has long, dark, unkempt hair and a full beard, and looks straight out with a stern expression. He wears a garment of grey-white camel hair, painted in long wavy strands and tied at the waist with a red belt, under a red mantle knotted at the chest. His right hand is raised with the forefinger pointing upward, and his left hand rests at his waist. A thin cross-staff, now visible only as a red outline, rises behind his shoulder against the gold
caption: Simone Martini, Polyptych of Santa Caterina: Saint John the Baptist, c. 1319–1320. Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Miguel Hermoso Cuesta, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Panel with a half-length figure of Saint Peter Martyr under a gilded trefoil arch on a gold ground. He wears the black mantle and white habit of the Dominican order, with a tonsure of brown hair, and a thin red wound is visible at the top of his head. His face, with a short dark beard, is inclined to the left with a sombre, melancholy expression. In his right hand he holds a long green palm of martyrdom, and with his left he holds a red book with a gold-patterned border against his habit
caption: Simone Martini, Polyptych of Santa Caterina: Saint Peter Martyr, c. 1319–1320. Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Miguel Hermoso Cuesta, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Predella panel with three half-length figures under gilded trefoil arches on a gold ground. In the centre, the dead Christ, naked to the waist, stands in a tomb lined with green marble, his head bowed and eyes closed, his arms crossed over a white shroud, with the wound in his side and the marks of the nails visible. On the left, the Virgin in a deep blue mantle edged with gold, a small star on her shoulder, looks towards him with a sorrowful expression, one hand raised to her breast. On the right, Saint Mark, bearded, in a red mantle over a blue tunic, holds a quill and an open book, with the head of his lion beside him
caption: Simone Martini, Polyptych of Santa Caterina, predella: The Man of Sorrows between the Virgin and Saint Mark, c. 1319–1320. Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Miguel Hermoso Cuesta, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Predella panel with two half-length figures under gilded trefoil arches on a gold ground. On the left, a bearded pope wears a tall conical tiara of woven gold set with a jewelled crown, a red chasuble and a white pallium marked with black crosses; he blesses with his gloved right hand and holds a green book. On the right, a bearded saint with short brown hair, in a purple mantle over a blue tunic, holds a quill in one hand and an open book in the other, looking towards the left
caption: Simone Martini, Polyptych of Santa Caterina, predella: A Sainted Pope (Gregory the Great?) and an Evangelist, c. 1319–1320. Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Miguel Hermoso Cuesta, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Predella panel with two half-length figures under gilded trefoil arches on a gold ground. On the left, a young beardless deacon with short tonsured hair wears a pale yellow dalmatic with gold-embroidered collar and cuffs and holds a red book against his chest. On the right, a female saint wrapped in a red mantle drawn over her head, with a blue dress fastened by a gold quatrefoil brooch, looks out frontally; with one hand she gathers her mantle and with the other she holds a large dark key with a ring-shaped bow
caption: Simone Martini, Polyptych of Santa Caterina, predella: A Deacon Saint and a Female Saint with a Key, c. 1319–1320. Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Miguel Hermoso Cuesta, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Predella panel with two half-length figures under gilded trefoil arches on a gold ground. On the left, a bearded saint with grey hair, without a mitre, wears a pale blue-grey chasuble with a broad gold orphrey set with red and blue jewels over a silver-grey garment, and holds a red book in his gloved hands; a thin line behind his shoulder may be part of a staff. On the right, a female saint wears a jewelled band over a reddish headdress, a white wimple and a blue mantle over a deep red dress; she gathers a white cloth over her arm and holds up a small dark two-handled jar
caption: Simone Martini, Polyptych of Santa Caterina, predella: A Saint in Chasuble and a Female Saint with an Ointment Jar, c. 1319–1320. Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Miguel Hermoso Cuesta, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Predella panel with two half-length figures under gilded trefoil arches on a gold ground. On the left, Saint Agnes, with auburn hair bound by a jewelled crown, wears a pale rose mantle with a dark lining over a blue dress and a jewelled collar; her head inclines to the left and she holds an octagonal black medallion on which a white lamb with a halo carries a banner with a red cross. On the right, a beardless bishop saint in a jewelled white mitre and a pale yellow chasuble with a gold orphrey set with red stones holds a crozier and a red book in his gloved hands
caption: Simone Martini, Polyptych of Santa Caterina, predella: Saint Agnes and a Bishop Saint, c. 1319–1320. Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Miguel Hermoso Cuesta, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Predella panel with two half-length figures under gilded trefoil arches on a gold ground. On the left, a young crowned saint with fair hair wears a jewelled crown with pearls, a deep red mantle over a dark red garment with a jewelled cross-shaped orphrey, and holds up a red banner with a white band. On the right, a young beardless deacon saint with short brown hair wears a rose-coloured dalmatic patterned with small motifs and edged with embroidered borders, and holds a pale blue book against his chest
caption: Simone Martini, Polyptych of Santa Caterina, predella: A Crowned Martyr with a Banner (Ursula?) and a Deacon Saint, c. 1319–1320. Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Miguel Hermoso Cuesta, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Predella panel with two half-length figures under gilded trefoil arches on a gold ground. On the left, a stout tonsured Dominican friar in a black mantle over a white habit, Saint Thomas Aquinas, looks out frontally with a heavy face and holds an open book inscribed in Gothic script, from which golden rays radiate across his dark mantle. On the right, a bearded bishop saint in a jewelled mitre and a blue chasuble with a richly patterned gold orphrey holds a crozier and a red book in his gloved hands
caption: Simone Martini, Polyptych of Santa Caterina, predella: Saint Thomas Aquinas and a Bishop Saint, c. 1319–1320. Tempera and gold on panel. Pisa, Museo Nazionale di San Matteo. Photo: Miguel Hermoso Cuesta, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small rectangular panel in an engaged gilded frame. Against a gold ground bordered by bands of punched lozenge and quatrefoil patterns, the Virgin is shown in half length in a deep blue mantle edged with gold over a white veil and a red dress, a gold star on her shoulder. Her long pale face inclines towards the Child, who sits on her left arm in a pale blue tunic, a rose-pink mantle wrapped round his legs, and grasps a fold of the pink cloth at his chest while looking out at the viewer. The Virgin's long fingers support his feet. Below, a narrow predella of five arches on twisted colonnettes contains tiny full-length figures: a crowned female saint holding a cross, a bearded saint with a sword, a Dominican friar with a lily and a red book, a deacon in a red dalmatic with a book, and a kneeling nun in a black habit with her hands raised in prayer
caption: Simone Martini (and Lippo Memmi?), Virgin and Child over Saints Helen, Paul, Dominic, Stephen (?) and a Dominican Nun, c. 1325–1330. Tempera and tooled gold on panel, 33.4 × 25.4 × 4.4 cm with engaged frame (painted surface 28.4 × 20.1 cm). Boston, Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, P30w8. Possibly from the convent of San Paolo, Orvieto. Photo: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, Boston (gardnermuseum.org).

alt: Five-part gabled polyptych on gold ground, each panel framed by twisted colonnettes under a trefoil arch and crowned by a triangular pinnacle. In the taller central panel, the Virgin in a dark blue-green mantle over a red dress holds the Christ Child, who wears a pink tunic and a red mantle and reaches up to touch her chin, while she holds a small spray of white flowers. In the pinnacle above, Christ shows his wounds and raises his hand in blessing. In the side panels, from left to right, stand Saint Paul with a sword and a green book, Saint Lucy veiled in a blue mantle sown with gold stars, Saint Catherine of Alexandria crowned, with an ermine collar, a palm, a book and her wheel, and Saint John the Baptist in a red mantle over a camel skin, pointing upward and holding a cross-staff. Angels in the side pinnacles blow trumpets or hold the instruments of the Passion. Blue bands at the base carry the names of the saints and the words AVE MARIA GRATIA PLENA
caption: Simone Martini and workshop, Virgin and Child with Saints Paul, Lucy, Catherine of Alexandria and John the Baptist, c. 1320–1325. Gold and tempera on panel, 131 × 274.3 cm overall (central panel 99 × 60.7 cm without pinnacle; side panels about 86.3 × 42.5 cm each). Boston, Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, P15e4.1-5. From the church of Santa Maria dei Servi, Orvieto. Photo: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, Boston (gardnermuseum.org).

alt: Tall gabled panel in a gilded frame with twisted colonnettes. In the triangular pinnacle, Christ appears in half length against the gold, his chest bare and a red mantle over one shoulder, raising his right hand in blessing and showing the wound in his left hand. Below, under a trefoil arch, the Virgin in half length wears a very dark blue mantle over a white veil and a red dress, a small star on her shoulder; she inclines her head and holds a small spray of white flowers. The Child, in a pink tunic and a red mantle, sits on her left arm, looks up into her face and reaches up to touch her chin. A blue band at the base carries the inscription AVE MARIA GRATIA PLENA in gold letters
caption: Simone Martini, Polyptych of Santa Maria dei Servi: The Virgin and Child, with the Blessing Christ in the pinnacle, c. 1320–1325. Tempera and gold on panel, central panel 99 × 60.7 cm without pinnacle. Boston, Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, P15e4. Inscribed AVE MARIA GRATIA PLENA. Photo: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, Boston, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Five gold-ground panels with pointed trefoil arches, the central one taller and gabled, displayed side by side without their original frame. In the centre, the Virgin in a blue mantle over a white veil holds the Christ Child, who sits on her arm half wrapped in a red mantle and holds a small scroll inscribed EGO SUM LUX M[UNDI]; she supports his bare foot with her hand. On the left stand Saint Peter, grey-haired and bearded, in an orange mantle with a white pallium marked with black crosses, holding the keys and a red book, and Mary Magdalene, wrapped in a red mantle drawn over her head, holding an ointment jar, with a tiny kneeling figure of a bishop at the lower edge of her panel. On the right stand Saint Paul, bald and bearded, in a blue tunic and brown mantle, holding a sword and a book inscribed AD ROMANOS, and Saint Dominic in the black and white Dominican habit, holding a stem of lilies and a red book. The gold ground is worn, with the red bole visible in many places
caption: Simone Martini, Polyptych of San Domenico: Virgin and Child with Saints Peter, Mary Magdalene, Paul and Dominic, with a kneeling Dominican bishop (Trasmondo Monaldeschi?), c. 1321–1325. Tempera and gold on panel, 113 × 257 cm. Orvieto, Museo dell'Opera del Duomo, from the church of San Domenico. Signed and dated, the date incomplete (MCCCXX…). Photo: Museo dell'Opera del Duomo, Orvieto, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Panel with a pointed trefoil arch on a worn gold ground. Mary Magdalene, in half length, is wrapped in a vermilion mantle drawn over her head, with a white veil framing her face and neck and a grey-blue dress lined in black. Her pale face is inclined to the left with heavy-lidded eyes. With her left hand she holds up a tall gilded ointment jar shaped like a small hexagonal tower with a pointed lid, and her right hand rests flat against her mantle. At the lower right corner, a tiny bishop kneels in profile with joined hands, wearing a white mitre and a white chasuble patterned with small red motifs over a black habit, a crozier beside him
caption: Simone Martini, Polyptych of San Domenico: Mary Magdalene with a Kneeling Dominican Bishop (Trasmondo Monaldeschi?), c. 1321–1325. Tempera and gold on panel, 94 × 48.5 cm. Orvieto, Museo dell'Opera del Duomo. Photo: Museo dell'Opera del Duomo, Orvieto, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Panel with a pointed trefoil arch on a heavily worn gold ground with much of the red bole showing. Saint Paul, in half length, is bald with a fringe of dark hair and a long, full dark beard, and looks to the left with a grave, intent expression. He wears a blue tunic with an embroidered neckline and a brown mantle edged with gold draped over his shoulder and across his body. With his right hand he holds upright a long sword, its blade reddish brown, and with his left a closed book whose edge is inscribed AD ROMANOS. The lower part of the panel is damaged and abraded
caption: Simone Martini, Polyptych of San Domenico: Saint Paul, c. 1321–1325. Tempera and gold on panel, 94 × 48.5 cm. Orvieto, Museo dell'Opera del Duomo. Photo: Museo dell'Opera del Duomo, Orvieto, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Gabled gold-ground panel set within a later Baroque frame of carved and gilded scrolls and acanthus leaves. In the main field, under a pointed trefoil arch, the Virgin is shown seated in half length, in a dark blue mantle over a deep red dress, with a jewelled collar and a white veil, her head inclined to the left. The Child sits on her right knee in a white tunic and a red mantle, looking out at the viewer, and holds a small scroll. Two small half-length angels appear in roundels in the spandrels above the arch. In the upper register, three pinnacles: in the centre, Christ in half length in a red mantle over a blue tunic, blessing with his right hand and holding a closed book; on either side, an angel, one in white with joined hands and one holding an open book
caption: Simone Martini, Madonna and Child with Angels and the Blessing Christ, c. 1320. Tempera and gold on panel, 165 × 57 cm. Orvieto, Museo dell'Opera del Duomo. Probably the central panel of a dismembered polyptych from the church of San Francesco, Orvieto; in a later Baroque frame. Photo: Museo dell'Opera del Duomo, Orvieto, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small gold-ground panel in its original moulded frame showing Saint John the Evangelist in half length, young and beardless with red-gold hair and a punched halo, his head inclined to the left in grief and his hands clasped; he wears a blue-green tunic with gold borders and a red mantle; an inscription with the date runs along the bottom.
caption: Simone Martini, Saint John the Evangelist, inscribed with the date 1320 (inscription very probably spurious), tempera on wood, 41.7 × 30.3 cm. Birmingham, Barber Institute of Fine Arts. Photo: Barber Institute of Fine Arts, Birmingham, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Damaged gabled panel showing the Virgin in half length with her head inclined, wearing a white veil and a red dress fastened with a round brooch, holding on her right arm the Christ Child as a swaddled infant who looks up at her; her left hand rests across her body; much of the gold ground and of the blue mantle is lost, revealing the preparation beneath.
caption: Simone Martini, Madonna and Child, c. 1321, tempera on wood, 88 × 51 cm. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale (from the Pieve di San Giovanni Battista, Lucignano d'Arbia). Photo: Pinacoteca Nazionale di Siena, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Gold-ground panel in its original rectangular frame decorated with small quatrefoils, showing the Virgin in half length in a dark blue mantle with gold borders and a white veil, her head inclined towards the Christ Child; the Child, with curly red-gold hair and a red tunic over pink sleeves, looks at the viewer and grasps the border of her mantle while she supports his bare feet.
caption: Simone Martini, Madonna and Child, c. 1326, tempera on wood, gold ground, 58.7 × 39.4 cm (framed 67.3 × 48.3 cm). New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Robert Lehman Collection (1975.1.12). Photo: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York

alt: Gold-ground panel in its original rectangular frame showing Saint Ansanus in half length, a young beardless man with red-gold hair and a plain gold halo, facing the viewer; he wears a green tunic with gold-embroidered cuffs and a dark purple cloak knotted on his right shoulder, holds a palm across his body and a staff with the black and white banner of Siena.
caption: Simone Martini, Saint Ansanus, c. 1326, tempera on wood, gold ground, 57.5 × 38.1 cm (framed 67.6 × 47.9 cm). New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Robert Lehman Collection (1975.1.13). Photo: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York

alt: Gold-ground panel showing Saint Peter in half length, an elderly man with curly grey hair and beard, glancing sideways to the right; he wears a blue tunic with a gold-embroidered collar and a large orange-yellow mantle with gold borders; in his right hand he holds two large keys, while his left hand rests on a closed green book with clasps and red ribbons placed on the lower edge of the panel.
caption: Simone Martini, Saint Peter, c. 1325–1328, tempera and gold on wood, 58 × 38.5 cm. Madrid, Museo Nacional Thyssen-Bornemisza, Carmen Thyssen Collection (CTB.1997.20). Photo: © Museo Nacional Thyssen-Bornemisza, Madrid.

alt: Gold-ground panel in its original rectangular frame showing Saint Andrew in half length, with long wavy grey-brown hair and beard and a punched halo, glancing to the side; he wears a blue tunic with a gold-embroidered collar and a pale pink mantle with gold borders, and holds a closed red book with clasps in both hands.
caption: Simone Martini, Saint Andrew, c. 1326, tempera on wood, gold ground, 57.2 × 37.8 cm. New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art (41.100.23). Photo: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York

alt: Gold-ground panel in its original engaged frame decorated with small quatrefoils, showing Saint Luke in half length, bearded, with short brown hair and a punched halo, writing with a pen in an open book; he wears a red tunic and a dark purple-brown mantle; the inscription S. LVC[A] / S EVLsTA flanks his head, and at the lower left a small winged ox holds an inkpot.
caption: Simone Martini, Saint Luke, c. 1326, tempera and gold leaf on wood, 67.5 × 48.3 × 3.8 cm (with engaged frame). Los Angeles, The J. Paul Getty Museum (82.PB.72). Photo: The J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles

alt: Shaped painted cross with star-shaped terminals: the dead Christ hangs with his head inclined on his right shoulder, his ivory body marked with blood at the side, hands and feet, wearing a transparent loincloth; behind him a panel with stylised red floral patterns; in the lateral terminals the mourning Virgin on the left and Saint John the Evangelist, resting his head on his hand, on the right; the upper terminal bears the titulus.
caption: Simone Martini, Painted Cross with the Mourning Virgin and Saint John the Evangelist, c. 1321–1325, tempera and gold on wood, 164 × 147 cm. San Casciano in Val di Pesa, Santa Maria del Prato (Chiesa della Misericordia). Photo: Santa Maria del Prato, San Casciano in Val di Pesa, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small gold-ground panel with a tooled border showing the kneeling Angel Gabriel in profile, with large multicoloured wings, a jewelled fillet in his golden hair and a punched halo, his hands crossed on his breast and holding a slender lily stem that rises above his head; he wears a pale gold-patterned mantle over a blue-green tunic.
caption: Simone Martini, The Angel of the Annunciation, panel of the Orsini polyptych, tempera and gold on wood, 23 × 14 cm. Antwerp, Koninklijk Museum voor Schone Kunsten. Photo: Koninklijk Museum voor Schone Kunsten Antwerpen, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small gold-ground panel with a tooled border showing the Virgin seated on a throne with white pinnacled sides and a red cloth, wearing a blue mantle with a gold border over a red dress; she rests her head on her right hand in meditation and holds a book on her lap; a small white dove descends at the upper left and a vase of lilies stands at the lower left.
caption: Simone Martini, The Virgin of the Annunciation, panel of the Orsini polyptych, tempera and gold on wood, 24 × 15 cm. Antwerp, Koninklijk Museum voor Schone Kunsten. Photo: Koninklijk Museum voor Schone Kunsten Antwerpen, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small panel showing a crowded procession leaving the crenellated gate of Jerusalem: Christ in a red robe carries the cross and turns back towards his mother, who is pushed away by a soldier with a sword; Mary Magdalene in red raises her arms; soldiers with spears, onlookers and children fill the scene.
caption: Simone Martini, The Carrying of the Cross, panel of the Orsini polyptych, tempera and gold on wood, 30 × 20.5 cm. Paris, Musée du Louvre. Photo: Musée du Louvre, Paris, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small gold-ground panel showing Christ on a tall cross with two angels flying beside him; a lance pierces his side from the left; at the foot of the cross Mary Magdalene in red embraces it, the Virgin swoons among the holy women and Saint John at the lower left, while on the right soldiers with spears and banners and a richly dressed centurion pointing upwards fill the scene.
caption: Simone Martini, The Crucifixion, panel of the Orsini polyptych, tempera and gold on wood, 24 × 14 cm. Antwerp, Koninklijk Museum voor Schone Kunsten. Photo: Koninklijk Museum voor Schone Kunsten Antwerpen, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small gold-ground panel showing the body of Christ being lowered from the cross by two men on a ladder, while the Virgin and Saint John reach up to receive him; a man removes the nails from the feet with pincers; on the right mourners raise their arms; at the bottom a small donor kneels beside a skull at the foot of the cross.
caption: Simone Martini, The Deposition, panel of the Orsini polyptych, tempera and gold on wood, 24 × 15 cm. Antwerp, Koninklijk Museum voor Schone Kunsten. Photo: Koninklijk Museum voor Schone Kunsten Antwerpen, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small panel with a dark sky and trees, including a palm and an orange tree, showing the body of Christ laid on a white shroud over the tomb; the Virgin embraces his head, Mary Magdalene and other mourners lament with raised arms, and haloed men anoint and prepare the body.
caption: Simone Martini, The Entombment, panel of the Orsini polyptych, tempera on wood, 23.7 × 16.7 cm. Berlin, Staatliche Museen, Gemäldegalerie. Photo: Gemäldegalerie, Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small gold-ground panel with a carved Gothic cusped arch, shown without its frame, depicting the Virgin seated on the left in a blue mantle, holding an open book and extending her hand towards the young Christ; in the centre Joseph, in a purple mantle over a red tunic, gestures towards her and rests his hand on the shoulder of the boy, who stands on the right in a blue tunic and red mantle, arms crossed and holding a small red book.
caption: Simone Martini, Christ Discovered in the Temple, 1342, tempera and gold leaf on wood, 49.5 × 35.1 cm (framed 63.5 × 49.9 × 9.1 cm). Liverpool, Walker Art Gallery (WAG 2787). Photo: Walker Art Gallery, National Museums Liverpool, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons; frame not shown.

alt: Small gold-ground panel showing the Angel Gabriel kneeling in profile on a red floor, with golden hair, a faint halo and large wings in orange and blue-grey; his robe is covered with gold brocade patterns scratched through pale pink paint; one hand is placed on his breast and the other holds a slender olive branch; a tooled border frames the gold ground.
caption: Simone Martini, The Angel of the Annunciation, c. 1330, tempera on poplar panel, painted surface 29.5 × 20.5 cm (overall 31 × 21.5 cm). Washington, National Gallery of Art, Samuel H. Kress Collection (1939.1.216). Photo: National Gallery of Art, Washington

alt: Small gold-ground panel with a tooled border showing the Virgin seated on a red cushion, wrapped in a wide deep blue mantle that covers her head and spreads over the floor; beneath it a red and gold brocaded dress; her head is inclined to the left and her eyes lowered, her right hand raised to her breast and her left hand holding a closed red book on her knee.
caption: Simone Martini, The Virgin of the Annunciation, tempera on poplar panel, 30.5 × 21.5 cm. Saint Petersburg, State Hermitage Museum (ГЭ-284). Photo: State Hermitage Museum, Saint Petersburg, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small round-arched gold-ground panel with an engaged frame showing Saint Matthew in half length, frontal, with grey hair and beard and a punched halo; he wears a pink-red tunic with an embroidered collar and a green mantle, holds a quill pen in his right hand and in his left an open red book with an inkpot; the inscription S(AN)C(TU)S MATHEV(S) flanks his head.
caption: Simone Martini, Saint Matthew, c. 1315–1320, tempera on panel, painted surface 26.4 × 19.6 cm (overall 30.8 × 23.2 cm). Washington, National Gallery of Art, Samuel H. Kress Collection (1952.5.23). Photo: National Gallery of Art, Washington

alt: Small round-arched gold-ground panel with an engaged frame showing Saint Simon in half length, with reddish-brown hair and beard and a punched halo, glancing to the side; he wears a dark tunic with a lattice-patterned collar and a large green mantle, and holds a closed blue-grey book with clasps in both hands; the inscription SANTVS SYMON flanks his head.
caption: Simone Martini, Saint Simon, c. 1315–1320, tempera on panel, painted surface 26.2 × 19.7 cm (overall 30.7 × 23.5 cm). Washington, National Gallery of Art, Samuel H. Kress Collection (1952.5.24). Photo: National Gallery of Art, Washington

alt: Small round-arched gold-ground panel with an engaged frame showing Saint James Major in half length, with brown hair and beard and a richly punched halo, glancing to the right; he wears an orange-yellow mantle over a dark tunic, holds a red book in his right hand and in his left a pilgrim's staff from which hangs a black pouch with a scallop shell; the inscription SĀTVS IACOBVS flanks his head.
caption: Simone Martini, Saint James Major, c. 1315–1320, tempera on panel, painted surface 26 × 20 cm (overall 30.7 × 23 cm). Washington, National Gallery of Art, Samuel H. Kress Collection (1952.5.25). Photo: National Gallery of Art, Washington

alt: Small round-arched gold-ground panel with an engaged frame showing Saint Judas Thaddeus as a young beardless man with reddish hair and a punched halo, his head bowed and turned to the left; he wears an orange-red mantle over a dark tunic with an embroidered collar, holds a pink book with clasps and gathers his mantle with his right hand; the inscription SANTVS TADEV(S) flanks his head.
caption: Simone Martini, Saint Judas Thaddeus, c. 1315–1320, tempera on panel, painted surface 26 × 19.7 cm (overall 30.7 × 23.3 cm). Washington, National Gallery of Art, Samuel H. Kress Collection (1952.5.26). Photo: National Gallery of Art, Washington

alt: Illuminated manuscript page with a deep blue sky and blue trees: on the right Virgil, crowned with laurel, reclines beneath a tree with a pen and a book, looking upwards; on the left Servius draws aside a transparent curtain and points to him, beside a soldier with a spear; below, a vinedresser pruning with a billhook and a shepherd milking a ewe; two scrolls in the centre bear Latin verses.
caption: Simone Martini, Allegory of Virgil, frontispiece of Petrarch's Virgil, c. 1340, tempera on parchment, 29.5 × 20 cm. Milan, Biblioteca Ambrosiana, A 79 inf. (formerly S.P. 10/27). Photo: Biblioteca Ambrosiana, Milan, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small gabled gold-ground panel showing Christ crucified on a dark wooden cross with the titulus INRI; his head, with a punched halo, falls on his right shoulder, his pale body hangs in a curve, wrapped in a transparent loincloth; streams of bright red blood flow from the hands, the side and the feet down the cross to a green mound, where they pool on the ground.
caption: Simone Martini, Christ on the Cross, c. 1340, tempera and gold on panel, 25 × 13.6 cm. Cambridge, Mass., Harvard Art Museums/Fogg Museum, Hervey E. Wetzel Bequest Fund (1919.51). Photo © President and Fellows of Harvard College; Harvard Art Museums, harvardartmuseums.org/collections/object/232070.

alt: Small hinged diptych with gilded engaged frames: on the left the Virgin in a dark blue mantle and white veil inclines her head against the cheek of the Christ Child, wrapped in a pink-red cloth, who touches her chin; on the right the dead Christ, with eyes closed and head inclined, stands half-length in the tomb with his arms crossed, showing the wounds in his hands and side; both figures have punched haloes on a gold ground.
caption: Simone Martini and Lippo Memmi, Diptych with the Madonna and Child and the Man of Sorrows, 1326–1328, tempera and gold on panel, 28 × 38 cm (open). Florence, Museo Horne (inv. 55, 56). Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small, badly damaged gold-ground panel with eroded edges and deep scratches, showing Christ on the cross at the centre; on the left the Virgin in a dark mantle raises her hands; at the foot of the cross Mary Magdalene in red kneels and embraces it; on the right Saint John in a red mantle looks up towards Christ; the figures stand on a dark ground.
caption: Simone Martini, Crucifixion with the Virgin, Mary Magdalene and Saint John the Evangelist, c. 1315–1320, tempera and gold on panel, 25 × 26 cm. Florence, Museo Horne (inv. 54). Photo: Museo Horne, Florence, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small gold-ground panel with a tooled foliate border in its gilded frame, showing Christ in a long red robe, barefoot and with a punched halo, carrying a large wooden cross on his shoulder as he walks towards a dark hill on the right, turning his gaze back; at the lower left a small Dominican friar in a black mantle over a white habit kneels with joined hands, looking up at him.
caption: Circle of Simone Martini, Christ Bearing the Cross, with a Dominican Friar, c. 1350, tempera on panel, 30.5 × 21.6 cm. New York, The Frick Collection, Gift of Miss Helen Clay Frick, 1927 (1927.1.01). Photo: The Frick Collection, New York, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A white marble altar-tomb with a tall triangular gable against a black background. In the gable, the Virgin sits enthroned with the Christ Child on her knee, flanked by two angels. Above her a dove descends and the hand of God emerges from a cloud near the apex. The gable is framed by rosettes and blocks. On the left, a bearded saint in a shaggy hair garment presents a kneeling man in a cap to the Virgin. On the right, a standing bearded saint presents a second, smaller kneeling figure. Gothic niches at either side hold winged cherub heads. Below, a chest divided by small pinnacled columns, with streaks of red marble, contains three reliefs. On the left, the hair-clad saint stands beside a figure and a miniature model of the tomb itself. In the centre, the saint is enthroned frontally between two kneeling devotees. On the right, a group of figures lays relics into the tomb.
caption: Arca-altare of Saint Rainerius (San Ranieri), c. 1306–1312. Marble with red marble inlays. Commissioned by Burgundio di Tado, operaio of the cathedral works. Pisa, Museo dell’Opera del Duomo.

alt: A white marble statuette of the standing Virgin holding the Christ Child, set on an octagonal base inscribed in Gothic capitals. The Virgin wears an open crown over a veil and turns her head toward the Child. With her right hand she lifts the hem of her mantle, which falls in deep folds edged with a pierced, lace-like border. The curly-haired Child sits high on her left arm, nude to the waist, a cloth wrapped around his legs. He rests his right arm on his mother’s shoulder, his hand at the brooch of her mantle, holds a small rolled object in his left hand, and looks at her smiling. Faint traces of colour and gilding remain on the surface.
caption: Virgin and Child, 1312–1315, signed on the base. Marble with traces of polychromy and gilding, 65 × 25 × 30 cm. Turin, Museo Civico d’Arte Antica, Palazzo Madama, inv. 0291/PM.

alt: A white marble relief in a rectangular frame. Under a pointed arch carried on two slender colonnettes, the half-length figure of the dead Christ stands out from a dark ground. His head falls toward his right shoulder, his eyes are almost closed and his mouth slightly open. Long, wavy hair and a curling beard are deeply drilled. His torso is bare and lean, the ribs and breastbone marked in shallow ridges, with a small wound in his side. His forearms are crossed at the wrists in front of his body, and the back of the upper hand shows two round nail holes. A band of cloth wraps his hips at the lower edge of the relief.
caption: Attributed to Tino di Camaino, Christ as Man of Sorrows, c. 1300–1325. Marble. Pisa, Palazzo dell’Opera della Primaziale.

alt: A white marble tomb set against a cathedral wall. At the top, on the cornice against a pale wall and beneath a framed painted panel, the effigy of the emperor lies on his back, his head on a large cushion and his body covered to the feet by a long mantle. Below, the front of the sarcophagus shows twelve standing apostles side by side under a row of round arches, with small carved heads between the arches. Panels of red marble close the chest at both ends, and a thin red marble band runs beneath it. Under a heavy moulded cornice, a deep base carries a five-line Latin inscription in Roman capitals.
caption: Tomb of Emperor Henry VII, 1313–1315: effigy and sarcophagus with the Twelve Apostles (one a modern replacement). Marble with red marble inlays. Reassembled in 1494 with the inscribed base and recomposed in 1921. Pisa, Cathedral, east wall of the right transept.

alt: A museum display of white marble statues against a dark wall. At the centre, on a raised plinth, a crowned man sits on a throne. He wears a tall pointed crown, and his mantle falls in deep folds over his knees; his right hand is raised and his left rests near a round object on his lap. Two standing men flank him on each side. The figure at far left wears a hooded mantle and looks upward; the next has long hair and holds a small object; the two on the right wear plain ankle-length tunics, one hand laid on the chest. At both ends stand broken column shafts carved with spiralling foliage and small figures. Above, on dark angled brackets, are four smaller statues: two young figures gathering their robes, a curly-haired youth holding a book, and, at the far right, a veiled woman with a hand on her breast. On a separate bracket at right is a single male head.
caption: Emperor Henry VII Enthroned with Four Councillors, with associated statues, a councillor’s head, and fragments of twisted columns from the tomb of Henry VII, 1313–1315. Marble. Pisa, Museo dell’Opera del Duomo.

alt: A nearly square marble slab, worn and slightly chipped at the edges, carved with a deep circular recess. Its inner rim is lined with a ring of small square blocks. Within the circle, the Virgin appears at half length, crowned with an open crown of fleurons over a veil, her head tilted toward the Child. Her mantle falls in broad folds from her shoulders and is gathered across her lap. The Christ Child sits on her left arm, curly-haired and smiling. He raises his right hand in blessing and holds a scroll in his left. One of his feet emerges at the bottom of the circle.
caption: Virgin and Child, relief from the tomb (arca) of Saint Octavian in Volterra Cathedral, 1318–1320. Marble, 45.7 × 49.5 × 10.2 cm. Raleigh, North Carolina Museum of Art, Gift of the Samuel H. Kress Foundation, GL.60.17.4.

alt: A white marble statue of the standing Virgin holding the Christ Child, against a dark background. The Virgin wears a crown with a pierced band over a veil that falls to her shoulders, and she inclines her head toward the Child with a gentle expression. With her right hand she lifts the hem of her mantle, which falls in broad, deep folds edged with a pierced, lace-like border. The curly-haired Child sits on her left arm, nude to the waist, a cloth over his legs, both bare feet showing. He looks up at her and clasps something at his chest with both hands. A broken stump projects from his side where a part of the group has been lost.
caption: Virgin and Child, c. 1315–1320. Marble. Lucca, Museo Nazionale di Villa Guinigi.

alt: A painted wooden statue of the seated Virgin holding the Christ Child, placed in a niche beneath a carved shell. The Virgin wears a white veil and a dark blue mantle over a red gown gathered under the breast. Her hair is golden brown, and she looks out to her left with a calm, slightly serious expression. In her right hand she holds a small red book. The Child stands on her left knee, curly-haired, wearing a red tunic and a green mantle, and he raises his right hand in blessing while turning his face toward her. Her left hand supports him at his side. The blue mantle falls in broad folds over her knees to her feet; along its edges, paint losses reveal the pale wood beneath.
caption: Virgin and Child, c. 1315–1320. Polychrome wood. Anghiari, church of the Badia di San Bartolomeo.

alt: A tall marble wall tomb against the black-and-white striped wall of Siena Cathedral. Four leafy corbels at the bottom carry a low chest decorated with red marble panels and coats of arms. On it stand four draped figures who support a second chest, carved with three relief scenes: on the left a woman kneeling before Christ in a garden of trees, in the centre Christ rising from the tomb with a banner above sleeping soldiers, and on the right Christ showing his wound to a disciple. Standing statuettes separate the scenes. Above, two angels at the corners draw back a heavy curtain like a tent, revealing the cardinal lying on a bier. At the top, a Gothic tabernacle with three pointed gables holds three statues, the Virgin and Child at the centre between two saints. It is crowned by a small pinnacled gable.
caption: Tomb of Cardinal Riccardo Petroni, c. 1315–1316. Marble with red marble inlays. Siena, Cathedral, chapel of Sant’Ansano, in the 1951 recomposition.

alt: A marble wall tomb set against the bare stone of a cathedral wall. At the bottom, a broad console rests on two round arches. Between them a frontal figure with outstretched arms stands on a dragon-like creature, and groups of small figures crowd the spandrels at either side. Above the console, two lion heads and a central human mask support a sarcophagus flanked by two painted coats of arms, one with wavy bands and one with stripes. The front of the sarcophagus has two relief panels crowded with standing figures, with traces of gilding in the background. On top sits a statue of a bishop in mitre and vestments, his hands folded in his lap and his head bowed.
caption: Tomb of Bishop Antonio d’Orso, completed before 18 July 1321 (the cathedral dates it c. 1322). Marble, partly gilded, with traces of polychromy. Florence, Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore, inner façade, in a modern reassembly of the surviving parts.

alt: Two marble fragments side by side on wooden stands. On the left, the upper half of a nude male figure, cut off at the waist: Christ, with long hair falling to the shoulders, a forked beard and moustache, and a long, calm face with heavy-lidded eyes. His right hand is raised before his chest in blessing, two fingers extended; his left arm hangs at his side, the hand resting on the stand. His chest and ribs are carved in a series of shallow parallel ridges. On the right, a separate head of an older man turned in three-quarter view to the left, with deep-set eyes and a furrowed brow. A long, flowing beard and thick waves of hair are carved in deep, curling strands, drilled through in many places so that dark holes show between the locks.
caption: Blessing Christ and Head of Saint John the Baptist, fragments of the group of the Baptism of Christ from above a door of the Florence Baptistery (the museum’s records name both the east and the south door), c. 1320–1324. Marble. Florence, Museo dell’Opera del Duomo.

alt: A white marble bust of a young woman, cut off below the chest and set on a wooden stand. She wears a crown of carved leaves over a veil that frames her face, falls to her shoulders, and wraps around her neck like a scarf. Her face is oval and calm, with smooth almond-shaped eyes without pupils, a small mouth, and a broken nose. Her hair is parted in the centre and waves down beside her cheeks. Her close-fitting gown is fastened down the front by two rows of round buttons. The arms are lost, and the edge of one shoulder is chipped.
caption: Faith (traditional title), fragment of a group of the Theological Virtues from above a door of the Florence Baptistery, c. 1320–1324. Marble. Florence, Museo dell’Opera del Duomo.

alt: A white marble head with its neck, broken off at the base and set on a wooden stand. The face is full and youthful, with heavy-lidded almond eyes, a straight nose worn at the tip, and a small, full-lipped mouth. Thick, wavy hair is swept back from the forehead and gathered in heavy curls around the head and over the ears. The surface is weathered, with small pits on the forehead and cheek and damage around the chin.
caption: Hope (the museum’s identification), head from a group of the Theological Virtues above a door of the Florence Baptistery, c. 1320–1324. Marble. Florence, Museo dell’Opera del Duomo.

alt: A white marble bust of a young woman, cut off at the waist, against a black background. She wears a narrow diadem over thick, wavy hair that falls to her shoulders, and she turns her face upward to one side, her lips slightly parted; the nose is broken. In her right hand, raised to her shoulder, she holds a vessel with a pierced rim from which rises a mass of flames. With both arms she holds a long curved horn of plenty across her body, its surface carved with overlapping leaves. Her gown has a trefoil-shaped neckline and gathered folds below the breast. The surface is worn, with losses on the hands, the flames, and the horn.
caption: Charity, fragment of a group of the Theological Virtues from above a door of the Florence Baptistery, 1320–1324. Marble. Florence, Museo dell’Opera del Duomo.

alt: A white marble statue of a standing young woman, wearing a low crown over hair braided and coiled around her head. Her head is turned to one side and bowed toward one of the two naked infants she carries against her body. Her long gown is fastened at the neck with buttons, and two pointed openings are outlined over her breasts. On the left, one child, seen from behind, climbs up her body and reaches toward her neckline, supported by her hand beneath him. On the right, the other child nurses at her breast, curled against her and held in her other hand. Below, the gown falls in long, heavy folds to the base. The surface is worn, and the end of one sleeve is broken.
caption: Charity, c. 1320–1322. Marble. Florence, Museo Stefano Bardini.

alt: The central part of a marble wall tomb, lit from the side against a pale wall. At the top, two standing angels at the ends of a shallow chamber draw back carved curtains, revealing the effigy of a prelate lying on a bier in vestments. Below a cornice with a band of leaf ornament, the front of the sarcophagus is carved with three relief scenes separated by standing figures, two of them holding open books with inscriptions. On the left, Christ raises his arm as a disciple touches the wound in his side. In the centre, Christ sits on the edge of the tomb holding a staff, above sleeping soldiers. On the right, a woman kneels before Christ among two trees. Four carved corbels support the chest from below.
caption: Tomb of Gastone della Torre, Patriarch of Aquileia, c. 1318–1320. Marble. Florence, Museo dell’Opera di Santa Croce; originally in the right aisle of Santa Croce.

alt: A white marble statue of the Virgin seated on a plain block throne. She wears a crown of fleurons over a veil that falls to her shoulders, and a gown with an embroidered band at the neckline and a belt at the waist. Her face, slightly damaged, looks out calmly. In her right hand she holds a closed book with clasps, resting it upright on the throne. On her left knee sits the curly-haired Christ Child, his head resting against her shoulder and his eyes closed as if asleep. One small hand lies on his chest under her spread fingers; the other grasps the edge of her mantle. The mantle, edged with a decorated border, falls over her knees in deep folds to her feet. The base is inscribed SEDES SAPIENTIAE in Roman capitals.
caption: Virgin and Child (known as the Sedes Sapientiae), c. 1318–1320, probably from the tomb of Gastone della Torre in Santa Croce. Marble; the inscription on the base is a later addition. Florence, Museo Nazionale del Bargello.

alt: A broken marble slab, its upper right corner missing along a diagonal break. At the top left, only the lower half of the Virgin’s face survives, with nose and mouth, framed by her veil. On her mantle, at the shoulder, is a small star. Her open right hand is raised beside the Christ Child, who sits frontally on her lap. He has a plump face, curly hair tied with a small bow, and bare feet. He raises his right hand in blessing and holds a small bird with spread wings in his left, while his mother’s hand supports him from below. A curved moulding, part of a circular frame, sweeps across the lower part of the relief. Along the bottom and down the right edge runs an inscription in Gothic capitals, partly legible.
caption: Virgin and Child, fragment of the front of the tomb of Bartolomeo di Capua, Naples Cathedral, 1328–1329. Marble with traces of red and blue paint, 44.5 × 39.4 × 6.4 cm. Raleigh, North Carolina Museum of Art, Gift of W. R. Valentiner, G.57.34.11.

alt: The pointed lunette of a Gothic portal, framed by deep mouldings. Its archivolt is carved with a row of small half-length figures and, at the apex, winged angels. At the centre of the lunette, on a pedestal inscribed in Gothic letters, sits the crowned Virgin, holding the Christ Child standing on her knee. To the left stands a bearded saint in a heavy mantle. To the right stands a saint in a bishop’s mitre and cope, and before him kneels a cardinal wearing his broad-brimmed hat, his hands joined. Below, a long marble band carries a four-line Latin inscription in two columns. The surfaces are weathered and the figures partly worn.
caption: Lunette of the central portal of Naples Cathedral. Centre: Tino di Camaino, Virgin and Child, c. 1325–1336. Sides: Antonio Baboccio da Piperno, Saints Peter and Januarius and the Kneeling Cardinal Enrico Minutolo, 1407. Marble. Naples, Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta.

alt: A free-standing marble canopy tomb in the ambulatory of a Gothic church, seen from one side. Two spiral columns inlaid with bands of coloured mosaic rise from carved lions and support a pointed trefoil arch. The arch is framed by a band of blue mosaic with white flowers and crowned by a crocketed gable with pinnacles. In the gable, a roundel holds a small relief of the Virgin and Child. Under the arch, a mosaic lunette shows the enthroned Virgin and Child in an oval frame against a gold ground, flanked by two kneeling figures. Below, the effigy of the duchess lies on a sarcophagus whose front is carved with three lobed medallions containing half-length friars holding books, set against mosaic inlay. Standing figures on lions support the sarcophagus from below. Through the open space beneath the tomb, a dark wooden door is visible in the wall behind.
caption: Tomb of Catherine of Austria, Duchess of Calabria, c. 1324–1325. Marble with glass mosaic inlay. Naples, San Lorenzo Maggiore, choir ambulatory.

alt: A tall marble wall tomb beneath a Gothic canopy, lit from below in a large church interior. Two piers inlaid with red and blue mosaic carry a cusped arch and a crocketed gable, with a half-length blessing figure in the gable and a standing statue on its summit. At the bottom, four winged figures stand side by side on pedestals, supporting the sarcophagus. Its front is divided into seven arched niches, each holding a seated crowned or haloed figure. Above, two angels draw back curtains to reveal the effigy of the queen lying on her bier, with two standing figures behind her. On top of the chamber, under the cusped arch, sits the Virgin with the Child, with smaller figures at the corners.
caption: Tino di Camaino, with Gagliardo Primario, Tomb of Mary of Hungary, Queen of Naples, 1325–1326. Marble with glass mosaic inlay. Naples, Santa Maria Donnaregina Vecchia.

alt: A tall marble wall tomb beneath a Gothic canopy, in a vaulted chapel with a checkered marble floor. Four spiral columns, the outer pair resting on carved lions, carry a pointed gable with crockets. In the gable two angels hold a coat of arms with a diagonal band, and a small statue stands on the summit. Beneath the canopy, three standing female figures support the tomb: at the centre a woman holding a child to her breast, and at the sides two crowned women holding attributes. Above them, a chest carved in relief shows a crowned figure enthroned at the centre, flanked by laymen in short tunics on the left and by friars and veiled women on the right. Higher still, two angels draw back curtains to reveal the effigy of the duchess, dark-robed, lying on a bier above an inscribed panel, with a row of standing figures behind her. A sloping roof carved with another coat of arms crowns the chamber, and on it stand the Virgin and Child between two female saints.
caption: Tino di Camaino and workshop, Tomb of Marie of Valois, Duchess of Calabria, c. 1335–1336, completed after the sculptor’s death. Marble. Naples, Basilica of Santa Chiara.

alt: A small white marble relief with a pointed, house-shaped frame. At the centre the crowned Virgin sits on a throne, her veil falling over her shoulders. The curly-haired Christ Child stands on her left knee, holding the edge of her garment. Behind her, two angels with spread wings hold up a cloth of honour, and two more angels stand at the sides with their hands crossed on their chests. On the left, a kneeling woman in a veil raises her joined hands. The Virgin reaches down and touches her head, while a standing female saint behind her lays a hand on her shoulder. On the right stands Saint Francis in his habit, bearded and tonsured, holding a small cross and a book. The base of the throne is decorated with a row of small arches.
caption: Madonna and Child with Queen Sancia, Saints, and Angels, c. 1335. Marble, 51.4 × 37.8 × 5.7 cm. Washington, National Gallery of Art, Samuel H. Kress Collection, 1960.5.1.

alt: A white marble slab carved as a small triptych, with three round-arched compartments beneath crocketed pointed gables. Each gable holds a carved foliate rosette, and the arches rest on small corbels carved with heads. In the centre, the crowned and veiled Virgin is shown at half length, holding on her left arm the curly-haired Christ Child, who raises his right hand in blessing and holds a book in his left. On the left, Saint Catherine of Alexandria, crowned, holds a palm and the spiked wheel of her martyrdom. On the right, Saint John the Baptist, bearded and long-haired, wears a camel-hair garment under his mantle and holds an unrolled scroll. Two small metal clamps at the sides hold the slab to its mount.
caption: Virgin and Child between Saint Catherine of Alexandria and Saint John the Baptist, front face of a double-sided marble triptych, 1329–1332. Marble. Siena, Collection of the Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena; formerly Borletti collection.

alt: A white marble panel shaped like a small altarpiece, seen against a black background. The pointed gable is edged with carved rosettes. In it, a bearded saint is shown at half length, holding a pair of keys in one hand. Below, under a round arch, the crowned Virgin is seen to the knees, her veil falling over her shoulders and her mantle gathered in heavy folds over her lap. In her right hand she holds a pomegranate. The curly-haired Christ Child sits on her left arm, reaching out to touch the fruit. Cracks run across the arch and the gable.
caption: Virgin and Child (Madonna della Melagrana), probably the central panel of a small portable triptych, c. 1330–1336. White marble, 50 × 32 cm. Castrovillari, Sanctuary of Santa Maria del Castello.

alt: A small marble relief with a pointed, house-shaped frame of stepped mouldings, its lower corners cut off diagonally. The marble has a warm, honey-coloured tone, and joins are visible in the left side of the frame. Inside, the Virgin is shown at half length, wearing an open crown over a veil that falls to her shoulders, her head inclined toward the Christ Child. In her right hand she holds a small cluster, perhaps of flowers or fruit. The curly-haired Child sits on her left arm, wearing a tunic fastened at the neck with a small brooch. He looks back at his mother and holds a small bird whose beak touches his fingers. One of his bare feet appears below, against the heavy folds of the Virgin’s mantle.
caption: Virgin and Child, c. 1330, probably made in Naples. Marble. London, Victoria and Albert Museum, A.31-1964.

alt: A small marble relief with a pointed, house-shaped frame of stepped mouldings, seen against a black background. The marble has a warm, honey-coloured tone. Inside, the Virgin is shown at half length, wearing an open crown of fleurons over a veil that falls to her shoulders. She turns her head toward the Christ Child and holds a small object in her right hand. The curly-haired Child sits on her left arm, both bare feet showing below, and looks back at her. In his hands he holds a small bird, its head turned toward his fingers. The mantle falls in broad folds across the lower part of the relief.
caption: Tino di Camaino or workshop, Mary as Queen of Heaven with the Christ Child, c. 1330–1337. Marble. Glens Falls, New York, The Hyde Collection.

alt: A white marble statuette of the standing Virgin holding the Christ Child, set on a turned wooden base. The Virgin wears a pointed crown over a veil and a mantle fastened at the neck with a brooch. With her right hand she lifts the hem of her mantle, which falls in deep folds edged with a carved border. The curly-haired Child sits on her left arm, nude to the waist, and holds a bird with spread wings against his chest. He turns his head to look up at her. The marble shows warm brownish stains on the surface.
caption: Madonna and Child, c. 1330–1337. Marble, 48.9 × 25.1 × 14.6 cm. Detroit Institute of Arts, City of Detroit Purchase, 25.147.

alt: A white marble statue of a standing young woman on a plain pedestal, wearing an open crown over short, wavy hair. She holds a sword diagonally across her chest in her right hand and, in her left, a pair of scales with two round pans. Her long gown and mantle fall in straight, heavy folds to her feet.
caption: Workshop of Tino di Camaino, Justice, c. 1340–1370, with parts of the late 19th or early 20th century. Marble. Detroit Institute of Arts, Gift of Virginia Booth Vogel, 43.53.

alt: A long rectangular marble relief divided into three round-arched compartments, with small rosettes in the spandrels between the arches. In the centre, the crowned and veiled Virgin holds the curly-haired Christ Child at half length. On the left, a tonsured saint in a hooded friar’s habit presents a small tonsured donor, who stretches out one open hand. On the right, another tonsured saint in a friar’s habit holds a lily and a book. Two small metal hooks at the top fix the slab to the wall.
caption: Follower of Tino di Camaino, Madonna and Child with Saints, mid-14th century. Marble, 62.1 × 125.3 × 8.7 cm. Detroit Institute of Arts, City of Detroit Purchase, 23.20.

alt: Small upright panel in its original gilded frame. The Virgin, in a deep blue mantle over a red dress and a white veil, sits on a green cushion upon a marble box-like throne whose front is carved with rosettes and acanthus leaves and whose step is inlaid with coloured marble. She inclines her head; the Child, standing on her knee in a pink cloth, reaches up to touch her face, one foot resting on her wrist. Two angels above hold up a red cloth embroidered in gold behind her, and two angels below, standing at the sides of the throne, look up at her, each resting a hand on an open book on the throne.
caption: Attributed to Ugolino di Nerio, The Virgin and Child with Four Angels, about 1305. Egg tempera on wood (probably poplar), 41.2 × 28.5 cm. London, National Gallery, NG6386; bought with contributions from the Lewis Fund and the Art Fund (Eugene Cremetti Fund), 1968. © The National Gallery, London, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

alt: Upright panel with a round-headed arch carved in relief, dark painted spandrels above and a gold ground. The Virgin, half-length, wrapped in a very dark blue mantle with gold stars on her forehead and shoulder, over a gold-bordered veil, inclines her head towards the Child. He sits on her left arm in a dark red cloth patterned with small gold motifs, his bare feet resting on her hand, and grasps her veil with both hands as he looks up at her face. Her long hands support him from below.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Virgin and Child, c. 1310. Tempera on panel, gold ground, 85 × 54 cm. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi, Contini Bonacossi Collection, inv. Contini Bonacossi 26. Image: Gallerie degli Uffizi, for educational use only.

alt: Panel with an arched top on a gold ground with engraved haloes. The Virgin, half-length, wears a dark blue-green mantle with a gold border and gold stars on the head and shoulder, over a white veil with a pseudo-Kufic border and a red sleeve at the wrist. She inclines her head and looks out with a melancholy expression; with long, slender hands she holds the Child on her left arm. The Child, with curly reddish hair and full cheeks, looks straight at the viewer; he wears a transparent white shirt and is wrapped in a purple mantle scattered with small gold stars, and he grasps the edge of the mantle at his chest. His bare feet hang down against his mother's dark mantle.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Madonna and Child, late 1310s. Tempera on wood, gold ground, arched top, 89.9 × 58.4 cm. New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Robert Lehman Collection, 1975.1.5. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, open access, CC0.

alt: Upright panel, unframed, with the outline of a lost rounded arch visible as bare wood around the gold ground at the top. The Virgin, half-length, wrapped in a very dark mantle with an olive-green lining over a pink dress, wears a white veil edged with a band of pseudo-Kufic lettering. She inclines her head to the left and looks out with a melancholy expression; her long, pale hands rest lightly on the Child. The Child, naked to the waist, with curly reddish hair and full cheeks, sits on her left arm wrapped in a mauve cloth; he turns his face up towards her and grasps the edge of her veil with his right hand.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Virgin and Child, central panel of a polyptych, c. 1315–1320. Tempera and gold on poplar, 69.5 × 47.5 cm. Paris, Musée du Louvre, Département des Peintures, RF 1986 56. © 2003 Musée du Louvre, Dist. GrandPalaisRmn / Angèle Dequier, image for non-commercial educational use.

alt: Upright panel in a gilded frame. On a gold ground Christ hangs dead on a Y-shaped cross made of a rough, lopped tree trunk, his arms stretched upward along the branches, his head fallen to his right. A red titulus at the top reads IHS NAZARENUS REX IUDEORUM. Blood runs from his feet down the trunk to the rocks below.
