At the foot of the cross Saint Francis, in a brown habit with a knotted cord, kneels and kisses Christ's feet, holding the trunk. At the left the Virgin, wrapped in a black mantle over a red dress, raises her hands in grief; at the right Saint John, in a pink mantle over a blue robe, clasps his hands and looks up at Christ.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, The Crucifixion with Saint Francis, c. 1310–1320. Tempera and gold on panel, 67 × 44.4 cm, with its original frame. Siena, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 34. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Lateral panel under a round arch with a dark spandrel and a band of quatrefoils below. On a gold ground, inscribed S. LODOVICUS, a young beardless bishop turned to the left wears a white mitre set with jewels over the hood of a brown Franciscan habit, and a dark grey-green cope. He raises his right hand in blessing and holds a crozier, its crook decorated with a small figure; the knotted cord of his order hangs at his waist, and a ring shows on his left hand.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Saint Louis of Toulouse, c. 1320. Tempera and gold leaf on wood panel, 75.6 × 35.6 cm. San Francisco, Fine Arts Museums, Legion of Honor, 1952.36; gift of Arthur Sachs. Image: public domain, via Web Gallery of Art.

alt: Lateral panel under a round arch with a dark spandrel and a band of quatrefoils below. On a gold ground, inscribed S. MARIA MAGDALENA, a female saint turned to the right wears a red mantle drawn over her head and fastened at the neck over a black dress. She holds in her left hand a small gilded box with a pointed lid, decorated with foliate ornament, and raises her right hand towards it.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Saint Mary Magdalene, c. 1320. Tempera and gold leaf on wood panel, 75.6 × 35.6 cm. San Francisco, Fine Arts Museums, Legion of Honor, 1952.37; gift of Arthur Sachs. Image: public domain, via Web Gallery of Art.

alt: Small rectangular fragment in a gilded frame. On a gold ground, with the outline of a halo cut off at the top and left, the bust of a young woman wrapped in a red mantle edged with gold, drawn over her head and falling over a red dress with a gold neckline; dark hair shows beside her face. She inclines her head to the left and looks down with a sorrowful expression. At the right of her head is a black Gothic letter M. Her right hand, with long fingers, is raised at the lower left, and the top of a small ointment jar is just visible at the lower edge.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Saint Mary Magdalen, about 1320. Tempera on panel, 36.5 × 24.8 cm. Boston, Museum of Fine Arts, 15.952; gift of Mrs. Walter Scott Fitz. Image: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, for non-commercial educational use.

alt: Round-topped panel in a plain gilded frame. On a worn and cracked gold ground with faint incised haloes, the Virgin, half-length, wears a dark blue mantle with a gold star on the shoulder, edged with a red lining, over a white veil. She inclines her head to the right and looks out. The Child, with curly hair and a solemn, almost sullen face, stands on her arm facing the viewer, naked to the waist, with a white cloth over his shoulder and a dark red cloth around his hips; he holds a small object at his breast. The Virgin's hand supports his crossed bare feet at the lower edge. The flesh tones have a strong greenish cast.
caption: Attributed to Ugolino di Nerio, Madonna and Child. Tempera on wood panel, 79.5 × 56 × 5 cm. Princeton, Princeton University Art Museum, y1937-357; gift of Dan Fellows Platt, Class of 1895. Image: Princeton University Art Museum, public domain.

alt: A seven-part polyptych in its gilded frame. At the centre, under a round arch with two angels in the spandrels, the Virgin in a dark blue mantle holds the Child, who sits on her arm wrapped in a red cloth and looks up at her. At either side, under round arches with angels in the spandrels, stand six half-length saints named in gold letters: Francis in a brown habit with a book, Andrew in a red mantle, Paul with a sword and book, Peter in a green mantle with a book, Stephen in a deacon's dalmatic, and Louis of Toulouse in a mitre and a cope patterned with fleurs-de-lis over a Franciscan habit. Above, seven triangular pinnacles: Christ blessing at the centre and six prophets holding scrolls.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Virgin and Child with Saints Francis, Andrew, Paul, Peter, Stephen, and Louis of Toulouse, c. 1317–21. Tempera and gold on panel, 163.7 × 341.4 cm. Williamstown, Massachusetts, Clark Art Institute, 1962.148; acquired by the Clark, 1962. Image: Clark Art Institute, for educational use only.

alt: A five-part polyptych in a frame painted red with quatrefoil ornament. Under round arches stand four half-length saints named in gold letters, Francis in a brown habit with a red book, John the Baptist in a hair shirt and pink mantle holding a tall reed cross, James in a green mantle raising his hand and holding a red book, and Mary Magdalene in a red mantle holding a small white ointment jar shaped like a domed building. At the centre the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle with a gold star, holds the Child, who wears a red tunic and a patterned mantle and reaches up to touch her cheek. Above, five triangular gables: the Crucifixion at the centre and four half-length apostles.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Virgin and Child with Saints, c. 1320. Tempera and gold on wood panel, 122.5 × 192.5 cm overall (framed 122.2 × 200.3 cm). Cleveland, Cleveland Museum of Art, Leonard C. Hanna Jr. Fund, 1961.40. Image: Cleveland Museum of Art, open access, CC0.

alt: Round-topped panel in a gilded frame with a running ornament in relief. On a gold ground, the Virgin, half-length, wears a dark blue mantle with gold stars on her forehead and shoulder, edged with a red lining, over a white veil bordered with pseudo-Kufic lettering. She inclines her head and looks out. The Child, with curly reddish hair, sits on her left arm in a transparent white shirt, wrapped in a red cloth patterned with small gold motifs, and pulls the edge of her veil with both hands. His bare foot rests on her right hand. Both haloes are richly punched with rosettes and foliate bands.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Virgin and Child, about 1325–30. Tempera on panel, 81.4 × 52.1 cm. Boston, Museum of Fine Arts, 16.65; gift of Mrs. Walter Scott Fitz. Image: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, for non-commercial educational use.

alt: Engraving-like drawing of a large polyptych in four tiers. At the centre of the main tier the Virgin, half-length, holds the standing Child under a pointed arch, with angels in the spandrels. At the left stand Saint John the Baptist with a scroll and Saint Paul with a sword, and an outer compartment whose figure is effaced; at the right Saint Peter with keys and a book, a compartment showing only a tonsured head, and a mitred bishop with crozier. Above runs a row of six panels with paired half-length saints, then six gabled pinnacles with prophets, and a tall central gable whose image is faded. Along the bottom the predella shows seven Passion scenes: Last Supper, Betrayal, Flagellation, Way to Calvary, Deposition, Entombment and Resurrection.
caption: Anonymous, The high altarpiece of Santa Croce, Florence, late eighteenth century. Drawing. Vatican City, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat. Lat. 9847, ff. 91v–92r. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Horizontal panel showing a room with a dark coffered ceiling, grey walls with two wall pegs and a hanging towel, and a small window at the right. Christ, at the far left, stands in a red robe and dark mantle and reaches towards the long table covered with a white cloth; the young John rests his head on the table beside him. Behind the table sit six apostles with punched gold haloes, among them Peter with white hair raising his hand, and a dark-bearded apostle cutting a fruit. In front, five apostles seen from behind kneel on a wooden bench, turning to look at Christ; the first at the left, without a halo, is Judas. At the right a further apostle sits at the end of the table. On the cloth are bowls, dark dishes with lamb, small round loaves, knives and red glasses of wine.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, The Last Supper, from the predella of the high altarpiece of Santa Croce, Florence, c. 1325. Tempera and gold on wood, painted surface 34.3 × 52.7 cm. New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Robert Lehman Collection, 1975.1.7. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, open access, CC0.

alt: Predella panel in its original gilded frame. Against a gold sky above a pale rocky landscape with three dark trees, a crowd presses around Christ at the centre, in a dark blue mantle over a red robe. Judas, in a yellow robe and red mantle, kisses him on the cheek. At the left Peter, white-haired, in a green mantle, grasps a man by the head and cuts off his ear with a knife; behind him bearded elders watch. At the right soldiers in dark helmets and chain mail, one in an ornate cuirass, lay hands on Christ, and spears, halberds and two red lanterns rise above their heads.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, The Betrayal of Christ, from the predella of the high altarpiece of Santa Croce, Florence, possibly 1325–8. Egg tempera on wood (probably poplar), 40.4 × 58.8 cm. London, National Gallery, NG1188; bought 1885. © The National Gallery, London, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

alt: Predella panel in its gilded frame. In a shallow room with a dark green panelled back wall, a ceiling of dark lozenge pattern and pale green corner consoles, Christ stands at the centre, naked but for a white loincloth, his wrists tied to a slender white column with a small capital. He looks out sadly at the viewer. At either side a tormentor in a short tunic, red at the left and violet at the right, raises a scourge high above his head; the man at the right grasps Christ's arm and leans back to strike.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, The Flagellation, from the predella of the high altarpiece of Santa Croce, Florence, c. 1325. Tempera on poplar, 40.6 × 58.4 cm with frame. Berlin, Staatliche Museen, Gemäldegalerie, 1635A; acquired on the English art market, 1906. Photo: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, Gemäldegalerie / Jörg P. Anders, Public Domain Mark 1.0.

alt: Predella panel in its original gilded frame. Christ, in a deep pink robe, carries the cross on his shoulder towards the right, turning his head back to look at his mother; a man in a brown tunic pulls him forward by a rope tied around his neck, and a crowd of bearded elders follows. Behind Christ soldiers in dark helmets and ornate leather cuirasses, carrying shields and spears, push him on. At the left the Virgin, in a dark mantle, raises her hand to her face in grief, accompanied by two holy women in violet and red. At the right a bearded old man in a violet mantle over blue gestures towards a rock.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, The Way to Calvary, from the predella of the high altarpiece of Santa Croce, Florence, possibly 1325–8. Egg tempera on wood (probably poplar), 40.8 × 58.5 cm. London, National Gallery, NG1189; bought 1885. © The National Gallery, London, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

alt: Predella panel in its original gilded frame. On a gold ground between bare green rocks stands the cross, with a ladder leaning against it. A white-haired man on the ladder lowers the dead Christ, whose pale body slumps into the arms of the Virgin, in a dark mantle, who presses her face to his. John, in a red mantle, embraces Christ's legs. At the lower right a bearded man kneels and pulls the nails from Christ's feet with pincers; blood runs down the foot of the cross and pools on the ground. At the left Mary Magdalene, in a red mantle, presses Christ's hand to her cheek, and two other holy women stand behind.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, The Deposition, from the predella of the high altarpiece of Santa Croce, Florence, possibly 1325–8. Egg tempera on wood (probably poplar), 40.7 × 58.6 cm. London, National Gallery, NG3375; presented by Henry Wagner, 1918. © The National Gallery, London, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

alt: Predella panel in its gilded frame. Against a backdrop of brown rocks, the body of Christ, wrapped in a white shroud, is laid on the edge of a pale stone sarcophagus with panelled sides. The Virgin, in a dark mantle, bends over and presses her face to his; John, in a red mantle at the left, holds his head; an old bearded man in a blue mantle, at the centre, lowers the body by the shroud. Behind the tomb holy women weep, one covering her face, while a woman in red at the back raises both arms in lament. At the right a woman in green and a bearded man in red look on.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, The Entombment, from the predella of the high altarpiece of Santa Croce, Florence, c. 1325. Tempera on poplar, 40.8 × 58 cm with frame. Berlin, Staatliche Museen, Gemäldegalerie, 1635B; acquired on the English art market, 1906. Photo: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, Gemäldegalerie / Jörg P. Anders, Public Domain Mark 1.0.

alt: Predella panel in its original gilded frame. Against a backdrop of steep brown rocks, Christ, bare-chested and wrapped in a pale violet mantle, steps out of a white marble sarcophagus, one foot on its rim, holding a staff with a white banner bearing a red cross. The lid of the tomb leans against the rocks behind. In the foreground four soldiers in chain-mail hoods and coloured tunics of yellow, pink, green and red sleep on the ground, slumped against their round shields.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, The Resurrection, from the predella of the high altarpiece of Santa Croce, Florence, possibly 1325–8. Egg tempera on wood (probably poplar), 41.5 × 58.1 cm. London, National Gallery, NG4191; presented by Viscount Rothermere, 1926. © The National Gallery, London, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

alt: Three tall panels side by side, each in a gilded frame with a pointed arch and two angels in the spandrels; above the first two runs a band of quatrefoils with small heads of prophets. At the left Saint John the Baptist, gaunt, with long dark hair and beard, in a hair shirt and a red mantle, points to himself and holds a scroll inscribed ECCE AGNUS DEI ECCE QUI TOLLIT PECCATA MUNDI HIC EST DE QUO DIXI. At the centre Saint Paul, balding with a long dark beard, in a dark mantle over a green tunic, holds a long sword and a red book. At the right Saint Peter, with white curly hair and beard, in a green mantle, holds two keys and a red book.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Saints John the Baptist, Paul and Peter, from the main tier of the high altarpiece of Santa Croce, Florence, c. 1325. Tempera on poplar; outer frame 191.6 × 61.5 cm. Berlin, Staatliche Museen, Gemäldegalerie, 1635; acquired on the English art market with the collection of Cyril B. Harcourt, London. Photo: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, Gemäldegalerie / Jörg P. Anders, Public Domain Mark 1.0.

alt: Panel in its gilded frame with two pointed arches carried on slender columns, a trefoil with a small decorative motif between them, and a band of quatrefoils below. Under the arches stand two half-length apostles on gold grounds: at the left Simon, bearded, in a brown mantle over a pink tunic, holding a red book; at the right Thaddeus, younger, in a violet mantle over a blue tunic. Large areas of both mantles are lost and filled with a neutral tone. In the quatrefoils below appear small painted heads of two bearded old men and a younger beardless man, alternating with animal motifs.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Saints Simon and Thaddeus, from the middle tier of the high altarpiece of Santa Croce, Florence, possibly 1325–8. Egg tempera on wood (probably poplar), 70.4 × 62.2 cm. London, National Gallery, NG3377; presented by Henry Wagner, 1919. © The National Gallery, London, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

alt: Panel in its gilded frame with two pointed arches on slender columns, a trefoil between them and a band of empty quatrefoils below. At the left Saint Bartholomew, with thick curly red hair and a long red beard, wears a purple mantle over a tunic patterned in gold with small coloured stones, and holds a small scroll; he looks to his left. At the right Saint Andrew, older, with long grey hair and beard, wears a blue tunic under an olive-green mantle and holds a red book with a gold clasp; he too looks to his left.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Saints Bartholomew and Andrew, from the middle tier of the high altarpiece of Santa Croce, Florence, possibly 1325–8. Egg tempera on wood (probably poplar), 70 × 62 cm. London, National Gallery, NG3473; presented by the Earl of Crawford and Balcarres through the Art Fund, 1919. © The National Gallery, London, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

alt: Panel in a gilded frame with two pointed arches, a trefoil between them and a band of quatrefoils below with small heads of a bearded saint, a crowned king and an old man, alternating with animal motifs. At the left Saint James the Greater, with dark brown hair and beard, in a dark green mantle over a red tunic, holds a scroll. At the right Saint Philip, young and beardless, in a red mantle over a green tunic, raises his hand and holds a dark book. Faded inscriptions flank their heads.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Saints James the Greater and Philip, from the middle tier of the high altarpiece of Santa Croce, Florence, c. 1325. Tempera on poplar. Berlin, Staatliche Museen, Gemäldegalerie, 1635C; gift of Helene Tepelmann-Vieweg, 1911. Photo: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, Gemäldegalerie / Jörg P. Anders, Public Domain Mark 1.0.

alt: Panel in a gilded frame with two pointed arches and a trefoil between them. At the left Saint Matthew, an old man with grey hair and beard, in a dark green mantle, raises his hand and holds a red book. At the right Saint James the Less, with long auburn hair and a short beard, in a red mantle over a dark tunic, places his hand on his breast and holds a red book.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Saints Matthew and James the Less, from the middle tier of the high altarpiece of Santa Croce, Florence, c. 1325. Tempera on poplar. Berlin, Staatliche Museen, Gemäldegalerie, 1635D; gift of Helene Tepelmann-Vieweg, 1911. Photo: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, Gemäldegalerie / Jörg P. Anders, Public Domain Mark 1.0.

alt: Panel in a gilded frame with two pointed arches and a trefoil between them, the gold much worn. At the left Saint Matthias, with dark hair and a long dark beard, in a red mantle over a green tunic, holds a dark book. At the right a female saint in a brown habit and a white veil and wimple places her hand on her breast and holds a small object.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Saint Matthias and a Female Saint (Elizabeth of Hungary or Clare), from the middle tier of the high altarpiece of Santa Croce, Florence, c. 1325. Tempera on poplar. Berlin, Staatliche Museen, Gemäldegalerie, 1635E; gift of Helene Tepelmann-Vieweg, 1911. Photo: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, Gemäldegalerie / Jörg P. Anders, Public Domain Mark 1.0.

alt: Gabled pinnacle panel, its frame lost, the bare wood visible around the gilded triangle and the small wooden blocks of a modern support at the sides. Within the gold field the prophet Isaiah, half-length, with long grey hair and beard and a stern expression, wears a red mantle and holds a scroll of which only the last letters, RI and NOMEN, survive. The letters SA remain at the left of his head. Much of the mantle is damaged.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Isaiah, pinnacle of the high altarpiece of Santa Croce, Florence, possibly 1325–8. Egg tempera on wood (probably poplar), 45.8 × 31.5 cm. London, National Gallery, NG3376; presented by Henry Wagner, 1918. © The National Gallery, London, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

alt: Gabled pinnacle panel in a moulded gilded frame. The prophet Moses, half-length, bald and white-bearded, in a green mantle over a blue tunic, holds an unrolled scroll across his body inscribed in Gothic letters VIDEBAM QUE RUBUS ARDEBAT ET NO COMBUREBATUR. The letters MOY and SES flank his head.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Moses, pinnacle of the high altarpiece of Santa Croce, Florence, possibly 1325–8. Egg tempera on wood (probably poplar), 55 × 31.4 cm. London, National Gallery, NG6484; bought 1983. © The National Gallery, London, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

alt: Gabled pinnacle panel in a moulded gilded frame. King David, half-length, with a short white beard and a jewelled crown, wears a dark blue cloak lined with white and spotted to resemble ermine, over a red and brown robe. He raises his right hand in blessing and holds a long scroll with a damaged inscription.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, David, pinnacle of the high altarpiece of Santa Croce, Florence, possibly 1325–8. Egg tempera on wood (probably poplar), 55.2 × 31.2 cm. London, National Gallery, NG6485; bought 1983. © The National Gallery, London, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

alt: Gabled pinnacle panel in a moulded gilded frame. The prophet Daniel, young and beardless, with curly auburn hair and a white pointed cap, inclines his head and looks down to the left. He wears a bright red-orange mantle over a brown tunic patterned in gold and a green undergarment, and holds across his body a scroll inscribed LAPIS ABSCISUS EST DE MONTE SINE MANIBUS, with the reference DANIEL II at the right.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Daniel, pinnacle of the high altarpiece of Santa Croce, Florence, c. 1325. Tempera and tooled gold on panel, 54 × 31 cm. Philadelphia Museum of Art, John G. Johnson Collection, 1917, cat. 89. Image: Philadelphia Museum of Art, for educational use only.

alt: Horizontal panel fragment showing the top of a pointed arch, its inner field now empty and showing the bare preparation and canvas. In the spandrels at either side two half-length angels with large wings lean on the arch: at the left an angel in a violet robe and orange mantle with crossed hands looks up; at the right an angel in a blue robe and pink mantle with folded hands looks across at him.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Spandrel Angels, from above the lost Saint Francis of the high altarpiece of Santa Croce, Florence, possibly 1325–8. Egg tempera on wood (probably poplar), 28.7 × 57.2 cm. London, National Gallery, NG3378; presented by Henry Wagner, 1919. © The National Gallery, London, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

alt: Horizontal panel fragment with the top of a gilded pointed arch framing an empty field of bare preparation. In the spandrels two angels with dark blue-green wings lean on the arch and look down: at the left an angel in a pink robe and violet mantle; at the right an angel in a blue mantle over a pink robe.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Spandrel Angels, from above the lost Saint Louis of Toulouse of the high altarpiece of Santa Croce, Florence, possibly 1325–8. Egg tempera on wood (probably poplar), 27.5 × 56.7 cm. London, National Gallery, NG6486; bought 1983. © The National Gallery, London, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0.

alt: Wide panel fragment under a gilded cornice, showing the top of a large pointed arch whose inner field is now empty and white. In the spandrels at either side, groups of half-length angels with gold haloes and dark wings crowd against the arch: at the left four angels, two of them almost entirely abraded, one in a blue mantle looking down with hands raised; at the right five angels in red, green, blue and violet, leaning on the arch, gesturing and looking down towards the centre.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Worshipping Angels, from above the central panel of the high altarpiece of Santa Croce, Florence, c. 1325. Tempera on panel, 44.4 × 74.9 cm. Los Angeles County Museum of Art, William Randolph Hearst Collection, 49.17.40. Photo: Wikimedia Commons contributor, CC0.

alt: Lateral panel of a polyptych under a round arch with a dark frieze above. On a gold ground with a punched halo, a young female saint is shown at half length, her head inclined to the right, with reddish-brown hair under a white veil falling over her shoulders. She wears a blue mantle sown with small gold fleurs-de-lis and edged with a jewelled gold border fastened at the breast by a square brooch, over a violet dress and a long white scarf. In her right hand she holds a small red cross with trefoil ends; her left hand rests at her waist.
caption: Attributed to Ugolino di Nerio, Saint Margaret Holding the Cross, c. 1330. Tempera on wood, 60.6 × 28.4 cm (image). Portland, Oregon, Portland Art Museum, 61.41; gift of the Samuel H. Kress Foundation. Image: Portland Art Museum, public domain.

alt: Bust-length panel of an elderly bearded saint on a gold ground. He faces the viewer almost frontally, with a furrowed brow, heavy-lidded brown eyes and a long, broad grey beard falling in wavy locks over his chest; his grey hair is swept back from the forehead. He wears a dark green tunic under a deep red mantle wrapped across his body. Behind his head a large halo is punched with three-petalled leaves and rosettes on a stippled ground, within bands of small circles. The gold margins at the upper corners are also punched.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Saint Matthew(?), late 1320s. Tempera on wood, gold ground, 38.4 × 32.4 cm. New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Robert Lehman Collection, 1975.1.6. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, open access, CC0.

alt: Small upright panel in a gilded frame with a band of painted lozenges. On a richly punched gold ground the Virgin, in a blue mantle over a red dress, sits on a marble throne hung with a red cloth patterned in gold; the Child, on her knee in a red cloth, reaches up to touch her chin. At the left stand Saint Peter with keys and book, and below him Saint John the Baptist in a hair shirt and red mantle; at the right Saint Paul with sword and book, and below him Saint Dominic in the white habit and black mantle of his order, raising his hand and holding a red book. A small Dominican friar kneels with joined hands at Dominic's feet. The floor is a green carpet patterned in gold, and the step of the throne carries a band of gold pseudo-lettering.
caption: Attributed to Ugolino di Nerio, Virgin and Child Enthroned with Saints Peter, Paul, John the Baptist, and Dominic and a Dominican Supplicant, c. 1325–1335. Tempera on panel, 37.2 × 23.2 cm (framed 43.4 × 29.1 cm). Chicago, The Art Institute of Chicago, Mr. and Mrs. Martin A. Ryerson Collection, 1937.1007. Image: Art Institute of Chicago, CC0.

alt: Triptych mounted on green velvet within a later gabled frame. Under round arches stand Saint Paul at the left, balding with a long dark beard, in a pink mantle, holding a book and a sword now reduced to its outline; the Virgin at the centre, in a dark mantle over a red dress, holding the Child, who wears a red cloth and pulls at her veil; and Saint Peter at the right, with curly white hair and beard, in a green mantle, holding a book and the remains of keys. Above, three gabled pinnacles: Christ blessing at the centre, the deacon Saint Stephen with a book at the left, and the white-bearded Saint Andrew at the right.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, probably with Bartolomeo Bulgarini, Virgin and Child with Saints Paul and Peter, from San Pietro in Villore, San Giovanni d'Asso, 1325–1330. Tempera on panel, gold ground, 148 × 152 cm. Florence, Gallerie degli Uffizi, Contini Bonacossi Collection, inv. Contini Bonacossi 4. Image: Gallerie degli Uffizi, for educational use only.

alt: Tall gabled panel on a gold ground. The Virgin, wrapped in a black mantle edged with a narrow gold border that falls in looping folds to the floor, sits on a broad white marble throne with inlaid lozenges, carved capitals and a red cloth of honour patterned in gold. She inclines her head towards the Child, who sits on her knee in a green tunic and an orange-red mantle and pulls her white veil towards him with both hands. At the lower right, very small, a donor in a brown habit kneels with joined hands on the red marble floor.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, Virgin and Child Enthroned with a Donor, c. 1334–1336. Tempera and gold on panel. San Casciano in Val di Pesa, Church of the Misericordia (formerly Santa Maria al Prato). Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Tall gabled panel, its frame lost and its edges of bare, worm-eaten wood. On a worn gold ground Christ hangs dead on a dark blue cross with a blank titulus, his head fallen on his right shoulder, his body long and pale, blood flowing from his hands, side and feet. Six small angels in pink, blue, violet and green, with multicoloured wings, fly around the cross: two in the gable, four beside the arms, some covering their faces, some raising their arms in lament. Below, cut off at the knees, the Virgin in a dark blue mantle bows her head and lowers her hands, and Saint John in a red mantle clasps his hands and looks down in sorrow.
caption: Ugolino di Nerio, The Crucifixion with the Virgin, Saint John and Angels, c. 1330–1335. Tempera and gold on panel, 135 × 89 cm. Madrid, Museo Nacional Thyssen-Bornemisza. Photo: Francesco Bini, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Tall round-topped gold-ground panel by Vitale da Bologna: the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle worked with worn gold motifs and a transparent white veil, sits on a white Gothic throne with pinnacled posts and red cushions, before a gold cloth of honour patterned with lozenges; she inclines her head towards the naked Christ Child, who stands on her lap, touches her chin with his right hand and stretches out his left arm; at the foot of the throne kneel two small donors, one in red with joined hands at left, one in a dark hooded garment at right, above a damaged inscription.
caption: Virgin and Child with Two Donors (the "Madonna dei Denti"), 1345. Tempera and gold on panel, 155 × 73 cm. Signed and dated at the foot. Bologna, Museo Civico d'Arte Industriale e Galleria Davia Bargellini, inv. 129. From the oratory beside the church of Sant'Apollonia at Mezzaratta, Bologna.

alt: Panel by Vitale da Bologna against a dark blue-green ground: Saint George, in gilded chain mail and a billowing red cloak, his blond hair streaming behind a gold halo, plunges forward on a rearing pale grey horse that throws back its head with open mouth, and drives a long lance diagonally down into the jaws of a winged, clawed golden-brown dragon writhing on red rocks at lower right; the horse's hindquarters bear a monogram of interlaced letters; at upper right, cut by the edge of the panel, a crowned princess looks back over her shoulder.
caption: Saint George and the Dragon, c. 1340. Tempera and gold on panel, 80 × 70 cm. Signed with a monogram on the horse's flank. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 6394.

alt: Fresco filling the semidome of the apse at Pomposa: at the centre Christ sits enthroned in a tall pointed mandorla of concentric red, white and blue-grey bands, blessing and holding an open book; clusters of angels fly in the upper corners; at left a procession of tall female saints in ermine-lined robes advances towards him, and smaller kneeling angels gather at the foot of the mandorla; at right, beside the mandorla, stands the armoured, winged Saint Michael, beyond which the plaster is largely lost; a frieze of roundels with heads runs round the rim, and an inscription in Gothic letters runs below the mandorla.
caption: Christ in Glory among Angels and Saints, dated 1351. Fresco. Pomposa (Codigoro, Ferrara), abbey church of Santa Maria, semidome of the apse.

alt: Detail of the Pomposa apse fresco: Christ, with long hair, a short beard and a gold halo, sits frontally on a throne draped in gold cloth inside a pointed mandorla of concentric red, white and blue-grey bands, against a dark blue ground scattered with gold stars; he wears a white tunic with red panels and a red mantle lined in green, raises his right hand in blessing and holds in his left an open book inscribed PACEM MEAM DO VOBIS; angels crowd in the upper corners and kneel at the lower corners; below the mandorla runs the inscription ASTRA POLI XPS NITET CUM CARNE BEATA.
caption: Christ in Glory, detail of the apse semidome, dated 1351. Fresco. Pomposa (Codigoro, Ferrara), abbey church of Santa Maria. Below the mandorla the verse ASTRA POLI XPS NITET CUM CARNE BEATA.

alt: The San Salvatore polyptych by Vitale da Bologna photographed against darkness: seven painted fields in an elaborately carved and gilded frame of crocketed ogival arches, twisted colonnettes and foliate cresting, the tall central panel rising under its own gable; at the centre the Coronation of the Virgin against a gold cloth patterned with dark quatrefoils, a band of angels on red in the cusp; at its sides two standing figures under arches, an archbishop in a rose cope with a small kneeling donor in a dark cloak over a white habit at the left and the gaunt Baptist in a rose mantle at the right; at the outer edges four small arched scenes in two tiers, a Nativity under an open-truss roof at the upper left and two enthroned, mitred doctors writing at their desks at the lower right among them.
caption: The San Salvatore polyptych ("Polittico di san Tommaso di Canterbury"), 1353. Tempera and gold on panel, c. 105 × 225 cm overall, in its original carved and gilded frame. Bologna, church of the Santissimo Salvatore, chapel of the right transept. Contracted 6 July 1353 by Raniero Ghisilieri for the altar of Saint Thomas Becket; from Santa Maria di Reno.

alt: Frescoed wall under a pointed arch in Udine Cathedral, divided by ornamental bands into a lunette and two registers: in the apex Christ blesses within a roundel, an open book in his hand, flanked by flying angels, and beneath him a small praying figure is borne up between two angels over the funeral of Saint Nicholas — the saint laid on a bed beside a bier draped in yellow, surrounded by clergy in white, a dignitary in red, a nun in black and crowds of laymen at both sides before a city wall; in the middle register a boat full of struggling sailors rides a dark sea at the left, a woman kneels before a shrine at the centre, and at the right, between domed aedicules, a bishop-saint in a red cope stands over a naked youth rising from a tub, held by a man in oriental dress; the lower register, badly ruined, keeps a scene of dignitaries gathered at a table at the left, with wide losses of plaster and a modern doorway cut at the lower right.
caption: Stories of Saint Nicholas, 1348–1349. Frescoes. Udine, cathedral, chapel of San Nicolò (Museo del Duomo). Painted for the confraternity of San Nicolò dei Fabbri; payments of 1348 and 4 October 1349.

alt: Long, severely damaged fresco frieze by Vitale da Bologna: along the upper zone survive the heads and upper bodies of haloed figures seated behind a long table, the table itself and the whole lower half reduced to bare plaster with scattered traces; at the centre a young blond apostle slumps forward asleep; to his right a figure in a red mantle, its head lost, points along the table; at the left a dark-haired apostle in red reaches across with an outstretched arm, beside a figure in a yellow mantle at the edge; at the far right a bowed, balding figure in a pale rose mantle faces a standing bearded saint in a dark robe; remains of dishes and a faint red circular trace survive in the ruined lower zone, framed by modern neutral infill.
caption: Last Supper with Saints Catherine, Louis of Toulouse, Anthony of Padua and the Archangel Raphael, before 1340. Detached fresco, 211 × 937 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 10032. From the Refettorio Nuovo of the convent of San Francesco, Bologna.

alt: The entrance wall of Santa Maria di Mezzaratta as reassembled in the Pinacoteca Nazionale of Bologna: detached fresco fragments mounted on a pale neutral ground in the wall's original shape, a broad gable with a blank circular oculus at the top flanked by the kneeling Archangel Gabriel at left and the standing Virgin Annunciate at right; below a decorative band, the main field holds the Nativity at its centre — the Virgin amid golden rays, the midwife's bath at her side, the wicker crib with the ass and ox beneath striped thatched roofs — flanked at left by a crowd of women with a tall angel and at right by seated figures among rocks, with a choir of haloed maidens and a frieze of kneeling angels beneath; two lower wings extend at the sides, the left with the Miraculous Healing and the ruined Dream of the Virgin, the right with the Annunciation to the Shepherds and the flock.
caption: The entrance wall of Santa Maria di Mezzaratta, general view of the reassembly. Detached frescoes by Vitale da Bologna, c. 1338–1355. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, Room 8.

alt: Colour detail of the centre of Vitale da Bologna's Mezzaratta Nativity: the haloed Virgin stands upright at the heart of the scene in a pale blue-white mantle, golden rays bursting around her, the paint before her breast abraded; at the left a midwife wrapped in a great ochre-yellow mantle bends over a brown basin and tests the water with spread fingers, while a companion in grey-green pours from a small jug and two fair-haired women look on; at the right the dark head of the ass and the golden-brown ox lean side by side over the plaited wicker rim of the crib, two fair-haired angels flying in above them; below, against dark ground, runs a frieze of kneeling angels in white, rose and green, hands joined or raised in adoration.
caption: Nativity ("Presepe"), detail of the central group. Early 1340s; the lower episodes added c. 1353–1355. Fresco, detached and transferred to canvas, 495 × 320 cm (the full field). Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 6346. From the entrance wall of the church of Santa Maria di Mezzaratta, Bologna.

alt: Fresco fragment by Vitale da Bologna in two zones: in the lower scene a sick woman lies in a bed under a white sheet and a yellow-patterned coverlet, her capped head on a scrolled bolster at the right beneath a gilded gabled canopy; behind the bed an elderly hooded man and a woman in a dark mantle pray with joined hands while a third woman in grey-blue reaches towards the patient; in the foreground a woman in a rose mantle sits on a stool with her head sunk in her hands, and at the far left a seated figure in ochre reads from a book; above, beyond a mottled red wall, the upper zone holds the Virgin and Child among haloed young women, Saint Catherine with her wheel among them, while from the right an angel with red wings and a red pointed cap flies down trailing a long inscribed scroll towards the bed; bare plaster and dark gaps interrupt the edges, with fragments of patterned border at the corners.
caption: The Miraculous Healing ("Guarigione miracolosa"), c. 1353–1355. Fresco, detached and transferred to canvas. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inventory not verified against the printed catalogues. From the entrance wall of the church of Santa Maria di Mezzaratta, Bologna, lower left wing.

alt: Severely ruined fresco fragment by Vitale da Bologna: at the upper left the Virgin lies asleep, her haloed head with loose blond hair resting on her joined hands against a white pillow, her body in a pale blue robe stretched diagonally across a red bed of which little more than the colour survives; around and beneath her run the traces of a walled town seen from above — a rose tower and church front at the upper left, clustered white houses and tiled rooftops below the bed, further towers and house-fronts at the right — the whole reduced to islands of paint on bare plaster, with a dark ruined strip at the right edge and a fragment of patterned border at the lower right.
caption: The Dream of the Virgin ("Sogno della Vergine"), c. 1353–1355. Fresco, detached and transferred to canvas; 114 × 155 cm and inv. 6347 according to the museum's online record, not verified against the printed catalogues. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale. From the entrance wall of the church of Santa Maria di Mezzaratta, Bologna, lower left wing.

alt: Fragmentary fresco by Vitale da Bologna framed by a geometric border at top and left: at the centre a tall angel with great spread wings, in a pale blue-grey gown, bows towards a kneeling young woman in rose-pink who clasps her hands; behind them a standing woman in white folds her arms and another bends deeply forward, while at the upper left corner two women embrace; above, a flying angel leans over a plaster lacuna holding up a basket; at the right, beneath the striped thatched roof of a hut against dark foliage, a figure in a voluminous ochre mantle bends to pour water from a blue jug into a basin, attended by two women, with a tall haloed figure cut by the fragment's edge at far right; along the bottom survive a choir of haloed maidens at the left, one holding a disc, and a row of kneeling winged angels at the right; oval plaster losses interrupt the upper zone.
caption: The Archangel Gabriel ("L'Arcangelo Gabriele"), early 1340s. Fresco, detached and transferred to canvas, 252 × 249 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 6349. From the entrance wall of the church of Santa Maria di Mezzaratta, Bologna.

alt: Fragmentary fresco by Vitale da Bologna: at the upper left a haloed angel in white leans down out of a pale aureole, red wing-tips showing at the corner, towards a shepherd who kneels in profile at the centre, raising joined hands, dressed in an ochre tunic and a dark speckled sheepskin with a white pointed hood; at the right a second shepherd in a rose-red mantle bends away, a yellow horn at his belt; below, on dark ground, two sheep with striated fleeces graze head-down beside a third animal that sits upright with raised head and pricked ears; a red border strip closes the scene at the foot, a fragment of decorative border survives at the upper right, and heavy cracks and white gaps between the detached pieces run through the field.
caption: The Annunciation to the Shepherds ("Annuncio ai pastori"), early 1340s. Fresco (detached), 114 × 155 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 6348 — catalogued online under the title "Discesa di Cristo al Limbo". From the entrance wall of the church of Santa Maria di Mezzaratta, Bologna.

alt: Gable-shaped detached fresco by Vitale da Bologna mounted on a dark wall, built around a large circular oculus ringed by a red-and-white patterned border, its opening now filled with a blank panel: at the left the Archangel Gabriel kneels on one knee facing the window, blond and haloed, in a rose mantle over a gold-patterned white tunic, with wings of green and russet and a partly legible inscribed band arcing beside his halo; at the right of the oculus the Virgin stands slight and inward, a grey-violet mantle drawn over her head, hands crossed on her breast and head bowed, beside an ochre wooden lectern and the trace of a slender Gothic aedicule; vertical bands of acanthus scroll frame the outer edges, a rosette medallion survives low on the right, a patterned band runs along the base, and wide bare losses of plaster open above the oculus and through both figures' fields.
caption: The Annunciation ("Annunciazione"), 1340s–1350s. Detached fresco, in its gable-shaped field around the oculus of the entrance wall. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, Room 8. From the entrance wall of the church of Santa Maria di Mezzaratta, Bologna; inventory number and measurements not verified against the printed catalogues.

alt: Detached fresco by Vitale da Bologna with irregular plaster edges and strips of red border at the sides: against a blue-grey ground scratched with small stars, the Virgin, in a rose-mauve mantle lined in green and drawn over a white veil, inclines her head towards the Christ Child seated at the right; her raised right hand pinches a thread at her breast above a white, gold-patterned cloth spread across her lap, and her left hand rests on the Child's arm; the Child, golden-curled and haloed, in a rose tunic, looks up at her open-mouthed and raises his left hand towards her; the lower corners of the plaster are lost.
caption: Madonna of the Embroidery (Madonna del Ricamo), 1330–1340. Detached fresco, 118 × 79 cm. Bologna, Museo della Storia di Bologna (Palazzo Pepoli), Fondazione Carisbo collection. From the basilica of San Francesco, Bologna.

alt: Stone funerary monument set against a pier in San Martino Maggiore, Bologna: a tall rectangular frame of carved stone with a moulded border, three quatrefoil medallions along the top — a larger one at the centre with a figure in relief, two smaller ones at the sides with carved emblems — enclosing a glazed recess in which an irregular fragment of fresco survives on a pale ground: the head of the dead Christ, eyes closed, inclined towards his right shoulder, long hair falling, within a large gold halo with ornamented cross-arms, set against the brown beam of the cross and the dark ground above it, with the edge of the shoulder below; beneath the recess a stone tablet carries a six-line epitaph in Gothic majuscule, flanked by two carved quatrefoil panels.
caption: Fragment of a Crucifixion: the Head of the Dead Christ, c. 1355–1360. Fresco, set within the tomb monument of Stefano Ayguani. Bologna, basilica of San Martino Maggiore, fifth pier on the right. Attributed by Cesare Gnudi (1962).

alt: Square gold-ground panel by Vitale da Bologna: at the centre the dead Christ is shown half-length, rising from the edge of his tomb, his greenish body naked, his head with long brown hair fallen onto his right shoulder and his eyes closed; his arms are crossed low over his body, the wounds in his hands and the wound in his side bleeding in thin red streams, and a faint halo is incised in the gold behind his head; at the left, much smaller, Saint Christopher in a yellow tunic over red strides forward, leaning on a dark palm-staff and carrying the Christ Child, in pink, on his shoulder; at the right Saint Anthony Abbot, bearded and hooded in a dark brown habit, stands with his hands joined in prayer.
caption: Christ in Pity between Saints Anthony Abbot and Christopher ("Gesù Cristo in pietà fra i Santi Antonio Abate e Cristoforo"), c. 1355. Tempera on panel, 53.5 × 54 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 6994. Probably from the suppressed convent of San Giovanni Battista, Bologna.

alt: Gold-ground panel by Vitale da Bologna with a polylobed arched frame in gilded pastiglia worked with foliage: the Virgin, in a mantle so dark it reads as black, edged with gold over a green lining, her blond hair showing beneath the veil, holds the half-naked Christ Child wrapped in pale rose on her left arm; both turn their large, heavy-lidded eyes down to the left, and the Child raises his right hand in blessing; in the lower left corner a group of small flagellants in white hooded habits, one hood marked with a cross, kneels in prayer behind a slender processional crucifix, the foremost holding a dark scourge; along the foot of the panel a white band carries the signature .VITALIS. DE BONONIA. F.
caption: Madonna dei Battuti ("Stendardo (?): Madonna dei Battuti"), 1345–1350. Tempera and gold on polylobed panel, frame in gilded pastiglia, 95.6 × 68 cm. Signed at the foot. Vatican City, Pinacoteca Vaticana, inv. MV.40017.0.0. From the church of the Ospedale dei Battuti Bianchi, Ferrara.

alt: Tall gold-ground panel by Vitale da Bologna with the three crosses of Calvary: at the centre Christ hangs on a high yellow cross, his grey-green body sagging, while small angels fly about his wounds; the two thieves hang on lower crosses at the sides, their arms bent back over the crossbeams, a tiny angel rising by the thief at the left and a small dark winged devil perched on the cross of the thief at the right; below, at the left, the Virgin in a bright blue mantle collapses into the arms of the holy women as the long-haired Magdalene grasps the shaft of the cross, with soldiers in pale hats and lances behind; at the centre and right a troop of cavalry crowds in — a horse masked in black netted mail with gilt ornaments, a white and a brown horse, an armoured centurion raising his hand — while bearded elders argue, a bare-backed man in green twists away, and in the lower corner soldiers crouch to cast lots over a white garment; blood runs down the cross to the rocky mound, beneath which a complete skeleton lies in a dark cavity at the foot of the panel.
caption: The Crucifixion, c. 1335. Tempera and gold on panel, 93 × 51.2 cm. Madrid, Museo Nacional Thyssen-Bornemisza, inv. 425 (1930.122). Photo: © Museo Nacional Thyssen-Bornemisza, Madrid.

alt: Shaped panel by Vitale da Bologna in an engaged gilded frame with a trefoil arch, the black spandrels holding two winged creatures, a haloed angel with a red book at the left and an eagle-headed figure with an inscribed scroll at the right: at the centre Christ hangs on a pale blue-grey cross against gold tooled with scrolling foliage, his corpse-toned body sagging, blood springing from his hands and running down the shaft from his feet, a curling titulus above his head; at the left the Virgin in a black mantle collapses into the arms of the holy women while the golden-haired Magdalene in red kneels and grasps the foot of the cross, and soldiers behind them drive a long lance upwards into Christ's side beneath a teal banner; at the right a bearded man in a red hood prays upwards amid armoured soldiers under an orange banner, a horse in chain mail turns its caparisoned rump to the viewer, and at the lower corner a group of men stretches out a white garment between them, swords at their belts.
caption: The Crucifixion, with symbols of Saints Matthew and John the Evangelist, c. 1335. Tempera and tooled gold on panel, 62.1 × 40 cm. Philadelphia, Philadelphia Museum of Art, John G. Johnson Collection, 1917, cat. 1164. Made in Bologna. Photo: Philadelphia Museum of Art. Image for educational use only.

alt: Arched gold-ground panel by Vitale da Bologna with its original mouldings: the Virgin sits at the left on a bench throne in a black, gold-hemmed mantle, holding the lively Child, who leans far out of her arms to lay his hand on the white head of the eldest magus, kneeling in a yellow mantle with his crown set aside by his halo; behind him a second magus in grey-green flings an arm high towards the cusp while the youngest, in a red damask tunic and yellow hose, carries a casket; an angel with red wings hovers at the upper left and a pale veiled figure at the upper right; at the lower left stand two crowned virgin saints, Ursula with her staff and companions crowding behind her and Catherine pointing, with her spiked golden wheel; at the lower right two grooms in tall hats wait among dark trees with the magi's horses, two pale and one dark.
caption: The Adoration of the Magi, c. 1353–1355. Tempera and gold on panel, 60.4 × 38.6 cm including the original mouldings. Edinburgh, National Galleries of Scotland, NG 952 (purchased 1908). Left wing of a diptych; the right wing, The Body of Christ Mourned by Saints, is in the Fondazione Longhi, Florence.

alt: Arched gold-ground panel by Vitale da Bologna in its engaged gilded frame, the four winged symbols of the Evangelists in the spandrels — the angel and the eagle at the upper left, the lion and the ox at the upper right: at the centre the dead Christ stands upright in a red sarcophagus, grey-green, his head fallen on his shoulder and his arms hanging over the rim, the side wound visible; the Virgin in a black mantle holds him from behind with both hands spread on his chest; at the left the Baptist in camel hair crosses his hands on his breast beside a young fair-haired mourner in red, and at the right the Magdalene, golden-haired and dressed in red, joins her hands in prayer; below, a white shroud hangs over the front of the tomb, flanked by two kneeling bishops in mitres and brocade copes with raised hands — at the left with an aged, bearded hermit in grey-blue behind him, at the right with a young female saint in green.
caption: The Body of Christ Mourned by Saints (Christ in Piety), c. 1353–1355. Tempera and gold on panel. Florence, Fondazione di Studi di Storia dell'Arte Roberto Longhi. Right wing of the diptych whose left wing, The Adoration of the Magi, is in the National Galleries of Scotland, Edinburgh.

alt: Gold-ground panel by Vitale da Bologna: before a sumptuous cloth of honour diapered in green, gold, blue and red lozenges, whose upper edge three angels hold aloft draped with a white swag, Christ sits at the right on a red-cushioned bench in a rose mantle and sets the crown with both hands on the head of the Virgin, who kneels at the left in a near-black mantle finely striated with gold, her hands crossed on her breast and her head bowed; clusters of punched haloes crowd both sides, a tall angel in yellow at the left holds up a dark disc rimmed in red, and at the right an aged, bearded saint in a silver damask robe prays with joined hands; the gold ground is crackled and worn at the lower edge.
caption: The Coronation of the Virgin ("Le Couronnement de la Vierge"), 14th century. Gold ground on poplar panel, 52 × 57 cm. Paris, Musée du Louvre, Département des Peintures, inv. RF 1996 19 (acquired 1996). Formerly Adolphe Stoclet collection, Brussels.

alt: Small panel by Vitale da Bologna, cut at the top and sides: on a throne with grey-green marble posts and an elaborately stepped base inlaid with coloured panels, before a cloth of honour patterned all over with rosettes of red, blue and green on gold, Christ, young and fair-haired, crowned and haloed, in a rose robe and mantle lined with green, sits at the right and raises his right hand high to set a small crown on the head of the Virgin, his left hand lifted beside her face; the Virgin sits at the left in a near-black mantle edged with gold and marked with gold stars at the shoulder and knee, her hands crossed on her breast and her head bowed towards him; both sit on a long red cushion embroidered with small gold flourishes; at the cut edges, left and right, survive fragments of angels.
caption: The Coronation of the Virgin, c. 1335–1340. Tempera and gold on panel, 42 × 30.5 cm. Budrio, Pinacoteca Civica Domenico Inzaghi, inv. C. 97. From the Inzaghi bequest (1824).

alt: Small gold-ground panel by Vitale da Bologna in a gilded tabernacle frame with pierced vine tracery and a crocketed ogival gable: the Virgin, in a dark blue robe and hooded mantle covered edge to edge with gold filigree ornament and a jewelled band across her brow, sits on the ground on a red carpet strewn with dark trefoils, inclining her head towards the half-naked Christ Child at her side, who looks up and touches her chin with one finger while she steadies him in a gold-shot green cloth; at the left stands Saint Catherine with her wheel and a green book, at the right a second virgin saint with a slender attribute, both at reduced scale; beside the Child a small round table carries little flasks and a bowl, and the tooled gold ground radiates around the Virgin's halo.
caption: Madonna of Humility with Two Female Saints ("Madonna dell'Umiltà"), c. 1353. Tempera and gold on panel, 41 × 24 cm. Milan, Museo Poldi Pezzoli, inv. 1574 (bequest of Gian Giacomo Poldi Pezzoli, 1879).

alt: Small panel by Vitale da Bologna in its engaged gilded frame with a red fillet: against a gold ground overlaid with a red lattice enclosing green quatrefoils, the Virgin is seen bust-length in a dark blue-green mantle with a gold-embroidered border drawn over her head, her heavy-lidded eyes turned to the left; across her arms lies the Christ Child in a transparent gold-hemmed shift, a gold bracelet at his wrist, his head ringed by a halo with a red cross, looking out at the viewer; the Virgin's long right hand supports his legs, her punched halo presses against the patterned ground, and the gilding of the frame is worn and cracked.
caption: Madonna and Child ("Madonna della Pace"), 1345–1355. Mixed technique on panel. Forlì, Museo Civico San Domenico, on deposit from the Dominican Order since 2013. From the church of San Giacomo Apostolo of the Dominicans, Forlì.

alt: Shaped gold-ground panel by Vitale da Bologna, its trilobed arch framed by a twisted-rope moulding with small notches at the spring of the arch: the Virgin, half-length in a deep blue mantle over a gold-embroidered collar band, her blond hair showing, inclines her head above an unusually large halo tooled with floral ornament that fills the arch; the Child, in a rose wrap shot with gold, twists in her arms away from her breast to look back over his shoulder and raise his right hand in blessing towards the lower right corner, where a small kneeling cardinal in a dark habit, a red wide-brimmed hat on his head, prays with joined hands, presented by a taller haloed figure in a pointed, crown-ringed headdress holding a thin staff; the gilding and punchwork are rubbed throughout.
caption: Madonna and Child with a Cardinal and a Holy Bishop, c. 1341–1350. Tempera and gold on panel. Viterbo, Museo Civico. Connected in the Fondazione Federico Zeri catalogue with the church of Santa Maria della Pace, Viterbo.

alt: Tall, narrow fragmentary panel by Vitale da Bologna in two episodes against gold punched with arcs: above, beside a rose-pink monastery with blind arcading and a tall grey tower, the haloed, bearded Anthony in a dark habit grasps a thin rope hanging from the tower and clasps the hand of a bowing monk who carries a gold lantern, while an older face watches from the doorway at the left; below, in a night-dark thicket of stippled bushes over red-brown rock, Anthony kneels and stretches a hand towards a Gothic fountain with a hexagonal basin and a white statuette on its stem, his lantern-bearing companion behind him; a golden-brown winged creature lies in the water of the basin, and at the lower right a man in a red tunic lies on his back with a hand raised towards the saint; the panel's edges are ragged where the paint breaks off.
caption: Stories of Saint Anthony Abbot: Anthony leaves the monastery of Patras; Anthony defeats the dragon that appeared to him at the spring, c. 1340–1345. Tempera on panel, 79 × 37 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 10042, Room 1 (on deposit since 1937; ICCD cat. 00065211). From the dismembered ensemble whose lost central image was signed Vitalis f(ecit).

alt: Tall, narrow fragmentary panel by Vitale da Bologna in two episodes: above, set against gold punched with arcs, an open red loggia with a dark tiled roof holds a king lying in bed under a striped coverlet, addressed by a man in a broad hat while a dark-skinned attendant in blue and white stands at the bedside and a flowering tree rises on the gold at the left; below, in a dense night-dark wood over a rose-coloured track, two laden camels descend at the left, one carrying a pannier of round loaves, while a wheel sheathed in blue flames hovers among the bushes at the centre, two brown-robed companions raise their hands towards it, and the haloed Anthony kneels in prayer at the lower right with gold rays scratched around him; the panel's edges are ragged with losses.
caption: Stories of Saint Anthony Abbot: a beggar urges the King of Palestine to send provisions to Anthony in the desert; the camels arrive, led by the wheel of fire, c. 1340–1345. Tempera on panel, 77 × 39 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 10039, Room 1 (on deposit since 1937; ICCD cat. 00065212). From the same dismembered ensemble.

alt: Tall, narrow fragmentary panel by Vitale da Bologna: against a gold sky punched with arcs, a great dark tree spreads at the top, and from its branch hangs a red-haired youth in a white shirt, his eyes closed; beneath his feet stands the haloed Anthony in grey, upholding the body, while a man in a white cap climbs the trunk at the right to reach the rope and a small man in yellow with a blue cap hoists a ladder; at the left a crowd of kin — veiled women, bearded men in orange and red — raise their hands in supplication; behind them a walled pink city with its gate stands at the left and a pink chapel beside blue water at the right; in the lower zone Anthony appears again, bending deeply with scratched gold rays over a fallen man whose red-clad body lies at the corner; the panel's edges are ragged.
caption: Stories of Saint Anthony Abbot: after his death Anthony supports the body of Efron, unjustly hanged; Anthony revives the men killed by wild beasts, c. 1340–1345. Tempera on panel, 78.5 × 38.5 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 10041, Room 1 (on deposit since 1937; ICCD cat. 00065215). From the same dismembered ensemble.

alt: Tall, narrow fragmentary panel by Vitale da Bologna: the saint's body in a black habit, its flesh darkened, lies on a bier draped with a red and gold brocade pall, tilted steeply towards the lower left on a cart with a great spoked wheel, red fire bursting beneath it; at the right a bishop in a white cope and mitre joins his hands among tonsured clergy; two richly dressed young women press towards the bier, one in a patterned rose gown reaching out, the other kneeling in a gown of dark netting; at the left a crowned emperor in red, blue and gold, attended by a man in a tall blue hat and courtiers, watches from a raised stand beneath a pink balcony; in the lower zone a crowd climbs through a black doorway onto a pavement of black and white triangles — hooded men, a youth in yellow with red hose, a woman with loose red hair; the gold ground is punched with arcs and the edges are ragged.
caption: Stories of Saint Anthony Abbot: the funeral of Saint Anthony, with the healing of Sofia, daughter of the Emperor Constantine, before Bishop Theophilus, c. 1340–1345. Tempera on panel, 78.5 × 38.5 cm. Bologna, Pinacoteca Nazionale, inv. 10040, Room 1 (on deposit since 1937; ICCD cat. 00065213).

alt: A wide paved square under a blue sky. At the left rises a large Baroque church of pale sandstone with a two-tower facade, a central pediment and two low domed side chapels. At the right, beyond a cypress and a terrace wall, stands a smaller medieval church of reddish stone with a round tower with a tall conical roof and a square tower with a pyramidal roof.
caption: Fulda, the cathedral square with the Baroque cathedral (left), built on the site of the Ratgar basilica, and St Michael’s Church (right). Photo: Verum, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Interior of a round church. Eight stout stone columns with simple capitals stand in a ring, carrying round arches above which a cylindrical wall rises to a gallery and a timber ceiling. Through the arches an altar is visible at the centre, and beyond, a small apse with a window. Around the columns runs a curved ambulatory with arched openings in the outer wall. The walls are plastered in warm ochre with red borders and fragments of painting.
caption: Fulda, St Michael’s Church, the rotunda, built 820–822 under Abbot Eigil and raised in the tenth and eleventh centuries. © Superbass / CC BY-SA 4.0 (via Wikimedia Commons), original.

alt: Frontal view of a large Baroque church of pale and reddish sandstone. Two tall towers with clocks and onion-shaped domes flank a central gabled front with columns, statues in niches and a large coat of arms over the main door; behind the gable a dome with a lantern and a statue. Low wings with grey domes extend to either side. A wide paved square in the foreground with a few people.
caption: Johann Dientzenhofer, Fulda Cathedral (St Salvator and St Boniface), 1704–1712, west front. © Raimond Spekking / CC BY-SA 4.0 (via Wikimedia Commons).

alt: A large altar of black marble with white veining set in a white vaulted chapel. Black columns with white Corinthian capitals frame a white alabaster relief of a bishop kneeling before soldiers, one of whom swings a sword. Above the cornice a coat of arms flanked by putti and a cross; at the sides two large white angels. The front of the altar table, covered with a purple cloth, is a second relief of a bishop rising from a tomb while angels lift the lid. Iron candlesticks stand on either side.
caption: Johann Neudecker the Elder (reliefs), tomb altar of Saint Boniface, early eighteenth century. Black marble and alabaster. Fulda Cathedral, crypt of Boniface. Photo: Harvey Kneeslapper, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Alabaster relief in a round-arched black marble frame. A bearded bishop in a richly ornamented chasuble kneels at the right and lifts a book above his head as a soldier in armour at the left raises a sword; other soldiers crowd behind. A mitre and a crozier lie on the ground; in the sky above, putti among clouds carry a wreath and a palm. In the background a tent.
caption: Johann Neudecker the Elder, the martyrdom of Saint Boniface, relief of the tomb altar. Alabaster. Fulda Cathedral, crypt of Boniface. Photo: Gerd Eichmann, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: White alabaster relief on the front of an altar table. A bearded bishop in mitre and vestments rises from a sarcophagus, his hands resting on its edge, while a winged angel at the right supports his mitre and a second angel at the upper left lifts the heavy slanting lid. Folds of a shroud fill the lower part.
caption: Johann Neudecker the Elder, Saint Boniface rising from the tomb, relief on the front of the tomb altar. Alabaster. Fulda Cathedral, crypt of Boniface. Photo: Gerd Eichmann, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: An open manuscript with two pages of parchment written in brown ink in an irregular early medieval script, with red and orange initials and display lines. The left page ends with an ornament of two circles linked by a knot; the right page has the red titles EXPLICIT EPISTULA AGNELLI and INCIPIT LIBELLUM FAUSTI CONFESSORIS and a large initial formed of interlaced fish and a cross in orange, yellow and brown. Deep vertical cuts run into the parchment from the top and bottom edges of both pages, and there are two round holes.
caption: Codex Ragyndrudis, fols. 38v–39r, with the end of the letter of Agnellus and the beginning of a treatise attributed to Faustus, c. 700. Ink and colours on parchment. Fulda, Hochschul- und Landesbibliothek, Codex Bonifatianus 2. Image: Hochschul- und Landesbibliothek Fulda, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Low vaulted crypt with plastered walls. In the centre a short thick stone column with a broad capital carved with two large spiral volutes supports the springing of the vault. At the right, against the curved wall, a small rectangular altar of rough stone blocks stands on a step beneath an arched niche closed by an iron grille. Faint traces of red painted lines on the vault.
caption: Fulda, St Michael’s Church, the crypt with its central column, 820–822. Photo: Qwertzu111111, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Manuscript page with a grid of capital letters in brown ink within a pale blue frame. Over the grid is painted a frontal figure of Christ with arms outstretched, a cross-nimbus in red and gold, a short red loincloth and bare legs, the letters within his body written in red and forming separate verses. The figure covers the grid from top to bottom.
caption: Hrabanus Maurus, In honorem sanctae crucis, carmen I: Christ with outstretched arms, ninth century. Ink and colours on parchment. Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, lat. 2422. Source: gallica.bnf.fr / Bibliothèque nationale de France.

alt: Manuscript page with a dense square grid of capital letters within a purple frame. Groups of letters are set off in small squares of red, green and gold, forming a large cross-shaped pattern across the grid and spelling separate verses.
caption: Hrabanus Maurus, In honorem sanctae crucis, figure poem with a cross formed of highlighted letters, ninth century. Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, lat. 2422. Source: gallica.bnf.fr / Bibliothèque nationale de France.

alt: Manuscript page with a grid of capital letters within a purple frame. A large grey-green cross is painted over the grid, its arms filled with letters. At the lower right a small monk in a grey habit kneels with his hands raised towards the cross; red letters inside his figure form a separate verse.
caption: Hrabanus Maurus, In honorem sanctae crucis, the final poem with the cross and the author kneeling in prayer, ninth century. Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, lat. 2422. Source: gallica.bnf.fr / Bibliothèque nationale de France.

alt: A long pale stone church seen from the side under a blue sky. At the right rises a square bell tower with arched openings and a very tall pointed stone spire with pinnacles. In the centre a square crossing tower with a low pyramidal roof stands above the choir, around which radiating chapels with small round roofs step down. At the left a long range of seventeenth-century conventual buildings with dormer windows ends in a round tower. Trees fill the foreground.
caption: Saint-Savin-sur-Gartempe, the abbey seen from the bridge over the Gartempe: the tower-porch with its spire, the nave, the crossing tower and the chevet, and the Maurist conventual buildings at the left. Photo: GuyFrancis, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: View straight up a tall nave. Slender cylindrical columns painted with wavy marbling and crowned by carved foliage capitals line both sides. Above them a continuous barrel vault is covered from end to end with painted friezes of figures, buildings and a ship, in ochre, red, green and white, divided lengthwise by an ornamental band. In the distance the vault is crossed by arches.
caption: The nave looking west: the painted barrel vault over the six eastern bays, continuous and without transverse arches, carried on tall cylindrical columns. Photo: Debressac, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A painted barrel vault seen from directly below. A narrow ornamental band runs down the middle; on either side two long registers of narrative scenes in ochre, brown and green, among them a large ship with arched windows. At the edges carved capitals and the tops of columns appear against a wall painted with false masonry. In the lower part of the image a transverse arch with painted roundels crosses the vault.
caption: The nave vault seen from below, with the Ark of Noah on the right-hand slope and, at the bottom, the first transverse arch of the western bays. Source: Web Gallery of Art, public domain.

alt: A faded wall painting. At the top a haloed figure with a cross-nimbus leans out from a curved band of sky, holding up two discs: one with a face surrounded by rays, the other pale. Below, on a white ground, stands a tree with three umbrella-shaped crowns, and beside it a second tree; the lower part of the painting is largely lost.
caption: The Creation of the sun and moon, with the trees of the third day, c. 1100. Wall painting. Saint-Savin-sur-Gartempe, nave vault. Photo: GO69, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A wall painting in tones of ochre. At the left a haloed figure bends over a naked man lying asleep on the ground and draws a woman from his side. In the centre the haloed figure, in a long robe and mantle, holds the woman by the hand and leads her towards the man, who stands naked at the right, his hand raised. At the far right part of another naked figure stands beside a tree.
caption: The Creation of Eve and God presenting Eve to Adam, c. 1100. Wall painting. Saint-Savin-sur-Gartempe, nave vault. Source: Web Gallery of Art, public domain.

alt: A damaged wall painting with ornamental borders above. At the left a man in a red mantle that billows behind him swings a club down on a figure in a yellow robe who has fallen to the ground before a dark red background. In the centre a tall haloed figure in a green mantle stands with one hand raised, turned towards a bearded man in a yellow and red mantle at the right, who raises his hand to his face.
caption: Cain kills Abel; God questions Cain, c. 1100. Wall painting. Saint-Savin-sur-Gartempe, nave vault. Photo: GO69, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A large wall painting of a ship with a curved hull of red-brown planks, its prow ending in an animal head. On the hull stand three tiers of arched cabins: at the bottom animals such as a lion, a goat and a bear; in the middle birds; at the top pairs of human heads. Two men stand on the ends of the hull holding the roof. A small house stands at the stern, a dove flies at the right, and drowned bodies float in the white water below.
caption: The Ark of Noah, c. 1100. Wall painting. Saint-Savin-sur-Gartempe, nave vault. Photo: GO69, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A wall painting with ornamental bands at the top. At the left a group of men and women stands before a haloed figure in an ochre and green mantle, who stretches out his arm. At the right an old bearded man in a pale mantle kneels before a draped altar holding a bird, with a lamb beside him, while a haloed figure in a dark mantle leans towards him from a frame at the right with a gesture of blessing. Below, part of another register is visible.
caption: Noah and his family after the Flood, and the sacrifice of Noah, c. 1100. Wall painting. Saint-Savin-sur-Gartempe, nave vault. Photo: GO69, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Two registers of wall painting. Above, at the left, a haloed figure stands beside a stylised tree and gestures towards a crowd of builders around a tower of brick drawn in perspective, its top open; men inside the tower take blocks handed up to them, while at the right a line of workers carries large blocks on their shoulders, the last a tall man in a green tunic lifting a block above his head. Below, damaged scenes with the inscription IOSEPH, a building and a woman at a doorway.
caption: The Building of the Tower of Babel (above) and scenes from the story of Joseph (below), c. 1100. Wall painting. Saint-Savin-sur-Gartempe, nave vault. Photo: GO69, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A wall painting on a white and ochre ground. At the left a haloed figure with a cross-nimbus, in a white robe and red mantle, raises one hand in blessing and stretches the other towards a bearded man in a long ochre mantle who bends forward with both hands held out. At the far left a vertical band of ornament contains roundels with busts.
caption: The Lord gives his instructions to Abraham, c. 1100. Wall painting. Saint-Savin-sur-Gartempe, nave vault. Photo: Antoine Garnier, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Two registers of wall painting under an ornamental border. Above, at the left, the Lord speaks to Abraham; then a tree with three rounded crowns with a small figure in it; then a group of men and women walking to the right led by a man in a long mantle with raised hands; at the right a damaged area with a figure and buildings. Below, horsemen and figures on foot moving to the right, and at the right a figure offering a dish to a seated old man.
caption: The cycle of Abraham in the western bays of the nave, c. 1100. Wall painting. Saint-Savin-sur-Gartempe, nave vault. Photo: GuyFrancis, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A damaged wall painting framed by an ornamental band with roundels at the right. In the lower register a man in a yellow mantle moves away to the left from a building; a woman in a green dress stands in an arched doorway; at the right, in another arch, a woman in a yellow mantle stands beside a small figure whose cloak she seems to hold. Above, the feet and robes of figures of another register.
caption: Scenes from the story of Joseph, with Joseph and the wife of Potiphar, c. 1100. Wall painting. Saint-Savin-sur-Gartempe, nave vault. Photo: GO69, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A wall painting with the inscription IOSEPH in large letters on an ochre panel. At the left a crowned king in a white robe and ochre mantle sits on a throne flanked by two creatures with red bodies, holding a staff. Before him a man in a green tunic leads a figure in a pink robe by the hand. At the right, inside a walled building, a figure crouches in a round enclosure.
caption: Joseph brought before Pharaoh, and Joseph in prison, c. 1100. Wall painting. Saint-Savin-sur-Gartempe, nave vault. Photo: GO69, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Two registers of wall painting. Above, Cain and Abel and the Lord. Below, a white sea with wavy lines in which horsemen on white horses and a two-wheeled chariot drawn by yellow horses plunge forward; a figure in the chariot raises a hand, another holds a shield, and a fallen soldier lies under the horses. Large areas of plaster are lost.
caption: The Egyptians engulfed in the Red Sea (below), with Cain and Abel above, c. 1100. Wall painting. Saint-Savin-sur-Gartempe, nave vault. Photo: GO69, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A wall painting. In the centre a haloed figure in a white robe and red mantle stands within a pointed mandorla and holds out two tablets to an old bearded man in an ochre mantle, who kneels at the left and receives them. At the left two angels blow long horns; at the right a third angel holds a horn. Above, the feet of figures of the upper register; the right side is largely lost.
caption: Moses receives the Tables of the Law, with angels blowing horns, c. 1100. Wall painting. Saint-Savin-sur-Gartempe, nave vault. Photo: GO69, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A wall painting. At the left a haloed man sits on a chest, raising one hand to his face. Above him, within an arc of heaven, a building with towers shelters a small golden chest. In the centre a haloed woman, with wings at her back, sits on a globe holding a haloed child, whom an angel lifts upward. At the right a great red dragon with several heads and a long coiling tail rears towards her, spewing a white stream.
caption: The Woman clothed with the Sun and the Dragon, with the Ark of the Covenant in the Temple and John the Evangelist (Apocalypse 11–12), c. 1100. Wall painting. Saint-Savin-sur-Gartempe, vestibule of the tower-porch. Source: Wikimedia Commons, public domain.

alt: A round-headed niche set in a wall painted with false stone joints. In the niche a crowned Virgin sits frontally on a throne within a double mandorla, holding the crowned Christ Child on her lap. At either side angels emerge from clouds swinging censers, and kneeling figures pray beside the throne. Small carved corbels with shields support the sill.
caption: The Virgin and Child enthroned with censing angels and kneeling monks, late twelfth or early thirteenth century. Wall painting. Saint-Savin-sur-Gartempe, west wall of the nave. Photo: PMRMaeyaert, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A wall painting on a dark red ground with buildings and towers along the top. At the left a figure sits enthroned in judgement. Before him executioners in short tunics bend two naked men backwards and tear at their bodies with long hooks, while other figures look on. An arch spans the centre of the scene.
caption: Saints Savin and Cyprian tortured before the judge, c. 1100. Wall painting. Saint-Savin-sur-Gartempe, crypt. Source: Web Gallery of Art, public domain.

alt: The Last Supper
caption: Domenico Ghirlandaio (1449-1494), The Last Supper, 1476, fresco, Badia di San Michele Arcangelo, Passignano.

alt: Expulsion from Paradise and Cain and Abel
caption: Bernardo di Stefano Rosselli (c. 1450–1526), Expulsion from Paradise and Cain and Abel, 1474, fresco, Badia di San Michele Arcangelo, Passignano.

alt: Episodes from the life of Giovanni Gualberto
caption: Alessandro Allori (1535–1607), Episodes from the life of Giovanni Gualberto, 1581, fresco, Badia di San Michele Arcangelo, Passignano.

alt: Eternal father with playing angels
caption: Domenico Cresti (1559–1638), Eternal Father with playing angels, 1601, fresco, Cappella Maggiore, Badia di San Michele Arcangelo, Passignano.

alt: funerary monument and sculpted effigy of San Giovanni Gualberto
caption: Giovanni Battista Caccini (1556-1613), Funerary monument and effigy of Saint John Gualbert, 1580, marble, Saint John Gualbert chapel, Badia di San Michele Arcangelo, Passignano.
