alt: Front of a small stone church seen from the west, standing on a lawn among bare trees. A tall gabled porch of mixed brick and rubble masonry opens in a single large round arch onto a dark atrium with a wooden door at the back. Behind it rises the higher gable of the nave with a small round window, and at the sides the curved walls of two apses with low roofs, one with a barred window.
caption: Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, the west front with the narthex rebuilt with a single arch in the seventeenth century. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Exterior of a small church seen from the east on a grassy mound under a cloudy sky. Two large semicircular apses with buttresses and low curved tiled roofs project from the body of the church: the one at the left is plastered, with a barred round-headed window, the one at the right is of exposed rubble and plaster with a large window. Between them rises the wall of the nave with two small arched windows, and at the far left a lower stone building with a brick doorway.
caption: Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, the apses seen from the east. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Interior of a small church looking east. The nave walls are of bare rubble masonry with small round-headed windows high up at both sides. In the end wall a wide round arch opens into an apse, in which frescoes are visible: a roundel with the bust of Christ above a single arched window, and fragments of scenes around it. Below the frescoes the apse wall is bare stone. Low posts with a rope guard the apse; information panels on easels stand at the right.
caption: Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, the nave looking towards the eastern apse. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Wide view of the curved wall of an apse with three arched windows. Fragmentary frescoes cover the upper part of the wall in two registers above a zone of bare masonry. Above the central window a roundel with the bust of Christ; to the left and right narrative scenes with figures, architecture and angels, partly lost. The lower part of the wall is rough stone and plaster.
caption: Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, the eastern apse with the fresco cycle. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Curved upper zone of an apse beneath a wooden ceiling. In the centre a large roundel framed in red contains the bust of Christ with a golden cross-nimbus against a blue ground. At the left a crowned priest in a jewelled robe holds a vessel to the lips of a woman in red, with an altar canopy behind them. At the right an angel in white flies towards a figure reclining in white, with a column hung with drapery at the left of the scene. Below the roundel the top of an arched window.
caption: Master of Castelseprio, The Trial of the Bitter Waters, the clipeus of Christ and the Dream of Joseph, ninth–tenth century, before 948. Fresco. Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, eastern apse, upper register. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Close view of a fresco roundel framed by a broad red band. Inside, against a blue ground, the bust of Christ with long reddish-brown hair parted in the middle, large dark eyes and a long nose, and a golden nimbus with a cross. He wears a red tunic with a gold clavus and blesses with his right hand; in his left hand he holds a rolled scroll. At the right edge a column with a drapery knotted around it; at the left part of a building.
caption: Master of Castelseprio, The clipeus of Christ, ninth–tenth century, before 948. Fresco. Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, eastern apse, above the central window. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Corner of an apse where the curved wall meets a side window, with fresco fragments in two registers and bare masonry below. In the upper register an angel in white flies towards a seated woman; in the lower register a temple-like building with figures in pale robes. A narrow window with a white light occupies the right side.
caption: Master of Castelseprio, The Annunciation and the Visitation, ninth–tenth century, before 948. Fresco. Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, eastern apse, north side, upper register. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Square fresco panel framed in red. At the left a haloed woman sits on a chair before a column and a building, holding a spindle, with a basket of wool beside her; behind her, at the far left, a woman looks out from a doorway and raises her hand. An angel with a pale nimbus and large wings strides in from above, holding a staff and stretching out his right hand towards the seated woman. At the far right a tall haloed woman in a long reddish mantle bends forward towards the left, part of a further scene, beside a large area of lost plaster.
caption: Master of Castelseprio, The Annunciation and the Visitation, ninth–tenth century, before 948. Fresco. Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, eastern apse, north side, upper register. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco fragment with a large area of lost plaster and exposed stone at the left. A woman with a golden halo, wrapped in a red mantle, drinks from a tall golden vessel held to her lips by a bearded old man with a blue halo, white hair and a tall headdress, who wears a red robe and a jewelled golden cloak studded with pearls. Behind them stands an altar under a round canopy on columns, with steps and a curved wall in pale tones. At the far left the bare feet of a third figure are visible below the lost area.
caption: Master of Castelseprio, The Trial of the Bitter Waters, ninth–tenth century, before 948. Fresco. Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, eastern apse, upper register. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Square fresco panel framed above and below by red bands. In the centre an angel with a pale grey nimbus and wings drawn with long strokes flies diagonally from the upper left towards the right, wearing a white tunic with gold bands and stretching out his right hand. Below him a figure reclines on a couch with a large blue-green cushion, wrapped in white and gold, his head propped on his hand. At the left a column with an ornate capital is hung with a knotted drapery; at the right a smaller column and a building with windows.
caption: Master of Castelseprio, The Dream of Joseph, ninth–tenth century, before 948. Fresco. Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, eastern apse, upper register. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Wide view of the south side of an apse, with an arched window in the centre and a pilaster at the right. In the upper left an angel flies towards a reclining figure; below it a temple building with figures in pale robes around an altar. To the right of the window, above, a woman with a halo rides a donkey led forward, with an old man walking behind; below, a woman reclines on a large white mattress, with a flying angel, sheep and a seated figure in blue. The lower half of the wall is bare stone and plaster.
caption: Master of Castelseprio, The Dream of Joseph, the Presentation in the Temple, the Journey to Bethlehem and the Nativity, ninth–tenth century, before 948. Fresco. Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, eastern apse, south side. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco panel surrounded by bare rubble masonry, with the edge of a window at the lower left. A young woman with a golden halo, wrapped in a long brown mantle, sits sideways on a brown donkey that walks towards the right. Behind her an old bearded man with white hair, in an ochre robe, bends forward leaning on a staff and stretches out his hand. Behind them stands a building with tall pale columns and an arched opening; at the far right the legs of a figure who leads the donkey. The ground is ochre, framed below by a red band.
caption: Master of Castelseprio, The Journey to Bethlehem, ninth–tenth century, before 948. Fresco. Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, eastern apse, south side, upper register. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco with many losses and small spots of later keying. At the left a haloed woman reclines on a large white mattress shaped like a crescent, wrapped in a grey-blue mantle, looking towards the centre. Below her a woman with a headscarf leans forward and another woman bends to the left over a lost area. In the centre a seated figure in a blue-green mantle. To the right an angel with large wings flies towards a shepherd with a staff, and sheep and goats graze among trees, with the walls and towers of a town in the background. A red band at the top separates the scene from the register above.
caption: Master of Castelseprio, The Nativity with the Annunciation to the Shepherds, ninth–tenth century, before 948. Fresco. Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, eastern apse, south side, lower register. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Detail of a fresco showing a hillside with goats and sheep, a young shepherd seated or reclining among them, and an angel flying in from above at the right, all in reddish and ochre tones on a pale ground, with many small spots of damage.
caption: Master of Castelseprio, The Annunciation to the Shepherds, detail of the Nativity, ninth–tenth century, before 948. Fresco. Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, eastern apse, south side, lower register. Photo: Rostkol, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco on the curved side of an arch, with the nave visible through the opening at the right. Above, in an ochre band, the lower part of a flying angel. Below, three men in short tunics, leggings and tall caps approach from the left: the first bends forward to offer a gift in a dish, the others follow with their gifts. They move towards a haloed woman seated on a throne at the upper right, holding a small child, with an angel flying above her pointing towards them. At the right a seated figure in a blue mantle; in the foreground a round box with its lid open.
caption: Master of Castelseprio, The Adoration of the Magi, ninth–tenth century, before 948. Fresco. Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, return of the triumphal arch. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Upper part of a triumphal arch in an ochre band beneath a wooden beam and ceiling. In the centre a large roundel framed in red contains a throne with a cushion and a cross with a pale nimbus. On either side an angel with a pale blue halo flies horizontally towards the centre, holding a globe in one hand and a long staff in the other. Below, the round opening of the arch shows the bare nave beyond, with two arched windows.
caption: Master of Castelseprio, The Etimasia between two angels, ninth–tenth century, before 948. Fresco. Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, triumphal arch, side facing the apse. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Close view of a fresco roundel framed in red on an ochre ground. Inside, a throne seen from above with a large cushion and drapery, surmounted by a pale grey-blue nimbus or crown shape and a small cross; a jewelled rosette appears on the front of the throne. At the sides, the globes held by the two flying angels, one blue-grey at the left, one pale at the right.
caption: Master of Castelseprio, The Etimasia, ninth–tenth century, before 948. Fresco. Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, triumphal arch, side facing the apse. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Detail of a fresco on an ochre ground. An angel with a pale blue halo and reddish-brown hair flies horizontally towards the right, his body wrapped in pale drapery, his wings spread behind him. In his left hand he holds a blue-grey globe surmounted by a small cross; a long staff runs diagonally across the field below him. At the left a large area of lost plaster.
caption: Master of Castelseprio, Angel with a globe, from the Etimasia, ninth–tenth century, before 948. Fresco. Castelseprio, Santa Maria foris portas, triumphal arch, side facing the apse. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Black-and-white photograph of a flat metal cross with square terminals, engraved all over. At the centre, a roundel shows the Lamb of God with a cross-staff, surrounded by an inscription. The four square terminals contain the evangelist symbols, each with a short inscription: the eagle at the top, the lion at the left, the ox at the right, the angel at the bottom. The arms carry scrolling foliage within borders of small stars; the lower shaft shows a standing archbishop in mitre and pallium holding a crozier and a book, under the inscription S MODOALDUS ARCHIEP. Small nail holes are visible along the edges.
caption: Helmarshausen workshop (formerly attributed to Roger of Helmarshausen), The Modoald Cross, back plate of a lost jewelled cross, c. 1107 (or 1120s). Engraved copper with traces of gilding, height 41.7 cm. Cologne, Museum Schnütgen, inv. G 579. Photo: Bildarchiv Foto Marburg / Albert Hirmer and Irmgard Ernstmeier-Hirmer, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

alt: Small rectangular casket on four bronze lion-paw feet, seen from above at an angle. The top is covered with engraved silver plates around a slab of green speckled marble framed by gold filigree, and a border set with cabochon stones and small gilt rosettes. The long side carries engraved gilt figures of seated apostles under arcades; the short end shows silver-gilt figures in relief, a seated Christ in a circular glory set with stones between two standing bishops. Inscribed silver bands run along the edges.
caption: Helmarshausen workshop (formerly attributed to Roger of Helmarshausen), Portable altar of Bishop Henry of Werl, c. 1120–1127. Oak core clad in partly gilt silver, engraved, nielloed and in repoussé; engraved gilt copper; gold and silver filigree; gems and pearls; gilt bronze feet with niello; altar stone of green marble; 16.5 × 21.2 × 34.5 cm. Paderborn, Hoher Dom, inv. DS 2, in the Erzbischöfliches Diözesanmuseum. Photo: Bildarchiv Foto Marburg / Michael Jeiter, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

alt: Short end of a metal casket. In the centre, within a circular glory set with stones and pearls, Christ sits on an arc, bearded, with a cross-nimbus, blessing with his right hand and holding an open book. At either side stands a bishop in chasuble and pallium with a crozier: the left one raises his hand in blessing, the right one holds an open book. Strips set with large cabochon stones frame the panel. The upper band is inscribed S KILIANUS, XPC and S LIBORIUS; the lower band reads OFFERT MENTE PIA DECUS HOC TIBI. The feet are decorated with a nielloed chequer pattern and end in lion paws.
caption: Portable altar of Bishop Henry of Werl, short end with Christ enthroned between Saints Kilian and Liborius. Photo: Bildarchiv Foto Marburg / Erich Müller-Cassel, CC BY-SA 4.0.

alt: Long side of a metal casket. On a gilt copper plate with a stippled ground, five apostles sit on thrones under a row of round arches carried by twisted and fluted columns, with scrolling foliage in the spandrels; the central figure holds keys. The upper band is inscribed S THADDEUS, S ANDREAS, S PETRUS, S THOMAS, S SYMON. Above, the top shows the green altar stone in a filigree frame between engraved silver plates. The base and feet are of silver and nielloed bronze.
caption: Portable altar of Bishop Henry of Werl, long side with five enthroned apostles, Peter at the centre. Photo: Bildarchiv Foto Marburg / Albert Hirmer and Irmgard Ernstmeier-Hirmer, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

alt: Rectangular casket on gilt lion-paw feet, seen from the long side. The top has a dark altar stone in a silver frame between silver plates with openwork figures. The long side is a continuous frieze of gilt copper in openwork against a dark ground: at left a man stands beside an idol on a column; a crowned ruler on a throne, with two hanging lamps above, hands a sword to a mounted soldier with a shield; soldiers in mail with shields and spears follow; an executioner swings his sword over a kneeling figure whose head falls to the ground; at right a figure raises his hands among fallen bodies and a rider.
caption: Westphalia or the Weser region (Helmarshausen?), Portable altar from the Benedictine abbey of Abdinghof, long side with the refusal of Felix to worship the idol, the ruler handing a sword to a horseman, and the beheading of the saint and his companions, c. 1120–1130. Oak core, engraved gilt copper in openwork (opus interrasile) over brown varnish, silver sheet, gilt bronze feet. Paderborn, Erzbischöfliches Diözesanmuseum, inv. PR 50 (on loan from the Franciscan friary). Photo: Bildarchiv Foto Marburg / Albert Hirmer and Irmgard Ernstmeier-Hirmer, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

alt: Black-and-white photograph of a full-page miniature. Within a broad frame of interlaced chain ornament, the evangelist Matthew, haloed and bearded, in a tunic and a mantle with dark striped folds, stands before drawn curtains between two twisted columns with foliate capitals. At the left a lectern holds an open book; he rests one hand on it and holds a closed book in the other. Above, in the gable of a pediment edged with scrolls, his symbol, a winged angel, holds a book.
caption: Helmarshausen, The evangelist Matthew, fol. 14v of the oldest Helmarshausen Gospels, first quarter of the twelfth century. Tempera and gold on parchment. Trier, Dombibliothek, Hs. 139 (Domschatz 68). Photo (1935): Bildarchiv Foto Marburg, CC BY-SA 4.0.

alt: Black-and-white photograph of the inside of a book cover lined with a woven silk. The pattern shows large interlocking roundels with pearl-like borders and smaller rosettes at their intersections; in the centre of one roundel a stylised plant motif. A small printed label at the upper right reads EX BIBLIOTHECA ECCLESIAE CATHEDRALIS TREVIRENSIS.
caption: Oldest Helmarshausen Gospels, inside of the front cover, lined with a Byzantine silk of the ninth century. Trier, Dombibliothek, Hs. 139. Photo (1966): Bildarchiv Foto Marburg, CC BY-SA 4.0.

alt: Full-page miniature in a frame of colourful foliate ornament. Under a heading in gold and silver capitals, INICIUM SCI EVANGELII SCDM LUCAM, the evangelist Luke, haloed, with long dark hair, sits on a cushioned chair with a high back before a gold rectangle on a blue ground. Wrapped in a green mantle over a pink tunic with a red cloak, he looks up and sharpens his quill with a knife. A scroll falls from a lectern on a baluster at the right, inscribed Fuit in diebus Herodis.
caption: Helmarshausen, Saint Luke, fol. 83v of a Gospel book, c. 1120–1140. Tempera colours, gold and silver on parchment, 22.9 × 16.5 cm. Los Angeles, J. Paul Getty Museum, Ms. Ludwig II 3. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Full-page decorated text page. Within a border of fret pattern in blue, green and white with gilt bosses, a large gold initial Q filled with interlaced foliage in gold and silver on blue and green grounds occupies the upper left. The following letters, QUONIAM QUIDEM MULTI CONATI SUNT ORDINARE NARRATIONEM, are written in alternating gold and silver capitals. The background imitates a woven textile with a pattern of pinkish-red arches and palmettes.
caption: Helmarshausen, decorated opening of the Gospel of Luke, Quoniam quidem multi, fol. 84 of the same Gospel book. Los Angeles, J. Paul Getty Museum, Ms. Ludwig II 3. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Full-page miniature in a frame of interlace and fret ornament. Under the heading INITIUM SCI EVANGELII SCDM IOHANNEM, the evangelist John, haloed and bearded, sits on a cushioned throne before a gold rectangle on a blue ground, wearing an orange mantle over a green tunic and a blue robe falling over his knees; he holds a pen-knife and an unrolled scroll inscribed In principio erat. At the right a lectern on a twisted column carries an open book.
caption: Helmarshausen, Saint John, from the same Gospel book. Los Angeles, J. Paul Getty Museum, Ms. Ludwig II 3. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Full-page decorated text page. A tall initial I of interlaced gold and silver ribbons with foliage on blue and green grounds runs down the left side, followed at upper right by a gold and silver N. The words of the opening of John, IN PRINCIPIO ERAT VERBUM ET VERBUM ERAT APUD DEUM, are written below in gold and silver capitals. The ground imitates a textile with pinkish-red roundels and rosettes, and the page is framed by striped bands with roundels containing gilt rosettes.
caption: Helmarshausen, decorated opening of the Gospel of John, In principio erat verbum, fol. 128 of the same Gospel book. Los Angeles, J. Paul Getty Museum, Ms. Ludwig II 3. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Full-page miniature of a standing woman on a gold ground, within a frame of gold fleur-de-lis stems on a blue and green ground with gold quatrefoils at the corners. She wears a white veil and a long pale robe with patterned sleeves, and a red mantle lined and patterned with gold crescents, fastened at the throat with a gold clasp. With a faint halo-like band around her head, she turns to the right and raises both hands, palms together, in prayer. She stands on a scalloped strip of ground.
caption: Helmarshausen, A noblewoman at prayer, fol. 6v of a psalter, second half of the twelfth century. Tempera and gold on parchment. Baltimore, Walters Art Museum, W.10. Image: The Walters Art Museum, CC BY-NC-SA 3.0.

alt: Decorated opening of a psalm. A large gold initial B, its bowls filled with scrolling foliage in gold, grey-blue and green, occupies most of a pinkish-purple field within a double frame bordered with small gold fleurs-de-lis. The letters EATUS follow vertically at the right in gold capitals, and the faint gold lines of the opening verse run below.
caption: The Helmarshausen Psalter, initial B of Psalm 1, Beatus vir, fol. 7r. Baltimore, Walters Art Museum, W.10. Image: The Walters Art Museum, CC BY-NC-SA 3.0.

alt: Full-page miniature of the Crucifixion on a gold ground framed by a border of gold arches enclosing pale blue and white rosettes. Christ hangs dead on a red cross with a titulus IHC NAZ REX IUD, his head bowed, wearing a red and white loincloth. Above the crossbar are a gold eight-pointed star or sun at left and a grey crescent moon at right. The Virgin, in a green mantle and red veil, stands at left with her hands crossed on her breast; Saint John, in a green mantle, stands at right raising one hand and holding a book.
caption: The Helmarshausen Psalter, The Crucifixion with the Virgin and Saint John, fol. 41v, before Psalm 51. Baltimore, Walters Art Museum, W.10. Image: The Walters Art Museum, CC BY-NC-SA 3.0.

alt: Full-page miniature of Christ in Majesty. Within a red-edged mandorla on a gold ground, Christ sits on an arc with his feet on a green globe, wearing a pale tunic, a green mantle and a red cloak, with a cross-nimbus; he raises his right hand in blessing and holds an open book. In the corners outside the mandorla, on a pale blue ground, the four evangelist symbols with gold haloes hold books: the angel and the eagle above, the lion and the ox below. A frame of green, blue and red leaves surrounds the scene.
caption: The Helmarshausen Psalter, Christ in Majesty with the symbols of the Evangelists, fol. 77v, before Psalm 101. Baltimore, Walters Art Museum, W.10. Image: The Walters Art Museum, CC BY-NC-SA 3.0.

alt: Detail of a densely painted miniature on a blue and gold ground. At the centre a duke in a patterned robe and a duchess in a white veil and gold-patterned mantle kneel facing each other, holding small crosses; two hands emerge from an arc of heaven above them and lower crowns onto their heads. On each side stand rows of crowned and richly dressed figures holding crosses, identified by inscriptions along the top: at left the empress Richenza, the emperor Lothar, the duchess Gertrud and Duke Henry; at right a king and a queen. Fragments of haloed saints appear in the lower corners.
caption: Herimann of Helmarshausen, The coronation of Henry the Lion and Mathilda, lower register of fol. 171v (detail), Gospels of Henry the Lion, c. 1188. Tempera and gold on parchment. Wolfenbüttel, Herzog August Bibliothek, Cod. Guelf. 105 Noviss. 2° (also Munich, Clm 30055). Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Ruins of a Romanesque church on a grassy hilltop against a blue sky. A tall cylindrical stone rotunda with small round-arched windows rises at the centre; lower, roofless rectangular arms project from it, one with a large open arch at the junction. At the left stand the ruined walls of a later castle building with tall window openings. Trees frame the view.
caption: Chapel of St John the Baptist on the Krukenberg, consecrated 1126, with the ruins of the Krukenburg castle (c. 1215–1220 and later). Helmarshausen (Bad Karlshafen, Hesse). Photo: Magnus Mertens, CC BY-SA 2.5, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Large house-shaped reliquary shrine on small feet with iron rings, seen from a corner. The roof is covered with gilt metal tiles and crowned by an openwork crest of gilt foliage with rock-crystal knobs. The long side shows six seated apostles in relief under round arches, set in panels studded with cabochon stones and rock crystals; the end shows three standing figures in relief under a gable with a further figure. A silver band with an inscription runs along the base.
caption: Hildesheim goldsmith, in the circle of the Helmarshausen workshop, Shrine of Saint Godehard, the side of Saint Paul and the end with the Deesis, c. 1131–1132 (renewed 1787, restored 1971–1972). Oak core, silver and copper, gilt, repoussé and chased; niello; gems and rock crystal; brown varnish; 65 × 122 × 51 cm. Hildesheim, Cathedral of St Mary, crypt (Dommuseum Hildesheim). Photo: Bildarchiv Foto Marburg / Dommuseum Hildesheim, no copyright, contractual restrictions apply (NoC-CR), for non-commercial educational use.

alt: Detail of a gilt relief: a bearded apostle sits frontally on a throne shaped like a small building with arched windows and cushions, raising his right hand and holding a closed book in his left. A silver band behind his head is inscribed S PHILIPPUS. The relief is set under a round arch in a panel studded with cabochon stones and rock crystals.
caption: Shrine of Saint Godehard, the apostle Philip. Photo: Bildarchiv Foto Marburg / Dommuseum Hildesheim / Lutz Engelhardt, NoC-CR, for non-commercial educational use.

alt: Detail of a gilt relief: a bearded apostle with large staring eyes sits on an architectural throne, wrapped in a mantle whose folds form deep curves over his knees, and holds an open book with an engraved geometric cover. A silver band behind his head is inscribed S THADDEUS. The relief is set under a round arch in a panel studded with stones.
caption: Shrine of Saint Godehard, the apostle Thaddeus. Photo: Bildarchiv Foto Marburg / Dommuseum Hildesheim / Lutz Engelhardt, NoC-CR, for non-commercial educational use.

alt: Madonna Lactans
caption: Bicci di Lorenzo (1373–1452), Madonna Lactans, 1400s, detached fresco, Pieve di San Leolino, Panzano in Chianti.

alt: The white stone west façade of a Romanesque cathedral under a blue sky, crossed by overhead tram wires. A tall central gable with a large rose window is flanked by lower side gables. A gallery of small arches on slender columns runs across the whole front. In the centre a projecting porch on two columns resting on lions frames the main door, with a loggia above; two smaller doors open at the sides. Long horizontal relief friezes are set into the wall on both sides of the porch and above the side doors. At the left rises a tall bell tower with an octagonal spire.
caption: Modena Cathedral, the west façade: Lanfranco's arcaded front with Wiligelmo's Genesis reliefs and main portal, the rose window and side doors added by the Campionese masters, and the Ghirlandina at the left. The small slab with Enoch and Elijah holding the foundation inscription is set into the wall to the left of the porch. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A wide sheet of parchment, stained and creased, displayed against a red background. It is covered with lines of tall, narrow cursive script with long upward strokes. At the lower left a monogram formed of letters arranged around a cross, with further signatures beside it; at the lower right a dark round wax seal is attached to the sheet.
caption: Diploma of Charlemagne granting immunity to the church of Modena, Gondreville, 26 September 782 (facsimile). The original is in Modena, Archivio Capitolare. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A rectangular marble slab set into a stone wall. In the centre a smooth tablet is carved with twelve lines of large Roman capitals. At either side stands a bearded prophet in a long mantle, holding the tablet with one hand and raising the other; the names ENOC and ELIA are carved on the base beneath them.
caption: Wiligelmo, Enoch and Elijah holding the foundation inscription of the cathedral, with the couplet naming the sculptor, 1099. Modena Cathedral, west façade. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A curved stone apse wall built of large pale blocks. In the upper part a rectangular marble plaque carries fourteen lines of inscription in Roman capitals, the last two in a different, more cursive lettering. Below it a round-headed window with an iron grille is framed by a carved arch of acanthus scrolls with a small bird and flowers, and a carved head with flowing hair in the lunette above the opening.
caption: The foundation inscription composed by the canon Aimo, naming Lanfranco as master of the work, 1099, with the addition of the massarius Bozzalino (thirteenth century). Modena Cathedral, main apse. Photo: Username.Ruge, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A large area of pale stone wall covered with sixteen long lines of carved inscription in Romanesque capitals with many abbreviations and ligatures, running across several blocks. An iron bracket projects from the wall at the top left.
caption: Inscription recording the consecration of the cathedral by Pope Lucius III on 12 July 1184. Modena Cathedral, exterior wall. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A long stone relief under a cornice and a row of small arches. At the left the bearded Creator, with an open book, sits in an almond-shaped glory held up by two kneeling angels. Next the Creator with a halo touches the head of the naked Adam. In the centre the Creator draws Eve from the side of Adam, who lies asleep with his legs drawn up. At the right Adam and Eve stand naked beside a tree, Eve holding a fruit, Adam raising his hand to his throat.
caption: Wiligelmo, the first slab of Genesis: the Creator in glory, the Creation of Adam, the Creation of Eve and the Fall, c. 1099–1110. Modena Cathedral, west façade, above the left side door. Photo: Szeder László, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A long stone relief seen from below and to one side. At the left the naked Adam and Eve, covering themselves with leaves, stand before the haloed Creator, who points at them and holds a scroll. Next an angel with large wings drives them out; they walk away bowed. At the right Eve, now clothed, bends with a hoe, and Adam, clothed, works the ground beside a tree.
caption: Wiligelmo, the second slab of Genesis: the Reproach, the Expulsion and the Labour of Adam and Eve, c. 1099–1110. Modena Cathedral, west façade, left of the main portal. Photo: Szeder László, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A long stone relief under a cornice and small arches. At the left Abel, holding a lamb, stands beside an inscription; next a small Creator blesses from a round glory above a kneeling figure. In the centre Cain, holding a sheaf of grain, offers it. Then Cain swings a club at Abel, who falls to his knees. At the right the haloed Creator lays his hand on the shoulder of Cain, who looks up.
caption: Wiligelmo, the third slab of Genesis: the offerings of Cain and Abel, the murder of Abel and God questioning Cain, c. 1099–1110. Modena Cathedral, west façade, right of the main portal. Photo: Mattis, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A long stone relief under a cornice and small arches. At the left a bearded archer in a pointed cap draws a large bow and shoots an arrow at a man half hidden among the branches of a tree. In the centre an ark is represented as a two-storey building of arches, with two heads looking out of the upper openings. At the right four men stand together, talking and pointing, one of them bearded and holding his cloak.
caption: Wiligelmo, the fourth slab of Genesis: Lamech kills Cain, the Ark of Noah, and Noah and his sons leaving the Ark, c. 1099–1110. Modena Cathedral, west façade, above the right side door. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The upper part of a round-arched portal. A broad carved archivolt is filled with scrolling vines inhabited by small human figures, animals and birds, set between bands of interlace and lattice ornament. Below, a long lintel is carved with vine scrolls bearing bunches of grapes, with a large mask with leafy hair at the centre and small figures among the leaves. Above the door a lunette is closed by an iron grille in front of round glass panes. Small crouching figures sit at the springing of the arch.
caption: Wiligelmo and workshop, the main portal: archivolt with inhabited vine scrolls and lintel with a foliate mask, c. 1099–1110. Modena Cathedral, west façade. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The upper part of a round-arched portal. The archivolt is carved with interlacing bands forming roundels that enclose small figures and animals. A long lintel below is divided into six panels of small figures under an inscription: a bishop on horseback, a ship with a sail, a saint healing a young woman before a crowned figure, a ruler offering a cup, a group riding, and a funeral with a body laid out before a building. A grilled lunette fills the arch.
caption: Workshop of Wiligelmo (Maestro di San Geminiano), the lintel of the Porta dei Principi with the life of Saint Geminianus, and the archivolt with inhabited interlace, c. 1106–1110. Modena Cathedral, south side. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A stone relief in a narrow rectangular frame under the inscription IOHANNES BAPTISTA. A long-haired, bearded man in a garment of shaggy hide raises one hand and holds before him a tablet inscribed ECCE AGNUS DEI ECCE QUI TOLLIT PECCATA MUNDI. His bare feet rest on a ledge.
caption: Workshop of Wiligelmo (Maestro dell'Agnus Dei), Saint John the Baptist, c. 1106–1110. Modena Cathedral, Porta dei Principi, underside of the lintel. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A stone relief of a winged angel in a long girdled robe, seen from below, stretching both arms upwards to hold the rim of a large disc above his head. His face is turned upwards. The inscription IOHANNES BAPTISTA runs along the frame below him.
caption: Workshop of Wiligelmo, an angel raising the roundel of the Lamb of God, c. 1106–1110. Modena Cathedral, Porta dei Principi, underside of the lintel. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A long stone relief seen from below. Two winged angels fly horizontally towards each other, their bodies stretched out and their robes swirling, holding between them a circular frame in which an animal is carved upside down.
caption: Workshop of Wiligelmo, two angels carrying the roundel with the Lamb of God, c. 1106–1110. Modena Cathedral, Porta dei Principi, underside of the lintel. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A stone relief of a young, beardless saint standing in an arched niche between two columns, his head turned upwards. He holds an open book inscribed IN PRINCIPIO ERAT VERBUM ET VERBUM. A zigzag band decorates the frame at the right.
caption: Workshop of Wiligelmo, Saint John the Evangelist with the opening words of his Gospel, c. 1106–1110. Modena Cathedral, Porta dei Principi, jamb. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A stone relief of a standing figure in a long mantle in an arched niche with a scalloped arch between two small towers. He holds a large closed book against his chest with one hand. The head is worn.
caption: Workshop of Wiligelmo, an apostle in a niche, c. 1106–1110. Modena Cathedral, Porta dei Principi, jamb. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A semicircular stone archivolt set into a brick arch, with a plain plastered lunette below. Along the archivolt, knights on horseback in mail armour with lances and shields ride towards the centre from both sides. At the top a castle with towers rises from water; in it stand a woman and a man, and wooden siege towers stand at either side. A man with a pick attacks the left tower. Inscriptions along the upper edge name the figures. The underside of the arch is carved with large leaves.
caption: Workshop of Wiligelmo, the archivolt of the Porta della Pescheria with the siege of a castle by Arthur and his knights, early twelfth century. Modena Cathedral, north side. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A detail of a stone archivolt. At the left a knight in mail armour with a hood rides a horse, holding a lance; to his right a bearded rider without armour, in a short tunic, gallops with a long lance. The inscription ISDERNUS is carved above them, and the beginning of another name at the right.
caption: The Porta della Pescheria, detail: the knight Isdernus (Yder) and a mounted companion. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A detail of a stone archivolt with the inscription ARTUS DE BRETANI carved above a knight in a mail hauberk and pointed helmet, riding a horse and holding a lance with a pennant. At the left another rider's lance points towards him.
caption: The Porta della Pescheria, detail: Artus de Bretania, King Arthur, with his lance and pennant. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A detail of a stone archivolt with inscriptions along its upper edge. At the left a bearded man in a short tunic swings a pick; in the centre a tall wooden tower built of crossed beams; at the right a veiled woman with a sad face looks out from behind a wall of stone above stylised waves.
caption: The Porta della Pescheria, detail: Burmaltus with his pick, a siege tower and Winlogee (Guinevere) within the walls of the castle. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A tall, narrow photograph of a carved portal jamb next to a wooden door, with a red metal prop in front. On the inner face, a column of small arched niches each holds a figure at work, with abbreviated names of months above: a man reaping, a man threshing, a man treading grapes in a vat, a man with a barrel, and others. The outer face is carved with dense vine scrolls inhabited by birds and animals.
caption: The Porta della Pescheria, left jamb: Labours of the Months in arched niches and inhabited vine scroll, early twelfth century. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A tall photograph of the right jamb of a portal beside a dark wooden door. On its inner face a column of small arched niches each contains a figure; the outer face is carved with dense foliage scrolls with birds and animals. At the bottom right a crouching stone lion supports a column; at the top, part of a lintel carved with animals.
caption: The Porta della Pescheria, right jamb with the remaining Months and vine scroll, the lion at the base of the porch and, above, part of the lintel with animal fables. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A pale stone lion lying on a rectangular base beside a column, its head turned to the viewer with open mouth, round drilled eyes and a curly mane. Between its forepaws it holds a sheep or ram. A column base rests on its back. A rusty drainpipe runs down the wall at the left.
caption: The Porta della Pescheria, stylophore lion holding a ram. Photo: Szeder László, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A worn stone lion lying on a rectangular base in front of a column, its head lowered and turned forwards, its mane carved in long incised strands. A column base sits on its back; its forepaws rest on the base. A hole has been made in its flank.
caption: The Porta della Pescheria, stylophore lion. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A large projecting porch of pinkish red and white marble against the striped stone wall of a church. A deep round arch with a frieze of rosettes covers a portal with many concentric mouldings carved with cables and zigzags, framing a tall wooden door with a grilled lunette above. Pairs of slender columns, some knotted, stand at the sides, and two large red marble lions lie on bases in front.
caption: Campionese masters, the Porta Regia, first half of the thirteenth century. Modena Cathedral, south side. Photo: Warburg, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The east end of a dark church interior. A raised platform runs across the width of the church on slender columns; its parapet is a continuous carved frieze of many small painted figures, with a curved projecting pulpit at the left. Below the platform three lit arches open into a crypt with gilded iron grilles. Above, behind a colonnade, the apse is painted with saints and ornament.
caption: The pontile and its ambo, with the crypt below and the raised presbytery above. Modena Cathedral, interior. Photo: Mattis, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A long painted marble relief on a parapet. At the left Christ kneels to wash the feet of Peter, who sits with his foot in a basin. In the centre a long table covered with a white cloth with deep folds; behind it the apostles sit in a row with gold haloes, in red, green and blue robes, with names carved above them. Christ in the middle gives a morsel to Judas, and John leans on his breast. At the right begins another scene with soldiers and an axe.
caption: Anselmo da Campione and workshop, the pontile: the Washing of the Feet and the Last Supper, c. 1160–1184, with modern recovery of the original colours. Modena Cathedral. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A painted marble relief on a parapet divided by red marble columns. At the left the end of the table of the Last Supper. Next, Judas kisses Christ among soldiers with axes and spears, while Peter cuts the ear of a kneeling servant. Then Christ stands before the seated Pilate. Then Christ is tied to a column and whipped. At the right a man carries a large cross. Below, carved capitals with figures crown the columns of the platform.
caption: Anselmo da Campione and workshop, the pontile: the Betrayal, Christ before Pilate, the Flagellation and the Way to Calvary, c. 1160–1184. Modena Cathedral. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A curved marble pulpit projecting from a parapet, carved with panels separated by small columns. In the centre Christ sits enthroned, blessing and holding a book, with the letters A and omega and an inscription above. At the left the winged angel and the winged lion with books; at the right the winged ox and the eagle. At the right edge part of the parapet with Christ washing Peter's feet. The pulpit rests on columns with carved capitals.
caption: Campionese masters, the ambo of the pontile: Christ enthroned among the symbols of the Evangelists, c. 1208–1225. Modena Cathedral. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A curved marble relief with a blue starry ground. In two panels separated by a column, four seated saints with haloes write in books: at the left Jerome and Ambrose, at the right Augustine and Gregory, with their names carved above. Angels fly down head first to touch their heads, and doves bend towards their ears. At the right edge the winged lion of Mark.
caption: Campionese masters, the ambo of the pontile: the Doctors of the Church, Jerome, Ambrose, Augustine and Gregory, inspired by angels and doves, c. 1208–1225. Modena Cathedral. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A manuscript page with a coloured drawing in a frame of orange lattice and blue bands. At the left bishops in mitres with crosiers and tonsured clergy stand in a group. At the right a woman in a green mantle with a staff, labelled Matildis comitissa, gestures towards them, accompanied by two women in white veils and a group of men. A line of red text runs above the frame and another line of text below.
caption: The Relatio, Matilda of Canossa receives the bishops for the translation of Saint Geminianus, c. 1200–1210 (facsimile). The original is in Modena, Archivio Capitolare, O.II.11. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A manuscript drawing in two registers in a frame of orange lattice and blue bands. In the upper register Matilda, Lanfranco in a cap and a bishop in a mitre lift a long green slab diagonally, while another bishop holds a chalice and figures watch at the sides; labels name them. In the lower register armed men in mail with swords and spears stand on either side, guarding the tomb.
caption: The Relatio, the opening of the tomb of Saint Geminianus, with Matilda, Lanfranco and the bishops above and the armed guards of the tomb below, c. 1200–1210 (facsimile). The original is in Modena, Archivio Capitolare, O.II.11. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Mantle of Roger II
caption: Mantle of Roger II, 1133/34 (Norman Sicily, Italy), textiles, patterned samite (kermes dye), gold and silk embroidery, pearls, gold with cellular enamel, rubies, spinels, sapphires, garnets, glass, tablet weave, 146 x 345 cm, Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.

caption: Mosaics of Christ Pantocrator (Dome), 1143, mosaic, Cappella Palatina, Palermo.

caption: Mosaics of Christ Pantocrator (Apse), 1143, mosaic, Cappella Palatina, Palermo.

caption: Mosaics of Christ Pantocrator with Saints Peter and Paul, after 1143, mosaic, Cappella Palatina, Palermo.

caption: Jan van Eyck (c. 1390–1441), Madonna of Chancellor Rolin, c. 1435, oil on panel, 66 x 62 cm, Paris, Musée du Louvre.

caption: Janus, the two-faced god (Allegory of January), 1225-30, red Verona marble, 94 × 48 cm, Museo della Cattedrale di San Giorgio, Ferrara.

caption: Reawakening of Nature and the King of the Months (Allegory of March and April), 1225-30, red Verona marble, Museo della Cattedrale di San Giorgio, Ferrara.

alt: Façade of a stone cathedral seen from the piazza, with a tall square bell tower at the left topped by a conical spire, and a wooded hill behind under a cloudy sky. At the bottom a Renaissance portico of five round arches with a balustrade above and a pulpit at each end. In the middle register five rose windows, the central one larger and set in a square frame. In the upper register, under a gable edged with stone crockets, three tall pointed arches, the central one containing a gold-ground mosaic of Christ enthroned between two standing figures, and three further rose windows.
caption: Spoleto, Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, façade, with the bell tower, the Renaissance portico (1491–1504) and the mosaic of Solsternus (1207). Photo: Fiat 500e, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Upper part of a cathedral façade of pale stone against a deep blue sky. A triangular gable edged with a row of small arches and projecting stone crockets is crowned by a cross. Within it a round rose window with radiating tracery sits near the apex. Below, three tall pointed arches: the two at the sides are blind, while the central one contains a gold-ground mosaic of Christ enthroned between the Virgin and Saint John, with two lines of inscription beneath. Two further rose windows, framed by pink stone rings, open between the arches. A band of small round arches on brackets runs across the façade below the mosaic. In the lower register five rose windows are visible, the central one large and set in a square frame with winged figures in its upper corners. The edge of a bell tower appears at the left.
caption: Spoleto, Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, upper part of the façade, with the rose windows, the mosaic of Solsternus (1207) and the central rose window of the middle register. Photo: Greymouser, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Middle register of a façade of pale stone with three rose windows. The central rose window is large and set in a square frame bordered with bands of small inlaid patterns. Its tracery consists of twelve radiating colonnettes joined by lobed arches around a central ring, within a wider ring of interlaced circles enclosing smaller round openings filled with leaded glass. In the four corners of the square frame are reliefs of the symbols of the Evangelists: a winged angel at the upper left, an eagle at the upper right, a winged lion at the lower left and a winged ox at the lower right. Below, a small blind loggia of colonnettes includes two standing figures carrying the cornice on their heads. At either side a smaller rose window with radiating tracery; the one at the right is framed by small circular inlays. Above runs a band of small round arches on brackets.
caption: Spoleto, Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, middle register of the façade, with the central rose window, the symbols of the Evangelists, the telamons of the blind loggia and two lateral rose windows. Photo: Effems, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Mosaic set in a pointed arch of white stone, framed by a border of small blue and pink plant motifs on a gold ground. In the centre Christ sits frontally on a broad jewelled throne, in a blue mantle, under a cross-shaped halo, blessing with his right hand and holding an open book; his bare feet rest on a dark green hemisphere. At the left stands the Virgin, labelled SCA MARIA, in a dark purple mantle, raising her hands towards him; at the right a young beardless saint labelled SCS IOHS, in pale grey and white garments, holding a jewelled book. Beneath the figures run two lines of inscription.
caption: Solsternus, Deesis: Christ Enthroned between the Virgin and Saint John, signed and dated 1207. Mosaic. Spoleto, Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, façade. Photo: Wolfgang Sauber, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Upper part of a doorway of white marble beneath a plastered vault, above dark wooden doors with rectangular panels. The jambs are carved with symmetrical scrolls of foliage. Above the door a lintel is carved with a running vine scroll forming six roundels, which enclose rosettes and vase-like plant motifs; at the centre a cross rises from a cluster of acanthus leaves. Above it a second, projecting lintel is carved with rows of dentils, egg-and-dart and other classical mouldings. In the lunette above are two large carved coats of arms in low relief and, at the centre, a small painted oval emblem of the archdiocese.
caption: Spoleto, Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, central portal of the façade, beneath the Renaissance portico: carved jambs and two lintels, with later coats of arms in the lunette above. Marble. Photo: MySpoleto, image for educational use only.

alt: Interior of a cathedral seen along the central nave towards the apse. White pilasters with gilded capitals separate tall round arches opening onto the aisles, and round windows with stone tracery are set in the walls above the arches. The nave is covered by a white barrel vault, with a dome over the crossing, and crystal chandeliers hang from the vault. At the end, the semi-dome of the apse is painted with the Coronation of the Virgin among crowds of angels and saints, above a wide fresco of the Dormition of the Virgin in a landscape. Rows of wooden pews stand on either side of a central aisle paved with inlaid marble in geometric patterns of circles and interlaces near the apse and of chevrons near the entrance. A gilded wooden pulpit is attached to a pier at the right.
caption: Spoleto, Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, the nave looking towards the apse, with the medieval pavement and the frescoes of Filippo Lippi and workshop (1467–1469) in the apse. Photo: Caba2011, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Close view of an inlaid stone floor. Broad bands of red stone and white marble curve and interlace, forming concentric rings around four round discs of coloured stone: a black stone, a veined breccia with pink and grey fragments, a dark stone with a grey patch and a blue-grey veined marble. Between the rings straight bands of red and white run diagonally across the floor. At the centre lies a small white slab carved with a worn relief, set among the bands. The stones are worn and crossed by cracks, and some pieces are broken.
caption: Spoleto, Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, pavement of the nave, detail of interlaced bands with roundels of coloured stone. Inlaid stone and marble. Photo: Zyance, CC BY-SA 2.5, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Shallow round-headed niche in a rough stone wall, its plaster painted in faded colours. In the upper part, within a rectangular field outlined in dark grey, appears the bust of a bearded man with large eyes and dark hair under an ochre halo, wearing a reddish-brown garment, his right hand raised before his chest. Below, broad horizontal bands of grey, white and ochre run across the niche, and at the bottom a painted curtain hangs in folds of grey and white, edged with red and ochre bands and decorated with round ochre medallions. Much of the plaster is lost or abraded, and the surrounding stone is bare.
caption: Spoleto, Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, crypt of San Primiano, painted niche with the bust of a saint above a painted curtain, 9th century (?). Fresco. Photo: Arcidiocesi di Spoleto-Norcia, image for educational use only.

alt: Painted wooden cross with a large figure of Christ alive on the cross, his eyes open, his head upright under a gold halo with raised bosses. His arms are stretched straight along the crossbar against a blue and red ground bordered with white bands and small red crosses, and his body is pale, with the muscles of the chest and abdomen drawn in rounded shapes. He wears a long white loincloth bound by a knotted blue cloth, and his feet rest side by side on a footrest. In the panel beside his body stand the Virgin, in a blue and red mantle, raising her hand to her face, and Saint John, in a pink mantle, labelled SCA MARIA and S IOHS. In the upper terminal Christ ascends in a blue mandorla among four angels, above a titulus. In the lower terminal blood runs down onto a skull in a red cavity, above an inscription with the date and the painter's name. Large iron nail heads stud the edges of the cross, and the wood is exposed at the ends of the arms.
caption: Alberto Sotio, Painted Cross (Christus triumphans), signed and dated 1187. Tempera on parchment over wood. Spoleto, Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, first chapel on the left, from the church of Santi Giovanni e Paolo, Spoleto. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (background modified).

alt: Interior of a richly decorated chapel seen from the entrance, with dark wooden pews on either side of a central passage. The walls are faced with pale marble pilasters with gilded capitals. Above, a blue vault scattered with gold stars carries a large gilded glory of rays with winged heads, above a triangular pediment with a cherub's head. At the end, under an arch flanked by two stucco angels, an altar of coloured marbles and gilding frames a small dark icon in a silver frame, flanked by two white marble statues of angels; candles burn on stands before the altar.
caption: Spoleto, Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, Chapel of the Santissima Icone, to the right of the apse, with the Byzantine icon of the Virgin on the altar. Photo: Effems, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Small icon of the Virgin in half length, turned towards the right, her head inclined, wearing a dark mantle drawn over her head. Her face is painted with greenish shadows and pink highlights. The painting is covered by a silver-gilt revetment worked in repoussé with small rosettes and lattice patterns, which leaves only the face and the dark mantle visible. A broad horseshoe-shaped halo of silver-gilt surrounds the head, and the Greek monograms of the Mother of God appear in two medallions at the top. At the right a Greek inscription runs in several short lines. The icon is set in an outer silver frame decorated with cabochons of dark blue and red stones and lozenge-shaped red stones.
caption: Byzantine painter, Icon of the Virgin Haghiosoritissa, 11th–12th century, with silver-gilt revetment. Tempera on panel. Spoleto, Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, Chapel of the Santissima Icone. Traditionally a gift of Frederick Barbarossa in 1185. Photo: Wolfgang Sauber, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Interior of a chapel whose walls are lined with tall wooden cupboards of carved and inlaid walnut. The upper part of the cupboards is divided by carved pilasters into tall panels painted with standing figures of prophets and sibyls in bright robes, some holding scrolls. At the centre of the end wall rises an altar with a carved and gilded tabernacle framing a small painting of the Virgin in glory above a group of figures; the altar front is inlaid with a radiating pattern around a central medallion. The lower panels of the cupboards are inlaid with ornament and small views. The vault above is frescoed with grotesques and, in a central octagonal frame, the Presentation of Christ in the Temple. The floor is of terracotta tiles.
caption: Spoleto, Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, Chapel of the Relics (1540), with the carved and inlaid cupboards (1548–1554) and the panels of prophets and sibyls (1553–1560). Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Reliquary in the form of a small classical temple, with two columns of blue lapis lazuli with silver Corinthian capitals supporting a silver entablature and a frieze of lapis lazuli decorated with silver winged heads and garlands. On top two silver putti hold a globe surmounted by a cross. Between the columns, on a stand with a winged head, a small rectangular frame of dark silver encloses a narrow piece of parchment written in brown ink in a medieval hand, with a silver cross above it. The whole rests on a stepped base of dark red veined jasper with silver feet.
caption: Reliquary of the autograph letter of Saint Francis to Brother Leo, in the form of a small temple. Lapis lazuli, jasper and silver. Gift of Pope Pius IX. Spoleto, Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, Chapel of the Relics. Photo: Luca Aless, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Narrow rectangular piece of parchment, yellowed and slightly creased, written in brown ink in nineteen short lines of irregular medieval script with many abbreviations. The letters are large and unevenly spaced, and some lines are crowded at the right edge. The parchment is set in a dark silver frame decorated with a pattern of crossed leaves.
caption: Saint Francis of Assisi, Autograph letter to Brother Leo, c. 1222–1226. Ink on goatskin parchment, about 13 × 6 cm, nineteen lines. Spoleto, Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, Chapel of the Relics. Photo: Luca Aless, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (cropped).

alt: A small rectangular church of rough pale stone among pine trees, with a pitched tiled roof. The gabled end wall has a stone bell-cote with a single bell at the top, a small carved rose window with radiating colonnettes, a long inscribed stone above it, and a doorway under a plain round arch. A long side wall recedes to the left.
caption: The oratory of San Pellegrino at Bominaco, the east end with the bell-cote, the rose window and the inscription of 1263. Photo: Pietro (Moto Itinerari), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The plain façade of a Romanesque church of pale ashlar under a deep blue sky, framed by bare branches and pines. A taller central gable with a round-headed window flanked by small carved figures rises above lower side walls; below, a doorway with a carved lintel and a round arch decorated with a band of interlace and rosettes.
caption: The abbey church of Santa Maria Assunta at Bominaco, the west façade, eleventh–twelfth century. Photo: Wanjan, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The end of a small stone church with a gabled wall, fronted by a lower portico of rough pale stone with round arches. Two of the arches rest on short columns with fluted lower parts set on a low parapet; a wooden door is visible inside the portico, with pots of geraniums on the parapet. Tall dark trees stand at both sides.
caption: The entrance of the oratory with the seventeenth-century portico, built with reused columns. Photo: Pietro (Moto Itinerari), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A close view of a stone wall. In the centre a circular rose window with eight radiating colonnettes joined by small arches to a central ring, framed by a band of carved scrolls and bunches of grapes with traces of red paint. Above it a long stone block carries two lines of worn carved capitals.
caption: The rose window of the east front and, above it, the inscription recording the renewal of the oratory under Abbot Teodino in 1263. Photo: Pietro (Moto Itinerari), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A view along a painted pointed barrel vault towards a doorway full of light. The nearest arch is painted with yellow strapwork forming stars; the next bay has standing prophets on blue and yellow grounds and, on both lower slopes, rows of tall narrow arched panels filled with small figures and lines of writing. Further bays and the end wall with a giant saint are visible beyond.
caption: The vault of the oratory seen towards the entrance, with prophets above and the calendar of the months on both slopes of the third bay. Photo: Zitumassin, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: The painted end wall of a vaulted interior around a doorway full of daylight. At the left a gigantic standing saint with a dotted tunic and bare legs in water fills the height of the wall, with a small friar and a hairy hermit beside him. To the right of a small round window are scenes of Christ riding a donkey into a city and, below, Christ washing the feet of an apostle, with an enthroned figure between them. The side walls and the vault are covered with scenes in registers.
caption: The counter-façade with Saint Christopher, Saint Francis, a hermit saint, the Entry into Jerusalem, Christ enthroned and the Washing of the Feet, 1263. Photo: Pietro (Moto Itinerari), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A curved painted vault surface. In the upper register four standing figures on blue and yellow grounds hold scrolls with inscriptions, labelled MOYSES, IOB, IONAS and YSAIAS. Below an ornamental band runs a row of twelve tall narrow arched panels: in alternate panels small figures perform tasks — a man warming himself by a fire, a man pruning, a youth pulling a thorn from his foot, a youth holding flowers, a rider on a horse, a man with a vessel — and the other panels contain columns of letters and names of saints, each with a zodiac sign at the top.
caption: The calendar, January to June, with the prophets Moses, Job, Jonah and Isaiah above, 1263. Bominaco, oratory of San Pellegrino, third bay of the vault. Photo: Pietro (Moto Itinerari), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A curved painted vault surface. Above, five seated figures under arches on blue grounds, one crowned, one holding a sword, each with an unrolled scroll inscribed in capitals. Below an ornamental band runs a row of twelve tall arched panels, more damaged, with faded figures of workers alternating with columns of writing, and zodiac signs such as a lion, a virgin and scales at the top.
caption: The calendar, July to December, with prophets and kings above (among them Samuel, Solomon and Elijah), 1263. Bominaco, oratory of San Pellegrino, third bay of the vault. Photo: Pietro (Moto Itinerari), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A painted wall in two registers under a band of leaf ornament. Above, an angel with a staff approaches the Virgin seated on a cushioned throne before a domed building; then the Virgin and an older woman labelled HELISABET embrace before a door, watched by a maid at a curtain. Below, a long white table with fish and cups, behind which Christ and the haloed apostles sit in a row, with John leaning on Christ and a small figure kneeling in front.
caption: The Annunciation and the Visitation, and below the Last Supper, 1263. Bominaco, oratory of San Pellegrino. Photo: Pietro (Moto Itinerari), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A painted vault surface in two registers under a band of roundels. Left, the Virgin lies on a red couch with the swaddled Child in a manger watched by an ox and an ass, angels above, women bathing the Child in a basin below and Joseph seated thoughtfully. Right, an angel flies over brown hills with a scroll above shepherds with their flocks. Below, a row of six small scenes with inscriptions, including a saint before a ruler, a saint preaching and a beheading.
caption: The Nativity and the Annunciation to the Shepherds, and below scenes from the life of Saint Pellegrino, 1263. Bominaco, oratory of San Pellegrino. Photo: Pietro (Moto Itinerari), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A painted wall under a dark starry vault. Three kings labelled GASPAR, BALTASAR and MELCHIOR bring gifts to the Virgin enthroned under a domed tower with the Child on her lap; Joseph stands beside her and a seated figure points upward. The right part is damaged. Below, a pale damaged scene shows riders on white horses leaving a towered city.
caption: The Adoration of the Magi, and below the journey of the Magi, 1263. Bominaco, oratory of San Pellegrino. Photo: Pietro (Moto Itinerari), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A curved painted wall with a band of roundels above. In the upper register, under painted arches with hanging lamps, a crowned woman, an old man and the Virgin hold the Child above an altar, with Joseph beside them; to the right a crowned figure is seated in a canopied building, and further right, in a separate frame, three crowned riders appear before a tree. The lower half of the wall has lost most of its painted surface.
caption: The Presentation in the Temple and scenes of Herod and the Magi, 1263. Bominaco, oratory of San Pellegrino. Photo: Pietro (Moto Itinerari), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A painted wall in two registers. In the upper register on a pale green ground, men in caps hand coins to a figure labelled IUDAS; Judas kisses Christ among a crowd while a kneeling figure is restrained; several men gesture; a tall figure in a dark red robe stands in front; to the right of a window a crowned seated figure holds a cup while a servant pours. In the lower register, on a dark ground, naked figures are tormented by black devils and entwined by grey serpents, and a hairy naked figure sits on a throne.
caption: Judas receiving the money and the Betrayal, Pilate washing his hands, and below the torments of the damned from the Last Judgment, 1263. Bominaco, oratory of San Pellegrino. Photo: Pietro (Moto Itinerari), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A painted wall in three registers. At the top, riders on white horses. In the middle, between painted cornices: Christ tied to a column and scourged by two men; Joseph on a ladder lowering the body of Christ from the cross while the Virgin kisses his face and John stands by; the body of Christ laid on a tomb mourned by the Virgin, angels and a youth. In the lower register on a dark blue ground, seated haloed figures hold small souls in their laps beside a tree, a woman stands, and a saint holds scales. At the far right a standing hermit covered in long hair.
caption: The Flagellation, the Deposition and the Lamentation; below the bosom of Abraham and Saint Michael weighing souls, 1263. Bominaco, oratory of San Pellegrino. Photo: Pietro (Moto Itinerari), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A painted wall around a narrow window. At the left a bearded man in a pilgrim's hat with a staff and a bag, labelled as Christ; then two haloed men labelled LUCAS and CLEOPAS, one holding a book. At the right a haloed rider on a white horse cuts his red cloak with a sword to share it with a half-naked beggar. Above, part of the calendar with lists of feasts; below, a band of scrolling ornament.
caption: Christ as a pilgrim with Luke and Cleopas on the road to Emmaus, and Saint Martin dividing his cloak, 1263. Bominaco, oratory of San Pellegrino. Photo: Pietro (Moto Itinerari), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A low relief carved in pale limestone of a griffin walking to the left: it has the head, wings and feathered breast of an eagle, with a hooked beak and a pointed ear, and the hind body, legs and curling tail of a lion. Its beak touches the rim of a footed chalice at the left edge. One clawed foreleg is raised.
caption: Griffin drinking from a chalice, relief on one of the stone screens (plutei) of the oratory. Bominaco, oratory of San Pellegrino. Photo: Kewerner, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fresco by Giotto in the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua. Against a deep blue ground, a white marble sanctuary enclosure occupies the left four fifths of the scene, with a canopied ciborium on twisted columns over the altar and a raised pulpit with stairs behind. Inside the enclosure a priest in a red robe leans towards a kneeling youth whose head alone is visible above the parapet. At the right, a second priest in green, seen from behind, pushes away the elderly, haloed Joachim, who clutches a small lamb in his draped arms and steps towards the edge of the platform and the empty blue beyond
caption: The Rejection of Joachim’s Sacrifice, c. 1303–1305, fresco, 200 x 185 cm. Padua, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), upper register of the south wall. The opening scene of the narrative cycle: the childless Joachim, bearing a lamb for sacrifice, is turned away from the Temple of Jerusalem by the priest, while the offering of another worshipper is accepted within the sanctuary enclosure.

alt: Fresco by Giotto in the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua. Before a rocky ochre ridge crowned with round-headed trees against a deep blue sky, the elderly haloed Joachim enters from the left, wrapped in a rose mantle, his head bowed and hands drawn into his drapery. A small white dog leaps up towards him. Facing him stand two young shepherds, one holding a tall staff, who look at each other rather than at the old man. At the right, a wooden hut with a pyramidal shingled roof shelters a dense flock of sheep pressing out of its dark doorway, led by a ram with curled horns
caption: Joachim among the Shepherds, c. 1303–1305, fresco, 200 x 185 cm. Padua, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), upper register of the south wall. Expelled from the Temple, Joachim withdraws in shame to his flocks in the wilderness: two shepherds exchange an uncertain glance, while only the small dog springs forward to welcome him.

alt: Fresco by Giotto in the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua. A house shown in cutaway against a deep blue ground: a gabled pediment with a fictive relief of a blessing figure between two angels crowns the main chamber, whose front wall is removed to reveal Anna kneeling in profile in a red gown, hands joined in prayer, a gold halo behind her head. Beside her stands a curtained bed; domestic objects hang on the rear wall. From a window at the upper right an angel with red wings and a halo leans into the room, head and shoulders only, hand raised towards Anna. At the left, under an external staircase with a balustraded landing, a maidservant in pale yellow sits spinning with spindle and distaff.
caption: The Annunciation to St Anne, c. 1303–1305, fresco, 200 x 185 cm. Padua, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), upper register of the south wall. In the chamber of her house, the praying Anna receives the angel who announces that she will conceive; the heavenly messenger thrusts head and shoulders through the window, while a maidservant sits spinning in the porch below the stairs, unaware of the miracle within.

alt: Fresco by Giotto in the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua. In a rocky ochre landscape against a deep blue sky, the elderly haloed Joachim kneels in profile in a rose mantle, leaning towards a pink masonry altar filled with flames, on whose top lie the skeletal remains of the sacrificed animal. Above the altar a small dark human figure, the soul of the offering, ascends towards a blessing hand emerging from the sky at the upper centre. At the right stands a haloed angel in pale rose, one hand raised towards the altar, the other holding a trefoil-tipped rod against the shoulder. At the left a young shepherd stands praying, hands joined; below, sheep and goats rest and graze on the barren slope
caption: The Sacrifice of Joachim, c. 1303–1305, fresco, 200 x 185 cm. Padua, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), upper register of the south wall. In the wilderness Joachim offers a burnt sacrifice to know whether his prayers are heard: the victim is consumed on the flaming altar, an angel attends the rite, and from the height of the blue the blessing hand of God appears to accept the offering.

alt: Fresco by Giotto in the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua. In a barren rocky landscape against a deep blue sky, the elderly haloed Joachim sits asleep at the right, completely wrapped in a rose mantle, his head sunk on his knees, before the dark doorway of a wooden hut with a pyramidal roof. From the upper left an angel with red wings and gold halo flies steeply down towards him, right arm extended, a trefoil-tipped rod in the left hand and a trail of cloud behind. At the left stand two shepherds: the hooded one in dark brown looks up and sees the angel, while his companion in a wide-brimmed hat, holding a staff, gazes ahead unaware. Sheep and goats rest on the pale slope between them and the sleeper
caption: The Dream of Joachim, c. 1303–1305, fresco, 200 x 185 cm. Padua, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), upper register of the south wall. Asleep before the sheepfold, Joachim receives in a dream the angel’s promise: his prayer has been heard, Anna has conceived, and he is to return to her without fear. Two shepherds and the flock attend the apparition from the left, but only the hooded one sees it.

alt: Fresco by Giotto in the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua. Before a pale city gate with two crenellated towers and a round arch gilded on its inner face, the elderly Joachim and Anna embrace on a stone bridge, their haloed heads pressed together in a kiss, her hand cradling his face. Behind Anna stand five women: one wrapped in a dark mantle that half hides her face, the others in festive dresses of cream, red and green, one carrying folded cloths. At the far left a young herdsman with a basket, a pole over his shoulder, enters the scene cut in half by the painted frame. The sky above is deep blue.
caption: The Meeting at the Golden Gate, c. 1303–1305, fresco, 200 x 185 cm. Padua, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), upper register of the south wall. Obeying the angel’s command, Joachim returns from the wilderness and Anna comes out of Jerusalem to meet him: the spouses embrace and kiss on the bridge before the gilded gate, the moment that medieval tradition read as the immaculate conception of the Virgin. A group of women attends the reunion, one wrapped in a dark mantle; at the left a herdsman of Joachim’s company enters the field, half cut by the frame.

alt: Fresco of the birth of the Virgin Mary. Inside a grey-green house open toward the viewer, Anna, haloed and dressed in red, sits up in a bed with a striped orange coverlet and stretches out both hands to receive the swaddled infant Mary, who is haloed and is offered to her by a standing attendant in a blue and gold dress; a second attendant in red stands behind. In the foreground, below the bed, two seated midwives tend the same haloed infant beside a basin, one washing her, the other preparing cloth. At the left, under the porch of the house, a young woman in cream hands a wrapped bundle through a half-open door to a veiled older woman inside. The pediment of the house bears a carved roundel with a bust flanked by two angels. Deep blue sky above, with losses to the pigment.
caption: The Birth of the Virgin, c. 1303–1305, fresco, 200 x 185 cm. Padua, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), upper register of the north wall. In the same house where the angel appeared to Anna, the promised child is born: below, two midwives wash the newborn Mary; above, already swaddled, she is handed to her mother, who reaches out from the bed to receive her. At the threshold of the porch a wrapped gift passes from hand to hand.

alt: Fresco of the presentation of the child Mary in the Temple. At the centre, a small haloed girl in a pale cream dress climbs a white external staircase toward a marble enclosure crowned by a canopy on slender columns; a priest in red vestments leans over the parapet with both arms extended to receive her. Behind the girl, her mother Anna, haloed and wrapped in a red mantle, bends forward on the stairs with her hands on the child. At the far left, a figure in a grey tunic, seen from behind, carries a large basket on his shoulder; behind him stand a haloed grey-bearded elder, a dark-bearded man and a veiled woman. Behind the enclosure a group of women’s heads looks on. At the right, seen from behind, a figure in a rose mantle raises a hand in speech beside a man in blue with an ochre hood; behind them rises a tower with arches, an external stair and a pyramidal roof. Deep blue sky with extensive pigment losses.
caption: The Presentation of the Virgin in the Temple, c. 1303–1305, fresco, 200 x 185 cm. Padua, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), upper register of the north wall. The three-year-old Mary climbs the steps of the Temple toward the priest who bends to receive her, Anna guiding her from behind and Joachim following a bearer who carries the offering on his shoulder. The sanctuary is the same marble enclosure from which Joachim’s sacrifice was driven away at the opening of the cycle: the Temple that expelled the father now opens its arms to the daughter.

alt: Fresco of suitors bringing rods to the Temple. At the right, inside an open sanctuary with a blue starred half-dome, an elderly high priest in a red mantle and white cap stands behind an altar draped in a patterned orange cloth and receives a thin rod from a young man in blue, who stretches it across the altar at arm’s length; a second rod lies on the altar, touched by a white-haired man in a green mantle standing at the far right. Behind the youth in blue a queue of men presses forward from the left — one in grey holding out his rod, others in blue and red carrying theirs upright — and at the very back, at the left edge, stands an older bearded man with a gold halo, dressed in blue and ochre, holding his rod low. Deep blue sky above with heavy pigment losses.
caption: The Bringing of the Rods to the Temple, c. 1303–1305, fresco, 200 x 185 cm. Padua, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), upper register of the north wall. The unmarried men of the house of David file past the altar of the Temple, each surrendering his rod to the high priest: the rod that flowers will mark Mary’s husband.
