alt: Fresco detail from the painted decorative bands of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua: a full vertical strip of fictive ornament. At the centre, a quatrefoil opens onto a blue sky with pale clouds: from the upper right a bearded figure with Christ’s features bends down, his darkened halo bearing traces of an inscribed cross, and delivers a single white tablet, unmarked by any writing; at the lower left an elderly bald-crowned man with a long white beard and a darkened halo of his own, wrapped in an ochre-yellow mantle, grasps the tablet with both hands. At the right, beside him, rises the bare rock of the mountain, which he does not touch. Above and below the quatrefoil run interlaced bands of fictive Cosmatesque inlay, and lozenge fields of red acanthus scrollwork close the strip at top and bottom.
caption: Moses on Mount Sinai, quadrilobe on the decorative bands, 1304–1306. Fresco. North wall, lower register, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. On the painted band between the Ascension and the Pentecost: God, bearing Christ’s features, bends down from the sky to deliver the white tablet of the Law into the grasping hands of Moses — the Sinai of the fiftieth day stationed beside the Pentecost of the fiftieth day, the Law in stone beside the Law in fire.

alt: Fresco detail from the painted decorative bands of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua: a vertical strip with two barbed quatrefoils on blue grounds, separated by a large panel of fictive rose marble in dark frames. In the upper quatrefoil, a young evangelist with short dark hair, a darkened halo, a pale tunic with an embroidered collar and a red mantle over one shoulder sits behind a wooden writing-desk, his right hand raised beside his face holding a slender pen, another pen lying on the desk. In the lower quatrefoil, an old evangelist with long white hair and beard and a darkened halo bends low over his wooden desk, reading his page, a darkened pen held still in his left hand.
caption: Two Evangelists, quadrilobes on the decorative bands, 1304–1306. Fresco. North wall, lower register, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. On the terminal band at the right of the Pentecost, where the cycle ends against the west wall: two haloed evangelists at their writing-desks — a young one pausing, pen raised, an old one bent close over his page — the story the walls have just told, caught in the act of becoming Scripture.

alt: Fresco detail of a painted ornamental band crossing the vault of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua: a vertical strip on deep red ground. At the top, a barbed quatrefoil on blue holds the bust of an old man with long flowing white hair and beard, a radiate gold halo and a red mantle, holding upright a darkened object that widens fan-wise as it rises past his left shoulder, perhaps a scourge, lower right, appears the small head and part of the bust of a child, his face turned up toward the elder. At the centre, blue acanthus scrollwork with gold flowers opens around the bust of a wingèd figure: a youthful face under a pointed leaf-like hood, grey-blue wings spread, a gold mantle clasped at the throat. At the bottom, a second barbed quatrefoil on blue holds the bust of a bearded man with a radiate gold halo and brown mantle, his right hand raised. Cosmatesque mosaic chevrons separate the compartments.
caption: Busts on the first decorative band of the vault (detail), c. 1303–1305. Fresco. Barrel vault, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. A stretch of the first of the three ornamental arches that cross the starry vault, at the right of which opens the field of the blessing Redeemer: haloed busts of the old covenant’s holy ones in barbed quatrefoils on blue — an elder with a child at his shoulder among them — alternating with winged figures born out of the acanthus scrollwork.

alt: Fresco detail of a painted decorative band on the north wall of the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua: a vertical strip. At top and bottom, barbed quatrefoils on grey-blue grounds each hold the bust of an elderly bearded man with a radiate gold halo and a rose-red mantle over a pale tunic. The upper elder, short grey-bearded, lays his right hand flat against his breast; the lower, long-bearded, rests his left hand on a staff. The blue of the grounds survives patchily, the azurite fallen in places.
caption: Decorative band with busts, detail, c. 1303–1305. Fresco. North wall, upper register, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. From the painted band at the left of the Birth of the Virgin: two haloed elders in barbed quatrefoils, one hand laid to the breast and the other on a staff, separated by a panel of fictive marble and flanked by candelabra strips — the crowned ancestors of the margins, stationed at the threshold of the birth their whole order waited for.

alt: Fresco detail of a painted decorative band in the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua: a vertical strip of fictive grey-green veined marble, bordered by ochre candelabra strips. At the centre, a barbed quatrefoil on a blue-grey ground holds the bust of a beardless young man with short dark hair and a radiate gold halo, wearing a pale mantle over a tunic, his right hand laid flat on the breast, his left holding a small closed red book, plain and unclasped, against his chest. Above and below the quatrefoil, two white lozenge frames enclose red cross-shaped leaf ornaments, with small gemmed squares at their points.
caption: Bust of a young saint with a book, quadrilobe on the decorative bands, c. 1303–1306. Fresco. Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. On the painted band between Joachim Expelled from the Temple and Joachim among the Shepherds (placement uncertain), south wall, upper register: a beardless young saint with a radiate halo, a red book held against the breast, in a barbed quatrefoil set in fictive grey-veined marble between two gemmed lozenge-crosses — a reader of the new covenant among the margins' crowned company.

alt: Fresco detail of a painted decorative band in the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua: a vertical strip that narrows slightly toward the top. In the upper barbed quatrefoil, on a dark ground, the bust of a beardless young saint with a radiate gold halo, in a pale mantle over red, his right index finger pointing across his own chest, his left hand holding a darkened upright object. In the lower quatrefoil, on a grey-blue ground, the bust of an old man with a radiate gold halo, unruly white hair and a long forked beard, his right hand raised before him, his left arm drawn across the body. Between them stands a tall plain cream-coloured panel in a painted frame; strips of candelabra ornament on ochre and brown flank the compartments.
caption: Decorative band with busts, detail, c. 1303–1305. Fresco. Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. From the chapel’s painted framing system: two haloed busts in barbed quatrefoils — above, a young saint pointing across his chest with his right hand, a darkened object in his left; below, a wild-bearded elder with his right hand raised — separated by a tall pale panel and flanked by candelabra strips.

alt: Fresco detail of a painted decorative band in the Scrovegni Chapel, Padua: a vertical strip of fictive grey-green veined marble flecked with dark markings. At the centre, a barbed quatrefoil on a muted violet-grey ground holds the bust of a young man with shoulder-length light brown hair, a short beard, and a radiate gold halo, wearing a rose mantle over one shoulder and a pale garment on the other, his right hand drawn before his breast. Above and below, two white lozenge frames enclose red-and-gold cross-shaped leaf ornaments with small gemmed squares at their points.
caption: Bust of a young saint, quadrilobe on the decorative bands, c. 1303–1305. Fresco. North wall, upper register, Scrovegni Chapel (Arena Chapel), Padua. On the painted band between the Marriage of the Virgin and the Wedding Procession: a long-haired young saint with a radiate halo, his right hand drawn to his breast, in a barbed quatrefoil set in fictive grey-green marble between two gemmed lozenge-crosses — a witness of the margins posted between the vow and the procession.

alt: Five-panel gold-ground altarpiece under pointed gables. At the centre Christ faces forward with a cruciform halo, blessing with his right hand and holding a red studded book. At the left of the centre the Virgin, in a grey veil and dark blue mantle over a red gown, lays her hand on her breast; at the far left the beardless young Saint John the Evangelist, in pink and green, holds a green book in both hands and looks almost straight out. At the right of the centre Saint John the Baptist, gaunt, with long dark hair and beard and a red mantle, holds a scroll with lines of script and glances aside beyond the frame; at the far right Saint Francis, in a brown habit, bows his head with his hands crossed on his chest, his face in shadow.
caption: Giotto di Bondone (and workshop), Christ Blessing with Saint John the Evangelist, the Virgin, Saint John the Baptist and Saint Francis ("Peruzzi Altarpiece"), c. 1310–1315, tempera and gilded gesso on poplar, 105.7 × 250.2 cm. Raleigh, North Carolina Museum of Art, gift of the Samuel H. Kress Foundation, 1961 (GL.60.17.7). The polyptych is often identified, on circumstantial grounds, as the altarpiece of the Peruzzi Chapel in Santa Croce, Florence.

alt: Upper half of a parchment page with an unframed painting. At the left a young shepherd sits under a tree playing a long pipe, with the heads of cattle looking out behind the trunk; in the centre a second shepherd stands with his arm raised, leading a goat; at the right a bushy tree with more animals. Below, lines of text in large capitals, the first in red. A round library stamp is printed in the centre.
caption: First painter, Tityrus and Meliboeus, Eclogue I, Vergilius Romanus, fol. 1r, late fifth or early sixth century. Pigments on parchment. Vatican City, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat. lat. 3867. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Parchment page with two lines of brown capitals at the top, then a framed picture on a pink ground: a young man in a white toga sits frontally on a cushioned chair holding a small red book; an orange lectern stands at the left and an orange round box with a lock and ring at the right. Below the frame the words POETA and CORYDON in red, and four lines of brown capitals with POE in red in the margin.
caption: Second painter, Portrait of Virgil, at the head of Eclogue II, Vergilius Romanus, fol. 3v, late fifth or early sixth century. Pigments on parchment. Vatican City, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat. lat. 3867. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Parchment page with eleven lines of large capitals in brown ink, with speakers' names in red in the margin. Below, a framed rectangular picture: a young man in a white toga sits frontally on a chair holding a small book, with a red round box with a lock and chain at the left and a red lectern at the right, on a pink ground.
caption: Second painter, Portrait of Virgil, at the end of Eclogue III, Vergilius Romanus, fol. 9r, late fifth or early sixth century. Pigments on parchment. Vatican City, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat. lat. 3867. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Parchment page with a line of capitals at the top, then a framed picture on an ochre ground: a young man in a white toga sits frontally on a cushioned chair holding a small red book; at the left an orange round box with a silver lock and a chain; at the right an orange lectern on a stand. Below, a line of red capitals and lines of brown capitals.
caption: Second painter, Portrait of Virgil, at the head of Eclogue VI, Vergilius Romanus, fol. 14r, late fifth or early sixth century. Pigments on parchment. Vatican City, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat. lat. 3867. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Square miniature in a red and gold frame on an ochre ground sprinkled with small plants. At the lower left a laurel-crowned shepherd sits on a pink rock playing a long pipe; at the right a second crowned shepherd stands adjusting his cloak. Between them goats, a leaping black horse, a dog with a collar, sheep and a mare with her foal; at the top a dark conical hut with a hanging flask and a red flower.
caption: Second painter, Herdsmen and their animals, Georgics III, Vergilius Romanus, fol. 44v, late fifth or early sixth century. Pigments on parchment. Vatican City, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat. lat. 3867. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Square miniature in a red and gold frame on an ochre ground with small plants. At the right a laurel-crowned herdsman sits on a pink rock holding a crook and stretching out his hand; at the upper left two horses leap; in the centre a seated dog with a collar and a red flower; at the bottom a red bull and a black bull lock horns; at the lower right a dark conical hut.
caption: Second painter, Herdsman with horses and fighting bulls, Georgics III, Vergilius Romanus, fol. 45r, late fifth or early sixth century. Pigments on parchment. Vatican City, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat. lat. 3867. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Square miniature in a gold frame on a pale ground. At the left an armed warrior with a crested helmet, scale armour, spear and a large purple shield sits under a leafy tree. At the right a winged female figure with a halo flies towards him beneath a rainbow, holding a pink veil and reaching out to him. Above at the left a small building with a gable; below, flowers and a quiver of arrows.
caption: Second painter, Iris appears to Turnus, Aeneid IX, Vergilius Romanus, fol. 74v, late fifth or early sixth century. Pigments on parchment. Vatican City, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat. lat. 3867. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Square miniature in a gold frame. Under a purple curtain hung in swags, three identical haloed figures in golden Phrygian helmets and purple mantles sit frontally on thrones, each holding a spear and pointing with the right hand. At the left a round tower and a doorway, and a young man in a short tunic sacrificing a goat. On the pink floor in front lie palm branches and two golden crowns.
caption: Second painter, The prizes for the funeral games of Anchises, with the presiding Trojans and a sacrifice, Aeneid V, Vergilius Romanus, fol. 76v, late fifth or early sixth century. Pigments on parchment. Vatican City, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat. lat. 3867. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Square miniature in a gold frame. Two ships with sails and oars carry helmeted warriors with round shields on a purple sea full of green sea monsters and fish; in the leading ship a figure raises both arms to the sky. Above, in a grey sky streaked with rain, two wind figures blow horns from the corners and a winged figure in red brandishes a fiery torch.
caption: Second painter, The Trojan fleet in the storm, Aeneid I, Vergilius Romanus, fol. 77r, late fifth or early sixth century. Pigments on parchment. Vatican City, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat. lat. 3867. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Parchment page with eighteen lines of large capitals within a painted frame of purple and olive-green panels edged with gold scrolls. The first three lines are written in red, the rest in brown. At the top, above the frame, two lines in a later cursive hand and the name Jehan Courtoys; the folio number 78 at the upper right.
caption: Opening of the Aeneid, Arma virumque cano, within a painted frame, Vergilius Romanus, fol. 78r, late fifth or early sixth century, with fifteenth-century additions. Ink and pigments on parchment. Vatican City, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat. lat. 3867. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Square miniature in a red and gold frame. Under a green curtain hung in swags, three haloed figures recline on a purple couch behind a semicircular cushion: in the centre a crowned woman in an orange mantle, at the left a man in a white tunic, at the right a man in a red Phrygian helmet drinking from a cup. In front, a round table with a fish on a plate; two young servants with jugs and cups stand at the sides.
caption: Second painter, The banquet of Dido and Aeneas, Aeneid I, Vergilius Romanus, fol. 100v, late fifth or early sixth century. Pigments on parchment. Vatican City, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat. lat. 3867. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Square miniature in a red and gold frame. Behind a crenellated white brick wall, a row of Trojans and two women look down. At the lower left a haloed bearded king in a long striped robe and purple mantle, surrounded by soldiers with spears and large shields, points at a naked young man with his arms bound behind his back who stands before him. At the right a tall harnessed horse stands against the wall.
caption: Second painter, Sinon brought before Priam, with the wooden horse, Aeneid II, Vergilius Romanus, fol. 101r, late fifth or early sixth century. Pigments on parchment. Vatican City, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat. lat. 3867. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Square miniature in a red and gold frame on a green ground with trees and streaks of rain. At the upper left a figure in a cloak sits on a rock under a large round red hat, holding a spear; beside him a seated warrior with a red-crested helmet, spear and orange shield. At the left two saddled horses stand. At the lower right, inside a white-edged cave, a woman in an orange mantle and a man in a purple mantle and helmet sit side by side, the woman's hand on his chest, with a spear and shield beside them.
caption: Second painter, The storm during the hunt: Dido and Aeneas in the cave, Aeneid IV, Vergilius Romanus, fol. 106r, late fifth or early sixth century. Pigments on parchment. Vatican City, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat. lat. 3867. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Square miniature in a red and gold frame on an ochre ground, much worn. At the left a group of young men with spears and shields; the foremost, in a white tunic and purple cloak, draws a bow and aims upward. A white stag with branching antlers leaps across the top of the picture, wounded, with red marks on its flank. At the right a young man in a green tunic and orange cloak holds a purple shield above his head and looks up. A striped quiver lies on the ground; two small roundels with busts are painted at the upper left.
caption: Second painter, Ascanius shooting the stag of Silvia, Aeneid VII, Vergilius Romanus, fol. 163r, late fifth or early sixth century. Pigments on parchment. Vatican City, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat. lat. 3867. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Square miniature in a gold frame on a pale pink ground. Two armies face each other with raised spears and large oval shields. At the front of the left group a warrior in scale armour, a gold helmet and a purple cloak draws a bow; at the front of the right group a warrior in scale armour and a gold helmet stretches out his arm, behind men with crested helmets and red, green and purple shields. Arrows fly between them, and a striped quiver lies on the ground.
caption: Second painter, Two armies facing each other with archers, Aeneid, Vergilius Romanus, fol. 188v, late fifth or early sixth century. Pigments on parchment. Vatican City, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat. lat. 3867. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Heavily stained and darkened vellum page from the Book of Mulling, with a single narrow column of small Irish minuscule script on the left containing the end of John's Gospel and the opening of the colophon; further colophon lines naming the scribe Mulling survive at the upper right, and long diagonal tears across the blank right half of the leaf are closed with stitched vellum repairs.
caption: Dublin, Trinity College Library, MS 60 (Book of Mulling), folio 94r. The recto of the manuscript's last leaf carries the closing portion of the Gospel of John — a later annotation at the foot of the column reads "Joh. 21."

alt: Severely stained brown vellum leaf, the last of the Book of Mulling. Faint lines of small Irish minuscule containing a liturgical office survive in the upper left; the circular diagram — two barely visible concentric circles with faded Irish captions — occupies the lower centre of the page. A long branching tear runs diagonally across the middle of the leaf, closed with visible zigzag thread stitching, and a large irregular lighter repair patch fills the damaged upper right corner.
caption: Dublin, Trinity College Library, MS 60 (Book of Mulling), folio 94v. The verso of the last leaf carries, side by side, a compressed devotional office and the manuscript's most debated image: two concentric circles, only a few centimetres across, ringed and filled with captioned crosses, with the four cardinal points written in Irish. On Lawlor's reading the outer line of writing names the crosses of Mark at the south, Matthew at the west, John at the north and Luke at the east, and the inner line names the prophets Jeremiah, Daniel and Ezekiel, with a fourth, Isaiah, restored; four further crosses inside the circles bear partly effaced captions naming the Holy Spirit, gifts, angels from above, and Christ with his apostles.

alt: Full-page miniature from the Book of Mulling showing a haloed, frontal standing evangelist with orange hair, wearing a mauve cloak over a blue tunic, its folds drawn as interlaced gold-edged bands; he holds a book against his chest with one hand laid flat over it. The figure stands in a rectangular frame with knotwork squares at the corners and tall side panels of interlaced elongated animal ornament on blue grounds; his halo overlaps the top of the frame. The vellum leaf is browned and worn at the edges
caption: Dublin, Trinity College Library, MS 60 (Book of Mulling), folio 81v. The portrait of John, the only evangelist portrait illustrated here; the identification rests on position alone, for the figure carries no inscription and no evangelist symbol. The number 53 at the upper right is the older numbering of the British Museum binders.

alt: Front face of the medieval book-shrine of the Book of Mulling: a rectangular metal box with worn silver surface, dominated by a large polished oval rock crystal held by dark claw mounts at the centre; rows of gilt Gothic lettering on silver foil are visible magnified through the crystal. Around it are several smaller settings — dark red and brown oval polished stones in decorated mounts, a small cross-shaped fitting and plain bosses — framed by twisted rope-like mouldings, with dents and losses at the corners. The shrine stands on a pale surface in a museum display
caption: Shrine (cumdach) of the Book of Mulling, from St Mullins, Co. Carlow; principal phase c. 1402, with settings added at various later dates. The box is built of copper-alloy sheets partly covered with silver and, unlike the shrine of the Book of Dimma, is ornamented on its front face only, which carries a deliberately heterogeneous display of eight settings accumulated over the object's history — polished oval cabochons in collared mounts, a small cross-shaped setting, and plain bosses, framed by rope-twist mouldings.

alt: A book cover of gold seen from the front. At the centre, in a frame of green and blue stones and pearls, a seated figure of Christ with a halo, in gold relief, holds an open book on his knee inside an oval. Around him four gold panels show seated figures writing, and four wider panels above and below show groups of standing figures before buildings. A broad outer frame is crowded with large green emeralds, blue sapphires and pearls in raised gold settings with filigree.
caption: Front cover with Christ in Majesty, the four evangelists and four scenes from the Gospels, gold repoussé, sapphires, emeralds and pearls, court workshop of Charles the Bald, c. 870. Codex Aureus of Saint Emmeram, Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 14000. Image: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek München, Clm 14000, front cover, urn:nbn:de:bvb:12-bsb00096095-8.

alt: The same gold book cover photographed at an angle from one corner, lying on a pale surface. caption: The front cover seen at an angle, showing the depth of the raised settings and the thickness of the book block. Codex Aureus of Saint Emmeram, c. 870, Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 14000. Image: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek München, Clm 14000, front cover, oblique view, urn:nbn:de:bvb:12-bsb00096095-8.

alt: A manuscript page framed by a border of red-orange acanthus on gold. At the left a tall initial letter I filled with gold interlace and coloured knotwork, with interlaced terminals in red, green, blue and yellow at top and bottom. To the right, four broad dark red bands carry gold capital letters reading NCIPIT, PRAEFATIO, SCI HIERONIMI and PBRI. Between the bands, a faint pale design of roundels with busts, a checkerboard and leaves shows through from the other side of the leaf. An oval library stamp reads BIBLIOTHECA REGIA MONACENSIS.
caption: Incipit of the preface of Saint Jerome, with a great initial I of Franco-Saxon type. Codex Aureus of Saint Emmeram, court school of Charles the Bald, 870, fol. 1v. Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 14000. Image: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek München, Clm 14000, fol. 1v, urn:nbn:de:bvb:12-bsb00096095-8.

alt: A manuscript page framed by a border of red and gold acanthus. A huge gold letter B, its shaft and bowls filled with interlace and knots in gold, blue, green and red, fills the upper left. To its right, gold capitals on dark red bands read BEATISSIMO PAPAE DAMASO HIERONIMUS. Below, a large gold letter N filled with interlace and leaves on blue and green, followed by further lines in gold on red bands reading NOVUM OPUS ME FACERE COGIS EX VETERE. Faint lines of writing show through between the bands.
caption: The opening of Jerome's letter to Pope Damasus, Novum opus, with the initials B and N. Codex Aureus of Saint Emmeram, court school of Charles the Bald, 870, fol. 2r. Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 14000. Image: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek München, Clm 14000, fol. 2r, urn:nbn:de:bvb:12-bsb00096095-8.

alt: A full-page painting. A crowned king with a moustache, in a gold mantle over a blue tunic with gold flowers, sits on a jewelled throne under a red and gold dome on columns, with a green and red curtain behind him and a hand reaching down from a circle of sky above. Two angels fly towards him at the top. Beside him stand two young men, one holding a sword in a sheath, the other a spear and a round shield; at the outer edges two crowned women hold up horns of plenty. Golden crowns hang under the side arches. Above and below the picture, panels of purple-red carry lines of gold capital letters.
caption: Charles the Bald enthroned, with armour-bearers, personifications of his lands and the hand of God. Codex Aureus of Saint Emmeram, court school of Charles the Bald, 870, fol. 5v. Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 14000. Image: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek München, Clm 14000, fol. 5v, urn:nbn:de:bvb:12-bsb00096095-8.

alt: A full-page painting. At the top, in a red and gold circle, a gold lamb with a cross halo stands on a scroll beside a chalice, against a dark blue sky with gold stars. Below, a great curved band of old men with white beards in pale robes, arranged in two crowded rows like the sides of a bowl, all lift gold crowns towards the lamb. A large gold star shines in the dark blue space between them. At the bottom left a half-naked man sits by blue water, and at the bottom right a dark-skinned woman with a horn of plenty sits on rocks. Below the picture, lines of gold capitals on a red panel.
caption: The Adoration of the Lamb by the twenty-four elders (Revelation 4–5), with the Earth and the Sea. Codex Aureus of Saint Emmeram, court school of Charles the Bald, 870, fol. 6r. Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 14000. Image: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek München, Clm 14000, fol. 6r, urn:nbn:de:bvb:12-bsb00096095-8.

alt: A full-page painting within a border of gold and pink leaves. At the centre, in a pointed oval of blue, green and red, Christ with a cross halo sits on a globe, holding a disc in his raised right hand and a red book on his knee. Four round medallions above, below and at the sides contain half-length bearded men holding scrolls. In the four corners, between curved bands of colour, four seated men write or hold scrolls, and small creatures appear between them: a winged man, an eagle, a lion and an ox. Gold capitals run across the top and bottom of the page.
caption: Christ in Majesty with the four evangelists, their symbols and the four major prophets. Codex Aureus of Saint Emmeram, court school of Charles the Bald, 870, fol. 6v. Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 14000. Image: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek München, Clm 14000, fol. 6v, urn:nbn:de:bvb:12-bsb00096095-8.

alt: A manuscript page with a large round arch on five painted columns. Inside the arch, on a dark blue ground, four winged creatures with gold halos hold an open book reading CANON PRIMUS IN QUO QUATTUOR: a winged man, a lion, an ox and an eagle. Two grey birds stand on a red band above the arch. Below, four small arches over the columns carry red labels with the names MATH, MARC, LUC, IOH, above four columns of Roman numerals written in gold. The columns are painted with marbling and zigzags, with gold capitals and bases. A broad border of gold rosettes on red frames the page.
caption: The first canon table, with the symbols of the four evangelists holding a book inscribed CANON PRIMUS IN QUO QUATTUOR. Codex Aureus of Saint Emmeram, court school of Charles the Bald, 870, fol. 7r. Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 14000. alt: A full-page painting under a round arch with a meander pattern, on columns. A bearded saint with a gold halo, in a purple-pink mantle, sits on a large jewelled throne set with white pearls, holding a pen near his chin and a scroll in his left hand, his eyes turned upward. On either side stands a tall tower-like building with open doors revealing scrolls, and a round box of scrolls stands at the right. Above, on a red band of sky with plants, a small winged angel points towards him. Below the throne lies a strip of green with white flowers and a large field speckled with gold and red.
caption: Saint Matthew with his symbol, the angel. Codex Aureus of Saint Emmeram, court school of Charles the Bald, 870, fol. 16r. Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 14000. Image: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek München, Clm 14000, fol. 16r, urn:nbn:de:bvb:12-bsb00096095-8.

alt: A manuscript page covered with gold ornament on red within a border of meander and pearls. At the centre, a large circle with a dark blue ground shows a golden lion with a shaggy mane standing on flames and waves, framed by a red ring with gold lettering. In the four corners, small green roundels hold a winged man, an eagle, a lion and an ox. The rest of the page is filled with gold scrolls, rosettes and leaves.

alt: A manuscript page covered with gold ornament within a border of meander and pearls. In the upper part, the large interlaced gold letters LIB, filled with dense knotwork in gold, blue and green, with the smaller letters ER beside them. Below, a red panel filled with gold scrolls carries three lines of gold capitals reading GENERATIONIS, IHU XPI FILII DAVID, FILII ABRAHAM. Gold bands form a lozenge around the letters, ending at the sides in roundels filled with leaf scrolls.
caption: Initial page of the Gospel of Matthew, Liber generationis Iesu Christi filii David filii Abraham (Matthew 1:1). Codex Aureus of Saint Emmeram, court school of Charles the Bald, 870, fol. 17r. Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 14000. Image: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek München, Clm 14000, fol. 17r, urn:nbn:de:bvb:12-bsb00096095-8.

alt: A full-page painting under a round arch decorated with a cable pattern and gold scrolls on dark red. A grey-haired saint with a gold halo sits on a throne whose sides end in lion heads, resting his cheek on his right hand, with a pen in his left. To the right, an open book stands on a tall lectern. Behind the throne, a curved building of many coloured storeys with windows fills the background against a blue sky. Above, beyond a band of blue waves, a small winged lion with a halo flies in an orange sky. Below, a band of waves and a large field speckled with red, gold and white.
caption: Saint Mark with his symbol, the lion. Codex Aureus of Saint Emmeram, court school of Charles the Bald, 870, fol. 46r. Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 14000. Image: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek München, Clm 14000, fol. 46r, urn:nbn:de:bvb:12-bsb00096095-8.

alt: A full-page painting under a round arch with gold scrolls and pink feathered bands. A bearded saint with a gold halo, in a grey-white mantle, sits frontally on a throne whose sides end in the heads of beasts, holding a pen in his right hand and an open book on a lectern at his left, his eyes raised. Behind him rise walls and towers of blue and purple masonry with windows and doors; scrolls lie on the walls. Above, in an orange sky with blue mountains, a winged ox with a halo flies at the left. Below, a band of speckled panels and a large field speckled with gold, pink and white.
caption: Saint Luke with his symbol, the ox. Codex Aureus of Saint Emmeram, court school of Charles the Bald, 870, fol. 65r. Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 14000. Image: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek München, Clm 14000, fol. 65r, urn:nbn:de:bvb:12-bsb00096095-8.

alt: A full-page painting under a round arch with gold leaves on green. An old saint with white hair and beard and a gold halo, in a purple mantle, sits on a throne whose arms end in lion heads, holding a closed white book on his knee and raising his right hand to his breast as he looks upward. Behind him, on a green ground with gold stars, rises a curved wall with arched windows and a row of knobs, with doorways at left and right showing rolled scrolls. Above, in a sky of blue clouds, orange and yellow, a winged eagle with a halo flies at the right. Below, a band of coloured jewels and a large field speckled with gold, pink and white with gold roundels.
caption: Saint John with his symbol, the eagle. Codex Aureus of Saint Emmeram, court school of Charles the Bald, 870, fol. 97r. Munich, Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, Clm 14000. Image: Bayerische Staatsbibliothek München, Clm 14000, fol. 97r, urn:nbn:de:bvb:12-bsb00096095-8.

alt: Medieval manuscript page with a blue and gold outer frame enclosing a broad purple border filled with small interlaced dragons, birds and beasts drawn in gold line; in the deeper purple central field, six lines of gold capital letters in three groups begin HUNC EGBTE LIBRUM and end QUE DEFERT PSUL HONORI

alt: Illuminated manuscript page on purple ground framed by gold foliate interlace: a tonsured archbishop in orange-red vestments sits enthroned holding a long staff, flanked by two small monks in blue-grey habits offering golden books; gold inscriptions name Egbertus, Keraldus and Heribertus
caption: Codex Egberti, fol. 2r: dedication miniature. Archbishop Egbert of Trier (977–993), enthroned and identified by the gold inscription EGBERTUS TREVERORUM ARCHIEPS, receives a golden book from the monk Keraldus, while Heribertus holds a second volume; both are labelled Augienses, "of Reichenau". The square halo marks Egbert as a living dignitary. Trier, Stadtbibliothek, Hs. 24, c. 980s.

alt: Medieval miniature in a dark red frame with gold ornament, under a bright blue sky above yellowish ground: at left a barefoot angel with large green wings and a gold halo, in a lilac tunic and pale green mantle, holds a cross-topped staff and raises his hand in speech; at right the Virgin, haloed in gold, in a white veil, red-brown mantle and white gown, stands with one hand raised palm outward and the other extended towards him, before a walled city with towers, red roofs and a pedimented gateway

alt: Medieval miniature in a red frame with gold ornament, between lines of text and above red lettering with a large gold initial: against a blue-green sky, a haloed angel with blue-grey wings, in half-length at upper left, holds a cross-topped staff and stretches his open hand towards a bearded man in a violet tunic asleep on a gilded bed with a green cover and red pillow; at right stands a white building with a pediment, an arch and a red tiled roof

alt: Medieval miniature in a dark frame with gold ornament, under a grey-violet sky: at left a crowned, bearded king in purple and red points forward, with spear-bearing guards behind him; in the centre three soldiers in short tunics attack naked children with swords and a lance, while dead children lie heaped on the ground; at right, before a walled city with towers and red roofs, mothers with loose hair and bared breasts lament, one raising her arms, one kneeling, one covering her face

alt: Miniature within a broad frame. In the centre, under a round arch flanked by towers with red domes, a nun in a black habit sits with a wax tablet and stylus on her knees, while five red tongues of flame descend on her head from above. At the right, in a narrow building separated by a column, a tonsured monk leans forward to look at her, holding a book.
caption: Rupertsberg, illuminator working for Hildegard of Bingen, Hildegard receiving the vision, with Volmar, Scivias, fol. 1r of the Rupertsberg codex, c. 1165–1180. Formerly Wiesbaden, Landesbibliothek, Hs. 1 (lost since 1945); reproduced from the hand-painted copy made at the Abbey of St Hildegard, Eibingen, 1927–1933. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Full-page miniature of an egg-shaped cosmos on a starry blue ground within a decorated frame. The outer zone is a ring of golden flames with a red star at the top; inside it lies a dark red band with white clusters, then a blue field with golden stars and a crescent moon, and at the centre a small globe of earth surrounded by wavy bands. Small heads blowing wind appear at the sides and bottom.
caption: Rupertsberg, illuminator working for Hildegard of Bingen, The Cosmos as an Egg, Scivias I.3, fol. 14r of the Rupertsberg codex, c. 1165–1180. Formerly Wiesbaden, Landesbibliothek, Hs. 1 (lost since 1945); reproduced from the hand-painted copy made at the Abbey of St Hildegard, Eibingen, 1927–1933. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Full-page miniature of a great disc of concentric rings breaking through its frame. The outer rings are filled with winged angels in pale colours, the inner rings with rows of faces and bands of gold and colour; at the centre a ring of red figures covered with eyes and a ring of golden flame-like forms surround an empty white circle.
caption: Rupertsberg, illuminator working for Hildegard of Bingen, The Choirs of Angels, Scivias I.6, fol. 38r of the Rupertsberg codex, c. 1165–1180. Formerly Wiesbaden, Landesbibliothek, Hs. 1 (lost since 1945); reproduced from the hand-painted copy made at the Abbey of St Hildegard, Eibingen, 1927–1933. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Full-page miniature on a deep blue ground within a red border filled with white and gold flower-like ornament. In the middle stands a frontal male figure in a long blue-grey robe, with dark shoulder-length hair, both hands raised with palms outward at chest height.
caption: Rupertsberg, illuminator working for Hildegard of Bingen, The Trinity, Scivias II.2, from the Rupertsberg codex, c. 1165–1180. alt: Miniature divided into four fields by a cross-shaped frame. Upper left, a crowned woman holds a scroll above a crowd and a stepped structure with organ-like pipes. Upper right, the crowned woman stands before Christ enthroned on an ornate altar-like block. Lower left, a figure in a triangle holds a scroll above red flames. Lower right, the crowned woman, a golden disc above her, receives dark naked figures into her body and releases them from her mouth.
caption: Rupertsberg, illuminator working for Hildegard of Bingen, Ecclesia as Mother: the Church and Baptism, Scivias II.3, from the Rupertsberg codex, c. 1165–1180. Formerly Wiesbaden, Landesbibliothek, Hs. 1 (lost since 1945); reproduced from the hand-painted copy made at the Abbey of St Hildegard, Eibingen, 1927–1933. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Miniature within a purple and gold frame. A tall crowned woman with a pale face fills the page; golden flame-like shapes rise from her shoulders like wings, and in her breast, held by her arms, is a group of small figures in red, blue and white. Her lower body is a column of white rocks outlined in black.
caption: Rupertsberg, illuminator working for Hildegard of Bingen, Ecclesia and the Orders of the Church, Scivias II.5, from the Rupertsberg codex, c. 1165–1180. Formerly Wiesbaden, Landesbibliothek, Hs. 1 (lost since 1945); reproduced from the hand-painted copy made at the Abbey of St Hildegard, Eibingen, 1927–1933. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Front cover of a large book bound in pale worn leather over wooden boards, tooled with lines and small stamps. Pierced metal corner pieces with animal motifs protect the four corners, a large pierced metal boss sits in the centre, and remains of clasps are visible on the right edge.
caption: Riesencodex, front cover, binding of the fifteenth or sixteenth century over a manuscript of c. 1180–1190. Pigskin over wooden boards with metal fittings. Wiesbaden, Hochschul- und Landesbibliothek RheinMain, Hs. 2. Image: Hochschul- und Landesbibliothek RheinMain, Wiesbaden, CC BY 4.0.

alt: Worn, stained parchment page covered with a long text in brown ink in a later cursive hand, under a heading in larger letters at the top. A number is written at the upper right margin.
caption: Riesencodex, fol. 1r, with a later heading Liber sancti Ruperti apud Pinguiam and notes on Hildegard as foundress, manuscript c. 1180–1190. Wiesbaden, Hochschul- und Landesbibliothek RheinMain, Hs. 2. Image: Hochschul- und Landesbibliothek RheinMain, Wiesbaden, CC BY 4.0.

alt: Manuscript page in two columns of dark brown script. At the top of the left column a red rubric, and below it a tall red initial E with foliate scrolls, followed by large red capital letters; the text continues in a regular Romanesque minuscule.
caption: Rupertsberg, Opening of the Scivias, with the Protestificatio, Riesencodex, fol. 3r, c. 1180–1190. Ink and red pigment on parchment. Wiesbaden, Hochschul- und Landesbibliothek RheinMain, Hs. 2. Image: Hochschul- und Landesbibliothek RheinMain, Wiesbaden, CC BY 4.0.

alt: Manuscript page in two columns of dark brown script. At the top of the left column a red rubric and a large red initial E with scrolls in its bowl, followed by the text in a regular minuscule.
caption: Rupertsberg, Opening of the third book of the Scivias, with the first vision, Riesencodex, fol. 73r, c. 1180–1190. Ink and red pigment on parchment. Wiesbaden, Hochschul- und Landesbibliothek RheinMain, Hs. 2. Image: Hochschul- und Landesbibliothek RheinMain, Wiesbaden, CC BY 4.0.

alt: Full-page drawing tinted in red, blue and green. At the top Christ sits in a mandorla within a large lobed circle filled with rows of angels, with wavy bands of water at the sides. At the left a dark strip shows rebel angels and a dragon falling. In the middle six roundels show the days of creation. At the bottom, between a gate and a small tower, scenes of Paradise: an angel with a sword at the gate, the four rivers, Adam and Eve at the tree with the serpent, and their expulsion.
caption: Zwiefalten or Salem, Initium creaturae dei: Christ among the angels, the fall of the rebel angels, the six days of creation and Paradise, Salem codex, fol. 2r, late twelfth century. Pen drawing and colours on parchment. Heidelberg, Universitätsbibliothek, Cod. Sal. X,16. Image: Universitätsbibliothek Heidelberg, Cod. Sal. X,16, public domain.

alt: Full-page drawing of a cosmic diagram. At the centre a crowned figure on a blue disc holds personifications; around it diamonds with faces, then a ring with the sun, the moon, a star and the seasons, then an outer ring with the signs of the zodiac in red and blue roundels. Figures of Dawn and Storm lie at top and bottom, a standing man and woman at the sides, and four naked wind figures blowing horns fill the corners.
caption: Zwiefalten or Salem, Annus: the Year with the seasons, the zodiac and the winds, Salem codex, fol. 2v, late twelfth century. Pen drawing and colours on parchment. Heidelberg, Universitätsbibliothek, Cod. Sal. X,16. Image: Universitätsbibliothek Heidelberg, Cod. Sal. X,16, public domain.

alt: Manuscript page with two columns of a chapter summary in dark script with red initials. In the lower right, a two-storey architectural frame: above, under a gable, a standing figure on a blue ground holds a tool and a pair of tablets; below, under an arch, a hooded figure sits on a chair writing at a lectern.
caption: Zwiefalten or Salem, The writer of the visions, with the summary of the Scivias, Salem codex, fol. 3v, late twelfth century. Pen drawing and colours on parchment. Heidelberg, Universitätsbibliothek, Cod. Sal. X,16. Image: Universitätsbibliothek Heidelberg, Cod. Sal. X,16, public domain.

alt: Manuscript page. At the left a tall painted panel with three linked roundels on a red, blue and green ground: at the top Christ enthroned with a book, in the middle a standing veiled figure, at the bottom a bearded man seated at the foot of a tree. At the right large display capitals in red, green and blue and a tall initial I with a climbing figure.
caption: Zwiefalten or Salem, Opening page with a painted panel and display capitals, Incipiunt capitula libri Scivias simplicis hominis, Salem codex, fol. 4r, late twelfth century. Colours on parchment. Heidelberg, Universitätsbibliothek, Cod. Sal. X,16. Image: Universitätsbibliothek Heidelberg, Cod. Sal. X,16, public domain.

alt: Manuscript page. In the left column the end of a list of chapters with red and green initials. At the right a heading in large green and red capitals, and below it a large painted initial E on a blue and red ground, filled with interlaced stems, leaves and small animals, followed by the letters CCE in coloured capitals.
caption: Zwiefalten or Salem, Opening of the first book with a painted initial E, Salem codex, fol. 5v, late twelfth century. Colours on parchment. Heidelberg, Universitätsbibliothek, Cod. Sal. X,16. Image: Universitätsbibliothek Heidelberg, Cod. Sal. X,16, public domain.

alt: Manuscript page. At the left a large pen drawing of a coiling serpent-like monster lying on its back, its tail curling upward and its head at the bottom, bound with a blue chain fixed to a circular pit of red flames. At the right a list of chapters with red and green initials.
caption: Zwiefalten or Salem, The horrible worm lying on its back, bound in chains, Scivias II.7, with the chapters of the third book, Salem codex, fol. 106r, late twelfth century. Pen drawing and colours on parchment. Heidelberg, Universitätsbibliothek, Cod. Sal. X,16. Image: Universitätsbibliothek Heidelberg, Cod. Sal. X,16, public domain.

alt: Manuscript page. Upper left, the end of a list of chapters. At the right a crowned figure sits on a rainbow within a circle with a scalloped blue border inscribed with text. Below, a star falls into a mass of drawn shapes with small figures, and a long curving tail of stars descends to a broad band of red flames with blue circles at the bottom.
caption: Zwiefalten or Salem, The one enthroned above the mountain and the fall of the star, Scivias III.1, Salem codex, fol. 111r, late twelfth century. Pen drawing and colours on parchment. Heidelberg, Universitätsbibliothek, Cod. Sal. X,16. Image: Universitätsbibliothek Heidelberg, Cod. Sal. X,16, public domain.

alt: Full-page drawing. Upper left, a large circle contains a square fortified building with towers seen from above, set among coloured mountain shapes; upper right, a crowned figure enthroned in a small circle. Below, five haloed figures stand under an arcade of five arches; at the left a crowned figure in a mandorla and a man with a banner and cross; at the right Abraham kneels at the foot of a column.
caption: Zwiefalten or Salem, The four-cornered building on the mountain, with five figures under the arches and Abraham at the column, Scivias III.2, Salem codex, fol. 111v, late twelfth century. Pen drawing and colours on parchment. Heidelberg, Universitätsbibliothek, Cod. Sal. X,16. Image: Universitätsbibliothek Heidelberg, Cod. Sal. X,16, public domain.

alt: Manuscript page in two columns. In the upper right a large painted initial P on a blue ground filled with interlace and animals, its tail descending as a long dragon. In the lower left margin a small drawing of a winged head with staring eyes and bared teeth at the corner of a framed structure, labelled Zelus dei.
caption: Zwiefalten or Salem, The Zeal of God, with a painted initial P, Scivias III.5, Salem codex, fol. 135v, late twelfth century. Colours and pen drawing on parchment. Heidelberg, Universitätsbibliothek, Cod. Sal. X,16. Image: Universitätsbibliothek Heidelberg, Cod. Sal. X,16, public domain.

alt: Manuscript page. At the upper left a drawing of a ladder set diagonally between two columns, with half-length figures on its rungs; below it a large painted initial E with red and green foliage on a blue ground. At the right two columns of text.
caption: Zwiefalten or Salem, The ladder of the virtues at the pillar of the humanity of the Saviour, with a painted initial E, Scivias III.8, Salem codex, fol. 156r, late twelfth century. Pen drawing and colours on parchment. Heidelberg, Universitätsbibliothek, Cod. Sal. X,16. Image: Universitätsbibliothek Heidelberg, Cod. Sal. X,16, public domain.

alt: Full-page drawing in two columns. Upper left, five beasts, a dog, a lion, a horse, a pig and a wolf, hang upside down by ropes from a row of hills. Lower left, two old haloed men with staffs. Right, a woman in a blue veil stands with a monstrous head at her lower body, while a figure sits above on a disc; below, concentric circles and a large grinning monstrous head rising above coloured mountain shapes, and a second inverted head at the bottom.
caption: Zwiefalten or Salem, The five beasts, Enoch and Elijah, and the woman with the monstrous head, Scivias III.11, Salem codex, fol. 177r, late twelfth century. Pen drawing and colours on parchment. Heidelberg, Universitätsbibliothek, Cod. Sal. X,16. Image: Universitätsbibliothek Heidelberg, Cod. Sal. X,16, public domain.

alt: Manuscript page in two columns. Upper right, a large painted initial E with a dragon-headed tail and interlace on a blue and red ground, and a red vertical heading. Lower left, a large circular drawing with a star-shaped border: rings of haloed figures in red and green surround a central blue disc with a crowned figure enthroned.
caption: Zwiefalten or Salem, The choirs of the blessed around Christ enthroned, with a painted initial E, Scivias III.13, Salem codex, fol. 196r, about 1220. Pen drawing and colours on parchment. Heidelberg, Universitätsbibliothek, Cod. Sal. X,16. Image: Universitätsbibliothek Heidelberg, Cod. Sal. X,16, public domain.

alt: Manuscript page with a tall miniature on a gold ground in a blue foliate border. A standing figure with a red face and a red robe edged with jewelled bands has a second, grey-haired and bearded head above her own. Two great pairs of brown, blue and white wings rise from her shoulders, the upper ones ending in the head of an eagle at the left and a human head at the right. She holds a small lamb against her breast and treads on a dark, scaly monster lying on the ground, around which a serpent is coiled. Below, a separate panel shows at the left a monk writing at a desk and, beyond a slender column, a nun seated with a red stream descending on her head, holding writing tablets, with a second nun standing behind her.
caption: Rhenish illuminator, Divine Love (Caritas), with Hildegard, Volmar and a nun, Liber divinorum operum I.1, fol. 1v, c. 1210–1230. Tempera and gold on parchment, page c. 39 × 25.5 cm. Lucca, Biblioteca Statale, MS 1942. Image: Biblioteca Statale di Lucca, MS 1942, World Digital Library (Library of Congress), no known copyright restrictions.

alt: Manuscript page with a full-page miniature on a gold ground in a red and pink border. A great red figure, whose bearded old man's head appears above her own head at the top and whose feet emerge at the bottom, embraces with her arms a large wheel of concentric bands: an outer ring of red fire with flickering edges, a twisted black and red band, a broad blue band of wavy white lines and a white inner field with fine rays and dark clouds. In the centre a naked man stands with arms outstretched before a dark disc, with golden lines running from the edges of the wheel towards him. Animal heads around the rings blow winds. At the lower left, in a small niche with a tiled roof, a nun sits writing at a lectern.
caption: Rhenish illuminator, The cosmic wheel and the universal man, Liber divinorum operum I.2, fol. 9r, c. 1210–1230. Tempera and gold on parchment, page c. 39 × 25.5 cm. Lucca, Biblioteca Statale, MS 1942. Image: Biblioteca Statale di Lucca, MS 1942, World Digital Library (Library of Congress), no known copyright restrictions.

alt: Manuscript page with a full-page miniature on a gold ground in a blue border with white scrolls. A large wheel without the figure of Love fills the page: an outer ring of red fire, a twisted black and red band, a broad blue band with wavy lines, and a white inner field crossed by fine rays, in which dark, curling cloud-creatures float. At the centre a naked man stands with arms outstretched before a dark globe crossed by a horizontal line. Around the rings are animal heads, among them a red crab-like head, a spotted leopard, a lion, a wolf, a bear and a stag, each blowing white streams of breath towards the centre. At the lower left a nun sits in a niche at a lectern with an open book.
caption: Rhenish illuminator, The winds and the humours, Liber divinorum operum I.3, fol. 28v, c. 1210–1230. Tempera and gold on parchment, page c. 39 × 25.5 cm. Lucca, Biblioteca Statale, MS 1942. Image: Biblioteca Statale di Lucca, MS 1942, World Digital Library (Library of Congress), no known copyright restrictions.

alt: Manuscript page with a full-page miniature on a gold ground in a blue foliate border. A great wheel of red fire, a twisted black and red band, a blue band with wavy lines and a white field surrounds a small globe divided into four quarters coloured green, dark red, brown and grey. Around the globe, set radially, are trees in different states and small human figures digging, reaping, beating with a pole, sitting and lying. Red drops and a yellowish vapour fall into the white zone. Animal heads around the rings, among them a stag, a bear and a red crab, blow winds. At the lower left a nun sits writing in an arched niche; below the wheel a hand holds a long white scroll.
caption: Rhenish illuminator, The earth, the seasons and human labour, Liber divinorum operum I.4, fol. 38r, c. 1210–1230. Tempera and gold on parchment, page c. 39 × 25.5 cm. Lucca, Biblioteca Statale, MS 1942. Image: Biblioteca Statale di Lucca, MS 1942, World Digital Library (Library of Congress), no known copyright restrictions.

alt: Manuscript page with a miniature on a gold ground within a stepped pink border. A great disc seen as if on its side is divided into zones: a white segment at the left, a dark blue segment at the right, a central horizontal band of red, blue and dark strips, and above and below it red compartments filled with heads in flames alternating with dark ones in which toads, serpents and worms crawl. At the right the disc is bordered by a red rim and a dark, cloudy mass with a monstrous head. At the left a red globe ringed with blue is set between two great pairs of feathered wings. Above the frame a hand in a blue roundel holds a white scroll. Below, in an arched niche, a nun sits with an open book.
caption: Rhenish illuminator, The earth in five parts, purgation and punishment, Liber divinorum operum II.1, fol. 88v, c. 1210–1230. Tempera and gold on parchment, page c. 39 × 25.5 cm. Lucca, Biblioteca Statale, MS 1942. Image: Biblioteca Statale di Lucca, MS 1942, World Digital Library (Library of Congress), no known copyright restrictions.

alt: Manuscript page with a full-page miniature on a gold ground in a pink border. At the upper left a group of winged angels appears above a white and dark cloud; at the top a green wind-head blows coloured streams across the page. Below the angels a column of red, white and blue stripes descends to a blue roundel with an eagle and to a pale, cream-coloured mountain. In the centre and at the right a square city is enclosed by a thick black wall and a white inner band, with towers, churches and houses inside. At the lower left a dark winged figure falls and a patch of blue water with dark shapes appears in the corner. At the lower right a nun sits writing in an arched niche.
caption: Rhenish illuminator, The city of God, the mountain and the mirror, Liber divinorum operum III.1, fol. 118r, c. 1210–1230. Tempera and gold on parchment, page c. 39 × 25.5 cm. Lucca, Biblioteca Statale, MS 1942. Image: Biblioteca Statale di Lucca, MS 1942, World Digital Library (Library of Congress), no known copyright restrictions.

alt: Manuscript page with a miniature on a gold ground in a blue foliate border, with a separate panel below. At the upper left two figures stand side by side: one with a hairy, lion-like head and body, the other a youth in a striped garment holding a sword horizontally. At the upper right crowned figures play harps, a fiddle and an organ in a blue cloud. Below them a group of bearded men in a cloud holds a long trumpet pointing into a square walled city with towers and churches. At the left a tall green tower or mountain with a red doorway, and rays from a red sun at the left edge. In the panel below, a nun sits writing at a lectern in a building with a tower.
caption: Rhenish illuminator, The city across the ages of history, Liber divinorum operum III.2, fol. 121v, c. 1210–1230. Tempera and gold on parchment, page c. 39 × 25.5 cm. Lucca, Biblioteca Statale, MS 1942. Image: Biblioteca Statale di Lucca, MS 1942, World Digital Library (Library of Congress), no known copyright restrictions.

alt: Manuscript page with a tall miniature on a gold ground in a pink border, with a separate panel below at the left. At the top a blue cloud holds a row of haloed saints, among them a bishop in a mitre and a young saint with a palm. Below them three slender women with long braided hair, one in grey and two in white, stand in a round basin of water. Under the basin a square city with a thick black and white wall encloses towers, churches and houses. In the panel below, a nun in black sits at a lectern with an open book.
caption: Rhenish illuminator, Divine Love, Humility and Peace, Liber divinorum operum III.3, fol. 132r, c. 1210–1230. Tempera and gold on parchment, page c. 39 × 25.5 cm. Lucca, Biblioteca Statale, MS 1942. Image: Biblioteca Statale di Lucca, MS 1942, World Digital Library (Library of Congress), no known copyright restrictions.

alt: Manuscript page with a full-page miniature on a gold ground in a pink border. In the upper half a square city with a thick black and white wall encloses towers and churches; at its right a dark cloud descends and a red, flame-like mass issues from it. Below, at the left, stands a female figure with a red face and long braided hair in a green robe with a jewelled hem. Beside her stands a winged figure with a radiant red sun-like head, a body covered with blue scales, a small bearded human head in the middle of the belly, and lion's feet; its six wings in blue, pink and red carry five dark blue roundels. Above the frame at the right a hand emerges from a cloud holding a scroll. At the lower right a nun sits writing in an arched niche.
caption: Rhenish illuminator, Wisdom and the image of almighty God, Liber divinorum operum III.4, fol. 135r, c. 1210–1230. Tempera and gold on parchment, page c. 39 × 25.5 cm. Lucca, Biblioteca Statale, MS 1942. Image: Biblioteca Statale di Lucca, MS 1942, World Digital Library (Library of Congress), no known copyright restrictions.

alt: Manuscript page with a miniature on a gold ground in a blue border, with a separate panel below. At the left a large circle is divided into coloured segments of green, red, white, blue wavy water and pale yellow; within it a figure with long hair in a blue-grey robe sits frontally, raising one hand and holding up a small tablet. Between the circle and a square walled city at the right rises a pale, cone-shaped form. Above the frame a hand within a blue and red rosette holds a scroll. In the panel below, a nun sits writing in an arched niche.
caption: Rhenish illuminator, Divine Love upon the wheel of eternity, Liber divinorum operum III.5, fol. 143r, c. 1210–1230. Tempera and gold on parchment, page c. 39 × 25.5 cm. Lucca, Biblioteca Statale, MS 1942. Image: Biblioteca Statale di Lucca, MS 1942, World Digital Library (Library of Congress), no known copyright restrictions.

alt: A tall ringed stone cross, weathered grey and covered with lichen, standing on a stepped base against a blue sky. Its shaft and arms are carved with raised bosses linked by interlacing serpents; slots in the ends of the arms show where extensions were once fitted.

alt: A very wide ringed cross of light grey stone seen from below against a blue sky. Its shaft, arms and ring are carved with spirals, bosses and interlaced serpents. Behind it is part of a stone building.

alt: A rectangular box covered with gilded and silvered metal plates, seen from the front. A large central panel shows a seated figure of Christ, his hand raised in blessing, set under an arch and surrounded by a frame studded with coloured stones and rock crystal. Smaller panels at the sides show a cleric holding a crozier and a crucifixion.
caption: Shrine of the Cathach, made c. 1062–1098 at Kells, with a front remodelled in the fourteenth century. Silver, gilt silver, copper alloy, rock crystal and glass on a wooden core. Dublin, National Museum of Ireland. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A small rectangular metal box seen from the front, its surface divided by a broad cross into four fields, each containing a stylised evangelist symbol, with panels of fine filigree ornament around the edges.
caption: Soiscél Molaise, shrine of the Gospels of St Molaise of Devenish, early eleventh century, for comparison. Silver-plated and gilt copper alloy on a wooden core. Dublin, National Museum of Ireland.

alt: A manuscript page filled entirely with ornament. A double-armed cross outlined in yellow and red occupies the centre, its arms ending in squares with small crosses. The background is a dense pattern of interlaced ribbons in green, yellow and red on a dark ground, within a frame of interlace.
caption: Book of Durrow, carpet page with a double-armed cross, fol. 1v, second half of the seventh century. Pigments on parchment. Dublin, Trinity College Library, MS 57. Image: The Board of Trinity College Dublin, CC BY 4.0.

alt: A manuscript page beginning with large decorated letters N and O, filled with spirals, trumpet patterns and interlace in yellow, red and green, and outlined with rows of red dots. The following lines of brown script diminish in size down the page.
caption: Book of Durrow, initial page of Jerome's letter Novum opus, fol. 4r. Pigments on parchment. Dublin, Trinity College Library, MS 57. Image: The Board of Trinity College Dublin, CC BY 4.0.

alt: A manuscript page with a frame of interlaced ribbons. In the centre stands a frontal figure with a large oval head, staring eyes and stylised hair; his body is a bell-shaped garment covered with a chequered pattern in red, yellow and green, from which two small feet in profile emerge at the bottom.
caption: Book of Durrow, the Man, symbol of Matthew, fol. 21v. Pigments on parchment. Dublin, Trinity College Library, MS 57. Image: The Board of Trinity College Dublin, CC BY 4.0.

alt: Large medieval fresco of the Triumph of Death by Buonamico Buffalmacco in the Camposanto of Pisa, c. 1336–41. At left, richly dressed riders halt before three coffins holding decaying corpses while a hermit displays a scroll; above, anchorites live peacefully in a rocky wilderness. At centre, Death as a winged hag with a scythe swoops over a mound of dead popes, kings, and nobles, as angels and demons fight over small nude souls. At right, young men and women make music in an orange grove, unaware of Death approaching.
caption: The Triumph of Death, 1336-41, fresco, 560 x 1500 cm, Camposanto Monumentale (South Wall), Pisa.
entry: The Baptistery of San Giovanni and the Camposanto Monumentale, Pisa

alt: Medieval fresco of Hell by Buonamico Buffalmacco in the Camposanto of Pisa, c. 1336–41. Hell is shown as the interior of a rocky mountain divided into levels where devils torment naked sinners with serpents, fire, a boiling cauldron, and a dragon's maw. At the centre a gigantic horned, tusked Lucifer chews one sinner while another emerges from a second face at his belly. At the left, haloed apostles and angels with the Cross preside as crowned and mitred figures among the damned are driven toward the abyss. Painted scrolls with inscriptions label the sins and punishments.
caption: Hell, 1336-41, fresco, Camposanto Monumentale (South Wall), Pisa.
entry: The Baptistery of San Giovanni and the Camposanto Monumentale, Pisa

alt: Large medieval fresco of the Thebaid by Buonamico Buffalmacco in the Camposanto of Pisa, c. 1336–41, showing the desert of the Egyptian hermits as a rocky landscape with palms and small chapels. Dozens of episodes from the lives of the Desert Fathers appear across the mountain: Mary of Egypt, covered by her own hair, kneels before the monk Zosimas; lions recall the legend of Paul the Hermit; a hermit at upper right confronts a winged demon; other monks weave baskets, dig, read, and pray. Along the bottom the Nile, full of fish, separates the desert from a walled city, with a camel driver, a fisherman, and a rider crossing a bridge. Areas of bare plaster mark losses from the 1944 fire.
caption: The Thebaid, 1336-41, fresco, Camposanto Monumentale (South Wall), Pisa.
entry: The Baptistery of San Giovanni and the Camposanto Monumentale, Pisa
