alt: A long horizontal gold-ground panel with a border of blue and red ornament and raised gilt bosses. At the centre an old bearded bishop in a white mitre, red cope and pink tunic sits enthroned on a red cushion, holding a white crosier, with a large raised gilt halo; the red letters ZANOBIUS stand beside his head. At his left a young deacon in an orange dalmatic holds a book; at his right a young deacon in blue and white holds a censer. At each side, two framed scenes with the bishop among clerics and lay people, figures lying on the ground and a black demon leaving a man.
caption: Maestro del Bigallo, dossal of San Zanobi with Saints Eugenius and Crescentius and four scenes, c. 1230–1250, tempera and gold on panel, 109 × 274 cm. Florence, Museo dell'Opera del Duomo, inv. 9152. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Detail of the gold-ground panel: an old bishop with a grey beard and a white mitre, framed by a large raised and fluted gilt halo, sits frontally on a throne with turned wooden supports and red cushions. He wears a red cope over a pink tunic and holds a long white crosier with a spiral head; his feet in gold shoes rest on a blue footstool. Beside his head, red letters ZANO BIUS. At the left, beside the throne, black letters in Gothic script in several lines. Raised gilt bosses and ornamental bands above and below.
caption: Maestro del Bigallo, dossal of San Zanobi, Zenobius enthroned, c. 1230–1250. Florence, Museo dell'Opera del Duomo. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (detail).

alt: A scene on a gold ground within a red border with white dots. At the centre-left an old bishop in a white mitre, red cope and pink tunic sits on a folding wooden stool, looking to the right. Behind him stand two young clerics, one holding a crosier. Before him stands a small boy in a light blue tunic and dark hose, his hands joined at his waist. At the right stand a woman in a white head-cloth and dark mantle, another woman in a white veil and red mantle, and a young man in a red cloak. A broad band of loss crosses all the figures at mid-height.
caption: Maestro del Bigallo, dossal of San Zanobi, a boy brought before the bishop, c. 1230–1250. Florence, Museo dell'Opera del Duomo. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (detail).

alt: A scene on a gold ground within a red border with white dots. A boy in a blue tunic lies on the ground at the centre. At the left stand two women in white veils, the nearer in a dark blue mantle and ochre dress, stretching out her hand towards the boy; a damaged figure stands at the far left. At the right an old bishop in a white mitre and red cope bends forward and stretches his hand over the boy, followed by a cleric in black and white with a crosier, a deacon in an ochre patterned dalmatic holding a book, and other men.
caption: Maestro del Bigallo, dossal of San Zanobi, the raising of a dead boy, c. 1230–1250. Florence, Museo dell'Opera del Duomo. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (detail).

alt: A scene on a gold ground within a double red border with white dots. At the left an old bishop in a white mitre, red cope and pink tunic stretches his hand towards a young man in red lying on the ground with his eyes closed. Behind the bishop stand three clerics, one holding a crosier and one a book. At the right stand three young men in red, blue and dark cloaks over tunics and hose. A band of loss crosses all the figures at mid-height.
caption: Maestro del Bigallo, dossal of San Zanobi, the raising of the messenger of Saint Ambrose, c. 1230–1250. Florence, Museo dell'Opera del Duomo. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (detail).

alt: A scene on a gold ground within a red border with white dots. At the centre an old bishop in a white mitre and red cope stretches his right hand towards a young man in a blue tunic and black hose, whose hands are bound behind him with red cords; a small black winged demon flies out above his head. Behind the bishop stand a bearded man in red, a deacon in an ochre dalmatic with a book, and a cleric in black and white with a crosier. At the right stand a woman in a white head-cloth and red dress, another figure in dark blue, and young men, one in a blue tunic pointing.
caption: Maestro del Bigallo, dossal of San Zanobi, the exorcism of a possessed young man, c. 1230–1250. Florence, Museo dell'Opera del Duomo. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (detail).

alt: A long horizontal panel with four scenes set in a street of classical palaces and a portico with orange columns. At the left a young man in pink turns away from a girl in yellow and a group of women. Next, a young man kneels half-naked over a large bronze basin and a bishop pours water on his head among clerics. Under the portico a woman bends over a basin while a bishop baptises her. At the right a bearded man in a cope kneels before a pope seated under a green canopy, while bishops place a mitre on his head.
caption: Sandro Botticelli, Four Scenes from the Early Life of Saint Zenobius, c. 1500, tempera on wood, 66.7 × 149.2 cm. London, National Gallery, NG3918. Photo: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A long horizontal panel set in a square between a grey classical building at the left and a pink palace with a loggia at the right, with hills and cypresses in the distance. At the left a bishop kneels beside a bier on which a young man rises from a blue sheet, among weeping clerics with processional crosses. In the centre a bishop kneels beside a dead young man lying on the ground next to an open coffin of relics, with horses and a kneeling man. At the right a cleric in white sprinkles a woman sitting up on a green mat while men stagger back in amazement; in the loggia behind, a bishop in bed hands something to a cleric.
caption: Sandro Botticelli, Three Miracles of Saint Zenobius, c. 1500, tempera on wood. New York, The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Photo: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, public domain (CC0).

alt: A tall Gothic panel with a pointed gable and pinnacles, hung on a grey stone pillar of the cathedral. In a roundel at the top Christ blesses, holding a book. In the main field an old bishop in a white mitre and a white cope patterned with gold stars sits enthroned, holding a crosier and a red book; two small figures stand at either side of his head, and at his feet two kneeling deacons in green and orange, one holding a book. Below, a predella with two small scenes, coats of arms at the sides, and a carved gilt and blue bracket.
caption: Giovanni del Biondo (attributed), San Zanobi enthroned with Saints Eugenius and Crescentius, c. 1380, tempera and gold on panel, 240 × 110 cm. Florence, Santa Maria del Fiore. Photo: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A long bronze relief in a moulded bronze frame. At the left children play among trees on a hillside. In the centre a woman kneels with outstretched arms before a small standing child, and a bishop kneels in prayer before them; crowds of standing figures in long draped robes fill both sides. In the background, buildings, a classical temple and the walls and towers of a city rise in very low relief against hills.
caption: Lorenzo Ghiberti, shrine of San Zanobi, the raising of a child, 1432–1442, bronze. Florence, Santa Maria del Fiore, chapel of San Zanobi. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (detail).

alt: A fresco of a bishop enthroned within a painted triumphal arch against a blue wall sown with gold lilies. The old bishop, in a jewelled mitre, red cope and green-backed throne, raises his right hand in blessing and holds a crosier; two young deacons in dalmatics stand at either side with joined hands. Above, in a lunette, the Virgin and Child with two kneeling angels in fictive white relief on gold. Two medallions with heads of Roman emperors flank the arch. At the left, part of a lion and a distant view of the cathedral dome; at the lower right, a marble doorframe cuts into the fresco.
caption: Domenico Ghirlandaio, Saint Zanobi enthroned between Saints Eugenius and Crescentius, c. 1482–1484, fresco. Florence, Palazzo Vecchio, Sala dei Gigli. Photo: Sailko, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A tall marble column with grey and white veining standing on a round stepped base inside an iron railing in a Florentine square. It carries a conical capital and a stone cross with trilobed ends; an iron ring of leaves surrounds the top of the shaft. Behind it rise the façades of houses with green shutters and restaurant umbrellas; at the right edge, part of the marble cathedral.
caption: The column of San Zanobi, fourteenth century. Florence, Piazza San Giovanni. Photo: Chabe01, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Close view of the upper part of a veined marble column below a dark metal ring, carved with many lines of worn Gothic capitals beginning with the words ANNO AB INCARNATIONE DOMINI. Yellow houses with shutters in the background.
caption: The column of San Zanobi, the inscription, first part. Florence, Piazza San Giovanni. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (detail).

alt: Close view of the same marble column from another side, with the Baptistery's green and white marble at the left, carved with worn Gothic capitals including the words S(AN)CTI LAURENTII, ZENOBII, ULMUS ARBOR and CUM CRUCE IN SIGNO NOTABILI.
caption: The column of San Zanobi, the inscription, second part. Florence, Piazza San Giovanni. Photo: Sailko, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons (detail).

alt: The east end of a Romanesque church of pale granite under a blue sky. Semicircular radiating chapels with tiled roofs, arched windows and engaged columns step up towards the apse; behind them rises a tall bell tower in several stages, with arched openings, gables at the corners of the upper stage and a pointed stone spire topped by a cross.
caption: Collegiate church of Saint-Léonard-de-Noblat, the east end with the radiating chapels and the bell tower, eleventh–twelfth century. Photo: Jochen Jahnke, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A tall stone church with a high gabled end wall and a single arched window, joined to a long two-storey building of stone and brick with small windows. In the foreground a low stone wall and a vaulted gateway with a dark wooden door, under a clear sky.
caption: The hermitage and church of San Leonardo al Lago, near Siena, twelfth–fourteenth century. Photo: Mongolo1984, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A fresco in a pointed arch framed by bands of geometric ornament. In the centre a flight of steps leads up to an open temple with columns and a domed lantern, where a high priest receives a small girl in white; at the left a group of women led by an older woman in a dark mantle, at the right bearded men. Below, a painted frieze with three small half-figures of female saints, one labelled Maria Magdalena; on the pilaster at the left a standing female saint and medallions with virtues.
caption: Lippo Vanni, The Presentation of the Virgin in the Temple, c. 1360–1370. Fresco. Monteriggioni, San Leonardo al Lago, presbytery. Photo: LigaDue, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A horizontal painted panel with a gold ground. In the centre the Virgin, in a dark blue mantle, sits enthroned nursing the Child, with two angels above. At the left stands a young tonsured saint in a red dalmatic holding a book and raising his hand, with an inscription beside his head; at the right Saint Peter in a pink mantle holding keys. At both sides small narrative scenes in three registers, including a figure behind a grille and an upside-down crucifixion. The panel is cracked horizontally and damaged at the bottom.
caption: Maestro del Dossale di Yale (Master of the Magdalen workshop?), Virgin and Child Enthroned between Saints Leonard and Peter, with Scenes from the Life of Saint Peter, c. 1265–1270. Tempera and gold on panel, 106 × 160 cm. New Haven, Yale University Art Gallery. Image: public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: A parchment page written in a single column of brown Romanesque minuscule with many abbreviations. Near the bottom a large red initial S opens a new text, whose first lines include the name Walerannus.
caption: The end of Anselm of Canterbury's reply on the sacraments and the beginning of a letter of Walram of Naumburg to Anselm, from a collection of Anselm's letters, twelfth century. Paris, Bibliothèque nationale de France, Latin 2478, fol. 120v. Source: gallica.bnf.fr / Bibliothèque nationale de France.

alt: Frontispiece of Bede's Life of St Cuthbert
caption: Frontispiece of Bede's Life of St Cuthbert, showing King Æthelstan (924–39) presenting a copy of the book to the saint himself. 29.2 x 20 cm. Originally from MS 183, folio 1v at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge.

alt: The Merciful Knight
caption: Edward Burne-Jones (1833-1898), The Merciful Knight, 1863, watercolour and bodycolour on paper, 100.3 x 69.2 cm, Birmingham City Museum and Art Gallery, Birmingham.

alt: St. John Gualbert Enthroned with Four Stories from his Life
caption: Giovanni dal Biondo (news from 1356 to 1398), St. John Gualbert Enthroned with Four Stories from his Life, c. 1370, tempera on panel, Museo dell'Opera di Santa Croce, Florence.

alt: Glory of St. John Gualbert
caption: Neri di Bicci (-1492), Glory of St. John Gualbert, 1455, fresco, Basilica di Santa Trinità, Florence.

alt: Miracle of St. John Gualbert
caption: Bicci di Lorenzo (1368-1452), Miracle of St. John Gualbert, 1434, tempera on panel, 27,5 x 31 cm, Private collection.

alt: B. ANGELA DE FVLGINIO
caption: Beata Angela da Foligno, XVII secolo, incisione in cavo su rame.

alt: Crucifix
caption: Vision of Blessed Angela of Foligno, c. 1791, oil on canvas, 62 x 40,5 cm. Staatsgalerie Stuttgart.

alt: Interior of a small Gothic chapel entirely covered with frescoes. A rib vault with decorated bands and the symbols of the Evangelists rises above the end wall, which shows a large Crucifixion with angels and crowds of riders and mourners; the side walls carry painted tabernacles and scenes in several registers.
caption: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco and a second painter, decoration of the Cappella di Santa Croce, 1333. Fresco. Montefalco, Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce. Photo: Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco, for educational use only.

alt: Large fresco in a pointed lunette above an altar. Christ hangs dead on a tall cross inscribed INRI, surrounded by six grieving angels on clouds. Below, at left, the fainting Virgin is supported by the holy women beside soldiers with lances and a red banner and a rider on a brown horse; at the centre the Magdalene in green embraces the foot of the cross, with a small kneeling cleric beside her; at right a rider on a white horse raises his hand, Saint John sits grieving, and a group of soldiers and elders stands behind. An inscription runs along the lower edge.
caption: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco, The Crucifixion, with the patron Jean d'Amiel, 1333. Fresco, end wall of the Cappella di Santa Croce. Montefalco, Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce. Photo: Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco, for educational use only.

alt: Detail of a fresco: the Magdalene, with long loose red-gold hair and a green mantle, kneels and embraces the foot of the cross, pressing her face to Christ's bloodied feet. Beside her kneels a small cleric in a black cape with his hands joined. A rider and a man with a lance stand at left; part of an inscription is visible at the bottom.
caption: Detail of the Crucifixion: the Magdalene at the foot of the cross and the kneeling patron Jean d'Amiel. Photo: Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco, for educational use only.

alt: Detail of a fresco: a bearded rider in a golden mail tunic on a white horse raises his right hand towards the cross, with helmeted soldiers holding lances and a shield behind him. Below the horse, Saint John, young, with golden hair and a halo, sits on the ground in a red mantle over a green tunic, his head resting on his hand. The small kneeling patron appears at the left edge, and part of the inscription runs along the bottom.
caption: Detail of the Crucifixion: the centurion on horseback and Saint John. Photo: Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco, for educational use only.

alt: Frescoed side wall of a chapel. At the top, in a lunette, Christ blesses between two angels. Below, a painted Gothic tabernacle with a pointed gable frames the Virgin and Child enthroned between two archangels, and underneath, Christ carrying a large cross before a kneeling nun, with a second nun holding a palm at right. To the upper left a tall woman in a grey mantle walks with a small girl praying behind her; to the upper right the Virgin before a patterned cloth lowers the Christ Child towards a little nun. Lower left, a bishop in a cave holding a cross, with a verse inscription; lower right, a bishop's head at a barred window and other small scenes.
caption: Primo Maestro della Beata Chiara da Montefalco, right wall of the Cappella di Santa Croce, with the painted tabernacle over the former tomb of Chiara, 1333. Fresco. Montefalco, Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce. Photo: Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco, for educational use only.

alt: Detail of a fresco: Christ, with long hair and a halo, wearing a dark red robe, carries a large red cross on his shoulder and bends towards a kneeling haloed nun in a white veil, who grasps the arm of the cross with both hands. At the right stands a second haloed nun in a brown habit holding a palm branch.
caption: Detail of the right wall: Christ with the cross appears to Chiara, with Blessed Giovanna. Photo: Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco, for educational use only.

alt: Frescoed side wall of a chapel. In the lunette, Christ in a mandorla, among angels, raises his hand; at left a bishop in a red cope presents a kneeling tonsured cleric with a bundle above him, at right a crowned female saint presents the same cleric holding a red shield with a white cross, with a small chapel above. A painted inscription runs below. In the lower register, at left, a nun sits up in bed among nuns and friars; in the centre, under a deep window, Christ as the Man of Sorrows; at right an angel descends as an executioner raises his sword over a crowned saint among a crowd before a city.
caption: Second painter of the Cappella di Santa Croce, left wall, with Christ in judgement and the patron Jean d'Amiel, the Death of Chiara, the Ecce Homo and the Martyrdom of Saint Catherine, 1333. Fresco. Montefalco, Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce. Photo: Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco, for educational use only.

alt: Detail of a fresco: in a room with a coffered ceiling of red and orange panels, a haloed nun in a dark habit and white veil sits upright in a bed with her hands folded, looking upwards. Two friars stand by her, one holding a red book; a crowd of veiled nuns presses in at the right, and a nun kneels in the foreground beside the bed, with another woman at its foot.
caption: Detail of the left wall: the Death of Chiara. Photo: Santuario di Santa Chiara della Croce, Montefalco, for educational use only.

alt: Small gold-ground panel showing the body of Christ being lowered from the cross by two men on a ladder, while the Virgin and Saint John reach up to receive him; a man removes the nails from the feet with pincers; on the right mourners raise their arms, among them a woman in a grey mantle and hood; at the bottom a small donor kneels beside a skull at the foot of the cross.
caption: Simone Martini, The Deposition, panel of the Orsini polyptych, tempera and gold on wood, 24 × 15 cm. Antwerp, Koninklijk Museum voor Schone Kunsten. Photo: Koninklijk Museum voor Schone Kunsten Antwerpen, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Fragment of a fresco on a pillar, surrounded by bare plaster. Above, the lower part of a larger figure in a red and blue robe stands on a ledge. Below, a painted inscription reads TA CLARA DE MONTE FALCHO, and under it, in a framed field with a mottled blue ground, the half-length figure of a nun in a black veil and white wimple, with a faint halo, holds a red heart in her right hand; a white lily rises at the right.
caption: Lombard painter, Saint Chiara of Montefalco, late fifteenth or early sixteenth century (?). Fresco fragment, pillar of the nave. Milan, Santa Maria Incoronata. Photo: Giovanni Dall'Orto, free use with attribution, via Wikimedia Commons.

alt: Pala della Santa Umiltà
caption: Pietro Lorenzetti (1280/90-1348) - Pala della santa Umiltà (detail), 1335-40, Galleria degli Uffizi, Florence.

alt: Vitae S. Humilitatis et S. Margaritae de Faventia
caption: Vitae S. Humilitatis et S. Margaritae de Faventia, cod. 271, folio 1r, 355 x 218 mm, Biblioteca Riccardiana, Florence.

alt: Saint Humility and Scenes from Her Life (Pala della beata Umiltà)
caption: Saint Humility and Scenes from Her Life (Pala della beata Umiltà), 1335-40, tempera and gold on panel, central panel 128 × 57 cm; each lateral narrative compartment 45 × 32 cm; each surviving pinnacle 51 × 21 cm; and each predella tondo 18 cm in diameter; 257 x 168 cm (assembled), Galleria degli Uffizi, Florence.

alt: St. Humility heals a sick Nun
caption: St. Humility heals a sick Nun, 1341, tempera and gold on poplar panel, 45 × 55 cm, Gemäldegalerie, Staatliche Museen zu Berlin.

alt: The Miracle of the Ice
caption: The Miracle of the Ice, 1340-41, tempera and gold on poplar panel, 42 × 32 cm, Gemäldegalerie, Staatliche Museen zu Berlin.
